celaleyn:92-92.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ جَاءَكُمْ مُوسَى بِالْبَيِّنَاتِ﴾ with the miracles, such as the staff, the hand and the parting of the sea ﴿ثُمَّ اتَّخَذْتُمُ الْعِجْلَ﴾ as a god ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِهِ﴾ after his going to the appointed meeting ﴿وَأَنْتُمْ ظَالِمُونَ﴾ by taking it.

celaleyn:93-93.t: ﴿وَإِذْ أَخَذْنَا مِيثَاقَكُمْ﴾ to act upon what is in the Torah ﴿وَ﴾ when We had ﴿رَفَعْنَا فَوْقَكُمُ الطُّورَ﴾ the mountain, when you refused to accept it, so that it would fall upon you, and We said: ﴿خُذُوا مَا آتَيْنَاكُمْ بِقُوَّةٍ﴾ with seriousness and effort ﴿وَاسْمَعُوا﴾ what you are commanded, with acceptance ﴿قَالُوا سَمِعْنَا﴾ your word ﴿وَعَصَيْنَا﴾ your command ﴿وَأُشْرِبُوا فِي قُلُوبِهِمُ الْعِجْلَ﴾ i.e. love of it permeated their hearts as drink permeates ﴿بِكُفْرِهِمْ قُلْ﴾ to them ﴿بِئْسَمَا﴾ a thing ﴿يَأْمُرُكُمْ بِهِ إِيمَانُكُمْ﴾ in the Torah: the worship of the calf ﴿إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ in it, as you claimed. The meaning is: you are not believers, because faith does not command the worship of the calf. What is meant is their forefathers, i.e. likewise you are not believers in the Torah, since you have denied Muhammad, and faith in it does not command denying him.

celaleyn:94-94.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾ to them ﴿إِنْ كَانَتْ لَكُمُ الدَّارُ الْآخِرَةُ﴾ i.e. the Garden ﴿عِنْدَ اللَّهِ خَالِصَةً﴾ exclusively ﴿مِنْ دُونِ النَّاسِ﴾ as you claimed ﴿فَتَمَنَّوُا الْمَوْتَ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صَادِقِينَ﴾ both conditions are attached to wishing for it, with the first being a restriction on the second; i.e. if you are truthful in your claim that it is yours, then whoever has it prefers it, and what leads to it is death, so wish for it.

celaleyn:95-95.t: ﴿وَلَنْ يَتَمَنَّوْهُ أَبَدًا بِمَا قَدَّمَتْ أَيْدِيهِمْ﴾ of their disbelief in the Prophet, which entails their lying ﴿وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ بِالظَّالِمِينَ﴾ the disbelievers, and He will requite them.

celaleyn:96-96.t: ﴿وَلَتَجِدَنَّهُمْ﴾ the lām of the oath ﴿أَحْرَصَ النَّاسِ عَلَى حَيَاةٍ وَ﴾ more eager ﴿مِنَ الَّذِينَ أَشْرَكُوا﴾ who deny the Resurrection, for it, because they know that their destination is the Fire, unlike the idolaters, since they deny it ﴿يَوَدُّ﴾ wishes ﴿أَحَدُهُمْ لَوْ يُعَمَّرُ أَلْفَ سَنَةٍ﴾ لَوْ is maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun), in the sense of أَنْ, and together with its ṣila it is an interpreted maṣdar, the mafʿūl (object) of يَوَدُّ ﴿وَمَا هُوَ﴾ i.e. any of them ﴿بِمُزَحْزِحِهِ﴾ removing him ﴿مِنَ الْعَذَابِ﴾ the Fire ﴿أَنْ يُعَمَّرَ﴾ the fāʿil (agent) of مُزَحْزِحِهِ, i.e. his long life ﴿وَاللَّهُ بَصِيرٌ بِمَا يَعْمَلُونَ﴾ with yāʾ and with tāʾ; and He will requite them. Ibn Ṣūriyā asked the Prophet, or ʿUmar, which of the angels brings the revelation; he said, "Gabriel." He said, "He is our enemy; he brings punishment. Had it been Michael we would have believed, because he brings fertility and peace." So the following was revealed:

celaleyn:97-97.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾ to them ﴿مَنْ كَانَ عَدُوًّا لِجِبْرِيلَ﴾ let him die of rage ﴿فَإِنَّهُ نَزَّلَهُ﴾ i.e. the Quran ﴿عَلَى قَلْبِكَ بِإِذْنِ﴾ by the command of ﴿اللَّهِ مُصَدِّقًا لِمَا بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ﴾ the scriptures before it ﴿وَهُدًى﴾ from misguidance ﴿وَبُشْرَى﴾ of the Garden ﴿لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾

celaleyn:98-98.t: ﴿مَنْ كَانَ عَدُوًّا لِلَّهِ وَمَلَائِكَتِهِ وَرُسُلِهِ وَجِبْرِيلَ﴾ with kasra and with fatḥa on the jīm, without hamza, and with hamza, with yāʾ and without it ﴿وَمِيكَالَ﴾ conjoined to الْمَلَائِكَةِ, a conjunction of the particular to the general; in one reading [مِيكَائِيلَ] with hamza and yāʾ, and in another without yāʾ ﴿فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ عَدُوٌّ لِلْكَافِرِينَ﴾ He put it in the place of لَهُمْ ("to them") to make their state clear.

celaleyn:99-99.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ أَنْزَلْنَا إِلَيْكَ﴾ O Muhammad ﴿آيَاتٍ بَيِّنَاتٍ﴾ i.e. clear, a ḥāl (circumstantial); a reply to Ibn Ṣūriyā's saying to the Prophet, "You have not brought us anything." ﴿وَمَا يَكْفُرُ بِهَا إِلَّا الْفَاسِقُونَ﴾

celaleyn:100-100.t: ﴿أَ﴾ did they disbelieve in them, ﴿وَكُلَّمَا عَاهَدُوا﴾ Allah ﴿عَهْدًا﴾ to believe in the Prophet if he came forth, or [made a covenant with] the Prophet not to aid the idolaters against him ﴿نَبَذَهُ﴾ cast it aside ﴿فَرِيقٌ مِنْهُمْ﴾ by breaking it; this is the answer (jawāb) of كُلَّمَا, and it is the locus of the disapproving interrogative ﴿بَلْ﴾ for transition (intiqāl) ﴿أَكْثَرُهُمْ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾

celaleyn:101-101.t: ﴿وَلَمَّا جَاءَهُمْ رَسُولٌ مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ﴾ Muhammad ﷺ ﴿مُصَدِّقٌ لِمَا مَعَهُمْ نَبَذَ فَرِيقٌ مِنَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ كِتَابَ اللَّهِ﴾ i.e. the Torah ﴿وَرَاءَ ظُهُورِهِمْ﴾ i.e. they did not act upon what is in it, such as belief in the Messenger and other things ﴿كَأَنَّهُمْ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ what is in it, that he is a true prophet, or that it is the Book of Allah.

celaleyn:102-102.t: ﴿وَاتَّبَعُوا﴾ conjoined to نَبَذَ ﴿مَا تَتْلُوا﴾ i.e. recited ﴿الشَّيَاطِينُ عَلَى﴾ in the time of ﴿مُلْكِ سُلَيْمَانَ﴾ of sorcery. They had buried it under his throne when his kingdom was taken from him; or they used to eavesdrop [on heaven], add lies to it and pass it on to the soothsayers, who recorded it; this spread, and it became widely held that the jinn know the unseen. So Solomon gathered the books and buried them, and when he died the devils showed people where they were; they dug them out and found sorcery in them, and said, "It was only by this that he ruled over you." So they learned it and rejected the books of their prophets. The Exalted said, clearing Solomon and refuting the Jews in their saying, "Look at Muhammad, mentioning Solomon among the prophets, when he was nothing but a sorcerer": ﴿وَمَا كَفَرَ سُلَيْمَانُ﴾ i.e. he did not practise sorcery, because it is disbelief ﴿وَلَكِنَّ﴾ with doubling and without ﴿الشَّيَاطِينَ كَفَرُوا يُعَلِّمُونَ النَّاسَ السِّحْرَ﴾ the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun of كَفَرُوا ﴿وَ﴾ they teach them ﴿مَا أُنْزِلَ عَلَى الْمَلَكَيْنِ﴾ i.e. what the two were inspired with of sorcery; it has also been read with kasra on the lām [i.e. al-malikayn, "the two kings"]; who were ﴿بِبَابِلَ﴾ a town in the Sawād of Iraq ﴿هَارُوتَ وَمَارُوتَ﴾ a badal (substitute) or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) of الْمَلَكَيْنِ. Ibn ʿAbbās said: "They were two sorcerers who taught sorcery." And it is said: two angels sent down to teach it, as a trial from Allah for people. ﴿وَمَا يُعَلِّمَانِ مِنْ﴾ zāʾida (redundant) ﴿أَحَدٍ حَتَّى يَقُولَا﴾ to him, as sincere advice ﴿إِنَّمَا نَحْنُ فِتْنَةٌ﴾ a trial from Allah for people, to test them by teaching it; whoever learns it disbelieves, and whoever leaves it is a believer ﴿فَلَا تَكْفُرْ﴾ by learning it. If he insisted on being taught, they taught him. ﴿فَيَتَعَلَّمُونَ مِنْهُمَا مَا يُفَرِّقُونَ بِهِ بَيْنَ الْمَرْءِ وَزَوْجِهِ﴾ by making each hateful to the other ﴿وَمَا هُمْ﴾ i.e. the sorcerers ﴿بِضَارِّينَ بِهِ﴾ by the sorcery ﴿مِنْ﴾ zāʾida ﴿أَحَدٍ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ﴾ by His will ﴿وَيَتَعَلَّمُونَ مَا يَضُرُّهُمْ﴾ in the Hereafter ﴿وَلَا يَنْفَعُهُمْ﴾ and that is sorcery ﴿وَلَقَدْ﴾ the lām of the oath ﴿عَلِمُوا﴾ i.e. the Jews ﴿لَمَنِ﴾ the lām of inception (lām al-ibtidāʾ), suspending (muʿalliqa) what precedes it [from governing], and مَنْ is a relative noun ﴿اشْتَرَاهُ﴾ chose it, or took it in exchange for the Book of Allah ﴿مَا لَهُ فِي الْآخِرَةِ مِنْ خَلَاقٍ﴾ a share in the Garden ﴿وَلَبِئْسَ مَا﴾ a thing ﴿شَرَوْا﴾ sold ﴿بِهِ أَنْفُسَهُمْ﴾ i.e. of those selling, i.e. their share of the Hereafter: that they learned it, since it made the Fire binding upon them ﴿لَوْ كَانُوا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ the reality of the punishment they will come to, they would not have learned it.

celaleyn:103-103.t: ﴿وَلَوْ أَنَّهُمْ﴾ i.e. the Jews ﴿آمَنُوا﴾ in the Prophet and the Quran ﴿وَاتَّقَوْا﴾ the punishment of Allah, by abandoning acts of disobedience to Him such as sorcery. The apodosis (jawāb) of لَوْ is omitted, i.e. "they would have been rewarded", indicated by ﴿لَمَثُوبَةٌ﴾ reward; it is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the lām in it is for the oath ﴿مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ خَيْرٌ﴾ its khabar (predicate), [i.e. better] than that for which they sold themselves ﴿لَوْ كَانُوا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ that it is better, they would not have preferred that to it.

celaleyn:104-104.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا تَقُولُوا﴾ to the Prophet ﴿رَاعِنَا﴾ an imperative from murāʿāt ("having regard"). They used to say that to him, and in the language of the Jews it is an insult, from ruʿūna ("folly"); so they were delighted with that and addressed the Prophet with it, and the believers were forbidden it ﴿وَقُولُوا﴾ in its place ﴿انْظُرْنَا﴾ i.e. look at us ﴿وَاسْمَعُوا﴾ what you are commanded, with acceptance ﴿وَلِلْكَافِرِينَ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ﴾ painful; it is the Fire.

celaleyn:213-213.t: ﴿كَانَ النَّاسُ أُمَّةً وَاحِدَةً﴾ upon faith, then they differed, some believing and some disbelieving; ﴿فَبَعَثَ اللَّهُ النَّبِيِّينَ﴾ to them ﴿مُبَشِّرِينَ﴾ giving glad tidings of Paradise to whoever believed ﴿وَمُنْذِرِينَ﴾ warning whoever disbelieved of the Fire; ﴿وَأَنْزَلَ مَعَهُمُ الْكِتَابَ﴾ in the sense of the Books ﴿بِالْحَقِّ﴾ attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أَنْزَلَ», ﴿لِيَحْكُمَ﴾ by it ﴿بَيْنَ النَّاسِ فِيمَا اخْتَلَفُوا فِيهِ﴾ of religion. ﴿وَمَا اخْتَلَفَ فِيهِ﴾ i.e. the religion ﴿إِلَّا الَّذِينَ أُوتُوهُ﴾ i.e. the Book, so some believed and some disbelieved, ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا جَاءَتْهُمُ الْبَيِّنَاتُ﴾ the clear proofs of tawḥīd. «مِنْ» is attached to «اخْتَلَفَ», and it and what follows it are placed before the exception in meaning. ﴿بَغْيًا﴾ on the part of the disbelievers ﴿بَيْنَهُمْ فَهَدَى اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لِمَا اخْتَلَفُوا فِيهِ مِنَ﴾ explicative (li-l-bayān) ﴿الْحَقِّ بِإِذْنِهِ﴾ by His will; ﴿وَاللَّهُ يَهْدِي مَنْ يَشَاءُ﴾ his guidance ﴿إِلَى صِرَاطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ﴾ the way of truth. And concerning a hardship that befell the Muslims there was revealed:

celaleyn:214-214.t: ﴿أَمْ﴾ [i.e.] "rather, did" (bal a-) ﴿حَسِبْتُمْ أَنْ تَدْخُلُوا الْجَنَّةَ وَلَمَّا﴾ [i.e.] lam (not) ﴿يَأْتِكُمْ مَثَلُ﴾ the like of what came to ﴿الَّذِينَ خَلَوْا مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ﴾ of the believers, of trials, so that you endure as they endured? ﴿مَسَّتْهُمْ﴾ a resumptive clause (jumla mustaʾnafa) explaining what precedes it ﴿الْبَأْسَاءُ﴾ extreme poverty ﴿وَالضَّرَّاءُ﴾ illness ﴿وَزُلْزِلُوا﴾ they were shaken by kinds of affliction, ﴿حَتَّى يَقُولَ﴾ with the accusative and the nominative, i.e. "said", ﴿الرَّسُولُ وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مَعَهُ﴾ finding the help slow in coming because of the extremity of the hardship upon them: ﴿مَتَى﴾ will come ﴿نَصْرُ اللَّهِ﴾ which we were promised? And they were answered from Allah: ﴿أَلَا إِنَّ نَصْرَ اللَّهِ قَرِيبٌ﴾ its coming.

celaleyn:215-215.t: ﴿يَسْأَلُونَكَ﴾ O Muhammad, ﴿مَاذَا يُنْفِقُونَ﴾ i.e. what it is that they should spend. The questioner was ʿAmr ibn al-Jamūḥ; he was an old man with wealth, and he asked him ﷺ about what to spend and on whom to spend. ﴿قُلْ﴾ to them: ﴿مَا أَنْفَقْتُمْ مِنْ خَيْرٍ﴾ an explication (bayān) of «مَا», covering little and much; in it is the explanation of what is spent, which is one of the two parts of the question; and He answered about the recipients, which is the other part, by His saying: ﴿فَلِلْوَالِدَيْنِ وَالْأَقْرَبِينَ وَالْيَتَامَى وَالْمَسَاكِينِ وَابْنِ السَّبِيلِ﴾ i.e. they are the most entitled to it. ﴿وَمَا تَفْعَلُوا مِنْ خَيْرٍ﴾ spending or other, ﴿فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ بِهِ عَلِيمٌ﴾ and will recompense it.

celaleyn:216-216.t: ﴿كُتِبَ﴾ is prescribed ﴿عَلَيْكُمُ الْقِتَالُ﴾ against the disbelievers, ﴿وَهُوَ كُرْهٌ﴾ disliked ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ by nature, because of its hardship. ﴿وَعَسَى أَنْ تَكْرَهُوا شَيْئًا وَهُوَ خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ وَعَسَى أَنْ تُحِبُّوا شَيْئًا وَهُوَ شَرٌّ لَكُمْ﴾ because the soul inclines to desires that bring about its ruin and shuns obligations that bring about its happiness; so perhaps there is good for you in fighting — even if you dislike it — because in it there is either victory and booty or martyrdom and reward; and [perhaps there is] evil in abandoning it — even if you love that — because in it there is humiliation, poverty and deprivation of reward. ﴿وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ﴾ what is good for you ﴿وَأَنْتُمْ لَا تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ that; so hasten to what He commands you. The Prophet ﷺ sent out the first of his raiding parties, under the command of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaḥsh; they fought the idolaters and killed Ibn al-Ḥaḍramī on the last day of Jumādā al-Ākhira, and it was confused for them with Rajab; so the disbelievers reproached them for violating it, and there was revealed:

celaleyn:217-217.t: ﴿يَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ الشَّهْرِ الْحَرَامِ﴾ the sacred [month], ﴿قِتَالٍ فِيهِ﴾ a badal ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion). ﴿قُلْ﴾ to them: ﴿قِتَالٌ فِيهِ كَبِيرٌ﴾ grave in sin — a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate); ﴿وَصَدٌّ﴾ a mubtadaʾ: preventing people ﴿عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ﴾ His religion, ﴿وَكُفْرٌ بِهِ﴾ in Allah, ﴿وَ﴾ barring from ﴿الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرَامِ﴾ i.e. Mecca, ﴿وَإِخْرَاجُ أَهْلِهِ مِنْهُ﴾ — and they are the Prophet ﷺ and the believers — and the khabar of the mubtadaʾ is ﴿أَكْبَرُ﴾ greater in sin ﴿عِنْدَ اللَّهِ﴾ than fighting in it; ﴿وَالْفِتْنَةُ﴾ your associating partners [with Allah] ﴿أَكْبَرُ مِنَ الْقَتْلِ﴾ by you in it. ﴿وَلَا يَزَالُونَ﴾ i.e. the disbelievers ﴿يُقَاتِلُونَكُمْ﴾ O believers ﴿حَتَّى﴾ so that ﴿يَرُدُّوكُمْ عَنْ دِينِكُمْ﴾ to disbelief ﴿إِنِ اسْتَطَاعُوا وَمَنْ يَرْتَدِدْ مِنْكُمْ عَنْ دِينِهِ فَيَمُتْ وَهُوَ كَافِرٌ فَأُولَئِكَ حَبِطَتْ﴾ are nullified ﴿أَعْمَالُهُمْ﴾ righteous ﴿فِي الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ﴾ so they are not counted and there is no reward for them. The restriction to dying in that state conveys that if he returned to Islam his deeds would not be nullified, so he would be rewarded for them and would not repeat them, such as the ḥajj for example; al-Shāfiʿī holds this view. ﴿وَأُولَئِكَ أَصْحَابُ النَّارِ هُمْ فِيهَا خَالِدُونَ﴾. And when the raiding party thought that even if they were free of sin they would get no reward, there was revealed:

celaleyn:218-218.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَالَّذِينَ هَاجَرُوا﴾ left their homelands ﴿وَجَاهَدُوا فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ﴾ to make His religion supreme, ﴿أُولَئِكَ يَرْجُونَ رَحْمَتَ اللَّهِ﴾ His reward; ﴿وَاللَّهُ غَفُورٌ﴾ to the believers ﴿رَحِيمٌ﴾ to them.

celaleyn:219-219.t: ﴿يَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ الْخَمْرِ وَالْمَيْسِرِ﴾ gambling: what is their ruling? ﴿قُلْ﴾ to them: ﴿فِيهِمَا﴾ i.e. in engaging in them ﴿إِثْمٌ كَبِيرٌ﴾ great — and in one reading with the thāʾ [i.e. كَثِيرٌ, "much"] — because of the quarrelling, mutual abuse and obscene talk that come about through them, ﴿وَمَنَافِعُ لِلنَّاسِ﴾ through the pleasure and joy in wine, and gaining wealth without toil in gambling; ﴿وَإِثْمُهُمَا﴾ i.e. the harms that arise from them ﴿أَكْبَرُ﴾ greater ﴿مِنْ نَفْعِهِمَا﴾. When it was revealed, some people drank it and others abstained, until the verse of al-Māʾida forbade it. ﴿وَيَسْأَلُونَكَ مَاذَا يُنْفِقُونَ﴾ i.e. what its amount is. ﴿قُلِ﴾ spend ﴿الْعَفْوَ﴾ i.e. what is surplus to need, and do not spend what you need and so ruin yourselves. In one reading it is nominative, with an implied "it is" (huwa). ﴿كَذَلِكَ﴾ i.e. just as He has made clear to you what has been mentioned, ﴿يُبَيِّنُ اللَّهُ لَكُمُ الْآيَاتِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَفَكَّرُونَ﴾

celaleyn:220-220.t: ﴿فِي﴾ the affair of ﴿الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ﴾ and so adopt what is most beneficial for you in both. ﴿وَيَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ الْيَتَامَى﴾ and the difficulty they meet concerning them: if they eat together with them they sin, and if they separate their wealth from their own and make food for them alone, it is a hardship. ﴿قُلْ إِصْلَاحٌ لَهُمْ﴾ in their wealth by making it grow, and your mixing [with them], is better (خَيْرٌ) than abandoning that; ﴿وَإِنْ تُخَالِطُوهُمْ﴾ i.e. mix your expenses with theirs, ﴿فَإِخْوَانُكُمْ﴾ i.e. they are your brothers in religion, and it is the way of a brother to mix with his brother; i.e. that is permitted to you. ﴿وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ الْمُفْسِدَ﴾ of their wealth by his mixing ﴿مِنَ الْمُصْلِحِ﴾ of it, and will recompense each of them. ﴿وَلَوْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ لَأَعْنَتَكُمْ﴾ He would have made it hard for you by forbidding mixing. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ﴾ prevailing over His affair, ﴿حَكِيمٌ﴾ in His making.

celaleyn:221-221.t: ﴿وَلَا تَنْكِحُوا﴾ marry, O Muslims, ﴿الْمُشْرِكَاتِ﴾ i.e. disbelieving women ﴿حَتَّى يُؤْمِنَّ وَلَأَمَةٌ مُؤْمِنَةٌ خَيْرٌ مِنْ مُشْرِكَةٍ﴾ free woman — because the occasion of its revelation was the reproach of one who married a slave woman and the encouragement of him to marry a free idolatress — ﴿وَلَوْ أَعْجَبَتْكُمْ﴾ for her beauty and her wealth. This is restricted to other than women of the Book, by the verse {وَالْمُحْصَنَاتُ مِنَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ}. ﴿وَلَا تُنْكِحُوا﴾ give in marriage ﴿الْمُشْرِكِينَ﴾ i.e. disbelievers, believing women ﴿حَتَّى يُؤْمِنُوا وَلَعَبْدٌ مُؤْمِنٌ خَيْرٌ مِنْ مُشْرِكٍ وَلَوْ أَعْجَبَكُمْ﴾ for his wealth and his good looks. ﴿أُولَئِكَ﴾ i.e. the people of shirk ﴿يَدْعُونَ إِلَى النَّارِ﴾ by calling to the deeds that bring it about, so intermarriage with them is not fitting; ﴿وَاللَّهُ يَدْعُو﴾ on the tongue of His messengers ﴿إِلَى الْجَنَّةِ وَالْمَغْفِرَةِ﴾ i.e. the deeds that bring them about ﴿بِإِذْنِهِ﴾ by His will, so responding to Him by marrying His friends is obligatory; ﴿وَيُبَيِّنُ آيَاتِهِ لِلنَّاسِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَذَكَّرُونَ﴾ take heed.

celaleyn:222-222.t: ﴿وَيَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ الْمَحِيضِ﴾ i.e. menstruation or its place: what is to be done with women during it? ﴿قُلْ هُوَ أَذًى﴾ filth, or its location. ﴿فَاعْتَزِلُوا النِّسَاءَ﴾ refrain from intercourse with them ﴿فِي الْمَحِيضِ﴾ i.e. its time or its place, ﴿وَلَا تَقْرَبُوهُنَّ﴾ through intercourse ﴿حَتَّى يَطْهُرْنَ﴾ with sukūn on the ṭāʾ, and with doubling of it and of the hāʾ [i.e. yaṭṭahharna], in which the tāʾ of the original form is assimilated into the ṭāʾ; i.e. they wash after it stops. ﴿فَإِذَا تَطَهَّرْنَ فَأْتُوهُنَّ﴾ through intercourse ﴿مِنْ حَيْثُ أَمَرَكُمُ اللَّهُ﴾ to avoid it during menstruation, namely the front (qubul), and do not go beyond it to another. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ﴾ rewards and honours ﴿التَّوَّابِينَ﴾ from sins ﴿وَيُحِبُّ الْمُتَطَهِّرِينَ﴾ from impurities.

celaleyn:223-223.t: ﴿نِسَاؤُكُمْ حَرْثٌ لَكُمْ﴾ i.e. the place where you sow offspring; ﴿فَأْتُوا حَرْثَكُمْ﴾ i.e. its place, which is the front (qubul), ﴿أَنَّى﴾ how ﴿شِئْتُمْ﴾ standing, sitting, lying, from the front or from behind. It was revealed in rebuttal of the Jews' saying: "Whoever comes to his wife in her front from the direction of her back, the child will be born cross-eyed." ﴿وَقَدِّمُوا لِأَنْفُسِكُمْ﴾ righteous deeds, such as saying the basmala at intercourse; ﴿وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ﴾ in His command and prohibition, ﴿وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّكُمْ مُلَاقُوهُ﴾ at the resurrection, and He will recompense you for your deeds; ﴿وَبَشِّرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ who fear Him, of Paradise.

celaleyn:224-224.t: ﴿وَلَا تَجْعَلُوا اللَّهَ﴾ i.e. swearing by Him ﴿عُرْضَةً﴾ a preventing cause ﴿لِأَيْمَانِكُمْ﴾ i.e. a target for them, by swearing by Him often, ﴿أَنْ﴾ not ﴿تَبَرُّوا وَتَتَّقُوا﴾ — for an oath upon that is disliked, and breaking it is recommended (sunna), with expiation; unlike an oath to do righteousness and the like, which is obedience — ﴿وَتُصْلِحُوا بَيْنَ النَّاسِ﴾. The meaning is: do not refrain from doing the righteousness and the like that has been mentioned when you have sworn [not to do] it; rather do it and expiate, because the occasion of its revelation was refraining from that. ﴿وَاللَّهُ سَمِيعٌ﴾ of your words, ﴿عَلِيمٌ﴾ of your states.

celaleyn:105-105.t: ﴿مَا يَوَدُّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ وَلَا الْمُشْرِكِينَ﴾ among the Arabs; conjoined to أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ, and مِنْ is explicative (li-l-bayān) ﴿أَنْ يُنَزَّلَ عَلَيْكُمْ مِنْ﴾ zāʾida (redundant) ﴿خَيْرٍ﴾ revelation ﴿مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ﴾ out of envy of you ﴿وَاللَّهُ يَخْتَصُّ بِرَحْمَتِهِ﴾ His prophethood ﴿مَنْ يَشَاءُ وَاللَّهُ ذُو الْفَضْلِ الْعَظِيمِ﴾

celaleyn:106-106.t: When the disbelievers attacked abrogation (naskh) and said, "Muhammad commands his Companions to do something today and forbids it tomorrow", the following was revealed: ﴿مَا﴾ conditional ﴿نَنْسَخْ مِنْ آيَةٍ﴾ We remove its ruling, either together with its wording or not. In one reading with ḍamma on the nūn [i.e. نُنْسِخْ], from ansakha, i.e. We command you or Gabriel to abrogate it ﴿أَوْ نَنْسَأْهَا﴾ We defer it, so that We do not remove its ruling but lift its recitation, or We defer it in the Preserved Tablet. In one reading [نُنْسِهَا], without hamza, from forgetting, i.e. We cause you to forget it, i.e. We erase it from your heart. The apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is ﴿نَأْتِ بِخَيْرٍ مِنْهَا﴾ more beneficial to the servants, in ease or in greater reward ﴿أَوْ مِثْلِهَا﴾ in obligation and reward ﴿أَلَمْ تَعْلَمْ أَنَّ اللَّهَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ﴾ and among that is abrogation and replacement. The interrogative is for affirmation (taqrīr).

celaleyn:107-107.t: ﴿أَلَمْ تَعْلَمْ أَنَّ اللَّهَ لَهُ مُلْكُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ He does in them whatever He wills ﴿وَمَا لَكُمْ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾ i.e. other than Him ﴿مِنْ﴾ zāʾida (redundant) ﴿وَلِيٍّ﴾ to protect you ﴿وَلَا نَصِيرٍ﴾ to keep His punishment from you if it comes to you. The following was revealed when the people of Mecca asked him to make it [i.e. Mecca] spacious and to turn al-Ṣafā into gold:

celaleyn:108-108.t: ﴿أَمْ﴾ rather, do ﴿تُرِيدُونَ أَنْ تَسْأَلُوا رَسُولَكُمْ كَمَا سُئِلَ مُوسَى﴾ i.e. his people asked him ﴿مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾ such as their saying "Show us Allah openly" and other things ﴿وَمَنْ يَتَبَدَّلِ الْكُفْرَ بِالْإِيمَانِ﴾ i.e. takes it in its place, by neglecting to consider the clear signs and demanding others ﴿فَقَدْ ضَلَّ سَوَاءَ السَّبِيلِ﴾ has missed the true path; sawāʾ originally means the middle.

celaleyn:109-109.t: ﴿وَدَّ كَثِيرٌ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ لَوْ﴾ maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun) ﴿يَرُدُّونَكُمْ مِنْ بَعْدِ إِيمَانِكُمْ كُفَّارًا حَسَدًا﴾ a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), being ﴿مِنْ عِنْدِ أَنْفُسِهِمْ﴾ i.e. their wicked souls drove them to it ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا تَبَيَّنَ لَهُمْ﴾ in the Torah ﴿الْحَقُّ﴾ concerning the Prophet ﴿فَاعْفُوا﴾ them, i.e. leave them ﴿وَاصْفَحُوا﴾ turn away, and do not requite them ﴿حَتَّى يَأْتِيَ اللَّهُ بِأَمْرِهِ﴾ concerning them, namely fighting ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ﴾

celaleyn:110-110.t: ﴿وَأَقِيمُوا الصَّلَوةَ وَآتُوا الزَّكَوةَ وَمَا تُقَدِّمُوا لِأَنْفُسِكُمْ مِنْ خَيْرٍ﴾ an act of obedience, such as maintaining ties and charity ﴿تَجِدُوهُ﴾ i.e. its reward ﴿عِنْدَ اللَّهِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ﴾ and He will requite you for it.

celaleyn:111-111.t: ﴿وَقَالُوا لَنْ يَدْخُلَ الْجَنَّةَ إِلَّا مَنْ كَانَ هُودًا﴾ plural of hāʾid ("Jew") ﴿أَوْ نَصَارَى﴾ The Jews of Medina and the Christians of Najrān said that when they debated in the presence of the Prophet ﷺ; i.e. the Jews said, "None will enter it except the Jews", and the Christians said, "None will enter it except the Christians." ﴿تِلْكَ﴾ saying ﴿أَمَانِيُّهُمْ﴾ their vain desires ﴿قُلْ﴾ to them ﴿هَاتُوا بُرْهَانَكُمْ﴾ your proof for that ﴿إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صَادِقِينَ﴾ in it.

celaleyn:112-112.t: ﴿بَلَى﴾ others will enter the Garden: ﴿مَنْ أَسْلَمَ وَجْهَهُ لِلَّهِ﴾ i.e. submitted to His command. The face is singled out because it is the noblest of the limbs, so the rest are all the more so ﴿وَهُوَ مُحْسِنٌ﴾ affirming the oneness of God ﴿فَلَهُ أَجْرُهُ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِ﴾ i.e. the reward of his deeds, the Garden ﴿وَلَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ﴾ in the Hereafter.

celaleyn:113-113.t: ﴿وَقَالَتِ الْيَهُودُ لَيْسَتِ النَّصَارَى عَلَى شَيْءٍ﴾ worth considering, and they disbelieved in Jesus ﴿وَقَالَتِ النَّصَارَى لَيْسَتِ الْيَهُودُ عَلَى شَيْءٍ﴾ worth considering, and they disbelieved in Moses ﴿وَهُمْ﴾ i.e. both groups ﴿يَتْلُونَ الْكِتَابَ﴾ sent down to them; in the scripture of the Jews there is confirmation of Jesus, and in the scripture of the Christians confirmation of Moses. The clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿كَذَلِكَ﴾ just as these said ﴿قَالَ الَّذِينَ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ i.e. the idolaters among the Arabs and others ﴿مِثْلَ قَوْلِهِمْ﴾ an explanation (bayān) of the meaning of ذَلِكَ, i.e. they said of every adherent of a religion: "They are not on anything" ﴿فَاللَّهُ يَحْكُمُ بَيْنَهُمْ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ فِيمَا كَانُوا فِيهِ يَخْتَلِفُونَ﴾ in the matter of religion, and He will admit the one in the right to the Garden and the one in the wrong to the Fire.

celaleyn:114-114.t: ﴿وَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ﴾ i.e. no one is more unjust ﴿مِمَّنْ مَنَعَ مَسَاجِدَ اللَّهِ أَنْ يُذْكَرَ فِيهَا اسْمُهُ﴾ through prayer and glorification ﴿وَسَعَى فِي خَرَابِهَا﴾ by demolition or disuse. It was revealed as information about the Romans who ruined Jerusalem (Bayt al-Maqdis), or about the idolaters when they barred the Prophet ﷺ from the House in the year of al-Ḥudaybiya ﴿أُولَئِكَ مَا كَانَ لَهُمْ أَنْ يَدْخُلُوهَا إِلَّا خَائِفِينَ﴾ a declarative statement (khabar) in the sense of a command, i.e. make them afraid through jihād, so that none of them enters it in safety ﴿لَهُمْ فِي الدُّنْيَا خِزْيٌ﴾ contempt, through killing, captivity and the jizya ﴿وَلَهُمْ فِي الْآخِرَةِ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمٌ﴾ it is the Fire. The following was revealed when the Jews attacked the abrogation of the qibla, or the performance of the supererogatory prayer on a mount while travelling, in whatever direction it faces:

celaleyn:115-115.t: ﴿وَلِلَّهِ الْمَشْرِقُ وَالْمَغْرِبُ﴾ i.e. the whole earth, because they are its two sides ﴿فَأَيْنَمَا تُوَلُّوا﴾ your faces in prayer, by His command ﴿فَثَمَّ﴾ there ﴿وَجْهُ اللَّهِ﴾ His qibla with which He is pleased ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ وَاسِعٌ﴾ His bounty encompasses everything ﴿عَلِيمٌ﴾ of the management of His creation.

celaleyn:116-116.t: ﴿وَقَالُوا﴾ with wāw and without it; i.e. the Jews, the Christians, and those who claimed that the angels are the daughters of Allah ﴿اتَّخَذَ اللَّهُ وَلَدًا﴾ The Exalted said: ﴿سُبْحَانَهُ﴾ declaring Him free of that ﴿بَلْ لَهُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ as possession, creation and servants, and ownership is incompatible with begetting. He expressed it with مَا, giving precedence (taghlīb) to what is not rational ﴿كُلٌّ لَهُ قَانِتُونَ﴾ obedient, each in what is required of it; in it there is taghlīb of the rational.

celaleyn:117-117.t: ﴿بَدِيعُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ who brought them into being without any previous model ﴿وَإِذَا قَضَى﴾ willed ﴿أَمْرًا﴾ i.e. its coming into being ﴿فَإِنَّمَا يَقُولُ لَهُ كُنْ فَيَكُونُ﴾ i.e. then it is. In one reading it is in the accusative [i.e. فَيَكُونَ], as the answer to the command.

celaleyn:118-118.t: ﴿وَقَالَ الَّذِينَ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ i.e. the disbelievers of Mecca, to the Prophet ﷺ ﴿لَوْلَا﴾ why does not ﴿يُكَلِّمُنَا اللَّهُ﴾ [telling us] that you are His messenger ﴿أَوْ تَأْتِينَا آيَةٌ﴾ of those we have demanded, as proof of your truthfulness ﴿كَذَلِكَ﴾ just as these said ﴿قَالَ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ﴾ of the disbelievers of past nations, to their prophets ﴿مِثْلَ قَوْلِهِمْ﴾ of obstinacy and demanding signs ﴿تَشَابَهَتْ قُلُوبُهُمْ﴾ in disbelief and stubbornness; in it there is consolation for the Prophet ﷺ ﴿قَدْ بَيَّنَّا الْآيَاتِ لِقَوْمٍ يُوقِنُونَ﴾ know that they are signs, and so believe; demanding a sign in addition to them is obstinacy.

celaleyn:119-119.t: ﴿إِنَّا أَرْسَلْنَاكَ﴾ O Muhammad ﴿بِالْحَقِّ﴾ with guidance ﴿بَشِيرًا﴾ giving glad tidings of the Garden to whoever responds to it ﴿وَنَذِيرًا﴾ warning of the Fire whoever does not respond to it ﴿وَلَا تُسْأَلُ عَنْ أَصْحَابِ الْجَحِيمِ﴾ the Fire, i.e. the disbelievers, why they did not believe; your duty is only to convey. In one reading تُسْأَلْ is in the jussive, as a prohibition.

celaleyn:120-120.t: ﴿وَلَنْ تَرْضَى عَنْكَ الْيَهُودُ وَلَا النَّصَارَى حَتَّى تَتَّبِعَ مِلَّتَهُمْ﴾ their religion ﴿قُلْ إِنَّ هُدَى اللَّهِ﴾ i.e. Islam ﴿هُوَ الْهُدَى﴾ and everything else is misguidance ﴿وَلَئِنِ﴾ the lām of the oath ﴿اتَّبَعْتَ أَهْوَاءَهُمُ﴾ to which they call you, hypothetically ﴿بَعْدَ الَّذِي جَاءَكَ مِنَ الْعِلْمِ﴾ the revelation from Allah ﴿مَا لَكَ مِنَ اللَّهِ مِنْ وَلِيٍّ﴾ to protect you ﴿وَلَا نَصِيرٍ﴾ to defend you from Him.

celaleyn:121-121.t: ﴿الَّذِينَ آتَيْنَاهُمُ الْكِتَابَ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject) ﴿يَتْلُونَهُ حَقَّ تِلَاوَتِهِ﴾ i.e. they recite it as it was sent down; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and حَقَّ is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun) [i.e. a mafʿūl muṭlaq]; and the khabar (predicate) is ﴿أُولَئِكَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِهِ﴾ It was revealed about a group who came from Abyssinia and embraced Islam. ﴿وَمَنْ يَكْفُرْ بِهِ﴾ i.e. the Book that was given, by distorting it ﴿فَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الْخَاسِرُونَ﴾ because they end up in the Fire, made everlasting for them.

celaleyn:122-122.t: ﴿يَا بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ اذْكُرُوا نِعْمَتِيَ الَّتِي أَنْعَمْتُ عَلَيْكُمْ وَأَنِّي فَضَّلْتُكُمْ عَلَى الْعَالَمِينَ﴾ the like of it has preceded.

celaleyn:123-123.t: ﴿وَاتَّقُوا﴾ fear ﴿يَوْمًا لَا تَجْزِي﴾ avails ﴿نَفْسٌ عَنْ نَفْسٍ﴾ in which ﴿شَيْئًا وَلَا يُقْبَلُ مِنْهَا عَدْلٌ﴾ ransom ﴿وَلَا تَنْفَعُهَا شَفَاعَةٌ وَلَا هُمْ يُنْصَرُونَ﴾ protected from the punishment of Allah.

celaleyn:124-124.t: ﴿وَ﴾ remember ﴿إِذِ ابْتَلَى﴾ tested ﴿إِبْرَاهِيمَ﴾ and in one reading Ibrāhām ﴿رَبُّهُ بِكَلِمَاتٍ﴾ with commands and prohibitions that He charged him with. It is said they are the rites of Ḥajj; and it is said: rinsing the mouth, rinsing the nose, the tooth-stick, trimming the moustache, parting the hair, cutting the nails, plucking the armpit hair, shaving the pubic hair, circumcision and cleaning oneself with water after relieving oneself ﴿فَأَتَمَّهُنَّ﴾ he carried them out completely ﴿قَالَ﴾ the Exalted to him ﴿إِنِّي جَاعِلُكَ لِلنَّاسِ إِمَامًا﴾ an example in religion ﴿قَالَ وَمِنْ ذُرِّيَّتِي﴾ my children, make leaders ﴿قَالَ لَا يَنَالُ عَهْدِي﴾ of leadership ﴿الظَّالِمِينَ﴾ the disbelievers among them; this indicates that it does reach those who are not wrongdoers.

celaleyn:225-225.t: ﴿لَا يُؤَاخِذُكُمُ اللَّهُ بِاللَّغْوِ﴾ occurring ﴿فِي أَيْمَانِكُمْ﴾ — it is what the tongue runs to without intending an oath, such as "No, by Allah" and "Yes, by Allah"; there is no sin in it and no expiation — ﴿وَلَكِنْ يُؤَاخِذُكُمْ بِمَا كَسَبَتْ قُلُوبُكُمْ﴾ i.e. what they intended of oaths, when you break them. ﴿وَاللَّهُ غَفُورٌ﴾ of what was idle ﴿حَلِيمٌ﴾ in delaying punishment from the one who deserves it.

celaleyn:226-226.t: ﴿لِلَّذِينَ يُؤْلُونَ مِنْ نِسَائِهِمْ﴾ i.e. swear not to have intercourse with them, ﴿تَرَبُّصُ﴾ a waiting of ﴿أَرْبَعَةِ أَشْهُرٍ فَإِنْ فَاءُوا﴾ return, within it or after it, from the oath to intercourse, ﴿فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ﴾ to them, for the harm they did the woman by the oath, ﴿رَحِيمٌ﴾ to them.

celaleyn:227-227.t: ﴿وَإِنْ عَزَمُوا الطَّلَاقَ﴾ i.e. resolve upon it, by not returning, then let them carry it out; ﴿فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ سَمِيعٌ﴾ of their words, ﴿عَلِيمٌ﴾ of their resolve. The meaning is: after the waiting mentioned, they have nothing but returning or divorce.

celaleyn:228-228.t:
﴿وَالْمُطَلَّقَاتُ يَتَرَبَّصْنَ﴾ i.e. let them wait ﴿بِأَنْفُسِهِنَّ﴾ from marriage ﴿ثَلَاثَةَ قُرُوءٍ﴾ passing from the time of divorce; plural of qarʾ, with fatḥa on the qāf, which is purity or menstruation — two views. This is for those with whom the marriage was consummated; as for others, there is no waiting period (ʿidda) upon them, because of His saying {فَمَا لَكُمْ عَلَيْهِنَّ مِنْ عِدَّةٍ}; and for other than the woman past menstruation and the young girl, for their ʿidda is three months; and the pregnant, for their ʿidda is that they deliver their burden, as in Sūrat al-Ṭalāq; and slave women, for their ʿidda is two qarʾs by the Sunna. ﴿وَلَا يَحِلُّ لَهُنَّ أَنْ يَكْتُمْنَ مَا خَلَقَ اللَّهُ فِي أَرْحَامِهِنَّ﴾ of child or menstruation ﴿إِنْ كُنَّ يُؤْمِنَّ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ وَبُعُولَتُهُنَّ﴾ their husbands ﴿أَحَقُّ بِرَدِّهِنَّ﴾ by taking them back, even if they refuse, ﴿فِي ذَلِكَ﴾ i.e. in the waiting time, ﴿إِنْ أَرَادُوا إِصْلَاحًا﴾ between the two, not harming the woman. It is an urging to intend that, not a condition for the permissibility of taking back. This is in revocable divorce. «أَحَقُّ» has no comparative sense here, since no one other than them has any right to marry them during the ʿidda. ﴿وَلَهُنَّ﴾ over the husbands ﴿مِثْلُ الَّذِي﴾ they have ﴿عَلَيْهِنَّ﴾ of rights ﴿بِالْمَعْرُوفِ﴾ according to the Sharia, of kind companionship, not causing harm and the like; ﴿وَلِلرِّجَالِ عَلَيْهِنَّ دَرَجَةٌ﴾ a precedence in right, in the obligation of their obeying them, because of the dowry and maintenance they have provided. ﴿وَاللَّهُ عَزِيزٌ﴾ in His dominion, ﴿حَكِيمٌ﴾ in what He has arranged for His creation.
[Translator's note: «وَفِي غَيْرِ الْآيِسَةِ وَالصَّغِيرَةِ فَعِدَّتُهُنَّ ثَلَاثَةُ أَشْهُرٍ» is translated as written; the sense is that the three-qarʾ rule excludes these two, whose ʿidda is three months.]

celaleyn:229-229.t: ﴿الطَّلَاقُ﴾ i.e. the divorcing after which one may take back ﴿مَرَّتَانِ﴾ i.e. two; ﴿فَإِمْسَاكٌ﴾ i.e. then upon you is retaining them after it by taking them back ﴿بِمَعْرُوفٍ﴾ without causing harm, ﴿أَوْ تَسْرِيحٌ﴾ i.e. releasing them ﴿بِإِحْسَانٍ وَلَا يَحِلُّ لَكُمْ﴾ O husbands ﴿أَنْ تَأْخُذُوا مِمَّا آتَيْتُمُوهُنَّ﴾ of the dowries ﴿شَيْئًا﴾ when you divorce them, ﴿إِلَّا أَنْ يَخَافَا﴾ i.e. the two spouses, ﴿أَلَّا يُقِيمَا حُدُودَ اللَّهِ﴾ i.e. not fulfil the rights He has set for them. In one reading [يُخَافَا] in the passive, so «أَلَّا يُقِيمَا» is a badal ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion) from the pronoun in it; and it has been read with the upper-dotted letter [tāʾ] in the two verbs. ﴿فَإِنْ خِفْتُمْ أَلَّا يُقِيمَا حُدُودَ اللَّهِ فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْهِمَا فِيمَا افْتَدَتْ بِهِ﴾ herself, of wealth, so that he divorces her; i.e. there is no blame on the husband in taking it nor on the wife in giving it. ﴿تِلْكَ﴾ the stated rulings ﴿حُدُودُ اللَّهِ فَلَا تَعْتَدُوهَا وَمَنْ يَتَعَدَّ حُدُودَ اللَّهِ فَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الظَّالِمُونَ﴾

celaleyn:230-230.t: ﴿فَإِنْ طَلَّقَهَا﴾ the husband, after the two, ﴿فَلَا تَحِلُّ لَهُ مِنْ بَعْدُ﴾ i.e. after the third divorce, ﴿حَتَّى تَنْكِحَ﴾ marries ﴿زَوْجًا غَيْرَهُ﴾ and he has intercourse with her, as in the hadith narrated by the two Shaykhs [al-Bukhārī and Muslim]. ﴿فَإِنْ طَلَّقَهَا﴾ i.e. the second husband, ﴿فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْهِمَا﴾ i.e. the wife and the first husband ﴿أَنْ يَتَرَاجَعَا﴾ to marriage after the end of the ʿidda, ﴿إِنْ ظَنَّا أَنْ يُقِيمَا حُدُودَ اللَّهِ وَتِلْكَ﴾ the things mentioned ﴿حُدُودُ اللَّهِ يُبَيِّنُهَا لِقَوْمٍ يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ reflect.

celaleyn:231-231.t: ﴿وَإِذَا طَلَّقْتُمُ النِّسَاءَ فَبَلَغْنَ أَجَلَهُنَّ﴾ are close to the end of their ʿidda, ﴿فَأَمْسِكُوهُنَّ﴾ by taking them back ﴿بِمَعْرُوفٍ﴾ without harm, ﴿أَوْ سَرِّحُوهُنَّ بِمَعْرُوفٍ﴾ leave them until their ʿidda ends; ﴿وَلَا تُمْسِكُوهُنَّ﴾ by taking back ﴿ضِرَارًا﴾ a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose) ﴿لِتَعْتَدُوا﴾ against them by forcing them to ransom themselves and be divorced, and by prolonging the confinement. ﴿وَمَنْ يَفْعَلْ ذَلِكَ فَقَدْ ظَلَمَ نَفْسَهُ﴾ by exposing it to the punishment of Allah. ﴿وَلَا تَتَّخِذُوا آيَاتِ اللَّهِ هُزُوًا﴾ an object of mockery, by contravening them; ﴿وَاذْكُرُوا نِعْمَتَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ through Islam ﴿وَمَا أَنْزَلَ عَلَيْكُمْ مِنَ الْكِتَابِ﴾ the Quran ﴿وَالْحِكْمَةِ﴾ the rulings in it, ﴿يَعِظُكُمْ بِهِ﴾ that you should give thanks for it by acting on it; ﴿وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ﴾ and nothing is hidden from Him.

celaleyn:232-232.t: ﴿وَإِذَا طَلَّقْتُمُ النِّسَاءَ فَبَلَغْنَ أَجَلَهُنَّ﴾ their ʿidda has ended, ﴿فَلَا تَعْضُلُوهُنَّ﴾ an address to the guardians, i.e. do not prevent them from ﴿أَنْ يَنْكِحْنَ أَزْوَاجَهُنَّ﴾ who divorced them — because the occasion of its revelation was that the sister of Maʿqil ibn Yasār was divorced by her husband, and he wanted to take her back, but Maʿqil ibn Yasār prevented her, as al-Ḥākim narrated — ﴿إِذَا تَرَاضَوْا﴾ i.e. the husbands and the women ﴿بَيْنَهُمْ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ﴾ according to the Sharia. ﴿ذَلِكَ﴾ the prohibition of preventing ﴿يُوعَظُ بِهِ مَنْ كَانَ مِنْكُمْ يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ﴾ because he is the one who benefits from it. ﴿ذَلِكُمْ﴾ i.e. abstaining from preventing ﴿أَزْكَى﴾ better ﴿لَكُمْ وَأَطْهَرُ﴾ for you and for them, because of the suspicion feared for the two spouses on account of the attachment between them. ﴿وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ﴾ what contains benefit ﴿وَأَنْتُمْ لَا تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ that; so follow His command.

celaleyn:233-233.t: ﴿وَالْوَالِدَاتُ يُرْضِعْنَ﴾ i.e. let them suckle ﴿أَوْلَادَهُنَّ حَوْلَيْنِ﴾ two years ﴿كَامِلَيْنِ﴾ an emphasizing adjective (ṣifa muʾakkida); that is ﴿لِمَنْ أَرَادَ أَنْ يُتِمَّ الرَّضَاعَةَ﴾ and there is nothing beyond it. ﴿وَعَلَى الْمَوْلُودِ لَهُ﴾ i.e. the father ﴿رِزْقُهُنَّ﴾ feeding the mothers ﴿وَكِسْوَتُهُنَّ﴾ for the suckling, when they are divorced, ﴿بِالْمَعْرُوفِ﴾ according to his means. ﴿لَا تُكَلَّفُ نَفْسٌ إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا﴾ its capacity. ﴿لَا تُضَارَّ وَالِدَةٌ بِوَلَدِهَا﴾ i.e. because of it, by being forced to suckle it if she refuses, ﴿وَلَا﴾ is harmed ﴿مَوْلُودٌ لَهُ بِوَلَدِهِ﴾ i.e. because of it, by being burdened beyond his means. Attaching the child to each of them in the two places is to arouse compassion. ﴿وَعَلَى الْوَارِثِ﴾ i.e. the father's heir, who is the child, i.e. [it is] upon his guardian, from his wealth, ﴿مِثْلُ ذَلِكَ﴾ which is upon the father for the mother, of provision and clothing. ﴿فَإِنْ أَرَادَا﴾ i.e. the parents ﴿فِصَالًا﴾ weaning him before the two years, issuing ﴿عَنْ تَرَاضٍ﴾ agreement ﴿مِنْهُمَا وَتَشَاوُرٍ﴾ between them, so that the child's benefit in it becomes clear, ﴿فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْهِمَا﴾ in that. ﴿وَإِنْ أَرَدْتُمْ﴾ an address to the fathers ﴿أَنْ تَسْتَرْضِعُوا أَوْلَادَكُمْ﴾ wet-nurses other than the mothers, ﴿فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ in it ﴿إِذَا سَلَّمْتُمْ﴾ to them ﴿مَا آتَيْتُمْ﴾ i.e. what you intended to give them of the wage ﴿بِالْمَعْرُوفِ﴾ graciously, such as with a willing heart. ﴿وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ﴾ nothing of it is hidden from Him.

celaleyn:234-234.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ يُتَوَفَّوْنَ﴾ die ﴿مِنْكُمْ وَيَذَرُونَ﴾ leave ﴿أَزْوَاجًا يَتَرَبَّصْنَ﴾ i.e. let them wait ﴿بِأَنْفُسِهِنَّ﴾ after them, from marriage, ﴿أَرْبَعَةَ أَشْهُرٍ وَعَشْرًا﴾ nights. This is for those not pregnant; as for the pregnant, their ʿidda is that they deliver their burden, by the verse of al-Ṭalāq; and the slave woman has half of that, by the Sunna. ﴿فَإِذَا بَلَغْنَ أَجَلَهُنَّ﴾ the period of their waiting has ended, ﴿فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ O guardians ﴿فِيمَا فَعَلْنَ فِي أَنْفُسِهِنَّ﴾ of adorning themselves and presenting themselves to suitors ﴿بِالْمَعْرُوفِ﴾ according to the Sharia. ﴿وَاللَّهُ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرٌ﴾ knowing its inward as its outward.

celaleyn:235-235.t: ﴿وَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكُمْ فِيمَا عَرَّضْتُمْ﴾ hinted ﴿بِهِ مِنْ خِطْبَةِ النِّسَاءِ﴾ whose husbands have died, during the ʿidda, such as a man's saying, for example, "You are indeed beautiful," "Who could find one like you?" and "Many a one desires you," ﴿أَوْ أَكْنَنْتُمْ﴾ concealed ﴿فِي أَنْفُسِكُمْ﴾ of the intention to marry them. ﴿عَلِمَ اللَّهُ أَنَّكُمْ سَتَذْكُرُونَهُنَّ﴾ with proposals, and will not be patient about them, so He has permitted you to hint. ﴿وَلَكِنْ لَا تُوَاعِدُوهُنَّ سِرًّا﴾ i.e. marriage, ﴿إِلَّا﴾ but ﴿أَنْ تَقُولُوا قَوْلًا مَعْرُوفًا﴾ i.e. what is recognized by the Sharia, of hinting; that is permitted you. ﴿وَلَا تَعْزِمُوا عُقْدَةَ النِّكَاحِ﴾ i.e. upon contracting it ﴿حَتَّى يَبْلُغَ الْكِتَابُ﴾ i.e. what is prescribed of the ʿidda ﴿أَجَلَهُ﴾ by its ending. ﴿وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ يَعْلَمُ مَا فِي أَنْفُسِكُمْ﴾ of resolve and other things, ﴿فَاحْذَرُوهُ﴾ lest He punish you if you resolve; ﴿وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ﴾ to one who is wary of Him, ﴿حَلِيمٌ﴾ in delaying punishment from the one who deserves it.

celaleyn:236-236.t: ﴿لَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكُمْ إِنْ طَلَّقْتُمُ النِّسَاءَ مَا لَمْ تَمَسُّوهُنَّ﴾ — in one reading [تُمَاسُّوهُنَّ] — i.e. have intercourse with them, ﴿أَوْ﴾ have not ﴿تَفْرِضُوا لَهُنَّ فَرِيضَةً﴾ a dowry. «مَا» is maṣdariyya ẓarfiyya (temporal-verbal); i.e. there is no consequence upon you in divorcing at a time of no touching and no fixing [of dowry], whether sin or dowry; so divorce them ﴿وَمَتِّعُوهُنَّ﴾ give them something to enjoy, ﴿عَلَى الْمُوسِعِ﴾ the rich among you ﴿قَدَرُهُ وَعَلَى الْمُقْتِرِ﴾ the one of straitened provision ﴿قَدَرُهُ﴾ — this conveys that no regard is given to the wife's standing — ﴿مَتَاعًا﴾ a provision ﴿بِالْمَعْرُوفِ﴾ according to the Sharia; an adjective (ṣifa) of «مَتَاعًا»; ﴿حَقًّا﴾ a second adjective, or an emphasizing maṣdar (verbal noun), ﴿عَلَى الْمُحْسِنِينَ﴾ the obedient.

celaleyn:125-125.t: ﴿وَإِذْ جَعَلْنَا الْبَيْتَ﴾ the Kaaba ﴿مَثَابَةً لِلنَّاسِ﴾ a place of return to which they come back from every side ﴿وَأَمْنًا﴾ a place of safety for them from the oppression and raids that occur elsewhere; a man would meet his father's killer there and not provoke him ﴿وَاتَّخِذُوا﴾ O people ﴿مِنْ مَقَامِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ﴾ it is the stone on which he stood while building the House ﴿مُصَلًّى﴾ a place of prayer, by praying behind it the two rakʿas of ṭawāf (circumambulation). In one reading with fatḥa on the khāʾ [i.e. وَاتَّخَذُوا], as a declarative statement ﴿وَعَهِدْنَا إِلَى إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَإِسْمَاعِيلَ﴾ We commanded them ﴿أَنْ﴾ i.e. بِأَنْ ("to") ﴿طَهِّرَا بَيْتِيَ﴾ of idols ﴿لِلطَّائِفِينَ وَالْعَاكِفِينَ﴾ those who stay in it ﴿وَالرُّكَّعِ السُّجُودِ﴾ plural of rākiʿ and sājid: those who pray.

celaleyn:126-126.t: ﴿وَإِذْ قَالَ إِبْرَاهِيمُ رَبِّ اجْعَلْ هَذَا﴾ place ﴿بَلَدًا آمِنًا﴾ possessing safety. Allah answered his supplication and made it a sanctuary (ḥaram) in which no human blood is shed, no one is wronged, its game is not hunted and its fresh herbage is not cut ﴿وَارْزُقْ أَهْلَهُ مِنَ الثَّمَرَاتِ﴾ and this was done by moving al-Ṭāʾif from Syria to it, when it had been barren, with no crops and no water ﴿مَنْ آمَنَ مِنْهُمْ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ﴾ a badal (substitute) from أَهْلَهُ; he singled them out in the supplication in keeping with His words "لَا يَنَالُ عَهْدِي الظَّالِمِينَ" ﴿قَالَ﴾ the Exalted ﴿وَ﴾ I will provide for ﴿مَنْ كَفَرَ فَأُمَتِّعُهُ﴾ with doubling and without, in this world with provision ﴿قَلِيلًا﴾ for the span of his life ﴿ثُمَّ أَضْطَرُّهُ﴾ I will force him, in the Hereafter ﴿إِلَى عَذَابِ النَّارِ﴾ and he will find no escape from it ﴿وَبِئْسَ الْمَصِيرُ﴾ the place of return, it is.

celaleyn:127-127.t: ﴿وَ﴾ remember ﴿إِذْ يَرْفَعُ إِبْرَاهِيمُ الْقَوَاعِدَ﴾ the foundations, or the walls ﴿مِنَ الْبَيْتِ﴾ building it; attached (mutaʿalliq) to يَرْفَعُ ﴿وَإِسْمَاعِيلُ﴾ conjoined to إِبْرَاهِيمُ, both saying: ﴿رَبَّنَا تَقَبَّلْ مِنَّا﴾ our building ﴿إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ السَّمِيعُ﴾ of speech ﴿الْعَلِيمُ﴾ of action.

celaleyn:128-128.t: ﴿رَبَّنَا وَاجْعَلْنَا مُسْلِمَيْنِ﴾ submissive ﴿لَكَ وَ﴾ make ﴿مِنْ ذُرِّيَّتِنَا﴾ our children ﴿أُمَّةً﴾ a community ﴿مُسْلِمَةً لَكَ﴾ مِنْ is partitive (li-l-tabʿīḍ), and he used it because of His earlier saying to him "لَا يَنَالُ عَهْدِي الظَّالِمِينَ" ﴿وَأَرِنَا﴾ teach us ﴿مَنَاسِكَنَا﴾ the laws of our worship, or of our Ḥajj ﴿وَتُبْ عَلَيْنَا إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ التَّوَّابُ الرَّحِيمُ﴾ They asked Him for repentance despite their being protected from sin, out of humility and to teach their descendants.

celaleyn:129-129.t: ﴿رَبَّنَا وَابْعَثْ فِيهِمْ﴾ i.e. the people of the House ﴿رَسُولًا مِنْهُمْ﴾ from among themselves; and Allah answered his supplication with Muhammad ﷺ ﴿يَتْلُوا عَلَيْهِمْ آيَاتِكَ﴾ the Quran ﴿وَيُعَلِّمُهُمُ الْكِتَابَ﴾ the Quran ﴿وَالْحِكْمَةَ﴾ i.e. the rulings it contains ﴿وَيُزَكِّيهِمْ﴾ purify them of shirk ﴿إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ الْعَزِيزُ﴾ the Overpowering ﴿الْحَكِيمُ﴾ in His making.

celaleyn:130-130.t: ﴿وَمَنْ﴾ i.e. none ﴿يَرْغَبُ عَنْ مِلَّةِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ﴾ and so abandons it ﴿إِلَّا مَنْ سَفِهَ نَفْسَهُ﴾ is ignorant that it is created by Allah and must worship Him, or holds it cheap and debases it ﴿وَلَقَدِ اصْطَفَيْنَاهُ﴾ We chose him ﴿فِي الدُّنْيَا﴾ for messengership and close friendship (khulla) ﴿وَإِنَّهُ فِي الْآخِرَةِ لَمِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ﴾ who have the highest ranks. And remember:

celaleyn:131-131.t: ﴿إِذْ قَالَ لَهُ رَبُّهُ أَسْلِمْ﴾ submit to Allah and make your religion sincerely His ﴿قَالَ أَسْلَمْتُ لِرَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ﴾

celaleyn:132-132.t: ﴿وَوَصَّى﴾ in one reading [أَوْصَى] ﴿بِهَا﴾ the religion (milla) ﴿إِبْرَاهِيمُ بَنِيهِ وَيَعْقُوبُ﴾ his sons; he said: ﴿يَا بَنِيَّ إِنَّ اللَّهَ اصْطَفَى لَكُمُ الدِّينَ﴾ the religion of Islam ﴿فَلَا تَمُوتُنَّ إِلَّا وَأَنْتُمْ مُسْلِمُونَ﴾ a prohibition against abandoning Islam and a command to hold firm to it until death comes. When the Jews said to the Prophet, "Do you not know that Jacob, on the day he died, enjoined Judaism upon his sons?", the following was revealed:

celaleyn:133-133.t: ﴿أَمْ كُنْتُمْ شُهَدَاءَ﴾ present ﴿إِذْ حَضَرَ يَعْقُوبَ الْمَوْتُ إِذْ﴾ a badal (substitute) from the إِذْ before it ﴿قَالَ لِبَنِيهِ مَا تَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ بَعْدِي﴾ after my death ﴿قَالُوا نَعْبُدُ إِلَهَكَ وَإِلَهَ آبَائِكَ إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَإِسْمَاعِيلَ وَإِسْحَاقَ﴾ Ishmael is counted among the fathers by taghlīb (giving precedence to the majority), and because a paternal uncle has the standing of a father ﴿إِلَهًا وَاحِدًا﴾ a badal from إِلَهَكَ ﴿وَنَحْنُ لَهُ مُسْلِمُونَ﴾ أَمْ has the sense of the hamza of disapproval (inkār), i.e. you were not present at the time of his death, so how can you attribute to him what does not befit him?

celaleyn:134-134.t: ﴿تِلْكَ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject); it points to Abraham, Jacob and their sons, and is feminine because its khabar (predicate) is feminine ﴿أُمَّةٌ قَدْ خَلَتْ﴾ has passed ﴿لَهَا مَا كَسَبَتْ﴾ of deeds, i.e. its recompense; a resumptive clause (istiʾnāf) ﴿وَلَكُمْ﴾ the address is to the Jews ﴿مَا كَسَبْتُمْ وَلَا تُسْأَلُونَ عَمَّا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ﴾ just as they will not be asked about your deeds; the clause is an emphasis (taʾkīd) of what precedes it.

celaleyn:135-135.t: ﴿وَقَالُوا كُونُوا هُودًا أَوْ نَصَارَى تَهْتَدُوا﴾ أَوْ is for distribution (tafṣīl): the speakers of the first are the Jews of Medina and of the second the Christians of Najrān ﴿قُلْ﴾ to them ﴿بَلْ﴾ we follow ﴿مِلَّةَ إِبْرَاهِيمَ حَنِيفًا﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial) from إِبْرَاهِيمَ: inclining away from all religions to the upright religion ﴿وَمَا كَانَ مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ﴾

celaleyn:136-136.t: ﴿قُولُوا﴾ an address to the believers ﴿آمَنَّا بِاللَّهِ وَمَا أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْنَا﴾ of the Quran ﴿وَمَا أُنْزِلَ إِلَى إِبْرَاهِيمَ﴾ of the ten scrolls ﴿وَإِسْمَاعِيلَ وَإِسْحَاقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ وَالْأَسْبَاطِ﴾ his children ﴿وَمَا أُوتِيَ مُوسَى﴾ of the Torah ﴿وَعِيسَى﴾ of the Gospel ﴿وَمَا أُوتِيَ النَّبِيُّونَ مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ﴾ of scriptures and signs ﴿لَا نُفَرِّقُ بَيْنَ أَحَدٍ مِنْهُمْ﴾ believing in some and disbelieving in others, like the Jews and the Christians ﴿وَنَحْنُ لَهُ مُسْلِمُونَ﴾

celaleyn:137-137.t: ﴿فَإِنْ آمَنُوا﴾ i.e. the Jews and the Christians ﴿بِمِثْلِ﴾ مِثْلِ is zāʾida (redundant) ﴿مَا آمَنْتُمْ بِهِ فَقَدِ اهْتَدَوْا وَإِنْ تَوَلَّوْا﴾ from believing in it ﴿فَإِنَّمَا هُمْ فِي شِقَاقٍ﴾ in opposition to you ﴿فَسَيَكْفِيكَهُمُ اللَّهُ﴾ O Muhammad, their opposition ﴿وَهُوَ السَّمِيعُ﴾ of their words ﴿الْعَلِيمُ﴾ of their states. And He did suffice him against them, through the killing of Qurayẓa, the banishment of al-Naḍīr and the imposition of the jizya on them.

celaleyn:138-138.t: ﴿صِبْغَةَ اللَّهِ﴾ a maṣdar (verbal noun) emphasising آمَنَّا, accusative through an implied (muqaddar) verb, i.e. "Allah has dyed us". What is meant by it is His religion upon which He created people, because its mark shows on the one who holds it, like dye on a garment ﴿وَمَنْ﴾ i.e. no one ﴿أَحْسَنُ مِنَ اللَّهِ صِبْغَةً﴾ a tamyīz (specification) ﴿وَنَحْنُ لَهُ عَابِدُونَ﴾ The Jews said to the Muslims: "We are the people of the first scripture, our qibla is older, and the prophets were not from the Arabs; had Muhammad been a prophet, he would have been from us." So the following was revealed:

celaleyn:139-139.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾ to them ﴿أَتُحَاجُّونَنَا﴾ do you dispute with us ﴿فِي اللَّهِ﴾ that He chose a prophet from the Arabs ﴿وَهُوَ رَبُّنَا وَرَبُّكُمْ﴾ so it is His right to choose whomever He wills of His servants ﴿وَلَنَا أَعْمَالُنَا﴾ for which we are requited ﴿وَلَكُمْ أَعْمَالُكُمْ﴾ for which you are requited; so it is not unlikely that among our deeds there is something by which we deserve to be honoured ﴿وَنَحْنُ لَهُ مُخْلِصُونَ﴾ in religion and deeds, unlike you; so we are more entitled to be chosen. The hamza is for disapproval (inkār), and the three clauses are aḥwāl (circumstantial clauses).

celaleyn:140-140.t: ﴿أَمْ﴾ rather, do ﴿تَقُولُونَ﴾ with tāʾ, and with yāʾ [يَقُولُونَ] ﴿إِنَّ إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَإِسْمَاعِيلَ وَإِسْحَاقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ وَالْأَسْبَاطَ كَانُوا هُودًا أَوْ نَصَارَى قُلْ﴾ to them ﴿أَأَنْتُمْ أَعْلَمُ أَمِ اللَّهُ﴾ i.e. Allah knows better; and He has declared Abraham free of both by His words "مَا كَانَ إِبْرَاهِيمُ يَهُودِيًّا وَلَا نَصْرَانِيًّا", and those mentioned with him follow him ﴿وَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ مِمَّنْ كَتَمَ﴾ hid from people ﴿شَهَادَةً عِنْدَهُ﴾ that is ﴿مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾ i.e. no one is more unjust than he. They are the Jews: they concealed Allah's testimony in the Torah to Abraham's ḥanīf faith ﴿وَمَا اللَّهُ بِغَافِلٍ عَمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ a threat to them.

celaleyn:141-141.t: ﴿تِلْكَ أُمَّةٌ قَدْ خَلَتْ لَهَا مَا كَسَبَتْ وَلَكُمْ مَا كَسَبْتُمْ وَلَا تُسْأَلُونَ عَمَّا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ﴾ the like of it has preceded.

celaleyn:142-142.t: ﴿سَيَقُولُ السُّفَهَاءُ﴾ the ignorant ﴿مِنَ النَّاسِ﴾ the Jews and the idolaters ﴿مَا وَلَّاهُمْ﴾ what turned the Prophet ﷺ and the believers ﴿عَنْ قِبْلَتِهِمُ الَّتِي كَانُوا عَلَيْهَا﴾ facing it in prayer, namely Jerusalem (Bayt al-Maqdis). Using the sīn, which indicates the future, is part of informing about the unseen. ﴿قُلْ لِلَّهِ الْمَشْرِقُ وَالْمَغْرِبُ﴾ i.e. all directions; so He commands turning to whichever direction He wills, and there is no objecting to Him ﴿يَهْدِي مَنْ يَشَاءُ﴾ to guide ﴿إِلَى صِرَاطٍ﴾ a path ﴿مُسْتَقِيمٍ﴾ the religion of Islam; i.e. and among them are you. And among them … [Translator's note: the text reads «وَمِنْهُمْ أَنْتُمْ وَمِنْهُمْ دَلَّ عَلَى هَذَا»; the second «وَمِنْهُمْ» appears superfluous. The sense is: "and among them are you", which is indicated by what follows (ayah 143).]

celaleyn:237-237.t: ﴿وَإِنْ طَلَّقْتُمُوهُنَّ مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ تَمَسُّوهُنَّ وَقَدْ فَرَضْتُمْ لَهُنَّ فَرِيضَةً فَنِصْفُ مَا فَرَضْتُمْ﴾ is due to them, and the [other] half returns to you, ﴿إِلَّا﴾ but ﴿أَنْ يَعْفُونَ﴾ i.e. the wives, and they forgo it, ﴿أَوْ يَعْفُوَ الَّذِي بِيَدِهِ عُقْدَةُ النِّكَاحِ﴾ — and he is the husband — and he leaves her the whole. From Ibn ʿAbbās: [it is] the guardian, if she is under legal restriction (maḥjūra); and there is no blame in that. ﴿وَأَنْ تَعْفُوا﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is ﴿أَقْرَبُ لِلتَّقْوَى وَلَا تَنْسَوُا الْفَضْلَ بَيْنَكُمْ﴾ i.e. that some of you be generous to others. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ﴾ and He will recompense you for it.

celaleyn:238-238.t: ﴿حَافِظُوا عَلَى الصَّلَوَاتِ﴾ the five, by performing them in their times, ﴿وَالصَّلَوةِ الْوُسْطَى﴾ it is ʿaṣr, or ṣubḥ, or ẓuhr, or another — [several] views; He singled it out for mention because of its excellence. ﴿وَقُومُوا لِلَّهِ﴾ in the prayer ﴿قَانِتِينَ﴾ it is said: obedient, because of his ﷺ saying, "Every qunūt in the Quran is obedience," narrated by Aḥmad and others; and it is said: silent, because of the hadith of Zayd ibn Arqam: "We used to talk in the prayer until it was revealed, and we were commanded to be silent and forbidden to speak," narrated by the two Shaykhs [al-Bukhārī and Muslim].

celaleyn:239-239.t: ﴿فَإِنْ خِفْتُمْ﴾ from an enemy, a flood or a wild beast, ﴿فَرِجَالًا﴾ plural of rājil, i.e. pray on foot, ﴿أَوْ رُكْبَانًا﴾ plural of rākib, i.e. however possible, facing the qibla or otherwise, and indicate the bowing and prostration by gestures. ﴿فَإِذَا أَمِنْتُمْ﴾ from fear, ﴿فَاذْكُرُوا اللَّهَ﴾ i.e. pray ﴿كَمَا عَلَّمَكُمْ مَا لَمْ تَكُونُوا تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ before His teaching, of its obligations and its due rights. The kāf is in the sense of "like" (mithl), and «مَا» is maṣdariyya or a relative noun.

celaleyn:240-240.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ يُتَوَفَّوْنَ مِنْكُمْ وَيَذَرُونَ أَزْوَاجًا﴾ let them bequeath ﴿وَصِيَّةً﴾ — in one reading nominative, i.e. "[is] upon them" — ﴿لِأَزْوَاجِهِمْ﴾ and let them give them ﴿مَتَاعًا﴾ what they may enjoy, of maintenance and clothing, ﴿إِلَى﴾ the completion of ﴿الْحَوْلِ﴾ from their death, which they were obliged to wait out, ﴿غَيْرَ إِخْرَاجٍ﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. not being expelled from their dwelling. ﴿فَإِنْ خَرَجْنَ﴾ of their own accord, ﴿فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ O guardians of the deceased, ﴿فِي مَا فَعَلْنَ فِي أَنْفُسِهِنَّ مِنْ مَعْرُوفٍ﴾ according to the Sharia, such as adorning herself, abandoning mourning (iḥdād), and [your] cutting off maintenance from her. ﴿وَاللَّهُ عَزِيزٌ﴾ in His dominion, ﴿حَكِيمٌ﴾ in His making. The bequest mentioned is abrogated by the verse of inheritance, and the year's waiting by the verse {أَرْبَعَةَ أَشْهُرٍ وَعَشْرًا}, which precedes [in the text] but is later in revelation; and lodging remains established for her according to al-Shāfiʿī, may Allah have mercy on him.

celaleyn:241-241.t: ﴿وَلِلْمُطَلَّقَاتِ مَتَاعٌ﴾ which they are given ﴿بِالْمَعْرُوفِ﴾ according to what is possible, ﴿حَقًّا﴾ accusative by its implied (muqaddar) verb, ﴿عَلَى الْمُتَّقِينَ﴾ [of] Allah the Exalted. He repeated it so that it covers the woman with whom the marriage was consummated as well, since the preceding verse is about other than her.

celaleyn:242-242.t: ﴿كَذَلِكَ﴾ just as He makes clear to you what has been mentioned, ﴿يُبَيِّنُ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ آيَاتِهِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَعْقِلُونَ﴾ reflect.

celaleyn:243-243.t: ﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ﴾ an interrogative of wonder and of arousing eagerness to hear what follows it, i.e. has your knowledge not reached ﴿إِلَى الَّذِينَ خَرَجُوا مِنْ دِيَارِهِمْ وَهُمْ أُلُوفٌ﴾ four, or eight, or ten, or thirty, or forty, or seventy thousand, ﴿حَذَرَ الْمَوْتِ﴾ a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose)? They were a people of the Children of Israel; the plague struck their land and they fled. ﴿فَقَالَ لَهُمُ اللَّهُ مُوتُوا﴾ and they died; ﴿ثُمَّ أَحْيَاهُمْ﴾ after eight days or more, through the supplication of their prophet Ḥizqīl — with kasra on the unpointed [ḥāʾ] and on the qāf, and sukūn on the zāy — and they lived for a long time with the trace of death upon them; they would not put on a garment but it became like a shroud, and this continued among their descendants. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَذُو فَضْلٍ عَلَى النَّاسِ﴾ and part of it is reviving these, ﴿وَلَكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ﴾ — and they are the disbelievers — ﴿لَا يَشْكُرُونَ﴾. The purpose of mentioning the account of these is to encourage the believers to fight; and for that reason there is conjoined to it:

celaleyn:244-244.t: ﴿وَقَاتِلُوا فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ﴾ i.e. to make His religion supreme, ﴿وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ سَمِيعٌ﴾ of your words, ﴿عَلِيمٌ﴾ of your states, and will recompense you.

celaleyn:245-245.t: ﴿مَنْ ذَا الَّذِي يُقْرِضُ اللَّهَ﴾ by spending his wealth in the way of Allah ﴿قَرْضًا حَسَنًا﴾ by spending it for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, with a willing heart, ﴿فَيُضَاعِفَهُ﴾ — in one reading [فَيُضَعِّفَهُ] with doubling — ﴿لَهُ أَضْعَافًا كَثِيرَةً﴾ from ten to more than seven hundred, as will come. ﴿وَاللَّهُ يَقْبِضُ﴾ withholds provision from whom He wills, as a test, ﴿وَيَبْسُطُ﴾ makes it ample for whom He wills, as a trial; ﴿وَإِلَيْهِ تُرْجَعُونَ﴾ in the Hereafter, at the resurrection, and He will recompense you for your deeds.

celaleyn:246-246.t: ﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى الْمَلَإِ﴾ the group ﴿مِنْ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ مِنْ بَعْدِ﴾ the death of ﴿مُوسَى﴾ i.e. to their story and their account, ﴿إِذْ قَالُوا لِنَبِيٍّ لَهُمْ﴾ he is Shamwīl (Samuel), ﴿ابْعَثْ﴾ set up ﴿لَنَا مَلِكًا نُقَاتِلْ﴾ with him ﴿فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ﴾ — by whom our word will be united and to whom we will refer? ﴿قَالَ﴾ the prophet to them: ﴿هَلْ عَسَيْتُمْ﴾ with fatḥa and kasra [on the sīn] ﴿إِنْ كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمُ الْقِتَالُ أَلَّا تُقَاتِلُوا﴾ the khabar (predicate) of «عَسَى»; the interrogative is to affirm the expectation conveyed by it. ﴿قَالُوا وَمَا لَنَا أَلَّا نُقَاتِلَ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ وَقَدْ أُخْرِجْنَا مِنْ دِيَارِنَا وَأَبْنَائِنَا﴾ by their being captured and killed — the people of Jālūt (Goliath) had done that to them — i.e. nothing prevents us from it while what calls for it exists. The Exalted said: ﴿فَلَمَّا كُتِبَ عَلَيْهِمُ الْقِتَالُ تَوَلَّوْا﴾ from it and were cowardly, ﴿إِلَّا قَلِيلًا مِنْهُمْ﴾ — they are the ones who crossed the river with Ṭālūt (Saul), as will come. ﴿وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ بِالظَّالِمِينَ﴾ and will recompense them. The prophet asked his Lord to send a king, and He answered him by sending Ṭālūt.

celaleyn:247-247.t: ﴿وَقَالَ لَهُمْ نَبِيُّهُمْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ قَدْ بَعَثَ لَكُمْ طَالُوتَ مَلِكًا قَالُوا أَنَّى﴾ how ﴿يَكُونُ لَهُ الْمُلْكُ عَلَيْنَا وَنَحْنُ أَحَقُّ بِالْمُلْكِ مِنْهُ﴾ because he was not from the tribe of kingship nor of prophethood, and he was a tanner or a shepherd, ﴿وَلَمْ يُؤْتَ سَعَةً مِنَ الْمَالِ﴾ with which to help himself in establishing the kingship? ﴿قَالَ﴾ the prophet to them: ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ اصْطَفَاهُ﴾ chose him for the kingship ﴿عَلَيْكُمْ وَزَادَهُ بَسْطَةً﴾ amplitude ﴿فِي الْعِلْمِ وَالْجِسْمِ﴾ — he was the most knowledgeable of the Children of Israel at that time, the most handsome of them and the most perfect in form. ﴿وَاللَّهُ يُؤْتِي مُلْكَهُ مَنْ يَشَاءُ﴾ to give it to; there is no objecting to Him. ﴿وَاللَّهُ وَاسِعٌ﴾ in His bounty, ﴿عَلِيمٌ﴾ of who is worthy of it.

celaleyn:248-248.t: ﴿وَقَالَ لَهُمْ نَبِيُّهُمْ﴾ when they asked him for a sign of his kingship: ﴿إِنَّ آيَةَ مُلْكِهِ أَنْ يَأْتِيَكُمُ التَّابُوتُ﴾ the chest, in which were images of the prophets; Allah sent it down to Ādam and it continued down to them; then the Amalekites overpowered them for it and took it. They used to seek victory over their enemy through it, put it in front in battle, and find tranquillity in it, as the Exalted said: ﴿فِيهِ سَكِينَةٌ﴾ reassurance for your hearts ﴿مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ وَبَقِيَّةٌ مِمَّا تَرَكَ آلُ مُوسَى وَآلُ هَارُونَ﴾ i.e. what the two of them left; it is the sandals of Mūsā and his staff, the turban of Hārūn, a qafīz (measure) of the manna that used to come down upon them, and fragments of the Tablets. ﴿تَحْمِلُهُ الْمَلَائِكَةُ﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «يَأْتِيَكُمُ». ﴿إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لَآيَةً لَكُمْ﴾ of his kingship ﴿إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ﴾. So the angels carried it between heaven and earth while they watched it, until they set it down with Ṭālūt; then they acknowledged his kingship and hastened to jihad, and he chose seventy thousand of their young men.

celaleyn:249-249.t: ﴿فَلَمَّا فَصَلَ﴾ went out ﴿طَالُوتُ بِالْجُنُودِ﴾ from Bayt al-Maqdis — it was intensely hot and they asked him for water — ﴿قَالَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ مُبْتَلِيكُمْ﴾ will test you ﴿بِنَهَرٍ﴾ so that the obedient among you and the disobedient become manifest; it is between the Jordan and Palestine. ﴿فَمَنْ شَرِبَ مِنْهُ﴾ i.e. of its water, ﴿فَلَيْسَ مِنِّي﴾ i.e. of my followers, ﴿وَمَنْ لَمْ يَطْعَمْهُ﴾ taste it ﴿فَإِنَّهُ مِنِّي إِلَّا مَنِ اغْتَرَفَ غُرْفَةً﴾ with fatḥa and ḍamma [غَرْفَةً] ﴿بِيَدِهِ﴾ and was content with it and did not exceed it — he is of me. ﴿فَشَرِبُوا مِنْهُ﴾ when they reached it, abundantly, ﴿إِلَّا قَلِيلًا مِنْهُمْ﴾ who confined themselves to the handful. It is narrated that it sufficed them for their drinking and their mounts, and they were three hundred and some ten-odd men. ﴿فَلَمَّا جَاوَزَهُ هُوَ وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مَعَهُ﴾ — and they are those who confined themselves to the handful — ﴿قَالُوا﴾ i.e. those who drank: ﴿لَا طَاقَةَ﴾ strength ﴿لَنَا الْيَوْمَ بِجَالُوتَ وَجُنُودِهِ﴾ i.e. to fight them; and they were cowardly and did not cross it. ﴿قَالَ الَّذِينَ يَظُنُّونَ﴾ are certain ﴿أَنَّهُمْ مُلَاقُوا اللَّهِ﴾ at the resurrection — and they are those who crossed it —: ﴿كَمْ﴾ declarative (khabariyya), in the sense of "many" ﴿مِنْ فِئَةٍ﴾ a group ﴿قَلِيلَةٍ غَلَبَتْ فِئَةً كَثِيرَةً بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ﴾ by His will; ﴿وَاللَّهُ مَعَ الصَّابِرِينَ﴾ with help and victory.

daas-irab:1-5.t:
﴿الم﴾: disjointed letters (ḥurūf muqaṭṭaʿa) with no grammatical position, or a khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "هذه ألم" (this is Alif Lām Mīm). ﴿ذلِكَ﴾: ذا is a demonstrative, indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ; the lām is for distance and the kāf is for address. ﴿الْكِتابُ﴾: a badal (substitute) from the demonstrative, nominative; it may also be parsed as the khabar of the demonstrative. ﴿لا رَيْبَ﴾: لا is the lā of generic negation, working like إنّ. ريب is its noun, indeclinable on fatḥa, in the position of accusative. ﴿فِيهِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, both attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar, its implied form being "حاصل" (existing); the clause لا ريب فيه is a khabar of the demonstrative. ﴿هُدىً﴾: a second khabar of the demonstrative, nominative with an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma.
﴿لِلْمُتَّقِينَ﴾: المتقين is a noun, genitive with the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural; both are attached to هدى. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾: a relative noun, indeclinable on fatḥa, in the position of genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of المتقين. ﴿يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn because it is one of the five verbs; the wāw is an attached pronoun in the position of nominative as fāʿil (agent). ﴿بِالْغَيْبِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, both attached to the verb يؤمنون. The clause ﴿يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَيُقِيمُونَ﴾: its i'rab is like يؤمنون ... and the clause is conjoined to the clause before it. ﴿الصَّلاةَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿وَمِمَّا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction and من is a preposition; ما is a relative noun, indeclinable on sukūn, in the position of genitive by the preposition. ﴿رَزَقْناهُمْ﴾: a past verb, indeclinable on sukūn; نا is the fāʿil, the hāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi, and the mīm is the sign of the masculine plural. The returning pronoun (ʿāʾid) is omitted, and it is the second object; the implied form is "مما رزقناهم إياه" (of what We provided them with it), and the clause is the ṣila of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. ﴿يُنْفِقُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾: maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the relative noun before it. ﴿يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. ﴿بِما﴾: the bāʾ is a preposition; ما is a relative noun in the position of genitive by the preposition. ﴿أُنْزِلَ﴾: a passive past verb; the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "هو" (it), referring back to ما.
﴿إِلَيْكَ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, both attached to the verb أنزل; the clause is the ṣila of the relative noun. ﴿وَما أُنْزِلَ﴾: its i'rab is like the i'rab of the preceding one, and the clause is the ṣila of the relative noun. ﴿مِنْ قَبْلِكَ﴾: both attached to the verb أنزل; the kāf is in the position of genitive by annexation (iḍāfa).
﴿وَبِالْآخِرَةِ﴾: both attached to the verb يوقنون. ﴿هُمْ﴾: a detached nominative pronoun, indeclinable on sukūn, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ; the nominal clause is conjoined to the clause يؤمنون. ﴿يُوقِنُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ هم.
﴿أُولئِكَ﴾: a demonstrative, indeclinable on kasra, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ, and the kāf is for address. ﴿عَلى هُدىً﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, both attached to an omitted khabar; the implied form is "أولئك سائرون على هدى" (those are proceeding upon guidance). ﴿مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ﴾: both attached to an omitted naʿt of هدى, the implied form being "هدى نازل" (guidance sent down); the clause أولئك is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿وَأُولئِكَ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; أولئك is a demonstrative, mubtadaʾ. ﴿هُمُ﴾: a second mubtadaʾ, a detached pronoun. ﴿الْمُفْلِحُونَ﴾: khabar of هم, nominative with the wāw because it is a sound masculine plural; the clause هم المفلحون is the khabar of أولئك.

daas-irab:165-165.t:
﴿وَمِنَ﴾ The wāw is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya). ﴿مِنَ النَّاسِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, both attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate). ﴿مِنَ﴾ a relative noun in the position of the nominative (in the position of rafʿ) as a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject). [Translator's note: the source prints the word as ﴿مِنَ﴾; the relative noun meant here is ﴿مَنْ﴾.] ﴿يَتَّخِذُ﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) being implied as "huwa" (he), referring back to مَن; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun.
﴿مِنْ دُونِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, both attached to يتخذ. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿أَنْداداً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿يُحِبُّونَهُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb; the wāw is the fāʿil and the hāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi; the clause is a ṣifa (adjective) of أندادا. ﴿كَحُبِّ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, both attached to an omitted ṣifa of a maṣdar (verbal noun) functioning as a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. "a great love". ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾ the wāw is resumptive or circumstantial (ḥāliyya); الذين is a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ. ﴿آمَنُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila of the relative noun. ﴿أَشَدُّ﴾ khabar of the relative noun. ﴿حُبًّا﴾ tamyīz (specification). ﴿لِلَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty is genitive (majrūr), and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the maṣdar حبا; the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَلَوْ﴾ the wāw is resumptive; لو is a non-jussive conditional particle. ﴿يَرَى﴾ an imperfect verb.
﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ a relative noun, fāʿil (agent). ﴿ظَلَمُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, and the clause يرى الذين is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿إِذْ﴾ an adverb (ẓarf) for past time, attached to (mutaʿalliq) يرى; it has also been said that it is in the sense of إذا, and so would be an adverb for future time. ﴿يَرَوْنَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil. ﴿الْعَذابَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿أَنَّ﴾ a particle resembling the verb. ﴿الْقُوَّةَ﴾ its noun (ism). ﴿لِلَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty; they are a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted khabar (predicate). ﴿جَمِيعاً﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial); أنّ with its noun and khabar are interpreted as a maṣdar (interpreted maṣdar) standing in place of the two objects of يرى, and the apodosis (jawāb) of لو is omitted, its implied form being "they would have found an astonishing matter". ﴿وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ شَدِيدُ﴾ أنّ, the Name of Majesty is its noun and شديد is its khabar; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa). ﴿الْعَذابَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). [Translator's note: the muḍāf ilayhi here is written ﴿الْعَذابَ﴾ with fatḥa in the source; in the Quranic text it is ﴿الْعَذابِ﴾.]

daas-irab:166-167.t:
﴿إِذْ﴾ an adverb for past time; it is a badal (substitute) from إذ in the preceding verse. ﴿تَبَرَّأَ﴾ a past verb. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ a relative noun, fāʿil; the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation. ﴿اتُّبِعُوا﴾ a passive past verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is the ṣila of the relative noun. ﴿مِنَ الَّذِينَ﴾ both attached to تبرأ. ﴿اتُّبِعُوا﴾ a past verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. [Translator's note: the source prints this second word as ﴿اتُّبِعُوا﴾, but its analysis (active verb with fāʿil) corresponds to the Quranic ﴿اتَّبَعُوا﴾.] ﴿وَرَأَوُا﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); رأوا is a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, with قد implied before it. ﴿الْعَذابَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَتَقَطَّعَتْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; تقطع is a past verb and the tāʾ is for the feminine. ﴿بِهِمُ﴾ both attached to تقطعت. ﴿الْأَسْبابُ﴾ fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَقالَ﴾ a past verb. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ fāʿil. ﴿اتَّبَعُوا﴾ a past verb and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila of the relative noun. ﴿لَوْ﴾ a conditional particle containing the sense of wishing (tamannī). ﴿أَنَّ﴾ a particle resembling the verb. ﴿لَنا﴾ both attached to an omitted khabar of أنّ. ﴿كَرَّةً﴾ its noun; the clause is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the saying). ﴿فَنَتَبَرَّأَ﴾ the fāʾ is causal (al-sababiyya); نتبرأ is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an أن concealed after the fāʾ, and its fāʿil is implied as "نحن" (we). ﴿مِنْهُمْ﴾ both attached to نتبرأ; أن and the verb are interpreted as a maṣdar conjoined to a maṣdar implied from the preceding verb, the implied form being: "we want a return and a disavowal of these". ﴿كَما﴾ the kāf is a preposition; ما is maṣdariyya (infinitival).
﴿تَبَرَّؤُا﴾ a past verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the maṣdariyya ما with the verb is interpreted as a maṣdar in the position of the genitive by the kāf, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ṣifa (adjective) of an omitted accusative maṣdar functioning as a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), its implied form being: "we disavow like their disavowal".
﴿مِنَّا﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, both attached to the verb before them. ﴿كَذلِكَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, both attached to an omitted ṣifa of an omitted maṣdar, a mafʿūl muṭlaq, its implied form being: "Allah shows them a showing like that showing". ﴿يُرِيهِمُ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) with an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the yāʾ because of heaviness, and the hāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi. ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ the Name of Majesty, fāʿil. ﴿أَعْمالَهُمْ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿حَسَراتٍ﴾ ḥāl.
﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, both attached to حسرات; the clause كذلك is resumptive. ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; ما is the Ḥijāzī mā, which operates like ليس. ﴿هُمْ﴾ a detached pronoun, the noun of ما. ﴿بِخارِجِينَ﴾ the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida); خارجين is a noun genitive in form and accusative in position as the khabar of ما. ﴿مِنَ النَّارِ﴾ both attached to خارجين.

daas-irab:234-234.t:
﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾: the wāw is resumptive; الذين is a relative noun, in the position of nominative (marfūʿ) as mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿يُتَوَفَّوْنَ﴾: a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. ﴿مِنْكُمْ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَيَذَرُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is conjoined. ﴿أَزْواجاً﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿يَتَرَبَّصْنَ﴾: an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn, and the nūn of the feminine plural is the fāʿil; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being: "the wives of those who die among you wait"; and this nominal clause is the khabar of الذين. ﴿بِأَنْفُسِهِنَّ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb before them. ﴿أَرْبَعَةَ﴾: an adverb of time, attached to the verb before it. ﴿أَشْهُرٍ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (the genitive term of the construct). ﴿وَعَشْراً﴾: conjoined to أربعة, i.e. ten nights.
﴿فَإِذا﴾: the fāʾ is resumptive; إذا is an adverb of time. ﴿بَلَغْنَ﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿أَجَلَهُنَّ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is resumptive. ﴿فَلا جُناحَ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾: its iʿrāb has been repeated; the clause has no position in iʿrāb, being the answer of a non-jussive conditional. ﴿فِيما﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿فَعَلْنَ﴾: a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn, and the nūn of the feminine plural is the fāʿil. ﴿فِي أَنْفُسِهِنَّ﴾: attached to فعلن.
﴿بِالْمَعْرُوفِ﴾: attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "acting in accordance with what is right (bil-maʿrūf)". ﴿وَاللَّهُ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرٌ﴾: the iʿrāb of its like has already been given in the previous verse.

daas-irab:235-235.t:
﴿وَلا جُناحَ عَلَيْكُمْ فِيما عَرَّضْتُمْ بِهِ﴾: for its i'rab see verse 228. [Translator's note: a similar phrase is parsed in verse 229 («فلا جناح عليهما فيما افتدت به»), not 228; the verse number in the source appears to be wrong.] ﴿مِنْ خِطْبَةِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl. ﴿النِّساءِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (the genitive term of the construct). ﴿أَوْ أَكْنَنْتُمْ﴾: أو is a conjunction; أكننتم is a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿فِي أَنْفُسِكُمْ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to أكننتم; the clause is conjoined. ﴿عَلِمَ اللَّهُ﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿أَنَّكُمْ﴾: anna and its noun. ﴿سَتَذْكُرُونَهُنَّ﴾: the sīn is for the future; تذكروهن is an imperfect verb [Translator's note: so written in the source; تذكرونهن is meant.], its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is in the position of nominative (marfūʿ) as the khabar (predicate) of anna; and anna with what follows it stands in place of the two objects of عَلِمَ. The clause ﴿عَلِمَ اللَّهُ ... ﴾ is causal (taʿlīliyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿وَلكِنْ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; لكن is a particle of rectification (istidrāk). ﴿لا﴾: prohibitive, making the verb jussive. ﴿تُواعِدُوهُنَّ﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil and the hāʾ is the first mafʿūl bihi. ﴿سِرًّا﴾: second mafʿūl bihi; it is also said to be a ḥāl, or accusative by removal of the preposition. ﴿إِلَّا﴾: particle of exception. ﴿أَنْ تَقُولُوا﴾: the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) formed from the maṣdar-particle an and the imperfect verb after it is in the position of accusative (manṣūb) as the excepted. ﴿قَوْلًا﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿مَعْرُوفاً﴾: an adjective (ṣifa). ﴿وَلا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; لا is prohibitive, making the verb jussive. ﴿تَعْزِمُوا﴾: a jussive imperfect verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil. ﴿عُقْدَةَ﴾: accusative by removal of the preposition, its implied form being: "upon (على) the knot".
﴿النِّكاحِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿حَتَّى يَبْلُغَ﴾: the interpreted maṣdar formed from the an latent after حتى and the verb يبلغ is in the position of genitive (majrūr) by the preposition, and the two are attached to تعزموا. ﴿الْكِتابُ﴾: fāʿil. ﴿أَجَلَهُ﴾: mafʿūl bihi.
﴿وَاعْلَمُوا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; اعلموا is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is conjoined. ﴿أَنَّ اللَّهَ﴾: anna, and the Name of Majesty is its noun; and the clause ﴿يَعْلَمُ﴾ is its khabar; and anna with what follows it stands in place of the two objects of اعلموا. ﴿ما﴾: a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi. ﴿فِي أَنْفُسِكُمْ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause). ﴿فَاحْذَرُوهُ﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa. ﴿احذروه﴾: an imperative verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; the clause is the apodosis of an implied condition, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَاعْلَمُوا﴾: an imperative verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil. ﴿أَنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ﴾: anna, the Name of Majesty is its noun, and غفور is its khabar. ﴿حَلِيمٌ﴾: a second khabar. And anna with what follows it stands in place of the two objects of اعلموا. The clause اعلموا is conjoined.

daas-irab:236-236.t:
﴿لا جُناحَ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾: lā, its noun and its khabar (predicate); the clause is resumptive. ﴿إِنْ﴾: a conditional particle that makes the verb jussive. ﴿طَلَّقْتُمُ﴾: a past verb, and the tāʾ is the fāʿil (agent); it is in the position of jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). ﴿النِّساءَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is resumptive. ﴿ما لَمْ تَمَسُّوهُنَّ﴾: ما is the temporal maṣdar-particle; لم makes the verb jussive; تمسوهن is an imperfect verb, jussive by the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; and the maṣdar-particle ما with the verb is interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of genitive by حتى, and the two are attached to the verb before them. [Translator's note: so in the source — there is no حتى in the verse; the intended sense is presumably an implied temporal adverb ("as long as").] ﴿أَوْ﴾: a conjunction. ﴿تَفْرِضُوا﴾: conjoined to تمسوهن.
Some said that أو here means: "unless you assign (إلا an تفرضوا)" ... and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted. ﴿لَهُنَّ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb before them. ﴿فَرِيضَةً﴾: mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَمَتِّعُوهُنَّ﴾: the clause is conjoined to the omitted apodosis. ﴿عَلَى الْمُوسِعِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted fronted khabar. ﴿قَدَرُهُ﴾: a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause or resumptive. ﴿وَعَلَى الْمُقْتِرِ قَدَرُهُ﴾: conjoined.
﴿مَتاعاً﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿بِالْمَعْرُوفِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to متاعا. ﴿حَقًّا﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq of an omitted verb. ﴿عَلَى الْمُحْسِنِينَ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to حقا.

daas-irab:237-237.t:
﴿وَإِنْ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction. ﴿إِنْ﴾: a conditional particle that makes the verb jussive. ﴿طَلَّقْتُمُوهُنَّ﴾: a past verb; the tāʾ is the fāʿil (agent) and the hāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the mīm was given a ḍamma for lengthening (ishbāʿ); it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). ﴿مِنْ قَبْلِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb before them. ﴿أَنْ تَمَسُّوهُنَّ﴾: the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) formed from the verb and the subjunctive-making an is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَقَدْ﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); قد is a particle of verification (taḥqīq). ﴿فَرَضْتُمْ﴾: a verb and its fāʿil. ﴿لَهُنَّ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to فرضتم. ﴿فَرِيضَةً﴾: mafʿūl bihi. ﴿فَنِصْفُ﴾: the fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); نصف is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "then what is due is half", or it is a mubtadaʾ, the implied form being "then upon you is half"; the clause is in the position of jussive (majzūm) as the apodosis.
﴿ما فَرَضْتُمْ﴾: ما is a relative noun in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. ﴿إِلَّا﴾: a particle of restriction or of exception. ﴿إِنْ﴾: a maṣdar-particle that makes the verb subjunctive. [Translator's note: so in the source, written ﴿إِنْ﴾; the verse reads أَنْ.] ﴿يَعْفُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn, and the nūn of the feminine plural is the fāʿil; the interpreted maṣdar is in the position of genitive by a preposition, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), the implied form being: "then half of what you assigned, except in the case of their pardoning". ﴿أَوْ﴾: a conjunction. ﴿يَعْفُوَا﴾: an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) with fatḥa, conjoined. ﴿الَّذِي﴾: a relative noun, fāʿil. ﴿بِيَدِهِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted khabar. ﴿عُقْدَةُ﴾: a postponed mubtadaʾ. ﴿النِّكاحِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is the ṣila of the relative noun. ﴿وَإِنْ﴾: the wāw is resumptive. [Translator's note: so in the source, written ﴿وَإِنْ﴾; the verse reads وَأَنْ.] ﴿أَنْ تَعْفُوا﴾: the interpreted maṣdar formed from the verb and the subjunctive-making an is in the position of nominative (marfūʿ) as mubtadaʾ, its implied form being: "and pardoning ...".
