Abū ʿUbayda said: One says: khawat ʿurūshuhā: its houses.
And al-ʿurūsh are tents, which are the houses of the Bedouin.
Al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ said: The kāf in His words ﴿أوْ كَالَّذِي﴾ is conjoined to the sense of the speech, that is: Have you seen [anyone] like the one who disputed with Ibrāhīm, or like the one who passed by a town?
And it was said: it is redundant (zāʾida), as He said: ﴿لَيْسَ كَمِثْلِهِ شَيءٌ﴾.
* And His words: ﴿لَمْ يَتَسَنَّهْ﴾.
ʿIkrima and Qatāda said: it has not changed.
Mujāhid said: it has not gone putrid.
Some lexicographers said: lam yatasanna is from their saying āsana al-māʾu when water becomes putrid.
Abū ʿAmr al-Shaybānī said: ﴿لَمْ يَتَسَنَّهْ﴾ means it has not changed, from His words ﴿مِنْ حَمَأٍ مَسْنُونٍ﴾; then one of the two nūns was replaced by yāʾ, as is said taqaṣṣaytu and taẓannaytu, and qaṣṣaytu aẓfārī ("I clipped my nails").
Abū Jaʿfar said: Both views are mistaken. Had it been from their saying asina al-māʾu when it becomes putrid, it would be yataʾassan.
Abū Isḥāq said: Nor is it from masnūn, because masnūn means poured out in the shape (sunna) of the ground.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The correct view is that it is from al-sana (year), that is, the years have not changed it.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿وَلِنَجْعَلَكَ آيَةً لِلنَّاسِ﴾.
Sufyān said from al-Aʿmash: He returned to his sons [to find them] old men while he was young.
Al-Kisāʾī said: The speech is only [complete] by implying (iḍmār) a verb.
The meaning according to him is: We did this in order to make you a proof for people and a sign of Our power; and like it is ﴿وَحِفْظَاً﴾.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَٱنْظُرْ إِلَى ٱلعِظَامِ كَيْفَ نُنْشِزُهَا﴾.
That is, We bring them to life. ﴿ونُنْشِزُهَا﴾ with the dotted zāy means: We set some of the bones upon others and raise some of them onto others.
And al-nashz and al-nashaz are raised ground.
And whoever read: ﴿قَالَ: أَعْلَمُ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ﴾ —
Qatāda said, regarding his reading: he began to look at how some of his bones were joined to others, because the first thing of him to be created was his head, and it was said to him: Look; so he said this about that.
Ṭāwūs narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿قَال اعْلَمْ﴾ as an imperative; that is, it was said to him.
Hārūn said: In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd]: ﴿قيل: اعْلَمْ﴾ as an imperative.
And it is also possible that he addressed himself with this.

nahhas-meani:260-260.t:
The words of Him, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَإِذْ قَالَ إِبْرَاهِيمُ رَبِّ أَرِنِي كَيْفَ تُحْيِـي ٱلْمَوْتَىٰ قَالَ أَوَلَمْ تُؤْمِن قَالَ بَلَىٰ وَلَـكِن لِّيَطْمَئِنَّ قَلْبِي﴾.
There are two views on it:
One of them: the meaning is "that my heart may be at rest through witnessing," as though his soul demanded of him to see that, and when he saw it, it was at rest. A person may know a thing from one direction, then seek to know it from another.
This view is the position of the eminent scholars; it is the position of Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḥasan.
Al-Ḥasan said: For the son of Adam, report is not like seeing with one's own eyes.
The other view: the meaning of ﴿وَلَـكِن لِّيَطْمَئِنَّ قَلْبِي﴾ is "[that my heart may be at rest] that when I ask You, You answer me,"
as Sufyān narrated from Qays ibn Muslim, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, who said: ﴿أَوَلَمْ تُؤمِنْ﴾ in the intimate friendship (khulla)? He said: [i.e.] are you not certain of the khulla?
And Abū al-Haytham narrated from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr: ﴿وَلَـكِن لِّيَطْمَئِنَّ قَلْبِي﴾: that it may increase.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿قَالَ فَخُذْ أَرْبَعَةً مِّنَ ٱلطَّيْرِ﴾.
ʿAbd al-Bāqī ibn Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz al-Umawī narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, saying: Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bukayr narrated to us: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Lahīʿa narrated to us from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Hubayra al-Sabīnī, from Ḥanash al-Ṣanʿānī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās, concerning the words of Allah, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فَخُذْ أَرْبَعَةً مِّنَ ٱلطَّيْرِ فَصُرْهُنَّ إِلَيْكَ﴾. He said: They are the pigeon, the peacock, the crane and the cock.
Al-Ḥakam ibn Abān narrated from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said:
"He took the cock, the peacock, the crow and the dove."
Mujāhid said: ﴿فَصُرْهُنَّ﴾ means pluck them, feathers and flesh.
Abū ʿUbayda said: ṣirtu means "I cut," and ṣurtu means "you gathered." [Translator's note: so in the source, «جَمَعْتَ» with the second person.]
And Abū ʿUbayda reported: ṣurtu ʿunuqahu, aṣūruhā, and ṣirtuhā, aṣīruhā: I bent it; and ṣawira [means it became bent].
It is read with ḍamma and with kasra, and most of the readers have ḍamma.
Al-Kisāʾī said: Whoever reads it with ḍamma takes it from ṣurtu al-shayʾa: I inclined it and drew it to myself. He said: and ṣur wajhaka ilayya, that is, turn it toward me.
The meaning on this reading is: draw them to yourself and cut them up; then "and cut them up" was omitted because ﴿ثُمَّ ٱجْعَلْ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ جَبَلٍ مِّنْهُنَّ جُزْءَاً﴾ indicates it.
And whoever read ﴿فَصِرْهُنَّ﴾ with kasra, there are two views about it:
One of them: it has the meaning of the first.
The other: Abū Mālik and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: cut them up.
Abū Ḥātim said: It is from ṣāra when one cuts. He said: In that case it involves fronting and postponement (taqdīm wa-taʾkhīr), as though He said: "Take four birds to yourself and cut them up."
Someone else said: From it a herd of wild cattle is called ṣiwār and ṣuwār, that is, it has broken off and gone apart; and for this reason pieces of musk are called aṣwira, as [the poet] said:
"إِذَا تَقُومُ يضُوغ المِسْكُ أَصْوِرَةً"
(When she rises, the musk wafts forth in pods.)
Abū Jaʿfar said: The most fitting thing said about the meaning of fa-ṣirhunna and fa-ṣurhunna is that they have one meaning, the meaning of cutting, with fronting and postponement, that is: "Take to yourself four birds and cut them up."
And the distinction [between the two] has not been found authentically from any of the early authorities.
﴿ثُمَّ ادْعُهُنَّ﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: "Come, by the permission of Allah!" — so the flesh of this one flew to the flesh of that one. ﴿سَعْيَاً﴾, that is, running on their feet; one does not say of a bird when it flies that it "ran" (saʿā).
﴿وَٱعْلَمْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ﴾, that is, nothing He wills is beyond Him.
﴿حَكِيمٌ﴾ in what He arranges.
Then, having related what contains proofs, He urged jihad, and made known that whoever strives after this proof — which only a prophet brings — has in his striving a great reward.

nahhas-meani:261-261.t:
He the Exalted said: ﴿مَّثَلُ ٱلَّذِينَ يُنْفِقُونَ أَمْوَالَهُمْ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ﴾ up to His words: ﴿وَاسِعٌ عَلِيمٌ﴾.
That is, Generous: what He bestows of His bounty does not diminish His abundance; ﴿عَلِيمٌ﴾ (All-Knowing) of where to place it.

nahhas-meani:264-264.t:
He the Exalted said: ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ لاَ تُبْطِلُواْ صَدَقَاتِكُم بِٱلْمَنِّ وَٱلأَذَىٰ﴾.
That is, do not remind [people] of what you have given and count it [as a favour], as though you intend that; and al-adhā (hurt) is that the recipient is reproached.
So He made known that these two nullify charity, just as the charity of the hypocrite who gives to be seen, to give the impression that he is a believer, is nullified.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿فَمَثَلُهُ﴾, that is, the likeness of his spending, ﴿كَمَثَلِ صَفْوَانٍ﴾, which is the smooth rock; and al-wābil is the rain of heavy drops.
﴿فَتَرَكَهُ صَلْدَاً﴾.
Qatāda said: with nothing on it.
And the meaning is: they had no power over their earnings at the time of their need; it was wiped out and taken away, just as the rain takes away the soil on the rock, finding nothing on the rock to hold it in place.

nahhas-meani:202-202.t:
He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَٱللَّهُ سَرِيعُ ٱلْحِسَابِ﴾.
I.e. He already knows what is in favour of the one being reckoned and what is against him before making him stand for his reckoning; and He reckons with him without needing to recall or deliberate, and the human being is not like that.

nahhas-meani:203-203.t:
He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَٱذْكُرُواْ ٱللَّهَ فِيۤ أَيَّامٍ مَّعْدُودَاتٍ﴾.
I.e. by affirming His oneness and extolling Him; ﴿فِيۤ أَيَّامٍ مَّعْدُودَاتٍ﴾, i.e. counted days.
They were commanded to pronounce the takbīr after the prayers, and at the stoning, with each pebble of the pebbles of the Jamarāt.
Sufyān related from Bukayr ibn ʿAṭāʾ from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Daylī, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The days of Minā are three days, "the days of Tashrīq"; whoever hastens [departure] in two days, there is no sin upon him."
Nāfiʿ related from Ibn ʿUmar: The "known days" and the "counted days" together are four days: the known days are the Day of Sacrifice and two days after it, and the counted days are three days after the Day of Sacrifice: ﴿وَٱذْكُرُواْ ٱللَّهَ فِيۤ أَيَّامٍ مَّعْدُودَاتٍ فَمَن تَعَجَّلَ فِي يَوْمَيْنِ فَلاَ إِثْمَ عَلَيْهِ وَمَن تَأَخَّرَ فَلاۤ إِثْمَ عَلَيْهِ﴾.
It is related from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, Ibn ʿUmar and Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿فَلاَ إِثْمَ عَلَيه﴾: he is forgiven.
ʿAṭāʾ, Ibrāhīm, Mujāhid and Qatāda said: ﴿فَمَن تَعَجَّلَ فِي يَوْمَيْنِ فَلاَ إِثْمَ عَلَيْهِ﴾ in his hastening, ﴿وَمَن تَأَخَّرَ فَلاۤ إِثْمَ عَلَيْهِ﴾ in his delaying.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿لِمَنِ ٱتَّقَىٰ﴾.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar said: This was made permissible for the hastening of whoever is God-fearing.
So the implied sense on this view is: the permission is for whoever is God-fearing.
Ibn Masʿūd said: It is forgiveness of sins for whoever was God-fearing in his ḥajj.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This view is like his first view. As for Ibrāhīm's view — ﴿وَمَن تَأَخَّرَ فَلاۤ إِثْمَ عَلَيْهِ﴾ in his delaying — it is a far-fetched interpretation, because the one who delays has reached the utmost, and one does not say [of him]: there is no blame on him.
And it was said: It is possible to say "there is no blame on him", because it is good to take up Allah's concessions; so Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, made known that there is no sin on him in his not taking up the concessions.
What indicates the soundness of Ibn Masʿūd's view is the ḥadīth of Shuʿba from Manṣūr from Abū Ḥāzim from Abū Hurayra from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Whoever performs ḥajj and does not engage in «رفث» or «فسق» returns as on the day his mother bore him."
The meaning on this view: whoever performs ḥajj and guards in his ḥajj against what diminishes it, there is no sin upon him from past sins.
I.e. the ḥajj has expiated [them] for him.
And the implied sense is: the expiation of sin is for whoever is God-fearing.
Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar al-Anbārī narrated to us, saying: Ḥājib ibn Sulaymān narrated to us, saying: Wakīʿ narrated to us, saying: Sufyān al-Thawrī narrated to us from Sumayy from Abū Ṣāliḥ from Abū Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The accepted ḥajj has no reward but Paradise."
Abū Jaʿfar said: And the saying of Abū al-ʿĀliya: (لا إِثْمَ عَلَيْهِ): his sin has gone entirely if he fears Allah in what remains, i.e. of his life.

nahhas-meani:204-204.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يُعْجِبُكَ قَوْلُهُ فِي ٱلْحَيَاةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: [I.e.] his outward [speech]. ﴿وَيُشِهدُ اللَّهَ﴾ in the dispute that what he wants is the right and that he does not seek wrong; ﴿وَهُوَ أَلَدُّ ٱلْخِصَامِ﴾: a wrongdoer.
Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb said: They are the hypocrites.
Ibn Muḥayṣin read: (وَيُشْهَدُ الَّلهُ) with a fatḥa on the yāʾ and the hāʾ, and the nominative [for the divine name], and its meaning is: and Allah knows.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَهُوَ أَلَدُّ ٱلْخِصَامِ﴾.
Mujāhid said: I.e. a wrongdoer who does not go straight.
Qatāda said: Intensely argumentative with falsehood.
Al-aladd in the language is one fierce in dispute, derived from al-ladīdān, which are the two sides of the neck.
I.e. whichever side of the dispute he takes, he prevails, as the poet said:
إنَّ تَحْتَ الأحْجَارِ حَزْمَاً وَجودَاً * وَخَصِيمَاً ألدَّ ذَا مِعْلاَقِ
(Beneath the stones lie resolve and generosity, and a fierce adversary who clings fast [in argument].)
And it is also related as "مِعْلاق". And it is said: it is from ladīdā al-wādī, i.e. its two sides.
So the possessor of this description takes one side and leaves uprightness; and al-ludūd is in one of the two sides.
Abū Isḥāq said: al-khiṣām is the plural of khaṣm (adversary).

nahhas-meani:205-205.t:
He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَإِذَا تَوَلَّىٰ سَعَىٰ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ لِيُفْسِدَ فِيِهَا وَيُهْلِكَ ٱلْحَرْثَ وَٱلنَّسْلَ﴾.
I.e. when he leaves you, he hastens to the ruin of tillage and offspring.
Abū Mālik related from Ibn ʿAbbās: "It was revealed about al-Akhnas ibn Sharīq. He went out from the Prophet ﷺ and passed by crops belonging to some Muslims, and donkeys; he burned the crops and hamstrung the donkeys."
Abū Isḥāq related from al-Tamīmī from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: «الحرث» is people's tillage, and al-nasl is the offspring of every creature.
Qatāda said: «الحرث» is crops, and al-nasl is the offspring of everything.
Muḥammad ibn Shuʿayb narrated to us, saying: Aḥmad ibn Saʿīd informed me, saying: Wahb ibn Jarīr narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam from al-Ḍaḥḥāk: As for His saying ﴿وَيُهْلِكَ ٱلْحَرْثَ وَٱلنَّسْلَ﴾, [al-nasl] is people and every creature; and as for «الحرث», it is gardens and the growing stock.
Abū Jaʿfar said: These views are close in meaning; and the meaning is: he burns, destroys and kills.

nahhas-meani:206-206.t:
He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُ ٱتَّقِ ٱللَّهَ أَخَذَتْهُ ٱلْعِزَّةُ بِٱلإِثْمِ﴾.
Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar al-Anbārī narrated to us, saying: Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbār narrated to us, saying: Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh narrated to us from Abū Isḥāq from Saʿīd ibn Wahb, who said: ʿAbd Allāh said: "It is sin enough for a man that his brother says to him: Fear Allah, and he says: Mind yourself! Are you commanding me?"

nahhas-meani:207-207.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يَشْرِي نَفْسَهُ ٱبْتِغَآءَ مَرْضَاتِ ٱللَّهِ وَٱللَّهُ﴾.
I.e. he sells; and the meaning of selling himself is: expending himself for Allah.
Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab said: Ṣuhayb came emigrating towards the Prophet ﷺ, and a band of the polytheists of Quraysh pursued him. He dismounted from his mount, scattered what was in his quiver, took his bow, and said: O company of Quraysh, you know that I am among the best archers of you; and by Allah, you will not reach me until I have shot what is in my quiver, then struck with my sword as long as anything of it remains in my hand; then do what you will. They said: Show us your house and your property in Mecca, and we will leave you alone.
They made a pact with him and he did so. When he came to the Prophet ﷺ, he said: "Abū Yaḥyā, the sale has profited, [the sale has profited]." So Allah revealed: ﴿وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يَشْرِي نَفْسَهُ ٱبْتِغَآءَ مَرْضَاتِ ٱللَّهِ وَٱللَّهُ﴾.
Qatāda said: They are the Emigrants and the Helpers.

nahhas-meani:208-208.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ ٱدْخُلُواْ فِي ٱلسِّلْمِ كَآفَّةً﴾.
Mujāhid said: He means Islam.
Abū Mālik related from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: He is saying: [enter] into Islam altogether.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The origin of al-silm is peace and reconciliation. It is possible that the meaning is: remain firm upon Islam; and it is possible that the meaning is [addressed] to whoever has believed with his tongue.
It has been related that some Jews became Muslim and persisted in holding the Sabbath sacred, so Allah commanded them to enter into all the laws of Islam.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَلاَ تَتَّبِعُواْ خُطُوَاتِ ٱلشَّيْطَانِ﴾.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: They are the sins which he commands.
Abū Isḥāq said: I.e. do not follow his tracks, because your abandoning any of the laws of Islam is following Satan.

nahhas-meani:209-209.t:
He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿فَإِن زَلَلْتُمْ مِّن بَعْدِ مَا جَآءَتْكُمُ ٱلْبَيِّنَاتُ﴾.
I.e. you turn aside from the right course.
﴿فَٱعْلَمُوۤاْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ﴾: you cannot frustrate Him and nothing frustrates Him; ﴿حَكِيمٌ﴾ in what He created you upon and laid down for you of His religion.

nahhas-meani:210-210.t:
He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿هَلْ يَنظُرُونَ إِلاَّ أَن يَأْتِيَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ فِي ظُلَلٍ مِّنَ ٱلْغَمَامِ وَٱلْمَلاۤئِكَةُ﴾.
Mujāhid said: Allah will come on the Day of Resurrection in canopies of cloud.
And it was said: ﴿هَلْ يَنظُرُونَ إِلاَّ أَن يَأْتِيَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ﴾ with what He promised them of good deeds [rewarded] and punishment.
﴿فَأَتَاهُمُ اللهُ مِنْ حَيْثُ لَمْ يَحْتَسِبُوا﴾, i.e. by His forsaking them.
This is the view of Abū Isḥāq.
Al-Akhfash Saʿīd said: ﴿أَن يَأْتِيَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ﴾ means His command.
Because Allah the Exalted does not move from place to place; as you say: "We feared that the Banū Umayya would come to us", meaning only their rule.
﴿وَقُضِيَ ٱلأَمْرُ﴾, i.e. what they were promised is finished for them.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَإِلَى ٱللَّهِ تُرْجَعُ ٱلأُمُورُ﴾.
Yet they are returning to Him at every time.
Quṭrub said: The meaning is that the questioning about deeds, and the reward and punishment for them, return to Him on the Day of Resurrection, because today they are not being called to account for them.
Someone else said: In this world there were matters in the hands of people who acted unjustly in them and took what was not theirs; so all of that returns to Allah, and He judges it with truth.
And after it: ﴿وَقُضِيَ ٱلأَمْرُ﴾, i.e. judgement was decided with justice between creatures.

nahhas-meani:211-211.t:
He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿سَلْ بَنِيۤ إِسْرَائِيلَ كَمْ آتَيْنَاهُم مِّنْ آيَةٍ بَيِّنَةٍ﴾.
I.e. confirming the matter of the Prophet ﷺ.
Mujāhid said: What is mentioned of them in the Qurʾān and what is not mentioned. He said: And they are the Jews.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَمَن يُبَدِّلْ نِعْمَةَ ٱللَّهِ مِن بَعْدِ مَا جَآءَتْهُ﴾.
Mujāhid said: I.e. disbelieves in it. This was said to them because they altered what was in their scriptures.

nahhas-meani:212-212.t:
He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿زُيِّنَ لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ ٱلْحَيَاةُ ٱلدُّنْيَا﴾.
Abū Isḥāq said: I.e. Iblīs made it attractive to them, because Allah has urged renunciation of it and made known that it is the enjoyment of delusion.
And it was said: Its meaning is that Allah created pleasing things, and those who disbelieved looked at them as worth more than their measure.
Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿وَيَسْخَرُونَ مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ﴾.
He said: I.e. in respect of what they possess.
Ibn Jurayj said: They mock them for seeking the Hereafter.
Qatāda said: ﴿فَوْقَهُمْ﴾, i.e. in Paradise.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَٱللَّهُ يَرْزُقُ مَن يَشَآءُ بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ﴾.
He does not provide for the believer according to the measure of his faith, nor provide for the unbeliever according to the measure of his unbelief.
I.e. He does not reckon provision in this world according to the measure of deeds.
Quṭrub said: The meaning — and Allah knows best — is that He gives [His servants from an allotted thing], not from a number greater than it from which He takes it, like a human giver giving a thousand out of two thousand.
He said: Another aspect is that whoever spends something for which he is not called to account, that is "without reckoning".

nahhas-meani:265-265.t:
He said: ﴿وَمَثَلُ ٱلَّذِينَ يُنْفِقُونَ أَمْوَالَهُمُ ٱبْتِغَآءَ مَرْضَاتِ ٱللَّهِ وَتَثْبِيتاً مِّنْ أَنْفُسِهِمْ﴾.
That is, they spend it acknowledging and firmly convinced that it is among what Allah rewards.
Al-Ḥasan said: When he wanted to spend, he would make sure (tathabbata): if it was for Allah, he went ahead; otherwise he held back.
Qatāda said: ﴿تَثْبِيتَاً﴾, that is, seeking reward (iḥtisāban).
Mujāhid said: They make sure where they place their wealth, that is, their zakāt.
Al-Shaʿbī said: [It means] affirmation and certainty.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Had it been as Mujāhid said, it would be "wa-tathabbutan," from tathabbattu, like takarramtu takarruman.
And Qatāda's saying "and seeking reward" is not known [linguistically], unless what is meant is that their souls make them firm while seeking reward; and this is far-fetched.
And al-Shaʿbī's view is good, that is, a strengthening on their behalf from their own souls in spending that in obedience to Allah, Majestic and Mighty. It is said: thabbattu fulānan fī hādhā al-amr, that is, I made his resolve sound and strengthened his judgement in it — uthabbituhu tathbītan. That is, their souls are certain and affirming of Allah's promise, upon their making sure in that.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿كَمَثَلِ جَنَّةٍ بِرَبْوَةٍ﴾.
Mujāhid said: It is level, elevated ground; it doubled its fruit.
Qatāda said: ﴿بِرَبْوَةٍ﴾, he says: on a raised piece of ground. He said: This is a parable Allah has struck for the deeds of the believer. He says: his good never fails, just as the good of this garden never fails in whatever state it is: whether "a downpour (wābil) strikes it" — which is heavy rain — or "a drizzle (ṭall)" strikes it.
Mujāhid said: [It is] dew.
And it was said: light rain that lasts.
Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] said: That is, the drizzle suffices it.

nahhas-meani:266-266.t:
He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿أَيَوَدُّ أَحَدُكُمْ أَن تَكُونَ لَهُ جَنَّةٌ﴾ up to His words: ﴿فَٱحْتَرَقَتْ﴾.
Ibn Abī Mulayka said, from ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr: ʿUmar asked them about this verse and mentioned it, and they said: "Allah knows best." ʿUmar became angry and said: "Say 'we know' or 'we do not know.'" He said: Ibn ʿAbbās said: "There is something in my mind about it." He said: "Speak, and do not belittle yourself." He said: "It was struck as a parable for deeds." He said: "Which deeds?" He said: Then ʿUmar said: "This is a man who used to act in obedience to Allah; then Satan was sent to him, and he committed sins, and so burned up [his] deeds."
And it is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās by a chain other than this: This is a parable Allah has struck for those who perform deeds for show; Allah will nullify them on the Day of Resurrection when they are most in need of them — like a man who had a garden and grew old, having small children who could not benefit him; then a whirlwind (iʿṣār) struck the garden — a violent wind containing intense scorching heat (samūm) — and it burned up, so he lost it when he was most in need of it.
And it is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: al-iʿṣār is the violent wind.
Abū Jaʿfar said: al-iʿṣār is what people call al-zawbaʿa (the whirlwind).

nahhas-meani:267-267.t:
He the Exalted said: ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُوۤاْ أَنْفِقُواْ مِن طَيِّبَاتِ مَا كَسَبْتُمْ﴾.
That is, give the good [part] in charity.
Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Salāma narrated to us, saying: Bakkār narrated to us, saying: Muʾammal narrated to us, saying: Sufyān narrated to us from al-Suddī, from Abū Mālik, from al-Barāʾ, who said: "They used to bring the worst of their dates and the worst of their food as charity; so there was revealed: ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُوۤاْ أَنْفِقُواْ مِن طَيِّبَاتِ مَا كَسَبْتُمْ﴾ up to His words: ﴿إِلاَّ أَن تُغْمِضُواْ فِيهِ﴾."
He said: Were it owed to you and he gave it to you, you would not take it except while considering that he had shortchanged you of your due.
Abū Isḥāq said concerning His words ﴿وَٱعْلَمُوۤاْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَنِيٌّ حَمِيدٌ﴾: that is, He did not command you to give charity out of [His] need; rather He tested your state, and He is praiseworthy for that and for all His blessings.

nahhas-meani:268-268.t:
He the Exalted said: ﴿ٱلشَّيْطَانُ يَعِدُكُمُ ٱلْفَقْرَ﴾.
That is, with poverty: he frightens you so that you give the inferior [part] in zakāt. ﴿وَيَأْمُرُكُم بِٱلْفَحْشَآءِ﴾: that you not give charity, and so disobey and cut [the ties of kinship] with one another.
﴿وَٱللَّهُ يَعِدُكُم مَّغْفِرَةً مِّنْهُ وَفَضْلاً﴾.
That is, that He will requite you for your charity with forgiveness and replacement.
﴿وَٱللَّهُ وَاسِعٌ عَلِيمٌ﴾.
He gives out of abundance, and knows where to place that, and knows the unseen and the seen.

nahhas-meani:269-269.t:
He the Exalted said: ﴿يُؤْتِي الْحِكْمَةَ مَن يَشَآءُ وَمَن يُؤْتَ الْحِكْمَةَ فَقَدْ أُوتِيَ خَيْراً كَثِيراً﴾.
ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿وَمَن يُؤْتَ الْحِكْمَةَ فَقَدْ أُوتِيَ خَيْراً كَثِيراً﴾ — he said: knowledge of the Qurʾān: its abrogating and abrogated [verses], its decisive and ambiguous [verses], what in it comes earlier and later, its lawful and unlawful, and its parables.
Mujāhid said: intelligence, chastity and being correct in speech.
Zayd ibn Aslam said: Wisdom («حكمة») is understanding in the religion of Allah.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: Wisdom is the Qurʾān.
Qatāda said: [It is] comprehension.
I say: These views agree. The basic sense of «حكمة» is that by which one is restrained from folly. Knowledge was called «حكمة» because by it one is restrained, and by it restraint from folly is known — folly being every ugly act; and likewise the Qurʾān, intelligence and comprehension.
Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī said: [It is] comprehension of the Qurʾān.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿وَمَا يَذَّكَّرُ إِلاَّ أُوْلُواْ ٱلأَلْبَابِ﴾.
That is, none reflects with a reflection by which he takes heed of the signs He has related except the possessors of intellect, and whoever has understood from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, His command and His prohibition.

nahhas-meani:270-270.t:
He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿وَمَآ أَنفَقْتُمْ مِّن نَّفَقَةٍ﴾.
Abū Isḥāq said: [That is,] in an obligatory [spending], because He mentioned the charity of zakāt.
﴿أَوْ نَذَرْتُمْ مِّن نَّذْرٍ﴾.
Everything a person intends to do voluntarily is a vow (nadhr).
And it was said: the meaning is: whatever spending you spend without a vow, or [whatever] you vowed and then bound yourselves to spend ﴿فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَعْلَمُهُ﴾, that is, it is not hidden from Him, so He will requite it.
Mujāhid said: ﴿يَعْلَمُهُ﴾, that is, He records it.

nahhas-meani:271-271.t:
He the Exalted said: ﴿إِن تُبْدُواْ ٱلصَّدَقَاتِ﴾.
That is, if you make them manifest.
And in the ḥadīth: "Secret charity extinguishes the anger of the Lord."
And it was said: This was in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; as for today, people think ill [of those who give secretly].
Al-Ḥasan said: Making zakāt manifest is better, and concealing voluntary [charity] is more excellent, because it is a stronger indication that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, alone is intended by it.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: This was acted upon by ﴿الَّذِينَ يُنْفِقُونَ أَمْوَالَهُمْ بالَّليْلِ والنَّهارِ سِرَّاً وَعَلاَنِيَةً﴾; then when "Barāʾa" was revealed with the obligation of charity and its details, charity came to rest on that.

nahhas-meani:272-272.t:
The words of Him, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿لَّيْسَ عَلَيْكَ هُدَاهُمْ﴾.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: They used to dislike giving charity to their relatives among the polytheists; then they were granted a dispensation in that, and there was revealed: ﴿لَّيْسَ عَلَيْكَ هُدَاهُمْ﴾ to the end of the verses.

nahhas-meani:273-273.t:
The words of Him, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿لِلْفُقَرَآءِ ٱلَّذِينَ أُحصِرُواْ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
Mujāhid said: He means the emigrants (muhājirūn) of Quraysh who were in Medina.
Someone else said: The meaning of ﴿أُحصِرُواْ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ﴾ is: the obligation of jihad prevented them from going about [earning a living].
And it was said: their enemy kept them busy with fighting from going about [earning a living].
Abū Jaʿfar said: The language requires that (أُحْصِرُوْا) be from illness, except that the meaning may be: they were found in this state.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿لاَ يَسْتَطِيعُونَ ضَرْباً فِي ٱلأَرْضِ﴾.
It was said: they have bound themselves to jihad, as it is said: "I cannot disobey you," that is, I have bound myself to obeying you.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿يَحْسَبُهُمُ ٱلْجَاهِلُ أَغْنِيَآءَ مِنَ ٱلتَّعَفُّفِ﴾.
Ignorance (jahl) here is not the opposite of intelligence; it is only the opposite of acquaintance (khibra).
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿تَعْرِفُهُم بِسِيْمَاهُمْ لاَ يَسْأَلُونَ ٱلنَّاسَ إِلْحَافاً﴾.
It is said: alḥafa fī al-masʾala, akhfā and alaḥḥa, with one meaning ("he was importunate in asking"). [Translator's note: «أخفى» is as written; the expected word is «أحفى».]
And in the ḥadīth from the Prophet ﷺ: "Whoever asks while he has forty dirhams has been importunate (alḥafa)."
Abū Isḥāq said: Its meaning is: he has been all-encompassing in asking; and from it liḥāf (a cover) is derived. He said: And the meaning of ﴿لاَ يَسْأَلُونَ ٱلنَّاسَ إِلْحَافاً﴾ is: no asking comes from them at all, such that there could be importunity, as the poet said:
على لاَ حِبٍ لا يُهْتَدَى بَمَنَارِهِ * إذَا سَافَهُ العَوْدُ النَّبَاطِيُّ جَرْجَرا
(On a well-trodden road whose waymarks give no guidance; when the old Nabataean camel sniffs it, it groans.)
That is, it has no waymark by which one could be guided.

nahhas-meani:213-213.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿كَانَ ٱلنَّاسُ أُمَّةً وَاحِدَةً﴾.
Mujāhid said: Adam [alone] was a single community.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr [Translator's note: so in the source; one would expect Saʿīd (ibn Abī ʿArūba) narrating from Qatāda] related from Qatāda, who said: He is saying: "They were all upon a law of truth."
It was mentioned to us that between Adam and Noah there were ten generations, all of them acting in obedience to Allah, upon guidance and upon the law of truth; then they differed after that, so Allah sent Noah.
Abū Jaʿfar said: (أُمَّة) is from their saying amamtu kadhā, i.e. I made for it (intended it).
So the meaning of (أُمَّة) is that their aim is one; and a solitary person is called an "umma", i.e. his aim is other than the aim of people.
And al-umma is stature, as if it were the aim of the rest of the body; and al-imma — with kasra — is also blessing (niʿma), because people make for it; and imām is so called because people aim at [following] what he does.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَأَنزَلَ مَعَهُمُ ٱلْكِتَابَ بِٱلْحَقِّ لِيَحْكُمَ بَيْنَ ٱلنَّاسِ فِيمَا ٱخْتَلَفُواْ فِيهِ﴾.
I.e. the Book decides by judgement.
Al-Jaḥdarī read: (ليُحْكَم) with a ḍamma on the yāʾ and a fatḥa on the kāf.
And al-Farazdaq said:
ضَرَبَتْ عَلَيْكَ العَنْكَبُوتُ بنَسْجِهَا * وقَضَى عَلَيْكَ بِهِ الكِتَابُ المُنْزَلُ
(The spider has spread its web over you, and the revealed Book has decreed it against you.)
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَمَا ٱخْتَلَفَ فِيهِ إِلاَّ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُوهُ﴾.
I.e. none differed about the Book except those who were given it.
Abū Isḥāq said: I.e. none differed about the truth of the Prophet's ﷺ matter except those who were given knowledge of its truth, upon him be blessing and peace.
﴿بَغْياً بَيْنَهُمْ﴾, i.e. for the sake of transgression; i.e. they brought about the disagreement only out of transgression.
* And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فَهَدَى ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ لِمَا ٱخْتَلَفُواْ فِيهِ مِنَ ٱلْحَقِّ بِإِذْنِهِ﴾.
Abū Mālik related from Ibn ʿAbbās: The unbelievers differed about it, and Allah guided those who believed to the truth of that.
Abū Hurayra related from the Prophet ﷺ that he said:
"We are the last and the first on the Day of Resurrection; we are the first of people to enter Paradise, except that they were given the Book before us and we were given it after them. So Allah guided us to the truth about which they differed. This is the day about which they differed, [and Allah guided us to it], so people follow us in it: tomorrow is for the Jews, and the day after tomorrow for the Christians."
And in a version of the ḥadīth: "Allah guided us to the day of Jumuʿa (Friday)."
Zayd ibn Aslam said: They differed: the Jews took the Sabbath and the Christians Sunday, and Allah guided the community of Muḥammad to Friday.
And they differed about the qibla, and they differed about prayer and fasting: some of them fast from some foods, and some of them fast part of the day.
And they differed about "Abraham", and Allah guided the community of Muḥammad to the truth of that.
Abū Zayd said: And they differed about Jesus: the Jews made him [the fruit of] a calumny, and the Christians made him a lord; and Allah guided the believers.
Abū Isḥāq said: ﴿بإذْنِهِ﴾, i.e. by His knowledge.

nahhas-meani:214-214.t:
He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿أَمْ حَسِبْتُمْ أَن تَدْخُلُواْ ٱلْجَنَّةَ﴾.
(أَمْ) here is for moving from one topic to another.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَلَمَّا يَأْتِكُم مَّثَلُ ٱلَّذِينَ خَلَوْاْ مِن قَبْلِكُم﴾.
Al-Naḍr ibn Shumayl reported that "مَثَل" may mean "description" (ṣifa).
And the meaning may be: and the like of what befell those before you has not yet befallen you. And (خَلَوْا), i.e. passed away.
﴿مَسَّتْهُم البَأْسَاء والضرَّاء﴾, i.e. poverty and illness.
(وزلْزِلُوا): they were made afraid and shaken by what harms.
Abū Isḥāq said: The origin of al-zalzala is from zalla al-shayʾ ʿan makānihi (the thing slipped from its place); so when you say zalzaltuhu, its meaning is: you repeated its slipping from its place.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿حَتَّىٰ يَقُولَ ٱلرَّسُولُ وَٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ مَعَهُ مَتَىٰ نَصْرُ ٱللَّهِ﴾? [verse 214].
I.e. strain reached them to the point that they thought the help slow in coming.
And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿أَلاۤ إِنَّ نَصْرَ ٱللَّهِ قَرِيبٌ﴾, i.e. He will help His friends without fail.

nahhas-meani:215-215.t:
He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿يَسْأَلُونَكَ مَاذَا يُنْفِقُونَ﴾? [verse 215].
I.e. give in charity and give.
﴿قُلْ مَآ أَنْفَقْتُمْ مِّنْ خَيْرٍ فَلِلْوَالِدَيْنِ وَٱلأَقْرَبِينَ وَٱلْيَتَامَىٰ وَٱلْمَسَاكِينِ وَٱبْنِ ٱلسَّبِيلِ﴾.
It was said: They had asked on whom they ought to bestow [their bounty].
So it was said: The most deserving of those on whom bounty is bestowed are these.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَمَا تَفْعَلُواْ مِنْ خَيْرٍ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ بِهِ عَلِيمٌ﴾.
I.e. He counts it, and when He has counted it He requites it.

nahhas-meani:216-216.t:
He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمُ ٱلْقِتَالُ﴾.
Most of the exegetes hold that jihād is obligatory, and that the meaning is: fighting has been made obligatory for you, except that some of them suffice in place of others.
Allah the Exalted said: ﴿وقاتِلُوا في سَبيلِ الله﴾.
Abū Ṭalḥa said concerning His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿انْفِروُا خِفَافَاً وَثِقَالاً﴾:
I have not heard that Allah excused anyone.
However, Sufyān al-Thawrī said: Jihād is voluntary, and the meaning of ﴿كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمُ ٱلْقِتَالُ﴾ is [prescribed] in the sense of its being meritorious.
Then He said: ﴿وَهُوَ كُرْهٌ لَّكُمْ﴾.
Abū Isḥāq said: The interpretation is: and it is a thing of aversion to you. [One says:] karihtu al-shayʾ kurhan, karhan, karāhatan and karāhiyatan.
Al-Kisāʾī said: It is as if al-kurh is from yourself, and al-karh — with a fatḥa — is what you are compelled to.
﴿وَعَسَىٰ أَن تَكْرَهُواْ شَيْئاً وَهُوَ خَيْرٌ لَّكُمْ﴾.
I.e. if he is killed he is a martyr, and if he kills he is rewarded and takes booty, and he demolishes the cause of unbelief, and by fighting brings about the entry into Islam of those he fights.
﴿وَعَسَىٰ أَن تُحِبُّواْ شَيْئاً﴾: staying back from fighting.

nahhas-meani:217-217.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿يَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلشَّهْرِ ٱلْحَرَامِ قِتَالٍ فِيهِ قُلْ قِتَالٌ فِيهِ كَبِيرٌ﴾.
Saʿīd related from Qatāda, who said: Fighting in it was a grave matter — as He, Exalted is He, said — then it was abrogated in Barāʾa: ﴿وَقَاتِلُوا المُشْرِكين كَافَّة كَمَا يُقَاتِلونَكُم كافَّةً﴾.
Abū al-Sayyār related from Jundab ibn ʿAbd Allāh that the Prophet ﷺ sent out a party and put over them Abū ʿUbayda ibn al-Ḥārith — or ʿUbayda ibn al-Ḥārith. When he went to set off, he wept out of longing for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; so he sent "ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaḥsh" instead, wrote a letter for him, and ordered him not to read the letter until he reached such-and-such a place, and said: Do not compel your companions to go on. When he reached the place he read the letter, said "To Allah we belong and to Him we return", and said: Hearing and obedience to Allah and His Messenger. He said: Two men went back, and the rest of them went on. They met al-Ḥaḍramī and killed him, not knowing that that day was of Rajab. The polytheists said: You have killed in the sacred month. So Allah the Exalted revealed ﴿يَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلشَّهْرِ ٱلْحَرَامِ﴾ — the verse.
And it was said: [They said:] If we have not incurred a burden of sin, then there is no reward for us either. So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ آمنوا والَّذِينَ هَاجَرُوا وَجَاهَدُوا في سَبِيلِ اللهِ﴾ to the end of the verse.
Mujāhid said: ﴿قُلْ قِتَالٌ فِيهِ كَبِيرٌ﴾, i.e. grievous.
And the sentence is complete [there]. Then He began anew and said: ﴿وَصَدٌّ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ وَكُفْرٌ بِهِ﴾, i.e. in Allah, ﴿وَٱلْمَسْجِدِ ٱلْحَرَامِ﴾, i.e. and barring from the Sacred Mosque;
﴿وَإِخْرَاجُ أَهْلِهِ مِنْهُ﴾, meaning the Sacred Mosque, ﴿أَكْبَرُ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ﴾ than killing in the sacred month.
﴿وَٱلْفِتْنَةُ أَكْبَرُ مِنَ ٱلْقَتْلِ﴾.
Al-Shaʿbī said: I.e. unbelief; and the meaning is: these deeds of yours [O polytheists] are unbelief, and unbelief is graver than killing in the sacred month.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَلاَ يَزَالُونَ يُقَاتِلُونَكُمْ حَتَّىٰ يَرُدُّوكُمْ عَن دِينِكُمْ إِن اسْتَطَاعُواْ﴾.
Mujāhid said: He means the unbelievers of Quraysh.
* And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿أُوْلۤـٰئِكَ يَرْجُونَ رَحْمَتَ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
And what is the meaning of ﴿يَرْجُونَ رَحْمَتَ ٱللَّهِ﴾ when He has already praised them?! [The answer is] that they do not know with what [end] their lives will be sealed.

nahhas-meani:274-274.t:
The words of Him, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ يُنْفِقُونَ أَمْوَالَهُمْ بِٱللَّيْلِ وَٱلنَّهَارِ﴾.
Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Nāfiʿ narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Wahhāb ibn Mujāhid informed us from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās, concerning His words ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ يُنْفِقُونَ أَمْوَالَهُمْ بِٱللَّيْلِ وَٱلنَّهَارِ سِرّاً وَعَلاَنِيَةً﴾; he said: "It was revealed about ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him. He had four dirhams with him, and he spent one dirham by night, one dirham by day, one dirham secretly and one dirham openly."

nahhas-meani:275-275.t:
The words of Him, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ يَأْكُلُونَ ٱلرِّبَا لاَ يَقُومُونَ إِلاَّ كَمَا يَقُومُ ٱلَّذِي يَتَخَبَّطُهُ ٱلشَّيْطَانُ مِنَ ٱلْمَسِّ﴾.
The meaning is: ﴿ٱلَّذِيْنَ يَأْكُلُونَ ٱلرِّبَا﴾ in this world ﴿لاَ يَقُومُونَ﴾ in the Hereafter ﴿إِلاَّ كَمَا يَقُومُ ٱلَّذِي يَتَخَبَّطُهُ ٱلشَّيْطَانُ مِنَ ٱلْمَسِّ﴾.
Qatāda said: that is, madness.
Someone else said: This is a mark for them on the Day of Resurrection. People will come out of their graves hurrying, as He the Exalted said: ﴿يَخْرُجوْنَ مِنَ الأَجْدَاثِ سِرَاعَاً﴾ — except those who devour usury (ribā): they rise and fall. Allah will swell the usury in their bellies on the Day of Resurrection until it weighs them down, so they get up and fall, wanting to hurry but unable.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿فَمَن جَآءَهُ مَوْعِظَةٌ مِّنْ رَّبِّهِ فَٱنْتَهَىٰ﴾.
Sufyān said: He means the Qurʾān.
And the meaning of ﴿فَلَهُ مَا سَلَفَ﴾ is: it is forgiven him.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿وَأَمْرُهُ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ﴾.
Abū Isḥāq said: That is, Allah, Majestic and Mighty, is his guardian.
Someone else said: ﴿وَأَمْرُهُ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ﴾ in His protecting him and granting him success: if He wills, He protects him from consuming it, and if He wills, He forsakes him in that.
Some exegetes said: ﴿وَأَمْرُهُ إِلَى ٱللَّهِِ﴾ in the future.
This is a good and clear view, that is: his affair is with Allah in the future; if He wills He keeps him firm upon the prohibition, and if He wills He makes it permissible.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿وَمَنْ عَادَ فَأُوْلَـٰئِكَ أَصْحَابُ ٱلنَّارِ هُمْ فِيهَا خَالِدُونَ﴾.
Sufyān said: whoever returns and practises usury until he dies.
Someone else said: whoever returns and says "Trade is only like usury" has disbelieved.

nahhas-meani:278-278.t:
The words of Him, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ ٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَذَرُواْ مَا بَقِيَ مِنَ ٱلرِّبَا﴾.
Mujāhid said: In the Jāhiliyya, a man would be owed a debt by another man, and [the debtor] would say: "You get such-and-such and you defer [payment] for me"; so he would defer it for him and he would give him more.

nahhas-meani:279-279.t:
The words of Him, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فَإِن لَّمْ تَفْعَلُواْ فَأْذَنُواْ بِحَرْبٍ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ﴾.
That is, be certain. It is said: adhintu bi-l-shayʾ, so I am adhīn bihi ("I am assured of it"), as [the poet] said:
* "فَإِنِّي أَذِينٌ إنْ رَجَعْتُ مُمَلَّكَاً" *
(For I am pledged/assured, if I return as one made king…)
And the meaning of "fa-ādhinū" [with the long vowel] is: inform others that you are at war with them.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿وَإِنْ تُبْتُمْ فَلَكُمْ رُؤُوسُ أَمْوَالِكُمْ لاَ تَظْلِمُونَ وَلاَ تُظْلَمُونَ﴾.
Then al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: In the Jāhiliyya they used to trade with usury; then Islam came while they still had wealth [outstanding], so they were commanded to take their capital and not take the usury with which they had charged interest, and they were commanded to give in charity to whoever was in hardship.

nahhas-meani:280-280.t:
He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَإِن كَانَ ذُو عُسْرَةٍ فَنَظِرَةٌ إِلَىٰ مَيْسَرَةٍ﴾.
Ibrāhīm said: It was revealed concerning usury.
Al-Rabīʿ ibn Khaytham said: It is for every one in hardship: he is granted respite.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This view is good, because the reading in the nominative (marfūʿ) means: "and if there occurs one in hardship" among all people — if among those you claim from or trade with there is one in hardship. [Translator's note: i.e. kāna here is complete (tāmma), "occur, be".]
Had it been about usury specifically, the accusative (naṣb) would have been the [proper] way, meaning: "and if the one who owes the usury is in hardship."
However, al-Muʿtamir narrated from Ḥajjāj al-Warrāq that in the codex of ʿUthmān [it is]: "وَإِنْ كَانَ ذَا عُسْرَة"; and the meaning is: then upon you is respite (naẓira), that is, deferral until he becomes well off.
And it is narrated from ʿAṭāʾ that he read "فَنَاظِرَةٌ إِلَى مَيْسَرَةٍ" by way of command.
[Translator's note: «فناظرة» is as written; the reading usually attributed to ʿAṭāʾ is «فناظِرْهُ», an imperative, which fits "by way of command".]
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿وَأَن تَصَدَّقُواْ خَيْرٌ لَّكُمْ إِن كُنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ﴾.
Ibrāhīm said: that is, with the capital.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: And that you give in charity from the capital is better than respite.
ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam narrated from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, who said: "Ibn ʿAbbās held that the last verse of the Qurʾān to be revealed was ﴿وَاتَّقُوا يَوْمَاً تُرْجَعُونَ فِيهِ إلَى اللهِ﴾."
It was read to Aḥmad ibn Shuʿayb, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAqīl, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, who said: My father narrated to me from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās, concerning His words ﴿وَاتَّقُوا يَوْمَاً تُرْجَعُونَ فِيهِ إلَى اللهِ﴾ — the verse — that it is the last verse revealed to the Messenger of Allah, upon him be peace.

nahhas-meani:283-283.t:
He the Exalted said: ﴿وَإِن كُنتُمْ عَلَىٰ سَفَرٍ وَلَمْ تَجِدُواْ كَاتِباً فَرِهَانٌ مَّقْبُوضَةٌ﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās read "كتاباً" (a writing).
And he said: A scribe may be found while no sheet is found.
Abū al-ʿĀliya, ʿIkrima, al-Ḍaḥḥāk and Mujāhid read likewise.
And it was said: kitāb is the plural of kātib, as one says qāyim [Translator's note: so written, for qāʾim] and qiyām.
And it was said: they [i.e. the two readings] are equivalent.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿فَرِهَانٌ مَّقْبُوضَةٌ﴾.
It has been read "فَرُهُنٌ مَقْبُوضَةٌ"; ruhun is the plural of rihān, and it may be the plural of rahn, like saqf and suquf.

nahhas-meani:219-219.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿يَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلْخَمْرِ وَٱلْمَيْسِرِ قُلْ فِيهِمَآ إِثْمٌ كَبِيرٌ وَمَنَافِعُ لِلنَّاسِ﴾.
ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿يَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلْخَمْرِ وَٱلْمَيْسِرِ قُلْ فِيهِمَآ إِثْمٌ كَبِيرٌ وَمَنَافِعُ لِلنَّاسِ﴾; then He revealed: ﴿لاَ تَقْرَبُوا الصَّلاةَ وَأنْتُم سُكَارَى حَتَّى تَعْلَموا ما تَقُولونَ﴾ [so they used to leave it off]; when they had prayed the ʿIshāʾ they would drink it, and by morning the intoxication would have left them; and when they had prayed the morning prayer they would drink it, and by the time of Ẓuhr the intoxication would have left them. Then some people drank it and fought one another and spoke what does not please Allah; so Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿إنَّما الخمرُ والميسرُ، والأنْصَابُ، والأَزْلامُ رِجْسٌ مِنْ عَمَل الشَّيْطانِ، فَاجْتَنِبُوهُ﴾.
So Allah forbade wine, prohibited it, and commanded that it be shunned, just as He commanded that idols be shunned.
Abū Tawba related from Ibn ʿUmar: ﴿إنَّما الخَمْرُ﴾ was revealed, up to His saying ﴿فَهَلْ أَنْتُم مُنْتَهونْ﴾, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: It has been forbidden.
ʿAmr ibn Shuraḥbīl said: ʿUmar said: We have desisted, for it takes away wealth and reason.
The exegetes hold that this is what made it forbidden.
Some jurists said: What made it forbidden is two verses:
One of them: ﴿قُلْ إنَّما حَرَّمَ رَبّي الفَواحِشَ ما ظَهَر مِنْها وما بَطَنَ وَالإثْم﴾.
Abū Isḥāq said: Wine is this [drink] agreed upon; and the analogy for everything that does what it does is that it be called wine and be in its position in prohibition. For the scholars agree that all gambling is forbidden, yet He mentioned only maysir among it, so all of it was made analogous to maysir — and maysir is gambling over slaughter-camels specifically; likewise everything that is like wine is in its position.
The interpretation of khamr in the language is: what covers the mind. Everything of trees and the like that covers a person is called khamar, and what covers him of trees specifically is al-ḍarā, with a short final alif.
And [one says] "he entered into the khumār of the people", i.e. into the great crowd in which one is concealed.
A woman's khimār is her veil, because it covers [the head]; and the khumra is what one prostrates on, because it screens the face from the ground. And every intoxicant is khamr, because it mixes with the mind and covers it; and so-and-so is makhmūr from any intoxicant.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and Mujāhid said: maysir is all gambling.
As for the sin in wine, it is enmity and hatred, and that it comes between a person and his reason by which he discerns and knows what is owed to his Creator.
And gambling breeds enmity, because a person's property passes to another without any return that he receives for it.
And the benefits: the pleasure of wine and the profit in [trading] it, and something coming to a person in gambling without toil.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: Their benefits were before the prohibition, and their sin after the prohibition.
* And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَيَسْأَلُونَكَ مَاذَا يُنفِقُونَ؟ قُلِ ٱلْعَفْوَ﴾.
Ṭāwūs said: A little of everything.
Khālid ibn Abī ʿImrān said: I asked al-Qāsim and Sālim, and they said: The surplus of wealth: what is given in charity out of sufficiency.
Qatāda said: It is the surplus.
Abū Jaʿfar said: These views come back to one thing, because al-ʿafw in the language is what is easy.
One says: "Take what has become easy (ʿafā) for you", i.e. what is easy for you.
And in the ḥadīth from the Prophet ﷺ: "The best charity is what is given out of sufficiency."
On this basis is the interpretation of the view of al-Qāsim and Sālim. And there is another view on the meaning:
Mujāhid said: It is the obligatory alms; but the apparent sense points to the first view.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿كَذٰلِكَ يُبيِّنُ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمُ ٱلآيَاتِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَفَكَّرُونَ فِي ٱلدُّنْيَا وَٱلآخِرَةِ﴾ [verses 219–220].
Abū Jaʿfar said: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Nāfiʿ narrated to us, saying: Salama ibn Shabīb narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, saying: Maʿmar informed us from Qatāda concerning His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَفَكَّرُونَ فِي ٱلدُّنْيَا وَٱلآخِرَةِ﴾.
He said: He is saying: that you may reflect on this world and the Hereafter, and so know the superiority of the Hereafter over this world.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The implied sense according to Qatāda's view is: that you may reflect on the affair of this world and the Hereafter.
And it was said: It involves advancing and postponing (taqdīm wa-taʾkhīr), i.e. thus Allah makes clear to you the signs concerning the affair of this world and the Hereafter, that you may reflect.

nahhas-meani:220-220.t:
He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَيَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلْيَتَامَىٰ قُلْ إِصْلاَحٌ لَّهُمْ خَيْرٌ﴾.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: When there was revealed ﴿إِنَّ الذَّينَ يَأْكُلونَ أَمْوَالَ اليَتَامى ظُلْماً﴾ to its end, they said: This is a binding [threat]; so they kept apart from them and abandoned mixing with them. That was hard on them, and they said to the Prophet ﷺ: The sheep have been left with no herdsman, and the food with no one to prepare it. So there was revealed: ﴿وَيَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلْيَتَامَىٰ قُلْ إِصْلاَحٌ لَّهُمْ خَيْرٌ﴾ to its end.
* And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَٱللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ ٱلْمُفْسِدَ مِنَ ٱلْمُصْلِحِ﴾.
I.e. He knows who mixes with them in order to betray, and who does not intend betrayal.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَلَوْ شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ لأَعْنَتَكُمْ﴾.
Mujāhid said: I.e. had He willed, He would not have permitted you to mix with them in food and pasture.
Al-Ḥakam related from Miqsam from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿وَلَوْ شَآءَ اللَّهَ لأَعْنَتَكُمْ﴾ — he said: had He willed, He would have made what you enjoyed of the orphans' property a cause of ruin.
Abū ʿUbayda said: ﴿لأَعْنَتَكُمْ﴾: He would have destroyed you.
Abū Isḥāq said: Its literal sense is: He would have charged you with what is hard on you, so that you would fall into hardship.
He said: The origin of al-ʿanat in the language is from their saying "ʿanita al-baʿīr ʿanatan", when a break occurs in its leg after it has been set, so that it cannot use it.
﴿إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ﴾, i.e. He does by His might what is required, and no one can avert it from Him.
﴿حَكِيمٌ﴾: possessed of wisdom in what He commanded you concerning orphans and other matters.

nahhas-meani:221-221.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَلاَ تَنْكِحُواْ ٱلْمُشْرِكَاتِ حَتَّىٰ يُؤْمِنَّ﴾.
Most scholars hold that this verse is abrogated; it was abrogated by ﴿اليَوْمَ أُحِّلَ لَكُمُ الطَّيِبَّاتُ﴾ up to His saying ﴿وَالمُحْصَناتُ مِنَ الَّذِيِنَ أُوتُوا الكِتَابِ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ﴾.
This is the view of Ibn ʿAbbās and Makḥūl, and it is the position of the jurists "Mālik, Sufyān and al-Awzāʿī".
Sufyān related from Ḥammād: I asked Saʿīd ibn Jubayr about marrying a Jewish or Christian woman, and he said: There is no harm in it. He said: I said: But Allah says: ﴿وَلاَ تَنْكِحُواْ ٱلْمُشْرِكَاتِ حَتَّىٰ يُؤْمِنَّ﴾. He said: [That is] the idolaters and the Magians.
Maʿmar related from Qatāda: ﴿وَلاَ تَنْكِحُواْ ٱلْمُشْرِكَاتِ﴾ — he said: the polytheist women who are not of the People of the Book; and Ḥudhayfa married a Jewish or a Christian woman.
As for ﴿المُحْصَناتُ مِنَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الكِتَابَ مِنْ قَبلِكُم﴾, it was said: they are the chaste women, and the slave women.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَلاَ تُنْكِحُواْ ٱلْمُشِرِكِينَ حَتَّىٰ يُؤْمِنُواْ﴾.
I.e. do not marry them to Muslim women; ﴿وَلَوْ أَعْجَبَكُمْ﴾, i.e. even if his affair in this world pleases you, his destination is the Fire.
﴿أُوْلَـٰئِكَ يَدْعُونَ إِلَى ٱلنَّارِ﴾.
I.e. they do the deeds of its people; so your offspring would be raised with one whose state is this.
﴿وَٱللَّهُ يَدْعُوۤاْ إِلَى ٱلْجَنَّةِ وَٱلْمَغْفِرَةِ بِإِذْنِهِ﴾.
[I.e. He calls you to the deeds of the people of Paradise.]
﴿وَالمَغْفِرَة بِإذْنِهِ﴾.
It was said: I.e. by His knowledge; i.e. what He called you to is a means of reaching them.
And it was said: by what He commanded you; ﴿وَيُبَيِّنُ آيَاتِهِ﴾, i.e. His signs.
﴿لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَذَكَّرُونَ﴾: so that they may be in hope of taking heed.

nahhas-meani:222-222.t:
He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَيَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلْمَحِيضِ قُلْ هُوَ أَذًى﴾.
Qatāda said: I.e. filth.
Thābit related from Anas (that when a woman menstruated, the Jews would put her out of the house, and would not eat with her, nor drink with her, nor keep company with her in a house. The Prophet ﷺ was asked about that, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿يَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلْمَحِيضِ قُلْ هُوَ أَذًى، فَٱعْتَزِلُواْ ٱلنِّسَآءَ فِي ٱلْمَحِيضِ﴾ — the verse. And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Keep company with them in the houses, and do everything except intercourse."
So by this ḥadīth the meaning of ﴿فَٱعْتَزِلُواْ ٱلنِّسَآءَ فِي ٱلْمَحِيضِ﴾ becomes clear: its meaning is: keep away from them in intercourse only.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَلاَ تَقْرَبُوهُنَّ حَتَّىٰ يَطْهُرْنَ﴾.
I.e. until the blood stops for them.
The people of Kufa read: ﴿يَطَّهَّرْنَ﴾, i.e. they wash themselves.
And likewise is the meaning of ﴿يَتَطَهَّرْنَ﴾, which Ibn Masʿūd and Ubayy read.
Some people found fault with ﴿يَطْهُرْنَ﴾ — without doubling — saying: because touching is not lawful until they have washed.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This does not follow; for its meaning may be like the meaning of ﴿يطَّهَّرْنَ﴾, and its meaning may be: until it becomes lawful for them to purify themselves, as one says of a divorced woman when her waiting period has ended: she has become lawful for men. And He made that clear by His saying: ﴿فَإِذَا تَطَهَّرْنَ﴾.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿فَأَتُوهُنَّ مِنْ حَيْثُ أَمَرَكُمُ ٱللَّهُ﴾.
Mujāhid said: From where they were forbidden it during their menstruation.
Ibrāhīm said: In the vagina.
Ibn al-Ḥanafiyya said: By way of marriage, by way of the lawful.
Abū Razīn said: By way of purity.
Abū al-ʿĀliya said: ﴿ويُحِبُّ المُتَطَهَّرِيَن﴾ from sins.
ʿAṭāʾ said: With water.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The view of ʿAṭāʾ is more fitting, because of the ḥadīth that the Prophet ﷺ said — to the people of the Mosque of Qubāʾ —: "Allah has praised you well in [the matter of] purification; will you not tell me [why]? They said: O Messenger of Allah, we find it written for us in the Torah: cleansing [after relieving oneself] with water."
And this was when there was revealed: ﴿فِيهِ رِجَالٌ يُحِبُّونَ أَنْ يَتَطَهَّروُا﴾.

nahhas-meani:282-282.t:
The words of Him, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُوۤاْ إِذَا تَدَايَنتُم بِدَيْنٍ إِلَىٰ أَجَلٍ مُّسَمًّى فَٱكْتُبُوهُ﴾.
There are several views on its meaning:
1- Among them: that this is by way of recommendation (nadb), not an absolute requirement.
2- Among them: that Abū Naḍra narrated from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī that he recited this verse, ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُوۤاْ إِذَا تَدَايَنتُم بِدَيْنٍ﴾, until he reached ﴿فَإنْ أَمِنَ بَعْضُكُمْ بَعْضَاً فَلْيُؤَدِّ الَّذِي ائْتُمِنَ أَمَانَتَهُ﴾, and said: This verse abrogated what preceded it.
3- And it was said: this [writing] is obligatory for deferred [transactions], and witnessing for immediate ones; the dispensation is only in [the matter of] the pledge (rahn).
It is said: dāyantu al-rajula when I lent to him and borrowed from him; and likewise tadāyana al-qawmu ("the people dealt in debts with one another").
Adantu al-rajula: I sold to him on credit; and dintu and iddantu mean I took on credit; and I am dāʾin and muddān.
And al-mudīn is the king, when people submit (dāna) to him, that is, hear and obey.
Among the questions asked is: What is the point of "بِدَيْنٍ" when "تَدَايَنْتُمْ" already indicates debt — can there be mutual debt-dealing without a debt?
The answer is that the Arabs say "tadāyannā," meaning "we requited one another" and "we exchanged taking and giving"; so "بِدَيْنٍ" came to make the intended meaning clear.
And His words, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَلْيَكْتُب بَّيْنَكُمْ كَاتِبٌ بِٱلْعَدْلِ﴾.
Al-Suddī said: with truth, that is, he does not write for the creditor more than what is his, nor less.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿وَلاَ يَأْبَ كَاتِبٌ أَنْ يَكْتُبَ كَمَا عَلَّمَهُ ٱللَّهُ﴾.
It was said: as Allah has taught him of writing with justice.
And it was said: as Allah has favoured him with the knowledge of writing.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿فَإن كَانَ ٱلَّذِي عَلَيْهِ ٱلْحَقُّ سَفِيهاً أَوْ ضَعِيفاً أَوْ لاَ يَسْتَطِيعُ أَن يُمِلَّ هُوَ﴾.
Ibn Wahb said: Yūnus informed me that he asked Rabīʿa: What is the description of the safīh (feeble-minded)?
He said: The one who does not make his wealth grow in his selling and buying, and does not deny himself any pleasure; he falls upon wealth as one who regards wealth as nothing; the one who is not seen to have any sense regarding wealth.
And it is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: The safīh is the one ignorant of dictation, and the ḍaʿīf (weak) is the clumsy.
Abū Isḥāq said: The safīh is the one light of intellect; and from this: tasaffahat al-rīḥu al-shayʾa, when the wind moves a thing and makes it light; and from it:
مَشَيْنَ كَمَا اهْتَزَّتْ رِمَاحٌ تَسَفَّهَتْ * أَعَالِيَهَا مَرُّ الرَّياح النَّواسِمِ
(They walked swaying as spears sway whose tops are tossed by the passing of gentle breezes.)
Someone else reported that safah is everything whose doing is ugly, that is, it is an act that is not well-made, from their saying thawb safīh when a garment is loosely woven.
As for the ḍaʿīf, he is — and Allah knows best — one in whom there is weakness, from muteness, senility or madness.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿فَلْيُمْلِلْ وَلِيُّهُ بِٱلْعَدْلِ﴾.
There are two views on the meaning of this:
Sufyān narrated from Yūnus, from al-Ḥasan: ﴿فَلْيُمْلِلْ وَلِيُّهُ بِٱلْعَدْلِ﴾.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: The guardian of the safīh is the one whose management of his affair is valid for him; he is his walī, that is, he takes charge of his affair; ﴿بِالعَدْلِ﴾: he is the one who dictates the right [owed].
[Translator's note: al-Ḥasan's explanation is not given in the source after the chain; the text moves straight to al-Ḍaḥḥāk.]
And the other view, from Ibn ʿAbbās, is that the meaning is: let the guardian of the one to whom [the right] is owed dictate.
[Translator's note: «وليّ الذي هو عليه» is translated as written, "the one to whom it is owed"; literally «عليه» would be "upon whom"; the known view of Ibn ʿAbbās is "the guardian of the creditor (walī al-ḥaqq)".]
This view was used as an argument by those who hold that there is no interdiction (ḥajr) on free, adult, sane persons; this is the position of Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn and Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī.
Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿وَٱسْتَشْهِدُواْ شَهِيدَيْنِ مِّن رِّجَالِكُمْ﴾.
It was said: from the people of your religion.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿مِمَّن تَرْضَوْنَ مِنَ ٱلشُّهَدَآءِ﴾.
That is, of those whose way of life you approve.
Ibrāhīm said: of those in whom no cause for suspicion has appeared.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿أَن تَضِلَّ إْحْدَاهُمَا فَتُذَكِّرَ إِحْدَاهُمَا ٱلأُخْرَىٰ﴾.
That is, that one of them should forget, so the other reminds her.
And it is narrated from al-Jaḥdarī: ﴿أنْ تُضِلَّ﴾, that is, she is made to forget, as is said: unsītu kadhā ("I was made to forget such-and-such").
As for what is narrated from Ibn ʿUyayna, that he said: [The other one] makes their testimony equivalent to the testimony of a male (dhakar) — the lexicographers do not know it, and it is also a mistake, because if its meaning were only "We make her equivalent to a male," there would be no need for "أَنْ تَضِلَّ", since she would make her equivalent to a male whether she forgot or not.
And it is not possible that she makes her equivalent to a male when she has forgotten her testimony.
As for the fatḥa of "أَنْ", we will mention it in [our book on] the iʿrāb, if Allah wills.
Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿وَلاَ يَأْبَ ٱلشُّهَدَآءُ إِذَا مَا دُعُواْ﴾.
Ibn Najīḥ [Translator's note: so in the source; elsewhere Ibn Abī Najīḥ] narrated from Mujāhid, who said: When he is called to testify having already been made a witness.
Al-Ḥasan said: And when they are called initially to [bear] witness, and they should not refuse when called to give it.
Abū Jaʿfar said: It was said: al-Ḥasan's view is more likely, because if that [refusal] were [allowed] to them, rights would be lost; and because after it comes ﴿وَلاَ تَسْأَمُوۤاْ أَن تَكْتُبُوهُ صَغِيراً أَو كَبِيراً إِلَىٰ أَجَلِهِ﴾, that is, do not grow weary of writing down the right, be it much or little, as it is said: "I will certainly give you your right, be it small or great."
Al-Akhfash said: ﴿أَنْ تَكْتُبُوهُ﴾ — so he implied (aḍmara) the witness; he said: and He said ﴿إلَى أَجَلِهِ﴾, that is, until the term in which his testimony is valid. And Allah knows best.
This is in the words of al-Akhfash verbatim.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Muḥammad ibn Jarīr [al-Ṭabarī] chose the view of Mujāhid: that the meaning of ﴿وَلاَ يَأْبَ ٱلشُّهَدَآءُ إِذَا مَا دُعُواْ﴾ is that, when you hold a testimony and are called; and this is the view of Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, ʿAṭāʾ, ʿIkrima, al-Shaʿbī and al-Nakhaʿī.
Muḥammad ibn Jarīr said: "Because Allah has given them the name 'witnesses' (shuhadāʾ), and the name 'witnesses' only applies to them if they have witnessed something before that; it is not permissible that they be called 'witnesses' when they have not witnessed.
Were that so, all people would be witnesses, in the sense that they [can] witness. So the meaning becomes: when they are called to give the testimony. Moreover, the entry of the alif and lām shows that the one intended by the prohibition is a known person."
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿ذَلِكُمْ أَقْسَطُ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ وَأَقْومُ لِلشَّهَادَةِ﴾.
Sufyān said: Its meaning is "more just." Then He said ﴿وَأقْومُ لِلشَّهَادَةِ﴾, that is, more firmly established, because the document reminds the witness of what he witnessed.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿وَأَدْنَىٰ أَلاَّ تَرْتَابُوۤاْ﴾.
That is, that you do not doubt.
Then He granted a dispensation to leave off writing in what frequently passes between people, and He the Exalted said: ﴿إِلاَّ أَن تَكُونَ تِجَارَةً حَاضِرَةً تُدِيرُونَهَا بَيْنَكُمْ﴾.
* And His words, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَلاَ يُضَآرَّ كَاتِبٌ وَلاَ شَهِيدٌ﴾.
There are several views on it:
1- Among them: the meaning — according to the view of ʿAṭāʾ — is: let them not refuse when they are called.
As Ibn ʿUyayna narrated from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, from ʿIkrima, who said:
ʿUmar used to read "وَلاَ يُضَارِرْ كَاتِبٌ ولا شَهِيدٌ" (with kasra: let no scribe or witness cause harm).
Ṭāwūs said: Let no scribe cause harm by writing what was not dictated to him.
Al-Ḥasan said: And let the witness not cause harm by adding to his testimony.
2- And it is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās and Mujāhid: ﴿وَلاَ يُضَآرَّ كَاتِبٌ وَلاَ شَهِيدٌ﴾ — they said: It was forbidden that one should come to the witness and the scribe and call them to writing and witnessing while they are busy, and so harm them, saying: "Allah has commanded you not to refuse," while he has no need of them.
The implied construction (taqdīr) on this view is "وَلاَ يُضَارَرْ" (with fatḥa: let no scribe or witness be harmed), and so Ibn Masʿūd read.
So Allah, Majestic and Mighty, forbade this, because had He left it unrestricted, it would distract them from the affairs of their religion and their livelihood.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَإِن تَفْعَلُواْ فَإِنَّهُ فُسُوقٌ بِكُمْ﴾.
Sufyān said: ﴿فَإنَّهُ فُسُوقٌ بِكُمْ﴾ — he said: disobedience.

nahhas-meani:284-284.t:
The words of Him, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَإِن تُبْدُواْ مَا فِيۤ أَنْفُسِكُمْ أَوْ تُخْفُوهُ يُحَاسِبْكُمْ بِهِ ٱللَّهُ﴾.
There are several views on it:
It is narrated from Ibn Masʿūd, Abū Hurayra and Ibn ʿAbbās that it is abrogated by His words ﴿لاَ يُكَلِّفُ اللهُ نَفْسَاً إلاَّ وُسْعَهَا﴾.
Except that ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: It was not abrogated; rather, when Allah gathers the creatures He will say: "I will inform you of what you concealed within yourselves." As for the believers, He will inform them and then forgive them.
As for the people of doubt and suspicion, He will inform them of the denial they concealed; that is His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿يُحَاسِبْكُمْ بِهِ ٱللَّهُ فَيَغْفِرُ لِمَن يَشَآءُ وَيُعَذِّبُ مَن يَشَآءُ﴾.
And it is His words, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَلَكِنْ يُؤَاخِذُكُمْ بِمَا كَسَبَتْ قُلُوبُكُمْ﴾, of doubt and hypocrisy.
Aḥmad ibn Shuʿayb narrated to us, saying: Maḥmūd ibn Ghaylān informed us, saying: Wakīʿ narrated to us, saying: Sufyān narrated to us from Ādam ibn Sulaymān, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "When this verse was revealed, ﴿وَإنْ تُبْدُوا مَا فِي أَنْفُسِكُمْ أَوْ تُخْفُوهُ يُحَاسِبْكُمْ بِهِ الله﴾, something entered their hearts from it that had not entered them before. The Prophet ﷺ said: Say: We hear, we obey and we submit. So Allah cast faith into their hearts, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿آمَنَ الرَّسُولُ بِمَا أُنْزِلَ إلَيْهِ مِنْ رَبِّهِ﴾ — the verse — and revealed ﴿لاَ يُكَلِّفُ اللهُ نَفْسَاً إِلاَّ وُسْعَهَا، لَهَا مَا كَسَبَتْ وَعَلَيْهَا مَا اكْتَسَبَتْ [رَبَّنَا لاَ تُؤَاخِذْنَا إنْ نَسِينَا أوْ أَخْطَأْنَا]﴾ — He said: I have done so — ﴿رَبَّنَا وَلاَ تَحْمِلْ عَلَيْنَا إصْرَاً كَمَا حَمَلْتَهُ عَلَى الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِنَا﴾ — He said: I have done so — ﴿رَبَّنَا وَلاَ تُحَمِّلْنَا مَا لاَ طَاقَةَ لَنا بِهِ، واعْفُ عَنَّا، واغْفِرْ لَنَا، وَارْحَمْنَا، أَنْتَ مَوْلانَا فَانْصُرْنَا عَلَى القَوْمِ الكَافِرينَ﴾ — He said: I have done so."
Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Khālid narrated from al-Shaʿbī, who said: "It was abrogated by the verse after it: ﴿لا يُكَلِّفُ اللهُ نَفْسَاً إِلاَّ وُسْعَهَا﴾."
Miqsam narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: It was revealed concerning testimony, that is, concerning disclosing and concealing it.
Mujāhid said: This is about doubt and certainty.
Ḥammād ibn Salama narrated from ʿAlī ibn Zayd, from Umayya, that she asked ʿĀʾisha about this verse, ﴿وَإِن تُبْدُواْ مَا فِيۤ أَنْفُسِكُمْ أَوْ تُخْفُوهُ يُحَاسِبْكُمْ بِهِ ٱللَّهُ﴾, and asked her about this verse, ﴿مَنْ يَعْمَلْ سُوءَاً يُجْزَ بِهِ﴾. ʿĀʾisha said: No one has asked me about them since I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about them, and he said: "O ʿĀʾisha, this is Allah's reproaching the servant through what befalls him [of fever, misfortune and the thorn-prick — even the goods he puts in his sleeve] and then misses, and is alarmed for it, then finds it in his armpit; until the believer comes out of his sins as red gold comes out of the bellows."
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: "Allah will inform him on the Day of Resurrection of what he used to keep secret, so that he may know that it was not hidden from Him."
And it was said: There can be no abrogation in this, because it is a statement of fact (khabar); rather, it is explained by ﴿إِنْ تَجْتَنِبُوا كَبَائِرَ مَا تُنْهَوْنَ عَنْهُ نُكَفِّرْ عَنْكُمْ سَيِّئَاتِكُمْ﴾.
So the meaning — and Allah knows best — is: whether you disclose what is within yourselves or conceal it, of the major sins. And what ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās is good; and Allah knows best what He meant.
As for what is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās regarding abrogation, it is among the things whose interpretation must be considered carefully, since abrogating and abrogated do not occur in reports (akhbār).
If it is authentic, its interpretation is that the second is like the first, as you say: "I copied (nasakhtu) this from this."
And another view was stated about it, whose meaning would be: so what had mixed with their hearts of that was removed, and [the matter] was made clear.

safi-cedvel:25-25.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (بشّر) an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) a latent (mustatir) pronoun whose implied form is "you" (أنت); (الذين) a relative noun in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (آمنوا) a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, and (الواو) is the fāʿil. (الواو) conjunction; (عملوا) a verb and its fāʿil; (الصالحات) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the kasra, since it is a sound feminine plural; (أنّ) a particle resembling the verb, for emphasis; (اللام) a preposition, and (هم) an attached pronoun in the position of genitive by the lām, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate).
(جنات) the noun of anna, postponed, accusative, the sign of its accusative being the kasra.
The interpreted maṣdar is in the position of genitive by an omitted bāʾ, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (بشّر) «[Note: This is the doctrine of al-Khalīl.. or it is in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi according to the doctrine of Sībawayh, but the first is more consistent with analogy.]» .
(تجري) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ; (من تحت) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (تجري) «[Note: In it a muḍāf is omitted, i.e.: the rivers flow from beneath its trees.]» and (ها) an attached pronoun in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; (الأنهار) fāʿil, nominative. (كلما) adverbial, conditional, non-jussivizing «[Note: See another way of parsing it at verse (20).]» . (رزقوا) a past verb in the passive, indeclinable on the ḍamma, and (الواو) an attached pronoun in the position of nominative as nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (من) a preposition and (ها) an attached pronoun in the position of genitive by (من), attached to (رزقوا) ; (من ثمرة) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of «رزقا» «[Note: Or it is a badal (substitute) from the preceding genitive (منها), a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl), so it is attached to what the substituted-for word is attached to.]» - a naʿt (adjective) that has been placed before the word it qualifies - (رزقا) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (قالوا) a verb and its fāʿil; (ها) a particle of alerting (tanbīh); (ذا) a demonstrative in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); (الذي) a relative noun in the position of nominative as khabar, and it involves the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "like that which we were provided".. (رزقنا) a past verb in the passive, and (نا) an attached pronoun in the position of nominative as nāʾib fāʿil - the second object is omitted, i.e. "we were provided it" (رزقناه) - (من) a preposition; (قبل) a noun indeclinable on the ḍamma in the position of genitive by (من), attached to (رزقنا) . (الواو) parenthetical or circumstantial; (أتوا) a past verb in the passive, and (الواو) nāʾib fāʿil; (الباء) a preposition and (الهاء) an attached pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (أتوا) ; (متشابها) a ḥāl, accusative, from the hāʾ in (به) . (الواو) conjunction; (اللام) a preposition and (هم) an attached pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to an omitted, fronted khabar; (في) a preposition, (ها) an attached pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to the omitted khabar; (أزواج) a postponed mubtadaʾ, nominative; (مطهّرة) a naʿt of (أزواج), nominative like it. (الواو) conjunction; (هم) a detached pronoun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ; (فيها) attached to (خالدون), which is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the wāw.
The clause «بشّر ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive; it is not valid to conjoin it to the clause «اتّقوا» in the previous verse.
The clause «آمنوا» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين) .
The clause «عملوا ... » has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The clause «تجري ... » is in the position of accusative as a naʿt of (جنّات) .
The clause «رزقوا ... » is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi «[Note: The utterance made up of the conditional particle, its protasis and its apodosis is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl of the fāʿil of «آمنوا», i.e. "being provided for perpetually"; it may also be a ḥāl of «جنّات» - since it has been qualified - and in the clause there is a pronoun referring back to it.]» The clause «قالوا ... » has no grammatical position, being the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussivizing condition.
The clause «هذا الذي ... » is in the position of accusative as the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «رزقنا» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (الذي) .
The clause «أتوا ... » has no grammatical position, being parenthetical, or circumstantial with «قد» implied.
The clause «لهم فيها أزواج» has no grammatical position, being cut off as resumptive «[Note: Or it is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause «تجري», and likewise the clause «هم فيها خالدون».]» .
The clause «هم فيها خالدون» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl of the pronoun in (لهم), the governing word (ʿāmil) in it being the notion of "being settled" (al-istiqrār).

* Morphology:
(الصالحات) , plural of صالحة, the feminine of الصالح, an active participle of the triliteral صلح, its pattern فاعل.
(جنّات) , plural of جنّة, a primitive (jāmid) noun taken from the verb جنّ meaning "to cover"; it was so called because it is a covered place, or a covering one, owing to the abundance of trees; its pattern is فعلة with fatḥa on the fāʾ and sukūn on the ʿayn.
(الأنهار) , plural of نهر, a primitive noun, its pattern فعل with fatḥa then sukūn, or with two fatḥas.
(أتوا) , in it there is an iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by deletion; its origin is أتيوا with ḍamma on the yāʾ; the ḍamma on the yāʾ was felt heavy, so the yāʾ was made quiescent and the ḍamma transferred to the tāʾ; then, when two quiescent letters met, the yāʾ was deleted; its pattern is فعوا.
(متشابها) , active participle of the five-letter verb تشابه; it is on the pattern of its imperfect, replacing the imperfect prefix with a mīm with ḍamma and putting kasra on the letter before the last.
(أزواج) , plural of زوج, a word used for the man and the woman, each of them being the زوج of the other; in the verse women are meant. زوج has the pattern فعل with fatḥa then sukūn.
(مطهّرة) , its masculine is مطهّر; it is a passive participle of the four-letter verb طهّر, and is on the pattern of its passive imperfect, replacing the imperfect prefix with a mīm with ḍamma.
(خالدون) , plural of خالد, active participle of خلد يخلد, of the class of نصر, its pattern فاعل.

* Rhetoric:
1- Synecdochic metaphor (al-majāz al-mursal): in the words of Allah the Exalted تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهارُ, the relation being locality (maḥalliyya); this is if النهر means the channel of the water; but if it means the water in the channel, then there is no figure in it.
2- The eloquent simile (al-tashbīh al-balīgh): in the words of Allah the Exalted هذَا الَّذِي رُزِقْنا مِنْ قَبْلُ, i.e. this is like that which we were provided before, i.e. before this, in this world; but since the resemblance between them was so firm, He made the one's very self the other's self. The particle of comparison has been omitted from it, and for that reason it is called "eloquent" (balīgh).

* Benefits:
In His words: وَبَشِّرِ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ أَنَّ لَهُمْ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهارُ.
- The dropping of the preposition is regular before the maṣdar-forming «أن» and the emphatic «أنّ» with fatḥa on the hamza: «وَبَشِّرِ ... أَنَّ لَهُمْ جَنَّاتٍ». Likewise the preposition may be omitted on the basis of attested usage (samāʿan), so that the genitive noun becomes accusative and is parsed as accusative by the dropping of the preposition - in the expression of the early grammarians «على نزع الخافض» (accusative by removal of the preposition) - as in the words of Jarīr: تمرّون الديار ولم تعوجوا ... (You pass by the abodes and do not turn aside ...); «الديار» has been made accusative after the dropping of the preposition.

safi-cedvel:26-26.t:
* I'rab:
(إنّ) a particle resembling the verb, for emphasis; (الله) the Name of Majesty, the noun of inna, accusative; (لا) negative; (يستحيي) an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of its nominative being the implied (muqaddar) ḍamma, and its fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun whose implied form is "he" (هو); (أن) a maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle; (يضرب) an imperfect verb, accusative, its fāʿil being "he"; (مثلا) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative; (ما) redundant (zāʾida), for emphasis «[Note: Or an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective, in the position of accusative as a second mafʿūl bihi, i.e.: He strikes as a likeness some thing among things; or it is an adjective of (مثلا) or a badal (substitute), and (بعوضة) is a badal from (ما) .]» , (بعوضة) a badal, an adjective or an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) of (مثلا), accusative like it; (الفاء) conjunction; (ما) a relative noun in the position of accusative, conjoined to «بعوضة» «[Note: Or an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective, in the position of accusative, conjoined to «بعوضة».]» , (فوق) an adverb of place, accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of «ما», and (ها) an attached pronoun in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The interpreted maṣdar formed from (أن) and the verb is in the position of genitive by an omitted (من), attached to (يستحيي) , i.e.: He is not ashamed of striking a likeness.
(الفاء) resumptive; (أمّا) a particle of condition and detailing (tafṣīl); (الذين) a mubtadaʾ (subject) in the position of nominative; (آمنوا) a verb and its fāʿil; (الفاء) connecting the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (يعلمون) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and (الواو) is the fāʿil; (أنّ) as before, and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of accusative as the noun of anna; (الحقّ) the khabar (predicate) of anna, nominative; (من ربّ) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of «الحقّ», and (هم) an attached pronoun in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi. (الواو) conjunction; (أمّا الذين كفروا فيقولون) is parsed like its counterpart.. (ما) an interrogative noun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ; (ذا) a relative noun in the position of nominative as khabar «[Note: It is permissible to parse (ماذا) as a single word: an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as a fronted mafʿūl bihi of the verb «أراد», the implied form being: what thing did Allah intend.]» - i.e.: "so what is it that" - (أراد) a past verb; (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative; (الباء) a preposition; (ها) a particle of alerting (tanbīh); (ذا) a demonstrative in the position of genitive by the bāʾ, attached to (أراد) ; (مثلا) a tamyīz (specification) of the demonstrative, accusative, or a ḥāl, i.e. "being given as a likeness". (يضلّ) an imperfect verb, nominative, its fāʿil a latent pronoun whose implied form is "he"; (الباء) a preposition and (الهاء) an attached pronoun in the position of genitive by the bāʾ, attached to (يضلّ) . (كثيرا) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (الواو) conjunction; (يهدي به كثيرا) is parsed like its preceding counterpart. (الواو) resumptive or circumstantial; (ما) negative; (يضلّ) like the first, and likewise (به) ; (إلا) a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (الفاسقين) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, the sign of its accusative being the yāʾ.
The clause «إنّ الله لا يستحيي ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «لا يستحيي ... » is in the position of nominative as the khabar of inna.
The clause «الذين آمنوا ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «آمنوا» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين) .
The clause «يعلمون ... » is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الذين) «[Note: In this expression the apodosis of (أمّا) must be joined with the fāʾ.. The fāʾ may enter the khabar of a mubtadaʾ, because His words: أما الذين آمنوا فيعلمون ... are originally: "whatever be the case, then those who believe know".. So when (أمّا) was substituted for (مهما) and its verb, the connecting fāʾ was moved to the khabar, in effect. And so in every expression where the mubtadaʾ comes after (أمّا), the fāʾ is joined to the khabar.]» .
The clause «الذين كفروا..» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the second resumptive clause.
The clause «كفروا» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the second relative noun (الذين) .
The clause «يقولون ... » is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the second mubtadaʾ (الذين) «[Note: See remark no. (2) on the previous page.]» The clause «ماذا ... » is in the position of accusative as the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl).
