(ما) may also be a complete indefinite (nakira tāmma), a tamyīz (specification) of the latent pronoun that is the fāʿil of نعم, i.e. "Excellent is it as a thing — its disclosure"; and it [هي] is the one specified for praise (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-madḥ), on the omission of a muḍāf.]»; (هي) a detached pronoun in the position of a nominative as a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), whose khabar (predicate) is the clause نعمّا; this pronoun is on the omission of a muḍāf, the original being إبداؤها (disclosing them); (الواو) conjunction; (ان تخفوها) like إن تبدوا الصدقات; (الواو) conjunction; (تؤتوا) imperfect verb, jussive, conjoined to (تخفوا), and the sign of the jussive is the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil, and (ها) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (الفقراء) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (الفاء) linking the apodosis; (هو) a detached pronoun in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ; (خير) khabar, nominative (marfūʿ); (اللام) preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (خير) or to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of خير; (الواو) resumptive; (يكفّر) imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as "He"; (عن) preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to (يكفّر); (من سيّئات) preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يكفّر), and من is partitive, and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) resumptive; (الله) the Divine Name, mubtadaʾ, nominative; (الباء) preposition; (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of a genitive, attached to (خبير) «[Note: (ما) may be a maṣdar-forming particle, with the interpreted maṣdar in the position of a genitive by the bāʾ, attached to خبير.]»; (تعملون) imperfect verb, nominative ... and (الواو) the fāʿil; (خبير) khabar of the mubtadaʾ, nominative.
The clause «إن تبدوا ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «نعمّا هي» is in the position of a nominative as the fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هي).
The nominal clause «هي ...» is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis of the jussive condition; the fāʾ came on the khabar.
The clause «إن تخفوها» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause إن تبدوا..
The clause «تؤتوها» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause تخفوها.
The clause هو خير لكم is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis of the second jussive condition, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «يكفّر» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «الله ...» خبير has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «تعملون» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the nominal or particle relative (ما).

* Morphology:
(نعمّا): with kasra on the ʿayn according to the original, because its verb is of the bāb فرح. It may come with sukūn on the ʿayn by transferring its vowel — the kasra — to the nūn, and the nūn may remain with fatḥa according to the original.
(تخفوها): it contains the dropping of the hamza and a weak-letter change by deletion (iʿlāl bi-l-ḥadhf), as in (تبدوا).
(تؤتوها): it contains the dropping of the hamza and a weak-letter change by deletion, as in (تبدوا).
(الفقراء): plural of فقير, a ṣifa mushabbaha (resembling adjective) from the three-letter (فقر); its pattern is فعيل, and the plural is فعلاء, with ḍamma on the fāʾ.
(سيئاتكم): plural of سيئة; its pattern is فيعلة. It contains a weak-letter change by substitution (iʿlāl bi-l-qalb): its origin is سيوئة, from ساء يسوء; the wāw and the yāʾ came together in the word, the first of them being quiescent, so the wāw was changed into a yāʾ and assimilated into the second yāʾ (verse 81).

safi-cedvel:272-272.t:
* I'rab:
(ليس) an incomplete (nāqiṣ), non-inflecting (jāmid) past verb; (على) preposition and (الكاف) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); (هدى) the postponed noun of ليس, nominative (marfūʿ), and the sign of the nominative is the implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the alif, and (هم) an attached pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) conjunction; (لكنّ) a particle of rectification (istidrāk) governing the accusative; (الله) the Divine Name, the noun of لكنّ, accusative (manṣūb); (يهدي) imperfect verb, nominative, and the sign of the nominative is the implied ḍamma on the yāʾ, and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as "He"; (من) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of an accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (يشاء) imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, implied as "He", i.e. Allah; (الواو) resumptive; (ما تنفقوا من خير) the i'rab of its parallel has been given «[Note: In verse (270) of this sūra.]»; (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (لأنفس) preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. هو; (الواو) parenthetical (iʿtirāḍiyya); (ما) negative; (تنفقون) imperfect verb, nominative.. and the wāw is the fāʿil; (إلّا) particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (ابتغاء) mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), accusative «[Note: Or a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "seeking".]»; (وجه) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (الله) the Divine Name, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (الواو) conjunction; (ما تنفقوا من خير) the i'rab of its parallel has been given «[Note: Or a maṣdar in the place of a ḥāl, i.e. "seeking".]» «[Translator's note: so in the source; this footnote repeats the one on ابتغاء and does not fit here.]»; (يوفّ) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the apodosis, and the sign of the jussive is the dropping of the weak letter, and it is passive, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is understood from the context of the verse, i.e. "its reward"; (إلى) preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to (يوفّ); (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya); (أنتم) a detached pronoun in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ; (لا) negative; (تظلمون) imperfect verb, passive, nominative.. and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil.
The clause «ليس عليك هداهم» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «لكنّ الله يهدي» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «يهدي» is in the position of a nominative as the khabar of لكنّ.
The clause «يشاء» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (من).
The clause «ما تنفقوا من خير» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «(هو) لأنفسكم» is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis of the jussive condition, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «ما تنفقون إلّا ...» has no grammatical position: parenthetical.
The clause «ما تنفقوا من خير» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «يوفّ إليكم» has no grammatical position: the apodosis of a jussive condition not joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «أنتم لا تظلمون» is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl of the genitive pronoun of address «[Note: The wāw may be resumptive, and the clause then has no grammatical position, being resumptive.]».
The clause «لا تظلمون» is in the position of a nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أنتم).

* Morphology:
(خير): a non-derived (jāmid) noun meaning wealth; it is also the maṣdar of خار.
(يوفّ): it contains a weak-letter change by deletion (iʿlāl bi-l-ḥadhf) because of the jussive; its pattern is يفعّ, with ḍamma on the yāʾ and fatḥa on the doubled ʿayn.

safi-cedvel:273-273.t:
* I'rab:
(للفقراء) preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate), with the mubtadaʾ (subject) implied, its implied form being الصدقات (the charities) «[Note: Or attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being اعجبوا (al-ʿUkbarī).]»; (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of a genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of الفقراء; (أحصروا) past verb, passive, indeclinable on the ḍamma.. and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (في سبيل) preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أحصروا); (الله) the Divine Name, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (لا) negative; (يستطيعون) imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ).
And the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (ضربا) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb); (في الأرض) preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a naʿt of (ضربا) «[Translator's note: the source has a stray closing quotation mark here.]»; (يحسب) imperfect verb, nominative, and (هم) an attached pronoun, first mafʿūl bihi; (الجاهل) fāʿil, nominative; (أغنياء) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative, barred from tanwīn because it is assimilated to the feminine nouns ending in a prolonged alif, on the pattern أفعلاء; (من التعفّف) preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يحسبهم), and من is causal «[Note: The prepositional phrase is in the place of a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose); the object did not come in the accusative because the agent of the verb and of the maṣdar differ.]»; (تعرف) imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as "you", and (هم) mafʿūl bihi; (بسيما) preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (تعرفهم), and the sign of the genitive is the implied (muqaddar) kasra on the alif, and (هم) muḍāf ilayhi; (لا) negative; (يسألون) imperfect verb, nominative.. and the wāw is the fāʿil; (الناس) first mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and the second object is implied, i.e. "wealth" or "charity"; (إلحافا) a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial) «[Note: Or a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar, since it is synonymous with it, i.e. "they do not importune in asking with importunity"; or it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi.]»; (الواو) resumptive; (ما تنفقوا من خير) its i'rab has been given «[Note: In verse (272), or in its parallel (270).]»; (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb, for emphasis; (الله) the Divine Name, the noun of إنّ, accusative; (الباء) preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to (عليم), the khabar of أنّ «[Translator's note: so in the source, for إنّ.]», nominative.-
The clause (الصدقات) للفقراء has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «أحصروا» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «لا يستطيعون» is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl of the agent of أحصروا.
The clause «يحسبهم الجاهل..» is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl of the agent of أحصروا «1».
The clause «تعرفهم..» is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl of the agent of أحصروا «2».
The clause «لا يسألون الناس ...» is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl of the agent of أحصروا «3». «[Translator's note: the footnotes marked 1–3 are not present in the source text.]»
The clause «ما تنفقوا من خير» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «إنّ الله به عليم» is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis of the jussive condition, joined with the fāʾ.

* Morphology:
(ضربا): an aurally transmitted (samāʿī) maṣdar of the verb ضرب — the second bāb; its pattern is فعل, with fatḥa then sukūn.
(الجاهل): active participle from جهل يجهل, of the bāb فرح; its pattern is فاعل (see verse 67 of this sūra).
(التعفّف): a regular (qiyāsī) maṣdar from the verb تعفّف; its pattern is تفعّل, with ḍamma on the doubled ʿayn.
(سيما): with a short final alif (maqṣūr), and it may be lengthened, in which case the hamza is for assimilation (ilḥāq), not for the feminine. The pattern of سيما is عفلا, with the ʿayn of the word placed before its fāʾ, because the origin is from الوسم; it is from السمة, i.e. the mark. The wāw came after a kasra, so it was changed into a yāʾ, and it was said سيما.
(إلحافا): a regular maṣdar from the verb ألحف, meaning ألحّ (to importune); its pattern is إفعال, with kasra on the hamza.

* Rhetoric:
His saying, Exalted is He: لا يَسْئَلُونَ النَّاسَ إِلْحافاً..
If you say: this implies that they used to ask gently, although He said يحسبهم الجاهل أغنياء من التعفف — I reply: what is meant is the negation of both the qualified thing and the qualification together, as in His saying, Exalted is He: لا ذَلُولٌ تُثِيرُ الْأَرْضَ.
This is one of the most original devices of eloquence, and the scholars of bayān call it "negating a thing by affirming it": what is negated in the outward wording is importunity in asking, not asking itself, figuratively; while what is negated in the inner sense of the words, in reality, is asking itself, whether importunate or otherwise.

safi-cedvel:274-274.t:
* I'rab:
(الذين ينفقون أموالهم) its i'rab has been given «[Note: In verse (262) of this sūra.]»; (بالليل) preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (ينفقون); (الواو) conjunction; (النهار) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to الليل, genitive like it; (سرّا) a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial) «[Note: Or a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar, since it is its description.]»; (الواو) conjunction; (علانية) maʿṭūf to (سرّا), accusative (manṣūb) like it; (الفاء) redundant (zāʾida), because the relative resembles a condition; (اللام) preposition and (هم) an attached pronoun in the position of a genitive by the lām, attached to an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); (أجر) postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), and (هم) muḍāf ilayhi; (عند) adverb of place, accusative, attached to an omitted ḥāl of أجرهم; (ربّ) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, and (هم) muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) conjunction; (لا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون) its i'rab has been given «[Note: In verse (262) of this sūra.]».
The clause «الذين ينفقون..» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «ينفقون أموالهم» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «لهم أجرهم» is in the position of a nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الذين).
The clause «لا خوف عليهم» is in the position of a nominative, conjoined to the clause لهم أجرهم.
The clause «لا هم يحزنون» is in the position of a nominative, conjoined to the clause لا خوف عليهم.
The clause «يحزنون» is in the position of a nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هم).

* Morphology:
(سرّا): a noun of the maṣdar (ism maṣdar) from the verb أسرّ (see verse 235 of this sūra).
(علانية): an aurally transmitted (samāʿī) maṣdar of the verb علن, of the bāb نصر, ضرب, فرح and كرم.. its pattern is فعالية.

* Rhetoric:
In the noble verse there is one of the devices of rhetoric, namely correspondence (al-muqābala), since antithesis (al-ṭibāq) is repeated between night and day and between secret and open.

safi-cedvel:275-275.t:
* I'rab:
(الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); (يأكلون) imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ).. and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (الربا) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), and the sign of the accusative is the implied (muqaddar) fatḥa on the alif; (لا) negative; (يقومون) imperfect verb like يأكلون; (إلّا) particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (الكاف) preposition «[Note: Or a noun meaning مثل (like), in the position of an accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar, its implied form being "a rising like the rising of the one whom Satan has struck"; or in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).]»; (ما) a maṣdar-forming particle; (يقوم) imperfect verb, nominative; (الذي) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of a nominative as fāʿil; (يتخبّط) like يقوم, and (الهاء) mafʿūl bihi; (الشيطان) fāʿil, nominative; (من المسّ) preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يتخبّطه) or to (يقوم), and من here is causal.
The interpreted maṣdar (ما يقوم) is in the position of a genitive by the kāf, attached to an omitted maṣdar that is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) — or to a ḥāl — i.e. "a rising like the rising of the one who.." — or "rising like the rising of the one who.." (ذا) a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ, and (اللام) for distance and (الكاف) for address; (الباء) a preposition of causation; (أنّ) a particle resembling the verb, and (هم) an attached pronoun in the position of an accusative as the noun of أنّ; (قالوا) past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma..
and the wāw is the fāʿil.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّهم قالوا) is in the position of a genitive by the bāʾ, attached to an omitted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (ذلك).
(إنّما) a restraining particle and the restrained particle (kāffa wa-makfūfa), without governing effect; (البيع) mubtadaʾ, nominative; (مثل) khabar, nominative; (الربا) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, and the sign of the genitive is the implied kasra on the alif; (الواو) resumptive; (أحلّ) past verb; (الله) the Divine Name, fāʿil, nominative; (البيع) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (الواو) conjunction; (حرّم الربا) like أحلّ البيع; (الفاء) resumptive; (من) a jussive conditional noun, indeclinable, in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ; (جاء) past verb, in the position of a jussive, and (الهاء) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (موعظة) fāʿil, nominative; (من ربّ) preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted naʿt of موعظة, and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi; (الفاء) conjunction; (انتهى) past verb, indeclinable on the implied fatḥa on the alif, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as "he"; (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (اللام) preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to an omitted fronted khabar; (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of a nominative as a postponed mubtadaʾ; (سلف) like أحلّ, and the fāʿil is "it", and it is the referent pronoun (ʿāʾid); (الواو) conjunction; (أمر) mubtadaʾ, nominative, and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (إلى الله) preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ; (الواو) conjunction; (من عاد) like من جاء; (الفاء) linking the apodosis; (أولاء) a demonstrative, indeclinable on the kasra, in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ, and (الكاف) a particle of address; (أصحاب) khabar, nominative; (النار) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (هم) a detached pronoun in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ; (في) preposition and (ها) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to (خالدون), which is a khabar, nominative, and the sign of the nominative is the wāw.
The clause «الذين يأكلون..» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يأكلون الربا» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «لا يقومون» is in the position of a nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الذين).
The clause «يقوم الذي ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the particle relative (ما).
The clause «يتخبّطه الشيطان» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative (الذي).
The clause «ذلك بأنّهم..» has no grammatical position: causal.
The clause «قالوا..» is in the position of a nominative as the khabar of (أنّ).
The clause «إنّما البيع مثل الربا» is in the position of an accusative as the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «أحلّ الله البيع» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «حرّم الربا» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause أحلّ الله البيع.
The clause «من جاءه موعظة» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «جاءه موعظة» is in the position of a nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) «1».
The clause «انتهى» is in the position of a nominative, conjoined to the clause جاءه موعظة.
The clause «له ما سلف» is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis of the jussive condition, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «سلف» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative (ما).
The clause «أمره إلى الله» is in the position of a jussive, conjoined to the clause له ما سلف.
The clause «من عاد» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause من جاءه ...
The clause «عاد» is in the position of a nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) «2». «[Translator's note: the footnotes marked 1 and 2 are not present in the source text.]»
The clause «أولئك أصحاب» is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis of the jussive condition, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «هم فيها خالدون» is in the position of a nominative as a second khabar of the mubtadaʾ أولئك «[Note: Or in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl of أصحاب.]».

* Morphology:
(الربا): the alif is originally a wāw, because it is from ربا يربو; for this reason the alif is written tall. The wāw had a vowel after a fatḥa, so it was changed into an alif.
(المسّ): the noun from مسّ يمسّ, of the bāb نصر, meaning madness.
(موعظة): a mīmī maṣdar (verbal noun) from وعظ, with an additional tāʾ at its end; its pattern is مفعلة, with kasra on the ʿayn, because its verb is weak in the fāʾ (assimilated), [the fāʾ being] dropped in the imperfect (see verse 66 of this sūra).
(قالوا): it contains a weak-letter change by substitution (iʿlāl bi-l-qalb): the wāw was changed into an alif because it came with a vowel after a fatḥa; its origin is قولوا (verse 14).
(عاد): it contains a weak-letter change by substitution: the wāw was changed into an alif because it came with a vowel after a fatḥa; its origin is عود.

* Rhetoric:
«إِلَّا كَما يَقُومُ الَّذِي يَتَخَبَّطُهُ الشَّيْطانُ».
1- Allegorical simile (al-tashbīh al-tamthīlī): He likened those who consume usury, when they come out of their graves, to the rising of the one stricken and seized by a fit, who has been afflicted with madness — just as it is said of one who hurries with erratic movements: "he has gone mad."
«قالُوا إِنَّمَا الْبَيْعُ مِثْلُ الرِّبا».
2- They wanted to string the two on a single thread, since both lead to profit. They made usury the base case of permissibility and likened sale to it, for exaggeration. This is what is called in the science of rhetoric the reversed simile (al-tashbīh al-maqlūb).
The simile may also be not reversed, based on their understanding that sale was made lawful only for the sake of gain and benefit, and that this is certain in usury and merely supposed in other [transactions].

semin-durr:1-1.t:
If it is said that the disjointed letters (al-ḥurūf al-muqaṭṭaʿa) at the openings of the surahs are the names of the letters of the alphabet — meaning that mīm is a name for "ma", and ʿayn a name for "ʿa" — and that their purpose is to inform them that this Qur'an is composed of the same kind of material from which you compose your speech, yet you are unable to match it, then they have no grammatical position in that case; they were brought only for this purpose and were cast out like the names of numbers, e.g. "wāḥid, ithnān" (one, two). This is the soundest of the three views; I mean that concerning nouns about which nothing is predicated and which are not themselves predicated there are three views. The first: what has preceded. The second: that they are declinable (muʿraba), meaning that they are fit for declension, but a condition is missing, namely being placed in a construction (tarkīb); al-Zamakhsharī inclined to this. The third: that they are suspended (mawqūfa), neither declinable nor indeclinable.
Or if it is said that they are the names of the surahs that open with them, or that they are parts of some of the names of Allah the Exalted, part of which was dropped and these letters remain from them pointing to them — which is the view of Ibn ʿAbbās, as when he said: the mīm is from ʿalīm (All-Knowing) and the ṣād from ṣādiq (Truthful) — then they have a grammatical position in that case, and the nominative and the genitive are possible / [Translator's note: the source says "the nominative and the genitive", but goes on to treat nominative, accusative and genitive; the accusative seems to have dropped from the text here]. The nominative is on one of two grounds: either as a mubtadaʾ (subject), or as a khabar (predicate), as will be explained in detail. The accusative is also on one of two grounds: either by an implied fitting verb, its implied form being "Read: alif lām mīm", or by dropping the particle of oath, as the poet said:
93 - إذا ما الخبزُ تَأْدِمُه بلَحْمٍ ... فذاك أمانةَ الله الثريدُ
(When you season bread with meat — that, by the trust of Allah, is tharīd.)
He means "wa-amānati llāh" (by the trust of Allah); likewise these letters: Allah the Exalted swore by them. Al-Zamakhsharī rejected this view with something whose meaning is: «القرآن» in {ص والقرآن ذِي الذكر} [Ṣād: 1] and «القلم» in {ن والقلم} [al-Qalam: 1] are sworn by, since the genitive appears overtly in them; so the wāw that enters upon them must be either for the oath or for conjunction. The first entails something to be avoided, namely combining two oaths for one thing sworn to — he said: "and they consider that repugnant" — and the second is not allowed because the genitive appears in what follows it, while the assumption is that you have taken what it is conjoined to as being in the position of the accusative. This is a clear refutation, unless it is said: they are in the position of the accusative except where the genitive appears after them, as in the two places mentioned and {حم والكتاب} [al-Zukhruf: 1-2] and {ق والقرآن} [Qāf: 1]; but whoever holds that view did not distinguish one place from another, so the refutation binds him.
The genitive is on one ground only, namely that they are sworn by, the particle of oath being omitted while its effect remains, as in their saying "Allāhi la-afʿalanna" (by Allah, I shall surely do it). Abū l-Qāsim al-Zamakhsharī and Abū l-Baqāʾ allowed this. It is weak, because that is one of the special properties of the Majestic Name, which nothing else shares with it.
To sum up what has preceded: in «الم» and the like there are six views: that they have no grammatical position; or that they have a position, which is the nominative as mubtadaʾ or as khabar, the accusative by an implied verb or by dropping the particle of oath, and the genitive by an implied particle of oath.
As for «ذلك الكتاب»: «ذلك» may be a second mubtadaʾ and «الكتاب» its khabar, the clause being the khabar of «ألم», the demonstrative serving as the link (rabṭ). «الم» may be a mubtadaʾ and «ذلك» its khabar, with «الكتاب» a naʿt (adjective) of «ذلك», or a badal (substitute) for it, or an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition). Or «ألم» may be a mubtadaʾ and «ذلك» a second mubtadaʾ, with «الكتاب» either a naʿt of it, a badal from it, or an ʿaṭf bayān for it,
and {لاَ رَيْبَ فِيهِ} the khabar of the second mubtadaʾ, which together with its khabar is the khabar of the first. «ألم» may also be the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "This is alif lām mīm", so that it is a clause independent in itself; «ذلك» is then a second mubtadaʾ and «الكتابُ» its khabar; or it may be a naʿt of it, a badal, or a bayān, with {لاَ رَيْبَ فِيهِ} being the khabar of «ذلك». Or «الكتابُ» may be a khabar of «ذلك» and {لاَ رَيْبَ فِيهِ} a second khabar; this is questionable in that the khabar is multiple while one of the two is a clause, but the apparent view is that it is allowed, as in the saying of the Exalted: {فَإِذَا هِيَ حَيَّةٌ تسعى} [Ṭā Hā: 20], if it is said that «تَسْعَى» is a khabar; but if it is made a naʿt, then no.
His saying {لاَ رَيْبَ فِيهِ}: it may be a khabar, as has been explained, and this clause may be in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), the governor in it being the sense of pointing. «لا» is the lā of generic negation, treated in its governing effect like its opposite «إنَّ». Its noun is either declinable or indeclinable: it is built (mabnī) on what it would have been made accusative with when it is a single (mufrad) indefinite noun. The reason for its being indeclinable is that it contains the sense of a particle, namely the «مِنْ» of comprehensiveness (istighrāqiyya); evidence of this is its overt appearance in the poet's saying:
94 - فقام يَذُوْدُ الناسَ عنها بسيفِه ... فقال: ألا لا مِن سبيلٍ إلى هندِ
(He stood driving people away from her with his sword, and said: "Indeed, there is no way at all to Hind.")
It has also been said that it is indeclinable because it is compounded with it as "khamsata ʿashara" (fifteen) is compounded; that is unsound, and its explanation is outside this book.
Al-Zajjāj claimed that the vowel of «لا رجلَ» and the like is a vowel of declension, and the tanwīn was only dropped for lightness; evidence of this, he held, is the return to this original form under poetic necessity, as in:
95 - ألا رجلاً جزاه اللهُ خيراً ... يَدُلُّ على مُحَصِّلَةٍ تَبيتُ
(Is there not a man — may Allah reward him with good — who will guide [me] to a capable woman who will stay the night?)
He has no evidence in it, because the implied form is: "Will you not show me a man?"
If it is not single — by which I mean the muḍāf and what resembles it — it is declined in the accusative, e.g. «لا خيراً من زيد» (none better than Zayd). It has no effect at all on a definite noun. As for examples such as:
96 - تُبَكِّي على زيدٍ ولا زيدَ مثلُهُ ... بريءٌ من الحُمَّى سليمُ الجوانِحِ
(You weep for Zayd — and there is no Zayd like him, free of fever, sound of ribs.)
and the saying of another: 97 - أرى الحاجاتِ عند أبي خُبَيْبٍ ... نَكِدْنَ ولا أُمَيَّةَ في البلادِ
(I see that needs, with Abū Khubayb, have become hard to fulfil, and there is no Umayya in the land.)
and the saying of another:
98 - لا هيثَم الليلةَ للمَطِّي ...
(No Haytham tonight for the mounts.)
and his saying, upon him be peace: "There is no Quraysh after today; when Kisrā perishes there will be no Kisrā after him" — these are interpreted [i.e. not taken at face value].
«ريبَ» is its noun, and its khabar may be the preposition and its genitive noun, namely «فيه»; however, the Banū Tamīm hardly ever mention its khabar, so it is preferable that it be omitted, its implied form being "lā rayba kāʾinun" (there is no doubt existing); the pause on «ريب» is then complete. Sometimes its noun is omitted and its khabar remains; they said: "lā ʿalayka", i.e. "lā baʾsa ʿalayka" (no harm upon you). The doctrine of Sībawayh is that it and its noun are in the position of the nominative as a subject (bi-l-ibtidāʾ) and it has no effect on the khabar; the doctrine of al-Akhfash is that its noun is in the position of the nominative and it governs the khabar.
It has many rules and widespread subdivisions mentioned in grammar.
Know that «لا» is a word shared between negation — in which it is of two kinds: a kind in which it negates the genus and so acts like «إنَّ», as has preceded, and a kind in which it negates unity (al-waḥda) and then acts like laysa — and prohibition and supplication, in which it puts a single verb in the jussive; and it sometimes comes as redundant (zāʾida), as has preceded in {وَلاَ الضآلين} [al-Fātiḥa: 7].
«ذلك» is a demonstrative: its noun is «ذا», the lām is for distance and the kāf for address. It has three ranks: near, which has the form free of lām and kāf, e.g. dhā, dhī, hādhā, hādhī; middle, which has the form joined to the particle of address, e.g. dhāka, dhayka, tayka; and far, which has / the form joined to lām and kāf, e.g. dhālika, tilka. The lām may not be brought except with the kāf. The particle of drawing attention (hā) may enter all demonstratives except with the lām, where it is barred because of length. Some grammarians mentioned only two ranks for it: near and other.
Grammarians differed about dhā: is it triliteral in its original form, or is its origin a single letter? The first is the view of the Basrans. They then differed: are its middle radical and final radical both yāʾ, so that it belongs to the pattern of ḥayiya, or is its middle radical wāw and final radical yāʾ, so that it belongs to the pattern of ṭawaytu? Then its final radical was dropped for lightness and the middle radical was turned into alif because it was vowelled and preceded by a fatḥa. All this is by way of exercise; otherwise it is indeclinable, and morphological derivation (taṣrīf) does not enter the indeclinable.
The demonstrative of the distant was used here only to magnify the thing pointed to; from this is:
99 - أقولُ له والرمحُ يَأطُر مَتْنَه ... تأمَّلْ خِفافاً إنَّني أنا ذلكا
(I say to him, while the spear bends his back: "Look well at Khufāf — I am that one!")
Or because, when it came down from heaven to earth, it was pointed to with the demonstrative of the distant; [or because it had been promised to His Prophet, upon him be peace; or it points to what He decreed and ordained in the Preserved Tablet. In the expression of the exegetes, "dhālika" points to the absent, by which they mean the distant; otherwise, what is pointed to can only be present, either mentally or to the senses, so they expressed what is mentally present as "absent", i.e. to the senses. The accurate statement is what I have mentioned to you.]
«الكتاب» is originally a maṣdar (verbal noun); the Exalted said: {كِتَابَ الله عَلَيْكُمْ} [al-Nisāʾ: 24]. It is sometimes meant as "what is written"; [the poet] said:
100 - بَشَرْتُ عيالي إذ رأيتُ صحيفةً ... أَتَتْكَ من الحَجَّاج يُتْلى كتابُها
(I gave my household good news when I saw a page that came to you from al-Ḥajjāj, its writing being read out.)
And similarly:
101 - تُؤَمِّلُ رَجْعَةً مني وفيها ... كتابٌ مثلَ ما لَصِق الغِراءُ
(She hopes for my return, while in it [i.e. the divorce] is a written decree that sticks as glue sticks.)
The root meaning of this material is gathering together; from it is katība (a squadron of the army), and "katabtu l-qirba": I sewed up the water-skin; al-kutba, with ḍamma on the kāf, is the stitch, plural kutab; [the poet] said:
102 - وَفْراءَ غَرْفيَّةٍ أَثْأى خوارِزُها ... مُشَلْشِلٌ ضَيَّعَتْهُ بينها الكُتَبُ
(A full [water-skin] of tanned hide, whose stitchers spoiled its seams; trickling, the stitches between them have let it leak.)
And "katabtu l-dābba": [when you join the two lips of its womb with a ring or a thong]; [the poet] said:
103 - لاَ تأْمَنَنَّ فزاريَّاً حَلَلْتَ به ... على قُلوصِك واكتبْها بأَسْيارِ
(Never trust a man of Fazāra with whom you stay, with your young she-camel — fasten her shut with thongs.)
Writing (kitāba) in usage is joining some letters of the alphabet to others.
«الرَّيْب» is doubt accompanied by suspicion; [the poet] said: 104 - ليس في الحقِ يا أُمَيمةُ رَيْبٌ ... إنما الريبُ ما يقول الكَذوبُ
(There is no doubt in the truth, O Umayma; doubt is only what the liar says.)
Its true sense, as al-Zamakhsharī said, is disquiet and agitation of the soul; from it is the ḥadīth: "Leave what makes you uneasy (yarībuka) for what does not make you uneasy", and that he passed by a frightened gazelle and said: "Let no one disturb it (lā yuribhu aḥad)". So the statement of whoever says "rayb is doubt absolutely" is not good; rather it is more specific than doubt, as has preceded.
Some said: rayb has three meanings. The first: doubt. Ibn al-Zibaʿrā said:
105 - ليسَ في الحقِ يا أميمةُ رَيْبٌ ...
(There is no doubt in the truth, O Umayma.)
The second is suspicion; Jamīl Buthayna said:
106 - بُثَيْنَةُ قالت: يا جميلُ أَرَبْتَني ... فقلت: كلانا يابُثَيْنُ مُريبُ
(Buthayna said: "O Jamīl, you have made me suspicious." I said: "Each of us, O Buthayn, arouses suspicion.")
The third is need; [the poet] said:
107 - قََضَيْنا من تِهامةَ كلَّ ريبٍ ... وخَيْبَرَ ثم أَجْمَعْنا السيوفا
(We fulfilled every need from Tihāma and Khaybar, then we resolved upon the swords.)
His saying {هُدًى لِّلْمُتَّقِينَ}: several views are possible in it. It may be a mubtadaʾ with «فيه» as its khabar placed before it, if we say the khabar of «لا» is omitted; and if we say «فيه» is the khabar of «لا», its khabar is omitted, indicated by the khabar of «لا», its implied form being "lā rayba fīhi, fīhi hudan" (no doubt in it; in it is guidance). It may be the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "huwa hudan" (it is guidance). It may be a second khabar of «ذلك», on the basis that «الكتاب» is a naʿt, badal or bayān and «لا ريب» a first khabar. It may be a third khabar of «ذلك», on the basis that «الكتاب» is a first khabar and «لا ريبَ» a second khabar. It may be in the accusative as a ḥāl from «ذلك» or from «الكتاب», the governor in it on both readings being the demonstrative. It may be a ḥāl from the pronoun in «فيه», the governor being the verbal sense contained in the preposition and its genitive noun. Making it a ḥāl from what has preceded is either by way of hyperbole, as though it were guidance itself, or by omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "dhā hudan" (possessing guidance), or by the maṣdar taking the place of the active participle. Likewise every maṣdar that occurs as a khabar, naʿt or ḥāl has these three views, the most preponderant being the first. They also allowed «فيه» to be a naʿt of «ريب», so that it is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted [word], and to be attached to «ريب» itself; but this is problematic, because it would then become "lengthened" (muṭawwal), and the noun of «لا» when lengthened is declined — unless what they mean is that it is governed by what «ريبَ» indicates, not by «ريب» itself.
The meaning of «الهدى» has preceded at the saying of the Exalted: {اهدنا الصراط المستقيم} [al-Fātiḥa: 6]. «هُدَى» is a maṣdar on the pattern fuʿal; they said: no maṣdar has come on this pattern except surā, bukā and hudā; but others have come, namely "laqītuhu luqā" (I met him); [the poet] said:
108 - وقد زعموا حِلْماً لُقاك ولم أَزِدْ ... بحمدِ الذي أَعْطَاك حِلْماً ولا عَقْلا
(They claimed that meeting you [brings] forbearance, yet — praise be to Him who gave you [what He gave] — I gained no increase in forbearance or in intellect.)
Hudā has two usages: masculine, and al-Liḥyānī mentioned nothing else; al-Farrāʾ said: "Some of the Banū Asad make it feminine and say: hādhihi hudan."
«في» means containment (ẓarfiyya), literally or figuratively, e.g. "Zayd is in the house", {وَلَكُمْ فِي القصاص حَيَاةٌ} [al-Baqara: 197] [Translator's note: this verse is al-Baqara: 179]. It has other meanings: accompaniment, e.g. {ادخلوا في أُمَمٍ} [al-Aʿrāf: 38]; causation: "A woman entered the Fire because of (fī) a cat"; agreeing with «على»: {وَلأُصَلِّبَنَّكُمْ فِي جُذُوعِ النخل} [Ṭā Hā: 71]; [agreeing with] the bāʾ: {يَذْرَؤُكُمْ فِيهِ} [al-Shūrā: 11], i.e. by means of it; and comparison: {فَمَا مَتَاعُ الحياة الدنيا فِي الآخرة} [al-Tawba: 38].
The hāʾ in «فيه» originally has ḍamma, as has preceded, since the hāʾ of allusion (the pronoun) originally has ḍamma; if it is preceded by a quiescent yāʾ or a kasra, those other than the Ḥijāzīs give it kasra. Ḥamza read «لأهلهُ امكثوا», and Ḥafṣ in «عاهد عليهُ الله» and «وما أنسانيهُ إلا», according to the dialect of the Ḥijāz. The well-known [practice] in it — when it is not followed by a quiescent and what precedes it is quiescent, e.g. fīhi, minhu — is ikhtilās (shortening the vowel), and ishbāʿ (lengthening) is allowed; Ibn Kathīr read with it. If what precedes it is vowelled, it is lengthened, and it may be shortened or made quiescent; some of that has been read, as will come in detail.
«للمتقين» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «هُدَى». It has also been said: it is a naʿt of «هدى», so it is attached to an omitted [word], and its position then is either nominative or accusative according to what has preceded about the noun it qualifies, i.e. "hudan kāʾinun" or "kāʾinan li-l-muttaqīn" (guidance existing for the God-fearing). The best of all these preceding views is that each clause be independent in itself: «ألم» is a clause if it is said to be the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, «ذلك الكتاب» is a clause, «لا ريبَ» is a clause, and «فيه هدى» is a clause. The conjunction was left out only because of the strength of the connection, since each clause is attached to what precedes it, taking hold of its neck, with an attachment that does not allow separation by conjunction. Al-Zamakhsharī said something whose meaning is: If you say: why was the adverbial not placed before «الريب», as it was placed before «الغَوْل» in the saying of the Exalted {لاَ فِيهَا غَوْلٌ} [al-Ṣāffāt: 47]? I say: because placing the adverbial first there conveys that what is negated of it is not negated of others; the meaning is: there is no ghawl (headache/intoxication) in it as there is in the wines of this world. Had the adverbial been placed first here, it would have conveyed this meaning, namely that other heavenly books have doubt in them, and that is not intended. It seems that what Abū l-Qāsim al-Zamakhsharī mentioned is built on his view that placing first conveys specification (ikhtiṣāṣ), as though the meaning were that the wine of the Hereafter alone has ghawl negated of it, unlike others; and there is room for dispute in this.
Someone tried to refute him by another route, namely that the Arabs also / described the wine of this world as not overpowering the mind; ʿAlqama said:
109 - تَشْفي الصُّداعَ ولا يُؤْذيكَ صالِبُها ... وَلاَ يُخَالِطُها في الرأسِ تَدْويمُ
(It cures the headache, its fever does not harm you, and no dizziness mingles with it in the head.)
How far this is from refuting him, since no account is taken of this speaker's description.
If it is said: doubt about the Qur'an has been found in many people, while the saying of the Exalted {لاَ رَيْبَ فِيهِ} negates that — the answer is in three ways. The first: what is negated is its being an object of doubt, meaning that it has with it such proofs that if a fair-minded seeker of truth contemplated them he would not doubt it; no account is taken of the doubt of whoever has doubt, because he has not looked properly, so his doubt is not counted.
The second: it is restricted, and the meaning is: there is no doubt in it among the believers. The third: it is a statement whose meaning is a prohibition, i.e. do not doubt it. The first is best.
«المتقين» is the plural of muttaqin; its origin is muttaqiyīn with two yāʾs, the first being the final radical of the word and the second the plural marker. The kasra was deemed heavy on the final radical, i.e. the first yāʾ, so it was dropped; two quiescents then met, so one of them, the first, was dropped. Muttaqin is from ittaqā yattaqī, and it is on the pattern muftaʿil from wiqāya (protection); however, it is regular for wāw and yāʾ, when they are the first radical and the tāʾ of iftiʿāl comes after them, to be replaced by tāʾ, e.g. ittaʿada from waʿd, and ittasara from yusr; doing that with hamza is anomalous (shādhdh): they said ittazara and ittakala from izār and akl.
Iftaʿala has twelve meanings: taking (ittikhādh), e.g. ittaqā; acting as a cause (tasabbub), e.g. iʿtamala; the agent's acting upon himself, e.g. iḍṭaraba; choosing, e.g. intakhaba; snatching, e.g. istalaba; reflexive compliance (muṭāwaʿa) with afʿala, e.g. intaṣafa, the reflexive of anṣafa; reflexive compliance with faʿʿala, e.g. "ʿammamtuhu fa-ʿtamma" (I put a turban on him and he wore a turban); agreeing with tafāʿala, tafaʿʿala and istafʿala, e.g. ijtawara, iqtasama and iʿtaṣara, meaning tajāwara, taqassama and istaʿṣama; agreeing with the bare form, e.g. iqtadara meaning qadara; and dispensing with it, e.g. "istalama l-ḥajar" (he touched the Stone), for which no bare form is uttered. [Translator's note: the author announces twelve meanings, but the list as given contains fewer explicitly separated items.]
Wiqāya is extreme preservation and intense guarding against what is disliked; from it is "faras wāqin", a horse whose hoof guards itself against the slightest thing that hits it. It has also been said: in the original language it is paucity of speech; in the ḥadīth: "The God-fearing one is bridled." From [the sense of] preservation is his saying:
110 - سَقَطَ النَّصِيفُ ولم تُرِدْ إسقاطَه ... فتناوَلَتْه واتَّقَتْنَا باليَدِ
(The veil fell, though she did not mean to let it fall; she took it up and shielded herself from us with her hand.)
Another said:
111 - فَأَلْقَتْ قناعاً دونَه الشمسُ واتَّقَتْ ... بأحسنِ مَوْصولينِ كَفٍّ ومِعْصَمِ
(She cast a veil before which the sun [is lesser], and shielded herself with the finest of two joined things, a palm and a wrist.)

semin-durr:13-13.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمْ: آمِنُواْ}: the discussion of it is like the discussion of its counterpart before it. (آمِنُوا) is a verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the clause is in the position of nominative because it stands in place of the fāʿil, as was set out under {وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمْ لاَ تُفْسِدُواْ} [al-Baqara: 11]; the views mentioned there recur here, so there is no need to mention them again.
The kāf in His saying {كَمَآ آمَنَ الناس} is in the position of accusative. Most of the parsers make it a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), the implied form being: "believe with a belief like the belief of the people". They say the same about «سِرْ عليه حثيثاً» ("travel on it swiftly"), i.e. "a swift travelling". This is not the doctrine of Sībawayh; his doctrine in this and similar cases is that it is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the implied maṣdar understood from the preceding verb.
What compelled Sībawayh to this is that omitting the qualified noun and putting the adjective in its place is permitted only in limited places, and this is not one of them. Those places are: that the adjective be specific to the qualified noun, as in "I passed by a writer"; or that it occur as a khabar (predicate), as in "Zayd is standing"; or as a ḥāl, as in "Zayd came riding"; or as an adjective of an adverb (ẓarf), as in "I sat near you"; or that it be used as nouns are used — and this is memorised and not used as a basis for analogy — as in «الأبطح» and «الأبرق». Outside these places omission of the qualified noun is not permitted. Do you not see that Sībawayh disallowed «ألا ماءَ ولو باردا» [as a naʿt], even though something indicating the qualified noun precedes it, and allowed «ألا ماءَ ولو بارداً» because it is accusative as a ḥāl? [Translator's note: the two phrases are identical in the text; the distinction is between parsing «بارداً» as an adjective of an omitted noun (disallowed) and as a ḥāl (allowed).]
And «ما» is maṣdariyya (infinitival), in the position of genitive by the kāf, and «آمَنَ الناسُ» is its ṣila (relative clause). Know that infinitival «ما» is connected to a past verb or to an inflecting imperfect; its connection to a non-inflecting verb is anomalous, as in the poet's saying:
191 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... بما لَسْتُما أهلَ الخيانةِ والغَدْرِ
(…because you two are not people of treachery and betrayal.)
Is it connected to nominal clauses? There is disagreement. Its permissibility has been argued from the poet's saying:
192 - واصِلْ خليلَك ما التواصلُ مُمْكِنٌ ... فلأَنْتَ أو هُو عن قليلٍ ذاهبُ
(Keep close to your friend as long as closeness is possible, for you or he will shortly be gone.)
and another's saying:
193 - أحلامُكم لِسَقامِ الجَهْل شافيةٌ ... كما دماؤُكُمُ تَشْفي من الكَلَب
(Your wisdom heals the sickness of ignorance, just as your blood heals from rabies.)
and another's saying:
194 - فإنَّ الحُمْرَ من شرِّ المَطايا ... كما الحَبِطاتُ شَرُّ بني تميمِ
(Donkeys are among the worst of mounts, just as al-Ḥabiṭāt are the worst of Banū Tamīm.)
However, this is frequent with it when it conveys time, as in his saying «واصلْ خليلَك…», the verse. Al-Zamakhsharī and Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed «ما» to be kāffa (restraining), restraining the kāf from governing, like it in your saying «ربما قام زيد». No necessity calls for this, because making it infinitival keeps the kāf on the governing that is known for it, unlike making it restraining. The alif and lām in «الناس» may be generic or of prior reference (ʿahdiyya). The hamza in «أنؤمن» is for disavowal or mockery, and the position of «أنؤمن» is accusative by «قالوا».
His saying {كَمَآ آمَنَ السفهآء}: what is said about the kāf and «ما» is as what was said about them before. The alif [and lām] in «السفهاء» may be generic or of prior reference. Whoever made it for dominance (ghalaba), like «العيّوق», went far off, because this description has not become dominant for them such that, when "the fools" is said, particular people are understood from it, as a particular star is understood from «العيّوق». [Translator's note: al-ʿAyyūq is the star Capella.]
Al-safah is lightness; you say «ثوبٌ سفيه», i.e. thin in weave. His saying {ألا إِنَّهُمْ هُمُ السفهآء ولكن لاَّ يَعْلَمُونَ} is like His saying earlier {ألا إِنَّهُمْ هُمُ المفسدون ولكن لاَّ يَشْعُرُونَ} [al-Baqara: 12], so there is no need to repeat it. The meaning of the istidrāk (correction by "but") is as its meaning there, except that there He said «لا يشعرون» ("they do not perceive"), because what was affirmed of them there is corruption, which is grasped with the least reflection since it is among sensible things needing no great thought; so He negated of them what is grasped by the senses (al-mashāʿir, i.e. the senses), in exaggeration of declaring them ignorant: namely that the perception which is affirmed even of beasts is denied of them. What is affirmed here is foolishness, and what it is introduced by is the command to believe, which needs deep thought and complete reflection leading to belief and assent; and the thing commanded, belief, did not occur from them, so negating knowledge of them was fitting. A second aspect: al-safah is lightness of intellect and ignorance of matters. Al-Samawʾal said:
195 - نخافُ أَنْ تَسْفَهَ أَحلامُنا ... فنجهلَ الجهلَ مع الجاهلِ
(We fear lest our minds become foolish, so that we act ignorantly along with the ignorant.)
Knowledge is the opposite of ignorance, so He matched it with His saying «لا يعلمون», since lack of knowledge of a thing is ignorance of it.

semin-durr:14-14.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {وَإِذَا لَقُواْ الذين آمَنُواْ قالوا آمَنَّا}: «إذا» is accusative by «قالوا», which is its apodosis; the disagreement about this has already been mentioned. «لَقُوا» is a verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the clause is in the position of genitive by the adverb's being annexed to it. The origin of «لَقُوا» is «لَقِيُوا» on the pattern of «شَرِبوا»; the ḍamma was felt heavy on the yāʾ, which is the final radical, so the ḍamma was dropped; then two quiescent letters met — the final radical and the wāw of the plural — and neither could be voweled, so the first, the yāʾ, was deleted, and the kasra on the qāf was changed to a ḍamma to harmonise with the wāw of the pronoun. So the pattern of «لَقُوا» is «فَعُوا». This is a regular rule, as in «خَشُوا» and «حَيُوا».
Fourteen patterns have been heard for the maṣdar (verbal noun) of «لقي»: «لُقْياً» and «لِقْيَةً» with kasra on the first radical and sukūn on the second; «لِقاء», «لِقاءة» [and «لَقاءة»] with fatḥa as well, with the long vowel in all three; «لَقَى» and «لُقَى» with fatḥa and ḍamma on the qāf; «لُقْيا» with ḍamma on the first radical and sukūn on the second; «لِقِيَّا» with kasra on both and doubling; «لُقِيَّا» with ḍamma on the first radical and kasra on the second, with doubling; «لُقْياناً» and «لِقْيانا» with ḍamma and kasra on the first radical; «لِقْيانة» with kasra on the first radical only; and «تِلْقاء». [Translator's note: the text says "fourteen" but the forms listed number fewer as printed; translated as written.]
«الذين آمنوا» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), «قالوا» is the apodosis of «إذا», and «آمنَّا» is in the position of accusative by the verb of saying.
His saying, Exalted is He: {وَإِذَا خَلَوْاْ إلى شَيَاطِينِهِمْ قالوا}: its counterpart has already been discussed. Most commonly «خلا» is made transitive with bāʾ, and it may be made transitive with «إلى». It was made transitive with «إلى» in this verse for a fine meaning: when it is made transitive with bāʾ it admits two meanings — one is being alone [with someone], the other is ridicule and mockery; you say «خَلَوْتُ به», i.e. "I ridiculed him" — whereas when made transitive with «إلى» it is explicit in being alone only. Or you may say: «خلا» was made to include (taḍmīn) the meaning of «صَرَف» ("turned"), so it was made transitive with «إلى», the meaning being: they turned their privacy to their devils; or it includes the meaning of "they went off and turned away", so it is like the saying of al-Farazdaq:
196 - ألم تراني قالِباً مِجنِّي ... قد قَتَل اللهُ زياداً عنِّي
(Do you not see me turning my shield over? Allah has killed Ziyād [and turned him] away from me.)
i.e. He turned him away by killing. It has also been said that here it means «مع» ("with"), as in His saying {وَلاَ تأكلوا أَمْوَالَهُمْ إلى أَمْوَالِكُمْ} [al-Nisāʾ: 2]. And it has been said that it means the bāʾ. These two views are only allowed by the Kufans; as for the Basrans, they do not allow figurative use of particles because of their weakness. It has also been said that the meaning is "when they go apart from the believers to their devils", so «إلى» is in its proper sense. I say: implying «من المؤمنين» does not keep it in its proper sense except through the taḍmīn mentioned above.
The origin of «خَلَوْا» is «خَلَوُوْا»: the first wāw, which is the final radical, was changed to alif because it was voweled and preceded by a fatḥa; it remained quiescent, and after it the wāw of the pronoun was quiescent, so two quiescent letters met, and the first of them, the alif, was deleted, the fatḥa remaining to indicate it.
«شياطينهم» is the broken plural of «شيطان»; its derivation has been discussed already, so the pattern of «شياطين» is either «فعاليل» or «فعالين» according to the two views given under the istiʿādha. The eloquent usage in «شياطين» and its class is to inflect it with vowels, since it is a broken plural; there is a poor minor dialect form which treats it like a sound masculine plural. It was heard from them: «لفلانٍ بستانٌ حولَه بساتون» ("so-and-so has a garden around which are gardens"), and it was read anomalously: {وَمَا تَنَزَّلَتْ بِهِ الشياطون} [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 210].
His saying, Exalted is He: {قالوا إِنَّا مَعَكُمْ}: «إنّ» and its noun, and «معكم» is its khabar (predicate). The origin of «إنَّا» is «إنَّنا», as in His saying, Exalted is He: {إِنَّنَآ سَمِعْنَا مُنَادِياً} [Āl ʿImrān: 93] [Translator's note: the verse is Āl ʿImrān 193; the reference is as printed]. One of the two nūns of «إنّ» was dropped, when it joined the nūn of «نا», for lightness. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "The middle nūn was dropped, according to the correct view, as it is dropped in «إنّ» when it is lightened."
«مع» is an adverb (ẓarf) and the pronoun after it is in the position of genitive by its being annexed to it; it is the khabar, as said, so it is attached to (mutaʿalliq) something omitted. It is an adverb of place, though understanding adverbiality from it is uneasy. They said: because it indicates companionship, and adverbiality is a concomitant of companionship. As for its being an adverb of place, that is because it is predicated of concrete beings, as in «زيدٌ معك» ("Zayd is with you"); were it an adverb of time this would not be allowed. Know that the middle letter of «مع» may not be made quiescent except in poetry, as in his saying:
197 - وريشي مِنْكُمُ وهَوايَ مَعْكُمْ ... وإنْ كانَتْ زيارتُكم لِماما
(My feathers [means] are from you and my love is with you, even if your visits are rare.)
In that case it remains an adverb, contrary to whoever claimed that it is then a preposition, even though al-Naḥḥās claimed consensus on that. It is one of the nouns that must be annexed; it may be cut off in wording, in which case it is mostly accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial): you say «جاء الزيدان معاً», i.e. accompanying each other. It may occur as a khabar; the poet said:
198 - حَنَنْتَ إلى رَيَّا ونفسُك باعَدَتْ ... مَزارَكَ مِنْ رَيَّا وشَعْبَاكُما مَعَا
(You yearned for Rayyā while your own soul put your visiting far from Rayyā — and your two companies were together.)
So «شعباكما» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «معاً» its khabar; though it is possible that the khabar is omitted and «معاً» is a ḥāl. They disagreed about «مع» when cut off from annexation: is it of the class of the maqṣūr, like «عصا» and «رحا», or of the manqūṣ, like «يد» and «دم»? Two views: the first is that of Yūnus and al-Akhfash, the second that of al-Khalīl and Sībawayh. The benefit of this appears if we name someone with it: on the first you say «جاءني معاً، ورأيت معاً، ومررت بمعاً», and on the second «جاءني معٌ، ورأيت معاً، ومررت بمعٍ», like «يد». There is no proof for the first view in his saying «وشَعْباكما معاً», because «معاً» is accusative as an adverb standing in for the khabar, as in «زيدٌ عندَك». There is longer discussion of it than this, which I have left out preferring brevity.
His saying: {إِنَّمَا نَحْنُ مُسْتَهْزِئُونَ} is like His saying {إِنَّمَا نَحْنُ مُصْلِحُونَ} [al-Baqara: 11]. The apparent view of this clause is that it has no grammatical position because it is resumptive (istiʾnāf), since it is an answer to their chiefs: as if, when they said to them «إنَّا معكم», a question was directed at them from the chiefs, namely: "Then what about you being with the believers, backing them in their religion?" — so they answered them with this clause. It has also been said that its position is accusative because it is a badal (substitute) from His saying «إنَّا معكم». The analogical way of lightening the hamza of «مستهزئون» and the like is to make it bayna bayna, i.e. between the hamza and the letter from which its vowel comes, namely the wāw; this is the view of Sībawayh. The doctrine of al-Akhfash is to change it into a pure yāʾ. Ḥamza paused on «مستهزئون» and {فَمَالِئُونَ} [al-Ṣāffāt: 66] and the like by dropping the written form of the hamza, following the script of the muṣḥaf.

semin-durr:3-3.t:
{الذين يُؤْمِنُونَ}: «الذين» admits the nominative, the accusative and the genitive, and the apparent one is the genitive, which is on three grounds; the most apparent: it is a naʿt (adjective) of «المتقين»; the second: a badal (substitute); the third: an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition). The nominative is on two grounds. The first: it is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject) in the sense of "cutting off" (qaṭʿ), which has preceded. The second: it is a mubtadaʾ, and about its khabar there are two views: one, it is the first «أولئك»; the other, it is the second «أولئك», the wāw being redundant (zāʾida). These two views are poor and objectionable, because his saying «والذين يؤمنون» prevents the first «أولئك» from being the khabar, and the presence of the wāw likewise prevents the second «أولئك» from being the khabar; their saying that the wāw is redundant deserves no attention. The accusative is by way of cutting off (qaṭʿ). «يؤمنون» is the ṣila (relative clause) and contains the returning pronoun (ʿāʾid); it is an imperfect verb, the sign of its nominative being the nūn, because it is one of the "five forms" (al-amthila al-khamsa). The five forms denote every imperfect verb to which the alif of the dual, the wāw of the plural or the yāʾ of the addressed feminine is attached, e.g. yuʾminān, tuʾminān, yuʾminūn, tuʾminūn, tuʾminīn. The imperfect is always declinable, unless it is directly attached to the nūn of emphasis or the nūn of the feminine plural, with details that will come, Allah the Exalted willing, in the course of this book.
It is the imperfect of āmana in the sense of ṣaddaqa (to believe as true), and āmana is taken from the triliteral amina. The hamza in «أَمِنَ» [Translator's note: i.e. in the form āmana] is for becoming (ṣayrūra), as in "aʿshaba l-makān", i.e. the place became grassy; or for reflexive compliance (muṭāwaʿa) with faʿʿala, as in "kabba fa-akabba". It is made transitive with the bāʾ only because it is made to include the sense of iʿtarafa (to acknowledge). It is sometimes made transitive with the lām, as in the saying of the Exalted: {وَمَآ أَنتَ بِمُؤْمِنٍ لَّنَا} [Yūsuf: 17], {فَمَآ آمَنَ لموسى} [Yūnus: 83]; however, transitivity with the lām contains within it transitivity with the bāʾ; this is the difference between the two kinds of transitivity.
The origin of «يُؤْمِنون» is yuʾaʾminūn with two hamzas: the first is the hamza of afʿala and the second the first radical of the word. The first was dropped according to a morphological rule, namely that the hamza of afʿala is dropped after the prefix of the imperfect and in its active and passive participles, e.g. ukrimu, tukrimu, yukrimu, nukrimu, and "you are mukrim / mukram". It was dropped only because in some places two hamzas come together, namely when the prefix of the imperfect is a hamza, e.g. "anā ukrimu"; the origin is uʾakrimu with two hamzas, the first for the imperfect and the second the hamza of afʿala. The second was dropped because the heaviness arose through it, and because the prefix of the imperfect is more deserving of preservation; then the rest of the pattern was made to follow that for consistency. The hamza of afʿala may not remain in any of that, except under poetic necessity, as in his saying:
112 - فإنَّه أَهْلٌ لأِنْ يُؤَكْرَما ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(For he is worthy of being honoured.)
«بالغيبِ» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يؤمنون», and it would be a maṣdar (verbal noun) taking the place of the active participle or the passive participle. The second is questionable, because it is from ghāba, which is intransitive; how could a passive participle be formed from it so that the maṣdar takes its place? Unless it is said that it takes the place of the passive participle of the doubled transitive faʿʿala, i.e. al-mughayyab (what is made hidden), and this is far-fetched. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It may be lightened from fayʿil, as hayn from hayyin, and mayt from mayyit." This is questionable, because one should not claim that for it until it is heard with the doubled form like its counterparts, for they were heard both lightened and doubled; and it is unlikely that it be said that the lightening was made obligatory in this word alone.
The bāʾ may also be for ḥāl (circumstantial), so that it is attached to an omitted [word], i.e. they believe while being in a state of absence from what is believed in; ghayb is then a maṣdar in its proper sense.
The hamza of «يُؤْمِنُون» — and likewise every quiescent hamza — may be made to follow the vowel before it and so be replaced by a letter / homogeneous with it, e.g. rās, bīr, yūmin. If it happens that another hamza precedes it, replacement is obligatory, e.g. īmān and āmana.
«يُقيمون» is conjoined to «يُؤمنون», so it is part of the ṣila with the returning pronoun. Its origin is yuʾaqwimūn: the hamza of afʿala was dropped because it came after the prefix of the imperfect, as has preceded, so it became yuqwimūn; then the kasra was deemed heavy on the wāw, and what was done in «مستقيم» was done to it, which has preceded in al-Fātiḥa. The meaning of yuqīmūn is: they perpetuate, or they make manifest; the poet said:
113 - أَقَمْنا لأهلِ العِراقَيْنِ سوقَ ال ... طِعانِ فخاموا وولَّوْا جميعاً
(We set up for the people of the two Iraqs a market of spear-thrusting, so they shrank back and all turned away.)
Another said:
114 - وإذا يُقال أتيتُمُ لم يَبْرحوا ... حتى تقيمَ الخيلُ سوقَ طِعانِ
(When it is said "You have been attacked", they do not leave until the horses set up a market of spear-thrusting.)
«الصلاةَ» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). Its pattern is faʿala, and its final radical is wāw, because of their saying ṣalawāt; the wāw was vowelled and preceded by a fatḥa, so it was turned into alif. It is derived from al-ṣalawān, which are two veins in the hips that branch off from al-ṣalā, a vein lying within the back, from which the two ṣalawān branch at the coccyx; that is because the one praying moves his two ṣalawān. From this is al-muṣallī in the racecourse, because it comes second at the ṣalawān of the winner. Ṣalāt linguistically is supplication; [the poet] said:
115 - تقول بِنْتي وقد قَرَّبْتُ مُرْتَحَلا ... يا ربِّ جَنِّبْ أبي الأَوْصَابَ والوَجَعا
عليكِ مثلُ الذي صَلَّيْتِ فاغتمضي ... يوماً فإنَّ لجَنْبِ المَرْءِ مُضطجَعَا
(My daughter says, as I have brought near a mount for departure: "O Lord, keep my father away from ailments and pain." Upon you be the like of what you prayed for — so close your eyes one day, for a man's side has a place to lie down.)
i.e. the like of what you supplicated. Similar is:
116 - لها حارِسٌ لا يَبْرَحُ الدهرَ بيتَها ... وإن ذُبِحَتْ صَلَّى عليها وَزَمْزَما
(It has a guard who never leaves its house; and if it is slaughtered he prays over it and murmurs.)
In the Sharia it is this well-known act of worship. It has also been said: it is taken from adherence; from it is "ṣaliya bi-l-nār", i.e. he clung to it; [he said]:
117 - لم أَكُنْ مِنْ جُناتِها عَلِمَ الل ... هُ وإني بحَرِّها اليومَ صالي
(I was not among those who brought it on — Allah knows — yet today I am burning in its heat.)
It has also been said: from "ṣalaytu l-ʿūd bi-l-nār", i.e. I straightened the stick with al-ṣilāʾ, which is the heat of fire — when you give it fatḥa you shorten it, and when you give it kasra you lengthen it — as though the one praying straightens himself; [the poet] said:
118 - فلا تَعْجَلْ بأمرِكَ واستَدِمْهُ ... فما صلى عَصاكَ كمُسْتديمِ
(Do not hasten in your affair; take it slowly, for none straightens your stick like one who takes his time.)
A group of eminent scholars mentioned that, but it is problematic, for ṣalāt has wāw as a radical while this is from yāʾ.
{وَمِمَّا رَزَقْنَاهُمْ} is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «يُنْفِقون», and «ينفقون» is conjoined to the ṣila before it. The genitive «ما» admits three views. The first: it is a noun meaning "alladhī" (that which), «رزقناهم» is its ṣila, and the returning pronoun is omitted. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "Its implied form is razaqnāhumūhu or razaqnāhum iyyāhu." Each of these two implied forms has a difficulty: implying it attached entails attaching the pronoun while the ranks are the same, where it must be detached; and implying it detached prevents its omission, because whenever the returning pronoun is detached its omission is barred — they stated this explicitly and gave as the reason that it was only detached for a purpose, and if it were omitted the indication of that purpose would be lost. The first may be answered: since the two pronouns differ in plural and singular, even if they are of one rank, attaching it is allowed, and it would be like his saying:
119 - وقد جَعَلَتْ نفسي تَطيبُ لِضَغمَةٍ ... لِضَغْمِهماها يَقْرَعُ العظمَ نَابُها
(My soul has begun to be glad at a bite — at the bite those two gave her — whose tooth knocks the bone.)
Also, prohibiting that when it is pronounced does not entail prohibiting it when implied, since the verbal ugliness is gone. And the second may be answered: it is only prohibited because of the resulting ambiguity, and there is no ambiguity here. The second: it may be an indefinite noun that is qualified; what is said about its returning pronoun is as what is said about its returning pronoun as a relative, in implied form, objection and answer. The third: it is maṣdariyya (forming a maṣdar), the maṣdar taking the place of the object, i.e. "what is provided" (marzūq). Abū l-Baqāʾ prohibited this view; he said: "because the act is not spent" — [this is] on the basis that the maṣdar is meant as the object. [Translator's note: the source text here is compressed and seems slightly disordered; translated as written.]
Rizq linguistically is giving, and it is a maṣdar; the Exalted said: {وَمَن رَّزَقْنَاهُ مِنَّا رِزْقاً حَسَناً} [al-Naḥl: 75], and the poet said:
120 - رُزِقْتَ مالاً ولم تُرْزَقْ منافِعَه ... إنَّ الشقيَّ هو المَحْرُوم ما رُزِقا
(You were given wealth but not given its benefits; the wretched one is he who is deprived of what he was given.)
It has also been said: it may be fiʿl in the sense of mafʿūl, like dhibḥ and riʿy, meaning "slaughtered" and "pastured". It has also been said: razq with fatḥa is the maṣdar and rizq with kasra is the noun; and in the dialect of Azd Shanūʾa it means gratitude; from it is {وَتَجْعَلُونَ رِزْقَكُمْ أَنَّكُمْ تُكَذِّبُونَ} [al-Wāqiʿa: 82], and it will come in its place.] [Translator's note: a closing bracket appears here in the source without a matching opening one.] "Nafaqa l-shayʾ" means it ran out. Everything that comes with nūn as first radical and fāʾ as second radical indicates the sense of going out, departing and the like, if you reflect — al-Zamakhsharī said this, and it is as he said — e.g. nafida, nafaqa, nafara, nafadha, nafasa, nafasha, nafatha, nafaḥa, nafakha, nafaḍa, nafala. "Nafaqa l-shayʾ bi-l-bayʿ nafāqan": the thing sold well; "nafaqat al-dābba nufūqan": the animal died. Al-nafaqa is the noun for what is spent.
«مِنْ» here is for the beginning of the extent (ibtidāʾ al-ghāya); it has also been said: for partition (tabʿīḍ). It has other meanings: clarifying the genus: {فاجتنبوا الرجس مِنَ الأوثان} [al-Ḥajj: 30]; causation: {يَجْعَلُونَ أَصْابِعَهُمْ في آذَانِهِم مِّنَ الصواعق} [al-Baqara: 19]; substitution: {بالحياة الدنيا مِنَ الآخرة} [al-Tawba: 38]; passing beyond (mujāwaza): {وَإِذْ غَدَوْتَ مِنْ أَهْلِكَ} [Āl ʿImrān: 121] — and the end of the extent is close to it; superiority (istiʿlāʾ): {وَنَصَرْنَاهُ مِنَ القوم} [al-Anbiyāʾ: 77]; separation: {يَعْلَمُ المفسد مِنَ المصلح} [al-Baqara: 220]; agreeing with the bāʾ and with fī: {يَنظُرُونَ مِن طَرْفٍ خَفِيٍّ} [al-Shūrā: 45], {مَاذَا خَلَقُواْ مِنَ الأرض} [Fāṭir: 40]; and redundancy, regularly, under two conditions: that the genitive noun be indefinite and the speech be non-affirmative. The Kufans stipulated indefiniteness only, and al-Akhfash stipulated nothing.
The hamza in «أَنْفَقَ» is for transitivity, and it was dropped from «ينفقون» for the reason that has preceded at {يُؤْمِنُونَ} [al-Baqara: 3].

semin-durr:24-24.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {فَإِن لَّمْ تَفْعَلُواْ وَلَن تَفْعَلُواْ}: the conditional «إنْ» enters upon the clause «لم تفعلوا», and «تفعلوا» is jussive (majzūm) by «لم», just as the conditional «إنْ» enters upon a verb negated with «لا», as in {إنْ لا تفعلوه} [al-Anfāl: 73]. So «لم تفعلوا» is in the position of the jussive by it [i.e. by «إنْ»].
His saying «فاتَّقوا» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and His saying «ولَنْ تفعلوا» is a parenthetical (iʿtirāḍiyya) clause between the condition and its consequence. A group of the exegetes said: the meaning of the verse is: "And call your witnesses other than Allah, if you are truthful — and you will not do so; so if you do not do so, then fear the Fire." There is an evident objection to this. Allah the Exalted said {فَإِن لَّمْ تَفْعَلُواْ وَلَن تَفْعَلُواْ}, expressing "bringing" (الإتيان) by the verb "doing" (الفعل), only because "doing" functions like a pronoun-substitute (kināya): it can express any action and spares one the length of what it stands for. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Had He not turned from the word 'bringing' to the word 'doing', it would have been lengthy to say: 'So if you do not bring a sūra like it — and you will not bring a sūra like it.'" The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "What he said does not follow, because had He said 'فإنْ لم تأتوا ولَنْ تأتوا', the meaning would have been as he mentioned, and He would have omitted that [object] for brevity, just as He omitted for brevity the object of {لَّمْ تَفْعَلُواْ وَلَن تَفْعَلُواْ}. Do you not see that the implied form is: 'So if you do not do the bringing of a sūra like it, and you will not do the bringing of a sūra like it'?"
«لَنْ» is a particle of the accusative (naṣb) whose meaning is negation of the future. Like «لم», it is restricted to the imperfect form. Its negation does not entail perpetuity; nor is it shorter in duration than negation with «لا»; nor is its nūn a substitute for the alif of «لا»; nor is it compounded from «لا أَنْ», contrary to al-Khalīl. Some claimed that it may sometimes put the verb in the jussive, among them Abū ʿUbayda, and they cited:
277 - لن يَخِبْ لانَ مِنْ رجائِك مَنْ حَرْ ... رَكِ مِنْ دونِ بابِك الحَلَقَهْ
(No one who has now rattled the ring at your door will be disappointed in his hope of you.)
And al-Nābigha said:
278 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... فلن أُعَرِّضْ أَبَيْتَ اللَّعْنَ بالصَّفَدِ
(… I shall not hint at [asking] a gift — may you refuse [what brings] the curse.)
This can be interpreted as a case where [the final letter] was made quiescent out of poetic necessity.
His saying, Exalted is He: {فاتقوا النار}: this is the apodosis of the condition, as already stated. The most common form in the language of the Arabs is «اتقى يتَّقي» on the pattern افْتَعَل يَفْتَعِلُ. The dialect of Tamīm and Asad has «تَقَى يَتْقي», like «رَمَى يَرْمي», making what follows the imperfect prefix quiescent; Sībawayh reported this dialect. Some of them give a vowel to what follows the imperfect prefix, and they cited:
279 - تَقُوه أيُّها الفِتْيانُ إنّي ... رأيتُ الله قد غَلَبَ الجُدودا
(Fear Him, O young men, for I have seen that Allah has overpowered [men's] fortunes.)
And another said:
280 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... تَقِ الله فينا والكتابَ الذي تتلو
(… Fear Allah regarding us, and the Book which you recite.)
His saying, Exalted is He: {النار} is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and «التي» is its naʿt (adjective). In it there are the four dialectal forms mentioned earlier, as in:
281 - شُغِفَتْ بك اللَّتْ تَيَّمَتْكَ فَمثلُ ما ... بك ما بها مِنْ لَوْعةٍ وغَرامِ
(She who has enslaved you with love is infatuated with you; the like of the anguish and passion in you is in her.)
And another said:
282 - فقلْ لِلَّتْ تَلُومُك إنَّ نَفْسي ... أراها لا تُعَوَّذُ بالتَّميمِ
(So say to her who blames you: my soul, I see it, is not to be protected by amulets.)
[Translator's note: the source prints this verse number as «28 - 2-»; it is verse 282 in the sequence.]
His saying {وَقُودُهَا الناس} is a clause of mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), the ṣila (relative clause), containing the referring pronoun. The alif-lām in «النار» is for prior acquaintance (al-ʿahd), because it was mentioned earlier in Sūrat al-Taḥrīm — which is Meccan — at His saying, Exalted is He: {قوا أَنفُسَكُمْ وَأَهْلِيكُمْ نَاراً} [al-Taḥrīm: 6].
[Translator's note: al-Taḥrīm is generally counted as Medinan; the text is translated as written.]
The well-known reading has fatḥa on the wāw of «الوَقود», and it is the name of that with which a fire is kindled (fuel). It was also said to be a maṣdar (verbal noun), like «الوَلوع», «القَبول», «الوَضوء» and «الطَّهور». No maṣdar on the pattern فَعُول has come other than these words, according to what Sībawayh reported. Al-Kisāʾī added «الوَزُوع», and in Sūrat Qāf {وما مسَّنا من لَغوب} [verse 38] was read in an irregular (shādhdh) reading [with fatḥa], so they become seven; I mentioned that reading there. But the well-known view is that «الوقود», «الوَضوء» and «الطَهور» with fatḥa are nouns and with ḍamma are maṣdars. It was read irregularly with ḍamma [«الوُقود»], and that is a maṣdar. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "Both have been reported for firewood, and both have been reported for the maṣdar." End of quote. If what is meant is the name of what is kindled with, then no interpretation is needed. If the maṣdar is meant by them, then an interpretation is unavoidable, which is either: hyperbole, i.e. they were made the very act of burning, as hyperbole in describing them with punishment; or the omission of a muḍāf — either from the first [term], i.e. "the people of its burning", or from the second, i.e. "its kindling is the burning of people" — then the muḍāf was omitted and the muḍāf ilayhi put in its place.
The hāʾ in «الحجارة» is for the feminine marking of the plural.
His saying, Exalted is He: {أُعِدَّتْ} is a verb whose agent is not named (passive), and what stands in place of the agent (nāʾib fāʿil, deputy agent) is the pronoun of «النار». The tāʾ is obligatory, because the verb is predicated of a feminine pronoun; no attention is paid to his saying:
283 - فلا مُزْنَةٌ وَدَقَتْ وَدْقَها ... ولا أرضَ أَبْقَلَ إبْقالَها
(No rain-cloud ever poured its rain as it did, and no land ever sprouted its herbage as it did.)
because that is poetic necessity — contrary to Ibn Kaysān. «للكافرين» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to it. The meaning of «أُعِدَّت» is "made ready". [The poet] said:
284 - أَعْدَدْتَ للحَدَثان سا ... بِغَةً وعَدَّاءً عَلَنْدى
(You have made ready for the vicissitudes of fortune an ample coat of mail and a sturdy, swift runner.)
It was also read «أُعْتِدَتْ», from «العَتاد» meaning equipment/provision. The apparent view is that this clause has no grammatical position, being resumptive (mustaʾnafa), an answer to someone who says: "For whom was it prepared?" Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "Its position is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «النار», and the governing word in it is «اتقوا»." It was said: there is an objection to this, since it is prepared for the disbelievers whether they fear it or not, so it would be a permanent ḥāl; but the basic rule for a ḥāl that is not for emphasis is that it be transitory, so it is preferable that it be resumptive. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is not permissible for it to be a ḥāl from the pronoun in «وَقُودُها», for three reasons. First: it [the pronoun] is a muḍāf ilayhi. Second: firewood does not govern" — meaning it is an inert (jāmid) noun. "Third: the separation, by the khabar «الناس», between the maṣdar (or what acts like it) and what it governs." He means that «الوُقود» with ḍamma, even if it is a maṣdar capable of governing, still does not allow this, because it would govern the ḥāl, and you would have separated it from it by an extraneous element, namely «الناس». Al-Sijistānī said: {أُعِدَّتْ لِلْكَافِرِينَ} is part of the ṣila of «التي», like His saying {واتقوا النار التي أُعِدَّتْ لِلْكَافِرِينَ} [Āl ʿImrān: 131]. Ibn al-Anbārī said: "This is a mistake, because «التي» here has been given a ṣila in His saying {وَقُودُهَا الناس}, so it is not permissible to give it a second ṣila, unlike «التي» in Āl ʿImrān." I say: it is possible that it is not a mistake, because we do not concede that {وَقُودُهَا الناس} is, in this case, a ṣila; rather it is either parenthetical, since it contains emphasis, or a ḥāl — and neither meaning nor grammatical technique precludes these two views.

semin-durr:4-4.t:
The saying of the Exalted: {والذين يُؤْمِنُونَ}: «الذين» is conjoined to «الذين» before it, and then you have two considerations. [The first:] that it is a case of conjoining some attributes to others, as in his saying:
121 - إلى المَلِكِ القَرْمِ وابنِ الهُمامِ ... وليثِ الكتيبة في المُزْدَحَمْ
(To the king, the noble chief, the son of the valiant lord, the lion of the squadron in the crush.)
and his saying:
122 - يا ويحَ زيَّابَة للحارثِ ال ... صابحِ فالغانمِ فالآئِبِ
(Woe to Zayyāba [i.e. his mother] for al-Ḥārith, who attacked at dawn, then took the spoils, then returned.)
meaning that they combine these attributes, if it is said that what is meant by both is one [group].
The second: that they are others than them. On both views, its position is judged with the same grammatical rulings as the position of the preceding «الذين»: nominative, accusative and genitive, by cutting off (qaṭʿ) and by following (itbāʿ), as detailed earlier. It may also be conjoined to «المتقين», or be a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is «أولئك» and what follows it, if it is said that they are other than the first «الذين». «يؤمنون» is the ṣila (relative clause) and contains the returning pronoun (ʿāʾid).
«بما أُنْزِلَ» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) it. «ما» is a nominal relative, and «أُنْزِلَ» is its ṣila; it is a passive verb, and the returning pronoun is the pronoun standing in place of the fāʿil (agent). It is weak for it to be an indefinite qualified noun; Abū l-Baqāʾ prohibited that, saying: "because the indefinite qualified noun has no generality in it, and faith is not complete except with all that was sent down."
«إليك» is attached to «أُنزل». The meaning of «إلى» is the end of the extent (intihāʾ al-ghāya). It has other meanings: accompaniment: {وَلاَ تأكلوا أَمْوَالَهُمْ إلى أَمْوَالِكُمْ} [al-Nisāʾ: 2]; clarification (tabyīn): {رَبِّ السجن أَحَبُّ إِلَيَّ} [Yūsuf: 33]; and agreeing with the lām, fī and min: {والأمر إِلَيْكِ} [al-Naml: 33], i.e. "laki" (yours). Al-Nābigha said:
