123 - فلاَ تَتْرُكَنِّي بالوعيدِ كأنني ... إلى الناسِ مَطْلِيٌّ به القار أَجْرَبُ
(Do not leave me under threat as though I were, among people, a mangy [camel] smeared with tar.)
i.e. "among (fī) people". Another said:
124 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ...
أَيُسْقَى فلا يُرْوى إليَّ ابنُ أَحْمَرا
(Is Ibn Aḥmar given drink and yet not quenched by me?)
i.e. "he is not quenched from (min) me". It is sometimes added [redundantly]; it was read: «تهوى إليهم» with fatḥa on the wāw.
The kāf is in the position of the genitive; it is the pronoun of the one addressed, and what indicates dual and plural, masculine and feminine, is attached to it, like the tāʾ of the one addressed. Nuzūl (descending) is arriving and alighting without the condition of height; the Exalted said: {فَإِذَا نَزَلَ بِسَاحَتِهِمْ} [al-Ṣāffāt: 177], i.e. alighted and arrived. The second «ما» with its ṣila is conjoined to the first «ما» before it, so what is said about it and its ṣila is as what is said about the «ما» before it; let it be considered.
«مِنْ قبلِك» is attached to «أُنْزِلَ»; «مِنْ» is for the beginning of the extent, and «قبل» is an adverb of time requiring precedence; it is the opposite of «بعد». Both of them, whenever they are indefinite or in construct, are declined; whenever they are cut off from the construct in wording / while it is intended in meaning, they are built (mabnī) on ḍamma. Of the declined [use] is his saying:
125 - فساغَ ليَ الشرابُ وكنت قَبْلاً ... أكاد أَغَصُّ بالماءِ القَراحِ
(Then drink became pleasant to me, whereas before I almost choked on pure water.)
Another said:
126 - ونحن قَتَلْنَا الأُسْدَ أُسْدَ خَفِيَّةٍ ... فما شَرِبوا بَعْداً على لَذَّةً خَمْرا
(We killed the lions, the lions of Khafiyya, and afterwards they never drank wine with pleasure.)
Of the indeclinable [use] is the saying of the Exalted: {لِلَّهِ الأمر مِن قَبْلُ وَمِن بَعْدُ} [al-Rūm: 4]. Some claimed that «قبل» was originally an adjective that obligatorily stood in for the noun it qualified; when you say "I stood before Zayd", the implied form is: "I stood at a time before the time of Zayd's standing"; all this was omitted and "qabla Zayd" stood in for it. This is questionable in a way not hidden from whoever reflects on it.
Know that the ruling of fawq, taḥt, ʿalā and awwal is the ruling of qabl and baʿd in what has preceded. It was read: «بما أَنْزَلَ إليك» in the active voice, the agent being Allah the Exalted or Gabriel. It was also read «أُنْزِلْ لَيْكَ» with a doubled lām; its explanation is that he made the last letter of the verb quiescent, as another made it quiescent in his saying:
127 - إنما شِعْريَ مِلْحٌ ... قد خُلْط بجُلْجُلانْ
(My poetry is but salt that has been mixed with sesame.)
with «خُلْط» made quiescent; then he dropped the hamza of «إليك», so two identical letters met and he assimilated them.
«بالآخرةِ» is attached to «يوقنون», and «يُوقنون» is the khabar of «هم». The genitive [phrase] was placed first out of concern for it, as what is spent was placed first in his saying {وَممَّا رَزَقْنَاهُمْ يُنْفِقُونَ} [al-Baqara: 3] for that reason. This is a nominal clause conjoined to the verbal clause before it, so it too is part of the ṣila. But here the clause came as a mubtadaʾ and khabar, unlike {وَممَّا رَزَقْنَاهُمْ يُنْفِقُونَ}, because describing them as certain of the Hereafter is weightier than describing them as spending from provision, so emphasis by means of the nominal clause was fitting; or so that the wording would not be repeated if it were said "wa-mimmā razaqnāhum hum yunfiqūn".
Īqān (certainty) is verifying a thing because of its clarity and stillness; it is said "yaqina l-māʾ" when the water became still so that what is beneath it appeared; and "yaqintu l-amr" with kasra on the qāf. «يُوقنون» is from ayqana in the sense of istayqana; it has preceded that afʿala comes in the sense of istafʿala.
«الآخرة» is the feminine of ākhir, the counterpart of awwal (first). It is originally an adjective that came to be treated like nouns, and the implied form is "al-dār al-ākhira" (the last abode) or "al-nashʾa al-ākhira" (the last creation); these two qualified nouns have been stated explicitly: the Exalted said {وَلَلدَّارُ الآخرة خَيْرٌ} [al-Anʿām: 32], and said {ثُمَّ الله يُنشِىءُ النشأة الآخرة} [al-ʿAnkabūt: 20]. It was read «يُؤْقِنُون» with the wāw made a hamza, as though they placed the ḍamma of the yāʾ on the wāw, because the vowel of a letter is [pronounced] before it. A wāw with ḍamma is regularly turned into hamza under conditions, among them: that the vowel not be accidental, that it not be possible to lighten it, that it not have something assimilated into it, and that it not be augmentative — with disagreement about this last one. Examples of that will come in Sūrat Āl ʿImrān at his saying {وَلاَ تَلْوُونَ على أحَدٍ} [Āl ʿImrān: 153]. So they treated the quiescent wāw preceded by ḍamma like the wāw with ḍamma itself, for the reason I mentioned. Similar to this reading is Qunbul's reading «بالسُّؤْقِ» [Ṣād: 33] and «على سُؤْقِه» [al-Fatḥ: 29]; and the poet said:
128 - أَحَبُّ المُؤْقِدينَ إليَّ موسى ... وجَعْدَةُ إذ أضاءَهُما الوَقودُ
(The dearest of fire-kindlers to me are Mūsā and Jaʿda, when the fuel lit them up.)
with «المُؤْقدين» given a hamza. He brought the five verbs in the imperfect form to indicate renewal and occurrence, and that they do that at every time. He brought «أُنْزِل» in the past, even though their faith [came] before its sending down was complete, giving predominance to the present, already sent down, over what had not yet been sent down; because it must inevitably occur, it is as if it had been sent down. So it is of the kind of his saying {أتى أَمْرُ الله} [al-Naḥl: 1], indeed closer than it, since part of it had already been sent down.

semin-durr:15-15.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {الله يَسْتَهْزِىءُ بِهِمْ}: «الله» is nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and «يستهزئ» is a verbal clause in the position of its khabar (predicate); «بهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) it. This clause has no grammatical position because it is resumptive. «ويمدّهم» is also in the position of nominative because it is conjoined to the khabar, «يستهزئ». «يعمهون» is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the object in «يمدّهم», or of the pronoun in «طغيانهم»; the ḥāl comes from the muḍāf ilayhi because the muḍāf is a maṣdar (verbal noun). «في طغيانهم» may be attached to «يمدّهم» or to «يعمهون», having been placed before it — except when «يعمهون» is made a ḥāl of the pronoun in «طغيانهم», for then it is not attached to it, because the meaning would be corrupted.
Abū al-Baqāʾ disallowed «في طغيانهم» and «يعمهون» being two ḥāls of the pronoun in «يمدّهم», giving as reason that a single governor does not govern two ḥāls. This is on the view of those who disallow that; as for those who allow multiple ḥāls without multiple possessors of the ḥāl, they allow it. However, in this verse it ought to be disallowed, not for the reason Abū al-Baqāʾ gave, but because the meaning refuses making this preposition-and-genitive a ḥāl, since the meaning is directed to its being attached to one of the two verbs, I mean «يمدّهم» or «يعمهون», not to something omitted as a ḥāl.
The well-known reading is with fatḥa on the yāʾ of «يَمُدُّهم», and it was read anomalously with ḍamma. It has been said: the triliteral and the quadriliteral have one meaning; you say «مَدَّه» and «أَمَدَّه» with such-and-such. It has been said: «مَدَّه» is when one increases him with something of its own kind, and «أَمَدَّه» when one increases him with something of another kind. And it has been said: «مَدَّه» is in evil, as in His saying, Exalted is He: {وَنَمُدُّ لَهُ مِنَ العذاب مَدّاً} [Maryam: 79], and «أَمَدَّه» in good, as in His saying {وَيُمْدِدْكُمْ بِأَمْوَالٍ وَبَنِينَ} [Nūḥ: 12], {وَأَمْدَدْنَاهُم بِفَاكِهَةٍ وَلَحْمٍ} [al-Ṭūr: 22], {أَن يُمِدَّكُمْ رَبُّكُمْ بِثَلاَثَةِ آلاَفٍ} [Āl ʿImrān: 124]. However, what troubles these two distinctions is that {وَإِخْوَانُهُمْ يَمُدُّونَهُمْ فِي الغي} [al-Aʿrāf: 202] was read in both forms. It may be answered with what al-Fārisī said in explaining the ḍamma of the yāʾ: that it is like His saying, Exalted is He: {فَبَشِّرْهُم بِعَذَابٍ} [Āl ʿImrān: 21], {فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُ للعسرى} [al-Layl: 10] — Abū ʿAlī, may Allah the Exalted have mercy on him, means by that that it is by way of sarcasm (tahakkum).
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: why did you claim that it is from «المَدَد» (reinforcement) rather than from «المَدّ» (extension) in life, granting respite and delay? I say: sufficient proof of that is the reading of Ibn Kathīr and Ibn Muḥayṣin «ويُمِدُّهم» and the reading of Nāfiʿ «وإخوانُهم يُمِدُّونهم»; moreover, the one meaning 'He granted him respite' is only «مَدَّ له», with the lām, like «أَمْلى له»."
Al-istihzāʾ (mockery) in language is ridicule and play: one says «هَزِئَ به» and «استهزأ». [The poet] said:
199 - قد هَزِئَتْ مني أمُّ طَيْسَلَهْ ... قالَتْ: أراه مُعْدِماً لا مالَ لَهْ
(Umm Ṭaysala mocked me; she said: I see him destitute, he has no wealth.)
It has been said that its origin is vengeance, and he recited:
200 - قد استهْزَؤوا منا بألفَيْ مُدَجَّجٍ ... سَراتُهُمُ وَسْطَ الصَّحاصِحِ جُثَّمُ
(They took vengeance on us with two thousand fully armed men; their nobles lie prostrate in the midst of the barren plains.)
On this second view, attributing mockery to Him, Exalted is He, is on its apparent sense; on the first view it must be interpreted.
It has been said: the meaning is "He requites them for their mockery", so He called the punishment by the name of the sin so that the speech would be paired (izdiwāj); of this kind are {وَجَزَآءُ سَيِّئَةٍ سَيِّئَةٌ مِّثْلُهَا} [al-Shūrā: 40] and {فَمَنِ اعتدى عَلَيْكُمْ فاعتدوا عَلَيْهِ} [al-Baqara: 194]. And ʿAmr ibn Kulthūm said:
201 - ألا لا يَجْهَلَنْ أَحدٌ علينا ... فَنَجْهَلَ فوقَ جَهْلِ الجاهِلينا
(Let no one act ignorantly against us, lest we act ignorantly beyond the ignorance of the ignorant.)
The origin of al-madad is increase. Al-ṭughyān is the maṣdar of «طغى يطغى», «طِغْياناً» and «طُغْياناً» with kasra and ḍamma on the ṭāʾ. The final radical of «طغى» is said to be yāʾ and said to be wāw; one says «طَغَيْتُ» and «طَغَوْتُ». The root's basic sense is exceeding the limit; from it «طغى الماء» ("the water overflowed"). Al-ʿamah is wavering and bewilderment; it is close to al-ʿamā (blindness), except that between them there is a relation of general and particular, because al-ʿamā is used for loss of the eye's sight and for error in opinion, while al-ʿamah is used only for error in opinion. One says «عَمِهَ يَعْمَهُ عَمَهاً وعَمَهاناً», so he is «عَمِهٌ» and «عامِهٌ».

semin-durr:16-16.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {أولئك الذين اشتروا الضلالة بالهدى}: «أولئك» is nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and «الذين» with its ṣila (relative clause) is its khabar (predicate). His saying, Exalted is He: {فَمَا رَبِحَتْ تِّجَارَتُهُمْ}: this clause is conjoined to the clause occurring as the ṣila, namely «اشتروا». Some claimed that it is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ and that the fāʾ entered the khabar because the relative contains the meaning of a condition, making it parallel to His saying {الذين يُنْفِقُونَ أَمْوَالَهُمْ} [al-Baqara: 274], after which He said {فَلَهُمْ أَجْرُهُمْ}. This is a mistake, because «الذين اشتروا» is not a mubtadaʾ so that the fāʾ could be claimed to enter its khabar; rather it is the khabar of «أولئك», as said. If it is said: let the relative be a second mubtadaʾ, so that the fāʾ entered its khabar — the answer is that this entails absence of a link between the mubtadaʾ and the clause occurring as its khabar; and also the ṣila is past in meaning. If it is said: let «الذين» be a badal (substitute) from «أولئك» — the answer is that the relative would then become specific by being substituted from something specific, and also the ṣila is past. If it is said: let «الذين» be an adjective of «أولئك», so it becomes parallel to your saying «الرجلُ الذي يأتيني فله درهمٌ» — the answer is that it is rejected by what the second objection was rejected by, and because it may not be its adjective, since [«أولئك»] is more definite than it. So the invalidity of this view is clear.
The well-known reading is with ḍamma on the wāw of «اشتروا» because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. It was given ḍamma by analogy with the tāʾ of the agent. It has been said: to distinguish between the wāw of the plural and an original wāw, as in «لو استطعنا». It has been said: because ḍamma here is lighter than kasra since it is of the same kind as wāw. It has been said: it was voweled with the vowel of the deleted yāʾ, since the origin is «اشْتَرَيُوا», as will come. And it has been said: it is for the plural, so it is like «نحن». It was read with kasra, according to the basic rule for two meeting quiescents, and with fatḥa because it is lighter. Al-Kisāʾī allowed giving it a hamza, by analogy with «أَدْؤُر» and «أَثْؤُب»; this is weak, because its ḍamma is not inherent. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "Some of them slur it (ikhtilās), deleting it because of the meeting of two quiescents; this is very weak, because before it is a fatḥa, and the fatḥa does not indicate it."
The origin of «اشْتَرَوا» is «اشْتَرَيُوا» [Translator's note: printed «اسْتَرَيُوا»; translated as the evident intended form]: the yāʾ was voweled with a fatḥa before it, so it was changed to alif, then deleted because of the meeting of two quiescents, the fatḥa remaining to indicate it. It has also been said: rather the ḍamma was dropped from the yāʾ so it became quiescent; two quiescents met, so the yāʾ was deleted because of their meeting. If it is said: the wāw of the plural has been voweled, so the deleted quiescent should return — the answer is that this vowel is accidental, so it has the status of a quiescent; that [return] has come only in poetic licence. Al-Kisāʾī recited:
202 - يا صَباحِ لَمْ تنامِ العَشِيَّا
(O Ṣabāḥ, you did not sleep in the evening.)
He restored the alif when the mīm was given an accidental vowel.
«الضلالة» is its object, and «بالهدى» is attached to «اشتروا». The bāʾ here is for exchange (ʿiwaḍ), and it always enters on what is given up. As for His saying, Exalted is He: {فَلْيُقَاتِلْ فِي سَبِيلِ الله الذين يَشْرُونَ الحياة الدنيا بالآخرة} [al-Nisāʾ: 74], whose apparent sense is that the Hereafter is what is taken, not what is given up — the answer is what al-Zamakhsharī, may Allah the Exalted have mercy on him, said: that those meant by the purchasers are the laggards, who were exhorted to change the hypocrisy in them, make faith in Allah the Exalted and His Messenger sincere, and strive for Allah as He should be striven for; so in that case the bāʾ enters only on what is given up.
Purchase here is a metaphor for exchange, meaning that when they abandoned guidance and preferred error, they were put in the position of those who buy it with guidance. Then this metaphor was reinforced (tarshīḥ) by His saying, Exalted is He: {فَمَا رَبِحَتْ تِّجَارَتُهُمْ}, attributing profit to the trade, the meaning being: they did not profit in their trade. A parallel of this tarshīḥ is another's saying:
203 - بكى الخَزُّ مِنْ رَوْحٍ وأنكرَ جِلْدَه ... وَعجَّتْ عَجيجاً من جُذامَ المَطارِفُ
(Silk wept because of Rawḥ and disowned his skin, and the fine cloaks cried out loudly because of Judhām.)
Having metaphorically attributed weeping to the silk on account of this man, Rawḥ, and its disowning his skin, he reinforced it by saying «وعجّت المطارف من جذام», i.e. the garments cried for help because of this tribe. And another's saying:
204 - ولَمَّا رأيتُ النَّسْرَ عَزَّ ابنُ دايةٍ ... وعَشَّشَ في وَكْرَيْهِ جاشَ له صَدْري
(When I saw the vulture overpower the son of Dāya [the crow] and nest in its two nests, my breast surged at it.)
Having made the vulture stand for grey hair and Ibn Dāya, the crow, stand metaphorically for youth, he reinforced it by saying «وعشّش في وكريه». And another's saying:
205 - فما أُمُّ الرُّدَيْنِ وإنْ أَدَلَّتْ ... بعالمةٍ بأخلاقِ الكرامِ
إذا الشيطانُ قصَّع في قَفاها ... تَنَقَّفْناه بالحَبْل التُّؤامِ
(Umm al-Rudayn, though she presumes, does not know the manners of the noble; when the devil enters the hole at the back of her head, we drive him out through the other hole with the twin-stranded rope.)
When he said «قصّع في قفاها», i.e. entered through the qāṣiʿāʾ, which is one of the jerboa's burrows, he reinforced it by saying «تنقّفناه», i.e. we drove him out through the nāfiqāʾ, which is also one of the jerboa's burrows.
His saying, Exalted is He: {وَمَا كَانُواْ مُهْتَدِينَ}: this clause is conjoined to His saying {فَمَا رَبِحَتْ تِّجَارَتُهُمْ}. Al-ribḥ is increase over the capital. Al-muhtadī is the active participle of «اهتدى»; «افتعل» here is for reflexive compliance (muṭāwaʿa), and «افتعل» is for muṭāwaʿa only from a transitive verb. Some claimed it comes from an intransitive one, and argued for that with the poet's saying:
206 - حتى إذا اشْتَال سُهَيْلٌ في السِّحَرْ ... كشُعلةِ القابِس تَرْمِي بالشَّرَرْ
(Until, when Canopus rose high before dawn, like the torch of a fire-seeker throwing sparks.)
He said: "«اشتال» is «افتعل» for the muṭāwaʿa of «شال», which is intransitive." This is a mistake by this speaker, because «افتعل» here is not for muṭāwaʿa but has the meaning of the bare «فَعَل».

semin-durr:5-5.t:
The saying of the Exalted: {أولئك}: a mubtadaʾ (subject), whose khabar (predicate) is the preposition and its genitive noun after it, i.e. "being upon guidance". This clause is either resumptive (mustaʾnafa) or a khabar of his saying {الذين يُؤْمِنُونَ}, either the first or the second. «أولئك» alone may also be a khabar of {الذين يُؤْمِنُونَ}, either the first or the second, and «على هدى» in this view is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). All this applies if we parse {الذين يُؤْمِنُونَ} as a mubtadaʾ; if we make it other than a mubtadaʾ, its ruling is not hidden from what has preceded. {الذين يُؤْمِنُونَ} may also be a mubtadaʾ, «أولئك» a badal (substitute) or bayān (explicative apposition), and «على هدى» the khabar. «مِنْ ربهم» is in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of «هدى», and «مِنْ» is for the beginning of the extent. He made «هُدَى» indefinite so that its vagueness conveys magnification, as in his saying:
129 - فلا وأبي الطيرِ المُرِبَّة بِالضُّحى ... على خالدٍ لقد وقَعْتِ على لَحْمِ
(No — by the father of the birds that keep hovering at forenoon over Khālid — you have indeed alighted on [noble] flesh!)
«مِنْ ربهم» is transmitted without nasalization (ghunna), which is the well-known [way], and with nasalization, which is transmitted from Abū ʿAmr.
«أولئك» is a demonstrative shared by groups of males and females. It is indeclinable (mabnī) on kasra because it resembles the particle in its dependence. It has two forms: with the long vowel (madd) and with the short (qaṣr), but the long form is for the distant; and "ulā lika" is sometimes said; [the poet] said:
130 - أُولا لِك قومي لم يكونوا أُشَابَةً ... وهل يَعِظُ الضِّلِّيلَ إلا أُولا لِكَا
(Those are my people; they were not a motley mix — and does anything admonish the one far astray except those?)
According to some, the short form is for the near, the long for the middle, and "ulālika" for the distant. It has many dialectal forms. They wrote «أولئك» with an extra wāw before the lām; it is said: to distinguish it from «إليك».
{وأولئك هُمُ المفلحون}: «أولئك» is a mubtadaʾ, «هم» a second mubtadaʾ and «المفلحون» its khabar, and the clause is the khabar of the first. «هم» may also be a separating pronoun (faṣl) or a badal, with «المفلحون» the khabar. The benefit of the separating pronoun is distinguishing between the khabar and the follower, and that is why it is called faṣl; it also conveys tawkīd (emphasis). It has preceded that the first or second «أولئك» may be a khabar of «الذين يؤمنون», and the weakness of these two views has preceded. He repeated «أولئك» to point out that just as the distinction of guidance is established for them, so the distinction of success is established for them; each of the two distinctions, in distinguishing them from others, is made such that if it stood alone it would suffice as a distinguishing mark by itself.
Here he brought the wāw between the clauses of his saying {أولئك على هُدًى مِّن رَّبِّهِمْ وأولئك هُمُ المفلحون}, unlike the saying of the Exalted in the other verse: {أولئك كالأنعام بَلْ هُمْ أَضَلُّ أولئك هُمُ الغافلون} [al-Aʿrāf: 179], because the two predicates here are different, which called for conjunction; whereas in that noble verse the two predicates are one thing, since recording heedlessness against them and likening them to cattle are one meaning, so it was remote from conjunction. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "In the demonstrative «أولئك» there is an indication that those mentioned before it are worthy of acquiring what comes after it because of the qualities enumerated for them, like the saying of Ḥātim: «And to Allah [belongs the excellence of] a poor vagabond (ṣuʿlūk)», after which he enumerated excellent qualities of his, and then followed their enumeration with his saying:
131 - فذلك إن يَهْلِكْ فَحُسْنى ثناؤُه ... وإن عاش لم يَقْعُدْ ضعيفاً مُذَمَّماً
(That one: if he perishes, his praise is the finest; and if he lives, he does not sit idle, weak and blamed.)"
Falāḥ originally means splitting; from it is the saying: "Iron is split (yuflaḥ) by iron." From it is the saying of Bakr ibn al-Naṭṭāḥ:
132 - لاَ تَبْعَثَنَّ إلى ربيعةَ غيرَها ... إن الحديدَ بغيرِه لا يُفْلِح
(Do not send against Rabīʿa anyone but [one of] them; iron is not split by anything other than [iron].)
It is used to express winning and attaining one's desire, which is what the verse intends; and it is used to mean remaining (baqāʾ); [the poet] said:
133 - لو أن حَيَّاً مُدْرِكُ الفَلاحِ ... أَدْرَكه مُلاعِبُ الرِّماحِ
(If any living being could attain everlastingness, Mulāʿib al-Rimāḥ would have attained it.)
Another said:
134 - نَحُلُّ بلاداً كلُّها حَلَّ قبلَنا ... ونرجو الفَلاَح بعد عادٍ وحِمْيَرِ
(We settle in lands all of which others settled before us, and we hope for permanence after ʿĀd and Ḥimyar.)
And he said:
135 - لكلِّ هَمٍّ من الهُموم سَعَهْ ... والمُسْيُ والصُّبْحُ لا فَلاَح معه
(Every worry has some relief, but with evening and morning [succeeding] there is no permanence.)
Another said:
136 - أَفْلِحْ بما شِئْت فقد يُبْلَغُ بال ... ضَّعْفِ وقد يُخْدَعُ الأَريب
(Succeed by whatever means you wish, for [the goal] is sometimes reached through weakness, and the shrewd man is sometimes deceived.)

semin-durr:25-25.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {وَبَشِّرِ الذين آمَنُواْ}: this clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it; He conjoined the clause of the believers' reward to the clause of the disbelievers' punishment. This is permissible because the doctrine of Sībawayh — and it is the correct one — is that agreement in meaning is not a condition for conjoining clauses; rather a request (ṭalabiyya) clause may be conjoined to an informative (khabariyya) clause and vice versa, as evidenced by his saying:
285 - تُناغي غَزالاً عند بابِ ابنِ عامرٍ ... وَكَحِّلْ أماقِيكَ الحسانَ بإِثْمِدِ
(You coo to a gazelle at the door of Ibn ʿĀmir — and line your fair eye-corners with antimony.)
And the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:
286 - وإنَّ شفائي عَبْرَةٌ مُهْرَاقَةٌ ... وهل عند رَسْمٍ دارسٍ مِنْ مُعَوَّلِ
(My cure is a tear poured out — yet is there any recourse at an effaced trace [of a dwelling]?)
[Translator's note: the source prints this verse number as «28 - 6-»; it is verse 286 in the sequence.]
Al-Zamakhsharī and Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed it to be conjoined to «فاتقوا», so as to conjoin a command to a command. The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] rejected this on the grounds that «فاتَّقُوا» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of the condition, so the conjoined element would be an apodosis too, since its ruling is the same as its ruling; but that is not sound, because His giving glad tidings to the believers is not consequent upon His saying «فإنْ لَمْ تَفْعَلوا».
It was also read «وبُشِّرَ», as a past verb in the passive. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is conjoined to «أُعِدَّت»." It was said: "This is not feasible on the analysis of «أُعِدَّتْ» as a ḥāl (circumstantial), because it [«وبُشِّر»] is not fit to be a ḥāl."
«البِشارة» (glad tidings) is the first news of something good or bad. They said: [it is so called] because its effect appears on the «البَشَرة», which is the outer skin of a human being. They cited:
287 - يُبَشِّرُني الغُرابُ بِبَيْنِ أهلي ... فقُلْتُ له: ثَكِلْتُكَ مِنْ بشيرِ
(The crow brings me tidings of my people's parting; so I said to it: may I be bereft of you, what a herald!)
And another said:
288 - وبَشَّرْتَنِي يا سَعْدُ أَنَّ أَحِبَّتِي ... جَفَوْنِي وأنَّ الوُدَّ موعدُهُ الحَشْرُ
(You brought me tidings, O Saʿd, that my loved ones have shunned me, and that [renewed] love's appointment is the Gathering.)
This is the view of Sībawayh; however, its use is mostly for good, and if it is used for evil it is with a qualifier, as in His saying, Exalted is He: {فَبَشِّرْهُم بِعَذَابٍ} [Āl ʿImrān: 21]; and when it is used unqualified it is for good. The apparent sense of al-Zamakhsharī's words is that it is restricted to good, because he interpreted the like of {فَبَشِّرْهُم بِعَذَابٍ} as reversal in speech, intended to increase the vexation and pain of the one being mocked. Its verb is «بَشَرَ» and «بَشَّر», light and doubled, as in his saying «بَشَرْتُ عيالي» (the verse); the doubling is for intensity with respect to the thing announced. The imperfect has been read both light and doubled; as for the past, it has only been read doubled, as in {فَبَشَّرْنَاهَا بِإِسْحَاقَ} [Hūd: 71]. There is another dialectal form: «أَبْشَرَ», like «أَكْرَمَ». Abū Ḥātim rejected the light form, but this is not correct, since its imperfect occurs. With the meaning of «البِشارة» there are also «البُشور», «التَبْشير» and «الإِبْشَار», even though their verbs differ. «البِشارة» also means beauty; «البَشير» is the beautiful one; and «تباشير الفجر» are the first signs of dawn.
[Zayd ibn ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with them both, read «وبُشِّرَ», as a past verb in the passive. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Conjoined to «أُعِدَّت»." End of quote. This is a mistake, because what it is conjoined to is [part of] the ṣila (relative clause), and there is nothing in this clause referring back to the relative noun, so it cannot be conjoined to «أُعِدَّت».]
The agent (fāʿil) of «بَشِّرْ» is either the pronoun of the Messenger, upon him be peace — and that is the clear view — or anyone from whom giving glad tidings is valid. That the ṣila of «الذين» is a past verb rather than an active participle is evidence that the one who deserves glad tidings by the grace of Allah is the one from whom faith has occurred and who has realised it, together with righteous deeds.
«الصالحات» is the plural of «صالحة», and it is one of the adjectives that have come to behave like nouns in being placed directly after governing words. [The poet] said:
289 - كيفَ الهجاءُ وما تَنْفَكُّ صالِحَةٌ ... مِنْ آلِ لأَْمٍ بظهرِ الغَيْبِ تَأْتِينِي
(How could I satirise, when a good deed from the family of Laʾm never ceases to come to me in [my] absence?)
The sign of its accusative is the kasra, because it belongs to the category of the sound feminine plural, standing in for the fatḥa, which is the basic sign of the accusative.
His saying, Exalted is He: {أَنَّ لَهُمْ جَنَّاتٍ}: «جنات» is the noun (ism) of «أنَّ», and «لهم» is a fronted khabar (predicate). Fronting the khabar of «أنَّ» and its sisters is not permissible unless it is an adverb or a preposition [phrase]. «أنَّ» together with what falls in its domain is in the position of the genitive according to al-Khalīl and al-Kisāʾī, and of the accusative according to Sībawayh and al-Farrāʾ, because the underlying form is: "And give glad tidings to those who believe that (بأنَّ) they have…"; the preposition was omitted with «أنَّ». This is a regular omission with it and with «أَنْ» that puts the imperfect in the accusative, provided ambiguity is avoided, because of their length with the ṣila. When the preposition was omitted, the aforementioned disagreement arose. Al-Khalīl and al-Kisāʾī say: it is as though the particle were present, so the genitive remains. Al-Akhfash argued for them with the poet's saying:
290 - وما زُرْتُ ليلى أنْ تَكُونَ حبيبةً ... إليَّ لا دَيْنٍ بها أنا طالِبُهْ
(I did not visit Laylā because she is dear to me, nor for a debt with her that I am claiming.)
Conjoining «دَيْنٍ» in the genitive to the position of «أن تكون» shows that it is genitive. It was said: it may be a case of conjunction by supposition (ʿaṭf al-tawahhum), so there is no proof in it. Al-Farrāʾ and Sībawayh say: we have found that when they omit the preposition they use the accusative, as in his saying:
291 - تَمُرُّونَ الديارَ وَلَمْ تَعُوجوا ... كلامُكُمُ عليَّ إذاً حَرَامُ
(You pass the dwellings and do not turn aside — then speaking with you is forbidden to me.)
i.e. "by the dwellings" (بالديار). The genitive is not permissible except in rare poetry, as in his saying:
292 - إذا قيلَ: أيُّ الناسِ شرُّ قبيلةٍ ... أَشَارتْ كليبٍ بالأَكفِّ الأصابعُ
(When it is asked: which people is the worst tribe? the fingers point with the hands at Kulayb.)
i.e. "to Kulayb" (إلى كُلَيْبٍ); and the saying of the other:
293 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... حتى تَبَذَّخَ فارتقى الأَعْلامِ
(… until he grew proud and climbed up the peaks.)
i.e. "to the peaks" (إلى الأعلام).
«الجَنَّة» is the garden; it was also said: land with trees. It is so called because it conceals (sitr) whoever is in it. From this comes «الجنين» (the foetus), because it is concealed; «المِجَنّ», the shield; likewise «الجُنَّة», because it covers its bearer; and «الجِنَّة» (the jinn), because they are concealed from people's eyes.
His saying: {تَجْرِي مِن تَحْتِهَا الأنهار}: this clause is in the position of the accusative because it is a naʿt (adjective) of «جنات». «تَجْرِي» is nominative (marfūʿ) because it is free of any accusative-governing or jussive-governing particle, and the sign of its nominative is a ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ because of heaviness. Likewise it is implied in every weak verb such as «يَدْعو» and «يَخْشَى», except that on the alif it is implied due to impossibility.
«الأنهار» is the plural of «نَهَر» with fatḥa, which is the higher (more eloquent) dialect; it also has a quiescent hāʾ [«نَهْر»]. However, the pattern أَفْعال is not regular for فَعْل with a quiescent middle radical; rather it is learned by hearing, as in «أَفْراخ», «أَزْنَاد» and «أَفراد».
A river (النهر) is smaller than a sea and larger than a stream (الجدول). Is it the channel of water or the flowing water itself? The first is more evident, because it is derived from «نَهَرْت», i.e. "I widened". Qays ibn al-Khaṭīm said, describing a spear-thrust:
294 - مَلَكْتُ بها كَفِّي فَأنْهَرْتُ فَتْقَها ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(I gripped it firmly with my hand and widened its rent …)
i.e. "I widened". From it comes «النهار» (daytime), because of the breadth of its light. It is applied to the water only figuratively, applying the name of the place to what occupies it.
{مِن تَحْتِهَا} is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «تجري». «تحت» is a place-adverb that is not used freely (lā yataṣarraf), the opposite of «فوق»; when the two are put into a genitive construct they are declined, and when cut off [from it] they are indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma. «مِنْ» is for the beginning of extent; it was also said to be redundant (zāʾida), and also that it means «في» — and both are weak.
Know that if it is said that «الجَنَّة» is land with trees, then a muḍāf must be omitted, i.e. "from beneath its palm-trees" or "its trees". If it is said that it is the trees themselves, then there is no need for that. If it is said that «الأنهار» is a name for the flowing water, then attributing flowing to it is literal; and if it is said that it is a name for the trench in which it flows, then attributing flowing to it is figurative, as in the saying of Muhalhil:
295 - نُبِّئْتُ أنَّ النارَ بعدكَ أُوْقِدَتْ ... واسْتَبَّ بعدَك يا كُلَيْبُ المَجْلِسُ
(I was told that after you the fire was kindled, and after you, O Kulayb, the assembly fell to trading insults.)
The Shaykh said: "Ibn ʿAṭiyya contradicted himself here, for he said: 'الأنهار are the waters in their long, wide channels', and then said: 'He attributed flowing to the river, though only the water flows, by way of extension and figurative usage, as He the Exalted said {وَسْئَلِ القرية} [Yūsuf: 82], and as [the poet] said: نُبِّئْتُ أنَّ النار (the verse).'"
The alif-lām in «الأنهار» is for the genus; it was also said to be for prior acquaintance (al-ʿahd), because they are mentioned in Sūrat al-Qitāl [Muḥammad]. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It may be a substitute for the pronoun, as in His saying {واشتعل الرأس شَيْباً} [Maryam: 4], i.e. 'its rivers'" — meaning that the underlying form is «واشتعلَ رأسي», and «أل» was made a substitute for the yāʾ of the first person. This is not the doctrine of the Basrans; rather some of the Kufans held it. It is rejected on the grounds that if «أل» were a substitute for the pronoun, they would not be combined; yet they have been combined. Al-Nābigha said:
296 - رَحِيبٌ قِطابُ الجَيْبِ منها رفيقةٌ ... بجَسِّ الندامى بَضَّةُ المُتَجَرِّدِ
(Wide is the opening of her collar, gentle to the touch of boon companions, soft-skinned where she is unclothed.)
[So he said: «الجيبِ منها».] As for what occurs whose apparent sense is that, its interpretation will come in its place.
His saying, Exalted is He: {كُلَّمَا رُزِقُواْ مِنْهَا مِن ثَمَرَةٍ}: discussion of «كُلَّما» has preceded. What governs it here is «قالوا». «منها» is attached to «رُزِقوا», and «مِنْ» is for the beginning of extent; likewise «مِنْ ثمرةٍ», because it is a badal (substitute) from His saying «منها» — a substitute of inclusion (badal ishtimāl) with repetition of the governing word. We said "substitute of inclusion" only because two particles with one meaning cannot be attached to one governing word except by way of substitution or conjunction. Al-Zamakhsharī allowed «مِنْ» to be explicative (li-l-bayān), as when you say "I saw in you a lion" (رأيت منكَ أسداً). There is an objection to this, because a condition of that is that a relative noun can take its place and that what precedes it be defined with the generic «أل»; moreover there is nothing before it to be explained by it, and its being an explanation of what follows it is very far-fetched and is not the accepted usage.
«رِزْقاً» is the second object of «رُزِقوا», and it has the meaning of «مَرْزوق» (thing provided). Its being a maṣdar is far-fetched because of His saying {هذا الذي رُزِقْنَا مِن قَبْلُ وَأُتُواْ بِهِ مُتَشَابِهاً}: a maṣdar is not brought "resembling"; rather it is the thing provided that is brought so.
His saying: «قالوا: هذا الذي رُزِقْنا مِنْ قبلُ»: «قالوا» is what governs «كلما», as preceded. {هذا الذي رُزِقْنَا} is a mubtadaʾ and khabar in the position of the accusative by the saying [as its object]. The referring pronoun of the relative is omitted since it fulfils the conditions, i.e. «رُزِقْناه». «مِنْ قَبلُ» is attached to it, and «مِنْ» is for the beginning of extent. When «قبلُ» was cut off [from the genitive construct] it became indeclinable, and it was made indeclinable on the ḍamma only because that is a vowel it did not have in its declined state.
There is disagreement over this clause. It was said: it has no grammatical position because it is resumptive, as though, when the gardens were described, it was asked: "What is their state?" and it was said: "Whenever they are provided, they say…". It was also said: it has a position. Then there was disagreement over it. It was said: nominative, as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ — and there is disagreement over that mubtadaʾ: it was said it is the pronoun of the gardens, i.e. "they are [such that] whenever…"; and it was said it is the pronoun of «الذين آمنوا», i.e. "they, whenever they are provided, say that." It was also said: its position is accusative as a ḥāl, the one it describes (ṣāḥib al-ḥāl) being either «الذين آمنوا» or «جنات» — this being permissible even though it is indefinite because it has been specified by the adjective. On these two views it is an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara), because at the time of the glad tidings of the gardens they were not being provided with that. It was also said: its position is accusative as another naʿt of «جنات».
His saying: {وَأُتُواْ بِهِ مُتَشَابِهاً}: the apparent view is that it is a resumptive clause. Al-Zamakhsharī said of it: "It is like your saying: 'So-and-so — how excellent [he is] to so-and-so!', and 'How good is what he did!', and 'He held such-and-such an opinion — and it was right'; and of this kind is {وجعلوا أَعِزَّةَ أَهْلِهَآ أَذِلَّةً وكذلك يَفْعَلُونَ} [al-Naml: 34], and similar clauses that are inserted in speech parenthetically and have no position, for confirmation." I say: by its being parenthetical he means between the descriptions of the states of the people of Paradise, since after it comes {وَلَهُمْ فِيهَآ أَزْوَاجٌ}; and if it is parenthetical it likewise has no position. It was also said: it is conjoined to «قالوا». And it was said: its position is accusative as a ḥāl, the one it describes being the agent of «قالوا», i.e. "they said these words in this state"; and «قد» must be implied before the verb, i.e. «وقد أُتوا». The underlying form of «أُتُوا» is «أُتِيُوا», like «ضُرِبوا», and it underwent weakening like its counterparts. It was also read «وأتَوا» in the active, the pronoun referring to the youths and servants, since they are explicitly mentioned in more than one place. The pronoun in «به» refers to the thing provided, namely the fruits, just as «هذا» points to it. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It refers to what was provided in this world and the Hereafter, because His saying {هذا الذي رُزِقْنَا مِن قَبْلُ} implicitly contains mention of what they were provided in both abodes. A parallel to this is His saying, Exalted is He: {إِن يَكُنْ غَنِيّاً أَوْ فَقَيراً فالله أولى بِهِمَا} [al-Nisāʾ: 135], i.e. to the two kinds, the rich and the poor, indicated by His saying 'rich or poor'." End of quote.
I say: by his saying "implicitly contains mention of what they were provided in both abodes" he means that since the implied form is "[this is] like that which we were provided", it implicitly contains both things provided together, just as your saying "Zayd is like Ḥātim" implicitly contains both Zayd and Ḥātim. The Shaykh said: "What he said is not evident, because the apparent sense is that it refers to what is provided in the Hereafter only, since that is what is being spoken about and what is likened to what they were provided before — especially if you interpret the 'before' as being in Paradise, for then it necessarily refers only to what is provided in Paradise. Likewise if you analyse the clause as a ḥāl, since the implied form becomes: 'They said: this is [like] that which we were provided before — and they had been brought it [resembling]', because what prompted them to this saying is that they were brought it resembling. On the assumption that it is conjoined to «قالوا», it cannot refer to what is provided in both abodes, because the bringing in that case cannot be past in meaning, since what governs «كلما» and what falls in its domain must here be future in meaning, as it is not devoid of the sense of condition. On the assumption that it is resumptive, that is not evident either, because these clauses speak about Paradise and its states."

semin-durr:6-6.t:
The saying of the Exalted: {إِنَّ الذين كَفَرُواْ سَوَآءٌ عَلَيْهِمْ أَأَنذَرْتَهُمْ} — the verse. «إنَّ» is a particle of emphasis that puts the noun in the accusative and the khabar (predicate) in the nominative, contrary to the Kufans, [who hold] that its nominative is due to what governed it before «إنَّ» entered. It may be lightened, and then it either governs or is left ungoverning; it may then be directly followed by verbs, but mostly by the abrogating verbs (nawāsikh). It is distinguished by the entry of the lām of inception (lām al-ibtidāʾ) into its khabar, or into what the khabar governs when placed first, or into its noun when placed later. Its khabar may not be placed first unless it is an adverbial or a genitive phrase. It is also distinguished by [allowing] conjunction to the position of its noun. It and its sisters have many rules that it is not fitting to mention in this book.
{الذين كَفَرُواْ} is its noun; «كفروا» is the ṣila (relative clause) with the returning pronoun; «لا يؤمنون» is its khabar, and what is between them is parenthetical. «سواءٌ» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «أأنذرتهم» with what follows it is equivalent, by interpretation, to a single word / which is the khabar; the implied form is: "Warning and its absence are equal to them." No link (rābiṭ) was needed here, because the clause is the mubtadaʾ itself. «سواءٌ» may also be a khabar placed first and «أنذرتهم», with the interpretation mentioned, a mubtadaʾ placed later, its implied form being "Warning and its absence are equal." This clause may be parenthetical between the noun of «إنَّ» and its khabar, which is «لا يؤمنون», as has preceded; or it may itself be the khabar of «إنَّ», with the clause «لا يؤمنون» in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), or resumptive, or a supplication against them that they not believe — which is far-fetched — or a khabar after a khabar according to the view of whoever allows that. «سواءٌ» alone may also be the khabar of «إنَّ», with «أأنذرتَهُم» and what follows it, by the interpretation mentioned, in the position of the nominative as its fāʿil (agent); the implied form is: "Warning and its absence became equal in their view"; and «لا يؤمنون» according to the views that have preceded, I mean the ḥāl, resumption, supplication and being a khabar.
The hamza in «أأنذرتَهُمْ» originally is for interrogation, but that is not intended here, since what is intended is equalization (taswiya). «أأنْذَرْتَهم» is a verb, its agent and its object.
«أم» here is a conjunction and is called "connected" (muttaṣila). There are two conditions for it to be connected. The first: that it be preceded by a hamza of interrogation or of equalization, in wording or by implication. The second: that what follows it be a single word or interpreted as a single word, as in this verse, for the clause in it is interpreted as a single word, as has preceded. Its answer is one of the two things or of the things, and it is not answered with "yes" or "no". If a condition is lacking it is called "cut off" (munqaṭiʿa) and "separated" (munfaṣila); it is then interpreted as bal plus the hamza, and its answer is "yes" or "no". It has other rules.
«لم» is a jussive particle meaning negation of the past absolutely, contrary to whoever restricts it to the discontinued past; evidence of this is the saying of the Exalted {وَلَمْ أَكُنْ بِدُعَآئِكَ رَبِّ شَقِيّاً} [Maryam: 4], {لَمْ يَلِدْ وَلَمْ يُولَدْ} [al-Ikhlāṣ: 3], in which discontinuity is inconceivable. It is particular to imperfect forms, but it makes them past in meaning, as has preceded. Did it change the form but not the meaning, or the meaning but not the form? Two views, the more apparent being the second. Its jussive verb is sometimes omitted.
Kufr is covering; from it the night was called kāfir; [the poet] said:
137 - فَوَرَدَتْ قبلَ انبلاجِ الفجرِ ... وابنُ ذُكَاءٍ كامِنٌ في كَفْرِ
(She came to the water before the breaking of dawn, while the son of Dhukāʾ [the morning] lay hidden in darkness.)
Another said:
138 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ...
أَلْقَتْ ذُكاءُ يمينَها في كافِر
(Dhukāʾ [the sun] laid its right hand in the coverer [the night].)
Another said:
139 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... في ليلةٍ كَفَر النجومَ غَمامُها
(On a night whose clouds covered the stars.)
«سواء» is a noun meaning equality (istiwāʾ), so it is a noun of the maṣdar (ism maṣdar). It is used as a qualifier in the sense of mustawin (equal), and then it bears a pronoun and puts an overt noun in the nominative; from this is their saying "marartu bi-rajulin sawāʾin wa-l-ʿadamu" (I passed by a man equal, he and nothingness), with «العدم» in the nominative as conjoined to the pronoun latent in «سواء»; the absence of separation is anomalous. It is not made dual or plural, either because it was originally a maṣdar, or because its dual is dispensed with by the dual of its counterpart, which is «سِيّ» meaning "like"; you say "humā siyyān", i.e. two alike; [the poet] said:
140 - مَنْ يَفْعَلِ الحسناتِ اللهُ يشكُرها ... والشرُّ بالشرِّ عند الله سِيَّانِ
(Whoever does good deeds, Allah appreciates them; and evil for evil are alike with Allah.)
Yet «سواءان» has been reported. The poet said:
141 - وليلٍ تقول الناسُ في ظُلُماته ... سواءٌ صحيحاتُ العيونِ وعُورُها
(Many a night in whose darkness people say: sound eyes and blind ones are equal.)
So «سواءٌ» is a khabar of a plural, namely «صحيحات». Its root meaning is justice; Zuhayr said: 142 - أَرُونا سُبَّةً لا عيبَ فيها ... يُسَوِّي بيننا فيها السَّواءُ
(Show us a plan with no fault in it, in which fairness judges equally between us.)
i.e. justice judges fairly between us. It is not the adverbial with which exception is made in your saying "qāmū sawāʾa Zayd" (they stood except Zayd), even though it shares its wording. Ibn ʿAṭiyya transmitted from al-Fārisī the four well-known dialectal forms of the «سواء» used for exception; this is strange, for those forms belong to the adverbial, not to «سواء» meaning equality. Most often there follows it a clause headed by the hamza balanced by «أم», as in this verse; it is sometimes omitted because it is indicated, as in the saying of the Exalted {فاصبروا أَوْ لاَ تَصْبِرُواْ سَوَآءٌ عَلَيْكُمْ} [al-Ṭūr: 16], i.e. whether you are patient or not patient. It is sometimes followed by an interrogative noun governed by what comes after it, as in the saying of ʿAlqama:
143 - سَواءٌ عليه أيَّ حينٍ أتيتَه ... أساعَة نَحْسٍ تُتَّقى أم بأَسْعَدِ
(It is all the same to him at whatever time you come to him — whether an ill-omened hour to be guarded against, or a most fortunate one.)
«أيَّ حين» is in the accusative by «أتيتَه». It is sometimes stripped of interrogation, which is the original, e.g.:
144 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... سواءٌ صحيحاتُ العيون وعُورُها
(Sound eyes and blind ones are equal.)
Indhār is frightening (warning). Some said: it is conveying [a message]; and it hardly occurs except in a frightening whose time allows for taking precautions; if its time does not allow for precaution, it is a notification (ishʿār), not a warning. [The poet] said:
145 - أنذَرْتُ عَمْرَاً وهو في مَهَل ... قبلَ الصباحِ فقد عصى عَمْرُو
(I warned ʿAmr while he had time, before the morning; but ʿAmr disobeyed.)
It is doubly transitive; the Exalted said {إِنَّآ أَنذَرْنَاكُمْ عَذَاباً} [al-Nabaʾ: 40], {أَنذَرْتُكُمْ صَاعِقَةً} [Fuṣṣilat: 13]. So the second [object] in this verse is omitted, its implied form being "Have you warned them of the punishment or not warned them of it?" It is better not to imply an object for it, as has preceded in similar cases.
The hamza in «أَنْذَرَ» is for transitivity. It has preceded that the sense of interrogation is not intended here. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "Its wording is the wording of interrogation and its meaning is a statement; the wording of interrogation was applied to it only because it contains the equalization that is in interrogation. Do you not see that when you say as a statement 'It is the same to me whether you stood or sat', and when you say as a question 'Did Zayd go out or stand?', the two matters are equal for you — these two in the statement and these two in the question — along with the lack of knowledge of which one specifically? So since equalization covered both, the wording of interrogation was applied to the statement because it shares vagueness with it. Every interrogation is an equalization, even if not every equalization is an interrogation." This is good speech.
However, the Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] disputed his saying "«أأنْذَرْتَهُم أم لم تنذرْهم»: its wording is the wording of interrogation and its meaning is a statement" with something whose meaning is: that this, whose form is the form of interrogation, does not mean a statement, because it is interpreted as a single word, as has preceded; on this basis it alone is not in the sense of a statement, / because a statement is a clause while this is interpreted as a single word. This is a verbal dispute.
A pause has been transmitted on his saying «أم لم تُنذِرْهم», beginning [anew] with his saying «لا يؤمنون» as a clause of mubtadaʾ and khabar. This ought to be rejected and given no attention, even though al-Hudhalī transmitted it in his "al-Waqf wa-l-Ibtidāʾ".
«أَأَنْذَرْتَهُمْ» was read with both hamzas pronounced fully (taḥqīq), which is the dialect of Banū Tamīm; with the second lightened "between-between" (bayna bayna), which is the dialect of the Ḥijāz; and with an alif inserted between the two hamzas, with lightening and with full pronunciation; from this is:
146 - أيا ظبيةَ الوَعْساء بين جُلاجِلٍ ... وبين النقا آأنتِ أَمْ أمُّ سالمِ
(O gazelle of the soft sands between Julājil and al-Naqā — is it you, or Umm Sālim?)
Another said:
147 - تطَالَلْتُ فاسْتَشْرَفْتُه فَعَرَفْتُهُ ... فقلت له آأنتَ زيدُ الأرانبِ
(I stretched up, looked out at him, and recognized him; I said to him: "Is it you, Zayd of the hares?")
It is transmitted from Warsh that he replaced the second [hamza] with a pure alif. Al-Zamakhsharī attributed this reading to error (laḥn); he said: "because it leads to combining two quiescents not in their proper manner, and because lightening such a hamza is only 'between-between'." This from him is not correct, since this reading is established by mass transmission (tawātur). The readers have much practice and widespread detail concerning verses like this.

semin-durr:17-17.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {مَثَلُهُمْ كَمَثَلِ الذي استوقد نَاراً}: «مثلهم» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «كمثل» is a preposition and its genitive noun forming its khabar (predicate), so it is attached to (mutaʿalliq) something omitted according to the rule of the chapter; no heed is paid to the dissent of whoever says that the kāf of comparison is not attached to anything. The implied form is: "their likeness is established as the likeness…". Abū al-Baqāʾ and Ibn ʿAṭiyya allowed the kāf to be a noun which is itself the khabar, and he cited as a parallel the poet's saying:
207 - أَتَنْتَهُون ولن ينهى ذوي شَطَط ... كالطَّعْن يَذْهَبُ فيه الزيتُ والفُتُل
(Will you desist? Nothing restrains the transgressors like a thrust in which the oil and the wicks disappear.)
This is the doctrine of al-Akhfash: he allows the kāf to be a noun without restriction. As for the doctrine of Sībawayh, he does not allow that except in poetry. As for citing the verse as a parallel, it is not as he said, because in the verse we are compelled to make it a noun since it is an agent, unlike in the verse of the Quran. What ought to be said is that the kāf of comparison has three states. A state in which it must be a noun: when it is an agent, or made genitive by a preposition or by annexation. An example of the agent is «أتنتهون ولن ينهى…», the verse. An example of its being made genitive by a preposition is the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:
208 - وَرُحْنا بكابْنِ الماء يُجْنَبُ وَسْطَنا ... تَصَوَّبُ فيه العينُ طوراً وتَرْتقي
(We went off in the evening with [a horse] like the water-bird, led at our side in our midst; the eye now descends over it, now rises.)
and his saying:
209 - وَزَعْتُ بكالهَراوةِ أَعْوَجِيٍّ ... إذا جَرَت الرياحُ لها وِثابا
(I held back [the enemy] with a cudgel-like steed of Aʿwaj's breed, leaping when the winds race.)
An example of its being made genitive by annexation is his saying:
210 - فَصُيِّروا مثلَ كعَصْفٍ مأكولْ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(So they were made like eaten-up straw…)
A state in which it must be a particle: when it occurs as a ṣila (relative clause), as in «جاء الذي كزيدٍ», because making it a noun entails omitting the resumptive pronoun that is a mubtadaʾ without the ṣila being long, which is disallowed by the Basrans. And a state in which both are allowed: whatever is other than that, as in «زيد كعمرو». Whoever claimed that it is redundant (zāʾida) in the noble verse, i.e. "their likeness is the likeness of the one who…", went far off; he cited as a parallel the saying «فصيّروا مثل كعصف», as if he made al-mithl and al-mathal one meaning. The correct view is that al-mathal here means "story", the implied form being: "their description and story is like the story of the one who kindled a fire"; so it is not redundant on this interpretation. But al-mathal with fatḥa originally means «مِثْل» and «مَثيل» ("like, similar"), as in «شِبْه», «شَبَه» and «شَبيه». It has also been said: rather it is originally "description". As for al-mathal in His saying «ضرب مثلاً», it is the current saying (proverb) that has some strangeness in some respect; for that reason its wording is preserved and not changed: so to everyone who neglected a matter that is hard to remedy one says «الصيفَ ضيّعتِ اللبنَ» ("In summer you [f.] wasted the milk"), whether the one addressed is singular, dual or plural, masculine or feminine, so that it thereby indicates the intent behind it.
«الذي» is in the position of genitive by annexation. It is a relative for the masculine singular, but what is meant by it here is a plural; that is why its meaning was observed in His saying {ذَهَبَ الله بِنُورِهِمْ وَتَرَكَهُمْ}, where the pronoun refers back to it in the plural. It is preferable to say that «الذي» occurred as an adjective of something that conveys plurality, and then that qualified noun was omitted because it is indicated; the implied form is: "their likeness is as the likeness of the party who kindled" or "the group who kindled". Thus the adjective was observed once, so the pronoun refers back to it in the singular in His saying «استوقد» and «حوله», and the qualified noun another time, so the pronoun refers back to it in the plural in His saying «بنورهم» and «وتركهم».
Abū al-Baqāʾ erred in making this verse of the class from which the nūn was dropped for lightness, the origin being «الذين», then lightened by deletion. It is as if he made it like His saying, Exalted is He, in the other verse {وَخُضْتُمْ كالذي خاضوا} [al-Tawba: 69], and the poet's saying:
211 - وإنَّ الذي حانَتْ بِفَلْجٍ دِمَاؤُهم ... هُمُ القومُ كلُّ القومِ يا أمَّ خالدِ
(Those whose blood was spilled for nothing at Falj — they are the people, all the people, O Umm Khālid.)
the origin being «كالذين خاضوا» and «وإنّ الذين حانت». This is a gross mistake, because if it were of the class from which the nūn was dropped, agreement of the pronoun in the plural would be obligatory, as in «كالذي خاضوا» and «دماؤهم». Since He, Exalted is He, said «استوقد» in the singular form, one of the two matters mentioned earlier becomes necessary: either making it of the class of the singular occurring in place of the plural because the genus is meant by it, or of the class where it occurs as an adjective of a qualified noun conveying plurality.
Al-Zamakhsharī said something whose meaning is: this verse is like His saying, Exalted is He, {كالذي خاضوا}, and he gave two reasons justifying that. One is that, since «الذي» is a link (wuṣla) for qualifying definite nouns, it was fitting to delete part of it because of its length. He said: "That is why they wore it down by deletion: they deleted its yāʾ, then its kasra, then limited themselves to its lām in active and passive participles." The second reason is that its plural is not like the plural of other words with wāw and nūn; that is only a sign for increasing the indication — do you not see that in all the other relatives the plural and singular forms are the same? This view is open to objection in two respects. First: his statement is explicit in making this verse of the class of deleting the nūn of «الذين», and there is in it what was said above, that the pronoun should have agreed in the plural, as in the other verse he cited as a parallel. Second: he believed the relative «أل» to be a remnant of «الذي», and it is not so; rather the relative «أل» is an independent relative noun, i.e. not taken from anything — besides which, what is preponderant in terms of proof is that the relative «أل» is a particle, not a noun, as will come. And no one who wishes to support al-Zamakhsharī's view may support it by their saying that the mīm in their phrase «مُ اللهِ» is a remnant of «ايمُن», so that if they wore «ايمن» down by deletion until it became one letter, it is more fitting to say so of what remained as two letters — because «أل» is additional to the essence of «الذي», so they would have deleted the whole noun and left what is additional to it, unlike the mīm of «ايمن». Moreover, the view that the mīm is a remnant of «أيمن» is a weak, rejected view which the view of the majority refuses.
In «الذي» there are dialect forms. The best known is retaining the yāʾ quiescent. It may be doubled with kasra in all cases, or inflected with the case endings, as in his saying:
212 - وليسَ المالُ فاعلَمْهُ بمالٍ ... وإنْ أرضاكَ إلا لِلَّذيِّ
يَنالُ به العَلاءَ ويَصْطَفيه ... لأقربِ أَقْرِبيه وللقَصِيِّ
(Wealth — know it — is not wealth, even if it pleases you, except for the one who attains high rank by it and keeps it for the nearest of his relatives and for the distant.)
This may be indeclinable or declinable. [The yāʾ] may be deleted with what precedes it quiescent, as in another's saying:
213 - فلم أَرَ بيْتاً كان أكثرَ بهجةً ... مِنَ اللذْ به من آلِ عَزَّةَ عامرُ
(I have not seen a house more splendid than the one in which a resident of ʿAzza's family dwells.)
or with kasra, as in his saying:
214 - واللذِ لو شاء لكانَتْ بَرّاً ... أو جبلاً أَصَمَّ مُشَمْخِراً
(And the One who, had He willed, it would have been dry land, or a solid towering mountain.)
The same dialect forms are found in «التي» as well. Someone said: "Their saying that these are dialect forms is not good, because these have only come in poetic necessity, so they ought not to be called dialect forms."
«استوقد» is «استفعل» in the meaning of «أفعل», as «استجاب» means «أجاب»; this is the view of al-Akhfash, and on it is the poet's saying:
215 - وداعٍ دعا يا مَنْ يُجيبُ إلى الندى ... فلم يَسْتَجِبْهُ عندَ ذاكَ مُجيبُ
(Many a caller called: "O who will answer to generosity?" — and no answerer answered him then.)
i.e. "did not answer him". It has also been said: rather the sīn is for seeking. The view of al-Akhfash was preferred because its being for seeking requires omitting a clause — do you not see that the meaning would be "they sought a fire and kindled it, and when it lit up…" — because lighting up is not caused by seeking, it is caused only by kindling.
The fāʾ in «فلمّا» is causal. Ibn al-Samayfaʿ read «كمثل الذين» in the plural form, with «استوقد» in the singular. It is problematic, and they explained it in ways weaker than it: namely tawahhum (as if the speaker had imagined another construction), i.e. as if he had uttered «مَن», since he referred a singular pronoun to a plural, as in their saying «ضربني وضربتُ قومَك», i.e. "whoever struck me"; or [the pronoun] refers to an active participle understood from «استوقد», and the resumptive referring to the relative is omitted, even though the conditions of omission are not complete, the implied form being: "a kindler kindled it for them". This reading strengthens the view of whoever says that the origin of «الذي» is «الذين», with the nūn deleted.
«لمّا» is a particle of "occurrence for occurrence" (wujūb li-wujūb); this is the doctrine of Sībawayh. Al-Fārisī claimed, and Abū al-Baqāʾ followed him, that it is an adverb meaning "when" (ḥīna), and that what governs it is its apodosis. This was refuted on the ground that it is answered by negative «ما» and by «إذا» of surprise. He, Exalted is He, said: {فَلَمَّا جَآءَهُمْ نَذِيرٌ مَّا زَادَهُمْ إِلاَّ نُفُوراً} [Fāṭir: 42], and He, Exalted is He, said: {فَلَمَّا نَجَّاهُمْ إِلَى البر إِذَا هُمْ يُشْرِكُونَ} [al-ʿAnkabūt: 65]; and what comes after negative «ما» and «إذا» of surprise does not govern what precedes them, so its being an adverb is excluded.
«لمّا» is also jussive-governing for one verb, its meaning being negation of the past connected to the present time; its jussive verb may be omitted. The poet said:
216 - فجِئْتُ قبورَهم بَدْءاً ولَمَّا ... فنادَيْتُ القبورَ فلم يُجِبْنَهْ
(I came to their graves as a newcomer, though not yet [their chief], and called out to the graves, but they did not answer.)
It also means «إلا»; He, Exalted is He, said: {وَإِن كُلُّ ذَلِكَ لَمَّا مَتَاعُ الحياة الدنيا} [al-Zukhruf: 35], in the reading of whoever read it so.
«أضاء» may be intransitive or transitive. If transitive, «ما» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and is a relative, and «حوله» is an adverb of place with the genitive by it, being its ṣila; it is not declined [freely], and with its meaning is «حَوال»; the poet said:
217 - وأنا أَمْشِي الدَّأَلَى حَوالَكا ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(While I walk with a hobbling gait around you…)
Both are made dual — he (peace be upon him) said: «اللهم حوالَيْنا» ("O Allah, around us") — and both have the plural «أحوال».
«ما» may also be an indefinite qualified noun and «حوله» its adjective. If [«أضاء»] is intransitive, the agent is likewise the pronoun of the fire, «ما» is redundant, and «حوله» is accusative as an adverb governed by «أضاء». Al-Zamakhsharī allowed «ما» to be the agent, either relative or an indefinite qualified noun, the verb being feminine according to the meaning, the implied form being: "when the side that was around him lit up", or "a side around him".
Abū al-Baqāʾ also allowed it to be accusative as an adverb, being then either in the meaning of «الذي» or an indefinite qualified noun, the implied form being: "when the fire lit up the place which was around him", or "a place around him". For he said: "One says «ضاءت النار» and «أضاءت» with one meaning; on this «ما» is an adverb, and in «ما» there are three aspects: first, that it means «الذي»; second, it is an indefinite qualified noun, i.e. a place around him; third, it is redundant." End of quotation.
His wording is open to some dispute: after judging «ما» to be adverbial, how can it then be redundant? He only meant: in this «ما», in general, there are three aspects. The poet's saying:
218 - أضاءَت لهم أحسابُهم ووجُوهُهم ... دجى الليلِ حتى نَظَّم الجَزْعَ ثاقِبُهْ
(Their noble lineage and their faces lit up the dark of night for them, so that the one piercing onyx beads could string them.)
admits transitivity and intransitivity, like the noble verse. Ibn al-Samayfaʿ read «ضاءت» as a triliteral.
His saying, Exalted is He: {ذَهَبَ الله بِنُورِهِمْ}: the apparent view is that this clause is the apodosis of «لمّا». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Its apodosis is omitted, the implied form being: when it lit up, it died out", and he made this more eloquent than mentioning the apodosis, and made the clause {ذَهَبَ الله بِنُورِهِمْ} resumptive or a badal (substitute) from the clause of the simile. Some refuted this in two ways. First: this is supplying something while there exists what makes it unnecessary, so there is no need for it, since supplying omitted elements is only done when necessary. Second: a verbal clause is not substituted from a nominal clause.
«بنورهم» is attached to «ذهب», and the bāʾ in it is for transitivity (taʿdiya), synonymous with the hamza in making transitive; this is the doctrine of the majority. Abū al-ʿAbbās [al-Mubarrad] claimed that there is a difference between them: with the bāʾ the agent's accompanying the object in the action he does to it is entailed, while with the hamza it is not. If you say «ذهبتُ بزيد», you must have accompanied him in going and gone with him; if you say «أذهبتُه», it may be that you accompanied him and may be that you did not. The majority refuted al-Mubarrad with this verse, because His accompanying them, Exalted is He, in going is impossible. But Abū al-Ḥasan Ibn ʿUṣfūr answered this by saying that it may be that He, Exalted is He, attributed to Himself a going that befits Him, as He attributed to Himself coming and arriving in a sense befitting Him. He is refuted rather by the poet's saying:
219 - ديارُ التي كانت ونحن على مِنى ... تَحِلُّ بنا لولا نَجاءُ الرَّكائِب
(The abodes of her who, while we were at Minā, would have released us [from iḥrām], were it not for the swiftness of the mounts.)
i.e. she would make us free of iḥrām after we had been in iḥrām for the pilgrimage, while she was not in iḥrām so as to accompany them in release. Likewise the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:
220 - كُمَيْتٍ يَزِلُّ اللَّبْدُ عن حالِ مَتْنِه ... كما زَلَّتِ الصَّفْواءُ بالمُتَنَزَّلِ
(A bay horse from the middle of whose back the saddle-felt slips, as the smooth rock makes the one alighting on it slip.)
Al-ṣafw is the rock, and it did not accompany the one it makes slip.
The pronoun in «بنورهم» refers to the meaning of «الذي», as said. Someone said: it refers to an omitted muḍāf, the implied form being "like the likeness of the companions of the one who kindled". This speaker needed this implication; he said: "So that the thing compared and the thing compared to correspond, because the thing compared is plural; if this muḍāf, «أصحاب», were not implied, it would follow that a plural is compared to a singular, namely the one who kindled." End of quotation.
I do not know what led this speaker to disallow comparing a plural to a singular in a quality uniting them. Moreover, the thing compared and the thing compared to are only the two stories; the comparison occurred only between two stories, one annexed to a plural and the other to a singular.
His saying, Exalted is He: {وَتَرَكَهُمْ فِي ظُلُمَاتٍ لاَّ يُبْصِرُونَ}: this clause is conjoined to His saying «ذهب الله». The origin of al-tark is leaving alone, and it is used to mean "making [into]", in which case it takes two objects according to the correct view, as in the poet's saying:
221 - أَمَرْتُكَ الخير فافعلْ ما أُمِرْتَ به ... فقد تَرَكْتُكَ ذا مال وذا نَشَبِ
(I commanded you to do good, so do what you were commanded; I have left you possessed of wealth and property.)
If we say it takes two objects, the first object is the pronoun, the second object is «في ظلمات», and «لا يبصرون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial); it is a corroborative ḥāl (muʾakkida), because whoever is in darkness does not see. The possessor of the ḥāl is either the accusative pronoun or the nominative pronoun latent in the preposition-and-genitive. It is not allowed that «في ظلمات» be a ḥāl and «لا يبصرون» the second object, because the second object is originally a khabar, and a khabar is not brought for emphasis; if you make «في ظلمات» a ḥāl, not seeing is understood from it, so your saying «لا يبصرون» after that would convey nothing but emphasis — but emphasis is not the business of predicates, rather the business of ḥāls, since they are surplus elements (faḍalāt). What supports what I have said is that when the grammarians parsed the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:
222 - إذا ما بكى مِنْ خَلْفِها انصَرفَتْ له ... بشِقٍّ وشِقٍّ عندنا لم يُحَوَّلِ
(When he cried behind her, she turned to him with one half, while a half with us was not turned away.)
they parsed «شِقّ» as mubtadaʾ and «عندنا» as its khabar, and «لم يحوّل» as a corroborative ḥāl clause. They said: beginning with an indefinite was allowed because it is a place of detailing (tafṣīl). They refused to make «لم يحوّل» the khabar and «عندنا» an adjective of «شق» licensing beginning with it, saying: because its meaning is understood from his saying «عندنا», since if it is with him it is known from it that it was not turned away. Abū al-Baqāʾ parsed it that way [Translator's note: i.e. with «لا يبصرون» as second object], and it is rejected by what I have mentioned to you.
If we make «لا يبصرون» the second object, «في ظلمات» may be attached to it or to «تركهم», the implied form being: "He left them not seeing in darknesses". If «ترك» takes one object, «في ظلمات» is attached to «ترك» and «لا يبصرون» is a corroborative ḥāl. «في ظلمات» may also be a ḥāl of the accusative pronoun in «تركهم», so it is attached to something omitted, and «لا يبصرون» is also a ḥāl: either of the accusative pronoun in «تركهم», so that it has two ḥāls and the disagreement mentioned earlier applies; or of the nominative pronoun latent in the preposition-and-genitive before it, so they are two nested (mutadākhila) ḥāls.

semin-durr:18-18.t:
The majority read them in the nominative, as the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "they are deaf, dumb, blind". The well-known disagreement about multiple predicates comes in here. Whoever allows that applies the verse to it without interpretation. Whoever disallows it says: these predicates, though multiple in wording, are one in meaning, because the meaning is: they do not speak the truth because of their blindness and deafness; so it is of the class of «هذا حُلوٌ حامِضٌ» ("this is sweet-sour"), i.e. sourish, and «هو أعسرُ يَسَرٌ», i.e. ambidextrous, and the poet's saying:
223 - ينامُ بإحدى مُقْلَتَيْهِ ويتَّقي ... بأخرى المَنايا فهو يَقْظانُ هاجِعُ
(He sleeps with one of his eyes and guards against death with the other, so he is awake and asleep.)
i.e. wary. Or a mubtadaʾ is implied for each predicate, the implied form being: "they are deaf, they are dumb, they are blind". The meaning is that they combine these three qualities; were it not for that, this verse could be of the class where the predicate is multiple because the subject is multiple, as in your saying «الزيدون فقهاءُ شعراءُ كاتبون» ("the Zayds are jurists, poets, scribes"), for it may mean that some of them are jurists, some poets and some scribes, and that they do not combine these three qualities, but some are distinguished by jurisprudence, others by poetry and others by writing.
They were read in the accusative, and in it there are three aspects. First: it is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and there are two views on this: one, it is a ḥāl of the accusative pronoun in «تركهم»; the other, of the nominative one in «لا يبصرون». Second: accusative of censure (dhamm), as in His saying {حَمَّالَةَ الحطب} [al-Masad: 4] and another's saying:
224 - سَقَوْني النَّسْءَ ثم تَكَنَّفوني ... عُدَاةَ اللهِ مِنْ كَذِبٍ وزُورِ
(They gave me diluted milk to drink, then surrounded me — enemies of Allah, out of lying and falsehood.)
i.e. "I censure the enemies of Allah". Third: that it is accusative by «ترك», i.e. "He left them deaf, dumb, blind".
Al-ṣamam is an ailment that prevents hearing; its origin is from hardness: one says «قناةٌ صمّاء», i.e. a hard spear-shaft. It has also been said its origin is from being blocked; from it «صَمَمْتُ القارورة», i.e. I stopped up the flask. Al-bakam is an ailment that prevents speech; it has been said it is lack of understanding, and it has been said the abkam is one born mute.
His saying {فَهُمْ لاَ يَرْجِعُونَ} is an informative clause conjoined to the informative clause before it. It has been said: rather the first is an imprecation against them with deafness; there is no need for that. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It has been said that «فهم لا يرجعون» is a ḥāl; this is a mistake, because the fāʾ sets in sequence, and there is no sequence in ḥāls." «رجع» is intransitive and transitive under two considerations — Hudhayl say «أرجعه غيره». When it means «عاد» ("returned") it is intransitive; when it means «أعاد» ("brought back") it is transitive. The noble verse admits both; if we make it transitive, the object is omitted, the implied form being "they do not return an answer", like His saying {إِنَّهُ على رَجْعِهِ لَقَادِرٌ} [al-Ṭāriq: 8]. Some claimed it is made to include the meaning of «صار» ("became"), so it puts the noun in the nominative and the predicate in the accusative, and they made of this his saying (peace be upon him): «لا ترجعوا بعدي كفاراً يضرب بعضكم رقاب بعض» ("Do not become, after me, disbelievers, striking one another's necks"); whoever disallows its being treated like «صار» makes the accusative a ḥāl.

semin-durr:7-7.t:
The saying of the Exalted: {خَتَمَ الله على قُلُوبِهمْ} … the verse. {على قُلُوبِهمْ} is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «خَتَم». «على سمعهم» may be conjoined to «قلوبهم», which is the apparent [reading] because this is stated explicitly — I mean attributing the sealing to hearing — in the saying of the Exalted {وَخَتَمَ على سَمْعِهِ} [al-Jāthiya: 23]. It may also be a khabar (predicate) placed first, with what follows conjoined to it, and «غِشَاوة» a mubtadaʾ (subject). Beginning with it is allowed because whenever the khabar of an indefinite noun is an adverbial or a complete genitive phrase placed before it, beginning with it is allowed; placing the khabar first is then obligatory to validate beginning with the indefinite noun, and the verse is of this kind. This differs from the saying of the Exalted {وَأَجَلٌ مُّسمًّى عِندَهُ} [al-Anʿām: 2], because in that verse there is another justification, namely the qualifying adjective. On the first possibility, one pauses at «سمعهم» and begins with what follows it, namely «وعلى أبصارهم غشاوةٌ», where «على أبصارهم» is a khabar placed first and «غشاوة» a mubtadaʾ placed later. On the second possibility, one pauses at «قلوبهم». The preposition «على» was repeated only to convey tawkīd (emphasis), or to indicate that the two sealings are different, namely that the sealing of the hearts is other than the sealing of the hearing. Grammarians distinguished between "I passed by Zayd and ʿAmr" and "I passed by Zayd and by ʿAmr", saying that in the first it is one passing and in the second they are two passings; this supports what I said. However, the explanation by emphasis covers both parsings — I mean making «وعلى سَمْعِهم» conjoined to his saying «على قلوبهم», and making it a khabar placed first — whereas the explanation by the difference of the two sealings only works on the first possibility. On the second possibility it may be said that the repetition of the particle indicates that the two coverings differ, namely that the covering on the hearing is other than the covering on the sight, as was said about the two sealings.
«غِشاوةً» was read in the accusative, and there are three views about it. The first: by an implied fitting verb, i.e. "and He placed a covering over their sight"; this governor is stated explicitly in the saying of the Exalted {وَجَعَلَ على بَصَرِهِ غِشَاوَةً} [al-Jāthiya: 23]. The second: accusative by removal of the preposition, with «وعلى أبصارهم» conjoined to what precedes it; the implied form is: "Allah sealed their hearts, their hearing and their sight with a covering"; then the preposition was omitted, so what follows it became accusative, as in his saying:
148 - تَمُرُّون الدِّيارَ ولم تَعُوجوا ... كلامُكُمُ عليَّ إذاً حَرامُ
(You pass the dwellings and do not turn aside? Then speaking with you is forbidden to me.)
i.e. "you pass by the dwellings"; but this is not a regular rule. The third: «غِشاوةً» is a noun put in the place of a maṣdar (verbal noun) that meets «خَتَم» in meaning, because sealing and covering share the meaning of concealment; as though it were said "and He sealed with a covering" by way of emphasis, so it is of the type "qaʿadtu julūsan" (I sat a sitting); their hearts, hearing and sight would then be sealed over and covered.
Al-Fārisī said: "The reading with the nominative is preferable, because as for the accusative, either you make it depend on the overt «خَتَم», in which case the problem arises that you have interposed between the conjunction and what is conjoined by it — and this, in our view, is only allowed in poetry — or you make it depend on a verb indicated by «خَتَم», its implied form being 'and He placed a covering over their sight', so the speech becomes of the type of:
149 - يا ليتَ زَوجَكَ قد غَدَا ... متقلِّداً سيفاً ورُمْحا
(Would that your husband had gone out in the morning girded with a sword and a spear.)
and his saying:
150 - عَلَفْتُها تِبْناً وماءً بارداً ... حتى شَتَتْ هَمَّالةً عَيْناها
(I fed her straw and cold water, until she spent the winter with her eyes streaming.)
and you hardly find this usage in conditions of freedom and choice [i.e. in prose]." Some found this wording problematic, and said: "I do not know what his saying means: 'because as for the accusative, either you make it depend on the overt «خَتَم»'; how could you make the accusative «غشاوةً» depend on «ختم», which is a verb, when there is no dependence possible here?" Then he said: "Unless he meant that the saying of the Exalted {خَتَمَ الله على قُلُوبِهمْ} is a supplication against them, not a statement, and «غشاوةً» is in the sense of a maṣdar invoked against them, standing in place of the verb, as though it were said 'and may Allah cover their sight'; it would then be conjoined to «خَتَم» as a maṣdar standing in for its verb in supplication is conjoined, as in 'May Allah have mercy on Zayd, and water for him (saqyan lahu)'; you would then have interposed between the conjoined «غشاوة» and «ختم», to which it is conjoined, with the preposition and its genitive noun." End of quote. This is a good interpretation, but it involves a verbal dispute, because al-Fārisī did not claim a separation between the conjoined and what it is conjoined to; he claimed only a separation between the conjunction and what is conjoined by it, i.e. by the particle. So the accurate form of the interpretation is to say: "you would then have interposed between «غشاوة» and the conjunction with the preposition and its genitive noun."
«غشاوة» was also read with fatḥa and with ḍamma on the ghayn [Translator's note: the source says "the ʿayn", which appears to mean the first letter], and «عشاوة» with the undotted ʿayn. The most correct of the readings is the well-known one, because things that indicate enclosing always come on this pattern, like ʿimāma / (turban), ḍimāma (bundle) and ʿiṣāba (headband).
Khatm linguistically is marking with a seal or the like. «القلب» was originally a maṣdar, then this organ was named with it — it is the cone-shaped lump of flesh — because of the speed with which thoughts come to it and their going back and forth over it; that is why [the poet] said: 151 - ما سُمِّي القلبُ إلاَّ مِنْ تقلُّبِه ... فاحذَرْ على القَلْبِ من قَلْبٍ وتَحْويلِ
(The heart (qalb) was named only from its turning about; so beware, for the heart, of overturning and change.)
When this organ was named with it, they adhered to giving it emphatic pronunciation (tafkhīm), to distinguish between it and its origin. [Translator's note: as written in the source.] It is often meant as the intellect, and it is also applied to the core of everything and its pure part.
Samʿ and samāʿ are two maṣdars of samiʿa; it is sometimes used in the sense of listening (istimāʿ); [the poet] said:
152 - وقد تَوَجَّس رِكْزاً مُقْفِرٌ نَدُسٌ ... بِنَبْأةِ الصوتِ ما في سَمْعِهِ كَذِبُ
(A keen [hunter] in the wilderness sensed a faint sound — the faint note of a voice; there is no falsehood in his hearing.)
i.e. in his listening. Al-simʿ, with kasra, is good repute, and it is also the offspring of the wolf from the hyena. It was made singular, even though the plural is meant, like the words before and after it, because it is truly a maṣdar; or because it is on omission of a muḍāf, i.e. the places of their hearing; or it is used as a metonym for the ear, and was made singular only because the meaning is understood, as in his saying:
153 - كُلُوا في بعض بَطْنِكُم تَعِفُّوا ... فإنَّ زمانَكمْ زَمَنٌ خَمِيصُ
(Eat in part of your belly [i.e. bellies] and be abstinent, for your time is a time of hunger.)
i.e. your bellies. Similar is:
