(We pierce them beneath the waist-wraps after striking them with gleaming, sharp blades where the turbans are wound.)
«ما» may be added to it, and it then puts two verbs in the jussive, as protasis and apodosis, like إنْ; it does not put them in the jussive without «ما», contrary to some people. It may also be imbued with the sense of causation. Al-Akhfash claimed that it can be an adverb of time and cited:
369 - للفتى عَقْلٌ يَعيشُ به ... حيث تَهْدي ساقَهُ قَدَمُهْ
(The young man has a mind by which he lives, wherever his foot guides his leg.)
There is no proof in it, because it is in its normal sense there.
What governs it here is «كُلا», i.e. "eat, the two of you, in whatever place you wish", as a granting of latitude to them. Abū al-Baqāʾ permitted it to be a badal (substitute) of «الجنَّة»; he said: "because al-janna is a direct object, so «حيث» would be a direct object". This is questionable, because it is not freely inflected, as has preceded, except for being put in the genitive by «مِنْ».
His saying: «شِئْتُمَا»: the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation of the adverb to it. Is the kasra on the shīn original, as in your saying جِئْتُما and خِفْتُما, or transformed from a fatḥa to indicate that the root has yāʾ, as in بِعْتما? Two views, built on what the pattern of شَاءَ is: al-Mubarrad's doctrine is that it is faʿala with a fatḥa on the middle radical, and Sībawayh's doctrine is that it is faʿila with a kasra on it; the morphology of both is evident.
His saying: {وَلاَ تَقْرَبَا هذه الشجرة}: lā is prohibitive, and «تَقْرَبا» is jussive by it, its nūn having been dropped. It has been read «تِقْرَبا» with a kasra on the imperfect prefix. The alif is the fāʿil (agent), and «هذه» is a mafʿūl bihi, the demonstrative for the feminine. It has dialectal forms: هذي, هذهِ [and هذهِ] with a kasra on the hāʾ, with lengthening and without it, هذهْ with the hāʾ quiescent, and ذِهْ with a kasra on the dhāl alone. The hāʾ is a substitute for the yāʾ, because of its closeness to it in faintness. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said — and it has also been transmitted from al-Naḥḥās —: "There is in the language no feminine hāʾ preceded by a kasra other than «هذه»." This is questionable, because that hāʾ which indicates the feminine is not this one, since that one is a substitute for the feminine tāʾ in pause; whereas this hāʾ has no indication of the feminine; rather what indicates it is the word as a whole, just as you say: the yāʾ in «هذي» is for the feminine. Its rule as regards nearness, distance and the intermediate, and the entry of the hāʾ of alerting and the kāf of address, is the rule of «ذا», which has preceded. One also says for it: تَيْك, تَيْلَكَ, تِلْكَ and تالِك. The poet said:
370 - تعلَّمْ أنَّ بعدَ الغَيِّ رُشْدا ... وأنَّ لتالِكَ الغُمَرِ انْحِسَاراً
(Know that after error comes right guidance, and that those floods of trouble have a receding.)
Hishām said: "One also says: تافَعَلَتْ", and they cited:
371 - خَليليَّ لولا ساكنُ الدارِ لم أُقِمْ ... بتا الدارِ إلاَّ عابرَ ابنِ سبيلٍ
(My two friends, were it not for the one who dwells in the house, I would not have stayed at this house except as a passing wayfarer.)
«الشجرةِ» is a badal of «هذه»; it has also been said: a naʿt of it, being interpreted as a derived word, i.e. "this one present among the trees". The well-known view is that when a derived word comes after a demonstrative, it is its naʿt, and if it is a non-derived (jāmid) noun, it is a badal of it. Al-shajara is the singular of al-shajar, a generic noun, and it is what stands on a trunk, unlike al-najm (stemless plants); their precise treatment will come in Sūrat al-Raḥmān, if Allah the Exalted wills. It has been read «الشجرة» with kasra on the shīn and the jīm, and with the jīm quiescent, and with the jīm replaced by yāʾ, with fatḥa or kasra on the shīn, because of its closeness to it in point of articulation, just as jīm was substituted for yāʾ in his saying:
372 - يا رَبِّ إنْ كنْتَ قَبِلْتَ حَجَّتِجْ ... فلا يَزالُ شاحِجٌ يأتيكَ بِجْ
(O Lord, if You have accepted my pilgrimage, then may a braying [mount] keep coming to You with me.)
By that he means حَجَّتي and بي. Another said:
373 - إذا لم يكُنْ فِيكُنَّ ظِلٌّ وَلاَ جَنًى ... فَأَبْعَدَكُنَّ اللهُ من شِيَرَاتِ
(If there is in you neither shade nor fruit, then may Allah banish you, O trees.)
Abū ʿAmr said: "Only the Berbers of Mecca and its Blacks read it so." Al-shajar has also been pluralized as shajrāʾ, and no plural has come on this pattern except qaṣaba / qaṣbāʾ, ṭarafa / ṭarfāʾ and ḥalafa / ḥalfāʾ; al-Aṣmaʿī used to say: "ḥalifa, with a kasra on the lām". According to Sībawayh these words are both singular and plural.
You say: قَرِبْتُ الأمرَ أقرَبه, with a kasra on the middle radical in the past and a fatḥa in the imperfect, i.e. "I became involved in it". Al-Jawharī said: "قَرُب with ḍamma, يقرُبُ, قُرْباً, i.e. he drew near; and قَرِبْتُهُ with kasra, قُرْبَاناً: I drew near [to it]; and قَرَبْتُ أقرُبُ قِرابَةً, like كَتَبْتُ أكتُبُ كِتابة, when you journey towards water and there is one night between you and it.
It has been said: when one says لا تَقْرَبْ with a fatḥa on the rāʾ, its meaning is 'do not become involved in the act', and when one says لا تَقْرُب with ḍamma, its meaning is 'do not draw near to it'."
His saying: {فَتَكُونَا مِنَ الظالمين}: there are two aspects in it. The first: that it is jussive, conjoined to «تَقْرَبَا», as in his saying:
374 - فقلت له: صَوِّبْ ولا تَجْهَدَنَّهُ ... فَيُذْرِكَ من أُخرى القَطَاةِ فَتَزْلَقِ
(So I said to him: "Keep low, and do not overtax it, lest it toss you from the back of its rump and you slip off.")
The second: that it is accusative as the answer to the prohibition, like His saying, Exalted is He: {لاَ تَطْغَوْاْ فِيهِ فَيَحِلَّ} [Ṭā Hā: 81]. The accusative is by an implied «أَنْ» according to the Basrans, by the fāʾ itself according to al-Jarmī, and by divergence (al-khilāf) according to the Kufans; and so it is with everything that comes like this.
{مِنَ الظالمين} is the khabar (predicate) of kāna. Al-ẓulm: putting a thing in other than its place; hence land that did not deserve digging and was dug is called maẓlūma ("wronged"). Al-Nābigha al-Dhubyānī said:
375 - إِلاَّ أَوارِيَّ لأَيَاً ما أُبَيِّنُهَا ... والنُّؤْيُ كالحوضِ بالمظلومةِ الجَلَدِ
(Except tethering-posts, which I can make out only with difficulty, and the trench [around the tent] like a trough in the "wronged", hard ground.)
It has also been said: it was called maẓlūma because rain does not come to it. ʿAmr ibn Qamīʾa said:
376 - ظَلَمَ البطاحَ له انهِلاَلُ حَرِيصةٍ ... فصفَا النِّطافُ له بُعَيْدَ المُقْلَعِ
(The pouring of a scouring rain "wronged" the valley-beds for it, so the pools cleared for it shortly after it ceased.)
And they said: "Whoever resembles his father has not done wrong." He said:
377 - بأبِهِ اقتدى عَدِيٌّ في الكَرَمْ ... ومَنْ يشابِهْ أَبَه فما ظَلَمْ
(ʿAdī followed his father's example in generosity, and whoever resembles his father has done no wrong.)

semin-durr:20-20.t:
The words of the Exalted: {يَكَادُ البرق يَخْطَفُ أَبْصَارَهُمْ}: «يكادُ» is the imperfect of كَادَ, which denotes nearness to the action (muqāraba). It operates as «كانَ» operates (i.e. it is one of kāna and its sisters in function), except that its khabar (predicate) can only be an imperfect verb; its coming as an explicit noun is anomalous (shādhdh). The poet said:
241 - فَأُبْتُ إلى فَهْمٍ وما كِدْتُ آيباً ... وكم مثلِها فارَقْتُها وهي تَصْفِرُ
(I returned to Fahm, though I was scarcely returning; and how many a one like it have I left while it whistled [empty].)
Most commonly its khabar is free of «أنْ», the reverse of «عسى»; its being joined to it is anomalous. Ruʾba said:
242 - قد كادَ مِنْ طولِ البلى أن يَمْحَصا ...
(From long decay it had nearly worn away.)
[It is anomalous] because «كاد» is for nearness to the action, while «أَنْ» confines [the verb] to the future, so the two are incompatible.
Know that when «كاد» itself is affirmative, its khabar is negative in meaning, because it denotes nearness: if you say «كاد زيدٌ يفعلُ», the meaning is that he came near to the action, but did not do it. When it is negated, its khabar is negated a fortiori, because if nearness to the action is negated, the action itself is negated all the more. For this reason the words of the Exalted {لَمْ يَكَدْ يَرَاهَا} [al-Nūr: 40] are more eloquent than if it had been said «لم يَرَها», because he did not even come near to seeing it, so how could he see it?
A group, among them Ibn Jinnī, Abū al-Baqāʾ and Ibn ʿAṭiyya, claimed that its negation is affirmation and its affirmation is negation, so much so that someone composed a riddle on it, saying:
243 - أَنَحْوِيَّ هذا العصرِ ما هي لفظةٌ ... جَرَتْ في لِسانَيْ جُرْهُمٍ وَثَمُودِ
إذا نُفِيَتْ - والله أعلمُ - أُثْبِتَتْ ... وإِنْ أُثْبِتَتْ قامَتْ مَقَامَ جُحُودِ
(O grammarian of this age, what is a word that ran on the tongues of Jurhum and Thamūd which, when negated — and Allah knows best — is affirmed, and when affirmed stands in the place of denial?)
They related of Dhū al-Rumma that when he recited his line:
244 - إذا غَيَّر النأيُ المحِبِّينَ لم يَكَدْ ... رسيسُ الهوى من حُبِّ مَيَّةَ يَبْرَحُ
(When distance changes lovers, the lingering touch of passion for Mayya scarcely departs.)
he was faulted for it, because he said «لَمْ يَكَدْ يَبْرَحُ», so that it would mean it had departed; so he changed it to «لم يَزَلْ» (it has not ceased), or something with its meaning.
What misled these people is the word of the Exalted: {فَذَبَحُوهَا وَمَا كَادُواْ يَفْعَلُونَ} [al-Baqara: 71]. They said: here it is negated and its khabar is affirmed in meaning, because the slaughter took place, given His words «فَذَبَحُوها». The answer concerning this verse is from two angles. First: it is understood as referring to two different times, i.e. they slaughtered it at one time, and they were not near to doing it at another time. Second: He expressed, by negating nearness to the action, how extreme their obstinacy and their difficulty in doing it were.
As for what they related of Dhū al-Rumma, the majority held Dhū al-Rumma to be mistaken in retracting his wording, and said: it is more eloquent and better than what he changed it to.
Know that the khabar of «كاد» and its sisters other than «عسى» can only have as its fāʿil (agent) a pronoun referring back to its ism (subject), because they are for nearness or for commencement — unlike «عسى», which is for hope: you say «عسى زيدٌ أن يقومَ أبوه» (perhaps Zayd's father will stand), and that is not permitted with the others. As for the poet's words:
245 - وَقَفْتُ على رَبْعٍ لِميَّةَ ناقتي ... فما زِلْتُ أبكي عندَهُ وأُخَاطِبُهْ
وَأَسْقِيهِ حتى كَادَ مِمَّا أَبُثُّه ... تُكَلِّمُنِي أَحْجَارُه ومَلاعِبُهْ
(I halted my she-camel at an abode of Mayya's, and kept weeping there and addressing it, and watering it [with tears], until, from the grief I poured out, its stones and playgrounds nearly spoke to me.)
where he brought the fāʿil overt: some took it as anomalous. But it ought to be said: this was permitted only because the stones and playgrounds are an expression for the abode itself, so they are it; it is as if it were said «حتى كاد يكلِّمني» (until it nearly spoke to me), but he expressed it by the sum of its parts. And the words of the other poet:
246 - وقد جَعَلْتُ إذا ما قُمْتُ يُثْقِلُني ... ثَوْبي فَأَنْهَضُ نَهْضَ الشاربِ السَّكِرِ
وكنتُ أمشي على رِجْلَيْنِ مُعْتَدِلاً ... فَصِرْتُ أمشي على أخرى من الشجر
(I have come to the point that whenever I stand, my garment weighs me down, and I rise as a drunken drinker rises; I used to walk upright on two legs, and now I walk on a third made of wood.)
where he brought the fāʿil of the [khabar of] «جعل» overt: two answers have been given. First: it is on the omission of a muḍāf, its implied form being «وقد جَعَل ثوبي إذا ما قمت يُثْقلني» (my garment has come to weigh me down whenever I stand). Second: it is of the type of putting the cause in place of the effect, for his rising in such a manner is caused by his garment's weighing him down; the meaning is: I have come to rise as the intoxicated drinker rises, because my garment weighs me down.
The pattern of «كاد» is كَوِدَ, with kasra on the middle radical; it is one of the wāw-verbs, like خاف يَخاف. There is another dialect in it: fatḥa on its middle radical; in this dialect its first radical takes ḍamma when it is attached to the tāʾ of the speaker and its sisters, so you say كُدْت and كُدْنا, like قُلْت and قُلْنا. Sometimes the kasra of its middle radical is transferred to its first radical when attached to an overt noun, as in the poet's words:
247 - وكِيدَ ضِباعُ القُفِّ يأكُلْنَ جُثَّتي ... وكِيدِ خِراشٌ عند ذلك يَيْتَمُ
(The hyenas of the rugged ground nearly devoured my corpse, and Khirāsh was nearly orphaned at that.)
It may not be redundant (zāʾida), contrary to al-Akhfash. All of this will come under the incomplete (nāqiṣa) «كاد». As for the complete (tāmma) «كاد» meaning «مَكَر» (to plot), it is on the pattern فَعَل with fatḥa on the middle radical, one of the yāʾ-verbs, as shown by His words: {إِنَّهُمْ يَكِيدُونَ كَيْداً * وَأَكِيدُ كَيْداً} [al-Ṭāriq: 15–16].
«البرق» is its ism, and «يخَطف» its khabar. One says خَطِف يَخْطَفُ, with kasra on the middle radical of the past and fatḥa in the imperfect, and خَطَف يخطِف, the reverse of the first dialect. There are many readings in it; the well-known one is the first. The second: يَخْطِف, with kasra on the ṭāʾ.
The third: يَخَطَّفُ, with fatḥa on the yāʾ, the khāʾ and the ṭāʾ, and the ṭāʾ doubled; the origin is يَخْتَطِفُ, and the tāʾ of the iftiʿāl form was changed to ṭāʾ for assimilation. The fourth: likewise, except that it has kasra on the khāʾ, following the kasra of the ṭāʾ. The sixth: likewise, except that it has kasra on the yāʾ as well, following the khāʾ. [Translator's note: the source passes from the fourth to the sixth; no fifth reading is listed.] The seventh: يَخْتَطِف, on the original form. The eighth: يَخْطِّف, with fatḥa on the yāʾ, sukūn on the khāʾ and the ṭāʾ doubled; this is poor, because it leads to the meeting of two vowelless letters. The ninth: with ḍamma on the yāʾ, fatḥa on the khāʾ, and the ṭāʾ doubled with kasra; the doubling in it is for intensification (takthīr), not for making it transitive. The tenth: يَتَخَطَّف.
الخَطْفُ is taking something quickly. This clause — I mean His words «يكاد البرق يَخْطَف» — has no grammatical position, because it is resumptive (istiʾnāf), as if it had been asked: "What is their state with that lightning?" and it was said: "It nearly snatches." It may also be in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of the omitted «ذوي», the implied form being: «أو كذوي صيبٍ كائدٍ البرقُ يَخْطَف» (or like the people of a rainstorm whose lightning nearly snatches).
The words of the Exalted: {كُلَّمَا أَضَآءَ لَهُمْ مَّشَوْاْ فِيهِ}: «كل» is accusative as an adverb of time (ẓarfiyya), because it is annexed to the temporal «ما»; what governs it is its apodosis, namely «مَشَوا». It was also said: «ما» is an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective (nakira mawṣūfa), also meaning "time", and the referring pronoun is omitted, its implied form being «كلَّ وقتٍ أضاءَ لهم فيه» (every time it gave them light in it). So «أضاء» has no grammatical position on the first view, being a ṣila (relative clause), and its position is genitive on the second.
«أضاء» may be intransitive. Al-Mubarrad said: "It is transitive, and its object is omitted", i.e. the lightning lit the road for them. So the hāʾ in «فيه» refers to the lightning according to the majority, and to the omitted «الطريق» (road) according to al-Mubarrad.
«فيه» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «مَشَوا», and «في» has its basic meaning, i.e. the light surrounds them. It was also said: it is in the sense of the bāʾ. On both views an omission is necessary, i.e. they walked in its light, or by its light. The clause «مَشَوا» has no grammatical position, because it is resumptive.
Know that «كُلّ» is one of the words of generality. It is a collective noun (ism jamʿ) that is necessarily annexed, though what it is annexed to may be omitted; is its tanwīn in that case the tanwīn of compensation (ʿiwaḍ) or the tanwīn of declinability (ṣarf)? There are two views. If what «كل» is annexed to is definite and is omitted, it remains definite; for this reason a ḥāl (circumstantial) can be made accusative from it, and the definite article does not enter it, even though that occurs in the wording of some. Sometimes it is made accusative as a ḥāl. Its original use is as tawkīd (emphasis), like «أجمع», and the best use of it is as a mubtadaʾ (subject). Its being a direct object is not restricted to what is heard (samāʿ), nor peculiar to poetry, contrary to whoever claimed that.
When it is annexed to an indefinite noun, or to one made definite by the lām of the genus, it may well follow verbal governing words. When annexed to an indefinite noun, that indefinite noun must be taken into account in the pronoun and so on referring to it: you say «كلُّ رجال أتَوْكَ فأكرِمْهم» (all men who come to you, honour them), and it is not permitted to take account of the wording of «كل» and say «كلُّ رجال أتاكَ فأكرمه»; and [you say] «كلُّ رجلٍ أتاك فأكرمه» (every man who comes to you, honour him), and you do not say «أَتَوْك فأكرِمْهم», taking account of the meaning. As for the poet's words:
248 - جادَتْ عليه كلُّ عَيْن ثَرَّةٍ ... فتركْنَ كلَّ حدَيقةٍ كالدرهم
(Every abundant spring [cloud] poured generously on it, and they left every garden like a silver coin.)
where he took account of the meaning, it is anomalous and not taken as a basis for analogy. When it is annexed to a definite noun there are two options, whether the annexation is in wording, as in {وَكُلُّهُمْ آتِيهِ يَوْمَ القيامة فَرْداً} [Maryam: 95], where the wording of «كل» is taken into account, or in meaning, as in {فَكُلاًّ أَخَذْنَا بِذَنبِهِ} [al-ʿAnkabūt: 40], where its wording is taken into account, and He said {وَكُلٌّ أَتَوْهُ دَاخِرِينَ} [al-Naml: 87], where the meaning is taken into account.
As for some people's statement that «كُلَّما» conveys repetition, that is not part of its original coinage: if you say «كلما جِئْتَني أَكْرَمْتُك», the meaning is: I honour you on each and every one of your comings to me.
It was read «ضاء» as a triliteral verb, which shows that the quadriliteral [أضاء] is intransitive. It was also read «وإذا أُظْلِم», in the passive, and al-Zamakhsharī took this as showing that «أَظْلَمَ» is transitive; he also cited in support the words of Ḥabīb [Abū Tammām]:
249 - هما أَظْلما حالَيَّ ثُمَّتَ أَجْلَيَا ... ظَلامَيْهِما عن وجهِ أَمْرَدَ أَشْيَبِ
(These two darkened both my states, then cleared away their two darknesses from the face of one beardless yet grey.)
But there is no proof in the verse, since its origin may be «وإذا أَظْلم الليلُ عليهم» (when the night grew dark upon them); when it was made passive, «الليل» was omitted and «عليهم» stood in its place. As for Ḥabīb, he is a post-classical (muwallad) poet [and not cited as evidence].
As for why the first clause is introduced with «كلما» and the second with «إذا», al-Zamakhsharī said: "Because they were eager for the existence of what their concern was bound to — the possibility and feasibility of walking — so whenever they met with an opportunity for it they seized it; stopping and being held back are not like that." What he said is the apparent view, except that some grammarians held that «إذا» also conveys repetition, and recited:
250 - إذا وَجَدْتُ أُوارَ الحُبِّ في كَبْدِي ... أَقْبَلْتُ نحو سِقاءِ القومِ أَبْتَرِدُ
(Whenever I find the burning heat of love in my liver, I go to the people's water-skin to cool myself.)
He said: "Its meaning is the meaning of «كلما»."
The words of the Exalted: {وَلَوْ شَآءَ الله لَذَهَبَ بِسَمْعِهِمْ وَأَبْصَارِهِمْ}: «لو» is "a particle for what would have occurred because of the occurrence of something else"; this is Sībawayh's wording, and it is preferable to the wording of others, "a particle of impossibility for impossibility" (ḥarf imtināʿ li-mtināʿ), because the first wording is valid in cases such as the word of the Exalted {لَّوْ كَانَ البحر مِدَاداً لِّكَلِمَاتِ رَبِّي لَنَفِدَ البحر} [al-Kahf: 109], and in his words (peace be upon him): «نِعْمَ العبدُ صُهَيْبٌ لو لم يَخَفِ اللهَ لم يُعْصِه» (What an excellent servant is Ṣuhayb: had he not feared Allah, he would not have disobeyed Him), whereas the second is not valid there, as will come in detail; and because of the unsoundness [on the second wording] of a statement such as «لو كان إنساناً لكان حيواناً» (if it were a human, it would be an animal), since the impossibility of being human does not entail the impossibility of being an animal.
It does not make the verb jussive, contrary to some. As for the poet's words:
251 - لو يَشَأْ طارَ به ذو مَيْعَةٍ ... لاحِقُ الآطالِ نَهْدٌ ذو خُصَلْ
(Had he wished, a spirited steed would have flown off with him, lean-flanked, sturdy, with flowing forelocks.)
and the other's words:
252 - تامَتْ فؤادَك لو يَحْزُنْكَ مَا صَنَعَتْ ... إحدى نساءِ بني ذُهْلِ بنِ شَيْبَانا
(One of the women of Banū Dhuhl ibn Shaybān enslaved your heart — if only what she did grieved you.)
these are from making a vowelled letter vowelless out of poetic necessity.
It is mostly a conditional in the past, but it may come in the sense of «إنْ», as in the word of the Exalted: {وَلْيَخْشَ الذين لَوْ تَرَكُواْ مِنْ خَلْفِهِمْ ذُرِّيَّةً ضِعَافاً خَافُواْ عَلَيْهِمْ} [al-Nisāʾ: 9], and the poet's words:
253 - ولَوْ أَنَّ ليلى الأخيليَّةَ سَلَّمَتْ ... عليَّ ودوني جَنْدَلٌ وصَفائِحُ
لسَلَّمْتُ تسليمَ البشاشةِ أَوْزَقَا ... إليها صَدَىً مِنْ جانبِ القبرِ صائحُ
(If Laylā al-Akhyaliyya were to greet me, with rocks and slabs [of the grave] over me, I would return a joyful greeting, or an owl-spirit would cry out to her from the side of the grave.)
According to the correct view it is not maṣdariyya (infinitival). It may be imbued with the meaning of wishing, and then the imperfect after the fāʾ is made accusative as its answer, as in {فَلَوْ أَنَّ لَنَا كَرَّةً فَنَكُونَ} [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 102]; this will be set out in its place.
«شاء» was originally شَيِئَ, on the pattern فَعِلَ with kasra on the middle radical; the yāʾ was changed into alif by the established rule. Its object is omitted, its implied form being «ولو شاء الله إذهابَ» (had Allah willed the taking away [of their hearing]). The omission of its object and of the object of «أراد» became so frequent that it is hardly pronounced except for something unusual, as in the poet's words:
254 - ولو شِئْتُ أن أبكي دَماً لبكَيتُه ... عليهِ ولكنْ ساحةُ الصبرِ أَوْسَعُ
(Had I wished to weep blood over him, I would have wept it; but the courtyard of patience is wider.)
The Exalted said: {لَّوْ أَرَادَ الله أَن يَتَّخِذَ وَلَداً} [al-Zumar: 4].
The lām in «لذهب» is the answer of «لو». Know that the lām frequently enters its answer when it is affirmative, though it may be omitted; the Exalted said: {لَوْ نَشَآءُ جَعَلْنَاهُ أُجَاجاً} [al-Wāqiʿa: 70]. Its entering it is rare when the answer is negated with «ما», and it is impossible when the answer is negated with something other than «ما», as in «لو قُمْتَ لم أَقُمْ» (had you stood, I would not have stood), because two lāms would follow one another and that is heavy. [The answer] may be omitted, as in the poet's words:
255 - لا يُلْفِكَ الراجُوك إلا مُظْهِراً ... خُلُقَ الكرامِ ولو تكونُ عَدِيماً
(Let those who hope in you find you only displaying the character of the noble, even if you are destitute.)
«بسَمْعِهم» is attached to «ذَهَب». It was read «لأَذْهَبَ», in which case the bāʾ is redundant, or فَعَل and أَفْعَل have one meaning; similar to it is {تَنبُتُ بالدهن} [al-Muʾminūn: 20].
The words of the Exalted: {إِنَّ الله على كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ}: this clause confirms the meaning of what precedes it. «على كل شيء» is attached to «قدير», which is فَعِيل in the sense of فاعِل (active participle), derived from القُدْرَة, which is strength and ability. Its verb is قَدَر, with fatḥa on the middle radical, and it has thirteen maṣdars (verbal nouns): قدرة with the qāf taking any of the three vowels, مَقْدرة with the dāl taking any of the three vowels, and قَدْراً, قَدَراً, قُدَراً, قَداراً, قُدْراناً, مَقْدِراً and مَقْدَراً. «قدير» is more intensive than «قادر»; al-Zajjāj said this. It was also said: they have the same meaning; al-Harawī said this.
الشيء is that which can be known in some respect and be spoken of. It is originally the maṣdar of شاء يشاء. Whether it applies to the non-existent and the impossible is a well-known disagreement.

semin-durr:50-50.t:
His saying: {وَإِذْ فَرَقْنَا بِكُمُ البحر}. As for «بكم», the apparent view is that the bāʾ keeps its basic sense of entering upon the instrument, as though He parted [the sea] by means of them, just as two things are separated by what comes between them. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It may also be the transitivizing [bāʾ] (al-muʿaddiya), as in your saying: ذهبتُ بزيدٍ ('I took Zayd away'), so that the implied meaning is: أَفْرَقْناكم البحرَ ('We made you part the sea'), and it would then be in the sense of {وَجَاوَزْنَا ببني إِسْرَآئِيلَ البحر} [al-Aʿrāf: 138]." This is close to the first [view]. The bāʾ may also be causal, i.e. "because of you"; and it may be for the ḥāl (circumstantial) from «البحر», i.e. "We parted it while it was in contact with you". Al-Zamakhsharī compared it to the poet's saying:
454 - . . . . . . . . . . . ... تَدُوس بنا الجماجِمَ والتَّريبا
(…[the horse] tramples skulls and breastbones with us [upon it]), i.e. it tramples them while we are riding it. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "I.e. We parted the sea while you were in it, so it is either an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara) or a concurrent one (muqārina)." I say: what need is there for him to make it an anticipated ḥāl, when it was only parted by them at the very time they were travelling through it? He also said: "And «بكم» is in the position of the accusative as the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of فَرَقْنا, and «البحرَ» is the first object; the bāʾ here has the sense of the lām." This is open to question (fīhi naẓar), because even granting that the bāʾ has the sense of the lām, it would then be the lām of cause, and what is made genitive by the lām of cause is not said to be a second object: were you to say ضَرَبْتُ زيداً لأجلِك ('I struck Zayd for your sake'), no grammarian would say that «ضَرَبَ» is transitive to two objects, to one of them by itself and to the other by a preposition.
Al-farq and al-falq are one and the same: separating and distinguishing. From it is {وَقُرْآناً فَرَقْنَاهُ} [al-Isrāʾ: 106] [i.e. We separated it] and distinguished it by clear exposition; the Quran is a furqān because it distinguishes between truth and falsehood; and the parting of the hair (farq al-raʾs) [is so called] because of its clearness. The basic meaning of al-baḥr ("sea") is a wide split; from it is al-baḥīra [the she-camel so called] because its ear is slit. The disagreement mentioned earlier about al-nahr ("river"), whether it is literal for the water or for the channel, applies here too, so let it be consulted. Is fresh water called baḥr, or is the word restricted to salt water? This is a disagreement whose verification will come in its place. One says: أَبْحَرَ الماءُ, i.e. "the water became salty". Nuṣayb said:
455 - وقد عادَ ماءُ الأرضِ بَحْراً فزادني ... إلى مَرَضي أَنْ أَبْحَرَ المَشْرَبُ العَذْبُ
(The water of the land has turned salty, and it added to my sickness that the sweet drinking-water became brackish.)
Al-gharaq ("drowning") is sinking down in water; it is used figuratively for becoming immersed in something, so one says: أَغْرَق فلانٌ في اللَّهْو ("so-and-so became immersed in amusement"). One says: غَرِقَ, so he is غَرِقٌ and غارِق. Abū al-Najm said:
456 - مِنْ بَيْنِ مقتولٍ وطافٍ غارِقِ
(Among one slain and one floating, drowned.)
It is also applied to killing of any kind. [The poet] said:
457 - . . . . . . . . . . . ... ألا لَيْتَ قَيْساً غَرَّقَتْهُ القَوابِلُ
(…Would that the midwives had drowned Qays [at birth]!)
The origin of this is that in a year of drought the midwife would drown the newborn in the blood of the afterbirth so that it would die, whether male or female; then every killing was called "drowning". From it is the saying of Dhū al-Rumma:
458 - إذا غَرَّقْتَ أرباضُها ثِنْيَ بَكْرَةٍ ... بتَيْهاءَ لم تُصْبِحْ رَؤوماً سَلُوبُها
(When its bellies "drown" [i.e. kill] the second-born of a young she-camel in a trackless desert, the bereaved mother does not wake up tender [toward another].)
His saying: {وَأَنْتُمْ تَنظُرُونَ} is a clause made of a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from «آل فرعون», the governing word being «أَغْرقنا». It may also be a ḥāl from the object of «أنْجَيْناكم». The "looking" may be with the eyes, because they could see one another owing to their nearness; it has also been said that the people of Pharaoh floated on the water and they [the Israelites] looked at them. Or it may be with insight and taking heed. It has also been said: the meaning is "while you were in the state of one who looks, were you to look", and for this reason no object is mentioned for it.

semin-durr:51-51.t:
The saying of the Exalted: {وَاعَدْنَا}. Abū ʿAmr read it here, and wherever it is similar, as a triliteral [verb, i.e. وَعَدْنا], while the rest read «واعَدنْا» with an alif. Abū ʿUbayd chose the reading of Abū ʿAmr and preferred it on the grounds that mutual promising (muwāʿada) takes place only among human beings, whereas Allah the Exalted is alone in promising and threatening; this is how we have found the Quran, e.g. {وَعَدَ الله الذين آمَنُواْ مِنْكُمْ} [al-Nūr: 55], {وَعَدَكُمُ الله مَغَانِمَ} [al-Fatḥ: 20], {وَعَدَكُمْ وَعْدَ الحق} [Ibrāhīm: 22], {وَإِذْ يَعِدُكُمُ الله} [al-Anfāl: 7]. Makkī, also preferring the reading of Abū ʿAmr, said: "Moreover, the apparent wording contains a promise from Allah to Moses, and contains no promise from Moses, so it must be taken as [the act of] one party, according to the apparent sense of the text." Then he mentioned a group of eminent readers who read it so. Abū Ḥātim, also preferring it, said: "The reading of the generality in our view is وَعَدْنا without an alif, because muwāʿada mostly takes place between created beings and between equals." People have answered the saying of Abū ʿUbayd, Abū Ḥātim and Makkī by [saying] that the mufāʿala [form] is sound here, in the sense that Moses' acceptance of the commitment to fulfil is treated as a promise from him; or that he promised to attend to what his Lord had charged him with. Makkī said: "Muwāʿada originally takes place between two parties, but it may come in the sense of faʿala, as in طارَقْتُ النَّعْلَ ('I double-soled the sandal')", so he made the two readings have one meaning; but the first [answer] is better. Some preferred «واعدنا». Al-Kisāʾī said: "The saying of Allah {وَعَدَ الله الذين آمَنُواْ} [al-Nūr: 55] does not belong to this category in any way, because واعَدْنا موسى belongs only to the category of meeting at an appointment (muwāfāh), and has nothing to do with promising; it is rather from your saying: 'your appointment is on such-and-such a day and at such-and-such a place', and the eloquent form in this is «واعَدْنا»." Al-Zajjāj said: "«واعَدْنا» with the alif is good, because obedience in accepting is equivalent to mutual promising: from Allah there is a promise, and from Moses acceptance and following, so it is treated like muwāʿada." Makkī also said: "The [preferred] choice is «واعَدْنا» with the alif, because it is in the sense of وَعَدْنَا in one of its two meanings, and because Moses must have had a promise or an acceptance standing in place of a promise, so the mufāʿala is sound." [Translator's note: Makkī is quoted here as both preferring Abū ʿAmr's reading and choosing «واعَدْنا»; translated as written.]
And «وعدَ» is transitive to two objects: «موسى» is the first object and «أربعين» the second object, and a muḍāf must be omitted, i.e. "the completion of forty". It may not be accusative as an adverb (ẓarf) because that would corrupt the meaning. The sign of its accusative is the yāʾ because it is treated like the sound masculine plural, though originally it is a singular collective noun (ism jamʿ) with which this decade of number was named. For that reason some declined it with vowels, and from that, according to one of two views, is [the poet's] saying:
459 - وماذا يَبْتَغِي الشعراءُ مني ... وقد جاوَزْتُ حَدَّ الأربعينِ
(What do the poets want from me, when I have passed the limit of forty?)
with a kasra on the nūn. «ليلةً» is accusative as a tamyīz (specification); the decades from twenty to ninety, and eleven to nineteen, are all specified by an accusative singular.
«موسى» is a foreign (aʿjamī) noun [and a diptote]. It is originally, as is said, a compound, the original being mūshā with a shīn, because water in their language is called mū and trees are called shā; the Arabs Arabized it and said Mūsā. They said: the people of Pharaoh found him beside water and trees.
As for their disagreement about «موسى»: whether it is mufʿal derived from أَوْسَيْتُ رأسَه ("I shaved his head"), so that it is mūsā, like أعطيتُه فهو مُعْطَىً; or whether it is fuʿlā derived from ماسَ يميس, i.e. to walk with a swagger and to sway, the yāʾ being changed into wāw because of the ḍamma before it, as in مُوْقِن from al-yaqīn — [this] concerns only the iron mūsā (razor), the instrument of shaving, because it moves and quivers when one shaves with it. Mūsā, the name of the Prophet, peace be upon him, has no derivation because it is foreign.
His saying: {ثُمَّ اتخذتم العجل}: اتَّخذ is transitive to two objects, and the second object is omitted, i.e. "then you took the calf as a god". It may be transitive to a single object when its meaning is "to make" or "to produce", as in {وَقَالُواْ اتخذ الله وَلَداً} [al-Baqara: 116]. Some said: تَخِذَ and اتَّخَذَ are transitive to two objects unless they convey the sense of acquiring, in which case they are transitive to one. There is disagreement about اتَّخَذَ. It has been said: it is iftaʿala from al-akhdh ("taking"), the original being اأتخذ: the first [hamza] is the connective hamza and the second is the first radical (fāʾ) of the word; two hamzas thus came together, the second of them quiescent after another, so it had to be changed into yāʾ, as in إيمان; then the yāʾ came before the tāʾ of iftiʿāl, so it was changed into tāʾ and assimilated into the tāʾ of iftiʿāl, as in اتَّسر from al-yusr — except that this is rare among hamzated roots, e.g. اتَّكل from al-akl and اتَّزَرَ from al-izār. Abū ʿAlī said: it is iftaʿala from تَخِذَ يَتْخِذُ, and he recited:
460 - وقد تَخِذَتْ رِجْلِي إلى جَنْبِ غَرْزِهَا ... نَسيفاً كأُفْحوصِ القَطاةِ المُطَرِّقِ
(My foot has made, beside her stirrup, a worn mark like the nest-hollow of a sand-grouse about to lay.)
And the Exalted said: {لَتَخِذْتَ عَلَيْهِ أَجْراً} [al-Kahf: 77]. This is the easier of the two views.
The readers assimilate the dhāl into the tāʾ because of the closeness of their points of articulation, while Ibn Kathīr, and ʿĀṣim in the transmission of Ḥafṣ, pronounce it distinctly (iẓhār). This disagreement applies to the singular, e.g. اتَّخَذْتُ, and the plural, e.g. اتَّخَذْتُم. «ثُمَّ» is used in this clause to indicate that the taking took place after the appointment, after an interval.
His saying: «مِنْ بعدِه» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) اتَّخَذْتُمْ; «مِنْ» is for the beginning of the extent, and the pronoun refers to Moses. A muḍāf must be omitted, i.e. "after his departure" or "his going". Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It refers to Moses; [and it has been said: to his departure for the speaking [with Allah]; and it has been said: to the promise." There is some room for discussion in his words, for his saying "and it has been said: it refers to his departure" requires that it refer to Moses] without supposing a muḍāf, and that is inconceivable.
His saying: «وأنتم ظالمون» is a circumstantial clause from the fāʿil (agent) of «اتَّخَذْتُمْ».

semin-durr:52-52.t:
The saying of the Exalted: [{ثُمَّ عَفَوْنَا عَنكُم}]. Al-ʿafw is effacing. From it is «عَفَا اللهُ عنكم», i.e. He effaced your sins; and al-ʿāfiya ("well-being"), because it effaces illness; and عَفَتِ الريحُ الأثرَ ("the wind effaced the trace"). [The poet] said:
461 - فتُوضِحَ فالمِقْراةِ لم يَعْفُ رَسْمُها ... لِما نَسَجَتْها مِنْ جَنُوبٍ وشَمَأْلِ
(Then Tūḍiḥ and al-Miqrāt — its traces have not been effaced, because of what the south and north winds have woven over them.)
It has been said: عَفا كذا means "it became abundant", and from it is «وَأَعْفُوا اللِّحى» ("let the beards grow"), so it would be one of the words with opposite meanings (aḍdād). Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "Al-ʿafw is covering a trace and removing the former state, of sin or otherwise; al-ʿafw is not used in the sense of pardoning except with regard to sin." What he said is [close] to the explanation of al-ghufrān, because al-ghafr is covering and concealing, and from it is al-mighfar ("helmet"). But a distinction has been made between them: ʿafw may come after punishment and so coexist with it, whereas ghufrān does not come with punishment. Al-Rāghib said: "Al-ʿafw is aiming to take something. One says عَفَاه and اعْتَفَاه, i.e. he aimed at him, taking what he had; عَفَتِ الريحُ الترابَ: it aimed at it, taking its traces; عَفَتِ الديارُ: as though the dwellings aimed toward decay; عَفَا النبتُ والشَّعْرُ: it aimed at taking on increase; عَفَوْتُ عنك: as though he aimed to remove his sin, turning it away from him; and أَعْفَيْتُ كذا: I left it to grow and increase, and from it is «وأَعْفُوا اللحى»." So he made "aiming" a common factor in al-ʿafw, which negates its being one of the aḍdād; and this is a good statement. The poet said:
462 - . . . . . . . . . . . ... إذا ردَّ عافي القِدْرِ مَنْ يَسْتَعِيرُهَا
(…when what remains in the pot turns away the one who would borrow it.)
Its meaning is that al-ʿāfī here is what remains in the pot of broth and the like; when someone wants to borrow the pot, its owner excuses himself by the ʿāfī in it. So al-ʿāfī is the fāʿil (agent), and «مَنْ يستعيرُها» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); it is a case of figurative attribution (isnād majāzī), because the one who turns away is in reality the owner of the pot, because of the ʿāfī.
His saying: {تَشْكُرُونَ} is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of «لعلَّ». The explanation of shukr ("thanks") has preceded in discussing al-ḥamd. Al-Rāghib said: "It is conceiving of the blessing and manifesting it. It has been said: it is a metathesis of al-kashr, i.e. uncovering, and it is the opposite of kufr, which is covering up the blessing. It has also been said: its origin is from ʿayn shakrā, i.e. full [eye], so on this view it is being filled with the remembrance of the Benefactor." Shakara is one of the verbs that are transitive sometimes by themselves and sometimes by a preposition, neither being the origin of the other according to the correct view. Of the directly transitive use is the saying of ʿAmr ibn Luḥayy:
463 - همُ جَمَعُوا بؤسى ونعمى عليكُمُ ... فَهَلاَّ شكرْتَ القومَ إذ لم تُقاتِلِ
(They heaped upon you both hardship and favour; why then did you not thank the people, since you did not fight?)
And of that transitive by a preposition is the saying of the Exalted: {واشكروا لِي} [al-Baqara: 152], and its verification will come [there].

semin-durr:53-53.t:
The saying of the Exalted: {الكتاب والفرقان} is the second object of «آتينا». Is what is meant by al-kitāb and al-furqān one and the same thing, namely the Torah? As though it were said: that which combines being a revealed Book and a furqān that distinguishes between truth and falsehood, as in رأيت الغيثَ والليثَ ("I saw the rain and the lion", of one man), which belongs to the category of [the poet's] saying:
464 - إلى المَلِك القَرْمِ وابنِ الهُمَامِ ... . . . . . . . . . . .
(To the king, the chieftain, and the son of the valiant one…)
Or because, when the wording differs, that is permissible, as in his saying:
465 - فَقَدَّمَتِ الأَدِيمَ لراهِشَيْهِ ... وأَلْفَى قولَها كَذِباً وَمَيْنَا
(She presented the leather mat for [the cutting of] his veins, and he found her word to be lying and falsehood.)
and his saying:
466 - . . . . . . . . . . . ... وهندٌ أتى مِنْ دَوْنِها النَّأْيُ والبُعْدُ
(…and Hind — remoteness and distance have come between [us and] her.)
and his saying:
467 - . . . . . . . . . . . ... أَقْوَى وأَفْقَرَ بعدَ أُمِّ الهَيْثَمِ
(…it became deserted and empty after Umm al-Haytham.)
Al-Naḥḥās said: "This is permissible only in poetry; it is better that al-furqān be taken to mean what Allah taught Moses of the distinction between truth and falsehood." It has been said: the wāw is redundant (zāʾida), and «الفرقان» is a naʿt (adjective) of «الكتاب». Or «الكتابُ» is the Torah and «الفرقانُ» is that by which unbelief and faith are distinguished, such as the signs like the staff and the hand, or that by which the lawful and unlawful are distinguished among the laws.
Al-furqān is originally a maṣdar (verbal noun) like al-ghufrān; its meaning has preceded under {فَرَقْنَا بِكُمُ البحر} [al-Baqara: 50]. It has been said: al-furqān here is a name of the Quran; they said: the implied meaning is "And We gave Moses the Book, and Muhammad the Furqān". Al-Naḥḥās said: "This is an error in both i'rab and meaning. As for the i'rab, it is because what is conjoined to a thing is like it, and this differs from it; as for the meaning, it is because of His saying: {وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنَا موسى وَهَارُونَ الفرقان} [al-Anbiyāʾ: 48]."

semin-durr:9-9.t:
The saying of the Exalted: {يُخَادِعُونَ الله}: this verbal clause may be resumptive (mustaʾnafa), as an answer to an implied question, namely: "What is the matter with them that they said 'We believe' while they are not believers?" So it was said: "They try to deceive Allah." It may also be a badal (substitute) for the clause that serves as the ṣila (relative clause) of «مَنْ», namely «يقولُ», and this would be a substitute of inclusion (badal al-ishtimāl), because their saying such-and-such includes deception. It is thus analogous to the poet's saying:
172 - إنَّ عليَّ اللهَ أن تُبايعا ... تُؤْخَذَ كَرْهاً أو تَجِيءَ طائِعا
(I owe it to Allah that you shall pledge allegiance — be taken by force or come willingly.)
And another's saying:
173 - متى تَأْتِنا تُلْمِمْ بنا في ديارنا ... تَجِدْ حَطَباً جَزْلاً وناراً تَأجَّجَا
(Whenever you come to us — call on us in our dwellings — you will find thick firewood and a blazing fire.)
So «تُؤْخَذَ» is a badal of inclusion from «تُبايع», and likewise «تُلْمم» is a badal from «تأتِنا». On these two views this clause has no grammatical position. The clauses that have no grammatical position are four, not more than that — even if some have imagined otherwise — namely: the initial clause (al-mubtadaʾa), the ṣila, the parenthetical (al-muʿtariḍa) and the explicative (al-mufassira); their details will come in their places. This clause may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun latent (mustatir) in «يقول», its implied form being: "And among people is he who says, while they are deceiving." Abū al-Baqāʾ permitted it to be a ḥāl from the pronoun latent in «بمؤمنين», with the active participle governing it. Some refuted him with something whose meaning is that this noble verse is analogous to «ما زيدٌ أقبل ضاحكاً» ("Zayd did not come forward laughing"). He said: "The Arabs have two ways in a construction like this. One of them: negating the qualifier alone and affirming the root of the action; this is the more common, and the meaning is that the coming forward is affirmed and the laughing is negated. This meaning cannot conceivably be intended in the verse, I mean negating the deception and affirming faith. The second way: the qualifier is negated, so what governs it is negated too; it is as though it were said in the previous example: 'He did not come forward and did not laugh.' This meaning too is decisively not intended by the noble verse, I mean negating faith and deception together; rather, the meaning is upon negating faith and affirming deception. So making it a ḥāl from the pronoun in «بمؤمنين» is invalid." What is astonishing about Abū al-Baqāʾ is how he sensed this difficulty and so prohibited making this clause in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of «مؤمنين» — he said: "because that would entail negating their deception, whereas the meaning is upon affirming the deception" — and then made it a ḥāl from the pronoun of «مؤمنين», when there is no difference between the ḥāl and the adjective in this respect.
Al-khidāʿ (deception) is originally concealment; from it come al-akhdaʿān, two veins hidden in the neck, and from it mikhdaʿ al-bayt (the inner chamber of the house). So the meaning of «خادع» is: making one's companion imagine something other than the harm one intends for him. It was also said: it is corruption; the poet said:
174 - أبيضُ اللونِ لذيذٌ طَعْمُهُ ... طَيِّبُ الرِّيقِ إذا الريقُ خَدَعْ
(White of colour, delicious of taste, sweet of saliva when saliva has gone bad.)
i.e. "has gone bad". The maṣdar (verbal noun) is al-khidʿ, with kasra on the khāʾ, and similar to it is al-khadīʿa. The meaning of «يخادعون الله» is: in terms of outward form, not in terms of reality. It was also said: because of their lack of knowledge of Allah the Exalted and His attributes, they supposed Him to be one who can be deceived. Abū al-Qāsim al-Zamakhsharī said: "The name of Allah the Exalted is inserted (muqḥam), and the meaning is: they try to deceive those who believe; it is of the type «أعجبني زيدٌ وكرمُه» ('Zayd and his generosity pleased me'), the meaning being: Zayd's generosity pleased me, and «زيدٌ» was mentioned only as a lead-in to mentioning his generosity." He made that analogous to the saying of the Exalted: {والله وَرَسُولُهُ أَحَقُّ أَن يُرْضُوهُ} [al-Tawba: 62], {إِنَّ الذين يُؤْذُونَ الله وَرَسُولَهُ} [al-Aḥzāb: 57]. This of his is not satisfactory, because if attributing their deception to Allah the Exalted is valid on the aforementioned grounds, there is no necessity calling for claiming that the name of Allah the Exalted is redundant. As for «أعجبني زيدٌ وكرمُه», the pleasing is attributed to Zayd as a whole, then one of his attributes is conjoined to him, singling out this attribute from among all the attributes for its nobility; so in meaning it became analogous to the saying of the Exalted: {وملائكته وَرُسُلِهِ وَجِبْرِيلَ وَمِيكَالَ} [al-Baqara: 98].
The pattern «فاعَلَ» has five meanings: participation in meaning, as in «ضاربَ زيدٌ عمراً» ("Zayd and ʿAmr struck one another"); agreement with the bare form, as in «جاوَزْتُ زيداً», i.e. «جُزْتُه» ("I passed Zayd"); agreement with transitive «أَفْعَل», as in «باعَدْتُ زيداً» and «أَبْعدته» ("I distanced Zayd"); substituting for «أَفْعل», as in «وارَيْتُ الشيءَ» ("I concealed the thing"); and for the bare form, as in «سافَرْت» ("I travelled"), «قاسَيْت» ("I endured") and «عاقَبْت» ("I punished"). In the verse, «فاعَلَ» may bear the first two meanings. As for participation: their deceiving Allah the Exalted — its meaning has preceded; Allah's deceiving them is in that He applied to them the rulings of the Muslims in this world; and the believers' deceiving them is their carrying out the command of Allah the Exalted concerning them. As for its being in the sense of the bare form, the reading of Ibn Masʿūd and Abū Ḥaywa, «يَخْدَعون», makes it clear.
Abū ʿAmr and the two Ḥaramīs [Nāfiʿ and Ibn Kathīr] read «وما يُخَادِعون» like the first, and the rest «وما يَخْدعون». The two readings may have a single meaning, i.e. «فاعَلَ» being in the sense of «فَعَل»; or the mufāʿala may be in its proper sense, I mean issuing from two parties: they deceive their souls, in that they make them wish for falsehoods, and their souls deceive them, in that they too make them wish for that; so it is as though it were a dialogue between two. This would be close to the saying of another:
175 - لم تَدْرِ ما لا ولستَ قائلَها ... عُمْرَكَ ما عِشْت آخرَ الأبدِ
ولم تُؤامِرْ نَفْسَيْكَ مُمْتَرِياً ... فيها وفي أختِها لم تَكَدِ
(You did not know what "no" is, and you will not say it as long as you live, to the end of time; nor did you consult your two souls, doubting about it and its sister — you did not even come close.)
And another said:
176 - يؤامِرُ نَفْسَيْهِ وفي العيشِ فُسْحَةٌ ... أَيَسْتَوْقِعُ الذُّوبانَ أَمْ لا يَطورُها
(He consults his two souls, while there is room in life: should he await the wolves, or not approach them?)
His saying «إلا أنفسَهم»: «إلا» is originally a particle of exception, and «أنفسَهم» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). This exception is an emptied exception (istithnāʾ mufarragh), which is an expression [Translator's note: the source has the typo «عبادرة» for «عبارة»] for that in which what precedes «إلا» needs what follows it. Do you not see that «يُخادعون» needs an object? Similar to it is «ما قام إلا زيدٌ» ("none stood except Zayd"), for «قام» needs a fāʿil (agent). The complete (tāmm) exception is the opposite, i.e. that in which what precedes «إلاَّ» does not need what follows it, as in «قام القومُ إلا زيداً» ("the people stood except Zayd") and «ضربتُ القوم إلا بكراً» ("I struck the people except Bakr"): «قام» has taken its fāʿil and «ضربتُ» has taken its object. The condition of the emptied exception is that it come after a negation or what resembles it, such as interrogation and negation. [Translator's note: "and negation" (والنفي) here is probably a corruption of "and prohibition" (والنهي).] As for their saying «قرأتُ إلا يومَ كذا» ("I read except on such-and-such a day"), the meaning is upon an interpreted negation, its implied form being: "I did not leave off reading except on such-and-such a day." Similar to it are: {ويأبى الله إِلاَّ أَن يُتِمَّ نُورَهُ} [al-Tawba: 32] and {وَإِنَّهَا لَكَبِيرَةٌ إِلاَّ عَلَى الخاشعين} [al-Baqara: 45]. Exception has many rulings which will come in detail in the course of the book, if Allah the Exalted wills.
It was also read «وما يُخْدَعون», passive, and it is explained on the basis that the original was «وما يُخْدَعون إلا عن أنفسِهم»; when the preposition was omitted it became accusative, in the manner of:
177 - تَمُرُّون الديار ولم تَعُوجوا ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(You pass the dwellings and do not turn aside …)
And «يُخَدِّعون», from «خَدَّعَ» with doubling; and «يَخَدِّعون», with fatḥa on the yāʾ and doubling, the original being «يَخْتَدِعون», then it was assimilated.
{وَمَا يَشْعرونَ}: this verbal clause may have no grammatical position, because it is resumptive; or it may have a position, namely the accusative as a ḥāl from the fāʿil of «يَخْدعون», the meaning being: the evil consequence of their deception returns only upon themselves, while they are not aware of that. The object of «يَشْعُرون» is omitted because it is known, its implied form being: "and they are not aware that the evil consequence of their deception returns upon themselves", or "[they are not aware of] Allah's knowledge of them". It is better not to imply an object for it, because the purpose is to negate awareness of them altogether without regard to what it relates to. The first is called ellipsis for brevity (ḥadhf al-ikhtiṣār), meaning omitting something because of an indication; the second is called ellipsis of restriction (ḥadhf al-iqtiṣār), which is omitting something without an indication.
Al-shuʿūr (awareness) is perceiving a thing in a way that is subtle and hidden; it is derived from al-shaʿr (hair) because of its fineness. It was also said: it is perception by the senses, derived from al-shiʿār, which is the garment next to the body; and from it come mashāʿir al-insān, i.e. his five senses by which he perceives.

semin-durr:29-29.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {هُوَ الذي خَلَقَ لَكُمْ}: «هو» is a mubtadaʾ (subject); it is a detached nominative pronoun of the absent masculine. The well-known form is with its wāw light and with fatḥa; it is sometimes doubled, as in his saying:
320 - وإنَّ لِساني شُهْدَةٌ يُشْتَفَى بها ... وَهُوَّ على مَنْ صَبَّهُ اللهُ عَلْقَمُ
(My tongue is a honeycomb from which healing is sought, yet it is colocynth upon the one on whom Allah pours it.)
It is sometimes made quiescent (sukūn), and it is sometimes elided, as in his saying:
321 - فَبَيْنَاهُ يَشْرِي. . . . . . . . . . . ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(And while he was selling …)
The relative noun after it is a khabar (predicate) of it. «لكم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «خَلَقَ», and its meaning is causation, i.e. "for your sake"; it has been said: it is for ownership and permission, so it is a granting of ownership specific to what can be benefited from; and it has been said: for specification (ikhtiṣāṣ). «ما» is a relative noun and «في الأرض» is its ṣila (relative clause), and it [«ما»] is in the position of the accusative as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). «جميعاً» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the object, in the sense of "all"; it carries no indication of being together in time. This is the difference between your saying «جاؤوا جميعاً» (they came, all of them) and «جاؤوا معاً» (they came together), for «مع» entails accompaniment in time, unlike «جميع». It has been said: here it is an emphasising ḥāl (ḥāl muʾakkida), because His saying «ما في الأرضِ» is general.
His saying: {ثُمَّ استوى إِلَى السمآء فَسَوَّاهُنَّ سَبْعَ سَمَاوَاتٍ}: the basic sense of «ثُمَّ» is to entail a temporal delay, and there is no time here. So it has been said: it is an indication of the distance between the ranks of the creation of the earth and of the heaven. And it has been said: since between the creation of the earth and of the heaven there were other works — the placing of the mountains and the blessing and the measuring out of provisions, as He indicated in the other verse — He conjoined with «ثُمَّ», since between the creation of the earth and the turning (istiwāʾ) to the heaven there is a delay.
«استوى» in its lexical meaning is: became straight and level, from «استوى العُود» (the stick became straight). It has been said: it means rose and went up; the poet said:
322 - فَأَوْرَدْتُهُمْ مَاءً بفَيْفاءَ قَفْرَةٍ ... وقد حَلَّقَ النجمُ اليمانيُّ فاسْتَوَى
(I brought them down to water in a barren desert, when the Yemeni star had soared and risen high.)
And Allah the Exalted said: {فَإِذَا استويت أَنتَ وَمَن مَّعَكَ} [al-Muʾminūn: 28]. Its meaning here is: He directed Himself and intended. The fāʿil (agent) of «استوى» is a pronoun referring to Allah; it has been said that it refers to the smoke — Ibn ʿAṭiyya reported it — and this is an error for two reasons. The first: the absence of anything indicating it. The second: that His saying "then He turned to the heaven, while it was «دُخانٌ» (smoke)" refutes it. «إلى» is a particle of termination in its usual sense; it has been said that it is in the sense of «على», so that in meaning it would be like the poet's saying:
323 - قد استوى بِشْرٌ على العِراقِ ... مْنِ غيرِ سَيْفٍ وَدَمٍ مُهْرَاقِ
(Bishr has gained mastery over Iraq without a sword or blood poured out.)
i.e. gained control (istawlā); and like it is the saying of the other:
324 - فلمّا عَلَوْنَا واسْتَوَيْنَا عليهِمُ ... تَرَكْنَاهُمُ صَرْعَى لِنَسْرٍ وكاسِرِ
(When we rose up and mastered them, we left them felled for the vulture and the bird of prey.)
And it has been said: there is an omitted muḍāf, whose pronoun is the agent, i.e. "His command turned (istawā amruhu)." {إِلَى السمآء} is attached to «استوى». In «فَسَوَّاهُنَّ», the pronoun refers to «السماء», either because it is the plural of «سَماوَة», as has preceded, or because it is a generic noun (ism jins) applied to the plural. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «هُنَّ» is a vague pronoun, and «سبعَ سماواتٍ» explains it, as in their saying «رُبَّه رَجُلاً». This has been rejected against him, for it is not one of the places in which a pronoun is explained by what comes after it, because the grammarians limited that to seven places: the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn); the one made genitive by «رُبَّ»; the one made nominative by «نِعْمَ» and «بِئْسَ» and what runs their course; [the pronoun] with the first of two contending [verbs] (al-mutanāziʿayn); the one explained by its khabar; and [the pronoun] with the substituted-for (al-mubdal minhu). [Translator's note: the list as printed names six items, though the text says seven.] Then this objector said: "Unless it is imagined that «سبع سماواتٍ» is a badal (substitute) — and that is what his comparing it to «رُبَّه رجلاً» requires, for that is a vague pronoun not referring to anything before it. But this is weakened in that this construction makes it entirely unconnected with what precedes it, so He would have given two pieces of information: one of them, that He turned to the heaven;
and the second, that He fashioned seven heavens; whereas the apparent sense of the speech is that what He turned to is the very thing that was fashioned."
His saying: {سَبْعَ سَمَاوَاتٍ}: there are five aspects regarding its accusative. The best of them: that it is a badal of the pronoun in {فَسَوَّاهُنَّ}, which refers to «السماء», as in your saying «أخوك مررتُ به زيدٍ» (your brother — I passed by him, Zayd). The second: that it is also a badal of the pronoun, but this pronoun is explained by what comes after it; this is weakened by what weakened al-Zamakhsharī's view, which has just preceded. The third: that it is a mafʿūl bihi, the underlying form being «فَسَوَّى مِنْهُنَّ سبعَ سماواتٍ» (so He fashioned from them seven heavens), and they compared it to His saying, Exalted is He: {واختار موسى قَوْمَهُ سَبْعِينَ} [al-Aʿrāf: 155], i.e. "from his people"; Abū al-Baqāʾ and others said this. This is weak for two reasons: one with respect to the wording, and the second with respect to the meaning. As for the first: because it is not one of the verbs that take two objects, one of them by dropping the preposition, since these are restricted to «أمر» and «اختار» and their sisters. The second: that it would entail that there were many heavens, of which He fashioned seven, and that is not so. The fourth: that «سَوَّى» is in the sense of «صَيَّر» (made into), so it takes two objects, and «سبع» is a second object; this too has not been established, I mean making «سَوَّى» like «صَيَّرَ». The fifth: that it is accusative as a ḥāl; this is attributed to al-Akhfash. There is remoteness in it from two angles: one, that it is an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara), which is contrary to the basic rule; and the second, that it is interpreted as a derived word, which is also contrary to the basic rule.
His saying: {وَهُوَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ}: «هو» is a mubtadaʾ and «عليمٌ» its khabar, and the preposition-phrase before it is attached to it.
Know that it is permissible to make the hāʾ of «هو» and «هي» quiescent after the wāw, the fāʾ, the lām of inception (lām al-ibtidāʾ) and «ثم», e.g. {فَهِيَ كالحجارة} [al-Baqara: 74], {ثُمَّ هُوَ يَوْمَ القيامة} [al-Qaṣaṣ: 61], {لَهُوَ الغني} [al-Ḥajj: 64], {لَهِيَ الحيوان} [al-ʿAnkabūt: 64], by likening «هو» to «عَضُد» and «هي» to «كَتِف»: just as it is permissible to make the middle radical of «عَضُد» and «كَتِف» quiescent, it is permissible to make the hāʾ of «هو» and «هي» quiescent after the aforementioned letters, treating the detached like the attached because of how frequently they occur together. It is sometimes made quiescent after the kāf of comparison (kāf al-jarr), as in his saying:
325 - فَقُلْتُ لَهُمْ ما هُنَّ كَهْي فكيف لي ... سُلُوٌّ، ولا أَنْفَكُّ صَبَّاً مُتَيَّمَا
(I said to them: they are not like her — so how can I have consolation, while I remain ever a lovesick, enslaved lover?)
and after the hamza of interrogation, as in his saying:
326 - فقُمْتُ للطَّيْفِ مُرْتاعاً فَأَرَّقَنِي ... فقلتُ أَهْيَ سَرَتْ أم عادني حُلُمُ
(I rose, startled, at the phantom, and it kept me awake; I said: did she travel by night, or did a dream visit me?)
and after «لكنَّ» in the reading of Ibn Ḥamdūn: {لَّكِنَّ هْوَ الله رَبِّي} [al-Kahf: 38], and likewise in His saying: {يُمِلُّ هْوَ} [al-Baqara: 282].
If it is said: «عليم» is a faʿīl form from «عَلِم», which is transitive by itself, yet it was made transitive with the bāʾ; and it should properly, when its object comes first, reach it either by itself or with the strengthening lām, and when it comes later, reach it by itself only? [Translator's note: the answer formula, e.g. «فالجواب», appears to have dropped from the printed text; the answer follows.] [The answer is] that the intensive forms (amthilat al-mubālagha) differed from their verbs and their active participles for a reason, namely their resemblance to the elative (afʿal al-tafḍīl) by virtue of the meaning of intensiveness they share; and the elative has a rule regarding transitivity, so the intensive forms were given that rule. It is this: they are either from a verb transitive by itself or not. If the former, then either it conveys knowledge or ignorance or it does not. If the former, it is made transitive with the bāʾ, e.g.
{هُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِكُمْ} [al-Najm: 32], {وَهُوَ عَلِيمٌ بِذَاتِ الصدور} [al-Ḥadīd: 6], and «زيدٌ جهولٌ بك وأنت أجهل به» (Zayd is ignorant of you, and you are more ignorant of him). If the latter, it is made transitive with the lām, e.g. «أنا أضربُ لزيدٍ منك وأنا له ضرَّاب» (I strike Zayd more than you, and I am a frequent striker of him), and from it is {فَعَّالٌ لِّمَا يُرِيدُ} [Hūd: 107]. And if they are from a verb made transitive by a preposition, they are made transitive by that same preposition, e.g. «أنا أصبرُ على كذا، وأنا صبورٌ عليه» (I am more patient with such-and-such, and I am very patient with it), and «أزهدُ فيه منك، وزهيدٌ فيه» (more abstinent from it than you, and abstinent from it). This is established in the science of grammar.

semin-durr:36-36.t:
His saying: {فَأَزَلَّهُمَا الشيطان عَنْهَا}: the object here must come first because it is an attached pronoun and the fāʿil (agent) is an overt noun; everything of this kind has this rule. Ḥamza read: «فَأَزَالهما». The two readings may possibly have one meaning, namely that the reading of the majority, «أَزَلَّهما», may be from «زَلَّ عن المكان» (he slipped away from the place) when one moves away from it, so that it is from removal (al-zawāl), like Ḥamza's reading. This is indicated by the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:
378 - كُمَيْتٍ يَزِلُّ اللِّبْدُ عن حالِ مَتْنِهِ ... كما زَلَّتِ الصَّفْواءُ بالمُتَنَزَّلِ
(A bay horse, from the middle of whose back the saddle-felt slips off, as the smooth rock causes the rain-torrent [or what descends on it] to slip away.)
He also said:
379 - يَزِلُّ الغلامُ الخِفُّ عن صَهَوَاتِهِ ... ويَلْوِي بأثوابِ العنيفِ المُثَقَّلِ
(The light youth slips off its saddle-back, and it flings away the garments of the rough, heavy rider.)
So we refer the reading of the majority back to Ḥamza's reading; or we refer Ḥamza's reading back to the reading of the majority by saying: the meaning of أزالَهما is "he turned them away from obedience to Allah the Exalted and thus made them fall into the slip", because his seducing them and making them fall into the slip is a cause of the removal. It is also possible that each reading conveys an independent meaning: the reading of the majority announces making them fall into the slip, so that زلَّ means "caused to slip"; and Ḥamza's reading announces removing them from their place. Figurative usage (majāz) is necessary in both readings, because al-zalal [originally] applies to the slipping of the foot, and here it has been used for a slip of judgment; and removal is not within Satan's power — he only has power over whispering, which is in the slip of judgment; and removal (al-taḥiyya) is not within Satan's power — he only has power over whispering, which is the cause of the removal. [Translator's note: the source repeats this sentence, the second time with «التحية» (greeting), evidently a slip for «التنحية» (removal); it has been translated as written, rendered by sense.] «عنها» is attached to the verb before it. The meaning of «عَنْ» here is causation if we refer the pronoun back to «الشجرة», i.e. "he made them fall into the slip because of the tree". It may also be in its normal sense of passing away from (al-mujāwaza) if the pronoun [refers] to «الجَنَّةِ», and that is the more apparent, since it has been mentioned before; on this view Ḥamza's reading comes out clearly, whereas his reading is not fully clear on the pronoun being for the tree. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "As for whoever read «أَزَالهما», it refers to the garden only." It has also been said: the pronoun is for obedience, or for the state, or for heaven, though no mention of it has occurred, because the context indicates it; and this is very far-fetched.
His saying: {فَأَخْرَجَهُمَا مِمَّا كَانَا فِيهِ}: the fāʾ here is clearly causal. Al-Mahdawī said: "If «فَأَزَلَّهما» is taken in the sense of 'slipped away from the place', then His saying, Exalted is He, {فَأَخْرَجَهُمَا مِمَّا كَانَا فِيهِ} is a tawkīd (emphasis), since it is possible that they move from one place they were in to another place." What al-Mahdawī said here most resembles foundation (taʾsīs), not emphasis, since it conveys a new meaning. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "Here there is an omission indicated by the apparent text, its implied form being: 'so they ate from the tree'", meaning by that that the omitted part is supposed before His saying «فَأزَلَّهما».
{مِمَّا كَانَا} is attached to أَخْرَجَ. «ما» may be a nominal relative noun, or an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective, i.e. "from the place or the bliss which they were in", or "from a place or bliss they were in". So the clause consisting of kāna, its noun and its predicate has no grammatical position on the first view, and its position is the genitive on the second. «مِنْ» is for the beginning of the extent.
His saying «اهبِطوا» is an imperative clause in the position of the accusative by the verb [before it]. It has been read «اهبُطوا» with ḍamma on the bāʾ, which is common in intransitive verbs. As for the past, it is هبَطَ with fatḥa only, and both forms have come in its imperfect. The maṣdar (verbal noun) is al-hubūṭ with ḍamma, and it means descending. It has also been said: moving in general. Al-Mufaḍḍal said: "Al-hubūṭ is going out of a town, and it is also entering it, so it is one of the words with opposite meanings (aḍdād)." The pronoun in «اهبطوا» apparently refers to a group. So it has been said: to Adam, Eve, the serpent and Iblīs; [and it has been said: to the two of them and the serpent]; and it has been said: to the two of them and the whispering — and in this there is far-fetchedness. It has also been said: to the children of Adam and the children of Iblīs; and this, even if transmitted from Mujāhid and al-Ḥasan, ought not to be said, because nothing was born to the two of them in the Garden, by agreement. [Translator's note: the printed text reads «الجنة» (the Garden) in the list of addressees, which does not fit the context; it is evidently a slip for «الحيّة» (the serpent), the reading commonly cited in this discussion, and has been rendered accordingly.] Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It refers to Adam and Eve, and what is meant is the two of them and their offspring, because since they were the root of humankind and the source from which they branch, they were treated as though they were all of humankind; and this is indicated by «قال اهبِطوا منها جميعاً»."
His saying: {بَعْضُكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوٌّ}: this is a clause of mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), and there are two views on it. The more correct of them: that it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "descend, being enemies to one another". The second: that it has no grammatical position, because it is a resumption (istiʾnāf) informing of the enmity. The word «عدو» is singular, even though a plural is meant by it, for one of two reasons: either in consideration of the wording of «بعض», which is singular; or because «عَدُوَّاً» resembles maṣdars in pattern, like al-qabūl and the like. Abū al-Baqāʾ stated explicitly that some made ʿaduww a maṣdar; he said in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ: "It has been said: ʿaduww is a maṣdar like al-qabūl and al-walūʿ, and for that reason it was not pluralized." Makkī's wording is close to this, for he said: "It was made singular though a plural precedes it only because it has the sense of a maṣdar, its implied form being: possessors of enmity." [Similar to it is: {فَإِنَّهُمْ عَدُوٌّ لي} [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 77] and His saying: {هُمُ العدو فاحذرهم} [al-Munāfiqūn: 4]. The derivation of al-ʿaduww is from عَدا يعدُو when one does wrong. It has also been said: from عَدَا يعدُو when one oversteps the right; and the two are close. It has also been said: from the two ʿudwas of the mountain, which are its two sides, so they considered the distance between them. One says ʿudwa; and it may be pluralized as aʿdāʾ.]
The lām in «لِبعض» is attached to «عَدُوّ», strengthening it. It may also originally be an adjective of «عدُوّ», and when it was put before it, it became accusative as a ḥāl, so the lām is then attached to an omitted element. For this ḥāl clause there is no need to claim that the wāw of the ḥāl has been omitted from it, because the link is achieved by the pronoun, even though most commonly a nominal clause occurring as a ḥāl is joined with the wāw.
Al-baʿḍ is originally the maṣdar of بَعَضَ الشيءَ يَبْعَضُه when one cuts it; then it was applied to a portion of people, because it is a piece of them. It is the counterpart of «كُلّ», and its rule is the latter's rule in being necessarily annexed in meaning and in being definite by the intention of annexation, so al- does not enter it and a ḥāl may be put in the accusative from it. You say: «مررت ببعضٍ جالساً» (I passed by some, sitting). It has a wording and a meaning; the establishment of all that has preceded under the word «كُل».
His saying: {وَلَكُمْ فِي الأرض مُسْتَقَرٌّ}: in this clause the two aspects mentioned for the clause before it are possible: being a ḥāl and being resumptive — as though it were said: "descend, being enemies to one another and entitled to settlement". «لكم» is a fronted khabar. {فِي الأرض} is attached to what the khabar is attached to, namely settledness (al-istiqrār). Its attachment to it is in two ways. The first: that it is a ḥāl. The second: that it is not a ḥāl but like other adverbial expressions. It may also be that {فِي الأرض} is the khabar and «لكم» is attached to what it is attached to, namely settledness — but on the basis that it is not a ḥāl, lest it entail putting a ḥāl before its abstract governor; although some grammarians permitted that when the ḥāl itself is an adverb or a preposition, as in this verse, in which case «لكم» also admits the two aspects. One of them said: "{فِي الأرض} cannot be attached to مستقرّ, whether it is taken as a place or as a maṣdar: as for its being a place, because nouns of place do not govern; and as for its being a maṣdar, because a maṣdar equivalent to a relative cannot have what it governs put before it." One might say: it is attached to it as a maṣdar, but one not interpreted with a maṣdar particle; rather it is like the maṣdar in their saying: «له ذكاءٌ ذكاءَ الحكماءِ» (he has intelligence, the intelligence of the wise). The proponent of this view himself offered this very excuse in another place like this one.
His saying: {إلى حِينٍ}: the apparent view is that it is attached to متاع, and that the question belongs to the chapter of governing (al-iʿmāl), because each one of His words {مُسْتَقَرٌّ وَمَتَاعٌ} calls for His saying {إلى حِينٍ} in terms of meaning. The iʿmāl here has come according to the preference of the Basrans, which is that the second governs and the first is left without effect; for that reason it was omitted from it, the implied form being: "and for you in the earth is a settlement until it and an enjoyment until a time". Had it come with the first governing, a pronoun would have been implied in the second. If it is said: one of the conditions of iʿmāl is that each of the two governors can properly exercise control over the governed word, and «مستقرٌ» cannot properly exercise control over it, lest it entail separating the maṣdar from what it governs, the maṣdar being equivalent to a relative — the answer is: what is forbidden is in the maṣdar by which the event is intended, and this one is not intended as an event, so it is not interpreted as a relative. Moreover, adverbial expressions and the like are governed even by mere scents of the verb, even proper names, as in his saying:
380 - أنا ابنُ مَأوِيَّةَ إذ جَدَّ النُّقُرْ ...
(I am Ibn Māwiyya when the clicking [to urge horses] becomes earnest.)
«مستقر» may be a noun of place or a noun of maṣdar, mustafʿal from al-qarār, which is staying; for that reason the earth was called qarāra. The poet said:
381 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... فَتَرَكْنَ كلَّ قَرارَةٍ كالدِّرْهَمِ
(…and they [the rain-clouds] left every hollow [of ground] like a silver dirham.)
One says: استقرَّ and قرَّ with one meaning. Al-matāʿ: subsistence, taken from مَتَع النهار, i.e. the day rose high. Abū al-Baqāʾ preferred that «إلى حين» be in the position of the nominative as an adjective of مَتاع.
Al-ḥīn: a portion of time, whether long or short; this is the well-known view. It has also been said: a distant time. One says: عامَلَتْهُ محايَنَةً (I dealt with him for a period), and أَحْيَنْتُ بالمكانِ: I stayed in the place for a while, and حانَ حينُ كذا: its time drew near. Buthayna said:
382 - وإنَّ سُلُوِّي عن جميلٍ لَساعةٌ ... من الدهرِ ما حانَتْ ولا حانَ حِينُها
(My forgetting Jamīl is an hour of time that has not come, nor has its time drawn near.)
Some said: "tāʾ is added to it, so one says: تحينَ قُمْتَ (at the time you stood)", and he cited:
383 - العاطفونَ تحينَ ما مِنْ عاطِفٍ ... والمُطْعِمُون زمانَ أين المُطْعِمُ
(Those who turn back [to help] at a time when there is none who turns back, and those who feed at a time [when one asks]: where is the one who feeds?)
It is not so, and the precise treatment of this will come, if Allah the Exalted wills.

semin-durr:21-21.t:
The words of the Exalted: {يَاأَيُّهَا الناس اعبدوا رَبَّكُمُ}. «يا» is a vocative particle, and it is the mother of the category. Some claimed that it is a verbal noun (ism fiʿl). It may be omitted, as in {يُوسُفُ أَعْرِضْ} [Yūsuf: 29]. The one lamented (al-mandūb) and the one called for help (al-mustaghāth) are called with it. The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "Despite how often the vocative occurs in the Qur'an, no vocative occurs except with it." I say: some claimed that in the reading {أَمَنْ هُوَ قَانِتٌ} [al-Zumar: 9] with the mīm unstressed, the hamza is vocative; this is strange.
It may be intended merely to draw attention (tanbīh), in which case nominal and verbal clauses follow it. The Exalted said: {أَلاَ يا اسْجُدوا} [al-Naml: 25], with «أَلا» unstressed; the poet said:
256 - ألا يا اسْقِياني قبلَ غارةِ سِنْجالِ ...
(Ho, give me drink, you two, before the raid of Sinjāl.)
and another said:
257 - يا لعنةُ اللهِ والأقوامِ كُلِّهمِ ... والصالحينَ على سِمْعانَ من جارِ
(O, the curse of Allah, of all peoples and of the righteous, be upon Simʿān as a neighbour!)
«أيّ» is a noun addressed in the vocative, in the position of the accusative, but it is indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma because it is a single definite noun. Al-Akhfash claimed that here it is a relative noun, and that the nominative after it is the khabar (predicate) of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), the clause being the ṣila (relative clause), the implied form being «يا الذين هم الناسُ» (O you who are the people). The correct view is the first: the nominative after it is a naʿt (adjective) of it which must be nominative, and it may not be made accusative according to the position, contrary to al-Māzinī. «ها» is redundant (zāʾida), for drawing attention, and necessarily attached to it. Its hāʾ is well known with fatḥa, and ḍamma is permitted, following the yāʾ; ʿĀmir read it so in some places, such as {أيُّهُ المؤمنون} [al-Nūr: 31], and the written form (al-marsūm) supports it. [Translator's note: the text has «عامر»; the reader known for this reading is Ibn ʿĀmir.]
This «أيّ» may only be qualified by something containing the definite article, or by a relative noun containing it, or by a demonstrative, as in {ياأيها الذي نُزِّلَ عَلَيْهِ الذكر} [al-Ḥijr: 6]; the poet said:
258 - ألا أيُّهذا النابِحُ السِّيدَ إنني ... على نَأْيها مُسْتَبْسِلٌ مِنْ ورائِها
(Ho, you who bark at the wolf: despite her distance, I am ready to die defending her from behind.)
«أيّ» has other meanings, such as interrogation, condition, being a relative noun, an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective, an adjective of an indefinite noun, and a ḥāl (circumstantial) of a definite noun.
«الناسُ» is an adjective of «أي», or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, according to the disagreement mentioned above. «اعبدوا رَبَّكُمُ» is an imperative clause with no grammatical position, because it is initial (ibtidāʾiyya).
The words of the Exalted: {الذي خَلَقَكُمْ}: there are three views on it. The most apparent: it is accusative as a naʿt of «ربكم». Second: it is accusative by severance (qaṭʿ). Third: it is nominative, also by severance; its meaning has been explained before.
The words of the Exalted: {والذين مِن قَبْلِكُمْ}: its position is accusative, being conjoined to the accusative [pronoun] in «خَلَقَكم». «مِنْ قبلكم» is the ṣila of «الذين», so it is attached to an omitted element, as has been established; and «مِنْ» is for the beginning of an extent.
Some found it problematic that «مِنْ قبلكم» should be a ṣila, in that whatever may be used as a predicate may be used as a ṣila, and «مِنْ قبلكم» is incomplete (nāqiṣ): there is no benefit in predicating it of concrete things except through interpretation, and the same applies to the ṣila. He said: "Its interpretation is that when an adverb of time is qualified, it becomes valid to use it as a predicate and a ṣila; you say «نحن في يومٍ طَيِّبٍ» (we are on a good day). So the implied form here — and Allah knows best — is: «والذين كانوا من زمان قبلَ زمانكم» (and those who were in a time before your time)." Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "The implied form is: «والذين خَلَقَهم من قبلِ خَلْقِكم» (and those whom He created before creating you); «الخَلْق» was omitted and the pronoun put in its place."
Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «والذين مَن قَبْلِكُمْ», with fatḥa on the mīm. Al-Zamakhsharī said: Its justification, problematic as it is, is to say that the second relative noun was inserted between the first and its ṣila for emphasis, just as Jarīr, in his words:
259 - يَا تَيْمَ تَيْمَ عَدِيٍّ لا أبَالكُمُ ...
(O Taym, Taym of ʿAdī — may you have no father!)
inserted the second «تَيْماً» between the first and what it is annexed to, and like their insertion of the lām of annexation between the muḍāf and the muḍāf ilayhi in such expressions as «لا أبالكَ». It was said: "What he said is the view of some, and from it are the poet's words:
260 - من النَفَر اللاءِ الذين إذا هُمُ ... يَهابُ اللِّئامُ حَلْقَةَ البابِ قَعْقَعُوا
(Of the band who, when the base fear [to touch] the door-knocker, rattle it.)
so «إذا» with its answer is the ṣila of «اللاء», and «الذين» has no ṣila because it is an emphasis of the first."
However, some reject this view and regard it as unsound, in that a particle is only emphasized by repeating what is attached to it, so the relative noun is all the more so. They explained the verse and the line as follows: «مَنْ قبلكم» is the ṣila of the second relative noun; the second relative noun with its ṣila is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ; and the mubtadaʾ with its khabar is the ṣila of the first; the implied form being «والذينَ هُمْ [مَنْ] قبلكم» (and those who are those before you).
