Likewise the line: you make «إذا» with its answer the ṣila of «الذين», and «الذين» the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, and that mubtadaʾ with its khabar the ṣila of «اللاء». The strain in this is not hidden. [Translator's note: the source text reads «والذينَ هُمْ قبلكم» without «مَن»; the bracketed «مَن» is added for clarity.]
الخَلْق is used in two senses. One: origination and invention; this attribute belongs to the Creator alone. The second: measuring out (taqdīr); Zuhayr said:
261 - ولأَنْتَ تَفْري ما خَلَقْتَ وبَعْ ... ضُ القومِ يَخْلُقُ ثم لاَ يَفْري
(You cut out what you have measured, while some people measure and then do not cut.)
And al-Ḥajjāj said: «ما خلقْتُ إلاَّ فَرَيْتُ ولا وَعَدْتُ إلا وَفَيْتُ» (I never measured without cutting, nor promised without fulfilling).
This attribute is not exclusive to Allah the Exalted. Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Baṣrī erred in holding that the name "Creator" (al-Khāliq) is not applied to Allah the Exalted; he said: because it is impossible, since measuring out and fashioning are impossible with respect to Allah the Exalted, as they denote reflection and conjecture. It is as if he had not heard the words of the Exalted: {هُوَ الله الخالق البارىء} [al-Ḥashr: 24], {الله خَالِقُ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ} [al-Zumar: 62], and as if he did not know that الخَلْق may denote bringing into being and invention.
The words of the Exalted: «لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَّقُونَ»: «لعلّ» with its ism (subject) and its khabar. When this occurs in the speech of Allah the Exalted, people hold three views about it. First: «لَعَلَّ» has its basic meaning of hope and raising expectation, but relative to those addressed, i.e. "that you may be God-fearing, according to your hope and expectation". Sībawayh said likewise of the word of the Exalted {لَّعَلَّهُ يَتَذَكَّرُ} [Ṭāhā: 44], i.e. go, the two of you, in your hope. Second: it is for giving a reason (taʿlīl), i.e. worship your Lord so that you may be God-fearing; Quṭrub, al-Ṭabarī and others held this, and they recited:
262 - وقُلْتُمْ لنا كُفُّوا الحروبَ لَعَلَّنا ... نَكُفُّ ووَثَّقْتُمْ لنا كلَّ مَوْثِقِ
فلمّا كَفَفْنَا الحربَ كانَتْ عهودُكُمْ ... كَلَمْعِ سَرابٍ في المَلاَ مُتَألِّقِ
(You said to us: "Stop the wars, so that we may stop", and you gave us every pledge; but when we stopped the war, your pacts were like the gleam of a mirage shimmering in the desert.)
[Translator's note: the verse number appears garbled in the source as «26 - 2-»; it is given here as 262.]
i.e. so that we may stop the war; had «لعلّ» been for hope, he would not have said «وَوَثَّقْتُمْ لنا كلَّ مَوْثِقِ». Third: it is for exposing oneself to a thing, as if it were said: do that, exposing yourselves to becoming God-fearing.
On every view this clause is connected in meaning to «اعبدوا», i.e. worship Him in your hope of God-fearingness, or in order to be God-fearing, or exposing yourselves to God-fearingness; al-Mahdawī and Abū al-Baqāʾ inclined to this.
Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "Its connection to «خَلَقَكم» is sound, in that every child is born upon the natural disposition (fiṭra), so he is in a state in which it is hoped that he will be God-fearing." But al-Mahdawī disallowed that, saying: "Because whomever Allah produced for Hell He did not create so that he might be God-fearing." Al-Zamakhsharī mentioned nothing but its connection to «خَلَقَكُمْ», and then built two questions on that. First: just as He created those addressed that they might be God-fearing, so He created those before them for that; so why did He single out those addressed for it, rather than those before them? He answered that He did not restrict it to them, but gave precedence in the wording to those addressed over those absent, while the meaning intends all. The second question: why was it not said «تعبدونَ» (you may worship) to match «اعبدوا», or «اتقوا» (be God-fearing) to match «تَتَّقُون», so that the two ends of the composition would correspond? He answered that God-fearingness is not something other than worship, such that this would lead to discord in the composition; rather, God-fearingness is the utmost aim of the worshipper and the furthest extent of his effort.
The Shaykh said: "As for his words 'so that the two ends of the composition would correspond', it is nothing, because correspondence of the two ends of the composition is not possible here, since the wording would be: 'Worship your Lord that you may worship', or 'Fear your Lord that you may fear'; and this is far-fetched in meaning, since it is like 'Strike Zayd that you may strike him' and 'Go to Khālid that you may go to him'; the feebleness of the wording and unsoundness of the meaning in that are not hidden. What makes its soundness apparent is that «لعلكم تتقون» be connected to His words «اعبدوا»: what they were called for is the command to worship, so it is fitting that this be connected to it. The relative noun with its ṣila was brought by way of clarification or praise of Him to whom the worship is directed; the relative noun was not brought in order to say something about it, but came within the object of worship, so it [the clause] would not be connected to it rather than to the main intent." I say: this is clear.
There are many dialectal forms of «لعلّ». It may make a noun genitive; the poet said:
263 - لَعلَّ اللهِ فَضَّلَكُمْ علينا ... بشيء أنَّ أمَّكُمُ شَرِيمُ
(Perhaps Allah has favoured you over us in something — that your mother is torn.)
According to the correct view it does not make both nouns accusative. «أَنْ» may enter its khabar by analogy with «عسى»; the poet said:
264 - لَعَلَّكَ يوماً أن تُلِمَّ مُلِمَّةٌ ...
(Perhaps one day a calamity may befall you.)
It may come for interrogation and for giving a reason, as mentioned. But its basic meaning is hope and expectation in things desired, and apprehension in things disliked, like «عسى». There is longer discussion of it than this, which will come in detail in the course of this book, if Allah the Exalted wills.
The origin of «تَتَّقُون» is تَوْتَقِيُون, because it is from الوقاية (protection). The wāw was changed into tāʾ before the tāʾ of the iftiʿāl form and assimilated into it; this was explained at {لِّلْمُتَّقِينَ} [al-Baqara: 2]. Then the ḍamma on the yāʾ was felt heavy, so it was made implied (muqaddar); the yāʾ and the wāw after it were then vowelless, so the yāʾ was dropped because of the meeting of two vowelless letters, and the qāf was given ḍamma to match it [the wāw]. So its pattern now is تَفْتَعُونَ.
This clause — I mean «لعلكم تتقونَ» — may not be a ḥāl, because it is a request (ṭalabiyya), even though the wording of some suggests that. The object of «تَتَّقون» is omitted, i.e. you guard against idolatry (shirk) or the Fire.

semin-durr:10-10.t:
The saying of the Exalted: {فِي قُلُوبِهِم مَّرَضٌ}: the verse. The preposition and its genitive noun are a fronted khabar (predicate), necessarily fronted, for the reason mentioned earlier on His saying: {وعلى أَبْصَارِهِمْ غِشَاوَةٌ} [al-Baqara: 7]. The well-known reading is with the rāʾ of «مَرَض» vowelled; al-Aṣmaʿī related from Abū ʿAmr its being unvowelled (sukūn). They are two dialectal forms of the maṣdar (verbal noun) of «مَرِضَ يَمْرَض». Al-maraḍ (sickness) is languor; it was also said: corruption; and it is applied to darkness, and they recited:
178 - في ليلةٍ مَرِضَتْ من كلِّ ناحيةٍ ... فما يُحَسُّ بها نَجمٌ ولا قَمَرُ
(On a night that was "sick" on every side, so that neither star nor moon could be perceived in it.)
i.e. because of its darkness. It is also possible that by «مَرِضَتْ» he meant "became corrupt", and then explained the aspect of the corruption as darkness.
His saying: {فَزَادَهُمُ الله مَرَضاً}: this is a verbal clause conjoined to the nominal clause before it, caused by it, meaning that the cause of the increase is the occurrence of sickness in their hearts, since what is meant by sickness here is rancour and envy at the manifestation of the religion of Allah the Exalted. «زاد» is used intransitively, and transitively to two objects, the second of which is other than the first, like «أعطى» (to give) and «كسا» (to clothe); so it is permissible to omit both its governed words or one of them, for brevity (ikhtiṣār) or restriction (iqtiṣār). You say «زاد المال» ("the wealth increased"), and this is intransitive; and «زِدْتُ زيداً خيراً» ("I increased Zayd in good"), and from it are {وَزِدْنَاهُمْ هُدًى} [al-Kahf: 13] and {فَزَادَهُمُ الله مَرَضاً}; and «زدتُ زيداً», without mentioning what you increased him in; and «زدْتُ مالاً», without mentioning whom you increased. The alif of «زاد» is converted from a yāʾ, because of their saying «يزيدُ».
{وَلَهُم عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ} is analogous to the saying of the Exalted: {وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ عظِيمٌ} [al-Baqara: 7], which has preceded. «أليم» here means «مُؤْلِم» (painful), as in the poet's saying:
179 - ونَرْفَعُ مِنْ صدورِ شَمَرْدَلاتٍ ... يَصُكُّ وجوهَها وَهَجٌ أليمُ
(We raise the chests of tall swift she-camels whose faces are struck by a painful blaze of heat.)
It is pluralised on «فُعَلاء», like «شريف» and «شُرَفَاء», and on «أَفْعال», like «شريف» and «أَشْراف». It is also possible that «فعيل» here is for intensiveness, converted from «فَعِلَ» with kasra on the ʿayn; on this view attributing pain to the punishment is figurative (majāz), because the pain befalls the one on whom the punishment falls, not the punishment itself; it is thus analogous to their saying «شِعْرٌ شاعِرٌ» ("poetic poetry").
{بِمَا كَانُوا يَكْذِبُونَ} is attached (mutaʿalliq) to the implied (muqaddar) notion of "being established" in «لهم», i.e. a painful punishment is established for them because of their giving the lie. «ما» may be maṣdariyya (forming a maṣdar), i.e. "because of their being liars"; this is on the view that «كان» has a maṣdar, which is the sound view according to some, because it is made explicit in the poet's saying:
180 - بِبَذْلٍ وحِلْمٍ ساد في قومه الفتى ... وكونُك إياه عليكَ يَسيرُ
(By generosity and forbearance the young man becomes master among his people, and your being him is easy for you.)
So he made «الكون» explicit. And it cannot be the maṣdar of complete (tāmma) «كان», since it puts [the khabar] after it in the accusative, namely «إياه»; though there is room for consideration regarding this verse which this is not the place for. On the view that it has a maṣdar, it is not permitted to make it explicit with it; you do not say «كان زيد قائماً كوناً». They said: because the khabar is like a compensation for the maṣdar, and the compensation and what it compensates for are not combined. In that case there is no need for a pronoun referring back to «ما», because it is a maṣdar-forming particle according to the sound view — contrary to al-Akhfash and Ibn al-Sarrāj in making the maṣdar-forming «ما» a noun. It is also possible that «ما» means «الذي» (that which), and in that case a referent must be implied, i.e. «بالذي كانوا يكذِّبونه» ("because of that which they used to deny"); the omission of the referent is permissible because the conditions are fulfilled, namely its being accusative, attached to a verb, and there being no other referent there.
Abū al-Baqāʾ claimed that «ما» being a nominal relative is the more apparent; he said: "because the implied hāʾ refers back to «الذي», not to the maṣdar." What he said is not binding, since someone may say: we do not concede that there must be an implied hāʾ, so that it would necessarily follow that «ما» is nominal. Rather, for one who reads «يَكْذِبون» without doubling, it is not transitive to an object; and for one who reads it with doubling, the object is omitted because the meaning is understood, i.e. «بما كانُوا يُكَذِّبون الرسولَ والقرآنَ» ("because they used to deny the Messenger and the Qur'an"); or the doubled form is in the sense of the undoubled. The Kufans [ʿĀṣim, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] read «يَكْذِبون» with fatḥa and without doubling, and the rest with ḍamma and doubling.
«يُكَذِّبون» is the imperfect of «كَذَّب» with doubling. This pattern has many meanings: imputing something [to someone], and from it is the noble verse; making transitive, as in «فَرَّحْتُ زيداً» ("I made Zayd glad"); multiplication, as in «قَطَّعْتُ الأثواب» ("I cut the garments to pieces"); making something have a quality, as in «قطَّرْتُه», i.e. I made him thrown on his side, and from it:
181 - قد عَلِمَتْ سَلْمى وجاراتُها ... مَا قَطَّر الفارسَ إلا أنا
(Salmā and her neighbours know that none threw the horseman down on his side but I.)
Naming, as in «فَسَّقْتُه», i.e. I called him a transgressor; supplication for someone, as in «سَقَّيْتُه», i.e. I said to him: "May Allah give you to drink"; or supplication against him, as in «عَقَّرْته», i.e. I said to him: "ʿAqran laka" (may you be wounded); attending upon something, as in «مَرَّضْتُه» ("I nursed him"); removal, as in «قَذَّيْتُ عينَه», i.e. I removed the mote from his eye; heading towards, as in «شَرَّق» and «غَرَّب», i.e. he headed east and west; abbreviating a quoted phrase, as in «أَمَّن», [meaning] he said "Āmīn"; agreement with «تَفَعَّل» and with undoubled «فَعَل», as in «ولَّى» in the sense of «تَوَلَّى» and «قَدَّر» in the sense of «قَدَر»; and substituting for «تَفَعَّل» and undoubled «فَعَل», as in «حَمَّر», i.e. he spoke the dialect of Ḥimyar — they said: «مَنْ دَخَلَ ظَفارِ حَمَّر» ("whoever enters Ẓafār speaks Ḥimyarī") — and «عَرَّد» (to flee) in battle, which is in the sense of undoubled «عَرِد», even though that is not pronounced.
As for «الكذب» (lying), people disagreed about it. One says: it is reporting about a thing other than as it is, both in the mind and externally. It was said: other than as it is externally, whether it agrees with the speaker's belief or not. And it was said: reporting about it contrary to the speaker's belief, whether it agrees with what is external or not. Truthfulness is its opposite; and this is not the place for weighing [between these views].

semin-durr:66-66.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {نَكَالاً}: a second mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of جَعَلَ, which here has the sense of صَيَّر ("to make into"). The first object is the pronoun, and there are several views about it. One of them: it refers back to the transformation (al-maskha). It is also said: to the town, because the discourse implies it, like His saying: {فَأَثَرْنَ بِهِ نَقْعاً} [al-ʿĀdiyāt: 4], i.e. "in the place". It is also said: to the punishment; and it is also said: to the community (al-umma).

النَّكال means prevention (al-manʿ). From it comes النِّكْل, a name for the iron fetter and for the bridle, because one is restrained by it. Punishment is called نكال because by it others than the one punished are prevented from doing what he did, and the one punished is prevented from returning to his former deed. التنكيل is to strike another with a نكال so that others are deterred. نَكَلَ عن كذا يَنْكُل نُكولاً means "he held back from such-and-such". In the hadith: «إنَّ الله يحبُ الرجلَ النَّكَل» ("Allah loves the man who is نَكَل"), i.e. strong on horseback. And المَنْكَل is that with which a person is made an example of. The poet said:

528 - فارمِ على أَقْفائِهم بِمَنْكَلِ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Strike the backs of their necks with a crushing blow.)

The pronoun in يديها and خلفها is like the pronoun in {جَعَلْنَاهَا}.

His words: {وَمَوْعِظَةً}: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to {نَكَالاً}. It is a mafʿila form from الوعظ, which is to put in fear. Al-Khalīl said: "[It is] reminding of good in a way that softens the heart; the noun is العِظَة, like العِدَة and الزِّنَة."

And {لِّلْمُتَّقِينَ} is attached to (mutaʿalliq) مَوْعِظة, and the lām is that of cause. The God-fearing are singled out for mention, even though it is an admonition to the whole world, righteous and wicked alike, because those who benefit from it are these and not others. It is also possible that the lām is a strengthening lām, because موعظة is secondary to the verb in governing, so it is parallel to {فَعَّالٌ لِّمَا يُرِيدُ} [Hūd: 107]; on that view it has no attachment, being redundant (zāʾida). It may also be attached to an omitted element because it is a naʿt (adjective) of موعظة, i.e. "an admonition that is for the God-fearing".

semin-durr:67-67.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {يَأْمُرُكُمْ}: the majority read the rāʾ with ḍamma, because it is a declinable imperfect verb free of any particle of the subjunctive or the jussive. It is reported from Abū ʿAmr that he read it with a pure sukūn, and also with a slurring (ikhtilās) of the vowel. That is because of the succession of vowels, and because rāʾ is a letter of repetition (takrīr), so it is as if it were two letters and its vowel two vowels. It is also said: he likened it to عَضُد and so made its middle quiescent, treating the separate as if it were joined. This is as was discussed earlier regarding the reading «بارِئْكم»; mention has already been made of the grammarians who considered it weak, and of the answers to them, which makes repeating it here unnecessary. It is also permissible to replace the hamza of «يَأْمركم» with an alif, and this is a regular rule.

«يَأْمركم»: this clause is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of إنَّ; إنَّ with what falls within its scope is in the position of the accusative as object of the verb "say" (القول); and "say" with what falls within its scope is in the position of the genitive by the annexation of the adverb (ẓarf) to it; and the adverb is governed by an omitted verb, i.e. "remember (اذكُرْ)".

His words: {أَنْ تَذْبَحُواْ بَقَرَةً}: «أَنْ» with what falls within its scope is the second object of يأمركم. Its position may be accusative or genitive according to the disagreement mentioned earlier, because the original is with the preposition dropped, i.e. بأَنْ تَذْبَحوا. It is possible that al-Khalīl would agree here that its position is accusative, because with this verb the bāʾ may be dropped even where it is not «أَنْ», as in: أمرتُكَ الخيرَ ("I commanded you good").

البقرة is the singular (unit noun) of البَقَر. It applies to male and female, like حَمامة, and a qualifying adjective distinguishes the male from the female: you say بقرةٌ ذكرٌ and بقرةٌ أنثى. It is also said that بقرة is a name for the female of this genus specifically, in contrast to ثور ("bull"), like ناقة and جَمَل, and أَتان and حمار. This genus was named so because it يَبْقُر the earth, i.e. splits it with ploughing. From this come بَقَر بطنَه ("he split open his belly") and "al-Bāqir", Abū Jaʿfar, for his splitting open knowledge. The plurals are: بَقَر, باقِر, بَيْقُور and بَقِير.

His words: {هُزُواً}: the second object of {أَتَتَّخِذُنَا}. Regarding «هُزُواً» occurring as a second object there are three views. First: it is on the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "people of mockery". Second: it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) standing in the place of the object, i.e. "mocked". Third: they were made mockery itself, by way of hyperbole. This is the most fitting. Al-Zamakhsharī said, and began with it: "Do you make us a place of mockery?" — and this is close to the above.

In {هُزُواً} there are six readings, three of them well known: هُزُؤاً with two ḍammas and the hamza; and هُزْءاً with sukūn on the middle radical/ and the hamza in continuous recitation. This is the reading of Ḥamza, may Allah have mercy on him. When he pauses he changes it to wāw; that is not the analogical way of lightening it — its analogical rule is to cast its vowel onto the quiescent letter before it. He only followed the script of the Muṣḥaf, for it is written there with wāw. For this reason he did not change it to wāw in pause in «جزءاً», because it is not written there with wāw, as will come shortly. His reading originally had the ḍamma, like the reading of the majority, except that it was lightened, as they say عُنْق for عُنُق. It is also said that it is an original form in its own right, not lightened from the ḍamma. Makkī reported from al-Akhfash from ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar: "Every triliteral noun whose first letter has ḍamma admits two dialects: the heavy and the light."

And «هُزُواً» with two ḍammas and wāw, both in continuous recitation and in pause, which is the reading of Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim. It is as though he changed the hamza to wāw for lightening; that is a regular analogical rule in every hamza with fatḥa preceded by ḍamma, such as جُوَن for جُؤَن, and {السفهآء ولا إِنَّهُمْ} [al-Baqara: 13]. «كُفُواً» in the words of Allah the Exalted {وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَّهُ كُفُواً أَحَدٌ} [al-Ikhlāṣ: 4] takes the same ruling as «هُزُواً» in everything mentioned above, both in reading and in justification.

And «هُزَاً», by casting the vowel of the hamza onto the zāy and dropping it; this too is a regular analogical rule. And هُزْواً with sukūn on the middle radical and wāw. And هُزَّاً with a doubled zāy without hamza, which is reported from Abū Jaʿfar. The meaning of الهُزْء was discussed at the beginning of the sūra.

His words: {أَعُوذُ بالله}: its i'rab was given earlier under the istiʿādha (seeking refuge). This is in meaning an answer to their question, as though he said: "I do not mock, seeking refuge with Allah from that, for the one who mocks is ignorant." And his words {أَنْ أَكُونَ} mean: "from being" (مِن أَنْ أكونَ), so the well-known disagreement applies here. «مِنَ الجاهلين» is its khabar. This is more eloquent than saying "that I be ignorant", for the meaning is: "that I be strung on the thread of a people characterised by ignorance".

semin-durr:68-68.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {قَالُواْ ادع لَنَا رَبَّكَ يُبَيِّنَ لَّنَا}: like His words {فادع لَنَا رَبَّكَ يُخْرِجْ لَنَا} [al-Baqara: 61], which has already been discussed.

His words: «ما هي»?: ما is interrogative, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); its implied sense is "what thing is it?". Interrogative «ما» is used sometimes to ask for the explanation of a name, as in "What is the ʿanqāʾ?", and at other times for the essence of the thing named, as in "What is motion?". Al-Sakkākī said: "With «ما» one asks about the genus — you say 'What do you have?', i.e. which of the genera of things do you have, and its answer is 'a book' and the like — or about the description — you say 'What is Zayd?', and its answer is 'generous'." This [latter] is what is meant in the verse. «هي» is a detached nominative pronoun in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of «ما». The clause is in the position of the accusative governed by يبيِّن, because the verb is suspended (muʿallaq) from the clause after it; this is permissible because it resembles the verbs of the heart.

His words: {لاَّ فَارِضٌ وَلاَ بِكْرٌ}: لا is negative, and «فارض» is a naʿt (adjective) of بقرة; «لا» has been interposed between the adjective and the thing qualified, as in: مَرَرْتُ برجلٍ لا طويلٍ ولا قصيرٍ ("I passed by a man neither tall nor short"). Abū al-Baqāʾ permitted it to be the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "it is not فارض". His words {وَلاَ بِكْرٌ} are like what preceded. «لا» is repeated because whenever it comes before a khabar, an adjective or a ḥāl (circumstantial), repeating it is obligatory. You say: زيدٌ لا قائمٌ ولا قاعدٌ ("Zayd is neither standing nor sitting"), and مررت به لا ضاحكاً ولا باكياً ("I passed him neither laughing nor weeping"). Not repeating it is permitted only in poetic necessity, contrary to al-Mubarrad and Ibn Kaysān. Among examples of that:

529 - وأنتَ امرؤٌ مِنَّا خُلِقْتَ لغيرِنا ... حياتُك لا نفعٌ وموتُك فاجِعُ
(You are a man of ours, yet created for others: your life is no benefit, and your death is a grief.)

And his words:

530 - قَهَرْتَ العِدَى لا مُسْتَعيناً بعُصْبَةٍ ... ولكنْ بأنواعِ الخدائعِ والمَكْرِ
(You subdued the enemies, not seeking the help of a band, but by all kinds of tricks and cunning.)

So he did not repeat it, either in the khabar or in the ḥāl.

الفارض is the old, decrepit cow. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is as though it was named so because it فَرَضَتْ its age, i.e. cut through it and reached its end." The poet said:

531 - لَعَمْرِي لقد أَعْطَيْتَ جارَك فارِضاً ... تُساقُ إليه ما تقومُ على رِجْلِ
(By my life, you gave your neighbour an aged cow, driven to him, unable to stand on a leg.)

And everything old is called فارض. He said:

532 - شَيَّبَ أصداغِي فرأسي أبيضُ ... محامِلٌ فيها رجالٌ فُرَّضُ
(My temples have been greyed, and my head is white, by litters in which are aged men.)

i.e. old and ancient. Another said:

533 - يا رُبَّ ذي ضِغْنٍ عليَّ فارضِ ... له قُروءٌ كقُروءِ الحائِضِ
(How many a one bearing an old grudge against me, who has periods [of rage] like the periods of a menstruating woman.)

Al-Rāghib said: "It was called فارض because it cuts through the earth, الفَرْض originally meaning cutting. It is also said: because it carries heavy loads. It is also said: because the obligatory due (farīḍa) on cattle is a تَبِيع (one-year-old) and a مُسِنَّة (two-year-old)." He said: "On this view الفارض is an Islamic term." One says فَرَضَتْ تفرِضُ, with fatḥa, فُروضاً; and it is also said فَرُضَتْ, with ḍamma.

البِكْر is one that has not conceived. It is also said: one that has given birth to a single offspring, and that offspring is also called بِكْر. He said:

534 - يا بِكْرَ بَكْرَيْنِ ويا خِلْبَ الكَبِدْ ... أصبحْتَ مني كذراعٍ من عَضُدْ
(O firstborn of two firstborns, O membrane of the liver: you have become to me like the forearm to the upper arm.)

البِكْر among animals is one that no stallion has covered. البَكْر with fatḥa is a young camel, and البَكارة with fatḥa is the maṣdar.

His words: {عَوَانٌ}: a naʿt of بقرة. It may also be the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "it is عوان", as was said for {لاَّ فَارِضٌ}. العَوان is النَّصَف, the middle between two things, and that is the strongest and best state a thing can be in. He said:

535 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... نواعِمُ بين أبكارٍ وعُونِ
(… soft-living women, between virgins and middle-aged ones.)

It is also said: it is the one that has given birth time after time. From it comes الحَرْبُ العَوان, i.e. a war that came after another war. Zuhayr said:

536 - إذا لَقِحَتْ حربٌ عَوانٌ مُضِرَّةٌ ... ضَروسٌ تُهِرُّ الناسَ أنيابُها عُصْلُ
(When a repeated, harmful war becomes pregnant, a biting one that makes people snarl, its fangs crooked.)

العُون with sukūn on the wāw is the plural; it may be given ḍamma in poetic necessity, as in his words:

537 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... . . . . في الأكُفِّ اللامِعاتِ سُوُرْ
(… on the gleaming palms are bracelets.)

with ḍamma on the wāw. Its parallel among sound words is قَذَال / قُذُل and حِمار / حُمُر.

His words: {بَيْنَ ذلك}: a naʿt of عوان, so it is in the position of the nominative and is attached to an omitted element, i.e. "being between that". «بين» is only annexed to two or more things; it is permitted here to be annexed to a singular because ذلك can point to the dual and the plural, as in his words:

538 - إنَّ للخيرِ وللشَّرِّ مَدَى ... وكِلا ذلك [وَجْهٌ وقَبَلْ]
(Good and evil each have a limit, and both of that are [a face and a front].)

It is as if it were said: "between what has been mentioned of the فارض and the بِكْر". Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: how can it point to two feminines when it is for pointing to the masculine? I say: because it is in the sense of 'what has been mentioned and what has preceded'." And he said: "The pronoun may be treated like the demonstrative in this./ Abū ʿUbayda said: I said to Ruʾba about his words:

539 - فيها خطوطٌ من سَوادٍ وبَلَقْ ... كأنَّهُ في الجِلْدِ تَوْلِيعُ البَهَقْ
(On it are streaks of black and piebald white, as though it were, on the hide, the mottling of vitiligo.)

'If you meant the streaks, say كأنها; if you meant the black and the piebald, say كأنهما.' He said: 'I meant: as though that were — woe to you!'" What made this acceptable is that the dual, plural and feminine of the demonstratives are not real [inflections]; likewise the relative nouns, and for that reason الذي has come in the sense of the plural.

His words: {مَا تُؤْمَرونَ}: «ما» is a relative noun in the sense of الذي, and the resumptive pronoun is omitted, its implied form being "تُؤْمَرون به". The bāʾ was dropped — a regular omission — so the pronoun became attached [to the verb] and was then omitted. It is not parallel to {كالذي خاضوا} [al-Tawba: 69], for the omission there is not analogical. It is weak for «ما» to be an indefinite noun qualified by a description; Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "because the meaning is general, and that is more akin to الذي". It may also be maṣdariyya, i.e. "your being commanded" in the sense of "what you are commanded", calling the object by the maṣdar, as in ضَرْبُ الأمير ("the prince's coinage"); al-Zamakhsharī said this. «تُؤْمَرون» is passive, and the wāw stands in place of the agent as nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). This clause has no grammatical position because it is a ṣila (relative clause).

semin-durr:69-69.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {مَا لَوْنُهَا}: like His words «[ما] هي»? Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "If «لونَها» were read in the accusative it would have an aspect, namely that «ما» be redundant, as in His words {أَيَّمَا الأجلين قَضَيْتُ} [al-Qaṣaṣ: 28], the implied sense being 'that He make clear to us its colour'. As for «ما هي», it is mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate) and nothing else, since «ما» cannot be made redundant, because «هي» cannot be the object of يبيِّن" — meaning that it has the nominative form. [But] this is not one of the places where «ما» is made redundant, so there is no need for this.

Colour (اللون) denotes redness, blackness and the like. اللون is also "kind" (النوع), and it is the دَقَل, a kind of palm. [Translator's note: the text as given reads النحل ("bees"), evidently for النخل ("palms").] Al-Akhfash said: "It is a collective; its singular is لِينة", and this will come. فلان يَتَلَوَّن means he does not stay in one state. The poet said:

540 - كلَّ يومٍ تتلوَّنْ ... غيرُ هذا بك أَجْمَلْ
(Every day you change colour; other than this would become you better.)

His words: {صَفْرَآءُ فَاقِعٌ لَّوْنُهَا}: «فاقع» may be an adjective, with «لونُها» as its fāʿil (agent); or it may be a fronted khabar with «لونُها» a delayed mubtadaʾ and the clause an adjective. Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned these. The first view is questionable, because some have transmitted that these intensifiers that follow colours do not govern as verbs do. If it is said: the governing belongs to صفراء, not to فاقع, as you say مررتُ برجلٍ أبيضَ ناصعٍ لونُه, where لونُه is nominative by أبيض, not by ناصع — the answer is that this is ruled out here on another ground, namely that صفراء is feminine in form; had it been what puts «لونُها» in the nominative, one would have said أصفرُ لونُها, just as you say مررت بامرأةٍ أصفرَ لونُها, and صفراءَ لونُها is not permissible, because the adjective is like the verb — unless it be said that, since it is annexed to a feminine, it acquired femininity from it and was treated accordingly, as will be mentioned.

It is also possible that «لونُها» is a mubtadaʾ and «تَسُرُّ» its khabar; the verb was made feminine only because it acquired the sense of femininity through annexation, as in his words:

541 - مَشَيْنَ كما اهتَزَّتْ رماحٌ تَسَفَّهَتْ ... أعاليهَا مَرُّ الرياحِ النَّواسِمِ
(They walked [swaying] as spears sway whose tops are tossed by the passing of gentle winds.)

and the words of another:

542 - وتَشْرَقُ بالقولِ الذي قد أَذَعْتَه ... كما شَرِقَتْ صدرُ القناةِ من الدمِ
(You will choke on the word you have spread, as the top of the spear chokes with blood.)

He made the verb of المَرّ and الصدر feminine because they are annexed to a feminine. And it has been read {تَلْتَقِطْهُ بَعْضُ السيارة} [Yūsuf: 10]. It is also said: because what is meant by اللون here is yellowness (الصفرة), which is feminine, so it was construed according to the meaning.

One says: أصفرُ فاقعٌ, أبيضُ ناصعٌ, يَقِق, لَهِق and لِهاق, أخضرُ ناصعٌ, أحمرُ قانئٌ, and أسودُ حالِك, حائِك, حَلَكُوك, حُلْكُوك, دَجُوجيّ, غِرْبيب and بهيم. It is also said: "البهيم is that which is pure of any [other] colour." From this it becomes clear that صفراء is in its proper sense, the known colour, not "black" as some have said, for being فاقع is a description of yellow specifically. Moreover, that would be a far-fetched metaphor, and it is only used for camels, because their blackness is close to yellow, as in the words of Allah the Exalted: {كَأَنَّهُ جِمَالَةٌ صُفْرٌ} [al-Mursalāt: 33]. And he said:

543 - تلك خَيْلِيْ منه وتلكَ رِكابي ... هُنَّ صُفْرٌ أولادُها كالزَّبيبِ
(Those are my horses from him, and those my riding camels: they are dark-yellow, their young like raisins.)

His words: {تَسُرُّ الناظرين}: a clause in the position of the nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of «بقرة» as well. It was said above that it may be the khabar of «لونها» on the two interpretations mentioned. السرور is a pleasure in the heart upon obtaining a benefit or expecting it. From it comes السرير, the couch on which one sits, when it belongs to people of comfort; and the bier of the dead (سرير الميت) is so called by resemblance to it in form and as a good omen.

semin-durr:70-70.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {مَا هِيَ}?: a second time; a repetition of the question about its condition and description, and a further seeking of disclosure so that they might gain more clarity about its description.

His words: {إِنَّ البقر تَشَابَهَ عَلَيْنَا}: «البقر» is the noun of إنَّ, and it is a generic noun, as was said before. It has been read «الباقِرُ», which has the same meaning, as was said before. «تَشَابه» is a verbal clause in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of إنَّ.

It has been read «تَشَّابَهُ», with doubling and also without doubling, as an imperfect verb; the original is تَتَشابهُ with two tāʾs, so [one] was assimilated, or [in the other] the other one was dropped, and both ways are analogical. It has also been read يَشَّابَهُ, with the lower-dotted yāʾ, originally يتشابه, also with assimilation. Making the verb masculine or feminine are both permissible, because its agent is a generic noun, and in it there are two usages: masculine and feminine. Allah the Exalted said {أَعْجَازُ نَخْلٍ خَاوِيَةٍ} [al-Ḥāqqa: 7], making it feminine, and {أَعْجَازُ نَخْلٍ مُّنقَعِرٍ} [al-Qamar: 20], making it masculine. There is a place where we shall examine this exhaustively, which will come, if Allah the Exalted wills. [Translator's note: the source names the sūra "الحافة"; the verse is al-Ḥāqqa 69:7.]

[Further readings:] تَتَشَابَهُ with two tāʾs, on the original form; تَشَّبَّهُ with doubled shīn and bāʾ without alif, the original being تَتَشَبَّهُ; تَشَّابَهَتْ; مُتَشَابِهَة; مُتَشَابِه; and مُتَشَبِّه, as the active participle of تشابه and تَشَبَّه. It has also been read تَشَبَّهَ as a past verb. In the codex of Ubayy: «تَشَّابَهَتْ» with doubled shīn. Abū Ḥātim said: "It is a mistake, because the tāʾ in this pattern is assimilated only in the imperfect." He is excused in that. It has also been read تَشَّابَهَ likewise, but with the tāʾ of the feminine dropped. The way to account for it, despite its difficulty, is that the original is إن البقرة تشابَهَتْ: the first tāʾ is from البقرة and the second tāʾ from the verb; when two close letters met he assimilated them, as in الشجرة . . . except that it is also problematic in تَشَّابه without the tāʾ, because the sign/ of the feminine ought to have been retained. The answer is that it is like:

544 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... ولا أرضَ أَبْقَلَ إبْقالَها
(… nor is there any land that put forth herbage as it did.)

besides the fact that Ibn Kaysān does not insist on that [feminine sign] even in free usage.

His words: {إِن شَآءَ الله}: this is a condition whose apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted because إنْ and what falls within its scope indicate it. The implied sense is: "If Allah wills our guidance to the cow, we shall be guided." But they expressed it as a nominal clause emphasised with two particles of emphasis, in strong pursuit of guidance, and interposed the condition to seek blessing through the will of Allah the Exalted. In «لمهتدونَ» the lām is the lām of commencement (lām al-ibtidāʾ) entering the khabar of «إنَّ».

Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "The apodosis of the condition is إنَّ and what it governs, according to Sībawayh. That was permissible because the condition is placed in the middle; the khabar of إنَّ is the apodosis of the condition in meaning and has come after it, so the implied sense becomes: 'If Allah wills, we shall be guided.'" What he said is not permissible, for whenever the apodosis of a condition is something that cannot be a protasis, it must be joined with the fāʾ; and this clause cannot occur as a protasis, so had it been an apodosis the fāʾ would have been required for it, and it is not dropped except in poetic necessity. Nor can Abū al-Baqāʾ mean that it indicates the apodosis and that he called it an apodosis figuratively, because he made that a doctrine of al-Mubarrad opposed to the doctrine of Sībawayh, saying: "Al-Mubarrad said: the apodosis is omitted and the clause indicates it, because the condition is parenthetical and is intended to come later, so it becomes like your saying: 'You are unjust if you do [it]'." What he transmitted from al-Mubarrad is what is transmitted from Sībawayh, and what he transmitted from Sībawayh is close to what is transmitted from the Kufans and Abū Zayd, namely that the apodosis of a condition may be placed before it. The Basrans refuted them with the Arabs' saying "أنتَ ظالمٌ إنْ فعلْتَ" ("You are unjust if you do [it]"), since had it been an apodosis it would have had to be joined with the fāʾ, for the reason I mentioned to you.

The original of «مُهْتَدُون» is مُهْتَدِيُون; it underwent a weak-letter change by deletion, and this is clear from what has preceded.

semin-durr:97-97.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {قُلْ مَن كَانَ عَدُوّاً لِّجِبْرِيلَ فَإِنَّهُ} . . . «مَنْ» is conditional, in the position of the nominative (marfūʿ) as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «كان» is its khabar (predicate) according to what is correct, as has preceded. Its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, its implied form being: "Whoever is an enemy to Gabriel, there is no ground for his enmity", or "then let him die of rage", and the like. It is not permissible for «فإنه نزَّله» to be the apodosis of the condition, for two reasons: one from the side of meaning, the second from the side of grammatical craft. As for the first: because the act of sending down is something whose pastness is established, whereas the apodosis can only be future. But someone may say: this is taken as referring to becoming clear, the meaning being: "then it has become clear that he sent it down", as they said regarding His saying: {وَإِنْ كَانَ قَمِيصُهُ قُدَّ [مِن دُبُرٍ فَكَذَبَتْ} [Yusuf: 26] and the like. As for the second: because] the apodosis clause must contain a pronoun referring back to the conditional noun, so one may not say: «مَنْ يَقُمْ فزيدٌ منطَلِقٌ» ("whoever stands, then Zayd is leaving"), and there is no pronoun in His saying «فإنَّه نَزَّله» referring back to «مَنْ», so it cannot be the apodosis of the condition. Many instances of this have occurred, but they interpreted them as having the referring pronoun omitted; among them is the saying:
624 - فَمَنْ تَكُنِ الحضارَةُ أَعْجَبَتْهُ ... فَأَيَّ رجالِ باديةٍ تَراني
(Whoever is charmed by settled life — then what sort of desert man do you see me to be!)
And the saying:
625 - فَمَنْ يَكُ أَمْسى بالمدينةِ رَحْلُه ... فإني وقَيَّارٌ بها لَغَريبُ
(Whoever has his lodging in Medina by evening — I and Qayyār are strangers there.)
This ought to be built upon the disagreement about the khabar of the conditional noun. If it is said that the khabar is the apodosis alone — or it together with the condition — then the pronoun is necessary; and if it is said that it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) alone, then there is no need for the pronoun. The saying of Abū al-Baqāʾ and others on this has preceded at His saying, Exalted is He: {فَمَن تَبِعَ هُدَايَ} [al-Baqara: 38]. Al-Zamakhsharī stated explicitly that it is the apodosis of the condition, and in this there is the objection mentioned, and its answer is what has preceded.
And «عَدُوَّاً» is the khabar of kāna; the singular and others are equal in it; He said: «هم العدُوُّ» ("they are the enemy"). And al-ʿadāwa (enmity) is transgression. Al-Rāghib said: "With the heart one says al-ʿadāwa; with walking one says al-ʿadw (running); with breaching justice one says al-ʿudwān (aggression); and with place or lineage one says qawmun ʿidan, that is, strangers." And «لِجبريلَ» may be a naʿt (adjective) of «عَدُوّاً», so it is attached to (mutaʿalliq) something omitted; or the lām may be strengthening, for the transitivity of «عَدُوَّاً» to it. Jibrīl (Gabriel) is the name of an angel and it is foreign (aʿjamī), and for that reason it is a diptote. The saying of whoever said: "It is derived from the jabarūt (majesty) of Allah" is far-fetched, because derivation does not occur in foreign [nouns]; likewise the saying of whoever said: "It is compounded in a construct (iḍāfa) compound, and jabr means 'servant' and īl is one of the names of Allah the Exalted, so it is equivalent to ʿAbd Allāh" — because the first part ought then to take the various inflections and the second ought to be declinable; and likewise the saying of al-Mahdawī that it is a blended compound (tarkīb mazj) like ḥaḍramawt, because the first part ought then to be indeclinable on the fatḥa only.
As for the Shaykh's [Translator's note: Abū Ḥayyān] rebuttal of him [al-Mahdawī], that if it were a blended compound it would be permissible to inflect it as the two parts of a construct, or to make it indeclinable on the fatḥa like aḥada ʿashara, since everything compounded by blending admits these options, and that the fact that neither indeclinability nor treatment as a construct is attested for it is evidence that it is not a blended compound — this is not a good rebuttal, because it came on one of the two permissible options, and it happened that it was only used that way.
The Arabs handled it freely according to their custom with foreign nouns, and produced thirteen dialectal forms of it. The most famous and most eloquent of them: جِبْرِيل on the pattern of qindīl; it is the reading of Abū ʿAmr, Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir and Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim, and it is the dialect of the Hijaz. Waraqa ibn Nawfal said:
626 - وجِبْريلُ يأتيه ومِيكالُ مَعْهُما ... مِنَ اللهِ وَحْيٌ يَشْرَحُ الصدرَ مُنْزَلُ
(Gabriel comes to him, and Michael with them both, with revelation sent down from Allah that expands the breast.)
And Ḥassān said:
627 - وجِبْريلٌ رسولُ اللهِ فينا ... وروحُ القُدْسِ ليسَ له كِفَاءُ
(And Gabriel, the messenger of Allah, is among us — the Holy Spirit, who has no equal.)
And ʿImrān ibn Ḥiṭṭān said:
628 - والروحُ جبريلُ منهم لا كِفَاءَ له ... وكانَ جِبْرِيلُ عند الله مَأْمُوناً
(And the Spirit, Gabriel, is of them, with no equal; and Gabriel was trusted with Allah.)
The second: the same except with fatḥa on the jīm [جَبْرِيل]; it is the reading of Ibn Kathīr and al-Ḥasan. Al-Farrāʾ said: "I do not like it, because there is no faʿlīl in their speech." What he said is of no weight, because what the Arabs brought into their language is of two kinds: a kind they assimilated to their own patterns, like lijām, and a kind they did not assimilate, like ibraysam; moreover it has been said that it is the counterpart of shamwīl, the name of a bird. And it is reported from Ibn Kathīr that he saw the Prophet ﷺ [Translator's note: presumably in a dream; the text says only "saw"] reciting: جَبْريلَ وميكائيل, and he said: "So I shall never cease reciting them thus." The third: جَبْرَئيل like ʿantarīs; it is the dialect of Qays and Tamīm, and Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read with it. Ḥassān said:
629 - شهِدْنَا فما تَلْقى لنا من كتيبةٍ ... َ الدهرِ الا جَبْرَئِيلُ أَمامَها
(We were present, and you will not meet any squadron of ours, through all time, but that Gabriel is in front of it.) [Translator's note: the second hemistich appears defective in the source text.]
And Jarīr said:
630 - عبَدوا الصليبَ وكَذَّبوا بمحمدٍ ... وبجَبْرَئِيلَ وكَذَّبوا مِيكالا
(They worshipped the cross and denied Muhammad, and Gabriel, and denied Michael.)
The fourth: the same except that there is no yāʾ after the hamza [جَبْرَئِل]; it is related from ʿĀṣim and Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar. The fifth: the same except that the lām is doubled [جَبْرَئِلّ]; it is also related from ʿĀṣim and Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar as well. They said: and «إلّ» with doubling is a name of Allah the Exalted; and in some commentaries on {لاَ يَرْقُبُونَ فِي مُؤْمِنٍ إِلاًّ وَلاَ ذِمَّةً} [al-Tawba: 10] it is said: its meaning is Allah. And it is related from Abū Bakr that when he heard Musaylima's rhymed prose he said: "This is speech that did not come out of an ill (a god)." The sixth: جَبْرَائِل with an alif after the rāʾ and a hamza with kasra after the alif; ʿIkrima read with it. The seventh: like it, except with a yāʾ after the hamza [جَبْرَائِيل]. The eighth: جِبْرايِيل with two yāʾs after the alif, without hamza; al-Aʿmash and Yaḥyā also read with it. The ninth: جِبْرال. The tenth: جِبْرايِل with the yāʾ and shortening; it is the reading of Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif. The eleventh: جَبْرِين with fatḥa on the jīm and with nūn. The twelfth: the same except with kasra on the jīm [جِبْرِين]. The thirteenth: جَبْرايين.
The clause from His saying «مَنْ كان» is in the position of the accusative (manṣūb) by the verb of saying. The pronoun in His saying «فإنَّه» refers to Gabriel, and in His saying «نَزَّلَه» it refers to the Qurʾān; this agrees with His saying {نَزَلَ بِهِ الروح الأمين} [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 193] in the reading of those who put «الروح» in the nominative, and with His saying «مصدِّقاً». It has been said: the first refers to Allah and the second refers to Gabriel; this agrees with the reading of those who read {نَزَلَ به الروحُ} with doubling and the accusative [Translator's note: i.e. نَزَّلَ بِهِ الرُّوحَ]. He used «على», which entails being above, rather than «إلى», which entails termination; and He singled out the heart for mention because it is the treasury of memory and the house of the Lord. He attached it to the pronoun of the one addressed rather than to the yāʾ of the speaker — even though the apparent sense of the speech requires it to be "upon my heart" — for one of two reasons: either out of regard for the state of being commanded to say, so that one relates its wording in the second person, as in your saying: "Say to your people: let them not insult you", and if you said "let them not insult me" it would be permissible; and of this is the saying of al-Farazdaq:
631 - ألم تَرَ أنِّي يومَ جَوِّ سُوَيْقَةٍ ... دَعَوْتُ فنادَتْني هُنَيْدَةُ: ما ليا
(Did you not see that on the day of Jaww Suwayqa I called out, and Hunayda called to me: "What is the matter with me?")
— so he secured the meaning and turned away from Hunayda's calling with "What is the matter with you?"; or because there is another, implied (muqaddar) verb of saying after «قُلْ», the implied form being: "Say, O Muhammad: Allah said: whoever is an enemy to Gabriel". Al-Zamakhsharī inclined toward this with his saying: "It came as a report of the speech of Allah the Exalted: say what I have spoken of My saying: whoever is an enemy to Gabriel, then he has sent it down upon your heart." On this view the conditional clause is governed by that implied verb of saying, and the implied saying is governed by the word «قُلْ». The apparent view is what preceded, that the clause is governed by the word «قُلْ» according to the interpretation mentioned first; and al-Zamakhsharī's saying does not contradict it, for he intended an explanation of the meaning, not an explanation of the i'rab.
His saying: {بِإِذْنِ الله} is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of «نَزَّله» if it is said that it is the pronoun of Gabriel, or from its object if it is said that the nominative pronoun in «نَزِّلَ» refers to Allah; the implied form being: "then he sent it down being permitted", or "with the permission of Allah accompanying it". [Al-idhn is originally knowledge of a thing, and al-īdhān is informing.] Adhina bihi: he knew of it; and ādhantuhu bi-kadhā: I informed him of it. Then it is used for enabling: adhina lī fī kadhā: he enabled me to do it; and for choice: faʿaltuhu bi-idhnika: that is, by your choice. And the saying of whoever said "by His leave, that is, by His facilitation" goes back to this.
His saying: «مُصَدِّقاً» is a ḥāl from the hāʾ in «نَزَّلَه» if the pronoun refers to the Qurʾān. If it refers to Gabriel there are two possibilities: one, that it is from the genitive (majrūr) omitted because the meaning is understood, the implied form being: "Allah sent down Gabriel with the Qurʾān, confirming"; the second, that it is from Gabriel, in the sense of "confirming the messengers who came before him", and it is an emphatic ḥāl. The hāʾ in «بين يديه» may refer to «القرآن» or to «جِبْريل».
And «هُدَىً وبُشْرَى» are two ḥāls conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the ḥāl before them; they are maṣdars (verbal nouns) put in the place of the active participle, or by way of hyperbole, or with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "possessing guidance". The alif of «بُشْرى» is for the feminine. This verbal ordering in these ḥāls came corresponding to the order of existence: that is, it came down confirming the scriptures because they are from one source; the second, that guidance was attained through it after its descent; and the third, that it is glad tidings for whoever attained guidance through it. He singled out the believers because they are the ones who benefit from it, to the exclusion of others; something similar has preceded.

semin-durr:37-37.t:
His saying: {فتلقى آدَمُ مِن رَّبِّهِ كَلِمَاتٍ}: the fāʾ [Translator's note: the printed text has «الفارُ», evidently a misprint for «الفاءُ»] conjoins this clause to what precedes it. «تلقَّى» is tafaʿʿala in the sense of the bare form. It has other meanings: the reflexive-resultative (muṭāwaʿa) of faʿʿala, as in كسَّرته فتكسَّرَ (I broke it and it broke); avoidance, as in تجنَّب, i.e. he kept to one side; affectation, as in تحلَّم (he affected forbearance); becoming, as in تَأثَّم; adopting, as in تَبَنَّيْتُ الصبيَّ, i.e. I took him as a son; continuing an action gradually, as in تَجَرَّع (he gulped by sips) and تَفَهَّمَ; agreement with istafʿala, as in تكبَّر; expectation, as in تَخَوَّف; seeking, as in تَنَجَّز حاجَته (he sought fulfilment of his need); multiplicity, as in تَغَطَّيت بالثياب (I wrapped myself in garments); putting on the thing named from which it is derived, as in تَقَمَّص (he put on a shirt), or acting during it, as in تَسَحَّر (he ate the pre-dawn meal); and stealth, as in تَغَفَّلْتُه (I caught him off guard). Some claimed that the origin of تلقَّى is تلقَّن with nūn, and that the nūn was changed into alif; this is a mistake, because that has only occurred in doubled roots, as in قَصَّيْتُ أظفاري, تَظَنَّيْتُ and أَمْلَيْتُ الكتابَ for قَصَصْتُ, تَظَنَّنْتُ and أَمْلَلْتُ.
{مِن رَّبِّهِ} is attached to it, and «مِنْ» is for the beginning of the extent, figuratively. Abū al-Baqāʾ permitted it to be originally an adjective of كلمات, which, when put before it, became accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), so that it is attached to an omitted element. «كلماتٍ» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
Ibn Kathīr read it with «آدم» in the accusative and «كلمات» in the nominative; that is because whoever meets you, you have met him, so the verb may properly be ascribed to each of the two. It has also been said: since the words were a cause of his repentance, they were made the agent. The verb is not feminine on this reading even though the agent is feminine, [because it is not a true feminine, and also because of the separation; and this is the way of every verb separated from its feminine agent by something, or whose agent is feminine] figuratively.
His saying, Exalted is He: {فَتَابَ عَلَيْهِ} is conjoined to what precedes it, and a clause must be supposed before it, i.e. "so he said them". Al-kalimāt is the plural of kalima, which is the utterance indicating a single meaning; it is applied to meaningful sentences figuratively, naming the whole by the name of the part, as in His saying, Exalted is He: {تَعَالَوْاْ إلى كَلِمَةٍ} [Āl ʿImrān: 64], which He then explained with His saying: {أَلاَّ نَعْبُدَ} to its end. And the Exalted said: {كَلاَّ إِنَّهَا كَلِمَةٌ} [al-Muʾminūn: 100], meaning his saying: {رَبِّ ارجعون} to its end. Labīd said:
384 - ألاَ كلُّ شيءٍ ما خَلاَ اللهَ باطلُ ... وكلُّ نعيمٍ لا مَحالةَ زائلُ
(Indeed, everything other than Allah is vain, and every bliss is, without doubt, passing away.)
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ called it a "word" (kalima), saying: "The truest word a poet has spoken is the word of Labīd."
Al-tawba is returning. The meaning of describing Allah the Exalted with it is that it expresses His turning in kindness to His servants and rescuing them from punishment; describing the servant with it is evident, because he returns from disobedience to obedience. Al-tawwāb and al-raḥīm are two intensive adjectives, and they are not exclusive to the Creator, Exalted is He; the Exalted said: {يُحِبُّ التوابين} [al-Baqara: 222]. The term «تائب» is not applied to Him, even though its verb is explicitly ascribed to Him, Exalted is He. Al-tawwāb was put before al-raḥīm to suit «فَتَاب عليه», and because it accords with ending the verse-endings (fawāṣil) with al-raḥīm.
His saying: {إِنَّهُ هُوَ التواب الرحيم} parallels His saying: {إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ العليم الحكيم} [al-Baqara: 32]. Abū ʿAmr assimilated the hāʾ of «إنه» into the hāʾ of «هو». Objection was raised to this, that between the two identical letters is something that prevents assimilation, namely the wāw. It was answered that the wāw is a redundant (zāʾida) extension (ṣila) which is not taken into account, as is proven by its dropping in his saying:
385 - لَهُ زَجَلٌ كَأَنَّه صوتُ حادٍ ... إذا طَلَبَ الوسِيقَةَ أو زَمِيرُ
(It has a clamour, as if it were the voice of a camel-driver when he seeks the driven herd, or the sound of a reed-pipe.)
And his saying:
386 - أو مُعْبَرُ الظهرِ يُنْبي عن وَلِيَّتِه ... ما حَجَّ في الدنيا ولا اعْتَمَرا
(Or one with a hairy back whose saddle-cloth shows that he has never in his life made the Ḥajj nor the ʿUmra.)
The well-known reading is «إنَّه» with a kasra on inna; it has also been read with fatḥa, on the supposition of the lām of cause.

semin-durr:111-111.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {إِلاَّ مَن كَانَ هُوداً}: «مَنْ» is the fāʿil (agent) of His words «يَدْخُلَ», and it is an emptied exception (istithnāʾ mufarragh), since what precedes «إلاَّ» stands in need of what follows it; the implied meaning is: "No one shall enter Paradise". On the view of al-Farrāʾ, two further aspects are permissible in «مَنْ»: the accusative as the excepted (mustathnā), and the nominative as a badal (substitute) from the omitted «أحد», for al-Farrāʾ takes account of the omitted element; were it stated explicitly, both of the aspects mentioned would be permissible in the excepted, and so likewise, in his view, when it is implied. The verification of the two positions has already been given.
The clause {لَن يَدْخُلَ الجنة إِلاَّ مَن} is in the position of the accusative as the object of the saying. The construction was first taken according to the wording (lafẓ) of «مَنْ», so the pronoun in «كان» was made singular, and then according to its meaning (maʿnā), so its khabar (predicate), namely «هوداً», was made plural. There is disagreement over these two kinds of construing — I mean where the khabar is not a verb but an adjective whose masculine and feminine are distinguished by the feminine tāʾ. The view of the majority of the Basrans and the Kufans is that it is permissible, while the view of others — among them Abū al-ʿAbbās [Translator's note: i.e. al-Mubarrad] — is that it is not; they are refuted by its being heard from the Arabs, as in this verse, for «هوداً» is the plural of هائد according to the more apparent of the two views, like بازِل and بُزْل, عائِد and عُود, حائل and حُول, بائِر and بُور; and «هائد» is one of the adjectives whose masculine and feminine are distinguished by the feminine tāʾ. The poet said:
678 - وأَيْقَظَ مَنْ كان مِنْكم نِياما ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(And he woke whoever among you was asleep.)
And «نيام» is the plural of نائم, so it is like the first. Concerning «هُود» there are three views. The first: it is the plural of هائد, as has been said. The second: it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) on the pattern فُعْل, like حُزْن and شُرْب, with which the singular and others are described, like عَدْل and صَوْم. The third — the view of al-Farrāʾ — is that its origin is «يَهود», with the yāʾ dropped from its beginning; and this is very far-fetched.
And «أو» here is for detailing and differentiation (tafṣīl and tanwīʿ), because when He wrapped up [both groups] in the pronoun of «وقالوا», He [then] distinguished the speakers; this is because the meaning is understood and confusion is safely avoided. The implied meaning is: "And the Jews said: none shall enter Paradise except whoever is a Jew; and the Christians said: none shall enter Paradise except whoever is a Christian", since it is known that the Jews do not say "none shall enter Paradise except whoever is a Christian", and likewise the Christians. Its parallel is: {قَالُواْ كُونُواْ هُوداً أَوْ نصارى} [al-Baqara: 135], since it is known that the Jews do not say "Be Christians", nor do the Christians say "Be Jews". The clause was headed with negation by «لن» because it restricts [the verb] to the future, and entering Paradise is in the future. The Jews were put before the Christians in wording because they preceded them in time.
His words: {تِلْكَ أَمَانِيُّهُمْ}: «تلك» is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and «أمانِيُّهم» its khabar. This clause has no grammatical position, since it is a parenthesis between His words «وقالوا» and {قُلْ هَاتُواْ بُرْهَانَكُمْ}; it is a parenthesis between the claim and its proof. As for what is pointed to by «تلك», there are three possibilities. The first: it is the statement understood from «َقَالُواْ لَن يَدْخُلَ», i.e. "that statement is their wishful thinking". If it is asked: how did He make the mubtadaʾ singular and the khabar plural? The answer is that «تلك» is an allusion to the statement, and "statement" (maqāla) is originally a maṣdar, and the maṣdar occurs in singular form for the singular, the dual and the plural; so what is meant by «تلك» is plural in meaning.
The second — stated by al-Zamakhsharī — is that it points to the wishes already mentioned, namely: their wish that no good be sent down upon the believers from their Lord, their wish to turn them back into disbelievers, and their wish that none but they should enter Paradise. The Shaykh [Translator's note: Abū Ḥayyān] said: "This is not apparent, because each clause in which their desire for something was mentioned was complete, separate and revealed independently, so it is unlikely that it is being pointed to." The third — also held by al-Zamakhsharī — is that it is on the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "the likes of that wish are their wishes", meaning that all their wishes are, in falsehood, like this wish of theirs. End of what he said; that is, he means it points to a single thing. The Shaykh said concerning this aspect: "In it is an inversion of the arrangement, since the basis is that «تلك» is the mubtadaʾ and «أمانيُّهم» the khabar, but he inverted this arrangement when he said: 'their wishes are, in falsehood, like this wish of theirs'. Also, whenever the khabar is that to which the mubtadaʾ is likened, the khabar is not put first, as in: زيدٌ زهيرٌ; if it is put first, that is a reversal of the simile, as in your saying: الأسدُ زيدٌ شجاعةً (the lion is Zayd in courage)."
His words: {هَاتُواْ بُرْهَانَكُمْ}: this clause is in the position of the accusative as the object of the saying. There is disagreement over «هاتِ» on three views. The first: it is a verb, and this is the correct view, because it is joined to overt nominative pronouns, as in هاتُوا, هاتي, هاتِيا, هاتِين. The second: it is a verbal noun (ism fiʿl) meaning أحْضِرْ (bring). The third — held by al-Zamakhsharī — is that it is a sound-noun (ism ṣawt) with the sense of «ها» which means أحْضِرْ.
If it is said to be a verb, there is again disagreement about it on three views. The soundest is that its hāʾ is radical in itself, and that its origin is هاتَى يُهاتي مُهاتاةً, like رامَى يُرامي مُراماة, so its pattern is فاعَلَ; one says: هاتِ يا زيدُ, هاتي يا هندُ, هاتوا, and هاتِين يا هندات, just as one says: رامِ, رامي, راميا, رامُوا, رامِينَ. Ibn ʿAṭiyya claimed that its conjugation is disused and only the imperative is said of it; but it is not so.
The second: that the hāʾ is a substitute for a hamza and that the origin is أَأْتى, on the pattern أَفْعَل like أَكْرم. This is not good, for two reasons. The first: آتى is transitive to two objects, while هاتى is transitive to one only. The second of the two reasons: the alif that replaced the hamza ought to have reverted to its origin, since what necessitated its change — namely the first hamza — has disappeared, and that has not been heard. The third: that this is the «ها» of alerting (tanbīh), which entered upon «أتى» and adhered to it, and the hamza of أتى was dropped obligatorily. This is rejected, for the meaning of هاتِ is "bring such-and-such", whereas the meaning of ائتِ is "come yourself", and the difference in meaning indicates a difference in root. So the outcome is seven views on «هاتُوا»: a verb, a verbal noun, or a sound-noun; and [if] the verb, whether it is conjugated or not conjugated, and whether its hāʾ is radical, or a substitute for a hamza, or the hāʾ of alerting added with its hamza dropped. The origin of هاتوا is هاتِيُوا; the ḍamma was felt heavy on the yāʾ and was dropped, so two quiescent letters met, the first of them was dropped and what preceded it was given ḍamma for harmony with the wāw, and it became هاتوا.
His words: {بُرْهَانَكُمْ}: a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). There is disagreement about it on two views. The first: it is derived from البُرْه, which is "cutting", since it is a proof that yields decisive (qaṭʿī) knowledge; and from it is بُرْهَةُ الزمان, i.e. a piece of time; so its pattern is فُعْلان. The second: its nūn is radical, since it remains in بَرْهَنَ يُبَرْهِنُ بَرْهَنَةً, and بَرْهَنَة is clarification; so بَرْهَنَ is فَعْلَلَ, not فَعْلَنَ, because فعلنَ does not exist among their patterns; so its pattern is فُعْلال. On these two views depends the disagreement over whether «بُرهان» is declined as a full triptote or not when used as a proper name.

semin-durr:112-112.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {وَهُوَ مُحْسِنٌ}: a clause in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and what governs it is «أَسْلم». He expressed it with "the face" because it is the noblest of the limbs and contains most of the senses; hence one says وَجْهُ الأمرِ, meaning the bulk of the matter. Al-Aʿshā said:
679 - أُؤوِّلُ الحُكْمَ على وَجْهِهِ ... ليسَ قضائي بالهوى الجائِرِ
(I interpret the judgement according to its proper face; my verdict is not by unjust caprice.)
The meaning of أَسْلَمَ is "submitted", and from it is:
680 - وأَسْلَمْتُ وَجْهي لِمَنْ أَسْلَمَتْ ... له المُزْنُ تَحْمِيلُ عَذْباً زُلالا
(I submitted my face to the One to whom the rain-clouds submitted, carrying sweet, pure water.)
This ḥāl is corroborative (muʾakkida), because whoever submits his face to Allah is a doer of good. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "and he is a doer of good in his deeds", so on his view it is explanatory (mubayyina), because those who submit their faces are of two kinds: one who does good in his deeds and one who does not. The Shaykh said: "This is an inclination on his part toward Muʿtazilism."
His words {فَلَهُ أَجْرُهُ}: the fāʾ is that of the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) if «مَنْ» is said to be conditional, or redundant (zāʾida) in the khabar (predicate) if it is said to be relative. The verification of the two views has already been given at His words {بلى مَن كَسَبَ سَيِّئَةً} [al-Baqara: 81]; this is the parallel of that, so let it be consulted. Here there is a further aspect beyond what is there, mentioned by al-Zamakhsharī, namely that «مَنْ» is the fāʿil (agent) of an omitted verb, i.e. "Yes, whoever submits shall enter it", and «فله أجرُه» is speech conjoined to "shall enter it". This is his wording. And «له أجره» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar, either in the position of the jussive or of the nominative, according to the disagreement mentioned over «مَنْ». The construction was taken according to the wording of «مَنْ», so the pronoun was made singular in His words {فَلَهُ أَجْرُهُ عِندَ رَبِّهِ}, and according to its meaning, so it was made plural in His words {عليهم وَلاَ هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ}; and this is the better of the two arrangements — I mean beginning with construing by the wording and then construing by the meaning. What governs «عند» is the [notion of] settledness (istiqrār) to which «له» is attached. When He referred his reward to Himself, He annexed the adverb to the word "Lord" because of the intimation it carries of setting right and governance, and did not annex it to the pronoun nor to the Majestic Name, saying "he has his reward with Him" or "with Allah", for the reason I mentioned to you. Discussion has already been given of His words «ولا خَوْفٌ» and the readings in it.

semin-durr:54-54.t:
The saying of the Exalted: {يَاقَوْمِ}. Know that in the munādā (the one addressed) annexed to the yāʾ of the first person there are six dialectal usages. The most eloquent of them is omitting it, the kasra sufficing in its place; this is the usage of the Quran. The second: keeping the yāʾ, quiescent. The third: keeping it with a fatḥa. The fourth: changing it into an alif. The fifth: omitting this alif, the fatḥa sufficing in its place, as in his saying:
468 - ولَسْتُ بِراجعٍ ما فاتَ مِنِّي ... بِلَهْفَ ولا بِلَيْتَ ولا لَوَنِّي
(I shall not bring back what has escaped me by "alas", nor by "would that", nor by "if only I…"), i.e. by my saying يا لَهْفا. The sixth: making the noun annexed to it indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, by analogy with the single [noun], as in the reading of the one who read: {قَالَ رَبُّ احكم بالحق} [al-Anbiyāʾ: 112]. Some said: "[This is] because «يا قوم» is in the implied sense of يا أيُّهَا القومُ"; this is of no account.
Al-qawm ("people") is a collective noun (ism jamʿ), because it denotes more than two, has no singular from its own wording, and is not of a pattern specific to the broken plural; its singular [in meaning] is rajul ("man"). Its derivation is from قام بالأمرِ يَقُوم به ("to take charge of a matter"); the Exalted said: {الرجال قَوَّامُونَ عَلَى النسآء} [al-Nisāʾ: 34]. Its basic application is to men, and for this reason it is set against women in His saying: {لاَ يَسْخَرْ قَوْمٌ مِّن قَوْمٍ. . . وَلاَ نِسَآءٌ مِّن نِّسَآءٍ} [al-Ḥujurāt: 11], and in the saying of Zuhayr:
469 - وما أَدْرِي وسوفُ إخالُ أَدْرِي ... أقومٌ آلُ حِصْنٍ أم نِساءُ
(I do not know — and I think I shall come to know — whether the family of Ḥiṣn are men or women.)
As for the saying of the Exalted: {كَذَّبَتْ قَوْمُ نُوحٍ} [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 105] and {كَذَّبَتْ قَوْمُ لُوطٍ} [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 160], where those who denied were men and women, this is only by way of predominance (taghlīb). It may not be applied to women alone at all, even if the wording of some suggests [that].
His saying: {باتخاذكم العجل}: the bāʾ is causal, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «ظَلَلْتُم». The disagreement about this root has preceded: whether its origin is أَخَذَ or تَخِذَ. «العجل» is the first object and the second is omitted, i.e. "as a god", as preceded. The maṣdar (verbal noun) here is annexed to its fāʿil (agent), and this is the better of the two options, for when a maṣdar has both its agent and its object, it is preferable to annex it to the agent, because its rank is precedence; and this is one of the cases in which the agent must come first. As for {قَتْلَ أَوْلاَدِهِمْ شُرَكَآؤُهُمْ} [al-Anʿām: 137], [full discussion of it] will come, if Allah the Exalted wills.
Al-ʿijl is well known: it is the calf, the young of the cow. Al-Rāghib said: "Al-ʿijl is the young of the cow, because of the haste (ʿajala) one conceives in it, which disappears from it when it becomes a bull." It has been said: it was only named ʿijl because they hastened (taʿajjalū) to worship it before Moses came; this is narrated from ʿAlī, but it is not authentic from him, for this name was known before that. The plural is ʿajājīl and ʿujūl.
His saying: «إلى بارِئِكم» is attached to «تُوبوا». The well-known [reading] is with kasra on the hamza, because it is the vowel of i'rab. Three other options are narrated from Abū ʿAmr: ikhtilās, which is pronouncing a slight, hidden vowel; and pure sukūn. A group of grammarians attacked this latter, and attributed its transmitter to error regarding Abū ʿAmr. Sībawayh said: "Abū ʿAmr only pronounced it slightly (ikhtalasa), and the transmitter thought that he made it quiescent, and did not record it accurately." Al-Mubarrad said: "Making [the vowel] quiescent with a succession of vowels on the letter of i'rab is not permissible in prose or in poetry, and the reading of Abū ʿAmr is a solecism (laḥn)." This is audacity on al-Mubarrad's part and ignorance of the poetry of the Arabs, for sukūn in place of the vowels of i'rab has occurred frequently in poetry. From it is the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:
470 - فاليومَ أشربْ غيرَ مُسْتَحْقِبٍ ... إثْماً مِن اللهِ ولا واغِلِ
(So today I drink, not carrying a sin before Allah, nor as an uninvited intruder.)
He made «أَشْرَبْ» quiescent. Jarīr said:
471 - . . . . . . . . . . . ... ونهرُ تيرى فما تَعْرِفْكُمُ العَرَبُ
(…and the river of Tīrā; so the Arabs do not know you.)
Another said:
472 - رُحْتِ وفي رِجْلَيْكِ ما فيهما ... وقد بَدَا هَنْكِ من المِئْزَرِ
(You went off in the evening with what [weakness] was in your legs, and your private part showed from the waist-wrapper.)
He means هَنُك and تَعْرِفُكم. These are vowels of i'rab, and they have been made quiescent. Ibn ʿAṭiyya and others recited, in reply to him:
473 - قالت سُلَيْمى اشْتَرْ لنا سَويقا
(Sulaymā said: buy us some barley-meal.)
and the saying of another:
474 - إذا اعْوَجَجْنَ قلتُ صاحِبْ قَوِّمِ
(When they [the camels] veer off, I say: companion, set them straight.)
and the saying of another:
475 - إنما شِعْريَ شَهْدٌ ... قد خُلْطَ بِجُلْجُلانْ
(My poetry is but honey mixed with sesame.)
But this is not good, because these are vowels of indeclinability (binaʾ), whereas he only forbade it in the vowels of i'rab. The reading of Abū ʿAmr is sound. That is because the hamza is a heavy letter, and for that reason every kind of lightening has been ventured upon it; the vowel was found heavy on it, so it was made implied (muqaddara). This reading resembles the reading of Ḥamza — may Allah the Exalted have mercy on him — in the saying of the Exalted: {وَمَكْرَ السيىء وَلاَ}, for he made the hamza of «السيء» quiescent in continuous recitation; the discussion of both is the same. What made it good here is that before the kasra of the hamza there is a rāʾ with a kasra, and the rāʾ is a letter of repetition, so it is as though three kasras came in succession, and therefore making it quiescent was good. Would that al-Mubarrad had followed Sībawayh in excusing Abū ʿAmr and in not being audacious toward him:
476 - وابنُ الَّلُبونِ إذا ما لُزَّ في قَرَنٍ ... لم يَسْتَطِعْ صَوْلَةَ البُزْل القَنَاعِيْسِ
(The two-year-old camel, when tied in one rope [with others], cannot withstand the assault of the mighty, full-grown camels.)
All of Abū ʿAmr's transmission revolves around lightening; for that reason he assimilates identical and close letters, softens the hamza, and makes quiescent [forms] such as {يَنصُرْكُمُ} [Āl ʿImrān: 160], {يَأْمُرُكُمْ} [al-Baqara: 67] and {بِأَعْلَمَ بالشاكرين} [al-Anʿām: 53], according to a detailed account known among the readers. It is also narrated [from him] that he changed this quiescent hamza into a yāʾ, as though he did not take the implied vowel into account; some deny that [from him]. These, then, are four readings of Abū ʿAmr. Ibn ʿAṭiyya narrated from al-Zuhrī «بارِيِِكم» with a kasra on the yāʾ without hamza; he said: "and it has been narrated from Nāfiʿ." I say: this reader ought to make the yāʾ quiescent, because the kasra is heavy on it, and its overt appearance is not permissible except under poetic necessity, as in the saying of Abū Ṭālib:
477 - كَذَبْتُمْ وبَيْتِ اللهِ نُبْزِي مُحَمَّداً ... ولم تَخْتَصِبْ سُمْرُ العَوالِيِّ بالدَّمِ
(You have lied, by the House of Allah: we shall not let Muhammad be overcome while the brown spear-heads have not yet been dyed with blood.)
Qatāda read: «فاقْتالوا», and said: it is from al-istiqāla ("seeking release"). Ibn Jinnī said: "اقتال is iftaʿala; its middle radical (ʿayn) may be a wāw [as in اقتادوا] or a yāʾ as in اقتاس; morphology makes it weak that it be from al-istiqāla." But one ought to think well of Qatāda, that he only brought it forward on the basis of a proof he had.
Al-Bāriʾ is the Creator: بَرَأَ اللهُ الخَلْقَ, i.e. He created them. Some distinguished between al-Khāliq and al-Bāriʾ: al-Bāriʾ is the Originator who brings into being, while al-Khāliq is the One who determines and moves from state to state. The basic meaning of this root indicates separation and distinction; from it: بَرَأَ المريضُ ("the sick man recovered"), with the maṣdar burʾ and barʾ; and بَرِئْتُ and بَرَأْتُ also from debt, with the maṣdar barāʾa. Al-bariyya is creation, because they separated from non-existence into existence, except that it is not pronounced with hamza. It has also been said: its origin is from al-barā, which is earth (dust). The verification of the two views will come in its place, if Allah the Exalted wills.
His saying: {ذَلِكُمْ خَيْرٌ لَّكُمْ}. Some said: «ذلكم» is singular standing in the place of the dual «ذانكم», because two things preceded: repentance and killing. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "This is of no account, because His saying {فاقتلوا} is the explanation of the repentance, so it is one thing." «خَيْر» is an elative (afʿal al-tafḍīl), originally أَخْيَرُ; its hamza was only omitted for lightness, and this hamza does not return except under [poetic] necessity. [The poet] said:
478 - بلالُ خيرُ الناسِ وابنُ الأَخْيَرِ
(Bilāl is the best of people and son of the best.)
Similarly شَرّ: أَشَرّ is not permissible except rarely; it has been read: {مَن الكّذَّابُ الأَشَرُّ} [al-Qamar: 26]. When a verb of wonder on the pattern afʿal is built from this root, its hamza is not omitted except rarely, as in their saying: «ما خَيْرَ اللبنِ للصحيحِ، وما شَرَّه للمبطونِ» ("How good milk is for the healthy, and how bad for the one with a stomach complaint!"). So خير and شر have departed from their counterparts in the chapters of the elative and of wonder. «خَيْر» is also a lightened form of خَيِّر on the pattern fayʿil, and then it does not belong to this chapter; from it is «فيهِنَّ خَيْراتٌ حِسانٌ»; some said: "lightened from خَيِّرات." The thing over which preference is given is omitted because it is known, i.e. better for you than not repenting. The elative has many rules and scattered conditions which [this] book cannot bear; we only bring of them what we are compelled to.
The saying of the Exalted: {فَتَابَ عَلَيْكُمْ}. There is an omission in the speech, namely: "so you did what you were commanded of killing, and He turned to you in forgiveness". The first fāʾ, in His saying «فتوبوا», is causal, because wrongdoing is the cause of repentance. The second is for immediate sequence, because the meaning is: resolve upon repentance, then kill yourselves. The third is attached to something omitted, and it must be one of two things: either it is part of Moses' speech to them, and so is attached to an omitted condition, as though: "and if you do so, He has turned to you"; or it is an address from Allah to them by way of iltifāt (a shift of person), so the implied meaning is: "so you did what Moses commanded you, and He turned to you." Al-Zamakhsharī said this.

semin-durr:55-55.t:
The saying of the Exalted: {لَن نُّؤْمِنَ لَكَ}: it is made transitive with the lām rather than the bāʾ for one of two reasons: either the implied meaning is "we will not believe because of your saying", or it is made to include (tuḍammana) the sense of acknowledging, i.e. "we will [not] acknowledge to you what you claim". Abū ʿAmr read it with assimilation of the nūn into the lām because of their closeness.
The saying of the Exalted: «جَهْرَةً». There are two views about it. The first: that it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), and on this there are two views. One is that what makes it accusative is omitted and is from its own wording, the implied form being "you spoke openly, an open speaking (جَهَرْتُمْ جَهْرةً)"; Abū al-Baqāʾ transmitted it. The second is that it is a maṣdar of a kind of the verb, so it is accusative in the way al-qurfuṣāʾ is in your saying قَعَدَ القُرْفُصاء ("he sat squatting") and اشتمل الصَمَّاء ("he wrapped himself in the ṣammāʾ manner"), for it is a kind of seeing; al-Zamakhsharī began with this. The second [main view]: that it is a maṣdar standing in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial), and on this there are four views. The first: it is a ḥāl from the fāʿil (agent) of «نرى», i.e. "possessed of openness"; al-Zamakhsharī said this. The second: it is a ḥāl from the agent of «قُلْتم», i.e. "you said that openly"; Abū al-Baqāʾ said this. Some said: there would then be a fronting and postponing in the speech, i.e. "you said openly: we will not believe you"; but of such a thing one does not say there is fronting and postponing; rather, he brought the object of the saying, then the ḥāl from its agent, so it is parallel to ضَرَبْتُ هنداً قائماً ("I struck Hind, [I] standing"). The third: it is a ḥāl from the name of Allah the Exalted, i.e. "we see Him manifest, not veiled". The fourth: it is a ḥāl from the agent of «نؤمن»; Ibn ʿAṭiyya transmitted it, and it has no meaning. The correct one of these six views is the second. [Translator's note: the source says "six views" (two under the maṣdar view plus four under the ḥāl view) and calls "the second" correct; which of the numbered views is meant is not specified further.]
Ibn ʿAbbās read «جَهَرَةً» with a fatḥa on the hāʾ, and there are two views about it. The first: it is a dialectal variant of جَهْرة. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It is a variant heard [from the Arabs] according to the Basrans in words in which a quiescent guttural letter is preceded by a fatḥa; the Kufans permit the fatḥa in it even if they have not heard it." The precise statement on that has preceded. The second: it is the plural of «جاهر», like خادِم and خَدَم; the meaning is: "until we see Allah, [we] uncovering this matter". This supports «جهرةً» being a ḥāl from the agent of «نَرى».
Al-jahr is the opposite of secrecy: it is uncovering and appearing. From it is جَهَرَ بالقراءةِ, i.e. he recited aloud. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is as though the one who sees with the eye is open in seeing, and the one who sees with the heart is muted in it."

semin-durr:57-57.t:
The saying of the Exalted: {وَظَلَّلْنَا عَلَيْكُمُ الغمام}: its implied meaning is "We made the clouds shade you". Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is not like your saying: ظَلَّلْتُ زيداً يُظَلُّ, because that would require the clouds to be covered by another shade." It has been said: the implied form is "with the clouds" (بالغَمامِ); but this is an explanation of meaning, not of i'rab, because the omission of the preposition is not by analogy (lā yanqās).
