The sukūn of the middle radical is the dialect of the Ḥijāz, and Yaḥyā and al-Ḥasan read with it; the ḍamma is the dialect of Tamīm. The Seven read according to the dialect of Tamīm, except Abū ʿAmr where it is annexed to «نا», «كم» or «هم», for he read with sukūn because of the succession of vowels.
His saying: «عيسى» is a non-Arabic proper name, and for that reason it is a diptote. The grammarians spoke about its pattern and derivation on the supposition that it was Arabic in origin. Sībawayh said: "Its pattern is «فِعْلى», and the yāʾ in it is an attachment (mulḥaqa) [making it conform] to quadriliteral roots, like the yāʾ of «مِعْزَى»" — meaning by "yāʾ" the alif; he called it yāʾ because it is written with yāʾ. Al-Fārisī said: "Its alif is not for the feminine, as in «ذِكْرى», as is shown by their declining it [as a triptote] when indefinite." ʿUthmān ibn Saʿīd al-Ṣayrafī said: "Its pattern is «فِعْلَل»," so the alif for him is radical, in the sense that it is changed from a radical letter. Ibn al-Bādhish refuted that against him on the grounds that yāʾ and wāw are not radicals in quadriliteral roots. So whoever said that «عِيسى» is derived from «العَيْس», which is whiteness mixed with a reddish tinge — like Abū al-Baqāʾ and others — is not correct, because derivation and morphological inflection do not apply to a non-Arabic word. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It was said: «عيسى» in Syriac is «أَيْسوع»."
His saying: «ابنَ مريم» is an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) or a badal (substitute); it may also be a naʿt (adjective), but the first is more appropriate, because «ابن مريم» has functioned like a proper name for him. Qualification by «ابن» has rulings specific to it which will come explained, if Allah the Exalted wills; and the derivation of «ابن» and its root form have preceded.
«مَرْيم» is originally, in Syriac, an adjective meaning "servant", then it was used as a name, and for that reason it is a diptote. In the language of the Arabs it is the woman who mixes much with men, like «الزِّير» among men, who is the one who mixes much with women. Ruʾba said:
602 - قلتُ لِزِيرٍ لم تَصِلْهُ مَرْيَمُهْ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(I said to a ladies' man whom his "maryam" did not join...)
The yāʾ of «الزير» is from a wāw, because it is from «زار يَزُور»; it was changed because of the kasra before it, like «الرِّيح». So the word «مريم» became shared between the two languages. Its pattern according to the grammarians is «مَفْعَل», not «فَعْيَل». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Because «فَعْيَل» with fatḥa on the first letter is not established among the patterns, as it is established in the like of «عِثْيَر» and «عِلْيَب»." Some established «فَعْيَل» and counted among it the like of «ضَمْيَد», the name of a place, «مَدْيَن» on the view that its mīm is radical, and «ضَهْيَا» with the short ending, which is the woman who does not menstruate, or who has no breasts — because it is derived from «ضاهَأَتْ», i.e. she resembled, since she resembled men in that; it may also be given the long ending, as al-Zajjāj said. Ibn Jinnī said: "As for «ضَمْيد» and «عَثْيَر», they are fabricated," so there is no evidence in them for the existence of «فَعْيَل». The soundness of the yāʾ in «مريم» is contrary to analogy, since it ought to have been weakened by transferring the vowel of the yāʾ to the rāʾ and then changing the yāʾ into alif, as in «مَباع» from «البَيْع»; but it is anomalous, [as are] «مَزْيَد» and «مَدْيَن». Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "«مَرْيَم» is a non-Arabic proper name; had it been derived from «رامَ يريم» it would have been «مَرِيم» with a quiescent yāʾ. Among proper names there has occurred [the form] with fatḥa on the yāʾ, such as «مَزْيَد», and that is contrary to analogy."
His saying: {وَأَيَّدْنَاهُ} is conjoined to His saying: {وَآتَيْنَا عِيسَى}. The majority read «أيَّدْناه» on the pattern «فَعَّلْناه»; Mujāhid and Ibn Muḥayṣin read — and it is narrated from Abū ʿAmr — «آيَدْنَاه» on the pattern «أَفْعَلْناه». The root form is «أَاْيَدَ» with two hamzas, the second of them quiescent, so the second had to be changed into alif, as in «أَأْمَنَ» and its class. The middle radical, which is the yāʾ, remained sound, as it remained sound in «أَغْيَلَت» and «أَغْيَمَت»; this is an anomalous retention of soundness, except in the verb of wonder (taʿajjub), as in «ما أَبْيَنَ» and «أَطْوَل». It is related from Abū Zayd that the soundness of «أَغْيَلَت» is regular. If it is said: why was «آيَدْناه» not weakened as the like of «أَبَعْناه» was weakened, so that it need not be construed as anomalous? The answer is that if it were weakened — by casting the vowel of the middle radical onto the first radical, so that two quiescent letters, the middle and final radicals, meet, so that the middle radical is elided because of the meeting of two quiescents; then two hamzas with fatḥa come together, so the second must be changed into wāw, as in «أَوادِم»; then the wāw is vowelled after a fatḥa and is changed into alif, so that the word becomes «أَادْناه» — that would lead to weakening both the first and the middle radicals. Since weakening it would lead to that, it was rejected, unlike «أَبَعْناه» and «أَقَمْناه», in which there is only weakening of the middle radical. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "If you say: why was the yāʾ which is the middle radical not elided, as it was elided in the like of «أَسَلْناه» from «سالَ يَسالُ»? It is said: had they done that, two weakenings would have followed one another: one of them changing the second hamza into alif, and then eliding the alif substituted for the yāʾ because of its quiescence and the quiescence of the alif before it; the word would have become «آدْناه», so the first and middle radicals would have been elided — and «أسلناه» is not like that, because there only the middle radical is elided."
Al-Zamakhsharī said in [Sūrat] al-Māʾida: "«آيَدْتُك» on the pattern «أَفْعَلْتُك»," and Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "on the pattern «فاعَلْتُك»," then he said: "It appears that the root form in both readings is «أَفْعَلْتُك», and then the weakening differed." End quote.
What appears is that «أيَّد» is «فَعَّل», because its imperfect comes as «يُؤَيِّدُ» with doubling; had «أَيَّد» with doubling been on the pattern «أَفْعَلَ», its imperfect would have been «يُؤْيِدُ», like «يُؤْمِنُ» from «آمَنَ». As for «آيَدَ», i.e. with prolongation, the transmission of its imperfect needs to be based on what is heard: if «يُؤايِدُ» like «يُقاتِل» is heard, then it is «فاعَل»; if «يُؤْيِدُ» like «يُكْرِمُ» is heard, then «آيد» is «أَفْعَل». The Shaykh mentioned all of this in al-Māʾida. Then he said: "Ibn ʿAṭiyya's statement 'the weakening differed' is not clear" — and that is correct. However, his saying "what appears is that «أيَّد» in the reading of the majority is «فَعَّل», not «أَفْعَل», etc." is questionable, because it suggests that something else is possible, which is impossible: how could it be imagined that «أيَّدَ» with doubling in the reading of the majority is on the pattern «أَفْعَل»? This is something that does not occur.
«الأَيْدُ» is strength. ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib said:
603 - الحمدُ للهِ الأَعزِّ الأكرمِ ... أَيَّدَنا يومَ زُحوفِ الأشْرَمِ
(Praise be to Allah, the Mightiest, the Most Generous, who strengthened us on the day of al-Ashram's advancing hosts.)
The correct view is that «فَعَّل» and «أَفْعَل» here have one meaning, which is "We strengthened him." Some distinguished between them, saying: "As for the prolonged form, its meaning is strength; as for the short form, its meaning is support and help" — and this in reality is no distinction. The Arabs have substituted jīm for the yāʾ in «آيَدَ» on the pattern «أَفْعَل», saying «آجَدَهُ», i.e. he strengthened him. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "One says: «الحمدُ لله الذي آجَدَني بعد ضَعْفٍ وأَوْجَدني بعد فَقْر» ('Praise be to Allah who strengthened me after weakness and enriched me after poverty')." This is just as they substituted jīm for its yāʾ [in «يد»], saying «لا أَفْعَل ذلك جَدَ الدهرِ», i.e. «يدَ الدهر» ("I will not do that ever"); it is a substitution that is not regular.
His saying: {بِرُوحِ القدس} is attached to «أيَّدْناه». Ibn Kathīr read «القُدْس» with a quiescent dāl, and the rest with ḍamma; they are two dialects: the ḍamma for the Ḥijāz and the sukūn for Tamīm, and that has preceded. Abū Ḥaywa read «القُدُوس» with a wāw. There is also a dialectal form with fatḥa on the qāf and the dāl. Its meaning is purity or blessing, as preceded at His saying «ونقدِّسُ لك». «الروح» originally is a name for the part by which life comes about in a living being — al-Rāghib said this — and what is meant by it is Jibrīl, upon him be peace, because of the saying of Ḥassān:
604 - وجبريلٌ رسولُ الله فينا ... وروحُ القُدْسِ ليس له كِفَاءُ
(And Jibrīl, Allah's messenger, is among us, and the Spirit of Holiness, who has no equal.)
He was so named because through him hearts come to life.
His saying: {أَفَكُلَّمَا جَآءَكُمْ رَسُولٌ}: the hamza here is for clarification (tawḍīḥ) [Translator's note: so in the source; probably a scribal error for «التوبيخ», reproach] and rebuke, and the fāʾ is for conjunction: it conjoined this clause to what precedes it, and the interrogative particle was given importance and fronted. The verification of that has passed, and [also] that al-Zamakhsharī supplies a clause between the hamza and the conjunction to which to conjoin it. This clause may be conjoined to what precedes it without omission of anything, as though He said: "We gave, O Children of Israel, your prophets what We gave them; so whenever a messenger came to you..." It is also possible to supply something omitted before it, i.e. "so you did what you did; then whenever a messenger came to you...". The discussion of «كلما» has preceded at His saying:
{كُلَّمَا أَضَآءَ} [al-Baqara: 20]. What makes it accusative here is «استكبرتم». «رسول» is «فَعُول» in the sense of «مَفْعُول», i.e. «مُرْسَل»; «فَعُول» in the sense of «مَفْعول» is rare — there occurs of it «الرَّكُوب» and «الحَلُّوب», i.e. that which is ridden and that which is milked. It may also be a maṣdar (verbal noun) meaning «الرسالة» (message); al-Zamakhsharī said this, and he cited:
605 - لقد كَذَبَ الواشون ما فُهْتُ عندَهم ... بِسِرٍّ ولا أَرْسَلْتُهُمْ برَسول
(The slanderers have lied: I uttered no secret before them, nor sent them with any message.)
i.e. «برسالة». Of this, according to him, is: {إِنَّا رَسُولُ رَبِّ العالمين} [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 16].
His saying: {بِمَا لاَ تهوى أَنْفُسُكُمْ} is attached to His saying «جاءكم». «جاء» is transitive by itself at times, as in this verse, and by a preposition at other times, as in «جِئْتُ إليه». «ما» is a relative noun meaning «الذي», and the returning pronoun is omitted because the conditions are fulfilled; the implied form is: «بما لا تهواه». «تهوى» is the imperfect of «هَوِي» with kasra on the middle radical, and its final radical is from yāʾ because its middle radical is wāw, and the class of «طَوَيْتُ» and «شَوَيْتُ» is more frequent than the class of «قوَّة» and «حُوَّة». There is no evidence in «هَوِيَ», because the middle radical has kasra, and it is like «شَقِي» from «الشَّقاوة»; their saying «هَوَيان» in the dual of its maṣdar is the clearest proof of that. The meaning of «تَهْوَى» is: it loves and chooses. The basic meaning of «الهَوَى» is inclination; it was so called because it makes its possessor fall (yahwī) into the Fire, and for that reason it is mostly used only of what has no good in it; but it is sometimes used of what is good. In the sound ḥadīth there is ʿUmar's saying about the captives of Badr: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ inclined to what Abū Bakr said and did not incline to what I said." And from ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her: "By Allah, I see your Lord only hastening to fulfil your desire (hawāk)." Its plural is «أَهْواء»; He the Exalted said: {بِأَهْوَائِهِم} [al-Anʿām: 119]. It is not pluralised as «أَهْوِية», even though «نَدَى» and «أَنْدِية» occurs; the poet said:
606 - في ليلةٍ من جُمادى ذاتِ أَنْدِيَةٍ ... لا يُبْصِرُ الكلبُ في ظَلْمائها الطُّنُبا
(On a dewy night of Jumādā, in whose darkness the dog cannot see the tent-ropes.)
As for «هوى يَهْوي», with fatḥa in the past and kasra in the imperfect, its meaning is falling. «الهَوِيُّ» with fatḥa on the hāʾ is going downward, and «الهُوِيُّ» is going upward; the verification of all that will come. He attributed the verb to the souls rather than to the addressees — He did not say «بما لا تَهْوون» — to draw attention to the fact that the evil act is mostly attributed to the soul, as in: {إِنَّ النفس لأَمَّارَةٌ بالسواء} [Yūsuf: 53], {بَلْ سَوَّلَتْ لَكُمْ أَنفُسُكُمْ} [Yūsuf: 18], {فَطَوَّعَتْ لَهُ نَفْسُهُ} [al-Māʾida: 30]. «استكبر» means «تَكَبَّرَ» (to be arrogant).
His saying: {فَفَرِيقاً كَذَّبْتُمْ}: the fāʾ conjoins the clause «كَذَّبْتم» to «استكبرتم». «فريقاً» is a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object), fronted so that the verse-endings agree; likewise {وَفَرِيقاً تَقْتُلُونَ}. There must be something omitted, i.e. «فريقاً منهم» ("a party of them"). The meaning is that from their arrogance there arose their hastening to reject one party of the messengers and to kill others. He put rejection first because it is the first evil they do, and because it is common to the one killed and others, for those killed were also rejected by them; it was not stated explicitly [for them] only because He mentioned something uglier than it in deed. «تقتلون» was brought as an imperfect either because it is future, since they were seeking to kill the Messenger of Allah ﷺ — together with what it involves of agreement with the verse-endings and fawāṣil — or because past action is meant [Translator's note: the source's «أن الأمر فظيع» lacks a connective here; the sense is "because the matter is so atrocious"] and it was intended to make it present in the souls and depict it in the hearts. Al-Rāghib allowed {فَفَرِيقاً كَذَّبْتُمْ} to be conjoined to His saying «وأَيَّدْناه», with «أفكلما» and what follows it being a separation between them by way of disapproval. The first is more apparent, although what he said is possible.

semin-durr:132-132.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {ووصى}: It has been read from «وصَّى», and in it there is the sense of multiplicity with respect to the object enjoined; and «أَوْصى» as a four-letter verb, which is the reading of Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir, and so it is in the codices of Medina and Syria. It has been said that «أَوْصى» and «وصَّى» have one meaning.

The pronoun in «بها» has six views. The first: that it refers back to the milla (religion) in His saying: {وَمَن يَرْغَبُ عَن مِّلَّةِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ}. The Shaykh said: "And with it al-Zamakhsharī began, and [al-Mahdawī] and others did not mention it." But al-Zamakhsharī — may Allah have mercy on him — did not mention this; he only mentioned its referring back to His saying «أَسَلَمْتُ», interpreting it as "the word". Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The pronoun in «بها» is for His saying {أَسْلَمْتُ لِرَبِّ العالمين}, on the interpretation of 'the word' and 'the sentence'; similar to it is the returning of the pronoun in His saying {وَجَعَلَهَا كَلِمَةً بَاقِيَةً} [al-Zukhruf: 28] to His saying {إِنَّنِي بَرَآءٌ مِّمَّا تَعْبُدُونَ إِلاَّ الذي فَطَرَنِي} [al-Zukhruf: 28] «[Translator's note: the latter citation is printed as al-Zukhruf: 28 in the source; the verse is al-Zukhruf 26–27.]»; and His saying «كلمةً باقيةً» is evidence that the feminine is on the sense of 'the word'." End quote. The second: that it refers back to the word understood from His saying «أَسْلَمْتُ», as its establishment from al-Zamakhsharī has preceded. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "And it is more correct, because it is the nearest thing mentioned." The third: that it refers back to something coming later, namely the word understood from His saying: {فَلاَ تَمُوتُنَّ إَلاَّ وَأَنْتُم مُّسْلِمُونَ}. The fourth: that it refers back to the word of sincere devotion (kalimat al-ikhlāṣ), even though there has been no [mention] of it. The fifth: that it refers back to obedience, it too being known. The sixth: that it refers back to the injunction (al-waṣiyya) indicated by His saying «ووصَّى». And «بها» is attached to «وصَّى», and «بنِيه» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

His saying: {وَيَعْقُوبُ}: The majority read it nominative, and there are two views on it. The more apparent of them: that it is conjoined to «إبراهيم», its object being omitted, i.e.: and Jacob too enjoined his sons. The second: that it is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) with its khabar (predicate) omitted, its implied form being: "and Jacob said: O my sons, Allah has chosen…". Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAbd Allāh and ʿAmr ibn Fāʾid read it accusative, conjoined to «بَنيه», i.e.: and Abraham enjoined Jacob too.

His saying: {يَا بَنِيَّ} has two aspects. The first: that it is part of what Abraham said, and that is on the view that Jacob is conjoined to Abraham, or on its reading in the accusative. The second: that it is part of what Jacob said, if we say that its nominative is as a mubtadaʾ, and then the speech of Abraham has been omitted because of the indication of it, its implied form being: "And Abraham enjoined his sons: O my sons". On every assumption, the clause «يا بَنِيَّ» and what follows it is [accusative] by an omitted verb of saying in the opinion of the Basrans, i.e.: "and he said: O my sons", and by the verb of enjoining, since it carries the meaning of saying, in the opinion of the Kufans. The rajaz poet said:
731 - رَجُلانِ مِنْ ضَبَّةَ أَخْبرانَا ... إنَّا رَأَيْنا رجلاً عُرْيانا
(Two men of Ḍabba informed us: "We saw a naked man.")
with the hamza [of «إنَّا»] given kasra, on the implying of a verb of saying, or by treating "informing" as "saying". Its connection with the injunction is supported by the reading of Ibn Masʿūd: «أَنْ يا بَنِيَّ», with explicative «أَنْ»; and it is not permissible for it to be maṣdar-forming here, since there is nothing from which a maṣdar (verbal noun) could be cast. Those who refuse to make it explicative — and they are the Kufans — make it redundant (zāʾida).

Yaʿqūb (Jacob) is a foreign proper name, and for that reason it is diptote. Whoever claims that he was named Yaʿqūb because he was born right after (ʿaqib) his brother al-ʿĪṣ (Esau), they being twins, or because his posterity (ʿaqib) and offspring became numerous, has erred; because it would then have had to be fully declinable, since it would be an Arabic derived word. Yaʿqūb is also the male partridge; if a male is named with it, it is declinable; the plural is yaʿāqiba and yaʿāqīb.

And «اصطفى»: its alif is from a yāʾ, that yāʾ being converted from a wāw, because it is from al-ṣafwa (the choicest); when the word became four letters or more, it was changed into a yāʾ and then changed into an alif. And «لكم» means "for your sake", and the alif and lām in «الدين» are for prior reference (al-ʿahd). «[Translator's note: the source prints «الذين»; the verse word is «الدِّين».]»

His saying: {فَلاَ تَمُوتُنَّ إلا}: This is in form a prohibition of death, but in reality it is a prohibition of their being in a state other than Islam when they die, like your saying: "Do not pray except while you are humble". Your prohibition to him is not of prayer; it is only of abandoning humility in the state of his prayer. The subtle point in bringing the particle of prohibition onto prayer, while it is not prohibited, is to show that prayer in which there is no humility is as if it were no prayer «[Translator's note: the source reads «كالصلاة» ("like prayer"); the sense requires "like no prayer", probably «كلا صلاة».]», as if he said: I forbid it to you if you do not pray it in this state. Likewise the meaning in the verse is to show that their dying not in the state of steadfastness in Islam is a death in which there is no good, and that what is due to this death is that it not be made to befall them.

The origin of «تموتُنَّ» is «تموتُونَنَّ»: the first nūn is the sign of the nominative, and the second, doubled one is for emphasis. Three similar letters came together, so the nūn of the nominative was elided, because the nūn of emphasis is more deserving of remaining, since it indicates an independent meaning. Then two quiescent letters met: the wāw and the first, assimilated nūn; so the wāw was elided for the meeting of two quiescents, and the ḍamma remained indicating it; and thus is every case of its like. {إَلاَّ وَأَنْتُم مُّسْلِمُونَ}: This is an emptied exception (istithnāʾ mufarragh) from the general states, and «أنتم مسلمون» is a mubtadaʾ and khabar in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), as though He, Exalted is He, said: "Do not die in any state except in this state"; and the governing word in it is what precedes «إلاَّ».

semin-durr:115-115.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {وَللَّهِ المشرق والمغرب}: a clause connected with His words «مَنَعَ مساجدِ الله، وسعى في خَرابِها»; that is, if someone strives to prevent the mention of Him the Exalted and to ruin His houses, that does not prevent performing worship elsewhere, because the East and the West and what is between them belong to Him the Exalted. The explicit mention of the East and the West rather than anything else is for one of two reasons. The first: their nobility, in that they were assigned to Allah the Exalted. The second: it may be an omission of the maʿṭūf (conjoined) because it is known, i.e. "to Allah belong the East and the West and what is between them", like His words «تَقِيكم الحَرَّ», i.e. "and the cold", and like the poet's saying:
687 - تَنْفي يداها الحصى في كلِّ هاجِرَةٍ ... نَفْيَ الدراهيمِ تَنْقادُ الصيّاريفِ
(Her forelegs scatter the pebbles in every midday heat, as the money-changers' testing scatters the dirhams.)
i.e. her forelegs and hindlegs; and similar to it:
688 - كأنَّ الحَصَى من خَلْفِها وأمامِها ... إذا نَجَلَتْه رِجْلُها خَذْفُ أَعْسَرَا
(As though the pebbles behind her and before her, when her foot kicks them, were the flicking of a left-handed man.)
i.e. her foot and her hand. Concerning «المشرق» and «المغرب» there are two views. The first: they are nouns of place of rising and setting. The second: they are quasi-maṣdars (ism maṣdar), i.e. "the rising" and "the setting", and the meaning is: to Allah belongs the management of the sun's rising from its place of rising and its setting in its place of setting; but His words «فأينما تُوَلُّوا» make this unlikely. He made «المشرق» and «المغرب» singular since what is meant is their two regions, or because they are maṣdars. «المشارق» and «المغارب» occur with regard to their occurring every day, and «المشرقَيْن» and «المغربَيْن» with regard to the rising-place of winter and summer and their two setting-places. By rights they should have had fatḥa on the middle radical, because of what has been said: when the middle radical of the imperfect does not take kasra, the quasi-maṣdar and the nouns of time and place by rights take fatḥa on the middle radical; that is permissible by analogy, but not in recitation.
His words: {فَأَيْنَمَا تُوَلُّواْ}: «أين» here is a conditional noun with the meaning of «إنْ», «ما» is added to it, and «تُوَلُّوا» is jussive (majzūm) by it. The addition of «ما» is not obligatory for it, as shown by the poet's saying:
689 - أَيْنَ تَضْرِبْ بنا العُداةَ تَجِدْنا ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Wherever you strike the enemies with us, you will find us…)
It is an adverb of place, and what puts it in the accusative is what follows it. It is also an interrogative noun, so it is a word shared between condition and interrogation, like «مَنْ» and «ما». Some claimed that its origin is asking about places. It is indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa because it includes the meaning of the conditional or interrogative particle. The origin of تُوَلُّوا is تُوَلِّيوا, and it underwent weakening by omission. The majority read «تُوَلُّوا» with ḍamma on the tāʾ and [shadda on] the lām, meaning "you face", for «وَلَّى», even though its predominant use is "to turn one's back", entails turning toward some direction; one says: وَلَّيْتُ عن كذا إلى كذا (I turned from such-and-such to such-and-such). Al-Ḥasan read «تَوَلَّوا» with fatḥa on both, and there are two aspects in it. The first: it is an imperfect, the origin being تَتَوَلَّوا, from التَّوْلِيَة, with one of the two tāʾs dropped for lightness, as in {تَنَزَّلُ الملائكة} [al-Qadr: 4]. The second: it is a past verb, and the pronoun is for the absent, going back to His words «لهم في الدنيا، ولهم في الآخرة», so that the pronouns are harmonious. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "The second: it is a past verb and the pronoun is for the absent, the implied form being: أَيْنما يَتَوَلَّوا" — meaning that although it is past in wording, it is future in meaning. Then he said: "It may also be a past verb that has actually occurred, and «أَيْنَ» is not conditional in wording but in meaning, as you say «ما صَنَعْتَ صنعتُ» (whatever you did, I did) when you mean the past. This is weak, because «أين» is either conditional or interrogative and has no third meaning."
End of quote; and it is not clear.
His words: {فَثَمَّ وَجْهُ الله}: the fāʾ and what follows it are the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), so the clause is in the position of the jussive. «ثَمَّ» is a fronted khabar (predicate), and «وجهُ الله» is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject). «ثَمَّ» is a demonstrative for a distant place specifically, like هُنا and هَنَّا with doubled nūn. It is indeclinable on fatḥa because it includes the meaning of a demonstrative particle or a particle of address. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "Because for what is present you say هُنا and for what is absent هُناك, and ثَمَّ stands in for هناك"; and this is worthless. It has been said: it is indeclinable because it resembles the particle in needing [something else], for it needs something pointed to, and it is not inflected beyond being put in the genitive by «مِنْ». For this reason some erred in making it a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) in His words {وَإِذَا رَأَيْتَ ثَمَّ [رَأَيْتَ]} [al-Insān: 20]; rather, the object of «رأيت» is omitted. The meaning of «وَجْهُ الله» is His direction which He approved as a qibla and commanded to be faced; or His Essence, as in {كُلُّ شَيْءٍ هَالِكٌ إِلاَّ وَجْهَهُ} [al-Qaṣaṣ: 88]; or what is meant is standing, i.e. "there is the majesty of Allah and His grandeur", from their saying "he is the face of the people"; or it is a redundant connective (ṣila zāʾida), which is worthless. It has been said: what is meant by it is deeds; al-Farrāʾ said this, and on it is the poet's saying:
690 - أسْتَغْفِرُ اللهَ ذَنْباً لسْتُ مُحْصِيَه ... ربُّ العبادِ إليه الوجهُ والعَمَلُ
(I seek Allah's forgiveness for sin I cannot count — the Lord of the servants, to Him is the face [i.e. the aim] and the deed.)

semin-durr:116-116.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {اتخذ الله وَلَداً سُبْحَانَهُ}: the majority [read] «وقالوا» with the wāw, conjoining this declarative clause to what precedes it, and this is better for the connection. It has been said: it is conjoined to His words «وسعى», so He would have conjoined to the ṣila (relative clause), along with the verb, these many clauses; and the Quran ought to be held above such a thing. Ibn ʿĀmir read — and so it is in the codices of Syria — «قالوا» without the wāw, and that admits two aspects. The first: resumption. The second: omission of the conjunction while it is intended, dispensed with because the pronoun links [it] to what precedes this clause. «اتَّخَذَ» may mean "made, produced", in which case it is transitive to one object, or it may mean "rendered", in which case it is transitive to two, and the first here is omitted, the implied form being: "And they said: Allah has taken some existing things as a son". Yet despite the frequent recurrence of this construction, only one object is ever mentioned with it: {وَقَالُواْ اتخذ الرحمن وَلَداً} [al-Anbiyāʾ: 26], {مَا اتخذ الله مِن وَلَدٍ} [al-Muʾminūn: 91], {وَمَا يَنبَغِي للرحمن أَن يَتَّخِذَ وَلَداً} [Maryam: 92]. «الوَلَد» is فَعَل in the sense of مَفْعول, like القَبْض and النَّقْص, and this is not regular by analogy. The maṣdar (verbal noun) is الوِلادة and الوَليديَّة, and this second one is very strange.
His words: {بَل لَّهُ مَا فِي السماوات والأرض}: «بَلْ» is for turning away (iḍrāb) and transition; «له» is a fronted khabar (predicate) and «ما» a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject). He used «ما» here because when the rational are mixed with others, the speaker has the choice between «ما» and «مَنْ»; for that reason, when He took the rational into account, He gave them precedence in His words «قانتون», using the sound-plural form specific to the rational. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: how did He use «ما», which is for those not endowed with knowledge, together with His words «قانتون»? I say: it is like their saying «سبحانَ ما سَخَّركُنَّ» (glory be to the One who subjected you [f. pl.]), and it is as though He used «ما» rather than «مَنْ» to belittle them and diminish their standing." This is an inclination on his part to the view that «ما» may apply to those endowed with knowledge, but the well-known view is otherwise. As for the saying «سبحانَ ما سَخَّركُنَّ لنا», «سبحان» is not annexed [there]; rather it is like the poet's saying:
691 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... سبحان مِنْ علقمةَ. . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(How remarkable [is it] of ʿAlqama…)
and «ما» is a maṣdariyya ẓarfiyya (temporal-verbal) particle. [Translator's note: i.e. "glory be, as long as He subjected you to us".]
His words: {كُلٌّ لَّهُ قَانِتُونَ}: a mubtadaʾ and khabar, and «كلٌّ» is annexed in implication to something omitted, i.e. "all who are in the heavens and the earth". Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It may be: all those whom they made a son to Allah." The Shaykh [Translator's note: Abū Ḥayyān] said: "This is very far-fetched, because the one made a son has not been mentioned, and because the predicate is shared by the one made [a son] and others." His saying "has not been mentioned" — rather, he has been mentioned, so there is nothing far-fetched in it.
He made «قانِتون» plural, construing according to the meaning, because of what has been said: when «كُلّ» is cut off from annexation, it is permissible to observe its wording and to observe its meaning, and the latter is more frequent, as in {كُلٌّ فِي فَلَكٍ يَسْبَحُونَ} [al-Anbiyāʾ: 33] and {وَكُلٌّ أَتَوْهُ دَاخِرِينَ} [al-Naml: 87]. Of observing the wording: {قُلْ كُلٌّ يَعْمَلُ على شَاكِلَتِهِ} [al-Isrāʾ: 84] and {فكُلاًّ أَخَذْنا بذَنْبِه} [al-ʿAnkabūt: 40]. The plural is fine here for the harmony of the verse-endings. «القُنُوت» is obedience and submission, or long standing [in prayer], or silence, or supplication.

semin-durr:58-58.t:
The saying of the Exalted: {هذه القرية}: «هذه» is accusative according to Sībawayh as an adverb (ẓarf), and according to al-Akhfash as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). That is because every specific adverb of place is not reached by the verb except through «في»: you say صَلَّيْتُ في البيتِ ("I prayed in the house"), and you do not say صَلَّيْتُ البيتَ — except for what has been excepted. Among what has been excepted is «دَخَلَ» with every specific place, e.g. دَخَلْتُ البيتَ والسوقَ ("I entered the house and the market"). This is the doctrine of Sībawayh. Al-Akhfash said: "What comes after «دَخَلْتُ» is a direct object, like what comes after هَدَمْتُ in your saying «هَدَمْتُ البيتَ» ('I demolished the house')." So if «دَخَلَ» comes with something other than an adverb, it is made transitive [with في, e.g. دَخَلْتُ في الأمر ("I entered into the matter"), and you do not say دَخَلْتُ الأمرَ; likewise, if a specific adverb comes with a verb other than «دَخَلَ», it is made transitive] with «في», except for what is anomalous, as in his saying:
481 - جَزَى اللهُ ربُّ الناسِ خيرَ جزائِه ... رفيقَيْن قالا خَيْمَتَيْ أمِّ مَعْبَدِ
(May Allah, Lord of mankind, give His best reward to two companions who rested at midday in the two tents of Umm Maʿbad.)
«القريةَ» is a naʿt (adjective) of «هذه», or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition), as preceded. Al-qarya ("town") is derived from قَرَيْتُ, i.e. "I gathered": you say قَرَيْتُ الماءَ في الحوضِ, i.e. "I gathered the water in the basin", and that water is called qiran, with kasra on the qāf. Al-miqrāh is the great bowl, plural maqārin. [The poet] said:
482 - عِظام المَقاري ضَيْفُهُمْ لا يُفَزَّعُ ... . . . . . . . . . . .
(Of great bowls; their guest is not alarmed…)
Al-qaryān is a name for the place where water collects. Al-qarya is originally a name for the place in which people gather, and it may be applied to them figuratively; the saying of the Exalted «واسألِ القريةَ» admits both options. Al-Rāghib said: "It is a name for the place and for the people together, and it is used for each of them."
The saying of the Exalted: {الباب سُجَّداً}: «سُجَّدا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «ادْخُلوا»; it is the plural of sājid. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is more intensive than sujūd", meaning that its plural on the pattern fuʿʿal has an intensiveness not found in its plural on the pattern fuʿūl; this is open to question. The origin of «باب» is bawab, because of their saying abwāb. It may be pluralized as abwiya for the sake of pairing words, as the poet said:
483 - هَتَّاكُ أَخْبِيَةٍ ولاَّجُ أبوبةٍ ... يَخْلِطُ بالبِرِّ منه الجِدِّ والِّلْينا
(A tearer-open of tents, a goer-in through doors, who mixes earnestness and gentleness with his kindness.)
His saying: «حِطَّة» has been read with the nominative and the accusative. The nominative is as the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "our request is ḥiṭṭa" or "your command is ḥiṭṭa". Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The original is the accusative, in the sense of 'remove our sins from us, a removing (ḥiṭṭatan)'; it was only made nominative to give [the sense of] permanence, as in his saying:
484 - شَكا إليَّ جَمَلي طُولَ السُّرَى ... صَبْرٌ جميلٌ فكِلانا مُبْتَلَى
(My camel complained to me of the long night journey: beautiful patience! for both of us are afflicted.)
the original being: صَبْراً عليَّ, i.e. اصبرْ صبراً." So he made it of the category of {سَلاَمٌ عَلَيْكُم} [al-Raʿd: 24], and the clause would be in the position of the accusative governed by the saying. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It has been said: they were commanded to say it in the nominative in this very wording", meaning by way of quotation (ḥikāya). On this [view] it alone, without supposing anything with it, is in the position of the accusative governed by the saying, and what prevented the accusative [ending] is the vowel of quotation. He also said: "ʿIkrima said: they were commanded to say 'there is no god but Allah', so that their sins might be removed by it", and he related two other views with the same meaning, then said: "On these views, it requires the accusative." He means that if the meaning is that what was commanded need not be in this specific wording, but rather anything that brings about the removal of sin, then what follows the saying ought to be accusative as a direct object, as in قُلْ لزيد خيراً ("say something good to Zayd"), the meaning being: say to him what is of the kind of good things.
Al-Naḥḥās said: "The nominative is preferable because of what is related from the Arabs about the meaning of بَدَّل. Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā said: 'One says بَدَّلْتُهُ, i.e. I changed it without removing its substance; and أَبْدَلْتُه: I removed its substance and its person', as in his saying:
485 - عَزْلَ الأميرِ للأميرِ المُبْدَلِ
(Like the commander's dismissal of the commander who is replaced.)
And the Exalted said: {ائت بِقُرْآنٍ غَيْرِ هاذآ أَوْ بَدِّلْهُ} [Yūnus: 15]. And the ḥadīth of Ibn Masʿūd, 'they said: ḥinṭa (wheat)', is an explanation on the basis of the nominative." He means that Allah the Exalted said «فبدَّل», which requires change, not removal of the substance, and this meaning requires the nominative, not the accusative.
Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «حِطَّةً» in the accusative, and there are two options for it. The first: it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) standing in for the verb, as in ضَرْباً زيداً ("strike Zayd!"). The second: it is accusative governed by the saying, i.e. "say this very wording", as preceded in the option on the nominative. On the first [option] it is accusative by the implied verb, and that implied verb together with its accusative is in the position of the accusative governed by the saying; al-Zamakhsharī preferred this option.
Al-ḥiṭṭa is a noun of manner (ism hayʾa) from al-ḥaṭṭ ("putting down"), like al-jilsa and al-qiʿda. It has been said: it is a word they were commanded to say, and we do not know its meaning. It has also been said: it is repentance, and [this verse] was recited:
486 - فاز بالحِطَّة التي جَعَلَ الل ... هُ بها ذنبَ عبدهِ مَغْفُورا
(He attained the ḥiṭṭa by which Allah made His servant's sin forgiven.)
His saying: «نَغْفِرْ» is jussive (majzūm) in answer to the command. The disagreement has preceded as to whether what makes it jussive is the clause itself or an implied condition, i.e. "if they say [it], We will forgive". «نَغْفِرْ» has been read with the nūn, which accords with what precedes it in His saying «وإذ قلنا»; and «تُغْفَرْ», passive, with tāʾ and with yāʾ, «خَطاياكم» being a nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent): the tāʾ is for the feminine of al-khaṭāyā, and the yāʾ because its femininity is not real, and also because of the separation by «لكم». It has also been read «يَغْفِرْ», active, the agent being Allah the Exalted; this has the meaning of the first reading, except that it contains an iltifāt (shift of person). «لكم» is attached to «نَغْفِرْ». Abū ʿAmr assimilated the rāʾ into the lām, and the grammarians consider this weak. They said: because the rāʾ is a letter of repetition, so it is stronger than the lām, and the rule is that the weaker is assimilated into the stronger, not the reverse. But there is no weakness in it, because the deviation (inḥirāf) of the lām counterbalances the repetition of the rāʾ. Abū al-Baqāʾ and others went on at length explaining its weakness, and the answer to that has preceded.
His saying: «خَطَايَاكُمْ» is either accusative by the verb before it or nominative, according to the readings mentioned. There are four views about it. The first, the view of al-Khalīl, may Allah have mercy on him, is that its original form is khaṭāyiʾu, with a yāʾ after the alif followed by a hamza, because it is the plural of khaṭīʾa, like ṣaḥīfa and ṣaḥāyif. Had it been left as it was, the yāʾ would have had to be changed into a hamza, because the long vowel of [the pattern] faʿāyil is treated thus, as established in morphology. So to avoid two hamzas coming together, he made a metathesis: he put the lām first and the long vowel after it, so it became khaṭāʾī. This was found heavy, on a letter heavy in itself and followed by a yāʾ of the same kind as the kasra, so they changed the kasra into a fatḥa; then the weak letter was vowelled with a fatḥa before it, so it was changed into an alif, and it became khaṭāʾā, with a hamza between two alifs. That was found heavy, for the hamza resembles the alif, so it was as though three alifs came together; so they changed the hamza into a yāʾ, because it stood in its place before the metathesis, and it became khaṭāyā on the pattern faʿālā. So there are four operations in it: metathesis, replacing the kasra with a fatḥa, changing the yāʾ into an alif, and replacing the hamza with a yāʾ. This is how the morphologists mention it, and it is the doctrine of al-Khalīl.
The second — Abū al-Baqāʾ also attributed it to him — is that it is khaṭāʾiʾ, with two hamzas, the first of them with a kasra, which is the one changed from the additional yāʾ in khaṭīʾa, so it is like ṣaḥīfa and ṣaḥāʾif. Combining the two hamzas was found heavy, so they moved the first hamza to the place of the second, and its pattern became faʿāliʾ. They only did this so that the one with the kasra would become final and be changed into a yāʾ, so it became faʿāliʾ [sic]. Then they replaced the kasra of the first hamza with a fatḥa, and the yāʾ after it was changed into an alif, as they said يا لَهَفى and يا أسفى. So the hamza came between two alifs, and a yāʾ was substituted for it, because the hamza is close to the alif and they disliked three alifs coming together. On this [view] there are five changes in it: putting the lām first, replacing the kasra with a fatḥa, replacing the last hamza with a yāʾ, then replacing that with an alif, then replacing the hamza that is the lām with a yāʾ. The first view is preferable because of fewer operations; so al-Khalīl has two views on the question. [Translator's note: the source gives the pattern as «فعالِئ» twice in this paragraph; the second presumably should be فعالي after the hamza becomes yāʾ. Translated as written.]
The third is the view of Sībawayh: its original form according to him is khaṭāyiʾ, as preceded; he replaced the additional yāʾ with a hamza, so two hamzas came together, and he necessarily replaced the second of them with a yāʾ; then he did the operation mentioned earlier. Its pattern according to him is faʿāʾil, like ṣaḥāʾif. On his view there are five changes in it: replacing the additional yāʾ with a hamza, replacing the radical hamza with a yāʾ, changing the kasra into a fatḥa, changing the radical yāʾ into an alif, and changing the additional hamza into a yāʾ.
The fourth is the view of al-Farrāʾ: khaṭāyā according to him is not the plural of khaṭīʾa with a hamza; it is only the plural of khaṭiyya, like hadiyya and hadāyā, and rakiyya and rakāyā. Al-Farrāʾ said: "Had khaṭīʾa been pluralized with the hamza, you would say khaṭāʾā" — meaning the hamza would not be changed into a yāʾ but would be kept as it was, without regard to three alifs coming together; but the Arabs did not say it, and that indicated to him that it is not the plural of the hamzated word. Al-Kisāʾī said: had it been pluralized with the hamza, the hamza would be assimilated into the hamza, like dawābb. It has been read «يَغْفِرْ لكم خطيئَاتكم» and «خطيئَتكم», in the plural and the singular, and with yāʾ and tāʾ in the passive; and «خَطَأْيَاكم» with a hamza on the first alif and not the second, and the reverse. The discussion of these readings is clear from what has preceded.
Al-ghafr is covering; from it is al-mighfar, the head-cover (helmet), and ghufrān of sins because it covers them. The difference between it and al-ʿafw has preceded. Al-ghifār is a cloth that protects the veil from the oil of the head touching it. Al-khaṭīʾa is from al-khaṭaʾ, whose basic meaning is deviating from the direction. It is of kinds. One of them is to will something other than what is good to will and to do it; this is complete error, and of it one says: خَطِئ يَخْطَأُ خِطْئاً وخَطْأَةً. The second is to will what is good to do, but it turns out otherwise; of it one says: أَخْطَأ خَطَأً فهو مُخْطِئٌ. In short, of one who intends something and something else comes about from him it is said أخْطَأَ, and if it comes about as he intended it is said أصاب. It may also be said of one who does a deed that is not good, or intends something unseemly, that he أَخْطأ. For this reason one says: أصابَ الخطأَ ("he hit upon the error"), أخطأَ الصوابَ ("he missed what is right"), أصابَ الصوابَ ("he hit upon what is right") and أخطأَ الخطأَ ("he missed the error"). The difference between them and al-sayyiʾa will come, if Allah the Exalted wills.

semin-durr:59-59.t:
The saying of the Exalted: {فَبَدَّلَ الذين ظَلَمُواْ قَوْلاً غَيْرَ الذي قِيلَ لَهُمْ}: this speech must be interpreted, since blame is directed at them only if they changed the saying that was said to them, not if they changed a saying other than it. So it has been said: its implied form is "so those who did wrong exchanged what was said to them [for a saying other than what was said to them]". So «بَدَّلَ» is transitive to one object by itself and to another by the bāʾ; what is made genitive by it is what is abandoned, and the accusative is what is present, as in the saying of Abū al-Najm:
487 - وبُدِّلَتْ والدهرُ ذو تَبَدُّلِ ... هَيْفاً دَبُوراً بالصَّيا والشَّمْأَلِ
(She was given in exchange — and time is full of changes — a hot west wind in place of the east wind and the north wind.)
So what was cut off from her is the ṣabā (east wind), and what she got is the hayf. Abū al-Baqāʾ said this. [Translator's note: the verse in the source reads «بالصَّيا», evidently a misprint for بالصَّبا, as the following explanation shows.] He [also] said: "It is possible that بَدَّل is construed according to the meaning, its implied form being: so those who did wrong said a saying other than what was said to them, because changing a saying is [replacing it] with a saying." So the accusative of «غير» on both these views according to him is as a naʿt (adjective) of «قولاً». It has also been said: its implied form is "so those who did wrong exchanged a saying for other than what [was said]", and the preposition was omitted so it became accusative. The meaning of tabdīl is changing, as though it were said: so they changed a saying for another, i.e. they brought another saying in place of the saying they were commanded to say, as is related in the story that instead of «حِطَّة» they said "ḥinṭa (wheat) in a barley-grain".
Al-ibdāl, al-istibdāl and al-tabdīl are putting a thing in place of another. Tabdīl may also be said to mean changing, even if a substitute for it is not brought. The difference between بَدَّل and أَبْدَلَ has preceded: بَدَّلَ is in the sense of changing without removing the substance, and أَبْدَلَ requires removing the substance — except that {عسى رَبُّنَآ أَن يُبْدِلَنَا} [al-Qalam: 32] and {فَأَرَدْنَآ أَن يُبْدِلَهُمَا رَبُّهُمَا} [al-Kahf: 81] have been read both ways, which requires that they be one in meaning, not different. Al-badīl and al-badal are of one meaning, and بَدَّله غيرُه. One says bidl and badal, like shibh and shabah, mithl and mathal, nikl and nakal. Abū ʿUbayda said: "No [pairs] on fiʿl and faʿal have been heard other than these words."
His saying: {مِّنَ السمآء}. [Two options are possible in it. The first: that it is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أَنْزلنا», with «مِنْ» for the beginning of the extent, i.e. from the direction of the sky; this option] is the apparent one. The second: that it is an adjective of «رِجْزاً», so it is attached to something omitted, and «مِنْ» is also for the beginning of the extent. His saying: {عَلَى الذين ظَلَمُواْ}: He mentioned them again as they were first mentioned, and did not say «عليهم», to draw attention to the fact that their wrongdoing was a cause of their punishment; it is a case of putting the overt noun in the place of the pronoun for this purpose. Putting the overt noun in the place of the pronoun is of two kinds: a kind that occurs after the speech is complete, like this verse and the saying of al-Khansāʾ:
488 - تَعَرَّقَنِي الدَّهرُ نَهْساً وحَزَّاً ... وأَوْجَعَني الدَّهْرُ قَرْعاً وغَمْزَا
(Time has stripped me to the bone with bites and cuts, and time has pained me with knocks and pinches.)
i.e. its calamities all struck me; and a kind that occurs within one speech, as in His saying {الحاقة مَا الحآقة} [al-Ḥāqqa: 1-2], and the saying of another:
489 - ليتَ الغُرابَ غداةَ يَنْعَبُ دائِباً ... كان الغرابُ مُقَطَّعَ الأَوْداجِ
(Would that the crow, on the morning it kept croaking, the crow had had its jugular veins cut.)
ʿAdī ibn Zayd combined the two meanings, saying:
490 - لا أرى الموتَ يَسْبِقُ الموتَ شيءٌ ... نَغَّصَ الموتُ ذا الغِنَى والفَقيرا
(I see that nothing outstrips death; death has spoiled [life] for the rich and the poor.)
In Sūrat al-Aʿrāf there came {فَأَرْسَلْنَا عَلَيْهِمُ} [al-Aʿrāf: 133]: there it came with the word "sending" (irsāl), and with the pronoun rather than the overt noun. That is because in this sūra the Exalted enumerated to them many great blessings, so directing blame at them and rebuking them for ingratitude for those blessings was more forceful [here] than there, since there He did not enumerate to them what He enumerated here; and the word "sending down" (inzāl) for punishment is more forceful than the word "sending". [Translator's note: the source cites al-Aʿrāf: 133, though the parallel verse with «فَأَرْسَلْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ رِجْزاً» is al-Aʿrāf: 162; translated as written.]
Al-rijz is punishment. There is another dialectal form of it, with a ḍamma on the rāʾ, and it has been read with both. It has been said: the form with ḍamma is the name of an idol, and from it is {والرجز فاهجر} [al-Muddaththir: 5]; that is because it is a cause of punishment. Al-Farrāʾ said: "Al-rijz and al-rijs, with zāy and sīn, have one meaning, like al-sudgh and al-zudgh." The correct view is that al-rijz is filth, and its explanation will come. Al-rajaz is a disease that afflicts camels so that they tremble from it, and from it is the rajaz metre in poetry.
His saying: «بما كانوا يفسُقُون» is attached to {أَنزَلْنَا}; the bāʾ is causal. «ما» may be maṣdariyya — this is the apparent [view] — i.e. "because of their transgressing"; or it may be a nominal relative, the returning pronoun being omitted by the gradual process mentioned in more than one place, the original being يَفْسُقُونَه. Making it an indefinite qualified noun is not strong. In Sūrat al-Aʿrāf He said {يَظْلِمُونَ} [verse: 162], to draw attention [to the fact] that they combine these two ugly qualities. The meaning of fisq has preceded. Ibn Waththāb read {يَفْسُقُونَ} with a kasra on the sīn; it has preceded that these are two dialectal forms.

semin-durr:31-31.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {وَعَلَّمَ آدَمَ الأسمآء كُلَّهَا}: this clause may have no grammatical position because it is resumptive, or its position may be the genitive because it is conjoined to «قال ربك». This «عَلَّم» is transitive to two objects; before the doubling it was transitive to one, because it is [the «علم»] of recognition (ʿirfāniyya), so by the doubling it became transitive to another. They distinguished between «عَلِم» of recognition and [«عَلِم»] of certainty in [the manner of] making them transitive: when they wanted to make the [verb] of recognition transitive [to a further object], they did so by doubling, and when they wanted to make the [verb] of certainty transitive, they did so by the hamza. Abū ʿAlī ʿAlī al-Shalawbīn mentioned that [Translator's note: so printed, with «علي» repeated; the scholar meant is Abū ʿAlī al-Shalawbīn]. The fāʿil (agent) of «عَلَّم» refers to the Creator, Exalted is He, and «آدمَ» is its object.
There are six views regarding it [«آدم»]. The most preponderant of them is [that it is] a foreign (aʿjamī), non-derived noun, its pattern fāʿal like its counterparts, e.g. «آزَر» and «شالَح»; it was made a diptote only because of its being a proper name and its personal foreignness. The second: that it is derived from «الأُدْمَة», which is a redness inclining to black. The third: that it is derived from «أَديم الأرض» (the surface of the earth) — [and this is the most plausible of them; and on these two views it was made a diptote because of the [verbal] pattern and its being a proper name. The fourth: that it is derived from «أديم الأرض»] also, but on this pattern, I mean the pattern fāʿal; and this is an error, because it should then have been fully declined. The fifth: that it is Hebrew, from «الإِدام», which is soil. The sixth: al-Ṭabarī said: "It is originally a quadriliteral verb like «أَكْرَم», and he was named with it for the purpose of manifesting the thing so that its aspect may be known." The upshot is that claiming derivation for it is far-fetched, because foreign nouns are not subject to derivation or morphological inflection. «آدم», though it is an object in wording, is an agent in meaning, and «الأسماءَ» is a second object; the matter belongs to the category of «أعطى» and «كسا» (gave, clothed), which has rules that will come, if Allah the Exalted wills.
It has been read «عُلِّم» as passive, with «آدمُ» in the nominative because it stands in the place of the agent [i.e. as nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent)]. «كلَّها» is a tawkīd (emphasis) of «الأسماء», always following [it], though it sometimes comes directly after governing words, as has preceded. As for His saying «الأسماء كلَّها», the apparent [view] is that it does not need a claim of omission, because the meaning is: and He taught Adam the names — [He did not specify for us particular names; rather «كلَّها» indicated comprehensiveness, and the wisdom is achieved by learning the names] — even if he did not know what they named; or [it may be that] He used «الأسماء» and meant the things named. On these two aspects there is no omission. It has been said: there must be an omission, and they disagreed about it. It has been said: its implied form is "the names of the things named," and the muḍāf ilayhi was omitted because it is known. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "And the lām [of the article] compensated for it, as in His saying, Exalted is He: {واشتعل الرأس شَيْباً} [Maryam: 4]." This view was given preponderance by His saying, Exalted is He: {أَنْبِئُونِي بِأَسْمَآءِ هؤلاء. . . فَلَمَّآ أَنْبَأَهُمْ بِأَسْمَآئِهِمْ} [al-Baqara: 31-33], and He did not say: "Inform me of these… and when he informed them of them." But there is an objection to his saying "and the lām compensated for it," because the alif and lām do not stand in the place of annexation according to the Basrans. It has been said: its implied form is "the things named by the names," so the muḍāf was omitted and the muḍāf ilayhi was made to stand in its place; this view was given preponderance by His saying, Exalted is He: {ثُمَّ عَرَضَهُمْ}, because names are not pluralised [with a pronoun] like that, so its referring back indicated the things named.
Similar to this verse is His saying, Exalted is He: {أَوْ كَظُلُمَاتٍ فِي بَحْرٍ لُّجِّيٍّ يَغْشَاهُ مَوْجٌ} [al-Nūr: 40]; its implied form is "or like one in darknesses," so the hāʾ in «يَغْشَاه» refers back to the omitted «ذي».
His saying: {ثُمَّ عَرَضَهُمْ عَلَى الملائكة}: «ثم» is a particle of delay, as has preceded. The pronoun in «عَرَضَهُمْ» is for the implied things named, or [it is] because «الأسماء» was used and the things named were meant, as has preceded. It has been said: it refers back to the names, and this is reported from Ibn ʿAbbās; it is supported by the reading of whoever read «عَرَضَها» and «عَرَضَهُنَّ». However, in this view the pronoun of non-rational beings is made like the pronoun of rational beings; or we say: Ibn ʿAbbās said that only on the basis that He used «الأسماء» and meant the things named, as has preceded, and this is clear. «على الملائكة» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «عرضهم».
His saying: {أَنْبِئُونِي بِأَسْمَآءِ هؤلاء}: al-inbāʾ is informing. The basic rule of «أنبأ» is that it is transitive to two [objects], the second of them by a preposition, as in this verse; the preposition is sometimes omitted — Allah the Exalted said: {مَنْ أَنبَأَكَ هذا} [al-Taḥrīm: 3], i.e. "of this" — and it sometimes includes the meaning of «أَعْلَم» of certainty, so it is made transitive as that is, to three objects. Like «أنبأ» are «نَبَّأ», «أخبر», «خبَّر» and «حدَّث». «هؤلاء» is in the position of the genitive by annexation. It is a demonstrative, and its rank is the near. It is pronounced long and short, as in his saying:
346 - هَؤُلا ثُمَّ هَؤُلا كُلاًّ أعطَيْ ... تَ نِعالاً محْذُوَّة بمِثالِ
(These, then these — to each you gave sandals cut to a pattern.)
The well-known [form] is its being indeclinable on kasra; it is sometimes [pronounced] with ḍamma, it is sometimes given nunation with kasra, and its hamza is sometimes replaced by hāʾ, so you say «هَؤُلاه»; and «هَوْلا» is sometimes said, as in his saying:
347 - تجلَّدْ لا يَقُلْ هَوْلا هَذَا ... بكَى لَمَّا بكى أَسَفا عليكما
(Be steadfast, lest these say: "This one wept when he wept in grief over you two.")
Its final radical, according to al-Fārisī, is a hamza, so its first and final radicals are from one root letter; according to al-Mubarrad its origin is yāʾ, and it was changed into a hamza only because it comes at the end after an augmentative alif.
His saying: {إِن كُنْتُمْ صَادِقِينَ}: its like has preceded. Its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, i.e. "if you are truthful, then inform me." The Kufans and al-Mubarrad hold that the apodosis is what precedes; this is refuted by their saying «أنتَ ظالمٌ إن فعلْتَ» (you are a wrongdoer if you do), because if it were an apodosis the fāʾ would be obligatory with it, just as it is obligatory when it comes later. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "That the apodosis is omitted is the opinion of al-Mubarrad, and that it is what precedes is the opinion of Sībawayh" — and that is a mistake.

semin-durr:32-32.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {قَالُواْ سُبْحَانَكَ}: «سُبْحان» is a noun of maṣdar (ism maṣdar), namely of «التسبيح»; it has been said: rather, it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), because a triliteral verb has been heard for it. It is one of the nouns that are bound to annexation, though it is sometimes used on its own; when used on its own it is a diptote because of definiteness and the augment of alif and nūn, as in his saying:
348 - أقولُ لَمَّا جاءني فَخْرُه ... سُبْحَانَ مِنْ علقَمَةَ الفاخِرِ
(I say, when his boasting reached me: how far removed [I am] from ʿAlqama the boaster!)
It has come with nunation, as in his saying:
349 - سبحانَه ثم سُبْحاناً نعوذُ به ... وقبلَنَا سبَّح الجُودِيُّ والجُمُدُ
(Glory be to Him, then glory — we seek refuge in Him; and before us al-Jūdī and al-Jumud glorified [Him].)
So it has been said: it was fully declined out of poetic necessity; and it has been said: it is like «قبلُ» and «بعدُ»: if its definiteness is intended it remains as it is, and if it is made indefinite it is declined as a fully declinable noun. This verse supports its being a maṣdar [and not a noun of maṣdar], because it occurs fully declined. The holder of the first view may answer it by [saying] that this is indefinite, not definite. It is one of the nouns bound to the accusative as a maṣdar [i.e. as a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object)], so it does not change its function, and what makes it accusative is an implied verb that may not be made overt. It has been related from al-Kisāʾī that he made it a vocative, its implied form being «يا سبحانَك», but the majority of grammarians rejected that. Its annexation [here] is to the object, because the meaning is "we glorify You." It has been said: rather, its annexation is to the agent, and the meaning is "You are transcendent and far removed from evil, and glory be to You." And [the clause with] what governs it is in the position of the accusative by «القول».
His saying: {لاَ عِلْمَ لَنَآ إِلاَّ مَا عَلَّمْتَنَآ} is like His saying, Exalted is He: {لاَ رَيْبَ فِيهِ} [al-Baqara: 2]. «إلاَّ» is a particle of exception, «ما» is a relative noun, «علَّمتنا» is its ṣila (relative clause), and its referent is omitted — on the basis that «عِلْم» is in the sense of «مَعْلُوم» (what is known). It may be maṣdariyya. It is in the position of the accusative as an excepted [term]; [it may not be made accusative by «العِلْم», which is the noun of «لا», because if it governed [anything] it would be declinable]. It has been said: it is in the position of the nominative as a badal (substitute) from the noun of «لا» according to [its] position. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It is a badal from the khabar (predicate) of the [lā of] exoneration (al-tabriʾa) [i.e. the lā of generic negation], as in their saying «لا إلهَ إلا اللهُ»." There is an objection to this, because exception is only from that about which a judgement is made, as qualified by the judgement, not from what is predicated. He also reported from al-Zahrāwī that «ما» is accusative by «علَّمْتَنَا» after it; this is unintelligible, because how can a relative noun be made accusative by its ṣila, with [the ṣila] governing it? The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "Unless a far-fetched aspect is contrived for it, namely that it is a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ) in the sense of «لكنْ», and «ما» is conditional, and «علَّمتنَا» makes it accusative and is in the position of the jussive by it, and the apodosis is omitted, the implied form being: 'but whatever You have taught us, we know it.'"
His saying: {إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ العليم الحكيم}: «أنتَ» admits three aspects: that it is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the noun of «إنَّ», so its position is accusative; that it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar is what follows it, and the clause is the khabar of «إنَّ»; and that it is a separating pronoun (faṣl). In this there is the well-known disagreement: does it have a grammatical position or not? And if it is said that it has a position, is it according to the case of what precedes it, as al-Farrāʾ says, so it is in the position of the accusative, or according to the case of what follows it, so it is in the position of the nominative, as al-Kisāʾī says? «الحكيمُ» is a second khabar or a naʿt (adjective) of «العليم». Both are [of the pattern] faʿīl in the sense of fāʿil, and in them there is intensiveness that is not in it [the fāʿil form].
Al-ḥukm, lexically, is perfecting and preventing from going outside what is intended; from it is «حَكَمَة الدابَّة» (the bit-ring of the riding animal); and Jarīr said:
350 - أبني حَنِيفَةَ أحْكِموا سفهاءَكُمْ ... إني أخافُ عليكُمُ أَنْ أغْضَبَا
(O Banū Ḥanīfa, restrain your fools; I fear for you that I may become angry.)
«العليم» was placed before «الحكيم» because it is what connects with His saying «عَلَّم» and their saying «لا عِلْمَ لنا», so its connection with it was fitting; and because wisdom arises from knowledge and is an effect of it, and the attribute of knowledge is often placed before it. «الحكيم» is an attribute of essence if it is explained as "possessor of wisdom," and an attribute of action if it is explained as "the One who perfects His making."

semin-durr:149-149.t: His saying, the Exalted: {وَمِنْ حَيْثُ خَرَجْتَ فَوَلِّ}: «مِنْ حيثُ» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to His saying «فولِّ», and «خرجْتَ» is in the position of the genitive (majrūr) because «حيث» is annexed to it. ʿAbd Allāh [Ibn Masʿūd] read «حيثَ» with fatḥa; it has already been mentioned that this is one of the dialectal forms. It cannot be conditional here, since «ما» is not added to it. As for the hāʾ in His saying «وإنَّه لَلْحَقُّ», the discussion of it is the same as the discussion of it given earlier. «تَعْلَمون» has been read with yāʾ and with tāʾ, and both are clear, as has already been explained.

semin-durr:150-150.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {لِئَلاَّ يَكُونَ}: this is the lām of purpose (lām kay), after which comes the maṣdar-forming (maṣdariyya) «أَنْ» that puts the imperfect verb in the accusative, and «لا» is a negative particle falling between the governor of the accusative and the word it governs, just as it falls between the governor of the jussive and the word it makes jussive, as in: {إِلاَّ تَفْعَلُوهُ تَكُنْ} [al-Anfāl: 73]. «أَنْ» here must be made overt, since if it were implied the wording would become heavy through two lāms following one another. The preposition lām is attached to His saying «فَوَلُّوا وجوهَكم». Abū al-Baqāʾ said: it is attached to an omitted element, its implied form being "We did that so that not…", but there is no need for that. «للناس» is the khabar (predicate) of «يكون», placed before its noun, which is «حُجَّةٌ». «عليكم» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), because it was originally a naʿt (adjective) of the indefinite noun; when it was placed before it, it became accusative as a ḥāl. It is not attached to «حُجَّة», lest it entail placing what the maṣdar (verbal noun) governs before it, which is impossible, since the maṣdar is equivalent to a relative particle and its ṣila (relative clause). Some said: "it is attached to «حُجَّة»", but that is weak. It is also possible that «عليكم» is the khabar of «يكون», and «للناسِ» is attached to «يكون», according to the view of those who hold that the incomplete (nāqiṣa) kāna governs adverbs and the like. The verb in His saying «يكونَ» is masculine because the femininity of «الحجة» is not real, and the separation [between verb and subject] also made that good.

His saying: {إِلاَّ الذين}: the majority read «إلاَّ» with kasra on the hamza and a doubled lām; Ibn ʿAbbās, Zayd ibn ʿAlī and Ibn Zayd read it with fatḥa and a light lām («أَلا»), as the opening particle (istiftāḥ). As for the reading of the majority, the grammarians differed over its interpretation in four views. The most evident of them — which is the choice of al-Ṭabarī, with which Ibn ʿAṭiyya began, and besides which al-Zamakhsharī mentioned nothing — is that it is a connected exception (istithnāʾ muttaṣil). Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Its meaning is: so that there be no argument for any of the Jews, except for the obstinate among them, who say: 'He only left our qibla for the Kaʿba out of inclination toward the religion of his people and love for them.' Their statement is called «حجة» because they presented it in the manner of an argument." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "The meaning is that no one has an argument against you except the refuted argument of those who did wrong among the Jews and others who spoke about this event; He called it an argument and judged it corrupt since it came from a wrongdoer."

The second: that it is a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ), rendered by «لكن» according to the Basrans and by «بل» according to the Kufans, because it is an exception from something other than the first [category]; the implied sense is: but those who did wrong cling to [something] against you with a specious doubt, which they put in the place of an argument. The source of the disagreement is: is «الحُجَّة» the sound proof, or argumentation, whether sound or corrupt? On the first [view] it is disconnected, and on the second it is connected.

The third — and it is the view of Abū ʿUbayda — is that «إلاَّ» has the meaning of the conjunctive wāw, and he counted among such [usages] the [poet's] saying:
774 - وكلُّ أخٍ مُفَارِقُه أَخوه ... لَعَمْرُ أبيك إلا الفَرْقَدان
(Every brother is parted from by his brother — by your father's life — except [i.e. and] the two Farqad stars.)
and the saying of the other:
775 - ما بالمدينةِ دارٌ غيرُ واحدةٍ ... دارُ الخليفةِ إلا دارُ مروانا
(There is not in Medina but one house — the house of the caliph — except [i.e. and] the house of Marwān.)
Its implied sense according to him is: "and nor those who did wrong", "and the two Farqads", "and the house of Marwān". The grammarians, such as al-Zajjāj and others, judged him wrong in that.

The fourth: that «إلا» has the meaning of «بَعْدَ» (after), i.e. after those who did wrong; and he counted among this the saying of Allah the Exalted: {لاَ يَذُوقُونَ فِيهَا الموت إِلاَّ الموتة الأولى} [al-Dukhān: 56] and His saying, the Exalted: {إِلاَّ مَا قَدْ سَلَفَ} [al-Nisāʾ: 22], its implied form being "after the first death" and "after what has passed". This is one of the most corrupt and objectionable of views; I have mentioned it only to draw attention to its weakness.

«الذين» is in the position of the accusative as the excepted (mustathnā), on both views, connected and disconnected. Quṭrub permitted that it be in the position of the genitive as a badal (substitute) from the second-person pronoun in «عليكم», the implied sense being: so that no argument be established for people against those who are not the wrongdoers among them, namely you, O you who are addressed with turning your faces toward the qibla. It is reported from him that he used to read: {إِلاَّ عَلَى الذين}, as though repeating the governor in the badal, after the manner of His saying: {لِلَّذِينَ استضعفوا لِمَنْ آمَنَ مِنْهُمْ} [al-Aʿrāf: 75]. This is impossible according to the majority of the Basrans, because it leads to an overt noun being a whole-for-whole badal of a pronoun of someone present; none of the Basrans permitted it except al-Akhfash, and others reinterpreted what has occurred of that.

As for the reading of Ibn ʿAbbās, «ألا» is the opening particle, and there are then three views on the position of «الذين». The most evident of them: that it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar is His saying «فلا تَخْشَوْهم». The fāʾ entered the khabar only because the relative noun contains the meaning of a condition, and the past verb serving as the ṣila is future in meaning, as though it were said: whoever wrongs people, do not fear them. Were it not for the entry of the fāʾ, the accusative by ishtighāl (preoccupation of the verb) would be preferable, i.e.: do not fear those who did wrong, do not fear them. The second: that it is accusative by an implied verb by way of ishtighāl, and that is according to the view of al-Akhfash, for he permits the fāʾ to be redundant (zāʾida). The third — reported by Ibn ʿAṭiyya —: that it is accusative by way of incitement (ighrāʾ).

It is reported from Ibn Mujāhid that he read: {إِلاَّ الذين ظَلَمُواْ} [Translator's note: as printed; the context indicates the reading meant is «إلى الذين»], and he took «إلى» as a preposition, interpreting it as meaning «مع» (with), the implied sense being: so that people have no argument against you, with those who… The evident thing is that this narrator heard «إلا الذين» with a light «إلا» and believed it to be so; and there are parallels to this mentioned among them [Translator's note: the closing quotation mark here is unmatched in the source]. «منهم» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, and so is attached to an omitted element; «مِنْ» may be partitive, or it may be explicative.

His saying: {وَلأُتِمَّ}: there are four views on it. The most evident of them: that it is conjoined to His saying «لئلا يكونَ», as though the meaning were: "We made known to you the right direction in your qibla, and the arguments are for you, so that people's arguments against you be removed and to complete the favour"; the making known is thus explained by these two reasons, and the separation by the exception and what follows it is as no separation, since it belongs to what is connected with the first reason. The second: that it is conjoined to an omitted reason, both of which explain the previously mentioned fearing, as though it were said: and fear Me so that I may fulfil [your due] to you and so that I may complete My favour upon you. The third: that it is attached to an omitted verb implied after it, its implied form being: "and in order to complete My favour upon you, I made known to you the matter of your qibla." The fourth — and it is the weakest of them —: that it is attached to the verb before it and the wāw is redundant, its implied form being: and fear Me so that I may complete My favour. This is the lām kay, with «أنْ» implied after it putting the imperfect verb in the accusative, so that from them a maṣdar is formed which is put in the genitive by the lām; its verification has been given earlier. «عليكم» has two views: one is that it is attached to «أُتِمَّ», and the second that it is attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl from «نعمتي», i.e. being upon you.

semin-durr:88-88.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {قُلُوبُنَا غُلْفٌ} ...: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), and the clause is in the position of accusative (manṣūb) by the [verb of] saying before it. The majority read «غُلْفٌ» with a quiescent lām, and there are two views on it. The first, and it is the more apparent: that it is the plural of «أَغْلَف», like «أحمر» and «حُمْر», «أصفر» and «صُفْر». The meaning on this view is that they were created and formed covered, so that the truth does not reach them — a metaphor taken from the «أغلف», the one who has not been circumcised. The second: that it is the plural of «غِلاف» (covering, sheath), the lām originally having ḍamma and then lightened, as in «حِمار» and «حُمُر», «كتاب» and «كُتُب». However, lightening «فُعُل» mostly occurs in the singular, as in «عُنْق» for «عُنُق». As for «فُعُل» of the plural, Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "Lightening it is not permissible except by poetic necessity" — but that is not so; rather it is rare, and others have stated explicitly that it is permissible. Ibn ʿAbbās read — and it is narrated from Abū ʿAmr — with ḍamma on the lām, and it is the plural of «غِلاف». In this reading «فُعُل» cannot be the plural of «أَغْلف», because making «فُعُل» of a sound middle radical heavy is not permissible except in poetry. The meaning according to this reading is: our hearts are vessels of knowledge, so they have no need of other knowledge. «التغليف» is like «التغشِيَة» (covering) in meaning.
His saying: {بَل لَّعَنَهُمُ الله}: «بل» is a particle of iḍrāb (digression/retraction), and the iḍrāb refers back to what their saying implied, namely that their hearts are covered; so Allah refuted that for them, [stating] that its cause is His cursing them for their previous disbelief. Iḍrāb is of two kinds: cancellation (ibṭāl) and transition (intiqāl). The first is as in «ما قام زيدٌ بل عمروٌ» ("Zayd did not stand, rather ʿAmr"). [Translator's note: the source does not go on to give an example of the second kind.] «بل» conjoins only single words, and it occurs in affirmation, negation and prohibition, and «لا» may be added before it for emphasis. «اللَّعْنُ» is driving away and remoteness; and of this is «شَأْوٌ لعين», i.e. a distant goal. Al-Shammākh said:
607 - ذَعَرْتُ به القَطا ونَفَيْتُ عنه ... مقامَ الذئبِ كالرَّجُلِ اللَّعينِ
(By it I startled the sandgrouse and drove from it the wolf's standing-place, like the outcast man.)
i.e. the distant one. The proper order of the speech would have been to say: «مقام الذئب اللعين كالرجل» ("the standing-place of the outcast wolf, like a man"). The bāʾ in «بكفرهم» is causal, and it is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «لَعَنَهُمْ». Al-Fārisī said: "It is intended to be fronted, i.e. 'and they said: our hearts are covered — because of their disbelief,' so that the bāʾ is attached to «قالوا» and «بل لعنهم» is a parenthetical clause." That is far-fetched. It may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the object in «لَعَنهم», i.e. He cursed them as disbelievers, meaning while they were clothed in disbelief, as in His saying: {وَقَدْ دَّخَلُواْ بالكفر} [al-Māʾida: 61].
His saying: {فَقَلِيلاً مَّا يُؤْمِنُونَ}: there are six views regarding the accusative of «قليلاً». The first, and it is the most apparent: that it is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "so with little belief they believe." The second: that it is a ḥāl from the pronoun of that omitted maṣdar, i.e. "so they believe it — i.e. the belief — in the state of its being little"; it has preceded that this is the doctrine of Sībawayh, and its exposition has preceded. The third: that it is an adjective of an omitted time, i.e. "so for a little time they believe," which is like His saying: {آمِنُواْ بالذي أُنْزِلَ عَلَى الذين آمَنُواْ وَجْهَ النهار واكفروا آخِرَهُ} [Āl ʿImrān: 72]. The fourth: that it is by removal of the preposition, the underlying form being «فبقليل يؤمنون» ("so in a little they believe"); when the preposition was omitted it became accusative. This is attributed to Abū ʿUbayda.
The fifth: that it is a ḥāl from the fāʿil (agent) of «يؤمنون», i.e. "so as a small group they believe," meaning the believer among them is few. Ibn ʿAbbās and Qatāda said something with this meaning. However, al-Mahdawī said: "Qatāda held that the meaning is: 'few of them are those who believe,' and the grammarians rejected it, saying: if it were so, «قليل» would have to be nominative." I say: the nominative is not required when holding the meaning Qatāda held, because of what preceded, namely that its being accusative as a ḥāl fulfils this meaning. On all these views «ما» is redundant (zāʾida) for emphasis. The sixth: that «ما» is negating, i.e. "so they do not believe, either little or much." Like it are: {قَلِيلاً مَّا تَشْكُرُونَ} [al-Aʿrāf: 10] and {قَلِيلاً مَّا تَذَكَّرُونَ} [al-Aʿrāf: 3]. This is strong in terms of meaning, and it is somewhat weak only in respect of what is in its domain being fronted before it; Abū al-Baqāʾ said this, and Ibn al-Anbārī held it. However, the Basrans did not allow fronting what is in its domain before it, while the Kufans allowed it. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "«ما» may not be maṣdariyya, because «قليلاً» would remain without anything to make it accusative." He means that if you make it maṣdariyya, what follows it is its ṣila, and the maṣdar is nominative by «قليلاً» as its fāʿil — so where is what makes it accusative? This is unlike His saying {كَانُواْ قَلِيلاً مِّن الليل مَا يَهْجَعُونَ} [al-Dhāriyāt: 17], for «ما» there may be maṣdariyya, because «قليلاً» is accusative by «كان». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Littleness may mean non-existence." The Shaykh said: "What he held — that «قليلاً» is meant as negation — is correct, but in other than this construction, I mean His saying, Exalted is He: {فَقَلِيلاً مَّا يُؤْمِنُونَ}, because «قليلاً» is made accusative by an affirmative verb, so it is parallel to «قُمْتُ قليلاً», i.e. «قمتُ قياماً قليلاً» ('I stood a little standing'). No one would hold that when you bring an affirmative verb and make «قليلاً» accusative as an adjective of that verb's maṣdar, the meaning — in the affirmative occurring with a certain quality or manner — is the complete negation of that affirmed [action] and its not occurring at all. What the grammarians transmitted is only that pure negation may be meant by littleness in their saying: «أقَلُّ رجلٍ يقول ذلك» and «قَلَّما يقوم زيد». Once this is established, construing littleness as pure negation here is not correct." End quote. I say: what Abū al-Qāsim al-Zamakhsharī, may Allah have mercy on him, said — that the meaning of littleness here is negation — was held by al-Wāḥidī before him, for he said: "i.e. neither little nor much, as you say: «قَلَّما يفعلُ كذا», i.e. he does not do it at all."

semin-durr:40-40.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {يَابَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ} … «بني» is the one addressed in the vocative (munādā), and the sign of its accusative is the yāʾ, because it is a sound masculine plural; its nūn was dropped because of the annexation. It resembles a broken plural because its singular changes; for that reason the Arabs treated it in some respects as a broken plural, attaching the feminine tāʾ to the verb predicated of it, as in: قالت بنو فلان (the sons of so-and-so said). The poet said:
400 - قالَتْ بنو عامِرٍ خالُوا بني أَسَدٍ ... يا بؤسَ للجهلِ ضَرَّاراً لأقوامِ
(Banū ʿĀmir said: "Break off with Banū Asad!" — O the misery of ignorance, harmful to peoples!)
They also declined it with vowels, joining [it] to the broken plural. The poet said:
401 - وكان لنا أبو حسنٍ عليٌّ ... أباً بَرًّا ونحنَ له بنينُ
(Abū Ḥasan ʿAlī was to us a kind father, and we were sons to him.)
with a ḍamma on the nūn. Is its final radical yāʾ, because it is derived from building (al-bināʾ), since the son is a branch of the father and built upon him; or wāw, because of their saying al-bunuwwa (sonship), like al-ubuwwa and al-ukhuwwa? Two views; the correct one is the first. As for al-bunuwwa, there is no indication in it, because they have said al-futuwwa, and there is no disagreement that it has a yāʾ root. However, al-Akhfash preferred the second on the ground that dropping a wāw is more common. Its pattern is disputed: it has been said banaya, with fatḥa on the middle radical, and it has been said banya, with it quiescent. It has preceded that it is one of the ten nouns whose first radical was made quiescent and whose final radical was compensated by the connecting hamza.
Isrāʾīl: genitive by annexation; it is a diptote because of being a proper name and foreign. It is compounded by annexation like ʿAbd Allāh, for «إسْرا» is "servant" in their language and «إيل» is Allah the Exalted. It has also been said: «إسْرا» is derived from al-asr, which is strength, so its meaning would be: the one whom Allah strengthened. It has also been said: because he journeyed by night (usriya bi-l-layl) emigrating to Allah the Exalted.
