And it has been said: because he captured (asara) a jinnī who used to extinguish the lamp of Jerusalem (Bayt al-Maqdis). One of them said: on this view part of the name would be Arabic and part foreign. The Arabs have handled it in many dialectal forms, the most eloquent of which is the form of the Quran, which is the reading of the majority. Abū Jaʿfar and al-Aʿmash read «إسْرايِل» with yāʾ after the alif without hamza. It has been narrated from Warsh: إسْرائِل with hamza after the alif and without yāʾ; and اسْرَأَلَ with a hamza with fatḥa between the rāʾ and the lām; [and اسْرَئِل with a hamza with kasra between the rāʾ and the lām]; and إسْرال with a pure alif between the rāʾ and the lām. The poet said:
402 - لا أرى مَنْ يُعْينُني في حياتي ... غيرَ نفسي إلا بني إسْرالِ
(I see no one who helps me in my life except myself — save the Children of Isrāl.)
It is also narrated as a reading from Nāfiʿ. And «إسرائِين»: they substituted nūn for the lām, as in uṣaylān for uṣaylāl. He said:
403 - قالَتْ وكنتُ رجلاً فَطِينا ... هذا وربِّ البيتِ إسرائينا
(She said — and I was a perceptive man — "This, by the Lord of the House, is an Isrāʾīn!")
It is pluralized as «أَساريل». The Kufans permitted أَسارِلَة and أسارِل, as though they permit compensation and its absence, as in فَرازِنة and فرازين. Al-Ṣaffār said: "We know of no one who permits dropping the hamza from its beginning."
His saying: {اذكروا نِعْمَتِيَ}: اذكروا is a verb and its agent, and نعمتي is the object. Ibn al-Anbārī said: "An omitted muḍāf must be supposed, its implied form being: thanks for My favour." Al-dhikr and al-dhukr, with kasra and ḍamma on the dhāl, have one meaning, and both may be with the tongue and with the heart. Al-Kisāʾī said: "With kasra it is for the tongue and with ḍamma for the heart." So the opposite of the one with kasra is silence, and the opposite of the one with ḍamma is forgetfulness. In sum, the remembrance whose seat is the heart has forgetfulness as its opposite, and that whose seat is the tongue has silence as its opposite, whether the two are said to have one meaning or not.
Al-niʿma is a noun for that with which favour is bestowed; it resembles fiʿl in the sense of mafʿūl, like dhibḥ (what is slaughtered) and riʿy (pasture). What is meant by it is the plural, because it is a generic noun; the Exalted said: {وَإِن تَعُدُّواْ نِعْمَتَ الله لاَ تُحْصُوهَا} [Ibrāhīm: 34]. {التي أَنْعَمْتُ} is its adjective, and the referring pronoun is omitted. If it is said: one of the conditions for omitting the relative's referring pronoun when it is in the genitive is that the relative be put in the genitive by the same preposition and that what both are attached to be the same, and here both conditions are lacking, since the origin is "which I bestowed with it" (التي أنعمتُ بها) — the answer is that it was omitted only after becoming accusative by the dropping of the preposition by extension, leaving أنعمتُها; it parallels {كالذي خاضوا} [al-Tawba: 69] on one of the aspects, and its precise treatment will come, if Allah the Exalted wills.
«عليكُمْ» is attached to it, and «على» was used to indicate the favour's encompassing them.
His saying: {وَأَوْفُواْ بعهدي}: this is an imperative clause conjoined to the imperative clause before it. One says: أَوْفَى, وَفَى and وَفَّى with and without doubling — three dialectal forms with one meaning. The poet said:
404 - أمَّا ابنُ طَوْقٍ فقد أَوْفَى بذِمَّتِه ... كما وَفَى بقِلاصِ النَّجْمِ حادِيها
(As for Ibn Ṭawq, he fulfilled his pledge, as the driver of the young she-camels of the Pleiades fulfils [his].)
So he combined two of the forms. One says: أَوْفَيْتُ and وفَيْتُ بالعهدِ (I fulfilled the covenant), and أَوْفَيت الكيلَ (I gave full measure), only with this form. It is reported from someone that the three forms occur in the Quran. As for «أَوْفى», as in this verse; as for «وفَّى» with doubling, as in His saying: {وَإِبْرَاهِيمَ الذي وفى} [al-Najm: 37]; as for «وَفَى» without doubling, it is not stated explicitly but is inferred from His saying, Exalted is He: {وَمَنْ أوفى بِعَهْدِهِ مِنَ الله} [al-Tawba: 111], because the elative afʿal is formed only from the triliteral, like the verb of wonder — this is the well-known view, even though there is much discussion in the question. It is related that the one who deduced that was Abū al-Qāsim al-Shāṭibī. «أَوْفَى» also comes in the sense of "rose up"; he said:
405 - رُبَّمَا أَوْفَيْتُ في عَلَمٍ ... تَرْفَعَنْ ثوبي شَمالاتُ
(Often I have climbed up on a high peak, the north winds lifting up my garment.)
«بعهدي» is attached to «أَوْفُوا». Al-ʿahd is a maṣdar (verbal noun), and it may be annexed to the agent or to the object. The meaning is: "what I covenanted with you, namely accepting obedience" — like {أَلَمْ أَعْهَدْ إِلَيْكُمْ يابني آدَمَ} [Yā Sīn: 60] — or "what you covenanted with Me", like {وَمَنْ أوفى بِمَا عَاهَدَ عَلَيْهِ الله} [al-Fatḥ: 10] and {صَدَقُواْ مَا عَاهَدُواْ الله عَلَيْهِ} [al-Aḥzāb: 23].
His saying: «أُوْفِ» is jussive as the answer to the imperative. Is what puts it in the jussive the request clause itself, because of the sense of condition it contains, or an implied conditional particle, its implied form being "if you fulfil My covenant, I shall fulfil"? Two views. This disagreement applies to everything put in the jussive in answer to a request.
«بعَهْدِكم» is attached to it, and it may be annexed to the agent or to the object, as has preceded.
His saying: {وَإِيَّايَ فارهبون}: «إيَّاي» is a detached accusative pronoun; what concerns it is known from al-Fātiḥa. It is accusative by an omitted verb which the overt verb after it explains, the implied form being: "and Me fear, so fear Me" (وإياي ارهبوا فارهبون). I have supposed it as coming after it only because supposing it before it is not good, given that the pronoun is detached — even though some have supposed it so. Regarding the fāʾ in «فارهبون» the grammarians have two views. The first: that it is the answer to an implied imperative, its implied form being "be alert, and fear Me" (تَنَبَّهوا فارهبون). It parallels their saying «زيداً فاضرب», i.e. "be alert and strike Zayd"; then تَنَبَّه was omitted, leaving فاضْرِب زيداً; then the object was put first to set the wording right, so that the fāʾ would not stand at the start. The fāʾ entered only to link these two clauses.
The second view about this fāʾ: that it is redundant (zāʾida). The Shaykh [Translator's note: i.e. Abū Ḥayyān, the author's teacher] said, after relating the first view: "The verse thus admits two aspects. The first: that the implied form is 'and Me fear; be alert, and fear Me' (وإياي ارهبوا تنبَّهُوا فارهبون), so that the fāʾ entered the answer to the imperative and is not displaced from an earlier position. The second aspect: that the implied form is 'and be alert, and fear Me' (وتنبَّهوا فارهبون); then the object was put first and became detached, and the fāʾ was brought when the object was put first; and the imperative verb, namely تنبَّهوا, is omitted, so that by its omission the wāw and the fāʾ met." He means that the implied form became وفإياي ارهَبُوا; then the object was put before the fāʾ to set the wording right, giving وإيَّاي فارهبوا; then the object was repeated by way of emphasis and to complete the verse-ending (fāṣila). On this view «فإيَّاي» is accusative by what follows it, not by an omitted verb; and emphasizing a detached pronoun by an attached one is not far-fetched, just as emphasizing an attached pronoun by a detached one is not prevented. This is questionable.
Al-rahab, al-rahb and al-rahba: fear, taken from al-rahāba, which is a bone in the chest which fear affects.

semin-durr:133-133.t:
His saying: {أَمْ}: Concerning this «أم» there are three views. The first — and it is the well-known one —: that it is disjunctive (munqaṭiʿa), and the disjunctive one is construed as «بل» plus the interrogative hamza, while some construe it as «بل» alone. The meaning of iḍrāb (digression) is a transition from one thing to another, not a cancellation of it; and the meaning of the interrogative is disapproval and rebuke, so its meaning comes down to negation, i.e.: rather, were you witnesses? meaning: you were not. The second: that it is in the sense of the interrogative hamza, and this is the view of Ibn ʿAṭiyya and al-Ṭabarī, except that the two differed about its place: Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "«أم» being in the sense of the interrogative alif at the head of speech is a Yemeni dialect", while al-Ṭabarī said: "«أم» is used to ask a question in the middle of speech whose beginning has preceded". The Shaykh said of Ibn ʿAṭiyya's view: "I have not come across any of the grammarians stating what he said", and he said of al-Ṭabarī's view: "This too is a strange view". The third: that it is conjunctive (muttaṣila), and this is the view of al-Zamakhsharī. Al-Zamakhsharī, after making it disjunctive and making the address to the believers, said after that: "And it has been said that the address is to the Jews, because they used to say: No prophet died except upon Judaism. However, had they witnessed him and heard what he said to his sons and what they said, his eagerness for the religion of Islam would have become evident to them and they would not have claimed Judaism for him. So the verse contradicts their claim; how then could it be said to them: Or were you witnesses? Rather, the [correct] aspect is that «أم» be conjunctive, on the assumption that something omitted is implied before it, as though it were said: Do you claim Judaism for the prophets, or were you witnesses? — meaning that your forebears among the Children of Israel were witnesses of him when he wanted his sons to hold to monotheism and the religion of Islam. So what is the matter with you that you claim for the prophets that of which they are innocent?"

The Shaykh said: "I do not know anyone who permitted the omission of this clause; it is not preserved in poetry or elsewhere. Were you to say «أم زيدٌ» meaning «أقام عمروٌ أم زيدٌ» ("Did ʿAmr stand or Zayd?"), it would not be permissible. The omission of the conjoined-to element is permissible only with the wāw and the fāʾ when some evidence indicates it, as in your saying «بلى وعمراً» ("Yes, and ʿAmr") to someone who said: He did not strike Zayd; and His saying, Exalted is He: {فانفجرت} [al-Baqara: 60], i.e.: so he struck, and it gushed forth. Its omission is rare with «أو», as in his saying:
732 - فَهل لكَ أو مِنْ والدٍ لَكَ قبلنا ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Have you, or any father of yours, before us …)
i.e.: of a brother or a father; and with «حتى», as in his saying:
733 - فواعَجَباً حتى كُلَيْبٌ تَسُبُّني ... كأن أباها نَهْشَلٌ أو مجاشِعُ
(How strange! Even Kulayb insults me, as though its father were Nahshal or Mujāshiʿ.)
i.e.: people insult me, even Kulayb — though there is some reservation about it. What is permissible is only the omission of «أم» together with what it conjoins, as in his saying:
734 - دعاني إليها القلبُ إني لأَمرِهِ ... سميعٌ فما أدري أَرُشْدٌ طِلابُها
(My heart called me to her — and I heed its command — yet I do not know whether seeking her is right guidance.)
i.e.: or error. That was permissible only because what is asked about in the affirmative includes its opposite, and it is permissible to omit the second, contrasting elements when the meaning indicates them. Do you not see His saying {تَقِيكُمُ الحر} [al-Naḥl: 81], how He omitted «والبردَ» ("and the cold")?" End quote. And «شهداء» is the khabar of «كان», and it is the plural of shāhid or shahīd; this has preceded at the beginning of the sūra.

His saying: {إِذْ حَضَرَ}: «إذ» is accusative by «شهداءَ», as an adverb (ẓarf), not as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e.: witnesses at the time of death's coming to him. And the coming of death is a metonymy for the coming of its causes and preliminaries. The poet said:
735 - وقلْ لهمْ بادِروا بالعُذْرِ والتمِسوا ... قولاً يُبَرِّئُكُم إني أنا الموتُ
(And say to them: Hasten with your excuse and seek a word that will acquit you — I am death.)
i.e.: I am its cause. The well-known reading has «يعقوب» accusative and «الموت» nominative; He put the object first out of concern for it. Some read it the other way round. And «حَضِر» was read with kasra on the ḍād; they said: and the imperfect «يَحْضُر» with ḍamma is anomalous, as if it were from the overlapping [of dialects]; it has preceded.

His saying: {إِذْ قَالَ}: This «إذ» has two views. The first: it is a badal (substitute) from the first, and the governing word in it is either the governing word of the first «إذ», if we say that the badal is not on the intention of repeating the governor, or an implied governor if we say that. The second: that it is an adverb (ẓarf) for «حَضَر».

His saying: {مَا تَعْبُدُونَ}?: «ما» is an interrogative noun in the position of accusative, because it is an object placed first, of «تعبدون»; and it must come first because it has the right to the head of the sentence. He used «ما» rather than «مَنْ» for one of four reasons. The first: that «ما» is for that whose matter is vague; once it is known, a distinction is made between «ما» and «مَنْ». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "And sufficient for you as evidence is the scholars' saying: «مَنْ» is for what is rational". The second: that it is a question about the attribute of the one worshipped. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "As you say: What is Zayd? meaning: Is he a jurist or a physician or some other attribute?" The third: that the objects of worship at that time were non-rational beings, like idols and images, the sun and the moon, so he asked with «ما», which is for the non-rational, and his sons knew what he meant and answered him with the truth. The fourth: that he was testing and examining them, so he asked them with «ما» rather than «مَنْ», lest the way to guidance be opened for them so that it would be like prompting them, while his aim was the test. And His saying «مِنْ بعدي» means: after my death.

His saying: {وإله آبَائِكَ}: He repeated the mention of «إله» so as not to conjoin to the genitive pronoun without repeating the preposition. The majority read «آبائِك», while al-Ḥasan, Yaḥyā and Abū Rajāʾ read «أبيك», and Ubayy read «وإلَه إبراهيم», dropping «آبائك». As for the reading of the majority, it is clear. In «إبراهيم» and what follows it there are then three aspects. The first: that it is a badal (substitute). The second: that it is ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition), and the meaning of the substitution in it is detailing. The third: that it is accusative by an implied «أعني» ("I mean"); the fatḥa on this view is the sign of the accusative, while on the two preceding views it is the sign of the genitive because of its being diptote. In it there is evidence for calling a grandfather and an uncle "father", for Abraham was his grandfather and Ishmael his uncle, just as "father" is applied to a maternal aunt; and from this is {وَرَفَعَ أَبَوَيْهِ} [Yūsuf: 100], on one of the two views. One of them said: "This is a case of taghlīb (giving predominance), meaning that he gave the father predominance over others". But there is some reservation about this, for this usage has come where there is neither a dual nor a plural in which predominance could be given; he, peace be upon him, said: "Return my father to me", meaning al-ʿAbbās.

As for the reading «أَبيك», it admits two aspects. The first: that it is a singular, not a plural. Then either it stands in the place of the plural or not. If it stands in the place of the plural, the discussion of «إبراهيم» and what follows it is like the discussion of it on the well-known reading. If it does not stand in its place, but rather the singular is intended in wording and meaning, then «إبراهيم» alone is on the three preceding aspects, and «إسماعيل» and what follows it are conjoined to «أبيك», i.e.: and the God of Ishmael. The second: that it is a sound plural with yāʾ and nūn, the nūn having been elided for the iḍāfa (genitive construct). The plural of «أب» has come as «أَبُون» in the nominative and «أبِين» in the genitive and accusative; Sībawayh reported it. The poet said:
736 - فلمَّا تَبَيَّنَّ أصواتَنا ... بَكَيْنَ وفَدَّيْنَنَا بالأِبِينا
(When they made out our voices, they wept and ransomed us with their fathers.)
And similar to it:
737 - فَقُلْنا أَسْلِموا إنَّا أَبُوكمْ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(So we said: Submit, for we are your fathers …)
And the discussion of «إبراهيم» and what follows it is like the discussion of it after the broken plural. Isḥāq (Isaac) is a foreign proper name; it can also be the maṣdar of «أَسْحق» «[Translator's note: the source text reads «أًسْحق» with a stray tanwīn mark; the verb meant is أسحق, "to become worn out".]», so if a male were named with it [in that sense] it would be declinable; the plural is asāḥiqa and asāḥīq.

His saying: {إلها وَاحِداً} has three aspects. The first: that it is a badal (substitute) from «إلهك», the substitution of a described indefinite noun from a definite one, as in His saying: {بالناصية نَاصِيَةٍ [كَاذِبَةٍ]} [al-ʿAlaq: 15] «[Translator's note: the verse is al-ʿAlaq 15–16.]». The Basrans do not stipulate the description, adducing as evidence his saying:
738 - فلا وأبيك خيرٍ منك ... إنِّي لَيُؤْذِيني التَّحَمْحُمُ والصَّهيلُ
(No, by your father — better than you! — the neighing and whinnying do trouble me.)
So «خيرٍ» is a badal from «أبيك», and it is an indefinite noun that is not described. The second: that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «إلهك», the governing word in it being «نعبدُ». The benefit of the badal and of the ḥāl is to state explicitly that the one they worship is single, since the annexation of a thing to many suggests a multiplicity of the annexed; so He made it explicit, negating that ambiguity. This ḥāl is called a "preparatory ḥāl" (ḥāl muwaṭṭiʾa), which is one in which you mention an entity that is described, as in: "Zayd came, a righteous man". The third — and al-Zamakhsharī inclined to it —: that it is accusative by way of specification (al-ikhtiṣāṣ), i.e.: by "your God" we mean one God. The Shaykh said: "The grammarians have stated explicitly that what is accusative by way of ikhtiṣāṣ is neither indefinite nor vague."

His saying: {وَنَحْنُ لَهُ مُسْلِمُونَ}: In this clause there are three aspects. The first: that it is conjoined to His saying «نعبد», meaning that it is the completion of their answer to him; so they answered him with something additional. The second: that it is a ḥāl from the agent of «نَعْبُدُ», the governing word being «نَعْبُد». The third — and al-Zamakhsharī inclined to it —: that it has no grammatical position, but rather is a parenthetical, emphasising clause, i.e.: and part of our state is that we are sincere to Him. The Shaykh said: "The grammarians have stated explicitly that a parenthetical clause is one which gives strength to the judgement, [coming] either between the two parts of a ṣila (relative clause) and its relative noun, as in his saying:
739 - ماذا - ولا عُتْبَ في المقدورِ - رُمْتَ أما ... يَكْفِيك بالنَّجْحِ أَمْ خُسْرٌ وتَضْلِيل
(What — and there is no blame for what is decreed — did you seek? Is it not enough for you, whether success or loss and going astray?)
and his saying:
740 - ذاكَ الذي - وأبيك - يَعْرِفُ مالكاً ... والحقُّ يَدْفَعُ تُرَّهَاتِ الباطِلِ
(That is the one who — by your father — knows Mālik; and truth repels the trifles of falsehood.)
or between the predicate and the subject of predication, as in his saying:
741 - وقد أَدْرَكَتْني - والحوادِثُ جَمَّةٌ ... أَسِنَّةُ قومٍ لا ضِعافٍ ولا عُزْلِ
(The spearheads of a people neither weak nor unarmed reached me — and calamities are many.)
or between a condition and its consequence, or an oath and its answer — among things between which there is some necessary connection. This clause has before it speech that is independent of what follows it. It cannot be said that there is a necessary connection between the one pointed to and the report about him, because what precedes it is part of the speech of the sons of Jacob, and what follows it is the speech of Allah the Exalted, by which He informed about them; and a parenthetical clause comes only from the one uttering the two connected elements, to emphasise his own speech." End quote, abridged. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "«ونحنُ لَه مسلمون» is a mubtadaʾ and khabar, i.e.: thus we were and we are." The Shaykh said: "It appears from this that he made this clause conjoined to an omitted clause, and there is no need for that."

semin-durr:60-60.t:
The saying of the Exalted: {استسقى موسى لِقَوْمِهِ}: the sīn is for requesting, by way of supplication, i.e. he asked for water (al-suqyā) for them. The alif of استسقى is changed from a yāʾ, because it is from al-saqy. The meaning of istafʿala has preceded in full at the beginning of the sūra. One says سَقَيْتُه and أَسْقَيْتُه with the same meaning, and [this] was recited:
491 - سَقَى قومي بني بكر وأَسْقَى ... نُمَيْراً والقبائلَ من هِلالِ
(May He give drink to my people, Banū Bakr, and give drink to Numayr and the tribes of Hilāl.)
It has been said: سَقَيْتُه means "I gave him what he drinks", and أَسْقَيْته "I made that available to him to take as he pleases"; on this [view] isqāʾ is more intensive than saqy. It has also been said: أَسْقَيْته means "I guided him to water". This will come, if Allah the Exalted wills, at His saying: {نُّسْقِيكُمْ مِّمَّا فِي بُطُونِهِ} [al-Naḥl: 66].
«لقومِه» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb, and the lām is for cause, i.e. "for the sake of"; or it is for clarification, since what is meant by it is supplication, like the one in their saying «سُقْياً لك» ("may you be watered"), so it is attached to something omitted, like its counterpart.
His saying: {اضرب بِّعَصَاكَ}: the assimilation [here] is obligatory, because whenever two identical [letters] come together in two words or one word, the first of them being quiescent, assimilation is obligatory, as in اضربْ بكرا ("strike Bakr"). The alif of «عصاك» is changed from a wāw, because of their saying in the relative adjective ʿaṣawī, and in the dual ʿaṣawān. [The poet] said:
492 - . . . . . . . . . . . ... على عَصَوَيْها سابِرِيٌّ مُشَبْرَقُ
(…on its two sticks a torn fine Sābirī garment.)
The plural is ʿiṣiyy and ʿuṣiyy, with ḍamma and with kasra on the ʿayn by assimilation [of vowels], and aʿṣin, like zaman and azmun; the original is ʿuṣuww and aʿṣuw, and it underwent weak-letter change. One says عَصَوْتُه بالعَصا ("I struck him with the stick") and عَصَيْتُه بالسيفِ ("I struck him with the sword"). «ألقى عصاه» ("he threw down his stick") expresses reaching one's abode. [The poet] said:
493 - فَأَلْقَتْ عَصاها واستقرَّ بها النَّوى ... كما قرَّ عَيْناً بالإِيابِ المسافِرُ
(So she threw down her stick, and her destination settled her, as the traveller is gladdened by his return.)
And انشقَّت العصا بين القومِ ("the stick split among the people"), i.e. disagreement arose. The poet said:
494 - إذا كانتِ الهيجاءُ وانشَقَّتِ العَصا ... فَحَسْبُك والضحاكُ سيفٌ مُهَنَّدُ
(When battle comes and the stick splits, then sufficient for you and al-Ḍaḥḥāk is an Indian sword.)
Al-Farrāʾ said: "The first solecism heard in Iraq was 'هذه عصاتي' ('this is my stick')", meaning with the tāʾ. «الحَجَرَ» is an object, and the al in it is for the known [referent] (ʿahd); it has also been said: for the genus.
His saying: {فانفجرت}: the fāʾ is a conjunction joining [it] to something omitted that must be supposed, its implied form being: "so he struck, and it gushed forth". Ibn ʿUṣfūr said: "This fāʾ that is present is the one that enters upon that omitted verb, and the fāʾ entering upon «انفجَرتْ» is omitted." It is as though he says: the first verb was omitted because the second indicates it, and the second fāʾ was omitted because the first indicates it. There is no need for that; rather it is said: a fāʾ and what it conjoins before it were omitted. Al-Zamakhsharī made it the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition. He said: "Or: so if you strike, it has gushed forth." He said: "On this [view] it is a fāʾ faṣīḥa (an eloquent fāʾ), which occurs only in eloquent speech." It seems that he intends an explanation of the meaning, not of the i'rab.
Al-infijār is splitting and opening; from it is al-fajr ("dawn"), because it splits with light. In al-Aʿrāf it is {فانبجست} [verse: 160]. It has been said: they have one meaning; it has also been said: al-inbijās is narrower, because it comes first and al-infijār second.
His saying: {اثنتا عَشْرَةَ عَيْناً} is the fāʿil (agent) of «انفجرت». The alif is the sign of the nominative, because it is treated like the dual, though it is not truly a dual since it has no singular from its own wording; likewise its masculine «اثنان». It is not annexed to a tamyīz (specification), since mentioning the counted thing in the dual makes it unnecessary: you say رجلان ("two men") and امرأتان ("two women"), and you do not say اثنا رجلٍ or اثنتا امرأةٍ, except for what has come rarely, on which no analogy is built. [The poet] said:
495 - كأنَّ خِصْيَيْهِ مِنَ التَّدَلْدُلِ ... ظَرْفُ عجوزٍ فيه ثِنْتا حَنْظَل
(As though his testicles, from their dangling, were an old woman's bag holding two colocynths.)
Thintān is like ithnatān. The rule for ithnān and ithnatān in compound numbers is that they are declined, unlike all their sisters. They said: this is because there has been omitted with them what is omitted in a declinable noun upon annexation, namely the nūn, so they resembled the declinable [noun] and were declined like the dual: with alif in the nominative and with yāʾ in the accusative and genitive. As for «عَشْرة», it is indeclinable (mabnī) because it is treated like the feminine tāʾ; it has many rules. «عَيْناً» is a tamyīz.
It has been read «عَشِرة» with a kasra on the shīn, and that is the dialect of Tamīm. Al-Naḥḥās said: "This is strange, for the dialect of Tamīm is ʿashira with kasra, though their way is lightening, and the dialect of the Ḥijāz is ʿashra with sukūn, though their way is making heavy." Al-Aʿmash read ʿasharah with a fatḥa. Al-ʿayn is a homonym shared by the human eye, the spring of water, the cloud, gold [coin], and the [tongue of the] balance; al-ʿayn is also rain lasting six or five [days]; al-ʿayn is the hole in a water-skin; and "a land with little ʿayn" means one with few people.
[His saying: {كُلُّ أُنَاسٍ}. The discussion that it is the origin of al-nās has preceded. Al-Zamakhsharī said in Sūrat al-Aʿrāf: it is a collective noun (ism jamʿ), not a broken plural. Then he said: "It is possible that the original was with kasra, and [it is] a broken plural, the ḍamma being a substitute for the kasra, as it was substituted for the fatḥa in sukārā." The precise investigation with him will come, if Allah the Exalted wills, in the sūra mentioned.]
His saying: {مَّشْرَبَهُمْ} is the object of «عَلِمَ» in the sense of "knew (recognized)". Al-mashrab here is the place of drinking, because it is narrated that each tribe had a spring out of the twelve springs which no other [tribe] shared with it. It has also been said: it is the drink itself, so it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) standing in the place of the direct object.
His saying: {كُلُواْ واشربوا}: these two clauses are in the position of the accusative governed by an implied "saying", its implied form being: "and We said to them: eat and drink". The morphology of «كل» and what has been omitted from it has preceded.
His saying: {مِن رِّزْقِ الله}: this is of the category of iʿmāl (rival governors), because each of the two verbs can properly govern it; it is a case of the second being made to govern, with omission from the first, the implied form being: "and eat of it". «مِنْ» may be for the beginning of the extent or partitive. The object of eating may also be omitted, and likewise the object of drinking, because they are indicated, the implied form being: "eat the manna and the quails" — since they were mentioned before in His saying {وَأَنزَلْنَا عَلَيْكُمُ المن والسلوى} [al-Baqara: 57] — "and drink the water of the springs that gushed forth". On this [view] the preposition and its genitive noun may be attached to the verb before it, or may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from that [omitted] object, and so attached to something omitted. It has also been said: what is meant by the provision is the water alone, and eating is ascribed to it because it is a cause of the growth and life of what is eaten, so it is a provision from which one eats and drinks. What is meant by al-rizq is what is provided (al-marzūq); it may be of the category of dhibḥ and riʿy [i.e. a fiʿl pattern with passive meaning], or of the category of «درهمٌ ضَرْبُ الأميرِ» ("a dirham, the striking of the emir", i.e. struck by him); the explanation of that has preceded.
His saying: {وَلاَ تَعْثَوْاْ فِي الأرض مُفْسِدِينَ}: the original of «تَعْثَوا» is taʿthayuwā. The ḍamma was found heavy on the yāʾ and was deleted; two quiescent letters then met, and the first of them, the yāʾ, was deleted. Or: since the yāʾ was vowelled and the letter before it had a fatḥa, it was changed into an alif; two quiescent letters met, the alif was deleted, and the fatḥa remained to indicate it. This is preferable. So its pattern is tafʿawn.
Al-ʿithiyy and al-ʿayth are the most severe corruption, and they are close [in meaning]. Some said: "Except that al-ʿayth is mostly said of what is perceived by the senses, and al-ʿithiyy of what is perceived by judgment." One says عَثَى يَعْثَى عِثِيَّاً, which is the usage of the Quran; and عثا يَعْثُو عُثُوّاً; and عاثَ يعيثُ عِثِيّاً. عاثَ is not a metathesis of عثى, like جَبَذَ and جَذَبَ, because their meanings differ, as preceded; though that is possible, each then being specialized for one kind. One also says عَثِيَ يعثى عِثِيّاً ومَعَاثاً. The original of عَثِي is not عَثِوَ with the wāw changed into yāʾ because of the kasra before it, like رَضِيَ from al-riḍwān, because al-ʿithiyy is established [as a form], even if some imagined that. And عَثَا is as preceded. One also says عَثَّ يَعُثُّ, doubled, i.e. "it decayed"; from it is al-ʿuththa, a moth that ruins wool. As for «عَتَا» with the dotted tāʾ, it is close to it in meaning, and its discussion will come.
«مُفْسدين» is a ḥāl from the agent of «تَعْثَوْا». It is an emphatic ḥāl (ḥāl muʾakkida), because its meaning is understood from its governing word; what made that good is the difference of the two words. Like it is {ثُمَّ وَلَّيْتُم مُّدْبِرِينَ} [al-Tawba: 25]. So they said. It may also be an explanatory ḥāl (ḥāl mubayyina), because corruption is more general and al-ʿithiyy more specific, as preceded. For this reason al-Zamakhsharī said: "So it was said to them: do not persist in corruption while you are corrupt, because they were persisting in it." So he distinguished between them, as you see.
{فِي الأرض} may be attached to «تَعْثَوْا», which is the apparent [view], or to «مفسدين».

semin-durr:171-171.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {وَمَثَلُ الذين كَفَرُواْ}: People have differed greatly over this verse and have been much at variance about it. With Allah's help I have summarised their views in an orderly form; and there is no way to know the i'rab except after knowing the meaning set forth in this verse.
They have differed over it: some said its meaning is that the parable is struck by likening the unbeliever to the one who shouts (al-nāʿiq). Some said it is struck by likening the unbeliever to the one shouted at (al-manʿūq bihi). Some said it is struck by likening the caller and the unbeliever to the one who shouts and the one shouted at. These are four views. «[Translator's note: only three views are listed here, although the text says "four"; the fourth — Sībawayh's view of a double ellipsis — is set out further below.]»
On the first view, the implied sense is: «And the likeness of those who disbelieve, in their little understanding, is as the likeness of herdsmen who speak to the beasts, while the beasts understand nothing». It has also been said that the implied sense is: And the likeness of those who disbelieve, in their calling upon their gods which do not understand their call, is as the likeness of one who shouts at his sheep and gains nothing from his shouting except that he is put to toil; likewise the unbeliever gets nothing from calling upon the gods except toil.
Al-Zamakhsharī said, having mentioned this view: «Except that His words {إِلاَّ دُعَآءً وَنِدَآءً} do not support it, because idols hear nothing». The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: «In this view al-Zamakhsharī had in mind a likening complete in every respect: just as the one shouted at hears nothing but a call and a cry, so too the one whom the unbeliever calls upon, i.e. the idol — yet the idol does not hear at all; hence this view was weak in his eyes». He said: «We say: the likening lies in calling as such, not in the particular features of the one called; so the unbeliever, in his calling upon the idol, is likened to the one who shouts at the beast, not in the particular features of the one shouted at».
It has also been said in connection with this view — I mean the view of those who say the implied sense is "And the likeness of those who disbelieve in their calling upon their gods" — that the one who shouts here is not meant to be one who shouts at beasts, but rather one who cries out in the hollow of a mountain and the echo answers him. The meaning then is: [like one who shouts] at that from which the shouter hears nothing but his own call and cry. On this view the fāʿil (agent) of «يسمع» is a pronoun referring back to the one who shouts (alladhī yanʿiqu), and the referent pronoun going back to «ما», which binds the ṣila (relative clause) to the relative noun, is omitted because the meaning is understood, its implied form being: "at that from which he hears nothing (bimā lā yasmaʿu minhu)". Yet the condition permitting such an omission is not present here, for it is governed by a preposition other than the one governing the relative noun, and moreover the things they attach to (mutaʿallaq) differ; nevertheless this has occurred in their speech. On the first two views, however, the fāʿil of «يَسْمَعُ» is a pronoun referring to the relative «ما», which is the one shouted at.
It has also been said: what is meant by "those who disbelieve" is those who are followed, not the followers; and the meaning is: the likeness of those who disbelieve in their calling upon their followers, and the fact that their followers gain nothing from them but disappointment, is as the likeness of one who shouts at sheep. On all these views «مثل» is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and «كمثلِ» its khabar (predicate), and there is nothing omitted in the speech except the point of comparison.
On the second of the four views mentioned above, it has been said that its meaning is: And the likeness of those who disbelieve, in being called to Allah the Exalted and their not hearing Him, is as the likeness of the beasts of the one who shouts. So it involves the omission of a qualification in the first part and the omission of a muḍāf in the second.
It has also been said that the implied sense is: And the likeness of those who disbelieve, in their not understanding from Allah and His Messenger, is as the likeness of the beasts that are shouted at, which understand nothing of command and prohibition except the sound. So "the one who shouts" is meant to be "the one shouted at", and this is a case of inversion (qalb). The one who held this said: it is as you say «the ring went into my hand and the boot into my foot». Al-Farrāʾ, Abū ʿUbayda and a group went to this interpretation; however, inversion, according to the correct view, occurs only under poetic necessity or rarely.
On the third view, the implied form is: And the likeness of the caller of those who disbelieve is as the likeness of one who shouts at his sheep, in that the unbeliever understands nothing of what his caller addresses to him except the hum of the voice, without bringing thought and mind to bear on it, just as the beast is likewise. So the speech involves the omission of a muḍāf from the first part. Al-Zamakhsharī «[Translator's note: the text misspells the name as «الزمشخري».]» said: «It is possible that by "that which hears nothing" is meant the one who is deaf and stone-deaf «[Translator's note: «الأصلج» as written; presumably «الأصلخ», "stone-deaf".]», who hears nothing of the speech of one who raises his voice in speaking except the cry and the sound, nothing else, without understanding the letters». This is an inclination on his part toward the permissibility of applying «ما» to rational beings; or, since such a person was treated as being on a level with the beasts that do not hear, he applied «ما» to him.
As for the fourth view — which is Sībawayh's choice in this verse — its implied form according to him is: «Your likeness, O Muḥammad, and the likeness of those who disbelieve is as the likeness of the one who shouts and the one shouted at». People differed in understanding Sībawayh's words: one said it is an explanation of meaning; it has also been said it is an explanation of i'rab. Then there are two omissions in the speech: an omission from the first part, namely the omission of «داعيهم» (their caller), whose counterpart is stated in the second; and an omission from the second part, namely the omission of "the one shouted at", whose counterpart is stated in the first. Thus He likened the caller of the unbelievers to the herdsman of sheep in his addressing those who do not understand him, and likened the unbelievers to the sheep in that they hear nothing of what they are called to except sounds whose meaning they do not know. In this interpretation there is much omission, since it involves the omission of two maʿṭūf (conjoined) elements, the technical implied form being: And the likeness of those who disbelieve and their caller is as the likeness of the one who shouts at that which is shouted at. A group went to this, among them Abū Bakr ibn Ṭāhir, Ibn Kharūf and al-Shalawbīn. They said: the Arabs consider this elegant, and it is among the marvels of their speech; and like it is His words: {وَأَدْخِلْ يَدَكَ فِي جَيْبِكَ تَخْرُجْ بَيْضَآءَ} [al-Naml: 12], its implied form being: "and put your hand into your bosom, it will go in; and take it out, it will come out"; so «تَدْخُلْ» was omitted because «تَخْرُجْ» indicates it, and «وَأَخْرِجْهَا» was omitted because «وَأَدْخِلْ» indicates it. They said: and like it is the poet's words:
812 - وإني لَتَعْروني لذاكراكِ فَتْرَةٌ ... كما انتَفَضَ العُصْفُورَ بَلَّلَهُ القَطْرُ
(And at the remembrance of you a languor comes over me, just as the sparrow shakes itself when the rain has wetted it.)
He did not mean to liken his languor to the sparrow's shaking itself when the rain has wetted it, because the two are opposites, being motion and stillness. Rather its implied sense is: when I remember you a trembling comes over me and then I grow languid, just as when the rain wets the sparrow a languor comes over it and then it shakes itself — except that the throbbing and agitation of his heart come before the languor, whereas the sparrow's languor comes before its shaking.
All of these views rest on the view that it is a likening of a single item to a single item, matching each part of the preceding speech with a part of the speech compared to. If, however, the likening is of the type of likening one whole statement to another, then no regard is paid to matching the individual words; rather regard is paid to the meaning. Abū al-Qāsim al-Rāghib inclined to this. Al-Rāghib said: «Since He likened the story of the unbelievers, in their turning away from the one calling them to the truth, to the story of the one who shouts, He mentioned the one who shouts first so that what proceeds from him and from the one shouted at might be built upon it».
The kāf is not redundant (zāʾida), contrary to some; because the one description is not identical with the other description, so the kāf is indispensable — so much so that if the speech had come without the kāf, we would believe it to be present by implication, to set the meaning right.
It emerges from the foregoing that «مثلُ الذين» is the mubtadaʾ and «كمثل الذي» its khabar: either without believing anything to be omitted; or with the omission of a muḍāf from the first part, i.e. "the likeness of the caller of those who"; or from the second, i.e. "as the likeness of the beasts of the one who"; or with two omissions: from the first was omitted that whose counterpart is stated in the second, and from the second that whose counterpart is stated in the first, as all this has been worked out above. This is the final word on this noble verse.
Al-naʿīq is the herdsman's calling and crying out to the sheep. The poet said:
813 - فانْعَقْ بضَأْنِك يا جريرُ فإنَّما ... مَنَّتْكَ نفسُك في الخَلاءِ ضَلالا
(So shout at your ewes, O Jarīr, for your soul has only beguiled you with error in the empty wilds.)
One says naʿaqa, with fatḥa on the ʿayn, yanʿiqu with kasra on it; the maṣdar (verbal noun) is al-naʿīq, al-nuʿāq and al-naʿq. As for «نَعَقَ الغرابُ» (the crow cawed), it is with the dotted letter [i.e. naghaqa]; it has also been said that it is with the undotted letter as well for the crow, but that is unusual.
His words: {إِلاَّ دُعَآءً}: this is an emptied exception (istithnāʾ mufarragh), because before it is «يَسْمَعُ», which has not taken its object. Some claimed that «إلاَّ» is redundant (zāʾida), so it is not an exception at all. This view is rejected, even though al-Aṣmaʿī held that «إلاَّ» is redundant in the poet's words:
814 - حَراجِيجُ لا تَنْفَكُّ إلا مُنَاخَةً ... على الخَسْفِ أو نَرْمِي بها بلدا قَفْرَا
(Lean, tall camels that never cease to be made to kneel in hardship, or else we hurl them at a desolate land.)
For people refuted him and did not accept his view. There is discussion of this verse that has preceded.
Some raised here a question concerning meaning, namely His words {لاَ يَسْمَعُ إِلاَّ دُعَآءً وَنِدَآءً}: what is heard is nothing but calling and crying, so how can He censure them for hearing nothing but calling — as if it were said "they hear nothing but what is heard", which is not admissible? The answer is that the speech is concise, and the meaning is only: they do not understand the meanings of what is said to them, just as beasts do not distinguish between the meanings of the words with which they are called, but understand only a little, which they have grasped through long practice and much repetition. It is as if it were said: they have nothing but the hearing of the call, without perceiving the meanings and purposes. This question is worthless from the outset, and had the Shaykh not mentioned it, I would not have mentioned it.
Here there is another question: is this a case of repetition with differing wording, since calling (duʿāʾ) and crying (nidāʾ) are one and the same? The answer is that it is not so, for duʿāʾ is the request for an action, and nidāʾ is the answering of the voice. ʿAlī ibn ʿĪsā mentioned this.

semin-durr:89-89.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {مِّنْ عِندِ الله} ...: there are two views on it. The first: that it is in the position of nominative (marfūʿ) as a naʿt (adjective) of «كتاب», so it is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted [word], i.e. "a book coming from Allah."
The second: that it is in the position of accusative (manṣūb), for the beginning of the extent of the coming; Abū al-Baqāʾ said this. The Shaykh rejected this view, saying: "It cannot be said that {مِّنْ عِندِ الله} may be attached to «جاءهم» and so not be an adjective, because of the separation between the adjective and the qualified noun by something governed by neither of them." He means that it is governed neither by the qualified noun nor by the adjective, so separating them by it is not tolerated.
The majority read «مُصَدِّقٌ» in the nominative as a second adjective. On this view it is said: there are two adjectives, one explicit and the other interpreted [i.e. a phrase], and the interpreted one has been put first; it has preceded that this is not impossible, even though some claimed it is permissible only by poetic necessity. What made fronting the non-explicit one good is that describing it as being from Allah is more emphatic, and that describing it as confirming arises from its being from Allah. Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «مُصَدِّقاً» in the accusative, and so it is in the codex of Ubayy. Its accusative is as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and there are two views about its possessor (ṣāḥib al-ḥāl). One of them is that it is «كتاب». If it is said: how has the ḥāl come from an indefinite noun? The answer is that it has come close to the definite because it is specified by the adjective, namely {مِّنْ عِندِ الله}, as preceded; besides which Sībawayh allowed its occurring from it without condition. Al-Zamakhsharī pointed to this view. The second: that it is the pronoun borne by the preposition and its genitive noun because it occurs as an adjective; the governor of it is either the adverbial phrase (ẓarf) or what it is attached to, according to the well-known disagreement. For this reason some objected to Sībawayh regarding his saying:
608 - لِمَيَّةَ موحِشاً طَلَلٌ ... يَلُوح كأنَّه خِلَلُ
(Mayya has a desolate ruin that gleams as though it were the ornamented scabbard-linings.)
that «موحشاً» is a ḥāl from «طَلَل», which was allowed because it is fronted; he said: there is no need for that, since it can be a ḥāl from the latent pronoun in his saying «لميَّةَ», which is the khabar (predicate) of «طلل». There is another place for answering that. The lām in {لِّمَا مَعَهُمْ} strengthens the transitivity of «مُصَدِّق», because it is a derivative [of the verb]. «ما» is a relative noun and the adverbial phrase is its ṣila (relative clause).
His saying: {وَكَانُواْ}: three views are permissible in it. The first: that it is conjoined to «جاءهم», so that the apodosis of «لَمَّا» is consequent upon both the coming and the being. The second: that it is a ḥāl, i.e. «وقد كانُوا» ("while they had been"), so that the apodosis of «لَمَّا» is consequent upon the coming with a restriction on its object, namely [Translator's note: the source has «وهم», read as «وهو»] their being ones who sought victory. The Shaykh said: "The apparent sense of al-Zamakhsharī's words is that «وكانوا» is neither conjoined to the verb after «لَمَّا» nor a ḥāl, because he supplied the apodosis of «لَمَّا» as omitted before explaining «يستفتحون»; this indicates that His saying «وكانوا» is a clause conjoined to the whole clause beginning with «ولَمَّا»." This is the third.
{مِن قَبْلُ} is attached to «يَسْتَفْتِحون»; the underlying form is «من قبلِ ذلك», and when it was cut off [from annexation] it was made indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma.
«يَسْتَفْتحون» is in the position of accusative as the khabar of «كان». The grammarians differed regarding the apodosis (jawāb) of the first and the second «لَمَّا». Al-Akhfash and al-Zajjāj held that the apodosis of the first is omitted, its implied form being: "and when a book came to them, they disbelieved in it." Al-Zamakhsharī supplied it as: "they belied it and made light of its coming," which is good. Al-Farrāʾ held that its apodosis is the fāʾ that enters upon «لَمَّا», and this for him is parallel to {فَإِمَّا يَأْتِيَنَّكُم مِّنِّي هُدًى فَمَن تَبِعَ هُدَايَ فَلاَ خَوْفٌ} [al-Baqara: 38]. He said: "The fāʾ cannot be conjunctive, since the wāw is not suitable in its place." «كفروا» is the apodosis of the second «لَمَّا» on both views. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "There are two views about the apodosis of the first «لَمَّا». The first: its apodosis is the second «لَمَّا» together with its apodosis. This is weak, because the fāʾ is with the second «لمَّا», and «لمَّا» is not answered with the fāʾ unless one believes the fāʾ to be redundant, according to what al-Akhfash allows." I say: even if al-Akhfash's view on the redundancy of the fāʾ were held in general, it is not possible here, because «لَمَّا» is not answered by its like; one does not say «لَمَّا جاء زيدٌ لَمَّا قَعَد أكرمتُك» with «لَمَّا قعد» as the apodosis of «لمَّا جاء». And Allah knows best.
Al-Mubarrad held that «كفروا» is the apodosis of the first «لَمَّا», and the second was repeated because of the length of the speech; this conveys the establishing and emphasising of the sin. It would be good, were it not that the fāʾ prevents it. Abū al-Baqāʾ said, after relating a first view: "The second: that «كفروا» is the apodosis of the first and the second, because what they require is one and the same. It was also said: the second is a repetition, so it needed no apodosis." I say: his saying "it was also said: the second is a repetition" is what I related from al-Mubarrad, and in reality it is not different from the view he mentioned before it, that «كفروا» is an apodosis for both; rather it is the same.
His saying: {فَلَعْنَةُ الله عَلَى الكافرين} is a clause of mubtadaʾ (subject) and [Translator's note: the source has «أو», read as «و»] khabar, resulting from what preceded. The maṣdar (verbal noun) here is annexed to its fāʿil (agent). He used «على» to draw attention to the fact that the curse has risen over them and encompassed them. He said {عَلَى الكافرين} and did not say «عليهم», putting the overt noun in place of the pronoun, to draw attention to the cause requiring that, namely disbelief.

semin-durr:74-74.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {أَوْ أَشَدُّ قَسْوَةً}: this «أو» is like the «أو» in His words {أَوْ كَصَيِّبٍ} [al-Baqara: 19], so everything said about it there may be said here. When Abū al-Aswad said:

551 - أُحِبُّ محمداً حُبَّاً شديداً ... وعَبَّاساً وحمزةَ أو عَلِيَّا
(I love Muḥammad with an intense love, and ʿAbbās, and Ḥamza, or ʿAlī.)

they objected to his use of «أو», which implies doubt, and said to him: "Are you in doubt?" He said: "Not at all", and cited as evidence the words of Allah the Exalted {وَإِنَّآ أَوْ إِيَّاكُمْ لعلى هُدًى أَوْ فِي ضَلاَلٍ} [Sabaʾ: 24], and said: "Was the One who informed of this in doubt?" He, may Allah have mercy on him, only intended to leave the matter vague for the addressee.

«أشدُّ» is nominative because it is conjoined to the position of «كالحجارة», i.e. "so they are like stones or harder". The kāf may be a particle, and so be attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted element, or a noun, and so not be attached to anything. It may also be the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "or they are harder". «قسوة» is accusative as a tamyīz (specification), because the vagueness arose in the attribution of the preference to it [i.e. to the hearts]. The thing over which preference is given is omitted because it is indicated, i.e. "harder than stones".

It has been read «أشدَّ» with fatḥa; the way to account for it is that it is conjoined to «الحجارة», i.e. "so they are like stones or like what is harder than them". Al-Zamakhsharī said, accounting for the nominative: "أشدُّ is conjoined to the kāf, either on the meaning 'or like what is harder', the muḍāf being omitted and the muḍāf ilayhi put in its place; and this is supported by the reading of al-Aʿmash with the dāl in the accusative, conjoined to الحجارة." On what he said, it is also possible that it is genitive by the omitted muḍāf, left in its state, like the reading {والله يُرِيدُ الآخرة} [al-Anfāl: 67] with الآخرة in the genitive, i.e. "the reward of the Hereafter". The outcome of this is that the fatḥa of the dāl may be either accusative or genitive [the diptote genitive].

Al-Zamakhsharī also said: "If you say: why was it said «أشدُّ قسوةً», when the verb of hardness is one from which the elative of preference and the verb of wonder can be formed?" — meaning that it fulfils the conditions: being triliteral, complete, not of colour or defect, inflected, and not bound to negation. Then he said: "I say: because it is clearer and more indicative of the excess of hardness. And there is another aspect: He does not intend the meaning of 'harder' (الأقسى); rather He intended to describe the hardness as intense, as though it were said: 'the hardness of stones has become intense, and their hearts are more intense in hardness'." This is a very fine statement, except that [the claim] that the verb of wonder may be formed from القسوة is questionable, since it is among innate qualities or among defects, and both of these bar the formation of the two patterns. It has also been read: قَساوة.

His words: {لَمَا يَتَفَجَّرُ مِنْهُ}: the lām is the lām of commencement (lām al-ibtidāʾ) entering the noun of «إنَّ», because the khabar, {مِنَ الحجارة}, comes first. ما is in the sense of الذي and in the position of the accusative. Had the khabar not come first, the lām could not enter the noun, lest two particles of emphasis follow one another, even though the original would require it. The pronoun in «منه» refers back to «ما», construed according to the form. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "Were it outside the Qurʾān, «منها» according to the meaning would be permissible." I say: this is what Ubayy ibn Kaʿb and al-Ḍaḥḥāk read.

Mālik ibn Dīnār read «يَنْفَجِرُ», from الانفجار. Qatāda read {وَإِنْ مِنَ الحجارة} with إنْ lightened from the heavy form, bringing the lām to distinguish it from negative «إنْ»; and likewise {وَإِنَّ مِنْهَا لَمَا يَشَّقَّقُ وَإِنَّ مِنْهَا لَمَا يَهْبِطُ}. In this reading «ما» may be in the position of the nominative, which is the well-known [view], or in the position of the accusative, because with lightened «إنْ» both governing and non-governing are heard. Allah the Exalted said {وَإِنَّ كُلاًّ لَّمَّا لَيُوَفِّيَنَّهُمْ} [Hūd: 111] in the reading of those who read it so, and in another place {وَإِن كُلٌّ لَّمَّا جَمِيعٌ} [Yā Sīn: 32]; but the well-known [usage] is non-governing.

{يَشَّقَّقُ}: its origin is يَتَشَقَّقُ, then assimilated; al-Aʿmash read with the original. Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif read «لَمَّا» with doubled mīm in both places; Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It is a reading without a sound justification." He also read «يَنْشَقُّ» with nūn; its fāʿil (agent) is the pronoun of «ما». Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "Its agent may be the pronoun of the water, because «يَشَّقَّقُ» may be assigned to the water according to the meaning; so you have two verbs, the second of which governs الماء, and the agent of the first is latent/ on condition of later explanation; according to the Kufans the first governs, so in the second there is a pronoun" — meaning that it belongs to the chapter of tanāzuʿ (two governors competing for one word). A resumptive pronoun must be omitted from «يَشَّقَّق» referring to relative «ما», indicated by His words «منه», the implied sense being: "and among the stones there is that from which the water cleaves, so the water comes out of it." He also said: "Had «تتفجَّر» been read with tāʾ, it would be permissible." I say: Abū Ḥātim said «لما تتفجَّر» with tāʾ is permissible because he made it feminine by the femininity of الأنهار, but this cannot be in تشَّقَّق — meaning the feminine. Al-Naḥḥās said: "What he rejected is permissible according to the meaning, because the meaning is: 'and among them there are stones that cleave'" — meaning that the meaning of «ما» is taken into account, since it refers to stones.

His words: {مِنْ خَشْيَةِ الله}: its position is accusative, attached to «يَهْبِط», and «مِنْ» is causal. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "[«مِنْ»] is in the position of the accusative by يهبط, as you say: يهبط بخشيةِ الله", so he made it in the sense of the transitivising bāʾ; this is obviously questionable. خشية is a maṣdar (verbal noun) annexed to its object, its implied form being: "from its fearing Allah".

Ascribing falling down to them [the stones] is a metaphor, as in his words:

552 - لَمَّا أَتى خبرُ الزُّبَيْرِ تواضَعَتْ ... سُورُ المدينةِ والجبالُ الخُشَّعُ
(When the news of al-Zubayr came, the wall of the city and the humbled mountains bowed low.)

It may also be literal, in the sense that Allah created in them a capacity for that. It is also said that the pronoun in «منها» refers to the hearts, but that is far-fetched because of the disharmony of the pronouns.

His words: {وَمَا الله بِغَافِلٍ}: this was discussed at His words {وَمَا هُم بِمُؤْمِنِينَ} [al-Baqara: 8], so let reference be made there.

His words: {عَمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ}: [attached to] بغافل. «ما» is a nominal relative, so a resumptive pronoun is needed, i.e. "[what] you do it"; or maṣdariyya, so none is needed, i.e. "of your doing". It may stand in the place of the object, and it may not. «يعملون» has been read with yāʾ and with tāʾ.

semin-durr:75-75.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {أَن يُؤْمِنُواْ لَكُمْ}: a subjunctive particle and a verb in the subjunctive (manṣūb); the sign of the subjunctive is the dropping of the nūn. The original is فِي أَنْ, so its position is accusative or genitive, as has been known more than once. «يؤمنوا» is made transitive with lām because it contains the sense of "that they bring about belief because of your call"; al-Zamakhsharī said this, and its verification has been given before.

His words: {وَقَدْ كَانَ}: the wāw is that of the ḥāl (circumstantial). Some said: "Its sign is that «إذ» can fit in its place." The implied sense is: "Do you hope for their belief, while they are liars, distorting the speech of Allah the Exalted?" «قد» brings the past near to the present, which allows it to occur as a ḥāl. «يَسْمَعُون» is the khabar (predicate) of كان, and «منهم» is in the position of the nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of فريق, i.e. "a party being of them". Some said: {يَسْمَعُونَ} is in the position of the nominative as an adjective of فريق, and «منهم» is in the position of the accusative as the khabar of كان; this is weak. الفريق is a collective noun (ism jamʿ) with no singular from its own root, like رهط and قوم. كان with what falls within its scope is in the position of the accusative, as said above.

It has been read {كَلِمَ الله}, which is a generic noun whose singular is كلمة. The grammarians distinguish between الكلام and الكَلِم: the condition of الكلام is that it convey a complete meaning, and the condition of الكَلِم is that it be composed of three or more [words], because it is plural in meaning and the minimum plural is three; so between them there is a relation of partial generality and particularity. The verification of this is mentioned in their books. Is الكلام a maṣdar (verbal noun) or a noun of the maṣdar? There is disagreement. The root indicates effect; from it comes الكَلْم, which is a wound, and speech affects the one addressed. He said:

553 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... وجُرْحُ اللسانِ كجُرْحِ اليَدِ
(… and the wound of the tongue is like the wound of the hand.)

In the language الكلام is also applied to writing and to gesture, as in his words:

554 - إذا كَلَّمَتْنِي بالعيونِ الفواتِرِ ... رَدَدْتُ عليها بالدموعِ البوادِرِ
(When she spoke to me with languid eyes, I answered her with hastening tears.)

and to inner [speech]. Al-Akhṭal said:

555 - إنَّ الكلامَ لفي الفؤادِ وإنما ... جُعِلَ اللسانُ على الفؤادِ دَلِيلا
(Speech is truly in the heart; the tongue has only been made a pointer to the heart.)

It is said that this verse has not been found in the dīwān of al-Akhṭal. As for the grammarians, it is applied only to an utterance that is composed and conveys a meaning by convention.

His words: {مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا عَقَلُوهُ}: attached to (mutaʿalliq) {يُحَرِّفُونَهُ}. التحريف is bending and turning aside. «ثم» is for delay, either in time or in rank. «ما» may be a nominal relative, i.e. "then they distort the speech after the meaning which they had understood and known". It may also be maṣdariyya, in which case the pronoun in «عَلَقوه» [Translator's note: so written in the source, for عَقَلوه] refers to the speech, i.e. "after their having understood it".

His words: {وَهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ}: a ḥāl clause. There are two views about what governs it. First: {عَقَلُوهُ}; but it follows from this that it would be an emphatic ḥāl, because its meaning has already been understood from «عَلَقوه» [Translator's note: i.e. عَقَلوه]. Second, which is the apparent one: يُحَرِّفونه, i.e. they distort it while knowing that.

semin-durr:76-76.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {وَإِذَا لَقُواْ} … the verse: its counterpart came at the beginning of the sūra, and the discussion of its individual words and its i'rab was given there, which makes repetition unnecessary.

This conditional clause admits two aspects. First: that it is resumptive, disclosing the states of the Jews and the hypocrites. Second: that it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), conjoined to the ḥāl clause before it, namely «وقد كان فريقٌ», the implied sense being: "How can you hope for their belief when their state is such-and-such?" Ibn al-Samayfaʿ read: لاقُوا, which has the meaning of لَقوا — فاعَل in the sense of فَعِل, as in سافر and طارَقْتُ النعل ("I stitched the sandal in layers").

His words: {بِمَا فَتَحَ الله}: attached to (mutaʿalliq) the [verb of] telling before it. ما is a relative noun in the sense of الذي, and the resumptive pronoun is omitted, i.e. "[what] Allah disclosed (فتحه)". Abū al-Baqāʾ permitted it to be an indefinite qualified by a description, or maṣdariyya, i.e. "a thing that He disclosed" — so the resumptive is omitted here too — or "by Allah's disclosing to you". Making it maṣdariyya is problematic, since the pronoun in His following words {لِيُحَآجُّوكُم بِهِ} refers to «ما» — this is the apparent [reading] — and maṣdariyya ما is a particle to which no pronoun refers, according to the well-known view, contrary to al-Akhfash and Abū Bakr ibn al-Sarrāj; unless one goes to the trouble of saying that the pronoun refers to the maṣdar understood from His words {أَتُحَدِّثُونَهُم} or from فتح, i.e. "so that they may argue against you by the telling with which you told them", or "by the disclosing which Allah disclosed to you".

The clause «أتُحَدِّثونهم» is in the position of the accusative governed by the verb "say". الفتح here means judgement and decree; it is also said that الفتّاح is "the judge" in the dialect of Yemen. It is also said: [it means] sending down. It is also said: informing/ or making clear, in the sense that He made clear to you the description of Muḥammad, upon him be peace; or bestowing favour, in the sense of the favour He bestowed on you by giving you victory over your enemy. All of these are views mentioned in tafsīr.

His words: {لِيُحَآجُّوكُم}: this lām is called the lām of kay, meaning that it is for causation just as «كي» is, not meaning that it puts what follows in the subjunctive by implying «كي», as will come. It is a preposition, and it enters the verb only because the verb is in the subjunctive by maṣdariyya أَنْ implied after it; with it the verb is interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "for the arguing", so it has entered only on a noun, though not an explicit one. The subjunctive is by implied أَنْ, as stated, not by كي, contrary to Ibn Kaysān and al-Sīrāfī, even though كي appears after it, as in the words of Allah the Exalted {لِّكَيْلاَ تَأْسَوْاْ} [al-Ḥadīd: 23], because «أَنْ» is the mother of the chapter, so claiming that it is implied is more fitting than claiming another. The Kufans said: "The subjunctive is by the lām itself, and the كي and أَنْ that appear after it are only by way of emphasis." The argumentation has a place in the books of grammar other than this.

أَنْ may be implied or made overt after this lām, except in one case, namely where «لا» comes after it, as in His words {لِّئَلاَّ يَعْلَمَ} [al-Ḥadīd: 29] and {لِئَلاَّ يَكُونَ لِلنَّاسِ} [al-Baqara: 150]; that is because of the succession of two lāms that would result, making the utterance heavy. The well-known usage in the language of the Arabs is to give this lām kasra, because it is a preposition; there is a rare, anomalous dialect with fatḥa.

This lām is attached to His words «أَتُحَدِّثُونهم». Some held that it is attached to «فَتَحَ», but that is not apparent, because the arguing is not the cause of the disclosing; it arose only from the telling — unless it be said that it is attached to it as the lām of consequence (lām al-ʿāqiba), which is a view that has been held, so that the meaning becomes: the consequence and outcome of the disclosing was that they argued against you. Or you say: the lām is the lām of cause in its proper sense, and it is attached to فتح only because that is a cause of the telling, and cause and effect are one in this.

His words: «به»: the pronoun refers to «ما» in His words {بِمَا فَتَحَ الله}. It was said above that the view that it is maṣdariyya is weak, and that it may refer to one of the two maṣdars understood from «أَتُحَدِّثُونهم» and «فتح».

His words: {عِنْدَ رَبِّكُمْ}: an adverb governed by His words {لِيُحَآجُّوكُم}, meaning "so that they may argue against you on the Day of Resurrection", which is alluded to by His words {عِنْدَ رَبِّكُمْ}. It is also said that «عند» is in the sense of في, i.e. "so that they may argue against you concerning your Lord", i.e. and so be more entitled to Him than you. It is also said that there is an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "at the mention of your Lord". It is also said that it is governed by His words {بِمَا فَتَحَ الله}, i.e. "by what Allah disclosed from your Lord, so that they may argue against you" — namely the description of him, upon him be peace, and the taking of their covenant to believe in him. Some preferred this and said: "It is the correct one, because the argument against them is by what was in this world." This is questionable from the standpoint of grammatical technique, for {لِيُحَآجُّوكُم} is attached to His words {أَتُحَدِّثُونَهُم} on the most apparent view, as stated, so it would follow that it separates the governor, فتح, from what it governs, عند ربك [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse has عِنْدَ رَبِّكُمْ], and that is not permissible, because it is foreign to both of them.

His words: {أَفَلاَ تَعْقِلُونَ}: the discussion of its counterpart has been given. There are two views about this clause. First: [that it] falls within the scope of the speech [of the Jews]. Second: that it is Allah the Exalted's address to the believers about that. So on the first its position is accusative, and on the second it has no grammatical position. The object of {تَعْقِلُونَ} may be intended, and may not.

semin-durr:77-77.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {أَوَلاَ يَعْلَمُونَ أَنَّ الله}: it was said earlier that the doctrine of the majority is that the wāw is intended to come before the hamza, because it is a conjunction, and it was only put after it because of the strength of the interrogative hamza; and that the doctrine of al-Zamakhsharī is to imply a verb after the hamza. لا is for negation.

{أَنَّ الله يَعْلَمُ} may be in the position of the accusative, and then there are two ways of construing it. First: that it stands in place of a single [object], if we take عَلِمَ in the sense of عَرَف ("to know, recognise"). Second: that it stands in place of two objects, if we take it as transitive to two, like ظنَنْتُ. It was said earlier that this is the doctrine of Sībawayh and the majority, and that al-Akhfash claims it stands in place of the first and the second is omitted.

«ما» may be in the sense of الذي with its resumptive pronoun omitted, i.e. "what they conceal and what they reveal (it)"; or it may be maṣdariyya, i.e. "He knows their concealment and their disclosure". Secrecy and openness are opposites.

semin-durr:134-134.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {تِلْكَ أُمَّةٌ}: «تلكَ» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «أمةٌ» is its khabar (predicate). It is also permissible for «أمةٌ» to be a badal (substitute) from «تلك», and «قد خَلَتْ» the khabar of the mubtadaʾ. The origin of «تلك» is «تي»; when the lām was brought for distance, the yāʾ was elided for the meeting of two quiescents. If it is said: Why was the lām not given kasra so that the yāʾ would not be elided? The answer is that the utterance becomes heavy by the yāʾ falling between two kasras. The Kufans claimed that the tāʾ alone is the noun, and that nothing there has been elided. His saying «قد خَلَتْ» is a verbal clause in the position of nominative as a naʿt (adjective) to «أمَّة», if it is said that that is the khabar of «تلك»; or it is the khabar of «تلك» if it is said that «أُمَّة» is a badal from «تلك», as has preceded. And «خَلَتْ» means: it went to al-khalāʾ, which is the land in which there is no companion; what is meant by it is: it died. What is pointed to is Abraham, Jacob and their sons.

His saying: {لَهَا مَا كَسَبَتْ}: In this clause there are three aspects. The first: that it is likewise a naʿt to «أمة», so its position is nominative. The second: that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «خَلَتْ», so its position is accusative, i.e.: it passed away with its earnings established for it. The third: that it is resumptive, so it has no grammatical position. And in «ما» in His saying «ما كَسَبَتْ» there are three aspects. The most apparent of them: that it is in the sense of «الذي» (a relative noun). The second: that it is an indefinite noun that is described; the returning pronoun on both views is omitted, i.e.: «كَسَبَتْه», except that the clause has no grammatical position on the first. The third: that it is maṣdar-forming, so it needs no returning pronoun on the well-known view, and the maṣdar stands in the place of the object, i.e.: for it is what it earned; or there is a muḍāf (annexed noun) there, i.e.: for it is the recompense of its earning. «[Translator's note: the source has «له مكسُوبُها» with a masculine «له»; the sense is "for it (the community)".]»

His saying: {وَلَكُمْ مَّا كَسَبْتُمْ}: If it is said that His saying {لَهَا مَا كَسَبَتْ} is resumptive, this clause is conjoined to it; and if it is said that it is a naʿt or a ḥāl, then not. As for the naʿt, it is because of the absence of a linking element in it; and as for the ḥāl, it is because the time of the establishment of its earning for it differs from the time of the establishment of the earning of those addressed, and conjoining a ḥāl to a ḥāl requires unity of time. And «ما» in His saying «ما كسبتم» is like the preceding «ما».

His saying: {وَلاَ تُسْأَلُونَ}: This clause is resumptive and nothing else, and its meaning is emphasis of what precedes it; because, since it has preceded that no one is benefited by another's earning, but rather it is particular to him, whether good or evil, therefore no one is asked about another. That is because the Jews boasted of their forebears, so they were informed of that. In «ما» the three aspects are permissible: its being a nominal relative, a particle relative (ḥarfiyya), or an indefinite noun. In the speech there is an omission, i.e.: and they will not be asked about what you used to do. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "And it is indicated by: «لَهَا ما كَسَبَتْ ولكم ما كَسَبْتُم»." End quote. Had the indicator been made His saying {وَلاَ تُسْأَلُونَ عَمَّا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ}, it would have been better, because it is a counterpart [to the omitted clause].

semin-durr:151-151.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {كَمَآ أَرْسَلْنَا}: there are two views on the kāf. The more evident of them: that it is for comparison (tashbīh). The second: that it is for giving a reason (taʿlīl). On the first view it is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun). People then differed over what it is attached to (mutaʿallaq) in five ways.

The first: that it is attached to His saying «ولأتِمَّ», its implied form being: "and so that I may complete My favour upon you with a completion like the completion [of favour] of the Messenger among you." What the two completions relate to differs: the first relates to reward in the Hereafter and the second to the sending of the Messenger in this world; or the first relates to the granting of Ibrāhīm's first supplication in His saying: {وَمِن ذُرِّيَّتِنَآ أُمَّةً مُّسْلِمَةً لَّكَ} [al-Baqara: 138] [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse is al-Baqara 128], and the second to the answering of the second supplication in His saying: {رَبَّنَا وابعث فِيهِمْ رَسُولاً مِّنْهُمْ} [al-Baqara: 12] [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse is al-Baqara 129]. [Makkī preferred it, because the context of the wording indicates that the meaning is]: "and so that I may complete My favour by clarifying the religion of your father Ibrāhīm, just as We answered his supplication concerning you and sent you a Messenger from among you."

The second: that it is attached to «يهتدون», its implied form being: "they are guided with a guidance like Our sending a Messenger among you"; the guidance is then compared to the sending in its reality and certainty, i.e. a guidance as real as the reality of Our sending.

The third — and it is the view of Abū Muslim —: that it is attached to His saying: {وَكَذَلِكَ جَعَلْنَاكُمْ أُمَّةً وَسَطاً} [al-Baqara: 143], i.e. a making like Our sending. This is very far-fetched because of the length of the separation, which signals a break.

The fourth: that it is attached to what follows it, namely «اذكروني». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Just as I remembered you by sending the messengers, so remember Me with obedience and I will remember you with reward. It is then on the assumption of an omitted maṣdar and on the assumption of an omitted muḍāf, i.e.: remember Me with a remembrance like Our remembering you by the sending; then it became: like the remembrance of Our sending; then the muḍāf was omitted and the muḍāf ilayhi put in its place. This is as when you say: 'Just as so-and-so came to you, he will honour you.' The fāʾ does not prevent that." Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "just as it does not prevent it in the chapter of the condition", meaning that what follows the fāʾ of the apodosis governs what precedes it. [Makkī rejected this on the ground that when an imperative has an answer, what precedes it is not attached to it], because it is occupied with its answer, and «اذكروني» has been answered by His saying «أذكرْكم», so what precedes it is not attached to it. He said: "That is permissible only by comparison with a condition that is answered with two answers, as in: 'If so-and-so comes to you, honour him, and you will be pleased with him'; then «كما» and «فأذكركم» would be two answers to the imperative. The first is more eloquent and better known. You say: 'Just as I have done good to you, so honour me', and it is valid to make the kāf attached to «أكرمني» since it has no answer."

As for what Makkī disallowed, the Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "We know of no disagreement over its permissibility. As for his saying 'unless it is compared to the condition', and his making «كما» an answer to the imperative, it is not a valid comparison and is not intelligible; arguing against it has a place other than this book." The Shaykh said: "What mars this in my view is only the presence of the fāʾ, for what comes after it does not govern what is before it, and its being redundant is unlikely." End of quotation. What I quoted from Abū al-Baqāʾ, that it does not prevent that, has already been given.

The fifth: that it is attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «نعمتي», the implied sense being: "and so that I may complete My favour, resembling Our sending a Messenger among you", i.e. resembling the favour of the sending; it is then on the assumption of an omitted muḍāf.

As for the view that it is for giving a reason, it is attached to what follows it, namely His saying «فاذكروني», i.e. remember Me because of Our sending a Messenger among you. The kāf being causal is clear; some counted among it: {واذكروه كَمَا هَدَاكُمْ} [al-Baqara: 198], and the saying of the other:
776 - لا تَشْتُمِ الناسَ كما لا تُشْتَمُ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Do not revile people, as [i.e. since] you are not reviled.)
i.e.: do not revile, because people refrain from reviling you.

On the «ما» joined to this kāf there are three views. The most evident of them: that it is maṣdar-forming (maṣdariyya); its exposition has been given before. The second: that it means «الذي», with the returning pronoun omitted, and «رسولاً» a badal (substitute) from it, the implied sense being: like the one whom We sent as a Messenger. This is very far-fetched; moreover it involves «ما» being applied to individual rational beings, which is a less favoured view. The third: that it is a restraining (kāffa) «ما» on the kāf, as in his saying:
777 - لَعَمْرُكَ إنني وأبا حُمَيْدٍ ... كما النَّشْوانُ والرجلُ الحليمُ
(By your life, I and Abū Ḥumayd are like the drunken man and the forbearing man.)
There is no need for this, for one resorts to it only where it is impossible to form a maṣdar from it and what follows it, as when it is joined to a nominal clause, like the verse just cited.

«منكم» is in the position of the accusative because it is a naʿt of «رسولاً», and likewise the clauses after it. It is also possible that the clauses after it are ḥāls, since the indefinite noun has been specified by being described with His saying «منكم». These attributes were given in the imperfect form because it indicates renewal and occurrence, which is what is intended here, unlike his being from among them, which is a fixed attribute of his. Here purification (tazkiya) is placed before teaching, while in Ibrāhīm's supplication it is the reverse. The difference is that purification here means cleansing from unbelief — and so they explained it — while there it means testifying that they are the best and the pure, and that comes after learning the laws and acting upon them. His saying: {وَيُعَلِّمُكُم مَّا لَمْ تَكُونُواْ تَعْلَمُونَ} after His saying: {وَيُعَلِّمُكُمُ الكتاب والحكمة} is a case of mentioning the general after the specific, which is rare, unlike its reverse.

semin-durr:152-152.t: And His saying, the Exalted: {واشكروا لِي}: it has already been stated that «شكر» is transitive sometimes by itself and sometimes by a preposition, equally so according to the correct view. Some said: when you say «شكرْتُ لزيدٍ», its meaning is "I thanked Zayd for his deed", so they made it transitive to two objects, one by itself and the other by the preposition. For that reason al-Zamakhsharī explained this passage by saying: "And give thanks to Me for what I have bestowed upon you." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "«واشكروا لي» and «واشكروني» have the same meaning, and «لي» is more eloquent and better known with «الشكر»; its meaning is: [thank] My favour and My bounties. Likewise when you say «شَكَرْتُك», the meaning is: I thanked you for your deed and mentioned it; the muḍāf was omitted, since the meaning of thanks is the mention of the favour and the mention of its bestower together, so whatever of that is omitted is an abridgement, because what remains indicates what was omitted."

semin-durr:154-154.t: His saying, the Exalted: {أَمْوَاتٌ بَلْ أَحْيَاءٌ}: [«أمواتٌ» is] the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e.: do not say: they are dead. Likewise «أحياءٌ» is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e.: rather they are alive. He took account of the wording of «مَنْ» once, and so used the singular in His saying «يُقْتَلُ», and of its meaning another time, and so used the plural in His saying {أَمْوَاتٌ بَلْ أَحْيَاءٌ}. The lām here is for reason (ʿilla), not for conveying [the speech to the addressee], because they did not convey this statement of theirs to the martyrs. The clause «هم أمواتٌ» is in the position of the accusative by the verb of saying, because it is reported speech with it. As for {بَلْ هُمْ أَحْيَاءٌ}, it admits two views. One: that it has no grammatical position, but is rather a statement from Allah the Exalted that they are alive; this is supported by His saying: {وَلَكِن لاَّ تَشْعُرُونَ}, since the meaning is: you have no perception of their life.
