820 - فلو أَنَّ حَيَّاً يقبلُ المالَ فِدْيةً ... لَسُقْنا إليه المالَ كالسيلِ مُفْعَما
ولكنْ أبى قومٌ أُصيب أخوهمُ ... رِضا العارِ واختاروا على اللبنِ الدِّما
(Had any tribe accepted wealth as ransom, we would have driven wealth to it like a brimming torrent; but a people whose brother was struck down refused to be content with disgrace, and chose blood over milk.)
And he said:
821 - أَكَلْتُ دماً إنْ لم أَرْعُكِ بِضَرَّةٍ ... بعيدةِ مَهْوى القِرْطِ طَيِّبَةِ النَّشْرِ
(May I have eaten blood [i.e. accepted blood-money] if I do not frighten you with a co-wife, long-necked and sweet of scent.)
And he said:
822 - يَأْكُلْن كَلَّ ليلةٍ إكافا ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(They eat a pack-saddle every night…)
He means: the price of a pack-saddle.
His words: {فِي بُطُونِهِمْ}: three interpretations are permissible. The most apparent: that it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to His words «يأكلون», being an adverbial of place for it. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: «It involves the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "the passage of their bellies"»; but there is no need for the implied form he gave. The second: that it is attached to something omitted, as a ḥāl from «النار». Abū al-Baqāʾ said: «The better view is that the ḥāl here is anticipated (muqaddara), because at the time of eating it is not in their bellies; it only comes to that. The implied form is: being established, or being, in their bellies». He said: «This entails placing the ḥāl before the particle of exception, which is weak — unless the object is made to be omitted and «في بطونهم» a ḥāl from it or an adjective of it, i.e. "in their bellies something"»; meaning that «إلا النار» would then be accusative as a complete exception, since it is excepted from that omitted element. However, he said after that: «This statement is figurative in meaning, and the i'rab follows the rule of the wording». The third: that it is an adjective or a ḥāl from the omitted object of «كُلوا» «[Translator's note: so in the text; the verb in this verse is «يأكلون».]», as was established above.

semin-durr:175-175.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {فَمَآ أَصْبَرَهُمْ}: there are five views about this «ما». The first — the view of Sībawayh and the majority — is that it is a complete indefinite noun, neither relative nor qualified, and that its meaning is wonder (taʿajjub); so when you say «ما أحسنَ زيداً» (how handsome Zayd is!), its meaning is: "something has made Zayd handsome". The second — to which al-Farrāʾ went — is that it is interrogative, accompanied by the meaning of wonder, as in {كَيْفَ تَكْفُرُونَ} [al-Baqara: 28]. The third — attributed to al-Akhfash — is that it is a relative noun. The fourth — also attributed to him — is that it is an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective. On these four views it is in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); its khabar (predicate) on the first two views is the verbal clause after it, while on al-Akhfash's two views the khabar is omitted, since the clause after it is either a ṣila (relative clause) or an adjective. They likewise differed over the «أَفْعل» that comes after it: is it a noun — the view of the Kufans — or a verb? The latter is correct. On this disagreement rests a disagreement over the accusative of the noun after it: is it a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), or likened to the mafʿūl bihi? These doctrines have proofs, objections and answers for which this is not the place.
What is meant by wonder here and in the rest of the Quran is the announcement that their state is such that one ought to wonder at it; otherwise wonder is impossible with respect to Him, the Exalted. The meaning of «على النار» is [i.e.] "for the deeds of the people of the Fire"; this is a figurative use of speech.
The fifth: that it is negative, i.e. "Allah did not make them patient in the Fire". Abū al-Baqāʾ reported it, and it is worthless.

semin-durr:176-176.t: The words of Allah the Exalted: {ذَلِكَ بِأَنَّ الله}: They differed over the grammatical position of «ذلك»: it has been said to be nominative, and it has been said to be accusative. Those who say it is nominative differed on three views. The first: that it is the fāʿil (agent) of an omitted verb, i.e. "that became due to them". The second: that «ذلك» is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and «بأنَّ الله» its khabar (predicate), i.e. "that punishment is deserved because of what Allah sent down in the Quran concerning the unbeliever's deserving punishment". The third: that it is a khabar whose mubtadaʾ is omitted, i.e. "the matter is that", the reference being to the punishment. Whoever said it is accusative gave as its implied form: "We did that", and the bāʾ is attached (mutaʿalliq) to that omitted element and has a causal sense.

semin-durr:78-78.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {وَمِنْهُمْ أُمِّيُّونَ}: «منهم» is a fronted khabar (predicate), so it is attached to an omitted element, and «أمِّيُّون» is a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject). On the opinion of al-Akhfash it may be a fāʿil (agent) of the adverbial expression before it, even though that does not lean on [anything]; I explained earlier what it leans on.

أمِّيُّون is the plural of أُمّيّ, one who neither writes nor reads. There is disagreement about what it is related to. It is said: to the mother (الأُم), and in this there are two senses. First: that he is in the state of his mother who bore him in not knowing writing, and not like his father, because writing is not among women's occupations. Second: that he is in the state in which his mother bore him, not having changed from it or moved on. It is also said: it is related to الأُمَّة in the sense of stature and natural form, meaning that he has of the people nothing but that. It is also said: it is related to the community (الأُمَّة) in its simplicity before it came to know things, as they say عامِّي, i.e. in the manner of the common people. From Ibn ʿAbbās: "They were called أمِّيُّون because they did not believe in the Mother of the Book." Abū ʿUbayda said: "They were called أُمِّيُّون because of the sending down of the Book upon them, as though they were related to the Mother of the Book."

Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «أُمِيُون» with a light yāʾ, as though he found the succession of two doublings heavy.

His words: {لاَ يَعْلَمُونَ}: a verbal clause in the position of the nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of أمِّيُّون, as though it were said: "unlettered, not knowing".

His words: {إِلاَّ أَمَانِيَّ}: this is a disjoined exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ), because "wishful fancies" are not of the genus of the Book, nor included under what it denotes; and that is what the disjoined [exception] is. But its condition is that its inclusion be conceivable in some way, as in His words {مَا لَهُمْ بِهِ مِنْ عِلْمٍ إِلاَّ اتباع الظن} [al-Nisāʾ: 157]/ and the words of al-Nābigha:

556 - حَلَفْتُ يميناً غيرَ ذي مَثْنَوِيَّةٍ ... ولا عِلْمَ إلا حُسْنُ ظنٍّ بصاحبِ
(I swore an oath without reservation — and I have no knowledge, only a good opinion of a companion.)

because by mentioning knowledge, opinion is called to mind. For this reason it is not permissible to say: "The horses neighed, except a donkey."

Know that the disjoined [exception] is of two kinds: a kind toward which the governor can properly be directed, such as "the people came except a donkey"; and a kind toward which it cannot, such as the grammarians' examples: "it increased only what it decreased" and "it benefited only what it harmed". In the first there are two dialects: the dialect of the Ḥijāz requires the accusative, and the dialect of Tamīm treats it like the joined [exception], so after negation and the like both the accusative and agreement (itbāʿ) are permitted. The noble verse is of the first kind, so its accusative admits two aspects. First: as a disjoined exception. Second: that it is a badal (substitute) from الكتاب. «إلا» in the disjoined [exception] is construed by the Basrans as «لكن» and by the Kufans as «بل».

The apparent sense of Abū al-Baqāʾ's words is that it is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun) by an omitted verb, for he said: "{إِلاَّ أَمَانِيَّ} is a disjoined exception, because wishful fancies are not of the genus of knowledge; «إلاَّ» in such a case is construed as «لكنْ», i.e. 'but they wish it wishes'." So for him it belongs to the chapter of the emptied (mufarragh) disjoined exception, and it becomes parallel to "I knew nothing but supposition". This is questionable.

الأمانيّ is the plural of أُمْنِيَّة, with doubled yāʾ in both. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "Lightening it is permissible in both." Abū Jaʿfar read it lightened, dropping one of the two yāʾs for lightening. Al-Akhfash said: "This is as is said in the plural of مفتاح: مفاتح and مفاتيح." Al-Naḥḥās said: "Dropping is more frequent in the weak [roots]", and recited the words of al-Nābigha:

557 - وهل يُرْجِعُ التسليمَ أو يَكْشِفُ العمى ... ثلاثُ الأَثافي والرسومُ البلاقِعُ
(Can the three hearthstones and the desolate traces return a greeting, or remove blindness?)

Abū Ḥātim said: "Everything of this kind whose singular has come doubled, you have both options in the plural", and its basis goes back to what al-Akhfash said.

The pattern of أُمْنِيَّة is أُفْعُولة, from منَّى يُمَنِّي, when one recites and reads. He said:

558 - تَمَنَّى كتابَ اللهِ آخرَ ليلِهِ ... تَمَنِّىِ داودَ الزبورَ على رِسْلِ
(He recited the Book of Allah at the end of his night, as David recited the Psalms, unhurriedly.)

Kaʿb ibn Mālik said:

559 - تَمَنَّى كتابَ اللهِ أوَّلَ لَيلهِ ... وآخِرَه لاقى حِمامَ المقادِرِ
(He recited the Book of Allah at the beginning of his night, and at its end he met the death decreed.)

And Allah the Exalted said: «إلا إذا تَمَنَّى ألقى الشيطانُ في أُمْنِيَّتِهِ», i.e. he recited and read. On this view the origin is أُمْنُوية, which underwent the change that ميِّت and سيِّد undergo, as has been discussed. It is also said: الأمنيّة is lying and fabrication. It is also said: what a person wishes for and desires. It is also said: what he estimates and conjectures, from مَنَّى when he lied, wished or estimated, as in his words:

560 - لا تأْمَنَنَّ وأنْ أمْسَيْت في حَرَمٍ ... حتى تُلاقِي ما يَمْني لكَ الماني
(Do not feel secure, even if you are in a sanctuary at evening, until you meet what the Determiner determines for you.)

i.e. what the Estimator estimates for you.

Al-Rāghib said: "المَنْي is measure (القَدْر); from it comes «المَنا», by which things are weighed; and from it المَنِيَّة, which is the term of death measured out for living beings. التمنِّي is estimating something in the soul and picturing it there; that may be from supposition and conjecture, and it may be built on reflection and a basis. But since most of it is from conjecture, lying has the greater hold on it, so most wishing is picturing what has no reality. الأُمْنِيَة is the image that arises in the soul from wishing for a thing. And since lying is picturing what has no reality and expressing it in words, wishing became like the starting point of lying [so it was used to express it; from this is the saying of ʿUthmān, may Allah be pleased with him: 'I have not sung, nor have I تَمَنَّيْتُ (lied), since I embraced Islam']."

Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The derivation from مَنَّى, when he estimated, [is] that the one who wishes estimates in his soul and conjectures what he wishes for; and likewise the fabricator; and the reciter estimates that such-and-such a word comes after such-and-such." So he made a shared measure among these meanings, and it is clear.

His words: {وَإِنْ هُمْ إِلاَّ يَظُنُّونَ}: «إنْ» is negative in the sense of ما. When it is negative, the well-known view is that it does not govern as Ḥijāzī «ما» does; some permitted that and attributed it to Sībawayh, and they recited:

561 - إنْ هُوَ مستولياً على أَحَدٍ ... إلاَّ على أَضْعَفِ المجانين
(He has no mastery over anyone, except over the weakest of madmen.)

«هو» is its noun and «مستولياً» its khabar. So His word «هم» is in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ, not the noun of «إنْ», since it does not govern on the well-known view; «إلاَّ» is for the emptied exception; and «يَظُنُّونَ» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of «هم». The two objects of ظنّ are omitted because they are known, or by way of restriction (iqtiṣār), which is a matter of disagreement.

semin-durr:79-79.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {فَوَيْلٌ لِّلَّذِينَ يَكْتُبُونَ}: وَيْلٌ is a mubtadaʾ (subject). Beginning with it is permitted although it is indefinite, because it is an imprecation against them, and imprecation is among the things that license [an indefinite mubtadaʾ], whether it is a prayer for someone, as in «سلامٌ عليكم», or against him, as in this verse. The preposition and its genitive noun after it is the khabar (predicate), so it is attached to an omitted element.

Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "Had it been in the accusative, it would have an aspect, construed as: 'Allah has made woe binding on them'; and the lām would be explicative, because the noun was not mentioned before the maṣdar." He means that the lām after the accusative is for clarification, so it is attached to an omitted element. And by his words "because the noun …" he means that if it had been mentioned before «ويل», so that you said "Allah has made woe binding on Zayd", it would not need clarification, unlike if it comes later. The wording of al-Jarmī suggests that the nominative is obligatory when it is cut off from annexation, but al-Akhfash stated explicitly that the accusative is permissible, for he said: "The accusative is permissible by implying a verb, i.e. 'Allah has made woe binding on them'."

Know that ويل and its sisters — وَيْح, وَيْس, وَيْب and عَوْل — are among the maṣdars (verbal nouns) put in the accusative by verbs not from their own root, and those verbs must be implied; it is not permissible to make them overt at all, because they [the maṣdars] have been made a substitute for pronouncing the verb. When it is separated from annexation, the nominative is better, as in «وَيْلٌ له»; and if it is annexed, it is accusative, as stated. Although al-Jarmī's wording suggests that the nominative is obligatory when it is cut off from annexation — for he said: "When you bring in the lām you use the nominative and say: ويلٌ له, وَوَيْحٌ له" — it is as though he means "in most cases". The Arabs did not use a verb from it because of the weakness of its second and first radicals. Ibn ʿArafa reported «تَوَيَّلَ الرجلُ» when he invoked woe, but this does not refute [the above], because it is like their saying «سَوَّفْتَ» and «لَوْلَيْتَ» when you say to him سوف and لو.

The meaning of الوَيْل is the intensity of evil; al-Khalīl said this. Al-Aṣmaʿī said: الوَيْل is lamenting, and الوَيْل is [also] expressing pity. Sībawayh said: "وَيْل is for one who has fallen into destruction, and وَيْح is a rebuke to one who is on the brink of destruction." It is also said: الويل is grief. Are وَيْل, وَيْح, وَيْس and وَيْب of one meaning, or is there a difference between them? There is disagreement; what Sībawayh distinguished among some of them has been given. Some said: وَيْل is in imprecation against someone, and وَيْح and what follows are expressions of pity for him. Al-Farrāʾ claimed that the origin of وَيْل is وَيْ, i.e. grief, as you say وَيْ لفلان, i.e. grief to him; then the Arabs joined it to the lām, considered [the lām] part of it, and declined it. This is very strange. One says وَيْل and وَيْلة with tāʾ. Imruʾ al-Qays said:

562 - له الويلُ إنْ أَمْسى ولا أمُّ عامرٍ ... لَدَيْهِ ولا البَسْباسَةُ ابنةُ يَشْكُرا
(Woe to him if he comes to evening with neither Umm ʿĀmir nor al-Basbāsa daughter of Yashkur with him.)

And he also said:

563 - ويومَ دَخَلْتَ الخِدْرَ خِدْرَ عُنَيْزَةٍ ... فقالَتْ: لَكَ الوَيْلاتُ إنَّك مُرْجِلي
(And the day I entered the litter, the litter of ʿUnayza, and she said: "Woes to you! You will make me go on foot.")

ويلات is the plural of وَيْلَة, not the plural of وَيْل as Ibn ʿAṭiyya claimed,/ because pluralising a masculine with alif and tāʾ is not analogical.

His words: {بِأَيْدِيهِمْ}: attached to (mutaʿalliq) يكتبون. Making it a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الكتاب» is far-fetched. الكتاب here is in the sense of "what is written", so it is accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object); making it a maṣdar in its proper sense is far-fetched. This belongs to the chapter of emphasis, for writing is not done other than with the hand; like it are {وَلاَ طَائِرٍ يَطِيرُ بِجَنَاحَيْهِ} [al-Anʿām: 38] and {يَقُولُونَ بِأَفْوَاهِهِم} [Āl ʿImrān: 167]. It is also said: the benefit of mentioning it is that they did it themselves and did not command others to do it, for your saying "so-and-so did such-and-such" may mean that he commanded it to be done without doing it himself, as in "the prince built the city"; so this was brought to remove that figurative sense. It is also said: its benefit is to show their audacity and openness, for the one who does the deed himself is more deeply involved than one who does not. These two views are close to emphasis, for the basis of emphasis is removing the supposition of a figurative sense. Ibn al-Sarrāj said: "The mention of the hands is an allusion to their having fabricated that of their own accord and from themselves." What he said does not necessarily follow.

الأيدي is the plural of يَد. The origin is أَيْدُيٌ with ḍamma on the dāl, like فَلْس / أَفْلُس in the plural of paucity. The ḍamma before the yāʾ was found heavy, so it was changed to kasra for harmony, as in بِيْض, plural of أَبْيض, the original being بُيْض with ḍamma on the yāʾ [Translator's note: so in the source; the ḍamma is on the bāʾ], like حُمْر, plural of أحمر. This is the opinion of Sībawayh — I mean that he keeps the letter and changes the vowel — and the doctrine of al-Akhfash is the reverse. The verification of their two doctrines will come at the mention of «معيشة», if Allah the Exalted wills.

The origin of يَد is يَدْي with sukūn on the middle radical. It is also said: يَدَي with a vowel on it; then the weak letter had a vowel and the letter before it had fatḥa, so it was changed to alif and it became يداً, like رَحىً. On this is based the dual يديان, and also his words:

564 - يا رُبَّ سارٍ باتَ لن يُوَسَّدا ... تحتَ ذِراعِ العَنْسِ أو كفَّ اليَدا
(How many a night traveller spent the night with no pillow but the foreleg of his strong she-camel, or the palm of his hand.)

The well-known [usage] in its dual is not restoring its third radical. Allah the Exalted said {بَلْ يَدَاهُ مَبْسُوطَتَانِ} [al-Māʾida: 64] and {تَبَّتْ يَدَآ أَبِي لَهَبٍ} [al-Masad: 1]. The restoration is anomalous in his saying «يَدَيان»:

565 - يَدَيَان بَيْضَاوان عِندَ مُحَلِّمٍ ... قد يَمْنَعانِكَ أَنْ تُضَامَ وتُقْهَرا
(Two white [generous] hands belonging to Muḥallim, which may protect you from being wronged and overpowered.)

أيادٍ is the plural of the plural, like كَلْب / أَكْلُب / أكالب.

In His words {يَكْتُبُونَ الكتاب} there must be an omission by which the meaning is sound. Al-Zamakhsharī construed it as: "they write the distorted book"; others construed it as a ḥāl from الكتاب: "they write the book distorted". This implication was needed only because disapproval is not directed at one who writes the Book with his hand unless he distorts and alters it.

His words: {لِيَشْتَرُواْ}: the lām is the lām of kay, which has been discussed. The pronoun in «به» refers to what they pointed to by their saying {هذا مِنْ عِنْدِ الله}, and «ثمناً» is its object. The verification of the bāʾ entering on what is not the price was given at His words {وَلاَ تَشْتَرُواْ بِآيَاتِي ثَمَناً قَلِيلاً} [al-Baqara: 41], so let reference be made there. The lām is attached to يقولون, i.e. "they say that for the sake of purchasing". Whoever made it attached to the [notion of] being (al-istiqrār) contained in His words {مِنْ عِنْدِ الله} went far astray.

His words: {مِّمَّا كَتَبَتْ أَيْدِيهِمْ}: attached to ويل, or to the [notion of] being in the khabar. «مِنْ» is causal. «ما» is a nominal relative and the resumptive pronoun is omitted. It may also be an indefinite qualified by a description — though this is not as strong as the first — and the resumptive is also omitted, i.e. "[which] they wrote (it)". It may also be maṣdariyya, i.e. "because of their writing". {وَوَيْلٌ لَّهُمْ مِّمَّا يَكْسِبُونَ} is like what preceded it. «الوَيْل» is repeated only to convey that destruction attaches to each of the two acts separately, not to the two together. And «كَتَبَتْ» was placed before «يَكْسبون» only because the writing comes first and its result is the earning of wealth: writing is the cause and earning the effect, so the composition came in accordance with this.

semin-durr:121-121.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {الذين آتَيْنَاهُمُ}: nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject). Concerning its khabar (predicate) there are two views. The first: it is «يَتْلُونه», and the clause «أولئكَ يؤمنون» is then either resumptive, which is the correct view, or a ḥāl (circumstantial) on a weak view whose like was given at the beginning of the sūra. The second: the khabar is the clause «أولئك يؤمنون», and «يتلونه» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, either from the object in «آتَيْناهم» or from «الكتاب». On both views it is an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara), because at the time of the giving they were not reciting, nor was the Book being recited. Al-Ḥūfī allowed «يَتْلونه» to be a khabar and «أولئك يؤمنون» a khabar after a khabar. He said: "Like their saying «هذا حلوٌ حامِضٌ» (this is sweet-sour)", as though he means making the two khabars into the sense of a single khabar. This is if what is meant by «الذين» is a specific group; but if what is meant by them is general, then «أولئكَ يُؤمِنونُ» is the khabar. A group — among them Ibn ʿAṭiyya and others — said: "«ويَتْلُونه» is a ḥāl that cannot be dispensed with, and the benefit lies in it." Abū al-Baqāʾ also said: "«يَتْلُونه» may not be the khabar, lest it follow that every believer recites the Book as it should be recited, however recitation is interpreted." The Shaykh said: "We say: what follows, preventing its being a khabar, follows also in making it a ḥāl, because not every believer is in the state of reciting, however recitation is interpreted."
His words: {حَقَّ تِلاَوَتِهِ}: there are three aspects in it. The first: it is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), its origin being «تلاوةً حقاً» (a true recitation); then the adjective was put first and annexed to the maṣdar, and it became the parallel of «ضَرَبْتَ شديدَ الضربِ», i.e. a severe beating; when the adjective of the maṣdar was put first, it was given its accusative. The second: it is a ḥāl from the agent of «يَتْلونه», i.e. they recite it rightfully. The third: it is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "«حَقَّ» is a maṣdar, and what governs it is an implied verb; it has the sense of أَفْعَل, and its annexation to a single defined [noun] is not permissible; it was permissible here only because the definiteness of «التلاوة» by its annexation to the pronoun is not pure definiteness; it is rather like their saying «رجلٌ واحدُ أمِّه» (a man unique of his mother) and «نسيج وحدِه» (one of a kind)." He means that it has the force of the elative (afʿal al-tafḍīl), meaning "the most rightful recitation", and it seems he holds that the annexation of أفعل is not pure. There is no need to imply a governor for it, since what precedes it requires it.
Concerning the pronoun in «به» there are four views. The first — and it is the apparent one — is that it refers back to «الكتاب». The second: it refers back to the Messenger. They said: "He has not been mentioned, but he is known"; there is no need for this excuse, for he is mentioned in His words «أَرْسلناك», except that there is a shift (iltifāt) in it from address to the third person. The third: it refers back to Allah the Exalted, and in it there is also a shift, from the pronoun of the speaker magnifying Himself in His words «أَرْسلناك» to the third person. The fourth: Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It refers back to «الهدى»", and he established that with good discussion.
His words: {وَإِذِ ابتلى إِبْرَاهِيمَ رَبُّهُ بِكَلِمَاتٍ}: what governs «إذا» is «قال». . . what governs it is an implied «اذكر» (remember), and it is an object; and it has been said that it is not inflected. So the preferable is what I mentioned first, and he implied. . . "such-and-such happened", so he made it an adverb, but its governor is implied. [Translator's note: the source has «إذا» here, while the verse has «إذ»; and the text has gaps at the two ellipses, translated as they stand.] «ابتلى» and what follows it are in the position of the genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it. The origin of «ابتلى» is ابتلَوَ, so its alif is from a wāw, since it is from بَلا يَبْلو, i.e. "tested". «إبراهيمَ» is a fronted object, and its fronting is obligatory according to the majority of the grammarians, because whenever a pronoun referring to the object is attached to the agent, its fronting is obligatory, lest the pronoun refer to something later both in wording and in rank. This is the well-known view, and what comes contrary to it they counted as poetic licence. Abū al-Fatḥ [Translator's note: Ibn Jinnī] differed, saying: "Just as the verb requires the agent, it requires the object, so the utterance of it carries an awareness and requirement [of it]." Ibn Mālik cited many verses in which the object whose pronoun is attached to the agent comes later; among them:
706 - لَمَّا عصى أصْحابُه مُصْعَباً ... أَدَّى إليه الكيلَ صاعاً بصاعْ
(When his companions disobeyed Muṣʿab, he repaid them measure for measure.)
And among them:
707 - جَزَى بَنُوه أَبا الغَيْلانِ عن كِبَرٍ ... وحُسْنِ فِعْلٍ كما يُجْزَى سِنِمَّارُ
(His sons repaid Abū al-Ghaylān, for his old age and good deeds, as Sinimmār was repaid.)
Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "He put the object first out of concern for the one on whom the testing fell, since it is known that Allah is the One who tests; and the attachment of the object's pronoun to the agent necessitates fronting." He means that what necessitates the fronting is two causes: a semantic cause and a technical cause.
«إبراهيم» is a non-Arabic proper name; it has been said that its meaning before transfer [into Arabic] is "merciful father". There are nine dialectal forms of it. The most famous: «إبراهيم» with alif and yāʾ; and «إبراهام» with two alifs, which Hishām read, and Ibn Dhakwān in one of his two ways, in al-Baqara; and Hishām alone read it in three places at the end of al-Nisāʾ, two places at the end of Barāʾa, one place at the end of al-Anʿām and at the end of al-ʿAnkabūt, in al-Najm, al-Shūrā, al-Dhāriyāt, al-Ḥadīd and the first of al-Mumtaḥana, in Ibrāhīm, in al-Naḥl in two places, and in Maryam three; these are thirty-three places, fifteen of them in al-Baqara and eighteen in the sūras mentioned. It is related from Ibn ʿĀmir that he read everything in the Quran thus. It is related that it was said to Mālik ibn Anas: "The people of Syria read thirty-six places as «إبراهام» with alif"; he said: "The people of Damascus are more knowledgeable about eating watermelon than about reading." It was said: "They claim it is the reading of ʿUthmān." He said: "This is the codex of ʿUthmān", and he brought it out and found it as had been reported to him. The third: «إبراهِم» with an alif after the rāʾ and kasra on the hāʾ, without yāʾ; Abū Bakr [Translator's note: Shuʿba, from ʿĀṣim] read thus. Zayd ibn ʿAmr ibn Nufayl said:
708 - عُذْتُ بما عاذَ به إبراهِمُ ... إذ قالَ وَجْهي لك عانٍ رَاغِمُ
(I took refuge in what Abraham took refuge in, when he said: my face is humbled and abased before You.)
The fourth: likewise, but with fatḥa on the hāʾ. The fifth: likewise, but with ḍamma on it.
The sixth: «إبْرَهَم» with fatḥa on the hāʾ, without alif or yāʾ. ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib said:
709 - نحنُ آلُ اللهِ في كَعْبته ... لم نَزَلْ ذاكَ على عهد ابْرَهَمْ
(We are the people of Allah at His Kaʿba; we have been so ever since the time of Abraham.)
The seventh: «إبراهوم» with wāw. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "Its plural is أَباره according to some and بَراهم according to others. It has also been said: أبارِهَة and بَراهِمَة; and أَبَارهة is permissible." Al-Mubarrad said: "One does not say بَراهِمَة, for the hamza may not be dropped." Thaʿlab related for its plural «بَراه», just as one says in its diminutive «بُرَيْه», with the augments dropped.
The majority read «إبراهيم» in the accusative and «ربُّه» in the nominative, as has been said; Ibn ʿAbbās, Abū al-Shaʿthāʾ and Abū Ḥanīfa read the reverse. They said: its interpretation is "he called upon his Lord", so He called his supplication "testing" figuratively, because in supplication there is a request to uncover what the decrees will bring about. Concerning the nominative pronoun in «فَأَتَّمَّهُنَّ» there are two views. The first: it refers back to «ربه», i.e. "He completed them". The second: it refers back to Abraham, i.e. he acted on them and fulfilled them.
His words: {قَالَ إِنِّي}: this clause of saying may be conjoined to what precedes it, if we say that it [i.e. «قال»] governs «إذ», because the implied form is: "and He said: I am making you, when He tested". It may be resumptive, if we say that what governs «إذ» is implied, as though it were asked: "So what did his Lord say to him when he completed the words?" and the reply was: "He said: I am making you". On this view it may also be an explanation of His words «ابتلى» and an interpretation of it, so that what is meant by «الكلمات» is what He mentioned of leadership, purifying the House, raising the foundations and what follows; al-Zamakhsharī reported that.
His words: {جَاعِلُكَ}: it is the active participle of «جَعَلَ» in the sense of "rendered", so it is transitive to two objects. The first is the kāf, and in it there is the well-known disagreement: is it in the position of the accusative or the genitive? That is because concerning the pronoun attached to the active participle there are three views. The first: it is in the position of the genitive by annexation. The second: it is in the position of the accusative, and the tanwīn was dropped only because of the close attachment of the pronoun. They said: this is shown by its presence under poetic licence, as in the poet's saying:
710 - فما أَدْري وظني كلَّ ظَنِّ ... أَمُسْلِمُني إلى قومي شُراحي
(I do not know — and my supposition is every supposition — whether Shurāḥī will hand me over to my people.)
And another said:
711 - هُمُ الفاعلونَ الخيرَ والآمِرُونه ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(They are the doers of good and the enjoiners of it…)
This is on conceding that the nūn of «مُسْلِمُني» is tanwīn; otherwise the correct view is that it is the nūn of protection (nūn al-wiqāya). The third — the position of Sībawayh — is that the pronoun's ruling is the ruling of its overt counterpart, so whatever is permissible in the overt noun is permissible in its pronoun. The second object is «إماماً».
His words: {لِلنَّاسِ}: two aspects are permissible in it. The first: it is attached to «جاعل», i.e. for the sake of the people. The second: it is a ḥāl from «إماماً», for it is an adjective of an indefinite noun placed before it, so it becomes a ḥāl from it, since the origin is «إماماً للناسِ»; on this it is attached to something omitted. «الإمام» is the name of that which is followed (yuʾtammu bihi), i.e. aimed at and followed, like «الإزار», the name of that with which one wraps oneself (yuʾtazaru bihi); from it the builder's line is called «إمام». In other contexts it is the plural of «آمّ», the active participle of أَمَّ يَؤُمُّ, like قائم and قِيام, نائِم and نِيام, جائِع and جِياع.
His words: {وَمِن ذُرِّيَّتِي}: there are three views on it. The first: «مِنْ ذريتي» is an adjective of an omitted qualified noun, which is the first object, and the second object and what governs them both are omitted, the implied form being: "He said: and make a group of my offspring leaders"; Abū al-Baqāʾ said this. The second: «ومِنْ ذُرِّيَّتي» is conjoined to the kāf, as though he said "and making some of my offspring", just as someone says to you "I will honour you" and you say "and Zayd". The Shaykh said: "Conjunction to the kāf is not sound, because it is genitive, and conjunction to it can only be with the repetition of the governing word, which has not been repeated; and because «مِنْ» cannot be supposed to have the governing word annexed to it, since it is a particle, and supposing it synonymous with «بعض» so that annexation to it becomes sound is not sound; nor is it sound to suppose the conjunction to be of the category of conjoining to the position of the kāf, since it is accusative, so that «مِنْ» would be put in the position of the accusative, because it is not among the cases where one conjoins to the position in the school of Sībawayh, since the condition [al-muḥriz] is lacking. Nor is it the parallel of what he mentioned, because the kāf in «سأكرمك» is in the position of the accusative." The third: the Shaykh said: "What the meaning requires is that «مِنْ ذرّيَّتي» be attached to something omitted, the implied form being: 'and make from my offspring a leader', because Abraham understood from His words «إني جاعلُك للناسِ إماماً» exclusiveness, so he asked that He make a leader from his offspring." If the Shaykh meant technical attachment, so that «جاعل» would be transitive to one object, this is not apparent; and if he meant attachment in meaning, he may mean what Abū al-Baqāʾ means. «مِنْ ذرِّيَّتي» may also be a second object put before the first, so that it is attached to something omitted; that is permissible because a mubtadaʾ and khabar can be formed from these two parts.
If you said «مِنْ ذُرِّيَّتي إمامٌ» (from my offspring is a leader), it would be sound. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It has been said: this is from him by way of asking about them, i.e. 'And from my offspring, O Lord, what will there be?'" On this it is attached to something omitted; and had he implied it before «مِنْ ذريتي» it would have been preferable, because what is within the scope of the interrogative does not precede it.
Concerning the derivation of «ذُرِّيَّة» and its morphology there is a long discussion which requires reflection from whoever examines it. Know that «ذرية» has three dialectal forms: with ḍamma, kasra and fatḥa on the dhāl. The majority read it with ḍamma, Abū Jaʿfar al-Madanī read it with fatḥa, and Zayd ibn Thābit read it with kasra. As for its derivation, there are four positions. The first: it is derived from ذَرَوْتُ. The second: from ذَرَيْتُ. The third: from ذَرَأَ اللهُ الخَلْقَ (Allah created the creatures). The fourth: from الذرّ (tiny ants / specks). As for its morphology: «ذُرِّيَّة» with ḍamma, if it is from ذَرَوْتُ, its pattern may be فُعُّولَة, the origin being ذُرُّوْوَة; two wāws came together, the first an augment for lengthening and the second the final radical; the final radical was changed into yāʾ for lightness, so the word became ذُرُّوْيَة; then a yāʾ and a wāw came together, the first of them quiescent, so the wāw was changed into yāʾ and assimilated into the yāʾ that was changed from the final radical, and what precedes the yāʾ, namely the rāʾ, was given kasra for harmony. Its pattern may also be فُعِّيْلَة, the origin being ذُرِّيْوَة; the yāʾ of lengthening and the wāw that is the final radical came together, the first of them quiescent, so the wāw was changed into yāʾ and the yāʾ of lengthening was assimilated into it.
If it is from ذَرَيْتُ, a dialectal variant of ذَرَوْتُ, its pattern may also be فُعُّولَة or فُعِّيلة, as has been said. If it is فُعُّولة, the origin is ذُرُّوْيَة, and the change and assimilation described were applied to it; if it is فُعِّيْلَة, the origin is ذُرِّيْيَة, and the augment yāʾ was assimilated into the yāʾ that is the final radical. If it is from ذَرَأَ, with hamza, its pattern is فُعِّيْلة, the origin being ذُرِّيْئَة; the hamza was lightened by being replaced with yāʾ, like the hamza of خطيئة and النسيء, then the augment yāʾ was assimilated into the yāʾ that replaced the hamza.
If it is from الذَّرّ, four aspects are possible for its pattern. The first: فُعْلِيَّة; this yāʾ may be that of relation (nisba), and they changed the dhāl from fatḥa to ḍamma, just as they said in relating to الدَّهْر «دُهْري» and to السَّهْل «سُهْلي», with ḍamma on the dāl and the sīn; or it may be for something other than relation, so it is like قُمْرِيَّة. The second: it is فُعِّيْلَة, like مُرِّيقَة, the origin being ذُرِّيْرة; the last rāʾ was changed into yāʾ because of the succession of identical letters, just as they said تَسَرَّيْتُ and تَظَنَّيْتُ for تَسَرَّرْتُ and تَظَنَّنْتُ. The third: it is فُعُّولة, like قُدُّوس and سُبُّوح, the origin being ذُرُّوْرة; the rāʾ was changed for the reason given, so it became ذُرُّوْيَة; then a wāw and a yāʾ came together, and the change and assimilation came about as has been said. The fourth: it is فُعْلُولة, the origin being ذُرُّوْرَة, and what was described in the preceding aspect was applied to it.
As for «ذِرِّيَّة» with kasra on the dhāl: if it is from ذَرَوْتُ, its pattern is فِعِّيْلَة, the origin being ذِرِّيْوَة; the wāw was replaced with yāʾ and assimilated into the yāʾ after it. If it is from ذَرَيْتُ, its pattern is also فِعِّيْلة; and if it is from ذَرَأَ, its pattern is also فِعِّيْلة, like بِطِّيْخة, the origin being ذِرِّيْئَة, and what was described for the form with ḍamma on the dhāl was applied to it. If it is from الذَّرّ, it admits three aspects. The first: its pattern is فِعْلِيَّة, a relation to الذرّ, irregularly as in the form with ḍamma. The second: it is فِعِّيْلَة. The third: it is فِعْلِيلَة, like حِلْتيت, the origin in it being ذِرِّيْرَة; and in both was done what has been described: replacing the last rāʾ with yāʾ and assimilating into it.
As for «ذَرِّيَّة» with fatḥa on the dhāl: if it is from ذَرَوْتُ or ذَرَيْتُ, its pattern is فَعِّيْلَة, like سَكِّينة, the origin being ذَرِّيْوَة or ذَرِّيْيَة; or فَعُّولة, the origin being ذَرُّوْوَة or ذَرُّوْيَة, and what was described in its parallel was applied to it. If it is from ذَرَأَ, its pattern is either فَعِّيْلَة, like سَكِّينة, the origin being ذَرِّيْئَة, or فَعُّولة, like خَرُّوبة, the origin being ذَرَّوْءة, and what was described in its parallel was applied to it. If it is from الذرّ, there are also four aspects in its pattern. The first: فَعْلِيَّة, and the yāʾ here too may be that of relation — and they did not deviate in it by a change as they deviated with ḍamma and kasra — or not, as in بَرْنِيَّة. The second: فَعُّولة, like خَرُّوبة, the origin being ذَرُّوْرَة. The third: فَعِّلية, like سَكِّينة, the origin being ذَرِّيْرَة. The fourth: فَعْلُولة, like بَكُّولَة, the origin also being ذَرُّوْرَة; and what was described in its parallel was applied to it: replacing the last rāʾ and assimilating what precedes into it, and the dhāl was given kasra by assimilation (itbāʿ). [Translator's note: so in the source; this final remark about kasra on the dhāl sits oddly in the section on the form with fatḥa.] By this careful setting-out that I have made, the discussion of this word — lexically, derivationally and morphologically — has become clear, for people have found this word problematic in relation to what I mentioned, and most of them erred in its morphology with respect to the operations I have set out; and praise be to Allah.
As for whoever constructed it on the pattern فَعْلَة, like جَفْنَة, in his view it is from ذَرَيْتُ. «الذُّرِّيَّة» is progeny; it applies to males and females, and the plural is «الذَراري». Some claimed that it applies to fathers just as it applies to sons, adducing His words {وَآيَةٌ لَّهُمْ أَنَّا حَمَلْنَا ذُرِّيَّتَهُمْ فِي الفلك المشحون} [Yā-Sīn: 41], meaning Noah and those with him; this will come in its place.
His words: {قَالَ لاَ يَنَالُ عَهْدِي الظالمين}: the majority read «الظالمين» in the accusative as the object, with «عَهْدي» as the agent, i.e. My covenant does not reach the wrongdoers so as to overtake them. Qatāda, al-Aʿmash and Abū Rajāʾ read «والظالمون» as the agent, with «عهدي» as the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). Both readings are clear, since the verb may properly be ascribed to each of them, for whoever attains you, you have attained him. «النَّيْل» is attaining, and it is also giving; نال ينال نَيْلاً, so he is نائل.

semin-durr:44-44.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {أَتَأْمُرُونَ الناس بالبر}: the hamza is for disapproval and rebuke, or for wonder at their state. «أَمَرَ» is transitive to two objects, one of them by itself and the other by a preposition, which may be omitted; the poet combined both in his saying:
423 - أَمَرْتُكَ الخيرَ فافْعَلْ ما أَمِرتَ به ... فَقَدْ تَرَكْتُكَ ذا مالٍ وذا نَشَبِ
(I commanded you to do good, so do what you have been commanded, for I have left you possessed of wealth and property.)
So «الناسَ» is the first object and «بالبِرِّ» the second object. Al-birr: abundance of good, in kindness to kin and obedience; from it come al-barr (the land) and al-bariyya (the open country), because of their vastness. The verb [from it] is بَرَّ يَبَرُّ, on faʿila yafʿalu, like عَلِمَ يَعْلَم. He said:
424 - لا هُمَّ ربِّ إنَّ بَكْراً دونكا ... يَبَرُّكَ الناسُ ويَفْجُرونكا
(O Allah, Lord, Bakr is before You: people obey You, while they act wickedly towards You.)
[i.e. they obey You. Al-birr is also the young of the fox, and the driving of sheep; of this is their saying: «لا يَعْرِفُ الهِرَّ من البِرِّ», i.e. he does not know calling them from driving them. Al-birr is also the heart; he said:
425 - أكونُ مكانَ البِرِّ منه ودونُه ... وأَجْعَلُ مالي دونَه وأُوامِرُهْ
(I am to him in the place of his heart, and nearer still, and I put my wealth before him and consult him.)
Al-barr with fatḥa: reverence and veneration; of this is: وَلَدٌ بَرٌّ بوالدَيْهِ (a child dutiful to his parents), i.e. he venerates them; and Allah the Exalted is Barr because of the abundance of His good towards His creation.]
His saying: «وَتَنْسَوْن» falls within the domain of the disapproval. The origin of تَنْسَوْن is تَنْسَيُون; it was modified by dropping the yāʾ on account of its quiescence, as has preceded in {اشتروا} [al-Baqara: 16]; so its pattern is tafʿawn. Al-nisyān is the opposite of remembrance; it is the inattention that occurs after knowledge has been acquired. It may be applied to leaving, and of this is: {نَسُواْ الله فَنَسِيَهُمْ} [al-Tawba: 67]. Suspension (taʿlīq) may enter it, by analogy with its opposite. He said:
426 - ومَنْ أنتمُ إنَّا نَسِينا مَنَ أنْتُمُ ... وريحُكُمُ من أيِّ ريحِ الأعاصِرِ
(And who are you? We have forgotten who you are, and of which whirlwind your wind is.)
His saying: {وَأَنْتُمْ تَتْلُونَ الكتاب} is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate) in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), governed by «تَنْسَوْن». Al-tilāwa is following in succession; of this is the recitation (tilāwa) of the Quran, because the reciter makes its words follow one another; and of it is: {والقمر إِذَا تَلاَهَا} [al-Shams: 2]. The origin of تَتْلُون is تَتْلُوون with two wāws; the ḍamma on the first wāw was felt heavy and dropped, so two quiescent letters met, and it was dropped; so its pattern is tafʿūn.
His saying: {أَفَلاَ تَعْقِلُونَ}: the hamza is likewise for disapproval, and it is intended to come after the fāʾ, because the fāʾ is a conjunction; likewise it comes before wāw and thumma, as in {أَوَلاَ يَعْلَمُونَ} [al-Baqara: 77], {أَثُمَّ إِذَا مَا وَقَعَ} [Yūnus: 51], the intention with it being postponement. It does not come before any other conjunctions: you say «ما قامَ زيدٌ بل أَقْعَدَ؟» [Translator's note: the example is as printed; its point is evidently that the hamza is not placed before «بل»]. This is the doctrine of the majority. Al-Zamakhsharī claimed that the hamza is in its own place with no intention of postponement, and he supposes before the fāʾ, wāw and thumma a verb to which what follows is conjoined; so here he supposes: "are you heedless, and do you not understand?", and likewise {أَفَلَمْ يَرَوْاْ} [Sabaʾ: 9], i.e. "were they blind and did not see?". He departed from this principle and agreed with the majority in places that will be pointed out. The object of «تَعْقِلون» is not intended, because the meaning is: "will there not be [understanding] from you?". It has also been said: its implied form is "will you not understand the ugliness of what you have committed of that?".
Al-ʿaql: perception that prevents from error. Its origin is prevention; of it is al-ʿiqāl (the hobble), because it restrains the camel; and ʿaql of blood-money, because it prevents the killing of the offender. Al-ʿaql is also an embroidered cloth. ʿAlqama said:
427 - عَقْلاً ورَقْماً تَظَلُّ الطيرُ تَتْبَعُهُ ... كأنَّه من دم الأَجْوافِ مَدْمُومُ
(Striped and figured cloth, which the birds keep following, as though it were smeared with the blood of [animals'] insides.)
Ibn Fāris said: "What is figured lengthwise is ʿaql, and what is figured in rounds is raqm." This clause has no grammatical position, because it is resumptive.
His saying: {واستعينوا بالصبر}: this imperative clause is conjoined to the commands before it, but these clauses were interposed between them. The origin of «استعينوا» is اسْتَعْوِنُوا, and what was done in {نَسْتَعِينُ} [al-Fātiḥa: 5] was done to it; its precise treatment and meaning have preceded. «وبالصبر» is attached to it, and the bāʾ is for instrument or for causation. That for which help is sought is omitted, so as to cover all the situations for which help is sought. «استعان» is transitive by itself, as in {وَإِيَّاكَ نَسْتَعِينُ} [al-Fātiḥa: 5]. The bāʾ may also be for the ḥāl, i.e. "clothed in patience". The apparent view is that it is transitive by itself and by the bāʾ: you say استَعَنْتُ [الله and استعنْتُ بالله]. It has preceded that the sīn is for seeking. Al-ṣabr: restraining oneself upon what is disliked; of this is «قُتِل فلانٌ صبراً» (so-and-so was killed in confinement). He said:
428 - فَصَبْراً في مجالِ الموتِ صَبْراً ... فما نَيْلُ الخلودِ بمُسْتَطَاعِ
(So patience in the arena of death, patience! For attaining immortality is not within one's power.)
His saying: {وَإِنَّهَا لَكَبِيرَةٌ إِلاَّ عَلَى الخاشعين}: inna, its noun and its khabar. As for the pronoun in «إنها», it has been said: it refers to the prayer, even though two things preceded, because it is more predominant and more important; it parallels His saying: {وَإِذَا رَأَوْاْ تِجَارَةً أَوْ لَهْواً انفضوا إِلَيْهَا} [al-Jumuʿa: 11], where He referred the pronoun to trade because it is more important and predominant — so it was said. This is questionable, because the conjoining there is with «أو», so the singular is obligatory; but what is meant is that He mentioned the more important of the two things, so it parallels it from this angle. It has also been said: it refers to the seeking of help understood from the verb, as in {هُوَ أَقْرَبُ} [al-Māʾida: 8]. And it has been said: to the worship indicated by patience and prayer. And it has been said: it refers to patience and prayer, even though it is in the singular; this amounts to nothing. And it has been said: it was omitted from the first because the second indicates it, the implied form being "and it is great", as in his saying:
429 - إنَّ شَرْخَ الشبابِ والشَّعْرَ الأسْ ... وَدَ ما لم يُعاصَ كان جُنوناً
(The prime of youth and black hair, so long as they are not resisted, are madness.)
His saying: {إِلاَّ عَلَى الخاشعين} is an emptied exception (istithnāʾ mufarragh). That is permissible even though the speech is affirmative, because it has the force of a negative, i.e. "it is not easy nor light except for these". So «على الخاشعين» is attached to «كبيرة», as in «كَبُر عليَّ هذا», i.e. it was great and hard for me. Al-khushūʿ is submission; its origin is softness and ease; of this is «الخُشْعَةُ» for a low-lying sand-hill, and in the ḥadīth: "It was a low mound upon the water, then afterwards it was spread out", i.e. the earth was soft. Al-Nābigha said:
430 - رَمادٌ ككُحْلِ العَيْنِ لأْيَا أُبِينُه ... ونُؤْيٌ كجِذْمِ الحَوْضِ أَثْلَمُ خاشِعُ
(Ashes like eye-kohl, which I can make out only with difficulty, and a trench like the base of a trough, broken and sunken.)
i.e. bearing the trace of abasement. Some distinguished between khuḍūʿ and khushūʿ, saying: khuḍūʿ is in the body specifically, while khushūʿ is in the body, the voice and the sight, so it is more general than it.

semin-durr:61-61.t:
The saying of the Exalted: {لَن نَّصْبِرَ على طَعَامٍ وَاحِدٍ}: [this is] a particle making the verb accusative (nāṣib) and its accusative verb, and the clause is in the position of the accusative governed by the saying. The discussion of «لن» has preceded. As for His saying «طعام واحد» ("one food"), when there were in fact two foods, the manna and the quails: [it is so] because what is meant by "one" is what does not vary or change, so what was intended is denying change and variety; or because they are a single kind, both being among the food of people of pleasure and luxury, [as though they said:] "we are people of farming and want only the varied things we are used to"; or because they used to eat one of them with the other; or because they were eaten at one time. It has also been said: they alluded thereby to wealth, as though they said: we will not be content for all of us to share in one thing, so that none of us serves another — and so they were; they were the first to take servants and slaves.
Al-ṭaʿām ("food") is a name for everything that is tasted (yuṭʿam), eaten or drunk; from it is {وَمَن لَّمْ يَطْعَمْهُ} [al-Baqara: 249]. It may be specific to certain foods, as in its specific use for wheat and dates; in the ḥadīth of [the] alms: «أو صاعاً من طعامٍ أو صاعاً من شعير» ("or a ṣāʿ of food or a ṣāʿ of barley"). Al-ṭaʿm with a fatḥa on the ṭāʾ is the maṣdar (verbal noun), or what is desired of food, or what taste conveys: you say "its taste is sweet" and "its taste is bitter". With a ḍamma (al-ṭuʿm) it is the thing eaten, like al-ukl and al-akl. Abū Khirāsh said:
496 - أَرُدُّ شُجاعَ البطنِ لو تَعْلَمِيْنَه ... وأُوْثِرُ غيري من عيالِك بالطَّعْمِ
وأَغْتَبِقُ الماءَ القُراحَ فأنتهي ... إذا الزادُ أمسى للمُزَلَّجِ ذا طَعْمِ
(I repel the serpent of hunger in my belly, if you only knew, and prefer others of your household to myself with food; and I take pure water as my evening drink and stop, when provisions have become something savoury for the base man.)
By the first he meant what is eaten, and by the second what is desired of it. It may also express giving: he, peace be upon him, said: «إذا اسْتَطْعَمَكم الإِمامُ فأطْعِموه» ("when the imam asks you to feed him, feed him"), i.e. when he seeks prompting [in recitation], prompt him. And: "So-and-so does not taste sleep except standing." [The poet] said:
497 - نَعاماً بوَجْرَةَ صُفْرَ الخُدو ... دِ ما تَطْعَمُ النَّومَ إلا صِياما
(Ostriches at Wajra, yellow-cheeked, which do not taste sleep except standing.)
His saying: {فادع}: the eloquent usage is «ادعُ» with a ḍamma on the ʿayn, from دَعَا يدعُو. The dialect of Banū ʿĀmir is فادْعِ with a kasra on the ʿayn. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "Because of the meeting of two quiescent letters; they treat the weak [verb] like the sound one and pay no regard to what is omitted", meaning that the ʿayn is quiescent because of the imperative and the dāl before it is quiescent, so the ʿayn was given a kasra. This is open to question, because the rule in this and the like is that the first of the two quiescent letters is given a kasra, not the second. So it may be that [in their dialect] it is دَعَى يَدْعي like رَمى يَرْمي. Al-duʿāʾ here is asking. It may also be in the sense of naming, as in his saying:
498 - دَعَتْني أخاها أمُّ عمروٍ. . . ... . . . . . . . . . . .
(Umm ʿAmr called me her brother…)
This has preceded. «لنا» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) it, and the lām is for cause.
His saying: «يُخْرِجْ» is jussive (majzūm) in answer to the command. Some said: "It is made jussive by an implied lām of command, i.e. لِيُخْرِجْ"; al-Zajjāj considered this weak. The discussion of the omission of the lām of command will come, if Allah the Exalted wills.
His saying: {مِمَّا تُنْبِتُ الأرض}: the object of «يُخْرِجْ» is omitted according to Sībawayh, its implied form being "something edible [of what]" or "something of what the earth grows". The preposition may be attached to the verb before it, «مِنْ» being for the beginning of the extent; or it may be an adjective of that omitted object, and so be attached to something implied, i.e. "something edible being of what the earth grows", «مِنْ» being partitive. The doctrine of al-Akhfash is that «مِنْ» is redundant (zāʾida) in the object, the implied form being "bring forth what the earth grows", because he does not stipulate any condition for its redundancy.
«ما» may be a nominal relative or an indefinite qualified noun, the returning pronoun being omitted, i.e. "of that which it grows" or "of something it grows". It may not be made maṣdariyya, because the omitted object cannot be described as "growing" (inbāt), since inbāt is a maṣdar and what is brought forth is a substance; likewise on the doctrine of al-Akhfash, because what is brought forth is a substance, not an act of growing.
His saying: {مِن بَقْلِهَا}: two options are possible in it. The first: that it is a badal (substitute) from «ما» with repetition of the governing word, «مِنْ» meaning explanation of the genus. The second: that it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the omitted pronoun referring to «ما», i.e. "of what the earth grows, while it is of its herbs", «مِنْ» also being for explanation. Al-baql is everything the earth grows of the najm, i.e. of what has no stem; its plural is buqūl. Al-qiththāʾ ("cucumbers") is well known; the singular is qiththāʾa, so it is of the category of qamḥ and qamḥa. There are two dialectal forms: the well-known one with a kasra on the qāf, and it has been read with a ḍamma. The hamza is radical in itself, [as shown] by their saying: أَقْثَأَتِ الأرضُ, i.e. its cucumbers became abundant. Its pattern is fiʿʿāl, and in its plural one says qathāʾī, like ʿilbāʾ and ʿalābī. Someone said: "Except that qiththāʾ is of the wāw roots: you say أَقْثَأْتُ القومَ, i.e. I fed them that; and فَثَأْتُ القِدْر, I calmed its boiling with water. [The poet] said:
499 - تفُورُ علينا قِدْرُهم فَنُديمُها ... ونَفْثَؤُها عَنَّا إذا حَمْيُها غَلا
(Their pot boils over against us, and we keep it simmering, and we calm it from us when its heat boils up.)"
This is a gross delusion on the part of this [speaker], because, having made it of the wāw roots, how can he adduce as evidence their saying «أَقْثَأْتُ القومَ» [with hamza]? Rather he ought to have said أَقْثَيْتُ, the original being أَقْثَوْتُ, but since the wāw occurs in a quadriliteral form it is changed into yāʾ, as in أَغْزَيْتُ from al-ghazw; and it ought to have been said فَثَوْتُ القِدْر with wāw, and the poet would have said نَفْثَوُها with wāw. Al-maqthaʾa and al-maqthuʾa, with fatḥa and ḍamma on the thāʾ, is the place of cucumbers. [Translator's note: the source says "with fatḥa and ḍamma on the tāʾ (التاء)"; the letter in question is the thāʾ.] Al-fūm is garlic (al-thūm); the fāʾ is substituted for the thāʾ: they said jadaf and jadath, ʿāthūr and ʿāfūr, maʿāthīr and maʿāfīr; but this is [not] by analogy. It has also been said: [it is] wheat, and Ibn ʿAbbās recited:
500 - قد كنتُ أغْنَى الناسِ شخصاً واحداً ... نَزَل المدينةَ عن زِراعة فُوْمِ
(I was the richest of men, a single person who came down to Medina from the cultivation of wheat.)
Other things have also been said.
His saying: «أَدْنى»: there are three views about it. The first, which is the apparent one and is the view of Abū Isḥāq al-Zajjāj, is that its original form is adnaw, from al-dunuww, which is nearness; the wāw was changed into an alif because it was vowelled and the letter before it had a fatḥa. The meaning of nearness in this has two aspects. The first: that it is "nearer" because of its low value and baseness. The second: that it is nearer to you because it is in this world, unlike that which is better, for by patience over it its benefit is obtained in the Hereafter. The second view is that of ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān al-Akhfash: its original is adnaʾ, with hamza, from دَنَأَ يَدْنَأُ دَناءة, which is the base thing, except that its hamza was lightened, as in his saying:
501 - . . . . . . . . . . . ... فارْعَيْ فَزارةُ لا هَناكِ المَرْتَعُ
(…so graze, Fazāra — may the pasture not be wholesome for you!)
This is indicated by the reading of Zuhayr al-Furqubī: «أَدْنَأُ» with hamza.
The third: its original is adwan, from al-shayʾ al-dūn, i.e. the inferior thing; it underwent metathesis, the middle radical being moved to the place of the final radical, so it became adnaw, and then it underwent weak-letter change as preceded; its pattern is aflaʿ. The meaning of al-istibdāl has preceded. «أدْنَى» is the khabar (predicate) of «هو», and the clause is a ṣila (relative clause) with its returning pronoun; likewise «هو خير» is also a ṣila with its returning pronoun.
His saying: «مِصْراً»: the majority read it with nunation, and that is the script of the muṣḥaf. It has been said: they were commanded to go down to one city (miṣr) among cities, and for that reason it is declined as a triptote. It has also been said: they were commanded [to go to] Miṣr (Egypt) itself, and it was only declined as a triptote because of its lightness, its middle letter being quiescent, like Hind and Daʿd; and [this verse] was recited:
502 - لم تَتَلَفَّعْ فَضْلِ مِئْزَرِها ... دَعْدٌ ولم تُسْقَ دَعْدُ في العُلَبِ
(Daʿd did not wrap herself in the surplus of her waist-wrapper, and Daʿd was not given drink in milking-bowls.)
So he combined the two treatments. Or it was declined as a triptote by taking it to mean "the place". Al-Ḥasan and others read «مصرَ» [without nunation], and so it is in some of the muṣḥafs of ʿUthmān and the muṣḥaf of Ubayy, as though they meant a particular place. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is Arabized from a foreign language, for its original is Miṣrāʾīm, and it was Arabized." On this [view], if it is said to be a proper name for a particular place, it ought not to be declined as a triptote at all, because foreignness is added to it, so it is parallel to Māh, Jawr and Ḥimṣ; for this reason the majority agreed on making it a diptote in His saying {ادخلوا مِصْرَ} [Yūsuf: 99]. Al-miṣr in the original language is "the boundary separating two things". It is related of the people of Hajar that when they wrote [a deed of] sale of a house they said: "So-and-so bought the house with its muṣūr", i.e. its boundaries. And [this verse] was recited:
503 - وجاعِلُ الشمسِ مِصْراً لا خَفَاءَ بهِ ... بين النهارِ وبينَ الليلِ قد فَصَلا
(And He who made the sun a boundary, with no obscurity in it, which has separated day and night.)
His saying: {مَّا سَأَلْتُمْ}: «ما» is in the position of the accusative as the noun (ism) of «إنَّ», and the khabar is in the preposition [phrase] before it. «ما» is in the sense of «الذي», the returning pronoun being omitted, i.e. "that which you asked for (سألتموه)". Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is weak for it to be an indefinite qualified noun", meaning that what they asked for was something specific, so it is not good that they be answered with something vague. It has been read «سِلْتُم», like بِعْتُم, taken from سالَ with alif. Ḥassān, may Allah be pleased with him, said:
504 - سَالَتْ هُذَيْلٌ رسولَ الله فاحِشَةً ... ضَلَّتْ هُذَيْلٌ بما سَالَتْ ولم تُصِبِ
(Hudhayl asked the Messenger of Allah for something obscene; Hudhayl went astray in what it asked and did not hit the mark.)
Is this alif changed from a yāʾ, or from a wāw — because of their saying يتساوَلان — or from a hamza? There are three views, whose explanation will come, if Allah wills, in Sūrat al-Maʿārij.
His saying: {وَضُرِبَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ الذلة والمسكنة}: «ضُرِبت» is passive, and «الذِّلَّةُ» stands in the place of the agent (nāʾib fāʿil). The meaning of «ضُرِبَتْ» is: they were made to bear it inseparably and it was decreed upon them, from the pitching (ḍarb) of tents. Al-Farazdaq said to Jarīr:
505 - ضَرَبَتْ عليك العنكبوتُ بِنَسْجِها ... وَقَضى عليكَ به الكتابُ المُنَزَّلُ
(The spider has spread its web over you, and the revealed Book has decreed it upon you.)
Al-dhilla is abasement. Al-dhull with ḍamma is what comes from subjugation, and with kasra (al-dhill) what comes after refractoriness without subjugation; al-Rāghib said this. Al-maskana is mafʿala from al-sukūn ("stillness"), because the poor man (miskīn) has little movement and rising, because of the poverty he suffers. Al-miskīn is mifʿīl from it, except that this mīm has become fixed in the derivation of this word: they said تَمَسْكَنَ يَتَمَسْكَنُ فهو مُتَمَسْكِنٌ, just as the mīm is fixed in تَمَنْدَلَ and تَمَدْرَعَ from al-nadl and al-darʿ; that does not indicate that it is radical, because derivation has ruled that it is additional.
Al-Rāghib said: "{وَضُرِبَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ الذلة والمسكنة}: the mīm in that is additional according to the sounder of the two views." Mentioning this disagreement implies that the nūn is additional and that it is from masaka. [Translator's note: the closing quotation mark in the source falls after "from masaka"; the precise extent of al-Rāghib's quotation is unclear.]
His saying: «وباؤُوا»: the alif of «باءَ بكذا» is changed from a wāw, because of their saying «باء يَبُوء», like قال يقول. He, peace and blessings be upon him, said: «أبُوْءُ بنعمتِك عليّ» ("I acknowledge Your blessing upon me"). The maṣdar is al-bawāʾ. Bāʾa means "returned". Someone recited:
506 - فآبُوا بالنَّهائِبِ والسَّبايا ... وأُبْنا بالمُلوكِ مُصَفَّدينا
(They returned with spoils and captives, and we returned with the kings in fetters.)
This is a mistake, because this verse is from the root آب يَؤُوب, whose root consists of hamza, wāw and bāʾ, while «باء» has the root bāʾ, wāw and hamza. Claiming metathesis in it is far-fetched, [because there is no known case of] both the middle and final radicals preceding the first radical in a metathesized form, and this would be such a case.
Al-bawāʾ is returning with retaliation (qawad); and "they are bawāʾ in this matter", i.e. equal. [The poet] said:
507 - ألا تَنْتَهي عنَّا مُلُوكٌ وتَتَّقي ... محارِمَنا لا يَبْوُؤُ الدمُ بالدَّمِ
(Will not kings desist from us and fear [violating] our sanctities? Blood is not requited with [mere] blood.)
i.e. blood is not returned for blood in retaliation. باءَ بكذا also means "he acknowledged", and from it is the ḥadīth mentioned before, i.e. "I acknowledge it [and bind myself to it]". [The poet] said:
508 - أَنْكَرْتُ باطِلَها وبُؤْتُ بحقِّها ... . . . . . . . . . . .
(I rejected its falsehood and acknowledged its truth…)
Al-Rāghib said: "The basic meaning of al-bawāʾ is the equality of parts in a place, the opposite of al-nabwa, which is the incompatibility of parts. His saying «وباؤُوا بغضبٍ» means they settled in an abode (mabwaʾ) accompanied by wrath. The use of «باء» draws attention to the fact that even in their suitable place the wrath of Allah clings to them, so how much more in other places; that is like {فَبَشِّرْهم بعذاب} [Āl ʿImrān: 21]." Then he said: "And the saying of whoever said that «بُؤْتُ بحقِّها» means 'I acknowledged' is not an explanation according to what the wording requires. And their saying حَيّاك الله وبَيَّاك: its original is بَوَّأَك ('He settled you'), and it was only altered for the sake of matching [the preceding word]; Khalaf al-Aḥmar said this."
His saying: «بغضب» is in the position of a ḥāl from the agent of «باؤوا», i.e. they returned as objects of wrath; it is not a direct object, as in مررتُ بزيدٍ. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is from your saying: باء فلانٌ بفلان, when he is deserving of being killed in retaliation for him because of his being equal and comparable to him, i.e. they became deserving of His wrath." This explanation negates the bāʾ being for the ḥāl.
His saying: «مِن الله»: the apparent [view] is that it is in the position of the genitive as an adjective of «غضب», so it is attached to something omitted, i.e. "with a wrath being from Allah", «مِنْ» being for the beginning of the extent figuratively. It has also been said: it is attached to the verb itself, i.e. "they returned from Allah with wrath"; this is not strong.
The saying of the Exalted: {ذَلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ}: «ذلك» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) by which reference is made to what preceded of the imposing of abasement and poverty and the "succession with wrath" (al-khilāfa bi-l-ghaḍab) [Translator's note: so in the source; the context suggests their "returning with wrath" (al-bawʾ bi-l-ghaḍab)], and «بأنهم» is the khabar. The bāʾ is causal, i.e. "that is deserved because of their unbelief". Al-Mahdawī said: "The bāʾ is in the sense of the lām, i.e. because they (لأنهم)." There is no need for this, for the causal bāʾ conveys causation by itself. «يكفرون» is in the position of the accusative as the khabar of «كان»; «كان» and what is in its scope are in the position of the nominative as the khabar of «أنَّ»; «أنَّ» and what is in its scope are in the position of the genitive by the bāʾ; and the bāʾ and what is in its scope are in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, as preceded.
His saying: «بآيات الله» is attached to «يكفرون», and the bāʾ is for transitivity.
His saying: «ويقتُلون» is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the khabar of «كان». It has been read «تَقْتُلون» in the second person, by iltifāt (shift of person) back to the earlier address after the third person; and «يُقَتِّلونَ» with doubling, for multiplicity.
His saying: «الأنبياءَ» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), plural of nabiyy. The readers do not pronounce the hamza in al-nubuwwa and its derived forms, while Nāfiʿ al-Madanī pronounces the hamza in all of them except two places in Sūrat al-Aḥzāb: «للنبيِّ إن أراد» and «[لا تَدْخُلوا] بيوتَ النبيِّ إلاَّ», for Qālūn related of him in continuous recitation [the same] as the generality; this will come. As for those who pronounce the hamza, they make it derived from al-nabaʾ, which is news; so al-nabiyy is faʿīl in the sense of fāʿil, i.e. one who informs from Allah of His message; it may also be in the sense of mafʿūl, i.e. he is informed by Allah of His commands and prohibitions. They adduced as evidence for that its plural nubaʾāʾ, like ẓarīf and ẓurafāʾ. Al-ʿAbbās ibn Mirdās said:
509 - يا خاتَم النُّبَآء إنَّك مُرْسَلٌ ... بالخيرِ، كلُّ هدى السبيلِ هُداكا
(O Seal of the Prophets, you are sent with good; all right guidance of the way is your guidance.)
The appearance of the two hamzas indicates that it is from al-nabaʾ. Some grammarians considered this reading weak. Abū ʿAlī said: "Sībawayh said: 'It has reached us that some people who pronounce the hamza fully pronounce nabīʾ and barīʾa [with hamza]'; he said: 'and it is poor'. He only considered it poor because the predominant [usage] is lightening." Abū ʿUbayd said: "The great majority of readers and common people drop the hamza from al-nabiyy and al-anbiyāʾ, and so do most of the Arabs, together with a ḥadīth we have narrated" — and he mentioned that a man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "O Nabīʾa Allah", with hamza, and he said: "I am not Nabīʾa Allah" — with hamza — "but Nabiyyu Allah" — without hamza; so he objected to the hamza. He said: "And Abū ʿUbayda said to me: the Arabs replace the hamza in three words: al-nabiyy, al-bariyya and al-khābiya, and their original is with hamza." Abū ʿUbayda said: "And among them is a fourth word: al-dhurriyya, from ذرأ يذرأ." What indicates that the original is with hamza is the saying of Sībawayh that all of them say تنبَّأ مسيلمة ("Musaylima claimed prophethood") with hamza. By this, the reading of this great imām ought not to be rejected. As for the ḥadīth, they have declared it weak. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "Among what strengthens its weakness is that when al-ʿAbbās recited to him «يا خاتم النُّبآء» he did not object to it, and there is no difference between the plural and the singular." But this ḥadīth has been mentioned by al-Ḥākim in al-Mustadrak, and he said: it is sound according to the condition of the two Shaykhs [al-Bukhārī and Muslim], though they did not include it. I say: if that is so, then an interpretation of the ḥadīth should be sought which serves as an answer regarding the reading of Nāfiʿ — although what is definitive is not opposed by what is probabilistic; we only mention it as an additional benefit. The answer regarding the ḥadīth is that Abū Zayd related: "نَبَأْتُ من أرضِ كذا إلى أَرض كذا", i.e. "I went out from it to it". So his saying «يا نبيءَ الله» with hamza suggests "O outcast of Allah", whom He drove out of his land to another; so he forbade him that because of its suggesting what we mentioned, not for a reason connected with the reading.
Parallel to that is his forbidding the believers from saying «راعِنا», when the Jews found in it a way of using it to insult in their language. Or it is an urging on his part, peace be upon him, to seek the most eloquent of the dialects in the Quran and elsewhere.
As for those who do not pronounce the hamza, two possibilities exist. The first: that it is from the hamzated [root] but lightened; this is preferable, so that it agrees with both readings, and because of the appearance of the hamza in their saying تَنَبَّأ مُسَيلَمَةُ and in his saying «يا خاتَم النُّبآء». The second: that it is another root by itself, derived from نَبا ينبو, when a thing appears and rises high; and there is no doubt that the rank of the Prophet is elevated and his station manifest, unlike the rest of creation. The original is nabīwun and anbiwāʾ: yāʾ and wāw came together, the first of them quiescent, so the wāw was changed into yāʾ and assimilated, as in mayyit from maywit; and in the plural the letter before the wāw had a kasra, so it was changed into yāʾ, and it became anbiyāʾ. The wāw in al-nubuwwa is a substitute for the hamza on the first [view] and radical in itself on the second. So it is faʿīl in the sense of fāʿil, i.e. manifest and elevated; or in the sense of mafʿūl, i.e. Allah has raised him above His creation. Or it may be taken from al-nabiyy, which is the road, because the Prophet is the road of Allah to His creation, by which they reach knowledge of their Creator. The poet said:
510 - لمَّا وَرَدْنَ نُبَيَّاً واسْتَتَبَّ بِنا ... مُسْحَنْفِرٌ كخُطوطِ النَّسْجِ مُنْسَحِلُ
(When they reached a road, and a wide, smooth path like the lines of weaving stretched straight before us.)
i.e. a road. And [another] said:
511 - لأَصْبَحَ رَتْماً دُقاقُ الحَصَى ... مكانَ النَّبِيِّ من الكاثِبِ
(The fine pebbles would have become crushed, in the place of the road (or: the height) at al-Kāthib.)
Al-ratm, with the dotted tāʾ and with the thāʾ alike, is breaking; and al-Kāthib, with the thāʾ, is the name of a mountain. In the diminutive of the prophethood of Musaylima they said: nubayyiʾa. They also said: its plural anbiyāʾ is a regular analogy for weak faʿīl, like waliyy and awliyāʾ, ṣafiyy and aṣfiyāʾ. As for Qālūn, he only omitted the hamza in the two places mentioned for another reason, namely that it is part of his method, when two hamzas with kasra come together across two words, to soften the first, unless a letter of prolongation precedes it, in which case it is replaced and assimilated. So he was bound to do here what he did in «بالسوء إلاَّ», namely replacement and assimilation — except that a disagreement is related from him regarding «بالسوء إلاَّ», while no disagreement is related from him here, as though he made the replacement binding because of the frequent use of this word and its kind. So in reality he did not omit the hamza of «النبيّ»; rather he pronounced it with hamza, and once he did so, the analogy of lightening it led him to that. What indicates this consideration is that he only does that where he continues [the recitation]; when he pauses, he pronounces the hamza in the two places because the said cause disappears. So he omits the hamza in pronunciation while bringing it in the underlying form.
The saying of the Exalted: {بِغَيْرِ الحق} is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the agent of «يَقْتُلون», its implied form being: "they kill them while acting falsely". It may also be an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, its implied form being "a killing that is without right", and so be attached to something omitted. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The killing of prophets can only be without right, so what is the benefit of mentioning it?" And he answered that its meaning is that they killed them without right even in their own view, because they [the prophets] had not killed nor caused corruption in the land so as to be killed; had they been asked and been fair to themselves, they would not have mentioned any ground by which they deserved killing in their view. It has also been said: their description by that only came out as a description of their killing, that it was a wrong against them, attached [to them]; and this is more forceful in [expressing] the hideousness and magnitude of their sins.
His saying: {ذلك بِمَا عَصَواْ} is like what preceded. There are two views concerning the repetition of the demonstrative. The first: that it points to what the first pointed to, by way of emphasis. The second is what al-Zamakhsharī said: that it points to the unbelief and the killing of the prophets, in the sense that that was because of their disobedience and transgression, because they were absorbed in them. «ما» is maṣdariyya and the bāʾ is causal, i.e. because of their disobedience, so «عَصَوا» has no grammatical position, occurring as a ṣila. The original of عَصَوْا is ʿaṣayū: the yāʾ was vowelled and the letter before it had a fatḥa, so it was changed into an alif; two quiescent letters met, it and the wāw, so it was deleted because it was the first of the two quiescent letters, and the fatḥa remained to indicate it; so its pattern is faʿaw. «وكانوا يعتدُون»: [the verb] is in the position of the accusative as the khabar of «كان», and «كان» and what follows it are conjoined to the ṣila of the maṣdariyya «ما».
The basic meaning of al-ʿiṣyān is hardness: اعتصَتِ النَّواةُ, "the date-stone became hard". Al-iʿtidāʾ is overstepping, from عدا يعدُو, so it is iftiʿāl from it. The object of the disobedience and transgression is not mentioned so that it includes everything in which disobedience and transgression occur.
The original of «يَعْتَدُون» is yaʿtadiyūna; what was done with {يتَّقون} [al-Baqara: 21] of deletion and weak-letter change was done with it, as preceded, so its pattern is yaftaʿūn. The wāw of «عَصَوْا» must be assimilated into the wāw after it because the letter before it has a fatḥa, so it has no prolongation preventing assimilation; similarly {فَقَدِ اهتدوا وَّإِن تَوَلَّوْاْ} [Āl ʿImrān: 20]. This is unlike when the letter before the wāw has a ḍamma, for then the prolongation stands as a barrier between the two identical letters, so pronouncing them distinctly is obligatory, as in {آمَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ} [al-Baqara: 25], and similarly {الذى يُوَسْوِسُ} [al-Baqara: 126]. [Translator's note: {الذى يُوَسْوِسُ} is al-Nās: 5, not al-Baqara: 126, and it illustrates a yāʾ rather than a wāw; translated as written.]

semin-durr:138-138.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {صِبْغَةَ الله}: The majority read «صبغةَ» in the accusative. Al-Ṭabarī said: "Whoever read «مِلَّةُ إبراهيمَ» in the nominative read «صبغةُ» in the nominative", and it has preceded that it is the reading of Ibn Hurmuz and Ibn Abī ʿAbla. As for the reading of the majority, there are four aspects in it. The first: that its accusative is the accusative of the emphasising maṣdar (verbal noun); al-Zamakhsharī chose this and said: "It is what Sībawayh mentioned, and the word is what Ḥadhām said" — end of his statement. «[Translator's note: "the word is what Ḥadhām said" is a proverb meaning "his authority settles the matter".]» There was then disagreement about what this maṣdar is in the accusative from: it was said, from His saying {وَنَحْنُ لَهُ مُسْلِمُونَ}, and it was said, from His saying {فَقَدِ اهتدوا}. The second: that its accusative is by way of incitement (al-ighrāʾ), i.e.: hold to the dye of Allah. The Shaykh said: "This is at odds with the end of the verse, namely His saying {وَنَحْنُ لَهُ عَابِدونَ}, unless a verb of saying is implied here — and that is an implication for which there is no need and no evidence in the speech." The third: that it is a badal (substitute) from «مِلَّةَ»; and this is weak, since the separation between them has occurred through many clauses. The fourth: its accusative by an implied verb, i.e.: follow the dye of Allah; Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned it together with the aspect of incitement, but in reality it is not an additional [aspect], for incitement too is accusative by an implied verb.

Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It — i.e. al-ṣibgha — is from ṣabagha, like al-jilsa from jalasa; it is the state in which the dyeing takes place. The meaning is Allah's purification, because faith purifies souls. The origin of it is that the Christians used to immerse their children in the water of baptism (al-maʿmūdiyya) and say it was a purification for them; so the Muslims were commanded to say: We have believed, and Allah has dyed us with a dye not like your dye. The word «الصِّبْغَة» was brought only by way of mushākala (correspondence of expression), as you say to someone who plants trees: Plant as so-and-so plants — meaning a man who fabricates speech." «[Translator's note: the source reads «يصطنعُ الكلامَ» ("fabricates speech"); in al-Kashshāf the phrase is «يصطنع الكرم» ("practises generosity"), which fits the example.]»

As for the nominative reading, it admits two aspects. The first: that it is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e.: that faith is the dye of Allah. The second: that it is a badal from «مِلَّة», because whoever made «صِبْغَة» nominative made «مِلَّة» nominative, as has preceded, so it is a badal from it, just as was said of that in the accusative reading.

His saying: {وَمَنْ أَحْسَنُ}: A mubtadaʾ and khabar. This is a question whose meaning is negation, i.e.: no one. «أَحْسَنُ» here has two possibilities. The first: that it is not for preference (tafḍīl), since goodness is negated from any dye other than Allah's. The second: that preference is intended with respect to someone who supposes there is some good in a dye other than Allah's, not that this is with respect to the reality of the thing. «مِنَ الله» is attached to «أحسنُ», so it is in the position of accusative. And «صبغةً» is accusative as a tamyīz (specification) of «أَحْسَنُ», and it is of the tamyīz transferred from the mubtadaʾ, the implied form being: "and whose dye is better than the dye of Allah?" So the preference runs only between the two dyes, not between the two dyers. And this is strange — I mean the tamyīz's being transferred from the mubtadaʾ.

His saying: {وَنَحْنُ لَهُ عَابِدونَ}: A clause made of a mubtadaʾ and khabar, conjoined to His saying {قولوا آمَنَّا بالله}, so it is in the position of accusative by the verb of saying. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "This conjunction refutes the view of whoever claimed that «صبغة الله» is a badal from «مِلَّةَ», or accusative by way of incitement in the sense of 'upon you is the dye of Allah', because of what that involves of breaking the arrangement and taking the speech out of its cohesion and order." The Shaykh said: "And his construing it, in [the case of] incitement, as 'upon you (ʿalaykum) the dye' is not good; because when incitement is done with adverbs and prepositional phrases, it is not permissible to omit that adverb or prepositional phrase; and for that reason, when we mentioned the aspect of incitement, we construed it as 'hold to the dye of Allah'."
