End quote. It is as though, because governing by adverbs and prepositional phrases is weak, their omission while keeping their governing effect is weak.

semin-durr:139-139.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {أَتُحَآجُّونَنَا}: The question here is for disapproval and rebuke. The majority read «أتحاجُّوننا» with two nūns, the first for the nominative and the second the nūn of «نا». Zayd, al-Ḥasan and al-Aʿmash read it with assimilation (idghām), and some permitted eliding the first nūn. As for the reading of the majority, it is clear. As for the reading with assimilation, it is because two similar letters came together, and what made the assimilation acceptable is the presence of a letter of prolongation and softness before it, which stands in place of a vowel. As for whoever elides, it is by analogy with the nūn of protection (nūn al-wiqāya), as in the reading {فَبِمَ تُبَشِّرُونَ} [al-Ḥijr: 54], and his saying:
750 - تَراه كالثَّغام يُعَلُّ مِسْكاً ... يَسُوءُ الفالياتِ إذا فَلَيْني
(You see it [my hair] like the white thaghām plant, drenched again and again with musk; it grieves the women who delouse me when they delouse me.)
meaning «فلينني». This verse is like His saying {أَفَغَيْرَ الله تأمروني أَعْبُدُ} [al-Zumar: 64], for it was read with the three aspects — separation, assimilation and elision — but in the mutawātir readings; whereas here it was read in the well-known [readings] only with separation, as has preceded. The position of this clause is accusative by the verb of saying before it. The pronoun in «قل» may be for the Prophet, peace be upon him, or for everyone fit to be addressed; and the nominative pronoun in «أتحاجُّوننا» is for the Jews and the Christians, or for the Arab polytheists. Al-muḥājja is a mufāʿala (reciprocal form) from ḥajjahu yaḥujjuhu (to overcome in argument). And His saying «في الله» requires the omission of a muḍāf (annexed noun), i.e.: concerning the affair of Allah or the religion of Allah.

His saying: {وَهُوَ رَبُّنَا}: A mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate) in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and likewise what is conjoined to it, namely His saying «ولنا أعمالُنا»; and a muḍāf must be omitted, i.e.: the recompense of our deeds, and for you the recompense of your deeds.

semin-durr:91-91.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {وَيَكْفُرونَ بِمَا وَرَآءَهُ}: two views are permissible regarding this clause. The first: that it is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya), begun anew to report that they disbelieve in what is other than the Torah, so it has no grammatical position. The second: that it is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. «وهم يكفرون» ("while they disbelieve"), the clause being in the position of accusative (manṣūb) as a ḥāl (circumstantial), its governor being «قالوا», i.e. they said "we believe" while disbelieving in such-and-such. Its governor cannot be «نؤمن»; Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "For if it were so, the wording of the ḥāl would be «ونكفر» or «ونحن نكفر»" — meaning that agreement would then be required. This mubtadaʾ must be supplied because of what preceded, namely that an affirmative imperfect is not joined with the wāw; it is parallel to his saying:
613 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... نَجَوْتُ وأَرْهَنُهُمْ مالِكا
(... I escaped, leaving them Mālik as a pledge.)
The fāʿil (agent) was omitted from His saying {بِمَا أَنْزَلَ} and the object was put in its place [i.e. the verb is passive] because it is known, since none sends down the heavenly scriptures but Allah; or because it has been mentioned before in His saying {بِمَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ}.
His saying: {بِمَا وَرَآءَهُ} is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يَكْفرون». «ما» is a relative noun and the adverbial phrase (ẓarf) is its ṣila (relative clause), so what it is attached to can only be a verb. The hāʾ in «وراءه» refers back to «ما» in His saying {نُؤْمِنُ بِمَآ أُنْزِلَ}. «وراء» is one of the adverbs of moderate inflectability; it is an adverb of place. The well-known view is that it means "behind", and it may mean "in front", so it is one of the words with opposite meanings (aḍdād). Al-Farrāʾ explained it here as meaning «سِوَى», which means «غَيْر» ("other than"), while Abū ʿUbayda and Qatāda explained it as meaning «بعد» ("after"). There are two views about its hamza. The first: that it is radical in itself; Ibn Jinnī held this, adducing its persistence in the diminutive in their saying «وُرَيْئَة». The second: that it is from yāʾ, because of their saying «تَوَارَيْتَ»; Abū al-Baqāʾ said this, and it is questionable. The hamza cannot be a substitute for wāw, because a word whose first radical is wāw does not have wāw as its final radical except rarely, as in «واو», the name of the letter of the alphabet. Its ruling is the ruling of «قبل» and «بعد» in that when annexed it is declinable, and when cut off [from annexation] it is indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma. Al-Akhfash cited for that the poet's saying:
614 - إذا أنا لم أُومِنْ عليكَ ولم يَكُنْ ... لقاؤُك إلا مِنْ وراءُ وراءُ وراءُ
(If I am not given safety in coming to you, and meeting you is only from behind, behind, behind...)
And in the ḥadīth about Ibrāhīm ﷺ: "I was an intimate friend only from behind, behind." The persistence of the [feminine] hāʾ in its diminutive is anomalous, because in the diminutive of a feminine [noun] of more than three letters the hāʾ does not persist except in two words that are anomalous, namely «وُرَيْئَة» and «قُدَيْدِيمة», the diminutives of «وراء» and «قُدَّام». Ibn ʿUṣfūr said: "Because they are not inflectable, so had they not been made feminine in the diminutive, it would have been imagined that they were masculine."
His saying: {وَهُوَ الحق} is a mubtadaʾ and khabar, and the clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl, its governor being His saying «ويَكفرون» and its possessor the fāʿil of «يكفرون». Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed the governor to be the [notion of] settledness (istiqrār) contained in His saying {بِمَا وَرَآءَهُ}, i.e. "in what is settled behind it, while it is the truth."
His saying: {مُصَدِّقاً} is an emphasising ḥāl (ḥāl muʾakkida), because His saying {وَهُوَ الحق} already contains its meaning. An emphasising ḥāl either emphasises its governor, as in:
{وَلاَ تَعْثَوْاْ فِي الأرض مُفْسِدِينَ} [al-Baqara: 60], or emphasises the content of a clause. If it is the second, its governor must be implied and it must come after the clause. Like it is what Sībawayh cited:
615 - أنا ابنُ دارةُ مَعْروفاً بها نَسَبي ... وهَلْ بدارةَ لَلنَّاسِ مِنْ عَارِ
(I am the son of Dāra, my lineage being known by her — and is there, for people, any shame in Dāra?)
The implied form is: "and it is the truth — I hold it true — confirming," and "the son of Dāra — I am known — known." This is the construal of the grammarians' speech. As for Abū al-Baqāʾ, he said: "«مصدقاً» is an emphasising [Translator's note: the source misprints «مركِّدة» for «مؤكِّدة»] ḥāl, and its governor is the verbal meaning in «الحقّ», since the meaning is: 'and it is established, confirming.' The possessor of the ḥāl is the latent pronoun in «الحقّ» according to some, and according to others the possessor of the ḥāl is a pronoun indicated by the speech" — and «الحقّ» is a maṣdar (verbal noun) that does not bear a pronoun in the way the active participle bears it according to them. So his saying "according to others" is what I presented first, and it is the correct view.
His saying: {فَلِمَ تَقْتُلُونَ}: the fāʾ is the apodosis (jawāb) of an implied condition, its implied form being: "if you have believed in what was sent down to you, then why did you kill the prophets?" This is giving them the lie, because belief in the Torah is incompatible with killing the noblest of His creation. «لِمَ» is a preposition and its genitive noun: the lām is a preposition and «ما» is interrogative, in the position of genitive, i.e. "for what thing?" But its alif was elided to distinguish it from the informative (khabariyya) «ما». The interrogative may be treated like the informative, so that its alif is retained; the poet said:
616 - على ما قامَ يَشْتِمُني لئيمٌ ... كخنزيرٍ تمرَّغَ في رَمادِ
(For what reason did a base man rise up to revile me, like a pig rolling in ashes?)
This should be restricted to poetic necessity, as some have stated explicitly, but al-Zamakhsharī allows it and explains some verses of the Quran on that basis. Likewise the informative may be treated like the interrogative in elision, in their saying «اصنعْ بِمَ شِئْتَ» ("do with what you wish") — this is merely due to verbal resemblance. When one pauses on the interrogative «ما» in the genitive: if it is in the genitive by a noun, the hāʾ of pausing (hāʾ al-sakt) must be attached, as in «مَجيء مَهْ» ("the coming of what?"); if it is in the genitive by a particle, attaching it is preferred. The difference is that the particle blends with what it enters upon, so the interrogative is strengthened by it, unlike the noun annexed to it, which is intended to be separate. This pause is permissible only when being tested (ibtilāʾ) or for running out of breath; and certainly some forbade pausing in this way, saying: "Because if one pauses without hāʾ it is a mistake, because of the loss of a letter, and if one pauses with hāʾ one contradicts the written text (al-sawād)." However, al-Bazzī paused with the hāʾ, and such a thing is not counted as contradicting the written text — do you not see that they retain some of the additional yāʾs (yāʾāt al-zawāʾid)? The preposition is attached to His saying «تقتلون», but it was necessarily fronted before it, because its genitive noun has the right to the head of the speech. The fāʾ and what follows it, «تقتلون», are in the position of jussive. «تقتلون», though in the form of the imperfect, has the meaning of the past because the meaning is understood, and also because His saying «من قبل» is with it. The killing could be attributed to them although they did not do it, because, since they were pleased with their forebears' deed, they were treated as though they themselves had done it.
His saying: {إِن كُنْتُمْ مُّؤْمِنِينَ}: there are two views on «إنْ». The first: that it is conditional and its apodosis is omitted, its implied form being: "if you are believers, then why did you do that?" So the condition and its apodosis have been repeated twice: the condition was omitted from the first clause and its apodosis remained, namely «فَلِمَ تقتلون», and the apodosis was omitted from the second and its condition remained; so from each one there was omitted what was retained in the other. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "Its apodosis precedes it, namely His saying «فَلِمَ»" — and this is possible only according to the view of the Kufans and Abū Zayd. The second: that «إنْ» is negating, meaning «ما», i.e. "you were not believers," because what issued from you is incompatible with belief.

semin-durr:92-92.t: His saying, Exalted is He: {بالبينات}: two views are permissible in it. The first: that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «موسى», i.e. he came to you possessing clear proofs and arguments, or with the clear proofs with him. The second: that it is an object [Translator's note: i.e. a dependent expressing cause], i.e. "by reason of establishing the clear proofs." The like of the clauses after it has preceded, so there is no need to repeat it.

semin-durr:93-93.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {وَأُشْرِبُواْ}: it may be conjoined to His saying «قالوا سَمِعْنا»; and it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «قالوا», i.e. they said that while they had been made to drink. «قد» must then be supplied, to bring the past close to the present — contrary to the Kufans, who said it is not needed. It may also be resumptive, merely to report that; Abū al-Baqāʾ considered this weak, saying: "Because He said after that: {قُلْ بِئْسَمَا يَأْمُرُكُمْ بِهِ}, which is the reply to their saying «سَمِعْنا وعَصَيْنا»; so it is more appropriate that there be nothing extraneous between them." The wāw in «أُشْرِبوا» is the first object, standing in place of the fāʿil [i.e. as nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent)], and the second is «العِجْلَ», because «شَرِبَ» is transitive by itself, and the hamza gave it another object. Two muḍāfs must be omitted before «العِجْل», the implied form being: «وأُشْرِبوا حُبَّ عبادةِ العِجْلِ» ("they were made to drink the love of worshipping the calf"). What made the omission of these two muḍāfs good is hyperbole in that, as though the calf itself were imagined to have been given them to drink. «الإشراب» is the mixing of a liquid with a solid; then its usage was extended until it was said of colours, as in «أُشْرِبَ بياضُه حُمْرةً» ("his whiteness was imbued with redness"). The meaning is that the love of worshipping it entered into them as dye enters a garment. Of this is:
617 - إذا ما القلبُ أُشْرِبَ حُبَّ شيءٍ ... فلا تَأْمَلْ له الدهرَ انْصِرافَا
(When the heart has been made to drink the love of something, do not ever hope for it to turn away.)
He expressed it with drinking rather than eating because drink penetrates to the inside of a thing, unlike eating, which passes through. Of this in meaning is:
618 - جَرَى حبُّها مَجْرى دَمي في مَفاصِلي ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Love of her ran the course of my blood through my joints...)
And one of them said:
619 - تَغَلْغَلَ حُبُّ عَثْمَةَ في فؤادي ... فبادِيه مع الخافي يَسيرُ
تَغَلْغَلَ حيثُ لم يَبْلُغْ شرابٌ ... ولا حُزْنٌ ولم يَبْلُغْ سُرورُ
أكادُ إذا ذَكَرْتُ العهدَ مِنْها ... أطيرُ لو أن إنساناً يَطيرُ
(Love of ʿAthma penetrated my heart, its manifest part travelling with its hidden part; it penetrated where no drink has reached, nor grief, nor has joy reached; when I recall the time spent with her I almost fly — if only a human being could fly.)
It was also said: the "making to drink" here is literal, because it is narrated that Mūsā, upon him be peace, filed the calf with a file, then put those filings in water and ordered them to drink it, and whoever loved the calf, the filings appeared on his lips. Although al-Suddī, Ibn Jurayj and others held this, it is refuted by His saying «في قُلوبهم» ("in their hearts").
His saying: «بكُفْرهم»: there are two views on it. The more apparent: that it [the bāʾ] is causal, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أُشْرِبوا», i.e. they were made to drink because of their previous disbelief. The second: that it means «مع» ("with"), by which they mean that it is for the ḥāl, its possessor in reality being that omitted muḍāf, i.e. they were made to drink the love of worshipping the calf mixed with their disbelief. The maṣdar (verbal noun) is annexed to its fāʿil, i.e. "by their having disbelieved." {قُلْ بِئْسَمَا يَأْمُرُكُمْ} is like His saying {بِئْسَمَا اشتروا} [al-Baqara: 90], so let one refer to it.
His saying: {إِن كُنْتُمْ مُّؤْمِنِينَ}: the two preceding views are permissible regarding it, namely its being negating or conditional, its apodosis (jawāb) being omitted, its implied form being: "then wretched is what it commands you." It was also said: its implied form is: "then do not kill Allah's prophets, nor belie the messengers, nor conceal the truth." He attributed belief to them in mockery of them, and there is no need to omit an adjective, i.e. "your false belief," or to omit a muḍāf, i.e. "the possessor of your belief." Al-Ḥasan read «بِهُو إيمانُكُمْ» with ḍamma on the hāʾ along with the wāw, and it has preceded that it is the original form.

semin-durr:103-103.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {وَلَوْ أَنَّهُمْ آمَنُواْ}: «لو» here — there are two views about it. One: that it is in its proper sense, being a particle for what would have occurred upon the occurrence of something else; the discussion of its apodosis will come. Al-Zamakhsharī permitted it to be for wishing, i.e. "would that they had believed", by way of figurative expression for Allah's willing their faith and their choosing it; on this view it need not have an apodosis, because in that case it may be answered with the fāʾ. In his words there is Muʿtazilism, whose place is other than this book.
And «أنهم آمنوا» is interpreted as a maṣdar (interpreted maṣdar) in the position of the nominative (marfūʿ). There is disagreement about that in two views. One — the view of Sībawayh: that it is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being "and if their faith were established"; the occurrence of a noun after «لو» is anomalous, even though it is specific to verbs, just as the accusative of «غُدْوَةً» after «لَدُنْ» is anomalous. It has also been said: this mubtadaʾ does not need a khabar, because the wording of the predicate and the subject run within the ṣila of «أَنَّ»; the Shaykh judged this correct in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ; and this resembles the disagreement about «أنَّ» occurring after ẓanna and its sisters, the precise statement of which has preceded; and Allah knows best. The second — the view of al-Mubarrad: that it is in the position of the nominative as an agent (fāʿil), whose governor is omitted, its implied form being "and if their faith had been established", because only a verb, overt or implied, follows it. Some rejected this on the ground that a verb is not implied after it unless explained by a verb like it; and this is held against al-Mubarrad. Each of the two views has proofs, and this is not their place. About the pronoun in «أنهم» there are two views: one, that it refers to the Jews; the second, to those who teach sorcery.
His saying: {لَمَثُوبَةٌ مِّنْ عِندِ الله}: about this lām there are two views. One: that it is the lām of commencement [Translator's note: the source has «لامُ لامُ», a duplication], and what follows it is a resumption reporting that, not connected to their faith and piety nor consequent upon it; on this view the apodosis of «لو» is omitted, if it is said that it is not for wishing — or if it is said that it is for wishing and has an apodosis — its implied form being: "they would have been rewarded". The second: that it is the apodosis of «لو», for «لو» may be answered with a nominal clause. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The nominal clause was preferred to the verbal in the apodosis of «لو» because of what it carries of indication of the permanence and stability of the reward, just as one turned from the accusative to the nominative in «سلامٌ عليكم»." The occurrence of the apodosis of «لو» as a nominal clause is open to objection, needing evidence other than the point in dispute. The Shaykh said: "The occurrence of a nominal clause as the apodosis of «لو» is not known in the speech of the Arabs; only this, whose explanation is disputed, has come, and universal rules are not established by what is open to more than one interpretation."
About «مَثُوبة» there are two views. One: that its pattern is mafʿūla, the original being mathwūba; the ḍamma was heavy on the wāw so it was transferred to the vowelless letter before it, then two vowelless letters met and one of them was dropped, like maqūla, majūza, maṣūn and mashūb. Maṣdars have come on the pattern mafʿūl, like al-maʿqūl, so it is a maṣdar (verbal noun); al-Wāḥidī transmitted that.
The second: that it is mafʿula from al-thawāb, with ḍamma on the middle radical, the ḍamma having merely been transferred from it to the thāʾ. One also says «مَثْوَبة» with sukūn on the thāʾ and fatḥa on the wāw; by rights it should have undergone weakening, so that one would say «مَثابة» like maqāma, but they kept it sound, as they kept sound makwaza among proper names; and Abū al-Sammāl and Qatāda read thus, like mashwara. The meaning of «لَمَثُوبة» is: reward and recompense from Allah [Translator's note: the source has «في من الله», apparently corrupt]. It has been said: a return to Allah.
His saying: {مِّنْ عِندِ الله} is in the position of the nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of «مَثُوبة», so it is attached to (mutaʿalliq) something omitted, i.e. "a reward being from Allah". The ʿindiyya ("with-ness") here is figurative, as preceded in its counterparts. The Shaykh said: "This description is what licenses beginning with an indefinite." I say: there is no need for this, because the licensing factor here is something else, namely resting on the lām of commencement, so that even if one said in speech «لَمَثُوبة خيرٌ» without description it would be valid. The indefiniteness in «لَمَثُوبَةٌ» conveys that something of reward — even if little — is better; therefore it is not called little. Its counterpart is: {وَرِضْوَانٌ مِّنَ الله أَكْبَرُ} [al-Tawba: 72].
His saying «خيرٌ» is the khabar of «مَثُوبَةٌ», and here it is not in the sense of the elative afʿal; rather it is to show that it is excellent, as in His saying: {أَصْحَابُ الجنة يَوْمَئِذٍ خَيْرٌ مُّسْتَقَرّاً} [al-Furqān: 24], {أَفَمَن يلقى فِي النار خَيْرٌ} [Fuṣṣilat: 40].
His saying: {لَّوْ كَانُواْ يَعْلَمُونَ}: its apodosis is omitted, its implied form being: "attaining the reward would have been better", i.e. attaining its means, namely faith and piety; and likewise some supposed it: "they would have believed". Regarding the object of «يَعْلَمُون» there are two aspects. One: that it is omitted for restriction [i.e. intransitively], i.e. "if they were among the possessors of knowledge". The second: that it is omitted for brevity, its implied form being: "if they knew the preference in that", or "knew that what is with Allah is better and more lasting".

semin-durr:104-104.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {لاَ تَقُولُواْ رَاعِنَا}: the majority read «راعِنا» as an imperative from al-murāʿāt, which is looking after a person's interests and managing his affairs. «راعِنا» entails mutuality, because its meaning is: "let there be from you regard for us, and from us regard for you"; so they were forbidden from that because in it is their making themselves equal with him, upon him be peace. Al-Ḥasan and Abū Ḥaywa read: «راعِناً» with tanwīn; its justification is that it is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "a rāʿin saying", and it is by way of attribution, like lābin and tāmir; the meaning is: "do not say a saying of ruʿūna". Al-ruʿūna is ignorance, foolishness and rashness. The root sense of ruʿūna is dispersal; from it: «جَيْشٌ أَرْعَنُ», i.e. scattered in every direction; and a man arʿan: who has no collected mind; and a woman raʿnāʾ. Basra was called al-raʿnāʾ; [the poet] said:
766 - لولا ابنُ عُتْبَةَ عمروٌ والرجاءُ له ... ما كانَتِ البصرةُ الرَّعْناءُ لي وَطَنا
[Translator's note: the source numbers this verse 766; the sequence suggests 667.]
(Were it not for Ibn ʿUtba, ʿAmr, and the hope placed in him, Basra the raʿnāʾ would not have been a homeland for me.)
It is said: it was so called because it resembled the raʿn of a mountain, which is its projecting part. Ibn Fāris said: "One says: raʿana the man, yarʿanu, raʿanan." Ubayy read: «راعُونا», and so it is in the codex of ʿAbd Allāh; they addressed him with the plural wording out of reverence. Also in the codex of ʿAbd Allāh: «ارْعَوْنا», for what has preceded. The clause is in the position of the accusative (manṣūb) by the verb of saying. He put the prohibition before the command because it belongs to the category of abstentions, so it is easier.
His saying: «انظُرْنا»: the clause is also in the position of the accusative by the verb of saying. The majority read «انظُرْنا» with a connective hamza and ḍamma on the ẓāʾ, as an imperative from the triliteral; it is naẓar from al-naẓira, which is deferment, i.e. "defer us and be patient with us". Imruʾ al-Qays said:
668 - فإنَّكما إنْ تَنْظُرانيَ ساعةً ... من الدَّهْرِ يَنْفَعْني لدى أمِّ جُنْدَبِ
(For you two, if you wait for me an hour of time, it will profit me with Umm Jundab.)
It has been said: it is from naẓara, i.e. he saw, then its usage was widened so it was made transitive by itself, because originally it is made transitive with «إلى»; and from that:
669 - ظاهراتُ الجَمالِ والحُسْنِ يَنْظُرْ ... نَ كما يَنْظُرُ الأَراكَ الظباءُ
(Manifest in beauty and loveliness, they gaze as gazelles gaze at the arāk trees.)
i.e. at the arāk. It has been said: from naẓara meaning he reflected, then its usage was likewise widened, for its origin is to be made transitive with «في»; and on this view a muḍāf must be omitted, i.e. "consider our affair". Ubayy and al-Aʿmash read: «أَنْظِرْنَا» with fatḥa on the hamza and kasra on the ẓāʾ, as an imperative from the quadriliteral, in the sense of "grant us respite and defer us". The poet said:
670 - أبا هندٍ فلا تَعْجَلْ عَلَيْنا ... وأَنْظِرْنا نُخْبِّرْكَ اليَقينا
(O Abū Hind, do not be hasty with us; give us respite and we will tell you the certain truth.)
i.e. "give us respite". This reading supports that the first is from al-naẓra in the sense of deferment, not from sight nor from insight. This verse is the counterpart of the one in al-Ḥadīd: «انظُرونا نقتبسْ», for it has been read in both ways.

semin-durr:105-105.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {مِنْ أَهْلِ الكتاب}: about «مِنْ» there are two views. One: that it is partitive, so it and its genitive noun are in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), attached to something omitted, i.e. "those who disbelieved, being of the People of the Book, do not wish". The second: that it is for explaining the genus; al-Zamakhsharī held this.
His saying: {وَلاَ المشركين} is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «أَهْلِ», which is in the genitive by «مِن», and «لا» is redundant (zāʾida) for emphasis, because the meaning is: "those who disbelieved among the People of the Book and the polytheists do not wish", as in His saying: {لَمْ يَكُنِ الذين كَفَرُواْ مِنْ أَهْلِ الكتاب والمشركين} [al-Bayyina: 1] without additional «لا». Some claimed that it is in the genitive by proximity (jiwār), and that the original is «ولا المشركون», conjoined to «الذين», and it was put in the genitive only for adjacency, as in «برؤوسكم وأرجلكِم» in the genitive reading; and this is not clear. Al-Naḥḥās said: "And «ولا المشركونَ» is permissible, by conjoining it to «الذين»." Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "If «ولا المشركون» has been read in the nominative, it is conjoined to the agent; and apparently it has not been read thus." These two sayings support the claim of the genitive by proximity.
His saying: {أَن يُنَزَّلَ}: a governor of the subjunctive and what it governs, interpreted as a maṣdar (interpreted maṣdar), the object of «يَوَدُّ», i.e. "they do not wish the sending down of good". The verb was made passive because the agent is known and because it is stated explicitly in His saying «من ربكم». He used «ما» in the negation rather than others because it is for negating the present, and they were engaged in that.
His saying: {مِّنْ خَيْرٍ}: this is what stands in the place of the agent (nāʾib fāʿil), and «مِنْ» is redundant, i.e. "that good be sent down from your Lord". Its redundancy is good here, even though «يُنَزَّل» is not directly preceded by the particle of negation, because the negation extends over it in terms of meaning: for if the wishing is negated, its object is negated.
This has counterparts in their speech, such as «ما أظنُّ أحداً يقولُ ذلك إلا زيدٌ» ("I do not think anyone says that except Zayd") with «زيدٌ» in the nominative as a badal (substitute) from the agent of «يقول», even though it is not directly negated, because it is in the force of: "no one says that except Zayd, in my opinion"; and His saying, Exalted is He: {أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْاْ أَنَّ الله الذي خَلَقَ السماوات والأرض وَلَمْ يَعْيَ بِخَلْقِهِنَّ بِقَادِرٍ} [al-Aḥqāf: 33], where the bāʾ was added because it is in the sense of: "Is not Allah able?" This is according to the opinion of Sībawayh and his followers; as for the Kufans and al-Akhfash, they need none of this. It has been said: «مِنْ» is partitive, i.e. "they do not wish that any good be sent down, little or much"; on this view what stands in the place of the agent is «عليكم», and the meaning is: "that there be sent down to you some good among goods".
His saying: {مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ}: about «مِنْ» there are also two views. One: that it is for the beginning of the extent, so it is attached to «يُنَزَّل». The second: that it is partitive, and then a muḍāf must be omitted, its implied form being "from the goods of your Lord", and it is then attached to something omitted, because it and its genitive noun are a naʿt (adjective) of His saying «مِنْ خيرٍ», i.e. "of good being among the goods of your Lord". Its position then has two aspects: the genitive according to the wording, and the nominative according to the position, because «مِنْ» is redundant in «خير», so it is nominative by supposition, standing in the place of the agent, as preceded.
To sum up what has preceded: for each occurrence of the word «مِنْ» there are two views. The first: it has been said it is partitive, and it has been said it is for explaining the genus. In the second there are two views: redundant or partitive. And in the third there are also two views: beginning of the extent or partitive.
His saying: {والله يَخْتَصُّ بِرَحْمَتِهِ مَن يَشَآءُ}: this is an initial clause containing the rebuttal of that wish of theirs. «يختصُّ» may here be transitive or intransitive. If it is transitive, there is a pronoun in it referring to Allah the Exalted, and «مَنْ» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e. "Allah singles out with His mercy the one whom He wills"; and the sense of iftaʿala here is the sense of the bare form, as in kasaba mālan and iktasabahu. If it is intransitive, there is no pronoun in it and its agent is «مَنْ», i.e. "and Allah — with His mercy is singled out the person whom He wills"; and iftaʿala is then in the sense of the agent acting upon himself, as in iḍṭaraba. Ikhtiṣāṣ (being singled out) is the opposite of sharing; and by this the error of whoever claimed it is only transitive here becomes clear. «مَنْ» may be a relative noun or an indefinite described noun, and on both suppositions a referring pronoun must be supposed, i.e. "He wills singling him out"; or «يشاء» may be made to include the sense of «يَخْتار» ("chooses"), and then there is no need to omit a muḍāf; rather you suppose a pronoun only, i.e. "whom He wills". «يشاءُ» on the first view has no position, being a ṣila; on the second its position is the accusative or the nominative, according to what was mentioned about the noun it describes, as agent or object.

semin-durr:159-159.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {مَآ أَنزَلْنَا}: the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of «يكتمون»; «أَنْزلنا» is its ṣila (relative clause), and its returning pronoun is omitted, i.e. «أنزلناه». «من البيناتِ» admits three views. The most evident of them: that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the relative «ما», and so is attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted element, i.e.: being of the clear proofs. The second: that it is attached to «أنزلنا», and so is a mafʿūl bihi — said by Abū al-Baqāʾ. There is a problem in this, in that if it were a mafʿūl bihi the verb would not take a pronoun as object, and if it did not take the pronoun of the relative noun as object, the relative noun would remain without a returning pronoun. The third: that it is a ḥāl from the pronoun referring back to the relative noun, the governor being «أنزلنا», because it governs the one whose state is described (ṣāḥib al-ḥāl).

His saying: {مِن بَعْدِ مَا بَيَّنَّاهُ}: attached to «يكتُمون»; it is not attached to «أَنْزَلْنا», because the meaning would be corrupted, since the sending down did not take place after the making clear, whereas the concealment is after the making clear. The pronoun in «بَيَّنَّاه» refers back to the relative «ما». The majority read «بَيَّنَّاه»; Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif read «بَيَّنه» with the third-person pronoun, which is a shift (iltifāt) from the first person to the third. «للناس» is attached to the verb before it.

And His saying: {فِي الكتاب} admits two views. One: that it is attached to His saying «بَيَّنَّاه». The second: that it is attached to an omitted element, because it is a ḥāl from the accusative pronoun in «بَيَّنَّاه», i.e.: We made it clear while it is settled, being in the Book.

His saying: {أولئك يَلعَنُهُمُ}: «أولئك» admits two views. One: that it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «يلعنُهم» its khabar (predicate), the clause being the khabar of «إنَّ الذين». The second: that it is a badal (substitute) from «الذين» and «يَلْعَنُهم» is the khabar, because His saying «ويَلْعَنُهم اللاعنون» may be conjoined to what precedes it, namely «يلعنهم الله», or may be resumptive. He gave the ṣila of «الذين» as an imperfect verb, and likewise the verb of cursing, to indicate renewal and occurrence, and that this recurs time after time; and the curse was repeated for emphasis in condemning them. In His saying «يَلْعَنُهم اللهُ» there is a shift (iltifāt), since if it had followed the course of the speech He would have said «نلعنهم», because of His saying «أنزلنا»; but in making this noble name overt there is what is not in the pronoun.

semin-durr:160-160.t:
His saying: {إِلاَّ الذين تَابُواْ}: there are two views on it. One: that it is a connected exception (istithnāʾ muttaṣil), the thing excepted from being the pronoun in «يلعنهم». The second: that it is a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ), because those who concealed were cursed before they repented, and the exception came only to make clear that repentance is accepted, because some of those who concealed were not cursed. Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned that, and it is worthless.

His saying: {وَمَاتُوا} [Translator's note: the words discussed belong to verse 161, {وَمَاتُوا وَهُمْ كُفَّارٌ}; the comment concerns the wāw of «وهم»]: this is the wāw of the ḥāl (circumstantial), and the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl. Retaining the wāw here is more eloquent, contrary to al-Farrāʾ and al-Zamakhsharī, who both said that its omission is anomalous.

And His saying: {أُولَئِكَ عَلَيْهِمْ لَعْنَةُ}: «أولئك» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «عليهم لعنةُ اللهِ» is a mubtadaʾ and khabar (predicate) serving as the khabar of «أولئك», and «أولئك» with its khabar is the khabar of «إنَّ». «لعنةُ» may also be nominative as the fāʿil (agent) of the preposition phrase before it, because it is supported, since it occurs as the khabar of «أولئك»; its exposition was given at {عَلَيْهِمْ صَلَوَاتٌ مِّن رَّبِّهِمْ} [al-Baqara: 157].

His saying: {والملائكة}: the majority put «الملائكة» in the genitive, conjoined to the name of Allah. Al-Ḥasan read with the nominative: {والملائكةُ والناسُ أَجْمَعُونَ}, and the grammarians explained it as conjunction to the position of the name of Allah the Exalted: for although it is genitive by the annexation of the maṣdar (verbal noun) to it, its position is nominative as an agent, because this maṣdar resolves into a maṣdar-forming particle and a verb, the implied sense being «أَنْ لَعَنَهم» or «أَنْ يَلْعَنَهم اللهُ», and «الملائكةُ» was conjoined on this assumption. The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "This is not permissible according to what has been established about conjunction to the position, for one of its conditions is that there be something that secures the position and demands it, and what demands the nominative [here] would be the presence of nunation in the maṣdar. This is if we grant that «لعنة» resolves into a maṣdar-forming particle and a verb, because the condition for resolving it thus is that it be meant as an action. Do you not see that in His saying: {أَلاَ لَعْنَةُ الله عَلَى الظالمين} [Hūd: 18] the meaning is not on the assumption 'that Allah curses the wrongdoers'; rather what is meant is the established curse, and it is annexed to Allah the Exalted by way of specification, not by way of occurrence." He reported from Sībawayh that in your saying «هذا ضاربُ زيدٍ غداً وعمراً», with «عمراً» in the accusative, its accusative is by an omitted verb, and he refused to make it accusative by conjunction to the position. Then, after granting all that, he said: "After the nunated maṣdar a nominative agent together with an accusative object has not been heard; the Basrans said it only by analogy with «أَنْ» and the verb, and al-Farrāʾ disallowed it, and that is correct."

He then explained this anomalous reading by one of three views. The first: that «الملائكةُ» is nominative by an omitted verb, i.e.: and the angels curse them, just as Sībawayh made «عمراً» accusative by an omitted verb in your saying «ضاربُ زيدٍ وعمراً». The second: that «الملائكة» is conjoined to «لعنة» on the assumption of an omitted muḍāf: and the curse of the angels; when the muḍāf was omitted, the muḍāf ilayhi was put in its place. The third: that it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar has been omitted, its implied form being: and the angels and all the people curse them. [End of quotation.]

These views are strained. The governing power of the nunated maṣdar is established; the most that can be said on the matter is that its agent may be omitted, as in His saying: {أَوْ إِطْعَامٌ فِي يَوْمٍ ذِي مَسْغَبَةٍ يَتِيماً} [al-Balad: 14]. Moreover, the Arabs have made a word follow what is put in the genitive by the maṣdar according to its position, in the nominative, [as in the saying of] the poet [Translator's note: the source reads «على الشاعر», evidently for «كقول الشاعر»]:
784 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... مَشْيَ الهَلوكِ عليها الخَيْعَلُ الفَضُلَ
(…like the walk of the swaying woman wearing a sleeveless shift, in a single garment.)
with «الفُضُلُ» in the nominative, it being an attribute of «الهَلوك» according to the position. If that is established for the naʿt (adjective), it is established for conjunction, because both are among the five appositives (tawābiʿ). «أجمعين» is one of the words of semantic tawkīd (emphasis), on a par with «كل».

semin-durr:162-162.t: His saying, the Exalted: {خَالِدِينَ}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «عليهم». His saying «لا يُخَفَّفُ» admits three views. The first: that it is resumptive. The second: that it is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «خالدين», so that they are two overlapping (mutadākhila) ḥāls. The third: that it is a second ḥāl from the pronoun in «عليهم», and that is according to those who permit multiple ḥāls. Abū al-Baqāʾ disallowed this view, basing himself on his doctrine on that point.

semin-durr:163-163.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وإلهكم إله وَاحِدٌ}: [«إله» is] the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject), and «واحدٌ» is a naʿt (adjective); it is in reality the khabar, because it is where the information lies. Do you not see that if one confined oneself to what precedes it, it would convey nothing? This resembles the paving ḥāl (al-ḥāl al-muwaṭṭiʾa), as in «مررتُ بزيد رجلاً صالحاً» (I passed by Zayd, a righteous man): «رجلاً» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) but is not what is intended; what is intended is only its attribute.

His saying: {إِلاَّ هُوَ}: «هو» is nominative as a badal (substitute) from the noun of «لا» according to its position, since its position is nominative as a mubtadaʾ; or it is a badal from «لا» together with what it governs, because it and what follows it are in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ; the exposition of that has been given. It is not permissible for «هو» to be the khabar of the «لا» of absolute negation (lā al-tabriʾa), because, as you know, it does not govern definite nouns; rather the khabar is omitted, i.e.: there is no god for us. This is if we proceed on the view that «لا», with which its noun is made indeclinable, governs the khabar. But if we make the khabar nominative by what it was nominative by before «لا» entered, «لا» having no effect on it — and this is the doctrine of Sībawayh — then «هو» ought to be the khabar, except that this is prevented by the mubtadaʾ being indefinite and the khabar definite, which is disallowed except in poetic licences in certain chapters.

The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] found it problematic that it should be a badal from «إله». He said: "Because the repetition of the governor is not possible: you do not say «لا رجلَ لا زيدَ». What appears to me is that it is not a badal from «إله», nor from «رجل» in your saying «لا رجلَ إلا زيدٌ»; rather it is a badal from the pronoun latent in the omitted khabar. When we say «لا رجلَ إلا زيدٌ», the implied sense is: there is no man existing or present except Zayd, so «زيد» is a badal from the pronoun latent in the khabar, not from «رجل». It is thus not a badal according to the position of the noun of «لا»; it is only a nominative badal from a nominative pronoun, that pronoun referring back to the noun of [«لا»]. Were it not for the grammarians' explicit statement that it is a badal according to the position from the noun of «لا», we would have interpreted their words as just interpreted." What he said is not problematic, because they did not say it is a badal from the noun of «لا» according to its wording, such that they would be bound to repeat the governor. It would only be problematic if they permitted substituting it for the noun of «لا» according to its wording, and they did not permit that, because repeating the governor is impossible. For that reason they disallowed the badal view in their saying «لا إله إلا اللهَ» [Translator's note: so vocalised in the source, i.e. with the excepted noun in the accusative] and made it accusative as an exception, while they permitted it in your saying «لا رجلَ في الدارِ إلا صاحباً لك» (there is no man in the house except a companion of yours), because the repetition of the governor is possible in it.

His saying: {الرحمن الرحيم}: there are four views on it. The first: that it is a badal from «هو», an overt noun substituted for a pronoun; but this leads to substitution with derived adjectives, which is rare. One can answer this by saying that these two attributes are treated like non-derived nouns, especially according to those who make «الرحمنُ» a proper name; the verification of that was given at the Basmala. The second: that it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e.: He is the Most Merciful; its omission was made good by the wording «هو» succeeding itself twice. The third: that it is a third khabar of His saying «وإلهُكم»: He predicated of it with His saying «إله واحد», with His saying «لا إله إلا هو», and with His saying «الرحمن الرحيم»; this is according to those who hold that multiple khabars are allowed without restriction. The fourth: that it is a naʿt of His saying «هو», and that is according to al-Kisāʾī, for he permits describing the third-person pronoun with an attribute of praise. He thus stipulated these two conditions for describing a pronoun: that it be third-person and that the attribute be one of praise — although the Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn ibn Mālik reported from him the permissibility of describing the third-person pronoun without restriction. It is not permissible for it to be the khabar of this «هو» mentioned here, because the excepted is not a clause.

semin-durr:187-187.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {لَيْلَةَ الصيام}: accusative (manṣūb) as an adverb (ẓarf). Regarding what makes it accusative there are three views. The first — and it is the well-known one among the grammarians who parse — is that it is «أُحِلَّ»; but this is nothing, because the permission was established before that time. The second: it is an implied verb indicated by the word «الرفث», its implied form being: "it has been made lawful for you to have intimate relations (أن تَرْفُثوا) on the night of the fast," just as they explained the words of the poet:
855 - وبعضُ الحِلْم عِند الجَهْ ... لِ للذلَّةِ إذْعان
(Some forbearance in the face of ignorance is a submission to humiliation.)
i.e. "a submission — submitting to humiliation." It is not permissible for it to be made accusative by «الرفث» itself, because it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) that is interpreted as a relative [i.e. أنْ plus a verb], and what is governed by the ṣila (relative clause) may not precede the relative; that is why we needed to imply a governing word from the root of the one mentioned. The third: it is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «الرفث», according to the opinion of those who allow latitude with adverbs and prepositional phrases; its verification has already been given.

The night was put in the genitive construct [with "the fast"] by way of latitude, because the condition of its validity, namely the intention, exists in it, and the genitive construct comes about by the slightest connection. Otherwise, it is the due of an adverb put in construct with an event that the event should occur in some part of that adverbial time, and fasting at night is not reckoned; but what permits it is what I have mentioned to you.

The majority read «أُحِلَّ» as passive, because the agent is known, namely Allah the Exalted. It has been read as active, and in that case there are two possibilities. The first: it is a case of implying [the agent] because the meaning is understood, i.e. "Allah made lawful," since it is known that He is the One who makes lawful and forbids. The second: the pronoun refers back to what is referred to in His words {فَلْيَسْتَجِيبُواْ لِي وَلْيُؤْمِنُواْ بِي}, namely the speaker, and this would be an iltifāt (shift of person). Likewise in His words «لكم» there is a shift from the third-person pronoun in «فَلْيَسْتجيبوا وَلْيؤمنوا». «الرفث» was made transitive with إلى, whereas it is normally made transitive with الباء, because it has been made to include the meaning of الإفضاء (going in unto); as if it were said: "going in unto your wives with intimacy has been made lawful for you."

ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd] read «الرَّفوث». In the language, الرَّفَثُ is the maṣdar of رَفَثَ يَرْفُث, when one speaks obscenely; and أَرْفَثَ means he came out with رَفَث. Al-ʿAjjāj said:
856 - ورُبَّ أسرابِ حجيجٍ كُظَّمِ ... عن اللَّغا وَرَفَثِ التكلُّم
(Many a band of pilgrims holding back from idle talk and obscene speech.)
Al-Zajjāj said — and it is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās —: "الرفث is a word comprising everything a man wants from a woman." It has also been said: الرفث is intercourse itself, and he recited:
857 - ويُرَيْنَ من أَنَسِ الحديثِ زوانيا ... ولَهُنَّ عن رَفَثِ الرجالِ نفارُ
(For the charm of their talk they are thought wanton, yet they shy away from the advances of men.)
and the words of another:
858 - فَظِلْنَا هنالِكَ في نِعْمَةٍ ... وكلِّ اللَّذاذَةِ غيرَ الرَّفَثْ
(We remained there in bliss and every pleasure except intimacy.)
But there is no proof in it, because of the possibility that the preliminaries of intercourse, such as fondling and kissing, are meant. Ibn ʿAbbās, while in the state of iḥrām, recited:
859 - وهُنَّ يَمْشِين بنا هَمِيسا ... إنْ يَصْدُقِ الطيرُ نَنِكَ لَمِيسا
(They walk with us softly; if the omen of the birds proves true, we shall lie with Lamīs.)
It was said to him: "You have committed رفث." He said: "رفث is only in the presence of women."

His words: {كُنتُمْ تَخْتانُونَ}: in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of «أنَّ», and «تَخْتانون» is in the position of accusative as the khabar of «كان». Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "«كُنْتُم» here has the form of the past and its meaning is past as well; the meaning is that the betrayal used to occur from them, and He turned to them in forgiveness from it. It has also been said that He meant betrayal in the future, and mentioned «كان» to narrate the state, as you say: 'If you do [such-and-such], you were a wrongdoer.'" In this statement there is an evident objection.

«تَخْتَانون» is of the form تَفْتَعِلُون from الخيانة (betrayal). The ʿayn [middle radical] of الخيانة is a wāw, because they say خانَ يخُون, and in the plural خَوَنَة. One says خانَ يَخُون خَوْناً وخِيانة; it is the opposite of trustworthiness. And تَخَوَّنْتُ الشيءَ means I diminished it. Zuhayr said:
860 - بآرِزَةِ الفَقَارَةِ لم يَخُنْهَا ... قِطافٌ في الرِّكاب ولا خِلاءُ
(On a she-camel with a firm spine, not diminished by short-stepping among the riding camels nor by balkiness.)
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "الاختيان is from الخيانة as الاكتساب is from الكَسْب; there is in it addition and intensity," meaning in that an addition in the wording indicates an addition in the meaning, as he set forth earlier regarding His words «الرحمنُ الرحيمُ». It has also been said here: «تختانون أَنْفُسَكُم» means "you tend to yourselves by going in unto women"; this would be in the sense of التخويل. One says تَخَوَّنه and تَخَوَّله, with nūn and with lām, meaning "he tended it," except that the nūn is a substitute for the lām, since it is better known with the lām.

As for «عَلِمَ»: if it is the one transitive to a single object in the sense of عَرَف (to know), then «أنَّ» together with what falls in its domain fills the place of one object; and if it is the one transitive to two objects, it fills the place of both objects according to the opinion of Sībawayh, and the place of one of them, with the other omitted, according to the school of al-Akhfash.

His words {هُنَّ لِبَاسٌ لَّكُمْ} have no grammatical position, because it is an explanation of the permission; it is resumptive and explicative. He put {هُنَّ لِبَاسٌ لَّكُمْ} before {وَأَنْتُمْ لِبَاسٌ لَّهُنَّ} to draw attention to how evident the man's need of the woman is and his inability to do without her, and because he is the one who initiates the request for it. He used "garment" as a metonymy for intense intimacy, as in the saying of — it is al-Nābigha al-Jaʿdī —:
861 - إذا ما الضجيعُ ثُنَى جيدَها ... تَثَنَّتْ عليه فكانَتْ لباسا
(When her bedfellow bends her neck, she bends over him and becomes a garment.)
And also in it [the same poem]:
862 - لَبِسْتُ أُناساً فَأَفْنَيْتُهُمْ ... وَأَفْنَيْتُ بعد أُناسٍ أُناسا
(I have "worn" [lived with] peoples and outlived them, and after one people I outlived another.)

His words: {فالآن بَاشِرُوهُنَّ}: discussion of «الآن» has already been given. Its occurring as an adverb for the imperative requires interpretation, since it is for the present time while the imperative is always future. Its interpretation is what Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "«الآن»: its literal sense is the time you are in; it may be used for the near past and for the near future, treating what is near as present, and that is what is meant here, because His words «فالآن باشِروهُنَّ» mean: 'so the time of the night in which intercourse used to be forbidden to you.'" It has also been said: this speech is taken according to its meaning, the implied form being: "so now We have permitted you to have relations with them"; the wording of the imperative indicates this omitted element, so «فالآن» is in its literal sense.

It has been read «واتَّبِعُوا» from الاتِّباع (following); this is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, Muʿāwiya ibn Qurra and al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī. They interpreted «ما كَتَبَ اللَّهُ» as the Night of Decree (Laylat al-Qadr), i.e. "follow its reward." Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is close to the innovations of exegesis."

His words: {حتى يَتَبَيَّنَ}: «حتى» here marks the limit of His words «كُلُوا واشربوا», in the sense of إلى (until). One says تَبَيَّن الشيءُ, أبان, استبان and بانَ, all with one meaning; all of them may be transitive or intransitive, except «بان», which is intransitive only. In «مِن الخيط», مِنْ is for the beginning of the extent, and it together with its genitive noun is in the position of accusative by يتبيَّن, because the meaning is: "until the white thread becomes distinct from the black."

«من الفجر» admits three views. The first: it is partitive, and is likewise attached to «يتبيَّن», because the white thread is part of the dawn and its beginning; and there is no harm in two prepositions of the same form being attached to one governing word, because their meanings differ. The second: it is attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in «الأبيض», i.e. "the thread which is white, being of the dawn"; on this view «مِنْ» may be for explaining the genus, as if it were said: "the white thread, which is the dawn." The third: it is a tamyīz (specification); but this is nothing. He explained «الخيط الأبيض» with «مِنَ الفجرِ» but did not explain the black thread by saying "of the night," being content with that; he mentioned this one rather than that one because it is the one on which the rulings mentioned — relations, eating and drinking — depend.

This is one of the finest similes, in that He likened the whiteness of the day to a white thread and the blackness of the night to a black thread; so much so that when ʿAdī ibn Ḥātim mentioned to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he had understood from the verse an actual thread, he was amazed at him and said: "Your pillow is indeed wide"; and it is narrated: "You are indeed broad of nape." It is narrated that some of the Companions did as ʿAdī did, and it is narrated that between His words «الخيط الأبيض» «من الخيط الأسود» [and «من الفجر»] there was a whole year in revelation. [Translator's note: the source text reads thus; the well-known report concerns the interval before «من الفجر» was revealed.] This kind belongs to the category of simile, not of metaphor (istiʿāra), because metaphor is that in which mention of the thing likened is folded away, while here it has been mentioned, namely His words «من الفجر». Its parallel is your saying: "I saw a lion of Zayd"; had you not mentioned "of Zayd," it would be a metaphor. But the simile here is more eloquent, because metaphor requires an indication from the context, and here there was no such indication; that is why some Companions continued to take it literally for a while, until «مِنَ الفَجْرِ» was revealed; so metaphor was abandoned, even though it is more eloquent, for the reason I have mentioned to you.

الفجر is the maṣdar of فَجَرَ يَفْجُرُ, i.e. it split open.

His words: {إِلَى الليل}: there are two views. The first: it is attached to "completing" (الإتمام), being its limit. The second: it is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl of «الصيام», attached to an omitted element, i.e. "extending until the night." When what comes after «إلى» is not of the same kind as what precedes it, it is not included in it, and the verse is of this kind.

«وأنتم عاكفون» is a circumstantial clause from the agent of «تباشروهُنَّ». The meaning is: "do not have relations with them while you have intended iʿtikāf in the mosque." What is meant is not the prohibition of having relations with them in the mosque restricted to iʿtikāf, because that is forbidden outside iʿtikāf as well.

العُكُوف is staying in and keeping to something. One says عَكَف with fatḥa, يَعْكِفُ with ḍamma and with kasra; {يَعْكُفُونَ على أَصْنَامٍ} [al-Aʿrāf: 138] has been read both ways. Al-Farazdaq said:
863 - تَرَى حَوْلَهُنَّ المُعْتَفِين كأنَّهم ... على صَنَمٍ في الجاهليةِ عُكَّفُ
(You see the seekers of favour around them as though they were devotees clinging to an idol in the Jāhiliyya.)
And al-Ṭirimmāḥ said:
864 - وظلَّ بناتُ الليلِ حولي عُكَّفاً ... عكوفَ البواكي بينهنَّ صَريعُ
(The "daughters of the night" [cares] stayed clustered around me, like weeping women clustered around one struck down among them.)
It is said: the iftiʿāl form of it is used for good, and the infiʿāl form for evil. As for iʿtikāf in the Sharia, it is a specific staying with conditions, and the discussion of it in relation to the legal reality is like the discussion of prayer. Qatāda read «عَكِفُون», as if one says عاكِفٌ and عَكِفٌ, like بارّ and بَرّ, رابّ and رَبّ. Al-Aʿmash read «في المسجدِ» in the singular, as if he meant the genus.

His words: {تِلْكَ حُدُودُ الله}: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). The demonstrative has been predicated by a plural, so it is not permissible that it point to what was forbidden in iʿtikāf, because that is a single thing; rather it points to what the verse of fasting contains from its beginning up to here. The verse of fasting contains several commands, and commanding a thing is forbidding its opposite; by this consideration they were several prohibitions. Then its end came as an explicit prohibition, namely «ولا تباشِرُوهُنَّ», so He applied "limits" to all of it, giving predominance to what is explicitly stated and taking account of those prohibitions contained in the commands; thus they were called limits. We were compelled to this interpretation only because of a commanded thing one does not say «فلا تَقْرَبُوها» (so do not approach them).

Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "The fāʾ entering here is conjunctive, upon something omitted, its implied form being: 'take heed, and do not approach them.'" It is not permissible for this fāʾ to be redundant (zāʾida) like the one in the words of Allah the Exalted {وَإِيَّايَ فارهبون} [al-Baqara: 40] on one of the two views, because then «حدودَ الله» ought to have been accusative by ishtighāl (occupation of the verb), since that is the eloquent usage for what comes before a command or prohibition, as in "زيداً فاضْرِبْه, وعمراً فلا تُهِنْهُ." Since the readers have agreed here on the nominative, we know that this clause, «فلا تَقْرَبُوها», is cut off from what precedes it; otherwise it would follow that something not eloquent exists in the Quran.

الحدود is the plural of حَدّ, which is prevention; hence the doorkeeper is called حَدَّاد, because he prevents passing. The حَدّ of a thing is its end and where it stops; therefore it is said: "the definition (الحَدّ) is exclusive and inclusive," i.e. it prevents what is not defined from entering into the defined. Forbidding approaching is more emphatic than forbidding being involved in the thing; that is why the noble verse came [so].

He said here «فلا تقْرَبُوها», and in other places {فَلاَ تَعْتَدُوهَا} [al-Baqara: 229], and likewise {وَمَن يَتَعَدَّ حُدُودَ الله} [al-Baqara: 229] and {وَيَتَعَدَّ حُدُودَهُ} [al-Nisāʾ: 14], because here He gave predominance to the aspect of prohibition, since it is what is followed by His words {تِلْكَ حُدُودُ الله}, and for what is forbidden to be done, forbidding approaching it is more emphatic. As for the other verses, «فلا تَعْتَدُوها» came after the explanation of rulings mentioned earlier, such as divorce, the waiting period, the oath of abstention (īlāʾ), menstruation and inheritance; so it was fitting to forbid transgressing in them, which is going beyond the limit Allah set in them.

His words: {كذلك يُبَيِّنُ الله}: the kāf is in the position of accusative, either as a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "a clarification like this clarification," or as a ḥāl of the omitted maṣdar, as is the school of Sībawayh.

semin-durr:46-46.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {الذين يَظُنُّونَ أَنَّهُم مُّلاَقُو رَبِّهِمْ}: the position of «الذين» admits all three case-vowels: the genitive on the basis that it follows what precedes it as a naʿt (adjective), which is the apparent view; and the nominative and accusative by way of cutting off (al-qaṭʿ), whose meaning has preceded. The origin of al-ẓann is the preponderance of one of two sides. As for this verse, there are two views on it. The first, which most hold: that ẓann here is in the sense of certainty; like it is: {إِنِّي ظَنَنتُ أَنِّي مُلاَقٍ حِسَابِيَهْ} [al-Ḥāqqa: 20], and his saying:
431 - فقلت لهم ظُنُّوا بألفَيْ مُدَجَّجٍ ... سَرَاتُهُمُ في الفارسيِّ المُسَرَّدِ
(So I said to them: be certain of two thousand fully armed warriors, their chiefs clad in close-woven Persian mail.)
Abū Duʾād said:
432 - رُبَّ همٍّ فَرَّجْتُه بعَزيمٍ ... وغُيوبٍ كَشَّفْتُها بظُنونِ
(Many a care I have relieved with resolve, and many hidden things I have uncovered with certain conjectures.)
So ẓann was used in the manner of certainty figuratively, just as ʿilm (knowledge) has been used in the manner of ẓann, as in His saying: {فَإِنْ عَلِمْتُمُوهُنَّ مُؤْمِنَاتٍ} [al-Mumtaḥana: 10]. However, the Arabs use ẓann in the manner of certainty only in what has not come out into sense-perception and observation, as in the two verses and the line of poetry; you do not find them saying of a man seen and present: "I think this is a human being."
The second view: that ẓann is in its normal sense, and there are then two interpretations of it. The first, mentioned by al-Mahdawī, al-Māwardī and others: that «بذنوبهم» (with their sins) is implied in the speech, as though they expect to meet Him as sinners. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "This is arbitrary." The second of the two interpretations: that they think they will meet the reward of their Lord, because they are not certain of reward rather than punishment, the implied form being: "they think that they will meet the reward of their Lord". But on this view the conjoining of {وَأَنَّهُمْ إِلَيْهِ رَاجِعُونَ} poses a difficulty, for ẓann does not suffice in it — that is, if we refer the pronoun in «إليه» to the Lord, Glorified and Exalted is He; but if we refer it to the implied reward, the difficulty disappears. Or it may be said: with respect to the first it is in the sense of ẓann in its normal meaning, and with respect to the second in the sense of certainty, so that literal and figurative meaning have been combined in a single word — and that is a disputed question. «أن» and what is in its domain stand [in the place of] the two objects according to the majority, and in the place of the first, with the second omitted, according to al-Akhfash; its precise treatment has preceded.
{مُّلاَقُو رَبِّهِمْ} belongs to the chapter of annexing the active participle to what it governs, a lightening annexation, because it is future. The nūn was dropped for the annexation; the origin is مُلاقونَ ربِّهم. The form mufāʿala here is in the sense of the triliteral, as in عافاك الله (may Allah grant you well-being); al-Mahdawī said it. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "This is weak, because «لَقِيَ» includes the meaning of «لاقى»." It seems he means that the root in itself entails mutuality, unlike other verbs such as عاقَبْت, طارقت and عافاك. It has preceded that there is an omission in the speech, its implied form being: "meeting the reward of their Lord and His punishment". Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "The meeting here may properly be the vision [of Allah] which the people of the Sunna hold and of which the mass-transmitted (mutawātir) ḥadīth speaks." On what he said, there is no need to suppose an omitted muḍāf. {وَأَنَّهُمْ إِلَيْهِ رَاجِعُونَ} is conjoined to «أَنَّهم» and what is in its domain. «إليه» is attached to «راجعون», and the pronoun is either for the Lord, Glorified is He, or for the reward, as has preceded, or for the meeting understood from «مُلاقُو».

semin-durr:47-47.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {وَأَنِّي فَضَّلْتُكُمْ عَلَى العالمين}: «أنَّ» and what is in its domain is in the position of the accusative, because it is conjoined to the accusative noun in His saying: {اذكروا نِعْمَتِي}, i.e. "remember My favour and My preferring you". The preposition-phrase is attached to it. This is of the chapter of conjoining the particular to the general, because the favour includes the preferring. Al-faḍl: increase in good. Its original usage is to be made transitive by «على», but it may be made transitive by «عَنْ», either by implication of another verb's meaning (taḍmīn) or by figurative usage in the omission, as in his saying:
433 - لاهِ ابنُ عَمِّك لا أَفْضَلْتَ في حَسَبٍ ... عني ولا أَنْتَ دَيَّاني فَتَخْزَوني
(By God, [you are] your cousin! You do not surpass me in lineage, nor are you my master that you should rule over me.)
It may also be transitive by itself, as in his saying:
434 - وَجَدْنا نَهْشَلاً فَضَلَتْ فُقَيْماً ... كفَضْلِ ابنِ المَخَاضِ على الفَصيلِ
(We found that Nahshal surpassed Fuqaym as the year-old camel surpasses the weanling.)
— and by «على». Its verb is فضَل يَفْضُل with ḍamma, like قَتَلَ يقتُل. As for the one whose meaning is al-faḍla of a thing, which is the remainder, its verb is also as has preceded, and one also says of it «فَضِل» with kasra, يَفْضَل with fatḥa, like عَلِم يعلَم; and some give it kasra in the past and ḍamma in the imperfect, which is an overlapping of the two dialects.

semin-durr:80-80.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {إِلاَّ أَيَّاماً مَّعْدُودَةً}: this is an emptied (mufarragh) exception, so أيّاماً is accusative as an adverb (ẓarf) by the verb before it. The implied sense is: "The Fire will never touch us except for a few days that counting can encompass", because counting encompasses [only] what is few. The origin of أيّام is أَيْوام, because it is the plural of يوم, like قَوْم / أَقْوام. The yāʾ and the wāw met, the first of them being quiescent, so the wāw had to be changed to yāʾ and the yāʾ assimilated into the yāʾ, as in هيّن and ميّت.

His words: {أَتَّخَذْتُمْ}: the hamza is interrogative, and its meaning is disapproval and reproach. By it the hamza of connection (hamzat al-waṣl) that enters «اتَّخَذْتُم» is dispensed with, as in His words {أفترى عَلَى الله} [Sabaʾ: 8], {أَصْطَفَى} [al-Ṣāffāt: 153] and their kind. The discussion of the morphology of {اتخذتم} [al-Baqara: 67] and Abū ʿAlī's disagreement about it has been given. Here it may be transitive to one object. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is in the sense of جَعَلْتُم, transitive to one object." But there is no need to make it in the sense of «جَعَل» for it to be transitive to one; rather the meaning is: "Have you taken (أَخَذْتُم) a covenant from Allah?" It may also be transitive to two, the first being «عهد» and the second «عند الله», placed before it. On the first view «عند الله» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) اتَّخَذْتُم, and on the second it is attached to an omitted element. It is permissible to transfer the vowel of the interrogative hamza to the lām of «قُلْ» before it, so that it takes fatḥa and the hamza is dropped; this is a regular usage, and Nāfiʿ read so in the transmission of Warsh from him.

His words: {فَلَنْ يُخْلِفَ الله}: this is the answer to the interrogative that preceded in His words {أَتَّخَذْتُمْ}. Is this by way of the interrogative containing the meaning of a condition, or by way of implying a condition after the interrogative and its sisters? There are two views, whose verification has been given. Al-Zamakhsharī chose the second view, for he said: "{فَلَنْ يُخْلِفَ} is attached to an omitted element, its implied form being: 'If you have taken a covenant with Allah, then Allah will not break His covenant'." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "فلن يُخْلِف اللهُ عهدَه is parenthetical in the midst of the speech." It is as though he means by that that His words «أم تَقُولون» are the counterpart (muʿādil) of His words «أَتَّخَذتم», so this clause occurred between the two counterparts as a parenthesis, the implied sense being: "Which of these two is the case: your having taken a covenant, or your speaking without knowledge?" On this view it has no grammatical position, and on the first its position is jussive.

His words: {أَمْ تَقُولُونَ}: this «أمْ» admits two aspects. First: that it is connected (muttaṣila), and so serves to set two things against each other, i.e. "which of these two is the case?" He presented it in the manner of something in doubt, even though it is known which of the two is the case — namely their saying about Allah what they do not know — for the sake of eliciting acknowledgement (taqrīr). Its parallel is {وَإِنَّآ أَوْ إِيَّاكُمْ لعلى هُدًى أَوْ فِي ضَلاَلٍ مُّبِينٍ} [Sabaʾ: 24], when it is known which of them is on guidance and which in error. You have learned the conditions of the connected [أم] at the beginning of the sūra.

It may also be disjoined (munqaṭiʿa), and so not be a conjunction, and be construed as بل together with the hamza,/ the implied sense being: "Nay, do you say …?", the interrogative being for disapproval because the saying of that did occur from them. This is the well-known [view] about disjoined أم. A group claimed that it is construed as «بل» alone without an interrogative hamza, so that what follows it is conjoined to what precedes it in i'rab; this was argued from their saying إنَّ لنا إبلاً أَمْ شاءً ("We have camels — nay, sheep"), with «شاء» in the accusative, and the words of another:

566 - وَليْتَ سليمى في المَنَامِ ضَجيعتي ... هنالِكَ أَمْ في جنةٍ أَمْ جَهَنَّمِ
(Would that Sulaymā were my bedfellow in sleep there — whether in Paradise or in Hell.)

its implied sense being "nay, in Hell". Had the interrogative hamza been implied after it, the nominative would have been required in «شاء» and «جهنم», as the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject). No one may say that it is connected in these two places, because it is known that its condition is that the hamza precede it, overtly or implicitly, and that is not suitable here.

His words: {مَا لاَ تَعْلَمُونَ}: «ما» is accusative by تقولون. It is a relative noun in the sense of الذي, or an indefinite qualified by a description; on both views the resumptive pronoun is omitted, i.e. "what you do not know (it)". So the clause has no grammatical position on the first view, and its position is accusative on the second. It is not permissible here for it to be maṣdariyya.

semin-durr:81-81.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {بلى}: a particle of answer, like نَعَم, جَيْرِ, أَجَلْ and إي, except that «بلى» is an answer to a preceding negation, whether an interrogative has entered it or not, and so it is an affirmation of it. For example, someone says "Zayd did not stand", and you say: "Yes indeed (بلى), he has stood." And you say: "Is Zayd not standing?", and [the answer] says "بلى", i.e. he is standing. Allah the Exalted said: {أَلَسْتُ بِرَبِّكُمْ قَالُواْ بلى} [al-Aʿrāf: 172], and it is reported from Ibn ʿAbbās that had they said "نَعَم" they would have disbelieved. As for his words:

567 - أليسَ الليلُ يَجْمَعُ أُمَّ عمروٍ ... وإيَّانا فَذَاكَ بِنا تَدانِي
نَعَمْ وترى الهلالَ كما أَراه ... وَيعْلُوها النهارُ كما عَلاني
(Does not the night bring Umm ʿAmr and us together? That is nearness for us. / Yes, and she sees the new moon as I see it, and the day rises over her as it rises over me.)

it is said that it is poetic necessity. It is also said that he looked to the meaning, because when an interrogative enters a negation it affirms it. On this basis it may be asked: how then is it transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās that had they said "نعم" they would have disbelieved, although the negation became an affirmation? It is also said: his word «نعم» is not an answer to «أليس»; it is only an answer to his words «فذاكَ بنا تَداني».

So the words of Allah the Exalted «بلى» are a rejection of their saying {لَن تَمَسَّنَا النار}, i.e. "Yes indeed, it will touch you forever", as shown by His words {هُمْ فِيهَا خَالِدُونَ}; al-Zamakhsharī said this. He means that "forever" is set against their saying {إِلاَّ أَيَّاماً مَّعْدُودَةً}, and it is a fine construal.

The Basrans say that «بلى» is a simple particle. The Kufans claimed that its origin is بل, which is for retraction (iḍrāb), to which the yāʾ was added so that pausing on it would be good, and the yāʾ was made to contain the meaning of affirmation. It is said: it indicates the rejection of the negation, and the yāʾ indicates affirmation — by "the yāʾ" they mean the alif; they only called it yāʾ because it is pronounced with imāla and written with yāʾ. The verification of the two doctrines has a place other than this, and the discussion of the rest of the particles of answer will come, if Allah wills.

His words: {مَن كَسَبَ}: two aspects are possible for «مَنْ». First: that it is a relative noun in the sense of الذي, and the khabar (predicate) is His words «فأولئك»; the fāʾ is permitted to enter the khabar because the conditions mentioned earlier are fulfilled. Its being qualified (mawṣūfa) [Translator's note: so in the source; the context requires "a relative noun (mawṣūla)"] is supported by the mention of its counterpart as a relative, namely His words {والذين كَفَرواْ}. Second: it may be conditional, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is His words «فأولئك». On both views its position is the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject). But if we say it is a relative, the khabar is «فأولئك» and what follows, without disagreement, and His words {كَسَبَ سَيِّئَةً} and what is conjoined to it have no grammatical position because they are a ṣila (relative clause). If we say it is conditional, the well-known disagreement about its khabar arises: either the protasis, or the apodosis, or both, as stated before; and His words «كَسَب» and what is conjoined to it are in the position of the jussive by the condition.

«سَيِّئَةً» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). Its origin is سَيْوِئة, because it is from ساءَ يسُوء, so its pattern is فَيْعِلة. The yāʾ and the wāw met, the first being quiescent, so it underwent the change of سَيّد and ميّت, as has been discussed.

He took account of the form of «مَنْ» once, using the singular in His words «كسب», «به» and «خطيئته», and of the meaning another time, using the plural in His words {فأولئك أَصْحَابُ النار هُمْ فِيهَا خَالِدُونَ}.

Nāfiʿ and the people of Medina read «خطيئاتُه» with the sound plural, and the majority «خطيئتُه» in the singular. The account of the two readings depends on knowing [what is meant by] السيئة and الخطيئة, about which there are views. First: they are two expressions for disbelief with two different words. Second: السيئة is disbelief and الخطيئة is a major sin. Third: the reverse of the second. So the account of the majority's reading on the first and third views is that what is meant by الخطيئة is disbelief, which is one; and on the second view that what is meant by it is the genus of major sin. The account of Nāfiʿ's reading on the first and third views is that what is meant by the خطيئات is the kinds of disbelief renewed at every time; and on the second view that what is meant is the major sins, which are many. It is also said: what is meant by الخطيئة is the very سيئة mentioned before, and He called it by these two names to show its ugliness, as though He said: "and that sin of his — i.e. the سيئة — encompassed him"; what is meant by السيئة is then disbelief. Or the disobedient are meant, and by eternity He meant a long stay, after which they come out.

His words {فأولئك أَصْحَابُ} to the end: its counterpart has been discussed, so there is no need to repeat it. It has been read «خطاياه» as a broken plural; this is at variance with the consonantal text (sawād) of the Muṣḥaf, for it is written «خطيئتُه» in the singular form. The discussion of the morphology of خطايا has been given.

semin-durr:125-125.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {وَإِذْ جَعَلْنَا البيت}: «إذ» is conjoined to the «إذْ» before it, and it has already been discussed. «جَعَلْنا» may mean «خَلَقَ» (created) and «وَضَعَ» (placed), in which case it is transitive to one object, namely «البَيْت», and «مَثَابةً» is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); or it may mean "rendered", in which case it is transitive to two objects, and «مثابةً» is the second object.
The origin of «مَثَابة» is مَثْوَبة; it underwent weakening (iʿlāl) by transfer [of the vowel] and change [of the wāw into alif]. Is it a maṣdar (verbal noun) or a noun of place? Two views. Is the hāʾ in it for hyperbole, like عَلاَّمة and نسَّابة, because of the multitude of those who resort (yathūbu) to it, i.e. return to it; or for the feminine of the maṣdar, like مقامة; or for the feminine of "the spot"? Three views. The omission of this hāʾ has occurred; Waraqa ibn Nawfal [Translator's note: the source prints «نوقل»] said:
712 - مَثَابٌ لأَفْناءِ القبائلِ كلِّها ... تَخُبُّ إليها اليَعْمَلاتُ الذَّوامِلُ
(A place of resort for the mixed folk of all the tribes, to which the sturdy, ambling camels trot.)
And [the poet] said:
713 - جَعَلَ البيتَ مثاباً لهُمُ ... ليس منه الدهرَ يَقْضُون الوطَرْ
(He made the House a place of return for them; never, through all time, do they fulfil their longing for it.)
Is its meaning from ثابَ يَثُوب, i.e. "returned", or from الثواب, which is reward? Two views, the more apparent of which is the first. Al-Aʿmash and Ṭalḥa read «مَثَابَاتٍ» in the plural; its justification is that it is a place of return for each one of the people.
His words: {لِّلنَّاسِ}: there are two aspects in it. The first: it is attached to something omitted, because it is an adjective of «مثابة», and its position is the accusative. The second: it is attached to «جَعَلَ», i.e. for the sake of the people, meaning their rites.
His words: {وَأَمْناً}: there are two aspects in it. The first: it is conjoined to «مَثَابة», and in it there are the well-known interpretations: either hyperbole in making it the maṣdar itself, or the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "a place of security", or the maṣdar standing in the place of the active participle, i.e. "secure", by way of figurative usage, as in His words «حَرَماً آمِناً». The second: it is governed by an omitted verb, the implied form being: "And when We made the House a place of return, so make it secure, no one transgressing against another in it". The meaning is that Allah made the House inviolable by His ruling; and this may be supported by the reading «اتَّخِذُوا» as an imperative. On this, «وأَمْناً» and what governs it belong to the category of conjoining clauses, an imperative clause being conjoined to a declarative one; on the first, it is a conjoining of single words.
His words: {واتخذوا}: Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read «واتَّخذوا» as a past verb in the form of a statement, and the rest in the form of an imperative. As for the reading as a statement, there are three aspects in it. The first: it is conjoined to «جَعَلْنا», which is in implication genitive by «إذ», so the speech is a single clause. The second: it is conjoined to the whole of His words «وإذ جَعَلْنا», so «إذ» needs to be implied, i.e. "and when they took", and the speech is two clauses. The third, mentioned by Abū al-Baqāʾ: it is conjoined to something omitted, the implied form being: "so they resorted [to it] and took".
As for the reading as an imperative, there are four aspects in it. The first: it is conjoined to «اذكروا», if it is said that the address here is to the Children of Israel, i.e. "remember My favour and take". The second: it is conjoined to the command implied in His words «مثابةً», as though He said: "resort [to it] and take". Al-Mahdawī mentioned these two aspects.
The third: it is governed by an omitted saying, i.e. "and We said: take", if it is said that the address is to Abraham and his offspring, or to Muḥammad, upon him be peace, and his community. The fourth: it is resumptive; Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned it.
His words: {مِن مَّقَامِ}: in «مِنْ» there are three aspects. The first: it is partitive, and this is the apparent one. The second: it means «في» (in). The third: it is redundant (zāʾida), on the view of al-Akhfash. These two [i.e. the latter] are worthless. «المَقام» here is the place of standing; it is also fit for time and for the maṣdar. Its origin is «مَقْوَم»; it underwent weakening by transferring the vowel of the wāw to the quiescent letter before it and changing it into alif. It is used figuratively for a gathering of people, just as they are referred to as «المجلس». Zuhayr said:
714 - وفيهمْ مَقاماتٌ حِسانٌ وجوهُهمْ ... وأَنْدِيَةٌ يَنْتابُها القولُ والفِعْلُ
(Among them are assemblies fair of face, and councils frequented by [wise] speech and deed.)
His words: {مُصَلًّى}: the object of «اتَّخِذُوا»; here too it is a noun of place, and in the exegesis it has come with the meaning of qibla. It has been said: it is a maṣdar, so the omission of a muḍāf is necessary, i.e. "a place of prayer". Its alif is changed from a wāw, the origin being «مُصَّلَّوَ», because الصلاة is from roots with final wāw, as was said at the beginning of the book.
His words: {وَإِسْمَاعِيلَ}: «إسماعيل» is a non-Arabic proper name, and it has two dialectal forms: with lām and with nūn; on the latter is the poet's saying:
715 - قال جواري الحَيِّ لمَّا جِينا ... هذا وربِّ البيتِ إسماعينا
(The girls of the tribe said when we came: "This, by the Lord of the House, is Ismāʿīn!")
Its plural is سَماعِلة, سَماعيل and أساميع. Among the strangest things reported about naming with it is that when Abraham, upon him be peace, prayed to Allah to grant him a son, he used to say: "Hear, Īl! Hear, Īl!" (اسْمَعْ إيل), and Īl is Allah the Exalted, so he named his son with that.
His words: {أَن طَهِّرَا}: two aspects are permissible in «أَنْ».
