What led Sībawayh to this, rather than making it shared between singular and plural like «جُنُب» and «شُلُل», is that had they intended sharing they would not have put it in the dual, just as they do not put «جُنُب» and «شُلُل» in the dual; when they put it in the dual and said «فُلْكان», we knew that they did not intend the sharing they intended in «جُنُب» and «شُلُل». Its parallel is «ناقةٌ هِجان» and «نوقٌ هِجان» (a pure-white she-camel / pure-white she-camels), and «دِرْع دِلاص» and «دُروع دِلاص» (a smooth coat of mail / smooth coats of mail): the kasra in the singular is like the kasra in «كتاب», and in the plural like the kasra in «رجال», because they said in the dual «هِجانان» and «دِلاصان».

The second: the doctrine of al-Akhfash, that it is a collective noun (ism jamʿ) like «صَحْب» and «رَكْب». The third: that it is the plural of «فَلَك» with two fatḥas, like «أَسَد» and «أُسْد». The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] chose that it is shared between singular and plural; he is refuted by the dual mentioned above, and he gave no reason for his choice.

When «فُلْك» is singular it is masculine; the Exalted said: {فِي الفلك المشحون}. They said — Abū al-Baqāʾ among them —: it may also be feminine, adducing His saying: {والفلك التي تَجْرِي}, where He described it with a feminine attribute. There is no proof in that, since the plural may be meant by it, and then it is described with what a single feminine noun is described with. Its origin is from turning round; from it are «فَلَك السماء» (the celestial sphere), because the stars revolve in it, «فَلْكَة المِغْزَل» (the whorl of the spindle), and «فَلَكَتِ الجاريةُ», [said when] the girl's breast became rounded. He gave the ṣila (relative clause) of «التي» as an imperfect verb to indicate renewal and occurrence. Attributing running to them [the ships] is figurative (majāz). His saying «في البحر» is emphasis, since it is known that they do not run anywhere else; it is like His saying: {يَطِيرُ بِجَنَاحَيْهِ} [al-Anʿām: 38].

His saying: «بما يَنْفَعُ»: there are two views on «ما». One: that it is a nominal relative; on this the bāʾ is for the ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e.: they run accompanied by the goods that benefit people. The second: that it is a particle [maṣdariyya]; on this the bāʾ is causal, i.e.: they run because of people's benefit in trade and other things.

His saying: {مِنَ السمآء مِن مَّآءٍ}: the first «مِنْ» means the beginning of the extent (ibtidāʾ al-ghāya), i.e.: He sent down from the direction of the sky. As for the second, it admits three views. The first: that it is for explaining the genus (bayān al-jins), for what is sent down from the sky is water and other things. The second: that it is partitive, for what is sent down of it is a part, not the whole. The third: that it and what follows it are a badal (substitute) from His saying «من السماء», a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl) with the governor repeated. Both of them — I mean the first «مِنْ» and the second — are attached to «أَنْزَلَ». If it is said: how can two identical particles be attached to a single governor? The answer is that what is disallowed is for them to be identical in meaning without conjunction or badal; you do not say «أخذت من الدراهم من الدنانير». As for the verse, the objection does not apply to it: if you make the second «مِنْ» explicative or partitive, it is clear, because their meanings differ, the first being for the beginning; and if you make it for the beginning of the extent, it and what follows it are a badal, and that is permissible [in] the badal, as stated. It is also possible for the first «مِنْ» to be attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl: either from the relative noun itself, namely «ما», or from its pronoun made accusative by «أنزل», i.e.: and what Allah sent down while it is from the sky.

His saying: {فَأَحْيَا بِهِ}: He conjoined «أحيا» to «أنزل», which is the ṣila, with the fāʾ of immediate sequence, to indicate the speed of growth. «به» is attached to «أحيا»; the bāʾ may be causal or the bāʾ of the instrument, and all of this is figurative, for He is exalted above that. The pronoun in «به» refers back to the relative noun.

His saying: {وَبَثَّ فِيهَا}: «بَثَّ» admits two views. The more evident of them: that it is conjoined to «أنزل», falling under the scope of the ṣila, because His saying «فَأَحْيا» is conjoined to «أنزل» and so joined to it, and the two together became like a single thing; it is as though it were said: "and what He sent down in the earth of water and spread in it of every creature", because they grow through fertility and live through the rain. This is the text of al-Zamakhsharī. The second: that it is conjoined to «أحيا».

The Shaykh found its conjunction to that problematic, because it is part of the ṣila of the relative noun, so there must be a pronoun returning from this clause, and there is no pronoun in the wording, since «فيها» refers back to the earth; it remains that it be omitted, its implied form being «وبث به فيها». But a pronoun put in the genitive by a preposition may not be omitted except under conditions: that the relative noun be put in the genitive by the same preposition, that what they are attached to be the same, that the pronoun not be restricted, that it be the only possible link, and that the prepositional phrase not stand in place of a nominative; and the relative noun here is not in the genitive at all. When he found this problematic for the reason he mentioned, he explained the verse as involving the omission of a nominal relative. He said: "That is permissible and widespread in their speech, though the Basrans do not permit it." He cited as evidence for it:
789 - ما الذي دأبُه احتياطَ وحَزْمٌ ... وهواه أطاع يَسْتويانِ
(He whose habit is caution and resolve, and [he who] obeyed his whim, are not equal.)
i.e. "and he who obeyed"; and his saying:
790 - أَمَنْ يهجو رسولَ الله منكم ... ويمدَحُه ويَنْصُره سَواءُ
(Is he among you who satirises the Messenger of Allah, and [he who] praises and supports him, equal?)
i.e. "and he who supports him"; and his saying:
791 - فواللهِ ما نِلْتُمْ وما نِيلَ منكمُ ... بمعتدلٍ وَفْقٍ ولا متقاربِ
(By Allah, what you obtained and what was obtained from you are not balanced and even, nor close.)
i.e. "what is it that you obtained"; and His saying, the Exalted: {وقولوا آمَنَّا بالذي أُنزِلَ إِلَيْنَا وَأُنزِلَ إِلَيْكُمْ} [al-ʿAnkabūt: 46], i.e. "and in what was sent down to you", so that it matches His saying: {والكتاب الذي نَزَّلَ على رَسُولِهِ والكتاب الذي أَنَزلَ مِن قَبْلُ} [al-Nisāʾ: 136]. Then the Shaykh said: "The first assumption may also work" — meaning the permissibility of the omission even though its condition is not met. He said: "That has occurred in their poetry", and he recited:
792 - وإنَّ لساني شُهْدَةٌ يُشْتَفَى بها ... وهُوَّ على مَنْ صَبَّه اللهُ عَلْقَمُ
(My tongue is a honeycomb by which one is healed, but it is colocynth to the one upon whom Allah pours it.)
i.e. colocynth to him; and his saying:
793 - لعلَّ الذي أَصْعَدْتِني أَنْ يَرُدَّني ... إلى الأرض إن لم يَقْدِرِ الخيرَ قِادرُه
(Perhaps that by which you raised me up will bring me back down to the earth, if the One who decrees does not decree good.)
i.e. "you raised me up by it".

His saying: {مِن كُلِّ دَآبَّةٍ}: «كل» admits three views. One: that it is in the position of the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of «بثَّ», with «مِنْ» partitive. The second: that «مِنْ» is redundant (zāʾida) according to the doctrine of al-Akhfash, and «كلَّ دابة» is likewise the mafʿūl bihi of «بَثَّ». The third: that it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the omitted object of «بَثَّ», if we say that there is an omitted relative noun there, its implied form being: and what He spread, being of every creature. «مِنْ» then admits two views: one, that it is explicative; the second, that it is partitive. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "The object of «بَثَّ» is omitted, its implied form being: and He spread in it creatures, every creature." The apparent sense of this is that {مِن كُلِّ دَآبَّةٍ} is a naʿt (adjective) of that omitted [noun], and it is an assumption that yields nothing.

«البَثُّ» is spreading and scattering. [The poet] said:
794 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... وفي الأرضِ مَبْثُوثاً شجاعٌ وعَقْربُ
(…and in the earth, spread about, are serpent and scorpion.)
Its imperfect is «يَبُثُّ» with ḍamma on the middle radical, which is the analogical rule for transitive doubled verbs; the kasra has occurred in a few words: they said «نَمَّ الحديثَ يَنِمُّه» (he carried tales) with both [vowels].

«الدابَّة» is a name for every animal. Some claimed that birds are excluded from it, and this was rejected by the saying of ʿAlqama:
795 - كأنَّهم صابَتْ عليهم سَحابةٌ ... صواعِقُها لطيرِهِنَّ دَبيبُ
(As though a cloud had poured upon them, whose thunderbolts make their birds creep.)
and by the saying of al-Aʿshā:
796 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... دبيبَ قَطا البَطْحَاءِ في كلِّ مَنْهَلِ
(…like the creeping of the sandgrouse of the valley-bed to every watering place.)
and by His saying: {والله خَلَقَ كُلَّ دَآبَّةٍ} [al-Nūr: 45], after which He detailed [them] with those that walk on two legs, which are humans and birds.

His saying: {وَتَصْرِيفِ الرياح}: «تصريف» is the maṣdar of «صَرَّف», which is turning back and turning about. It may be annexed to its agent, with the object omitted, its implied form being: and the winds' driving of the clouds, for they drive the clouds; or annexed to its object, with the agent omitted, i.e.: and Allah's directing of the wind. «الرياح» is the broken plural of «ريح». The yāʾ of «الريح» and «الرياح» derives from a wāw; the original is «رِوْح», because it is from «راح يروح». It was changed in «ريح» because it is quiescent and what precedes it has kasra, and in «رياح» because it is a middle radical in a plural after a kasra, followed by an alif, and it is quiescent in the singular; this is a regular substitution. For that reason, when the cause of its change was removed, it returned to its origin, and they said «أَرْواح». [The poet] said:
797 - أَرَبَّتْ بها الأرواحُ كلَّ عَشِيَّةٍ ... فلم يَبْقَ إلاَّ آلُ خَيْمٍ مُنَضَّدِ
(The winds kept at it every evening, until nothing remained but the poles of tents piled up.)
And similar to it:
798 - لَبَيْتٌ تَخْفُقُ الأرواحُ فيه ... أَحَبُّ إليَّ من قصرٍ مُنيفِ
(A tent in which the winds flutter is dearer to me than a lofty palace.)
ʿUmāra ibn ʿAqīl ibn Bilāl committed a solecism by saying «الأرياح» in his poetry. Abū Ḥātim said to him: "«الأرياح» is not permissible." ʿUmāra said to him: "Do you not hear their saying «رياح»?" Abū Ḥātim said: "That is different from this." He said: "You are right", and retracted. The Shaykh said: "In what I memorised long ago, «الأرياح» occurred in the poetry of one of the eloquent Arabs whose speech is cited as evidence, as though they built it on the singular even though the cause of the change is absent in the plural, just as they said «عيد» and «أعياد», the original being «أَعْواد» because it is from «عاد يَعُود»; but when the substitution was kept it was treated like a radical letter." I say: what the Shaykh said is supported by [the fact] that their keeping the yāʾ in «الأرياح» is because of confusion between it and «أَرْواح», the plural of «رُوح» (spirit), just as they said: the yāʾ was kept in «أعياد» to distinguish it from «أَعْواد», the plural of «عُود» (stick of firewood); for that reason they said in the diminutive «عُيَيْد», not «عُوَيْد», and explained it by the said confusion.

Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "In the Qur'an it has come in the plural with mercy and in the singular with punishment, except in His saying: {وَجَرَيْنَ بِهِم بِرِيحٍ طَيِّبَةٍ} [Yūnus: 22]. This is its predominant occurrence in speech. In the ḥadīth: '«الله [Translator's note: so in the source, for «اللهمّ»] اجعلها رياحاً ولا تَجْعَلْها ريحاً»' (O Allah, make it winds and do not make it a wind), because the wind of punishment is violent, its parts cohering as though it were a single body, while the wind of mercy is gentle and broken up. It was put in the singular with the ships — meaning in Yūnus — only because it is for making ships sail, and that is a single continuous [wind]; then it was described as good, so the overlap between it and the wind of punishment was removed." End of quotation. What he said is refuted by the readers' disagreement in eleven places, whose details will come. What should rather be said is that the plural never came with punishment at all, while the singular came with both; for that reason he [the Prophet], peace be upon him, specified the plural form in his supplication.

Here Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read «الريح» in the singular, and the rest in the plural. The plural is because of the diversity of their kinds — south wind, west wind, east wind and others — and the singular is meant as the genus.

«السحاب» is a generic noun whose singular is «سَحابة»; it was so called because of its being drawn along (insiḥāb), just as it was called «حَبِيّ» because it crawls (yaḥbū) — Abū ʿAlī [al-Fārisī] mentioned that. Considering it a generic noun, He described it with the attribute of a masculine singular in His saying «المُسَخَّر», as in His saying: {أَعْجَازُ نَخْلٍ مُّنقَعِرٍ} [al-Qamar: 20]; and when He considered its meaning on another occasion, He described it with what a plural is described with, in His saying: {سَحَاباً ثِقَالاً} [al-Aʿrāf: 57]. It may also be described with what a single feminine noun is described with, as in His saying: {أَعْجَازُ نَخْلٍ خَاوِيَةٍ} [al-Ḥāqqa: 7]. So it is with every generic noun: it has two usages, the masculine in consideration of the wording and the feminine in consideration of the meaning.

«التسخير» is subjugation and making a thing come under obedience. Al-Rāghib said: "It is compulsion to act, and it is stronger than coercion."

His saying: {بَيْنَ السمآء}: there are two views on «بين». One: that it is accusative by His saying «المُسخَّرِ», and so is an adverb of the subjugation. The second: that it is a ḥāl from the pronoun latent (mustatir) in the passive participle, and so is attached to an omitted element, i.e.: being between the sky [and the earth]. «لآياتٍ» is the noun of «إنَّ», and the prepositional phrase is its fronted khabar (predicate). The lām entered the noun because it comes after the khabar; had it been in its [normal] place, that would not have been permissible in it.

And His saying: {لِّقَوْمٍ} is in the position of the accusative because it is a naʿt of «آيات», and so is attached to an omitted element. And His saying «يَعْقِلون»: the clause is in the position of the genitive [Translator's note: the source reads «في محلذ شجرٍ», a misprint for «في محلّ جرٍّ»] because it is a naʿt of «قوم».

semin-durr:178-178.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {القصاص فِي القتلى}: i.e. because of the slain; «في» can be causal, as in his words (upon him be peace): «A woman entered the Fire in [the matter of] a cat», i.e. because of it. The pattern «فَعْلَى» is regularly a plural of faʿīl in the sense of mafʿūl (passive); something of this has preceded at His words: {وَإِن يَأتُوكُمْ أسارى} [al-Baqara: 85].
His words: {الحر بِالْحُرِّ}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate); the implied form is: "the free man is taken for the free man", or "is killed for the free man". So you supply a specific verb of being (kawn khāṣṣ), omitted because the context indicates it, since the bāʾ in it is causal. It is not permissible to supply a general verb of being (kawn muṭlaq), since there would be no benefit if you said "the free man is [existing] for the free man" — unless you supply a muḍāf, i.e. "the killing of the free man is for the free man". The Shaykh allowed «الحُرُّ» to be nominative by an omitted verb, its implied form being "the free man is killed for the free man", indicated by His words {القصاص فِي القتلى}, since «القصاص» suggests this implied verb; but this is far-fetched.
Al-qiṣāṣ is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of qāṣṣahu yuqāṣṣuhu qiṣāṣan and muqāṣṣatan, like qātaltuhu qitālan and muqātalatan. Its origin is from qaṣaṣtu al-shayʾ, [meaning] you followed its trace, because it is a following up of the blood of the slain.
Al-ḥurr (free) is an adjective, and the plural of an adjective of the pattern «فُعْل» on afʿāl is not regular; they said ḥurr and aḥrār, murr and amrār. The feminine is ḥurra, and its plural ḥarāʾir is likewise a matter of attested usage. One says: ḥarra the boy, yaḥarru, ḥurriyyatan (he became free).
His words: {فَمَنْ عُفِيَ}: two interpretations are permissible for «مَنْ». The first: that it is conditional. The second: that it is relative. On both, its position is nominative as mubtadaʾ. On the first, «عُفِي» is in the position of the jussive (majzūm) by the condition; on the second it has no position. The fāʾ in His words «فاتِّباع» is obligatory on the first, and its position together with what follows is jussive; and it is permissible on the second, and its position with what follows is nominative as khabar. The apparent view is that «مَنْ» is the killer, and that the pronoun in «له» and «أخيه» refers to «مَنْ»; «شيءٌ» is what stands in place of the fāʿil (i.e. nāʾib fāʿil, deputy agent), and by it the maṣdar is meant. «عُفِي» is made passive even though it is intransitive, because an intransitive verb passes over to the maṣdar, as in His words: {فَإِذَا نُفِخَ فِي الصور نَفْخَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ} [al-Muʾminūn: 101] «[Translator's note: the wording quoted combines al-Muʾminūn: 101 and al-Ḥāqqa: 13.]». The brother is the slain man or the next of kin of the blood; He called him a brother of the killer to incline him to compassion toward him. This maṣdar standing in place of the fāʿil means the blood that is pardoned. ʿAfā passes over to the offender and to the offence by «عن»: you say "I pardoned Zayd (ʿafawtu ʿan Zaydin)" and "I pardoned Zayd's sin (ʿafawtu ʿan dhanbi Zaydin)"; when it passes over to both together, it passes over to the offender with lām and to the offence with ʿan: you say "ʿafawtu li-Zaydin ʿan dhanbihi" (I pardoned Zayd his sin). The verse belongs to this class, i.e. "whoever is pardoned for his offence". It has also been said that «مَنْ» is the next of kin of the blood, i.e. whoever is granted, out of his brother's blood, a substitute for the blood, namely retaliation or blood-money; «شيء» then means that due right, and the brother means the slain. On this view the killer may also be meant by it, with «الشيء» meaning the blood-money. On these two views «عُفِي» means "was made easy"; it has also been said that it means "was left".
Al-Zamakhsharī denounced those who explained «عُفِيَ» as meaning «تُرِكَ» (was left). He said: If you say: why did you not explain «عُفي» as meaning «تُركَ», so that «شيء» would have the sense of a mafʿūl bihi (direct object)? I say: because ʿafā al-shayʾa meaning "he left it" is not established; rather [what is established is] «أعفاه», and from it «وَأَعْفوا اللَّحى» (and leave the beards to grow). If you say: their saying "ʿafā atharahu" when one effaces and removes it is established, so why not make its meaning: "whoever has something of his brother['s offence] effaced for him"? I say: it is an expression ill-suited to its place; whereas pardon (al-ʿafw) in the domain of offences is a current and well-known expression in the Book, the Sunna and people's usage, so one does not turn away from it to another expression that is ill-suited and out of place. You see many of those who engage in this science, when explaining a difficult passage of Allah's speech defeats them, venture to invent a usage and to impute to the Arabs what they did not know; and this is an audacity from which refuge is sought with Allah.
The Shaykh said: «If it is established that «عَفَا» means "effaced", it is not far-fetched to take the verse in that sense, and the attribution of «عَفَا» to its nominative would be a literal attribution, because it would then be an explicit mafʿūl bihi; whereas when it is intransitive, its attribution to its nominative is figurative, because it is a maṣdar likened to a mafʿūl bihi. So the two interpretations may balance each other: I mean intransitive ʿafā, because of its currency in [the domain of] offences, and transitive «عفا» meaning «مَحَا», because of its literal connection with its nominative». If it is said: «عَفَا» is made to include the meaning of «ترك» — the answer is that such inclusion (taḍmīn) is not a regular rule; yet Ibn ʿAṭiyya allowed ʿafā to mean taraka. It has also been said that «عُفِيَ» means "was in excess", the meaning being: whoever of the two parties has something of those blood-monies in excess over the other — from their saying ʿafā al-shayʾu when a thing became abundant. The most apparent of these views is the first.
His words: {فاتباع بالمعروف}: there are three interpretations of the nominative of «اتباع». The first: that it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ; Ibn ʿAṭiyya gave its implied form as "then the ruling, or the obligation, is following up", and al-Zamakhsharī as "then the matter is a following up". Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: «This is the way with obligatory things; recommended things come in the accusative, as in His words: {فَضَرْبَ الرقاب} [Muḥammad: 4]». The Shaykh said: «I do not know what the difference between the accusative and the nominative is, except what they have mentioned, that the nominal clause is more permanent and more emphatic; perhaps this is Ibn ʿAṭiyya's basis, as they said concerning His words: {قَالُواْ سَلاَماً قَالَ سَلاَمٌ} [Hūd: 69]».
The second: that it is nominative by an implied verb; al-Zamakhsharī gave its implied form as "then let there be a following up". The Shaykh said: «This is weak, since «كان» is generally not implied except after the conditional «إنْ» and «لو», where there is evidence indicating it».
The third: that it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted. Some supplied it before it, i.e. "then upon him is a following up", and some supplied it after it, i.e. "then a following up in fairness is upon him".
His words: {بالمعروف}: three interpretations. The first: that it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «اتِّباع», so its position is accusative. The second: that it is an adjective of His word «اتِّباع», so it is attached to something omitted and its position is nominative. The third: that it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the omitted hāʾ, its implied form being "then upon him is following it up, being just"; the governing word in the ḥāl is the sense of being-established (istiqrār).
His words: {وَأَدَآءٌ}: there are four interpretations of its nominative: the three stated for His words «فاتِّباعٌ», since it is conjoined to it; and the fourth: that it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the preposition and genitive noun after it, namely «بإحسان»; this is far-fetched. «إليه» is in the position of the accusative, being attached to «أداء»; and it may be in the position of the nominative as an adjective of «أداء», so attached to something omitted, i.e. "and a payment directed to him".
«بإحسانٍ» has four interpretations: the three stated for «بالمعروف», and the fourth: that it is the khabar of «الأداء», as preceded in the fourth interpretation of the nominative of «أداء». The hāʾ in «إليه» refers to the one who pardons even though he has not been mentioned, because «عَفَا» necessarily implies one who pardons; so it belongs to the class of explaining a pronoun by something that accompanies it in some way. Of this kind is {حتى تَوَارَتْ بالحجاب} [Ṣād: 32], i.e. the sun, because the mention of «العشيّ» (the evening) indicates it. Likewise:
828 - فإنَّك والتأبينَ عروةَ بعدَما ... دَعَاكَ وأيدينا إليه شَوارعُ
لكالرجلِ الحادي وقد تَلع الضحى ... وطيرُ المنايا فوقَهُنَّ أواقِعُ
(You, eulogising ʿUrwa after he had called you while our hands were stretched out toward him, are like the camel-driver singing when the forenoon has risen high, while the birds of death are alighting over them.)
The pronoun in «فوقهُنَّ» is for the camels, because the word «الحادي» (the camel-driver) indicates them, since they accompany him in some way.
His words: {ذلك تَخْفِيفٌ}: «ذلك» points to what He prescribed of pardon and blood-money. «من ربكم» is in the position of the nominative because it is an adjective of what precedes it, so it is attached to something omitted. «رَحمة» likewise has its adjective omitted, i.e. "and a mercy from your Lord".
His words: {فَمَنِ اعتدى}: «مَنْ» admits the two interpretations allowed in His words {فَمَنْ عُفِيَ لَهُ}, namely being conditional or relative, and everything mentioned there applies here.
His words: {وَلَكُمْ فِي القصاص حَيَاةٌ}: «لكم» may be the khabar, with «في القصاص» attached to the sense of being-established contained in «لكم»; or it may be attached to something omitted as a ḥāl from «حياةٌ», since it was originally an adjective of it, and when it was placed before it, it became accusative as a ḥāl. Or «في القصاص» may be the khabar, with «لكم» attached to the being-established contained in it. The full treatment of this has preceded at His words: {وَلَكُمْ فِي الأرض مُسْتَقَرٌّ} [al-Baqara: 36], and there are things there that do not apply here.
Abū al-Jawzāʾ read «في القَصَص», meaning by it the Quran. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: «It may also be a maṣdar like al-qiṣāṣ, i.e. when the killer's track is followed (quṣṣa), he is killed as he killed».
Al-qiṣāṣ is the maṣdar of qaṣṣa, i.e. he followed up; this is the root meaning of the material. So the meaning of al-qiṣāṣ is following up the blood by retaliation (qawad). From it comes «القصيص», for the pasture that is sought out after grazing; al-qaṣaṣ is following up reports, and likewise al-qaṣṣ. Al-qaṣṣ is also gypsum, and from it comes the ḥadīth: «He (upon him be blessing and peace) forbade the taqṣīṣ of graves», i.e. plastering them.
A parallel to this speech is the Arabs' saying: «Killing is most effective against killing (al-qatlu awfā li-l-qatl)»; it is also related as «most preventive of killing (anfā li-l-qatl)», and as «most restraining of killing (akaffu li-l-qatl)». Although this is eloquent, the scholars have shown numerous aspects of eloquence distinguishing the noble verse from it, found in the noble verse and not in it. Among them: their saying repeats the noun within a single sentence. Among them: an omission must be supplied in it, because «أَنْفَى», «أَوْفَى» and «أكفُّ» are elatives (afʿal al-tafḍīl), so the thing surpassed must be supplied, i.e. "more preventive of killing than leaving off killing". Among them: al-qiṣāṣ is more general «[Translator's note: the text reads «أَمُّ», evidently for «أَعَمُّ», "more general".]», since it occurs for life and for limbs, whereas killing occurs only for life. Among them: the apparent sense of their saying is that a thing's existence is a cause of its own negation. Among them: the verse contains a type of rhetorical embellishment (badīʿ) called ṭibāq (antithesis), which is setting a thing against its opposite; it resembles His words: {أَضْحَكَ وأبكى} [al-Najm: 43].
His words: {ياأولي الألباب}: an annexed vocative (munādā muḍāf), the sign of whose accusative is the yāʾ. Know that «أولي» is a collective noun (ism jamʿ), because its singular, namely «ذو», is from a different root-form. It is treated like the sound masculine plural, in its nominative with wāw and its accusative and genitive with yāʾ preceded by kasra; and its rule of necessarily being annexed to a generic noun is the rule of its singular. This has preceded at His words: {ذَوِي القربى} [al-Baqara: 177]. Its feminine counterpart is ulāt. Both are written in the codex with a wāw after the hamza; they said: in order to distinguish «أُولي كذا» (possessors of such-and-such) in the accusative and genitive from «إلى», which is a preposition; then the rest of the class was treated in the same way. This is as preceded in distinguishing «أولئك» as a demonstrative from «إليك» as a preposition and its genitive noun, and it has preceded. If you name [someone] with «أولي» taken from «أُولي كذا», you say "jāʾa ulūna" and "raʾaytu ulīna", restoring the nūn, because it is as though implied in the state of annexation; it is the parallel of ḍāribū Zaydin and ḍāribī Zaydin.
Al-albāb is the plural of «لُبّ», which is the intellect free of whim. It was so called for one of two reasons: either because it is built from labba bi-l-makān, he stayed in the place; or from al-lubāb, which is the pure part. One says labubtu bi-l-makān and labibtu, with ḍamma and kasra on the ʿayn. The occurrence of a doubled verb on faʿula with ḍamma on the ʿayn is anomalous; they dispensed with it by faʿala with fatḥa on the ʿayn. That is in a limited number of words, such as ʿazuztu, sarurtu, labubtu, damumtu and malultu; these are with ḍamma and with fatḥa, except labubtu, which is with ḍamma and kasra, as preceded.

semin-durr:96-96.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {وَلَتَجِدَنَّهُمْ أَحْرَصَ الناس} ...: this lām is the reply to an omitted oath, and the nūn is for emphasis; its implied form is: «واللهِ لَتَجِدَنَّهُم» ("By Allah, you will surely find them"). «وجَدَ» here takes two objects, the first of which is the pronoun and the second «أَحْرَصَ». When it takes two objects it is like «عَلِمَ» (to know) in meaning, as in: {وَإِن وَجَدْنَآ أَكْثَرَهُمْ لَفَاسِقِينَ} [al-Aʿrāf: 10] [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse is al-Aʿrāf: 102]. It may also take one object, its meaning being that of «لِقيَ» and «أصابَ» (to meet, come upon), and «أَحْرَصَ» is then accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial): either according to the opinion of those who do not stipulate indefiniteness in the ḥāl, or according to the opinion of those who hold that the annexation of «أَفْعَل» to a definite noun [is not real annexation]. [Translator's note: the source's sentence here appears defective.] So it came according to one of the two permissible options, I mean non-agreement. That is because when it is annexed to a definite noun with the intention of «مِنْ», two options are permissible in it: agreement with what precedes it, as in «الزيدان أَفْضَلا الرجالِ», «الزيدون أفاضل الرجال», «هند فُضْلى النساء» and «الهنودُ فُضْلَياتُ النساءِ» — and of this is His saying «أكابِرَ مجرميها» — and non-agreement, as in «الزيدون أَفْضَلُ الرجالِ» ("the Zayds are the best of men"), and on this is this verse. Both options are eloquent — contrary to Ibn al-Sarrāj, who claimed that the singular is obligatory, and to Abū Manṣūr al-Jawālīqī, who claimed that agreement is more eloquent. When it is annexed to a definite noun, it must be part of it; for that reason the grammarians disallowed «يوسُف أَحْسَنُ إخوته» ("Yūsuf is the most handsome of his brothers") in the sense of preference, and interpreted what gives the impression of otherwise, as in «الناقصُ والأشجُّ أعدلا بني مروان» ("al-Nāqiṣ and al-Ashajj are the two most just of the Banū Marwān"), as meaning "the two just ones among them." As for:
620 - يا رَبَّ موسى أَظْلَمِي وَأَظْلَمُهْ ... فاصبُبْ عليه مَلِكاً لا يَرْحَمُهْ
(O Lord of Mūsā, [whichever is] the more unjust of me and him, pour down upon him a king who will not have mercy on him.)
it is anomalous; what made it allowable is that the second «أَظْلَمَ» is inserted, as though he said: «أَظْلَمُنا» ("the more unjust of us"). As for when it is annexed to an indefinite noun, its ruling has preceded at His saying «أوَّل كافر».
His saying: {على حَيَاةٍ} is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أَحْرَصَ», because this verb is transitive by «على»; you say: «حَرَصْتُ عليه» ("I was eager for it"). The indefiniteness of «حياة» draws attention to the fact that He meant a particular life, namely prolonged life; for that reason the reading with it is more fitting than the reading of Ubayy, «على الحياة», with the definite article. It was also said that it is on the omission of a muḍāf, its implied form being «على طُولِ حياةٍ» ("for length of life"). The apparent view is that it needs no adjective or muḍāf to be supplied; rather the meaning is that they are the most eager of people for life of any kind. And if you say: "how [so], even if it is great?" — then it is more emphatic in describing them with that. [Translator's note: this sentence is obscure in the source.] The root form of «حياة» is «حَيَيَة»; the yāʾ was vowelled and the letter before it had fatḥa, so it was changed into alif.
His saying: {وَمِنَ الذين أَشْرَكُواْ}: it may be connected, falling under the elative (afʿal al-tafḍīl), and it may be cut off from it. On the view that it is connected to it there are three views. The first: that it is construed according to the meaning, for the meaning of «أحرصَ الناس» is «أَحْرَصَ من الناسِ» ("more eager than people"), so it is as though it were said: "more eager than people and than those who associated partners." The second: that [the elative] was omitted from the second because the first indicates it, the implied form being: «وأحرصَ من الذين أشركوا» ("and more eager than those who associated partners"). On what has been established — that {وَمِنَ الذين أَشْرَكُواْ} is connected to the elative — «مِنْ» must be mentioned, because «أَحرصَ» has been applied to the Jews; had it been conjoined without «مِنْ», it would have been conjoined to «الناس», and the meaning would have been: "you will find them the most eager of those who associated partners," which would entail annexing «أَفْعَل» to something under which they are not included, because the Jews are not among these particular polytheists, since in their exegesis they said that they are the Magians, or Arabs who worship idols — unless it is said that in what comes second there is tolerated what is not tolerated in what comes first; in that case, had «مِن» not been brought, it would have been permissible.
The third: that there is omission and transposition in the speech, the implied form being: "and you will surely find them, and a group of those who associated partners, the most eager of people," so that {وَمِنَ الذين أَشْرَكُواْ} is an adjective of something omitted, that omitted thing being conjoined to the pronoun in «لتجدنَّهم». Although this is correct in meaning, the construction is averse to it, especially on the view of those who restrict transposition to poetic necessity. On the view that it is cut off from «أفعل», {وَمِنَ الذين أَشْرَكُواْ} is a fronted khabar (predicate), and «يَوَدُّ أحدُهم» an adjective of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being: "and among those who associated partners are a people — or a party — each of whom would love." This is one of the places where omission of a qualified noun with its clause [as adjective] is regular, as in His saying: {وَمَا مِنَّآ إِلاَّ لَهُ مَقَامٌ مَّعْلُومٌ} [al-Ṣāffāt: 164], and their saying: «مِنَّا ظَعَنَ ومنَّا أقام» ("among us is one who departed and among us one who stayed"). The apparent view is that those who associated partners are other than the Jews, as has preceded. Al-Zamakhsharī allowed them to be of the Jews, because they said: "ʿUzayr is the son of Allah"; so it would be a report that among this group whose eagerness for life is intense there are those who would love to be given a life of a thousand years, and it would be a case of the overt noun, which suggests predominance, occurring in place of the pronoun, since the implied form is: "and among them are a people each of whom would love." It has become clear from what preceded that the speech belongs to the category of conjoining single words on the view that {وَمِنَ الذين أَشْرَكُواْ} falls under «أفعل», and to the category of conjoining clauses on the view that it is cut off.
His saying: «يَوَدُّ أحدُهم»: this is built on what preceded. If it is said that {وَمِنَ الذين أَشْرَكُواْ} falls under «أَفْعَلَ», there are five views on «يَوَدُّ». The first: that it is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «لَتَجِدَنَّهم», i.e. you will find them, each of them wishing. The second: that it is a ḥāl from «الذين أشركوا», so that its governor is the omitted «أَحْرَصَ». The third: that it is a ḥāl from the fāʿil (agent) of «أشْركوا». The fourth: that it is resumptive, begun anew to report the clarification of their state regarding the increase of their eagerness for life. The fifth, which is the view of the Kufans: that it is the ṣila of an omitted relative noun, that relative noun being an adjective of «الذين أشركوا», the implied form being: "and than those who associated partners, those each of whom would love." If the view of its being cut off is held, then it is in the position of nominative, because it is an adjective of an omitted mubtadaʾ, as preceded. «أحدٌ» here means «واحد» ("one"), and its hamza is a substitute for wāw; it is not the «أحد» used in negation, for that one's hamza is radical in itself, and it is not used in pure affirmation.
«يودُّ» is the imperfect of «وَدِدْتُ», with kasra on the middle radical in the past; for that reason the wāw was not elided in the imperfect, because it does not occur between a yāʾ and a kasra, unlike «يَعِد» and its class. Al-Kisāʾī related «ودَدْت» with fatḥa. Some said: "On this basis one would say «يَوِدُّ» with kasra on the wāw". «الوَدادة» is wishing.
His saying: «لو يُعَمَّر»: there are three views on this «لو». The first — which is in accord with the rules of the Basran grammarians — is that it is a particle [indicating] what would have occurred upon the occurrence of something else, and its apodosis is omitted because «يَوَدُّ» indicates it, and the object of «يَوَدُّ» is omitted because «لو يُعَمَّرَ» indicates it. The implied form is: "each of them would love long life; if he were given life for a thousand years, he would be pleased with that." So from each one was omitted what the other indicates, and it then has no grammatical position. The second — held by the Kufans, Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī and Abū al-Baqāʾ — is that it is maṣdariyya, like the «أَنْ» that makes [the imperfect] subjunctive, so it has no apodosis, and from it and what follows it a maṣdar (verbal noun) is formed which is the object of «يَوَدُّ», the implied form being: "each of them would love his being given life of a thousand years." Abū al-Baqāʾ adduced as evidence that the «لو» of impossibility (imtināʿiyya) has its meaning in the past, whereas this one necessarily has the future, like «أَنْ»; and that «يودُّ» takes an object and is not one of the verbs that are suspended (tuʿallaq); and that «أَن» has occurred after «يَوَدُّ» in His saying {أَيَوَدُّ أَحَدُكُمْ أَن تَكُونَ لَهُ جَنَّةٌ} [al-Baqara: 266], and this is frequent. The place for refuting him is other than this book. The third — to which al-Zamakhsharī inclined — is that its meaning is wishing (tamannī), so it needs no apodosis, because it is equivalent to «يا ليتني أُعَمَّر» ("would that I were given life"); the clause made up of «لو» and what is in its domain is in the position of accusative as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of «يَوَدُّ» by way of quotation (ḥikāya), treating it like [a verb of] saying. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: how is «لو يُعَمَّر» connected with «يَوَدُّ أحدُهم»? I say: it is a quotation of their wish, and «لو» has the meaning of wishing. Analogy would have required «لو أُعَمَّر» ('if only I were given life'), but it came in the wording of the third person because of His saying «يَوَدُّ أحدُهم», as in your saying: 'he swore by Allah that he would surely do (layafʿalanna).'" End quote. Its explanation has preceded, except for his saying "analogy would have required «لو أُعَمَّر»," by which he means that it ought to have come with the verb attributed to the speaker alone. He treated «يَوَدُّ» like [a verb of] saying only because «يَوَدُّ» is a verb of the heart, and saying arises from matters of the heart.
«ألفَ سَنَةٍ» is accusative as an adverb (ẓarf) by «يُعَمَّر», which is transitive to one object that has been put in place of the fāʿil [i.e. as nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent)]. There are two views about «سَنَة». The first: that its root form is «سَنَوة», because of their saying «سَنَوات», «سُنَيَّة» and «سانَيْتُ». The second: that it is from «سَنَهَة», because of their saying «سَنَهات», «سُنَيْهَة» and «سانَهْتُ». Both dialectal forms are established from the Arabs, as I have mentioned to you.
His saying: {وَمَا هُوَ بِمُزَحْزِحِهِ مِنَ العذاب}: there are five views regarding this pronoun. The first: that it refers back to «أحد», and then there are two views on it. The first: that it is the noun (ism) of the Ḥijāzī «ما», and «بمُزَحْزِحِه» is the khabar of «ما», so it is in the position of accusative, the bāʾ being redundant (zāʾida);
and «أَنْ يُعَمَّر» is the fāʿil of His saying «بمُزَحْزِحِه», the implied form being: "and none of them is one whom his being given life will remove." The second of the two views on «هو»: that it is a mubtadaʾ and «بمُزَحْزِحِهِ» its khabar, with «أَنْ يُعَمَّر» its fāʿil as preceded; this is on «ما» being Tamīmī. The first view is better, because the Quran was revealed in the dialect of the Ḥijāz and the accusative is overt in His saying {مَا هذا بَشَراً} [Yūsuf: 31] and {مَّا هُنَّ أُمَّهَاتِهِمْ} [al-Mujādila: 2].
The second of the views: that it refers back to the maṣdar understood from «يُعَمَّر», i.e. "and his being given life is not...", and His saying «أن يُعَمَّر» is a badal (substitute) from it; the nominative of «هو» is then on the two preceding views, I mean its being the ism of «ما» or a mubtadaʾ.
The third: that it is an allusion to the giving of life, not referring back to anything before it, and «أن يُعَمَّر» is a badal from it explaining it. The difference between this and the second view is that in that one, what explains it is something preceding, understood from the verb, whereas this one is explained by the badal after it. It has preceded that there is disagreement about that. This is what al-Zamakhsharī meant by his saying: "«هو» may be vague (mubham), with «أَنْ يُعَمَّر» clarifying it."
The fourth: that it is the pronoun of the matter and the story (ḍamīr al-amr wa-l-shaʾn); al-Fārisī inclined to this in «al-Ḥalabiyyāt», in agreement with the Kufans, for they explain the pronoun of the matter by other than a clause when a predication in meaning is formed from that, as in «ظَنَنْتُه قائماً الزيدانَ» and «ما هو بقائمٍ زيدٌ», because it is equivalent to «ظننتُه يقومُ الزيدان» and «ما هو يقومُ زيدٌ». The Basrans refuse to explain it except by a clause with both its parts stated explicitly, free of a preposition. The verification of the two views has preceded.
The fifth: that it is an ʿimād (support) — by which we mean the faṣl (separating pronoun) according to the Basrans; Ibn ʿAṭiyya transmitted it from al-Ṭabarī from a group. This needs clarification: some of the Kufans allow the ʿimād to be fronted together with the fronted khabar; they say for «زيدٌ هو القائمُ»: «هو القائمُ زيدٌ». Likewise here: the underlying form according to these is that «بمُزَحزِحِه» is a fronted khabar, «أَنْ يُعَمَّر» a delayed mubtadaʾ, and «هو» an ʿimād, the implied form being: "and his being given life is not what will remove him"; when the khabar was fronted, the ʿimād was fronted with it. The Basrans allow none of that.
«من العذابِ» is attached to His saying «بمُزَحْزِحِه», and «مِنْ» is for the beginning of the extent.
«الزَّحْزَحَة» is moving aside; you say: «زَحْزَحْتُه فَزَحْزَحَ» ("I moved him aside and he moved aside"), so it is intransitive and transitive. Of its occurrence as transitive is his saying:
621 - يا قباضَ الروحِ مِنْ نَفْسٍ إذا احْتَضَرَتْ ... وغافرَ الذنبِ زَحْزِحْني عَنِ النارِ
(O Taker of the spirit from a soul when it is at the point of death, and Forgiver of sin, move me away from the Fire.)
And Dhū al-Rumma recited it as:
622 - يا قابضَ الروح مِنْ جِسْم عَصَى زَمَنَاً ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(O Taker of the spirit from a body that disobeyed for a time...)
And of its occurrence as intransitive is the saying of the other:
623 - خليلَيَّ ما بالُ الدُّجى لا يُزَحْزَحُ ... وما بالُ ضوءِ الصبحِ لا يَتَوَضَّحُ
(My two friends, what is it with the darkness that it does not move away, and what is it with the light of dawn that it does not become clear?)
His saying: «أَنْ يُعَمَّر» is either a fāʿil, or a badal from «هو», or a mubtadaʾ, according to the preceding parsing of «هو».
{والله بَصِيرٌ بِمَا يَعْمَلُونَ} is a mubtadaʾ and its khabar, and «بما» is attached to «بصير». «ما» may be a relative noun (ismiyya) or an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective, and on both views the returning pronoun is omitted, i.e. «يَعْمَلُونه» ("[what] they do"); it may also be maṣdariyya, i.e. "their doing." The majority [read] «يعملون» with yāʾ, in sequence with what preceded, and al-Ḥasan and others «تَعْمَلُون» with tāʾ, in the second person, by iltifāt (a shift of person). He used the imperfect form, even though His knowledge encompasses their past deeds, in observance of the verse-endings and the closing of the fawāṣil.

semin-durr:64-64.t:
The saying of the Exalted: {فَلَوْلاَ فَضْلُ الله}: this «لولا» is a particle of non-occurrence because of the existence [of something else] (ḥarf imtināʿ li-wujūd). The apparent [view] is that it is simple. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is compounded of «لَوْ» and «لا». Before compounding, «لو» is that by which a thing does not occur because of the non-occurrence of another, and «لا» is for negation. Non-occurrence is negation in meaning, and the negation by «لا» has entered upon one of the two non-occurrences of «لو»; negation entering upon negation becomes affirmation. Hence the meaning of this «لولا» became: that by which a thing does not occur because of the existence of another." This is an affectation that has no benefit. «لولا» may also be a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ), and then it is restricted to verbs; its discussion will come, if Allah the Exalted wills. This «لولا» is restricted to the mubtadaʾ (subject), and verbs may not follow it; if something occurs whose apparent form is that, it is interpreted, as in his saying:
520 - ولولا يَحْسِبون الحِلْم عَجْزاً ... لَمَا عَدِم المُسيئون احتمالي
(Were it not that they reckon forbearance as weakness, the wrongdoers would not have lacked my tolerance.)
Its interpretation is that the original is ولولا أن يَحْسِبِوا; when «أن» was omitted the verb became nominative (indicative), as in his saying:
521 - ألا أيُّهذا الزاجري أحضرُ الوغى ... . . . . . . . . . . .
(O you who chide me for being present at the battle…)
i.e. أَنْ أَحضرَ. What is nominative after it is a mubtadaʾ — contrary to al-Kisāʾī, who made it nominative by an implied verb, and to al-Farrāʾ, who said: "It is made nominative by لولا itself." Its khabar (predicate) must be omitted, because it is indicated and because something stands in its place, namely its apodosis; the implied form is: "were it not that the bounty of Allah is existent (kāʾin) or present (ḥāṣil)". It may not be stated except under poetic necessity, and for that reason al-Maʿarrī was charged with a solecism in his saying:
522 - يُذيبُ الرُّعْبُ منه كلَّ عَضْبٍ ... فلولا الغِمْدُ يُمْسِكُه لَسالا
(Terror of him melts every sharp sword; were it not that the scabbard holds it, it would flow.)
since he stated its khabar after it. So they stated it without qualification. Some made a distinction, saying: "If the khabar of what follows it is general existence (kawn muṭlaq), omission is obligatory; on this the Revelation and most speech have come. If it is restricted existence (kawn muqayyad), it must be one of two cases: either there is evidence indicating it or not. If there is no evidence indicating it, it must be mentioned, as in his saying, peace be upon him: «لولا قومُكِ حديثو عهدٍ بكفر» ('were it not that your people are recently out of unbelief'), and the saying of another:
523 - فلولا بَنُوها حولَها لَخَبَطْتُها ... . . . . . . . . . . .
(Were it not for her sons around her, I would have struck her…)
If there is evidence indicating it, both mentioning and omitting are permissible, as in لولا زيدٌ لغُلِبْنا ('were it not for Zayd, we would have been overcome'), i.e. [were he not] brave." On this [basis] is the verse of al-Maʿarrī cited above. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "Omission of the khabar became binding because it is known and because of the length of the speech. If «أَنْ» occurs after it, the khabar appears, as in His saying: «فلولا أنَّه كان من المُسَبِّحين»; the khabar in the wording belongs to «أنَّ»." What he said is misleading: the khabar of «أنَّ» has no connection with the omitted khabar and does not replace it at all, so it is exactly like other [cases], the implied form being: "were it not that his being one who glorifies is present or existent". So what benefit is there in his mentioning this? The khabar must be omitted in other cases too, which would lengthen the book to mention and detail; they will come, if Allah wills, detailed in their places. The meaning of al-faḍl has preceded at His saying {فَضَّلْتُكُمْ عَلَى العالمين} [al-Baqara: 47].
His saying: {لَكُنْتُم مِّنَ الخاسرين}: the lām is [in] the apodosis of «لولا». Know that if its apodosis is affirmative, the lām usually enters, as in this verse and its counterparts, and its omission is infrequent. [The poet] said:
524 - لَوْلا الحياءُ وباقي الدينِ عِبْتُكُما ... ببعضِ ما فيكما إذْ عِبْتُما عَوَري
(Were it not for modesty and what remains of religion, I would have reproached you both with some of what is in you, since you reproached me for my one-eyedness.)
If it is negative, it must be one of two cases: either the particle of negation is «ما» or something else. If it is something else, omitting the lām is obligatory, as in لولا زيدٌ لم أقم or لن أقوم, so that two lāms do not come in succession. If it is with «ما», omission is usual and bringing it is infrequent. Such also is the rule for the apodosis of «لو» of non-occurrence; this has preceded at His saying: {وَلَوْ شَآءَ الله لَذَهَبَ بِسَمْعِهِمْ} [al-Baqara: 20]. Its apodosis has no grammatical position. {مِّنَ الخاسرين} is in the position of the accusative as the khabar of «كان», and «مِنْ» is partitive.

semin-durr:65-65.t:
The saying of the Exalted: {وَلَقَدْ عَلِمْتُمُ}: the lām is [the lām of] the answer to an omitted oath, its implied form being: "By Allah, indeed…" (والله لقد); and so is everything of its kind that occurs. «قد» is a particle of verification and expectation; with the imperfect it conveys infrequency, except with the acts of Allah the Exalted, for it is then for verification. It may also turn the imperfect to the past, as in his saying:
525 - قد أَتْرُكُ القِرْنَ مُصْفَّراً أناملُه ... كأنَّ أثوابَه مُجَّتْ بفُرصادِ
(I have often left the rival with yellowed fingertips, as though his clothes had been sprayed with mulberry juice.)
It is a particle restricted to the verb, and enters upon the past and the imperfect; with the past it brings it near to the present. In the wording of one of them: "«قد» is a particle that accompanies verbs, brings the past near to the present, and introduces infrequency in the future." It may also be a noun in the sense of حَسْب ("enough"), as in قدني درهمٌ, i.e. "a dirham is enough for me"; the nūn of protection (nūn al-wiqāya) is usually attached to it with the yāʾ of the first person, and the poet combined both forms, saying:
526 - قَدْنيَ مِنْ نَصْرِ الخُبَيْبَيْنِ قَدي ... . . . . . . . . . . .
(Enough for me of supporting the two Khubaybs, enough for me…)
When it is a particle, the verb after it may be omitted, as in his saying:
527 - أَفِدَ الترحُّلُ غيرَ أنَّ رِكابَنا ... لمَّا تَزُلْ برِحالِنا وكَأنَّ قَدِ
(The departure has drawn near, except that our camels have not yet moved off with our saddles — and yet it is as though they already have.)
i.e. قد زالت. The oath and its answer have rules that will come in detail, if Allah the Exalted wills. «عَلِمْتُمِ» is in the sense of عَرَفْتُم ("you knew/recognized"), so it is transitive to one object only. The difference between ʿilm and maʿrifa is that ʿilm requires knowledge of the entity and of the states it is in, as in عَلمتُ زيداً قائماً أو ضاحكاً ("I knew Zayd to be standing or laughing"), while maʿrifa requires knowledge of the entity. It has also been said: because maʿrifa is preceded by ignorance, while ʿilm may not be preceded by ignorance; for that reason it is not permissible to apply maʿrifa to Him, glory be to Him. {الذين اعتدوا}: the relative and its ṣila (relative clause) are in the position of the accusative as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). There is no need to omit a muḍāf, as some supposed, i.e. "the rulings of those who transgressed", because the meaning is: you knew their persons and their individuals. The original of اعتَدَوْا is iʿtadayū; it underwent weak-letter change by deletion, and its pattern is iftaʿaw. Its morphology and meaning are already known.
His saying: «منكم» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «اعتدَوا». It may also be from «الذين», i.e. "the transgressors, being from among you". «مِنْ» is partitive.
His saying: {فِي السبت} is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «اعتدَوا», and the meaning is: "regarding the ruling of the Sabbath". Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "They have said: اليومَ السبتُ ('today is the Sabbath'), making «اليومَ» the khabar of «السبت», as one says اليومَ القتالُ ('the fighting is today'). So according to what we have mentioned, there is an omission in the speech, its implied form being: on the day of the Sabbath." Al-sabt is originally the maṣdar (verbal noun) of سَبَتَ, i.e. "he cut off work". Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "Al-sabt is either taken from al-subūt, which is rest and ease, or from al-sabt, which is cutting, because on it things were cut off and their creation was completed; from it is their saying سَبَتَ رأسَه, i.e. he shaved it." Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Al-sabt is the maṣdar of سَبَتَتِ اليهودُ, when the Jews revered the Sabbath day." This is open to question, for this word existed, and its derivation is mentioned in the language of the Arabs, before the Jews did that — unless he means this particular Sabbath mentioned in this verse. Its origin is the maṣdar, as I mentioned; then this day of the week was named by it because it happened to occur on it, since, as preceded, the creation of things was completed and cut off. One may also say "the day of the Sabbath", so that it is a maṣdar. When "day" is mentioned with it, or with similar names of times that contain an action or event, "day" may be accusative or nominative, as in اليوم الجمعةُ and اليوم العيدُ, just as one says اليوم الاجتماعُ والعَودُ ("today is the gathering and the return"). If it is mentioned with «الأحد» ("Sunday") and its sisters, the nominative is obligatory according to the well-known view; its verification is mentioned in the books of grammar.
His saying: {قِرَدَةً خَاسِئِينَ}: four options are possible in it. The first: that they are two khabars. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "I.e. be combining apehood and abasement." He supposed this on the basis that the khabar is not multiple, so he made the two have the sense of a single khabar, of the category of هذا حُلْوٌ حامِضٌ ("this is sweet-sour"); the discussion of this has preceded. The second: that «خاسئين» is a naʿt (adjective) of «قِردة»; Abū al-Baqāʾ said this. This is open to question in that apes are not rational, while this is a plural of rational beings. If it is said: those addressed are rational — the answer is that this does not help, because the implied meaning in your view would then be: "be like apes whose quality is abasement", and those addressed have no connection with that. However, it may be said that they are likened to rational beings, as in His saying: {لِي سَاجِدِينَ} [Yūsuf: 4], {أَتَيْنَا طَآئِعِينَ} [Fuṣṣilat: 11]. The third: that it is a ḥāl from the noun of «كونوا», the governing word being «كونوا»; this is according to those who allow «كان» to govern adverbs and ḥāls. There is disagreement about it, whose verification will come at the saying of the Exalted: {أَكَانَ لِلنَّاسِ عَجَباً} [Yūnus: 2], if Allah the Exalted wills. The fourth, and it is the best: that it is a ḥāl from the latent pronoun in «قِرَدَةً», because it has the sense of a derived [adjective], i.e. "be transformed in this state". The plural of fiʿl on the pattern fiʿala is rare and not by analogy.
The root q-r-d indicates sticking and stillness: you say «قَرَد بمكان كذا», i.e. he stuck to it and stayed still; from it is «الصوفُ القَرَد», i.e. matted wool; and from it also is «القُراد», this well-known creature (the tick). One says خَسَأْتُه فَخَسَأَ ("I drove him off and he was driven off"), the transitive and intransitive being the same, as in زاد and غاض. It has also been said: one says خَسَأْتُه فَخَسِىءَ وانْخَسَأَ. The maṣdar is al-khusūʾ and al-khasʾ. Al-Kisāʾī said: "خَسَأْتُ الرجلَ خَسْئاً, and he خَسَأَ خُسُوءاً", so he distinguished between the two maṣdars. Al-khusūʾ is abasement, humiliation, being driven away and distance; from it is خَسَأْتُ الكلبَ ("I drove the dog away").

semin-durr:188-188.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {بَيْنَكُمْ}: regarding this adverb there are two views. The first: it is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «تأكلوا», in the sense of: "do not pass it among yourselves by consuming." The second: it is attached to an omitted element, because it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «أموالكم», i.e. "do not consume it while it is among you." Abū al-Baqāʾ also gave its implied form as "being among you" or "circulating among you," and in meaning it is like His words {إِلاَّ أَن تَكُونَ تِجَارَةً حَاضِرَةً تُدِيرُونَهَا بَيْنَكُمْ} [al-Baqara: 282]. In implying "circulating" — which is a restricted (specific) form of being — there is an evident objection, unless it be said that the context indicates it.

His words {بالباطل}: there are two views. The first: it is attached to the verb, i.e. "do not take it by a false means." The second: it is a ḥāl, and so attached to an omitted element; but as to the one it describes there are two possibilities. One: it is the wealth, as if the meaning were "do not consume it while it is bound up with falsehood." The other: it is the pronoun in «تأكلوا», as if the meaning were "do not consume it while acting falsely," i.e. being involved in falsehood.

His words {وَتُدْلُواْ بها}: regarding «تَدْلُوا» there are three views. The first: it is jussive (majzūm), conjoined to what precedes it; this is supported by the reading of Ubayy: «ولا تُدْلُوا», repeating the prohibitive lā. The second: it is accusative by "divergence" (al-ṣarf); the meaning of this has already been given, that it is the school of the Kufans and that it has not been established by proof. The third: it is accusative by an implied «أنْ» in the reply to the prohibition; this is the school of al-Akhfash, and Ibn ʿAṭiyya, al-Zamakhsharī, Makkī and Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed it. The Shaykh said: "As for al-Akhfash's parsing and al-Zamakhsharī's allowing it here, that is the question of 'لا تأكل السمك وتشربَ اللبن' (do not eat fish and [at the same time] drink milk)." [The Shaykh continued:] "The grammarians said: when it is made accusative [the prohibition is of combining the two]" — [and it is rejected here] for two reasons. [Translator's note: the source text appears abridged at this point; the bracketed words are added to make the sense continuous.] The first: forbidding the combination does not entail forbidding each of them separately, whereas forbidding each of them entails forbidding combining them, since combining them is the occurrence of each of them, and each of them is necessarily forbidden; do you not see that consuming wealth by falsehood is unlawful whether it is alone or combined with other unlawful things? The second — and it is stronger —: His words «لِتأكلوا» are the reason for what precedes them; had the prohibition been of the combination, the reason would not be valid for it, because it is composed of two things, and the reason cannot properly follow upon the existence of both; rather it follows only upon the existence of one of them, namely the conveying of wealth to the rulers."

«بها» is attached to «تُدْلُوا». Regarding the bāʾ there are two views. The first: it is for transitivity, i.e. "so that you send it to the rulers." The second: it is causal, in the sense that what is meant by الإدلاء is hastening with litigation over wealth, either because there is no evidence for it, or because it is a trust, such as the wealth of orphans. The apparent sense is that the pronoun in «بها» is for the wealth; it has also been said that it is for false testimony, since the context indicates it; but this is nothing.

«من أموال» is in the position of accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of «فريقاً», i.e. "a portion that is from the wealth of people."

His words: {بالإثم}: this bāʾ may be causal, and so attached to His words «لتأكلوا»; or it may be for accompaniment, and so be a ḥāl of the agent in «لتأكلوا», attached to an omitted element, i.e. "that you may consume while bound up with sin." «وأنتم تعلمون» is a clause in the position of accusative as a ḥāl of the agent of «لتأكلوا»; this is according to the opinion of those who allow multiple ḥāls; as for those who do not allow it, they make «بالإثم» not a ḥāl.

semin-durr:189-189.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {عَنِ الأهلة}: attached to (mutaʿalliq) the asking before it; one says «سألَ به» and «سأل عنه» with one meaning. The pronoun in «يَسْأَلُونك» is a plural pronoun, while in the story the askers were two; this admits two explanations. The first: that is because two are a plural. The second: it is attributing a thing to a group even though it issued only from one or two of them, and this is frequent in their speech.

The majority pronounce the nūn of «عَنْ» distinctly before the lām of «الأهلَّة», and Warsh follows his rule of transferring the vowel of the hamza to the vowelless letter before it. It has been read irregularly (shādhdh): «علَّ هِلَّة». Its explanation is that he transferred the vowel of the hamza of «أهلة» to the lām of the definite article, and assimilated the nūn of «عن» into the lām of the definite article, since the connective hamza drops in continuous reading. In this there is treating the transferred vowel of the hamza as counting, and it is the dialect of those who say «لَحْمَر» without a connective hamza.

الهلال (the crescent) was put in the plural, even though it is singular, in consideration of the difference of its times; they said: in that its being a crescent in one month is other than its being a crescent in another. الهلال is this well-known heavenly body. The lexicographers disagreed about until when it is called هلال. The majority said: it is called هلال for two nights, and it has been said: for three; then it is قمر (moon). Abū al-Haytham said: "It is called هلال for two nights at the beginning of the month and two nights at its end, and what is between them is قمر." Al-Aṣmaʿī said: "It is called هلال until it يُحَجِّر, and its تحجير is that it becomes circular, like a fine thread." It is called بَدْر from the twelfth to the fourteenth. It has also been said: "It is called هلال until its light overcomes the darkness of the night, and that happens only in seven nights." الهلال may be a name for this heavenly body, and it may be a maṣdar (verbal noun): one says هَلَّ الشهرُ هلالاً (the month began).

One says أُهِلَّ الهلالُ and اسْتُهِلَّ, as passive, and أَهْلَلْنَاه and اسْتَهْلَلْنَاهُ. It has also been said: one says أَهَلَّ and اسْتَهَلَّ as active, and he recited:
865 - وشهرٌ مُسْتَهِلٌّ بعدَ شهرٍ ... وحَوْلٌ بعدَهُ حولٌ جَدِيدُ
(A month appearing after a month, and a year followed by a new year.)
This heavenly body was called هلال because of the raising of voices on seeing it; and it has been said: because it is from clarity and appearance, i.e. because it appears at the time it is seen after being hidden; therefore one says تَهَلَّلَ وَجْهُهُ (his face lit up): joy and happiness appeared in it, even if he did not raise his voice... And of this is the saying of Taʾabbaṭa Sharran:
866 - وإذا نَظَرْتَ إلى أَسِرَّةِ وَجْهِه ... بَرَقَتْ كبَرْقِ العارضِ المُتَهَلِّلِ
(When you look at the lines of his face, they flash like the lightning of a raincloud bursting forth.)
It has already been said that الإهلال is crying out, at His words {وَمَآ أُهِلَّ لِغَيْرِ الله بِهِ} [al-Baqara: 173]. The doubled fiʿāl pattern regularly forms its broken plural on afʿila, as أَهِلَّة, and fiʿal occurs in it irregularly, as in their saying عِنَن and حِجَج for عِنَان and حِجاج.

Some implied a muḍāf before «الأهِلَّة», i.e. "about the ruling of the variation of the crescents," because asking about their essence is not useful; that is why they were answered with His words: «قل هي مواقيتُ». It has also been said: when they asked about something of little use, they were answered with something useful, and their question was turned aside since there was no benefit in it; on this view there is no need to imply a muḍāf.

«للناسِ» is attached to an omitted element, because it is a naʿt (adjective) of «مواقيت», i.e. "appointed times that are for people." المواقيت is the plural of ميقات; the wāw returned to its origin, since the origin is مِوْقات, from الوقت; it was changed to yāʾ only because of the kasra before it, and when the cause disappeared in the plural it was restored to wāw. It is a diptote because it has the pattern of the ultimate plural. الميقات is the end of a time.

His words: {والحج}: conjoined to «الناس». They said: its implied form is "and appointed times of the Hajj," the second being omitted, the first sufficing. Since the Hajj is among the greatest things whose times are sought and its months are best known by the crescents, it was singled out for mention; it is as though it were a specification after a generalization, since His words «مواقيتُ للناسِ» do not mean for the persons of people themselves; rather a muḍāf is necessary, i.e. "appointed times for the purposes of people that require timing." So in reality it is not conjoined to «الناس», but to the omitted muḍāf whose place «الناس» took in the parsing.

The majority read «الحج» with fatḥa throughout the Quran, except that Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī and Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim read {حِجُّ البيت} [Āl ʿImrān: 97] with kasra; al-Ḥasan and Ibn Abī Isḥāq read it with kasra throughout the Quran. Do they have one meaning or are they different? Sībawayh said: "They are two maṣdars": the one with fatḥa is like الردّ and الشدّ, and the one with kasra is like الذِّكر. It has also been said: with fatḥa it is a maṣdar, and with kasra it is a noun.

His words: {وَلَيْسَ البر بِأَن تَأْتُواْ} are like His words {لَّيْسَ البر أَن تُوَلُّواْ} [al-Baqara: 177], which has already been discussed; except that here there was no disagreement about the nominative of «البر», because the redundant bāʾ in the second [element] determined that it is the khabar (predicate). We have already said that it may be added in the noun [of laysa], and there is no need to repeat what has been said.

Abū ʿAmr, Ḥafṣ and Warsh read «البُيوت» and «بُيوت» with ḍamma on the bāʾ, and this is the original; the rest read with kasra on account of the yāʾ; and likewise in its diminutive. No concern is paid to passing from a kasra to a ḍamma, because the ḍamma is on the yāʾ, and the yāʾ is equivalent to two kasras, so the kasra on the bāʾ is as if it were next to a kasra; Abū al-Baqāʾ said this.

«مِنْ» in His words «مِنْ ظهورِها» and «من أبوابها» is attached to "coming," and its meaning is the beginning of the extent. The pronoun in «ظهورها» and «أبوابِها» is for the houses; it came like the singular feminine pronoun, because that is permissible in it.

His words: {ولكن البر مَنِ اتقى} are exactly like His words {ولكن البر مَنْ آمَنَ} [al-Baqara: 177]. Since two declarative clauses preceded, namely «وليس البرُّ» and {ولكن البر مَنِ اتقى}, two imperative clauses were conjoined to them, the first for the first and the second for the second, namely «وَأْتُوا البيوت» and «واتَّقوا الله». The explicit mention of the object in His words «واتقوا الله» indicates that it is omitted from «اتقى», i.e. "fears Allah."

semin-durr:142-142.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {مِنَ الناس}: It is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «السفهاء», the governing word in it being «سيقولُ». It is a clarifying ḥāl (ḥāl mubayyina), for foolishness, just as people are described by it, so others are described by it, such as inanimate things and animals; and just as speech is attributed to them literally, so it is attributed to others figuratively; so He removed the figurative [possibility] by His saying «مِن الناسِ». Ibn ʿAṭiyya and others mentioned it.

His saying: {مَا وَلاَّهُمْ}: «ما» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and it is interrogative; the clause after it is its khabar (predicate). «عن قِبْلَتِهم» is attached to «وَلاَّهم». A muḍāf (annexed noun) must be omitted in His saying «عليها», i.e.: upon facing it or upon believing in it. The interrogative clause is in the position of accusative by the verb of saying. The sense of being "upon" (al-istiʿlāʾ) in His saying «عليها» is figurative: He treated their persistence in keeping to it as [the state of] one who is mounted upon a thing.

semin-durr:190-190.t: The words of Allah the Exalted: {فِي سَبِيلِ الله}: attached to (mutaʿalliq) «قاتِلوا», in one of two senses. Either you imply a muḍāf, i.e. "in support of the way of Allah," the way meaning the religion of Allah — because السبيل originally means the road, and it was used figuratively for the religion since it is a road to Allah. Or you make «قاتلوا» include the meaning of "strive hard in fighting in support of the religion of Allah." «والذين يقاتلونكم» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of «قاتلوا».

semin-durr:143-143.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {وَكَذَلِكَ}: The kāf has in it the two well-known aspects, as has preceded more than once, namely: accusative either as a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), or as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the omitted maṣdar; the implied form is: We made you a middle community with a making like that. However, what is pointed to by «ذلك» is not mentioned in what preceded; only what indicates it has preceded. They differed about «ذلك» on five aspects. The first: that what is pointed to is the guidance «[Translator's note: the source prints «الهدف» ("the target"); the sense requires «الهُدى» ("the guidance").]» indicated by His saying {يَهْدِي مَن يَشَآءُ}, the implied form being: We made you a middle community just as We guided you. The second: that it is the making, the implied form being: We made you a middle community like that wondrous making in which there is your being singled out for guidance. The third: it was said the meaning is: just as We made your qibla middle, We made you a middle community. The fourth: it was said the meaning is: just as We made the qibla the middle of the earth, We made you a middle community. The fifth — and it is the most far-fetched of them —: that what is pointed to is His saying {وَلَقَدِ اصطفيناه فِي الدنيا}, i.e.: like that choosing We made you a middle community. And «جَعَل» is in the sense of «صَيَّر» (to make into), so it is transitive to two objects: the pronoun is the first object, «أمةً» is the second object, and «وسطاً» its naʿt. And al-wasaṭ, with the middle letter vowelled, is a noun for what is between the two ends; and it is applied to the best of a thing, because the middle parts are protected by the ends. Ḥabīb said:
752 - كانَتْ هي الوسَطَ المَحْمِيَّ فاكتَنَفَتْ ... بها الحوادثُ حتى أَصْبَحَتْ طَرَفا
(It was the protected middle, but calamities surrounded it until it became an edge.)
And the wasaṭ of a valley is the best place in it. Zuhayr said:
753 - هُمُ وسَطٌ تَرْضى الأنامُ بحُكْمِهِمْ ... إذا نَزَلَتْ إحدى الليالي بمُعْظَمِ
(They are a just middle whose judgement people accept when one of the nights brings a grave calamity.)
And his saying:
754 - وكُنْ من الناسِ جميعاً وسَطَا
(And be, among all people, in the middle.)
Some distinguished between wasaṭ with fatḥa and wasṭ with sukūn, saying: every place where the word «بَيْنَ» ("between") fits is said with sukūn, otherwise with the vowel. So you say: "I sat wasṭa the people", with sukūn. Al-Rāghib said: "The wasaṭ of a thing is that which has two ends equal in measure, and this is said of continuous quantity, like a single body, so you say: its wasaṭ is hard; and wasṭ with sukūn is said of discrete quantity, like something that separates between two bodies, as in 'wasṭ al-qawm' (amid the people) is such-and-such." The precise statement about it is that the one with fatḥa is originally a maṣdar, and for that reason the singular and others, the feminine and the masculine, are equal in being described by it; and the one with sukūn is an adverb (ẓarf), and the predominant [rule] in it is that it is not inflected out of its adverbial use; it has come fully declinable in the saying of al-Farazdaq:
755 - أتَتْه بمَجْلومٍ كأنَّ جبينَه ... صلاءَةُ وَرْسٍ وَسْطُها قد تَفَلَّقَا
(She brought him one shorn, as though his forehead were a grinding-stone for saffron whose middle had cracked.)
It is narrated with ḍamma on the ṭāʾ, the pronoun being for «صلاءة», and with fatḥa, the pronoun being for the woman who came.

His saying: «لتكونوا»: Two aspects are permissible in this lām. The first: that it is the lām of «كي», so it gives the cause. The second: that it is the lām of outcome (lām al-ṣayrūra). On both assumptions it is a preposition, after which there is an implied «أَنْ», and it [«أن»] together with what follows is in the position of genitive. He brought «شهداء», the plural of shahīd, which indicates intensiveness, rather than shāhidīn and shuhūd, the two plurals of shāhid.

In «على» there are two views. The first: that it is in its proper sense, and this is the apparent one. The second: that it is in the sense of the lām, meaning: you convey to them what you have learned of revelation and religion, as the Messenger, peace be upon him, conveyed it. The two views are likewise in the last «على», meaning that the testimony is in the sense of his, peace be upon him, vouching for them (tazkiya).

What the testimony is connected to was put first in the last case and put first in the first case «[Translator's note: so in the source («قُدِّم … آخِراً وقُدِّم أولاً»); the intended contrast is evidently that it was put first at the end («عليكم شهيداً») and put last at the beginning («شهداء على الناس»), i.e. «أُخِّر أولاً».]», for two reasons. The first — and it is what al-Zamakhsharī mentioned —: that the aim in the first is to establish their testimony against the nations, and in the last, their being singled out by the Messenger's being a witness over them. The second: that «شهيداً» is more similar to the verse-endings (fawāṣil) and cadences than «عليكم», so His saying «شهيداً» was the completion and cadence of the sentence rather than «عليكم». The Shaykh stated this aspect, choosing it and rejecting al-Zamakhsharī's doctrine that putting the object first conveys restriction (ikhtiṣāṣ); that has preceded.

His saying: {التي كُنتَ عَلَيْهَآ}: In this verse there are five aspects. The first: that «القِبلْة» is the first object and {التي كُنتَ عَلَيْهَآ} is the second object, since «الجَعْل» is in the sense of "making into"; and this is what al-Zamakhsharī asserted, for he said: "{التي كُنتَ عَلَيْهَآ} is not a naʿt of «القبلة»; it is only the second of the two objects of «جَعَلَ»; He means: and We did not make the qibla the direction that you were upon, namely the Kaʿba; because he ﷺ used to pray in Mecca towards the Kaʿba, then he was commanded to pray towards the Rock of Jerusalem (Bayt al-Maqdis), then he was turned to the Kaʿba."
The second: that «القِبلةَ» is the second object, only put first, and {التي كُنتَ عَلَيْهَآ} is the first; this is what the Shaykh chose, arguing for it that "making into" is moving from one state to another, so what is clothed in the first state [is the first object, and what is clothed] in the second state is the second object. Do you not see that you say: "I made the clay into pottery" and "I made the ignorant one learned"? The meaning here on this assumption is: and We did not make the Kaʿba, which was a qibla for you first and then you were turned from it to Jerusalem, your qibla now, except that We might know. And he attributed al-Zamakhsharī's making «القبلةَ» the first object to delusion. There is a reservation about this.
The third: that «القبلة» is the first object, «التي كنتَ» its naʿt, and the second object omitted, its implied form being: and We did not make the qibla that you were upon abrogated. When Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned this aspect he construed it as: and We did not make the qibla that you were upon a qibla — and there is no benefit in it.
The fourth: that «القبلةَ» is the first object and «إلا لِنَعْلَمَ» is the second object, and that is on the omission of a muḍāf (annexed noun), its implied form being: and We did not make the turning away of the qibla that you were upon except that We might know; like your saying: "Zayd's beating is for discipline", i.e.: is, or is established, for discipline.
The fifth: that «القبلةَ» is the first object, the second omitted, and {التي كُنتَ عَلَيْهَآ} a naʿt of that omitted element, the implied form being: and We did not make the qibla the qibla which…; Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned it, and it is weak. In His saying «كنت» there are two aspects. The first: that it is redundant (zāʾida); it is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās [that it means]: you are upon it; but this from him is an explanation of meaning, not of iʿrāb. «[Translator's note: the source announces two aspects for «كنت» but states only the first.]»

Al-qibla originally is a noun for the state in which the one facing is, like al-jilsa (manner of sitting); in convention it became a noun for the place faced, towards which one turns for prayer.
Quṭrub said: "They say: 'He has no qibla', i.e.: a direction to which he turns." Another said: when two men face each other, each one is a qibla for the other.

His saying: {إِلاَّ لِنَعْلَمَ}: It has preceded that on one of the aspects it is the second object; on the others it is an emptied exception (istithnāʾ mufarragh) from the general mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e.: the cause of turning the qibla was not for anything at all except for such-and-such. His saying «لنعلم» is not on its apparent sense, for His knowledge is eternal, not originated; so it must be interpreted, and there are aspects in it. The first: so as to distinguish the follower from the one who turns back — applying the cause while meaning the effect. It has been said: it is on the omission of a muḍāf, i.e.: so that Our Messenger may know, and it was omitted; or by it He meant the connection of [His] knowledge with their obedience and their disobedience in the matter of the qibla.

His saying: {مَن يَتَّبِعُ}: In «مَنْ» there are two aspects. The first: that it is a relative noun, «يتَّبع» its ṣila (relative clause), and the relative noun with its ṣila is in the position of the object of «نعلم», because it is transitive to one object. The second: that it is interrogative, in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), «يتَّبعُ» being its khabar (predicate), and the clause is in the position of accusative because it suspends (muʿalliqa) the [verb of] knowing, knowing being in its proper sense; al-Zamakhsharī inclined to this in one of his two views. Abū al-Baqāʾ rejected this aspect, saying: "Because it requires that «نعلم» be suspended from governing, and when it is suspended from it, «مِنْ» [in «مِمَّن ينقلب»] would have nothing left to which it could be attached, because what follows the interrogative is not attached to what precedes it; nor is its attachment to «يتَّبعُ» sound, because in meaning it is attached to «نَعْلَمَ», and the meaning is not: which party follows, of those who turn back?" End quote. This is a clear refutation, since the meaning is not that; the meaning is only that «مِمَّنْ ينقلِبُ» be attached to «نعلمَ», as in: "I knew who did you good from who did you harm".
