al-muhājara (emigration) is a mufāʿala form from al-hajr, and it is moving from one land to another; the root meaning of al-hajr is abandoning. al-mujāhada (striving) is a mufāʿala form from al-juhd, which is drawing out one's capacity and expending one's utmost effort; al-ijhād is expending one's utmost effort in seeking what is aimed at. al-rajāʾ (hope) is longing (al-ṭamaʿ). al-Rāghib said: it is a supposition that entails the attainment of something in which there is joy; and it is sometimes used for fear. He recited:

940 - إذا لَسَعَتْه النحلُ لَم يَرْجُ لَسْعَها ... وخالَفَها في بَيْتِ نُوبٍ عَواسلِ
(When the bees stung him he did not "yarju" their sting, but went against them into the home of honey-making bees.)

that is, he did not fear. And Allah the Exalted said: {لاَ يَرْجُونَ لِقَآءَنَا} [Yūnus: 7], that is, they do not fear. Is its use in this sense literal (ḥaqīqa) or figurative (majāz)? Some claimed that it is literal, and it would then be a case of homonymy (ishtirāk lafẓī); others claimed that it is one of the words with opposite meanings (al-aḍdād), which is also homonymy. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "This is not good," meaning that hope and fear are not opposites, since they can occur together. That is why al-Rāghib said, after reciting the verse above: "The explanation of [that] is that hope and fear entail one another," and Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "Hope is always accompanied by fear, just as fear is accompanied by hope." Others claimed it is figurative, because of the mutual entailment we reported from al-Rāghib and Ibn ʿAṭiyya.

al-Jāḥiẓ answered regarding the verse that its meaning is: he did not hope for healing from their sting and its removal, so rajāʾ keeps its usual meaning. As for His words {لاَ يَرْجُونَ لِقَآءَنَا}, that is, they do not hope for the reward of meeting Us, so rajāʾ also keeps its usual meaning; Ibn ʿAṭiyya said this. al-Aṣmaʿī said: "When rajāʾ is joined to a particle of negation it means fear, as in this verse and the āya." This is open to question, since negation does not change what words signify.

«رحمة» is written here with a (long) tāʾ: either following the dialect of those who pause on the feminine tāʾ with a tāʾ, or in consideration of its form in connected speech. In the Qurʾān it occurs in seven places, all written with tāʾ: here; in al-Aʿrāf: {إِنَّ رَحْمَةَ الله} [al-Aʿrāf: 56]; in Hūd: {رَحْمَةُ الله وَبَرَكَاتُهُ} [Hūd: 73]; in Maryam: {ذِكْرُ رَحْمَةِ رَبِّكَ} [Maryam: 2]; in al-Rūm: {فانظر إلى آثَارِ رَحْمَتِ الله} [al-Rūm: 50]; and in al-Zukhruf: {أَهُمْ يَقْسِمُونَ رَحْمَتَ رَبِّكَ. . . وَرَحْمَتُ رَبِّكَ خَيْرٌ} [al-Zukhruf: 32].

semin-durr:83-83.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {وَإِذْ أَخَذْنَا}: «إذ» is conjoined to the adverbs before it; what has been said about it — whether it is fully inflectable or not — has been given. «أَخَذْنا» is in the position of the genitive, i.e. "and remember the time of Our taking their covenant", or something like that.

His words: {لاَ تَعْبُدُونَ}: it has been read with yāʾ and with tāʾ, and this is clear. Whoever read it in the third person [did so] because the ruling of overt nouns is the third person; whoever read it in the second person — that is iltifāt (a shift of person), and its wisdom is that it is more conducive to the addressee's acceptance of the command and prohibition directed at him. Abū al-Baqāʾ took the second-person reading as implying the verb "say". He said: "It is read with tāʾ on the construal: 'We said to them: you shall not worship except Allah'." Taking it as iltifāt is better.

As for the i'rab of this negated clause, there are eight aspects. The most apparent: that it explains the taking of the covenant. That is, when Allah the Exalted mentioned that He took the covenant of the Children of Israel, there was in that a vagueness as to what the covenant was, so He brought this clause to explain it; it then has no grammatical position.

Second: that it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «بني إسرائيل», and then there are two aspects in it. One: that it is an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara), meaning: "We took their covenant, they being destined to [maintain] monotheism forever as long as they lived". The other: that it is a concomitant ḥāl, meaning: "We took their covenant, they binding themselves to remain upon monotheism"; Abū al-Baqāʾ said this, and Quṭrub and al-Mubarrad preceded him in it. This is questionable, in that the ḥāl comes from the muḍāf ilayhi/ outside the places where that is permitted, according to the correct view, contrary to those who permit it from the muḍāf ilayhi without restriction. It cannot be said that the muḍāf ilayhi is in meaning governed by ميثاق — since ميثاق is either a maṣdar (verbal noun) or in its ruling, so what follows would be either agent or object — and that is [not] permissible, because one of the conditions for a maṣdar's governing, when it does not stand in place of the verb, is that it can be resolved into a maṣdariyya particle and a verb, and this cannot be resolved into them: were you to construe "and when We took that We make a covenant with the Children of Israel" or "that the Children of Israel make a covenant with Us", it would not be sound. Do you not see that if you said "I took Zayd's knowledge", it could not be construed as "I took that Zayd knows"? For this reason Ibn al-Ṭarāwa refused, in Sībawayh's chapter heading «هذا بابُ علم ما الكِلمُ من العربية», that the maṣdar be construed as a maṣdariyya particle and a verb, and he rejected and censured those who permitted it.

Third: that it is the answer to an omitted oath indicated by the word الميثاق, i.e. "We made them swear", or "We said to them: By Allah, you shall not worship…". This aspect is attributed to Sībawayh, and al-Kisāʾī, al-Farrāʾ and al-Mubarrad agreed with him.

Fourth: that it is on the construal of the omission of a preposition and the omission of أَنْ, the implied sense being: "We took their covenant on condition that you not worship", or "that you not worship". The preposition was dropped, because its dropping is regular with أَنَّ and أَنْ, as has been said more than once; then subjunctive «أَنْ» was dropped, so the verb after it became nominative. Its parallel is the words of Ṭarafa:

568 - أَلا أَيُّهذا الزاجري أحضرُ الوغى ... وأَنْ أشهدَ اللذاتِ هل أَنْتَ مُخْلِدي
(O you who chide me for being present at battle and for attending pleasures — can you make me immortal?)

And they reported from the Arabs: «مُرْهُ يَحْفِرَها» ("command him to dig it"), i.e. "that he dig it"; the implied sense being "from my being present" and "that he dig it". This is questionable, for implying «أَنْ» is not analogical; it is permitted only in places that the grammarians have enumerated, and they made anything else anomalous and rare. This is the correct view, contrary to the Kufans. When «أَنْ» is dropped, the correct view is that both the subjunctive and the nominative are permissible; «مُرْه يَحْفِرها» and «أَحْضُر الوغى» have been transmitted both ways. This is the opinion of al-Mubarrad and the Kufans, contrary to Abū al-Ḥasan [al-Akhfash], who required the nominative. The discussion has a place other than this that is more suitable for it. Al-Zamakhsharī supported this fourth aspect with the reading of ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd]: «لاَ تَعْبُدوا», as a prohibition.

Fifth: that it is in the position of the accusative governed by an omitted verb "say", that saying being a ḥāl, its implied form being: "saying to them: you shall not worship except Allah". It would then be a statement with the meaning of a prohibition; this is supported by the reading of Ubayy mentioned before, and with this the conjoining of «وقولوا» to it becomes clear. Al-Farrāʾ held this.

Sixth: that subjunctive «أَنْ» is implied, as above, but it with what falls within its scope is in the position of the accusative as a badal (substitute) from «ميثاق». This is close to the first view, in that this clause explains the covenant; and it is subject to the objection mentioned before, namely the dropping of «أَنْ» outside the analogical places.

Seventh: that it is in the accusative by an omitted verb "say", that saying not being a ḥāl but mere information, the implied sense being "and We said that to them"; it would be a statement with the meaning of a prohibition. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "As you say: 'You go to so-and-so and say such-and-such to him', meaning a command. It is more eloquent than an explicit command and prohibition, because it is as though [the addressee] hastened to comply and desist, and He is reporting it. The reading of Ubayy and ʿAbd Allāh «لا تعبدوا» supports it, and the verb 'say' must be intended." End of quotation. It is a very fine statement.

Eighth: that the implied form is «أَنْ لا تعبدون», this being explicative «أَنْ», because in His words {أَخَذْنَا مِيثَاقَ بني إِسْرَائِيلَ} there is vagueness, as said before, and it contains the meaning of saying; then explicative «أَنْ» was dropped. Al-Zamakhsharī mentioned this. Claiming the omission of the particle of explanation is obviously questionable.

His words: {إِلاَّ الله}: an emptied (mufarragh) exception, because what precedes it needs it; its verification was given earlier. In it there is iltifāt from the first person to the third, since had the speech run on its course it would have said "you shall not worship except Us", because of His words «أَخَذْنَا». This iltifāt carries an indication of the greatness of this Name and of His uniqueness in it which is not in the pronoun. Also, the nouns occurring [around it] are overt, so it was fitting that overt should neighbour overt.

His words: {وبالوالدين إِحْسَاناً}: there are five aspects in it. First: that the bāʾ is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «إحساناً», on the basis that it is a maṣdar standing in the place of an imperative verb, the implied sense being "and do good to (بـ) parents"; the bāʾ is synonymous with «إلى» in this meaning: you say أَحْسَنْتُ به and إليه. [Or] in the sense that on this aspect there is an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "and make excellent the dutifulness to parents", meaning: make excellent towards them your dutifulness to them. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "An objection to this view is that what the maṣdar governs comes before it." What Ibn ʿAṭiyya made an objection to this view does not hold on the doctrine of the majority, for their doctrine is that what is governed by a maṣdar standing in place of an imperative verb may come before it: you say ضرباً زيداً, and if you wish زيداً ضرباً. It is the same for them whether we assign the governing to the implied verb or to the maṣdar standing in place of its verb: fronting is permissible for them. What is barred is only fronting what is governed by a maṣdar that resolves into a maṣdariyya particle and a verb, as was explained just now. It holds only on the doctrine of Abū al-Ḥasan, for he bars fronting what is governed by a maṣdar standing in place of the verb, and in that he differed from the majority.

Second: that it is attached to an omitted element. That omitted element may be construed as an imperative verb, in keeping with His words {لاَ تَعْبُدُونَ}, which has the meaning of prohibition as said before, as though He said: "Do not worship except Allah, and do good to parents." It may also be construed as a statement in keeping with the wording of «لا تعبدون», the implied form being "and you shall do good". Al-Zamakhsharī construed it with both these possibilities. «إحساناً» is then accusative as a maṣdar emphasising that omitted verb. This is questionable in that the omission of the governor of an emphatic [maṣdar] is explicitly stated to be impermissible; and there is a discussion of this for which this is not the place.

Third:/ that the implied sense is "and take care of (استوصُوا) parents", so the bāʾ is attached to this implied verb, and «إحساناً» is then accusative as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

Fourth: its implied sense is "and We enjoined them regarding parents", so the bāʾ is attached to the omitted element too, and «إحساناً» is then accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. "for the sake of Our doing good to those enjoined about", in that the doing good is caused by Our enjoining concerning them; or [to] those enjoined, because of the reward from Us that follows for them when they do good to them.

Fifth: that the bāʾ and what it governs are conjoined to His words {لاَ تَعْبُدُونَ}, if it is said that maṣdariyya «أَنْ» is implied; so from it and what follows it a maṣdar is formed to which this genitive phrase is conjoined, the implied sense being: "We took their covenant to devote worship solely to Allah, and to parents", i.e. "and to dutifulness to parents", or "to doing good to parents". The bāʾ is then attached to الميثاق because of the meaning of the verb in it, for adverbial expressions and the like are governed by the "scents of verbs". «إحساناً» is then accusative as a maṣdar from that omitted muḍāf, namely البِرّ, because it has its meaning, or [from] الإحسان which we construed.

The apparent one among these aspects is only the second, because of the absence of the implication that is necessary in the others, and because the occurrence of the maṣdar standing in place of an imperative verb is regular and widespread. What it governs was put first only out of concern for it and to call attention to the fact that they are more deserving of good than those mentioned with them.

الوالدان are the father and the mother; each of them is called والد. He said:

569 - ألا رُبَّ مولودٍ وليسَ لَهُ أبٌ ... وذي وَلَدْ لَمْ يَلْدَهُ أبوانِ
(How many a one born who has no father, and one with a child whom two parents did not beget.)

It is also said: one does not say والدة with tāʾ for the mother; rather "the two والد" was said of her and the father by giving the masculine predominance. الإحسان is bestowing favour on another. It is also said: rather it is more general than bestowing favour. It is also said: it is what benefits everything.

His words: {وَذِي القربى} and what follows it are conjoined to what is in the genitive by the bāʾ. The sign of the genitive in it is the yāʾ, because it is one of the Six Nouns, which are nominative with wāw, accusative with alif and genitive with yāʾ, under conditions mentioned by the grammarians. As to whether their declension is by letters or by something else, the grammarians have ten doctrines about it, and this is not the place to mention them. It is one of the nouns that are bound to annexation in form and meaning, to generic nouns, so that by it one can reach the qualification of an indefinite by a generic noun, as in مَرَرْتُ برجلٍ ذي مالٍ ("I passed by a man possessing wealth"). Its annexation to a pronoun is barred except in poetic necessity or rare speech, as in his words:

570 - صَبَحْنا الخَزْرَجِيَّةَ مُرْهَفاتٍ ... أبانَ ذوي أَرُومَتِها ذَوُوها
(In the morning we fell upon the Khazrajī [tribe] with sharpened blades, whose owners cut off the people of its root.)

And al-Kisāʾī recited:

571 - إنما يَعْرِفُ المَعْ ... روفَ في الناس ذَوُوه
(Only those who possess kindness recognise kindness among people.)

On this is based their saying: "O Allah, bless Muḥammad and ذَويه (his own people)." Its annexation to a proper name is very rare, and it is of two kinds: obligatory, when they are joined by original coinage, as in ذي يزن and ذي رَعين; and permissible, when they are not joined by original coinage, as in ذي قَطَري and ذي عمرو, i.e. "the bearer of this name". Rarer than that is its annexation to the pronoun of the addressee, as in his words:

572 - وإنَّا لَنَرْجُو عاجلاً منكَ مثلَ ما ... رَجَوْناه قِدْماً من ذَويك الأفاضلِ
(We hope soon from you for the like of what we hoped long ago from your excellent kinsmen.)

«ذو» also comes as a relative noun in the sense of الذي and its derived forms; the well-known [usage] then is that it is indeclinable and masculine [in form]. It has many rulings mentioned in the books of grammar.

«القُرْبى» is the muḍāf ilayhi; its alif is for the feminine. It is a maṣdar like الرُّجْعى and العُقْبى, and it is applied to kinship by lineage and by the womb. Ṭarafa said:

573 - وظُلْمُ ذوي القُرْبى أشدُّ مضاضةً ... على الحُرِّ مِنْ وَقْعِ الحُسامِ المُهَنَّدِ
(The injustice of kinsfolk is more painful to the free man than the blow of the Indian-forged sword.)

He also said:

574 - وَقرَّبْتُ بالقُرْبى وجَدِّك إنه ... متى يَكُ أَمْرٌ للنَّكِيثَةِ أَشْهَدِ
(I drew close through kinship — by your fortune! — for whenever there is an affair that tests one's strength, I am present.)

The root indicates nearness, the opposite of distance.

His words: {واليتامى}: its pattern is فَعالى, and its alif is for the feminine. It is the plural of يتيم, like نديم / نَدامى, and this plural is not analogical. اليُتْم is being alone; from it comes «اليتيم», because he is alone without his two parents or one of them; and دُرَّةٌ يتيمةٌ ("a unique pearl") when it has no equal. It is also said: اليُتْم is slowness, and from it comes صبيٌّ يتيم, because kindness is slow to reach him. It is also said: it is neglect, because the child is neglected as regards what is good for him. Al-Aṣmaʿī said: "Orphanhood among humans is through loss of the father, and among others through loss of the mother." Al-Māwardī said: "Orphanhood among people is also through loss of the mother." The first is what is known among the lexicographers. One says يَتُم يَيْتُم يُتْماً, like كرُم يكرُم and عَظُم يَعْظُم عُظْماً; and يَتِمَ يَيْتَم يَتْماً, like سَمِعَ يَسْمَع سَمْعاً. These are two well-known dialects reported by al-Farrāʾ. One says: أَيْتمه اللهُ إيتاماً, i.e. He did that to him.

The sign of the genitive in القربى and اليتامى is a kasra implied (muqaddar) on the alif, even though it is [the alif] of the feminine, because a diptote, when annexed or when al- enters it, takes the genitive with kasra. Is it then called declinable (munṣarif) or merely "genitive-taking" (munjarr)? There are three views; the third distinguishes between the case where one of its two causes is being a proper name — then it is called munṣarif, as in «يَعْمُرُكمْ» — and the case where it is not — then it is called munjarr, as in بالأحمر. القربى and اليتامى are of this latter kind.

His words: «والمساكين»: the plural of مِسْكين. They call it "a plural that has no counterpart among singulars" and "a plural on the pattern of the ultimate plurals (muntahā al-jumūʿ)", and it is one of the causes that stand in place of two causes [for diptosy]; its verification will come shortly in this sūra.

The discussion of its derivation was given at the mention of المَسْكَنة. There is disagreement about it: is it in the sense of الفقير (the poor), or worse off than him, as in His words {مِسْكِيناً ذَا مَتْرَبَةٍ} [al-Balad: 16], i.e. his skin cleaves to the dust, unlike the فقير, who has something? He said:

575 - أمَّا الفقيرُ الذي كانَتْ حَلُوبَتُه ... وَفْقَ العِيالِ فلم يُتْرَكْ له سَبَدُ
(As for the poor man whose milch-camel was just enough for the household, not a tuft of hair was left to him.)

Or is he better off, because Allah assigned them some property, saying {أَمَّا السفينة فَكَانَتْ لِمَسَاكِينَ} [al-Kahf: 79]? This is a well-known disagreement among the scholars, both jurists and lexicographers.

His words: {وَقُولُواْ لِلنَّاسِ حُسْناً}: this clause is conjoined in meaning to His words {لاَ تَعْبُدُونَ}, as though He said: "Do not worship except Allah, and do good to parents, and say…"; or to the implied «أَحْسِنوا», as was established at His words {وبالوالدين إِحْسَاناً}. Abū al-Baqāʾ permitted it to be governed by an omitted verb "say", its implied form being: "And We said to them: say…"

It has been read حَسَناً with two fatḥas, حُسُناً with two ḍammas, حُسْنى without tanwīn like حُبْلى, and إحساناً from the quadriliteral.

As for the reading «حُسْناً» with ḍamma and sukūn, it admits several aspects. First, which is the apparent one: it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) occurring as a qualifier of an omitted element, its implied form being "and say to people a حُسْن speech", i.e. one possessing goodness. Second: that it is used as a qualifier by way of hyperbole, as though the speech itself were made goodness. Third: that it is an adjective on the pattern فُعْل, not originally a maṣdar, but like الحُلْو and المُرّ, so that it has the meaning of «حَسَن» with two fatḥas; there would then be two dialects in it, حُسْن and حَسَن, like البُخْل / البَخَل, الحُزْن / الحَزَن and العُرْب / العَرَب. Fourth: that it is accusative as a maṣdar derived from the meaning, for the meaning is: "and let your speech be good with goodness".

As for the reading «حَسَناً» with two fatḥas, which is the reading of Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī, it is an adjective of an omitted element, its implied form being "a good speech", as was said in one of the aspects of «حُسْناً».

As for «حُسُناً» with two ḍammas, the ḍamma of the sīn is in harmony with the ḥāʾ, so it has the meaning of «حُسْناً» with sukūn, and the aforementioned aspects apply to it.

As for whoever [read] «حُسْنى» without tanwīn, حُسْنى is a maṣdar like البُشْرى and الرُّجْعى. Al-Naḥḥās said about this reading: "This is not permissible in Arabic; nothing of this [pattern] is said except with alif-lām, as in الكُبْرى and الفُضْلى. This is the view of Sībawayh." Ibn ʿAṭiyya followed him in this, for he said: "Sībawayh rejected it, because أَفْعَل and فُعْلى come only as definite, unless the sense of preference is removed from it and it remains a maṣdar, like العُقْبى; that is permissible, and it is the account of the reading with it." End of quotation.

The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] took issue with him and said: "There is confusion in his words, because he said: 'because أَفْعَل and فُعْلى come only as definite', and this is not correct. As for «أَفْعَل», it has three uses. First: that «مِنْ» be with it, overt or implied, or that it be annexed to an indefinite; in these two it is never definite. Second: that al- enter it, so that it becomes definite by it. Third: that it be annexed to a definite, so that it becomes definite, according to the correct view. As for «فُعْلى», it has two uses: first, with alif-lām; second, annexation to a definite, and in this there is the disagreement mentioned before. And his words 'unless the sense of preference is removed from it and it remains a maṣdar' — the apparent sense of this is that فُعْلى, the feminine of أَفْعَل, when the sense of preference is removed from it, remains a maṣdar; but it is not so. Rather, when the sense of preference is removed from فُعْلى, the feminine of أَفْعَل, it becomes like an adjective in which there is no preference; do you not see their interpretation of كُبْرى as meaning كبيرة and صُغْرى as meaning صغيرة? Moreover, فُعْلى as a maṣdar is not analogical; only a few words of it have come, like العُقْبى and البُشْرى."

Then the Shaykh answered this second point with something whose meaning is that the pronoun in his word «عنها» refers to «حُسْنى», not to فُعْلى the feminine of أَفْعَل, and that it is a disjoined exception, as though he said: "unless the sense of preference is removed from حُسْنى, which Ubayy read", the meaning becoming: "unless it is held that «حُسْنى» is a maṣdar, not the feminine of أَفْعَل"; and his words "and it is the account of the reading with it" mean: and the maṣdar is the account of the reading with it.

[Translator's note: the closing «انتهى» below indicates that what follows is still quoted from the Shaykh.] "This reading is accounted for in two ways. First: as a maṣdar, like البشرى, with the aspects mentioned before for «حُسْناً» as a maṣdar — except that it requires establishing حُسْنى as a maṣdar from the speech of the Arabs, حَسُنَ حُسْنى, as they say رَجَع رُجْعى, since فُعْلى coming as a maṣdar is not analogical. The second way: that it is an adjective of an omitted noun, i.e. 'and say to people a حُسْنى word' or 'a حُسْنى saying'. In qualifying with it there are then two aspects. One: that it is for preference, and its use without being made definite by al- or annexed to a definite is then anomalous, as in his words:

576 - وإنْ دَعَوْتِ إلى جُلَّى ومَكْرُمَةٍ ... يَوْماً سَراةَ كِرامِ الناسِ فادْعِينا
(And if one day you call the chiefs of noble people to a grave matter and an honourable deed, call us.)

and his words:

577 - في سَعْي دُنْيا طالما قَدْ مُدَّتِ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(In striving for a worldly life that has long been extended …)

The other aspect: that it is not for preference, but in the sense of حَسَنة, like كُبْرى in the sense of كبيرة, i.e. 'and say to people a good saying', just as they said 'Yūsuf is the أَحْسَن of his brothers' in the sense of 'the good one among his brothers'." End of quotation. From this the corruption of al-Naḥḥās's statement is known.

As for whoever read «إحساناً», it is a maṣdar occurring as a qualifier of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "a speech that is إحسان", and the well-known interpretation applies to it. إحساناً is the maṣdar of أَحْسَن whose hamza is for becoming (ṣayrūra), i.e. "a speech possessing goodness", as you say «أَعْشَبَتِ الأرضُ», i.e. it came to possess herbage.

His words: {وَأَقِيمُواْ الصلاة وَآتُواْ الزكاة} [al-Baqara: 43]: its counterpart has been discussed.

His words: {ثُمَّ تَوَلَّيْتُمْ إِلاَّ قَلِيلاً}: al-Zamakhsharī said: "By way of iltifāt (a shift of person)." What he said applies only to the reading «لا يَعْبدون» in the third person; on the second-person reading there is no iltifāt at all. It is possible that by iltifāt he meant the move from addressing the ancient Children of Israel to addressing those present in the time of the Prophet ﷺ; this has been said, and it is supported by the words of Allah the Exalted {إِلاَّ قَلِيلاً مِّنْكُمْ}, about which it is said that He means those who became Muslim in his time, upon him be peace, such as ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām and his like; it would then be iltifāt on both readings.

The well-known [reading] is «قليلاً» in the accusative as an exception, because it is from an/ affirmative [statement]. It is reported from Abū ʿAmr and others: «إلا قليلٌ» in the nominative. In this there are six views.

The most correct of them: that its nominative is as an adjective, by interpreting «إلا» and what follows it in the sense of غير. Sībawayh, may Allah have mercy on him, devoted a chapter to this in his Book, saying: "This is a chapter on that in which «إلاَّ» and what follows it are an adjective, like غير and مثل." Among the examples of this chapter he mentioned: "Had there been with us a man other than Zayd (إلا زيدٌ), we would have been overcome", and {لَوْ كَانَ فِيهِمَآ آلِهَةٌ إِلاَّ الله لَفَسَدَتَا} [al-Anbiyāʾ: 22], and:

578 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... قليلٌ بها الأصواتُ إلا بُغامُها
(… in it there are few sounds other than her [the camel's] soft groaning.)

[Translator's note: the source quotes Sībawayh's example as «لو كان معنا إلا رجلٌ إلا زيدٌ», with إلا twice; the usual form is «لو كان معنا رجلٌ إلا زيدٌ».]

He treated this as equivalent to the reading {لاَّ يَسْتَوِي القاعدون مِنَ المؤمنين غَيْرُ أُوْلِي الضرر} with «غير» in the nominative. In a case like «ما قامَ القومُ إلا زيدٌ» with the nominative he permitted both badal (substitute) and adjective, and on this he accounted for his words:

579 - وكلُّ أخٍ مُفارِقُه أَخوه ... لَعَمْرُ أبيكَ إلا الفَرْقَدانِ
(Every brother will be parted from by his brother — by your father's life! — except the two Farqad stars.)

as though he said: "And every brother other than the two Farqads will be parted from by his brother"; as al-Shammākh said:

580 - وكلُّ خليلٍ غيرُ هاضمِ نفسِه ... لِوَصْلِ خليلٍ صارمٌ أو معارِزُ
(Every friend who does not humble himself to keep a friend's bond will cut off or turn aside.)

Others recited:

581 - لدَمٍ ضائِعٍ تغيَّبَ عنه ... أَقْربوه إلا الصَّبا والجَنُوبُ
(For blood shed in vain, whose nearest kin stayed away from it — all but the east wind and the south wind.)

and his words:

582 - وبالصَّريمةِ منهم منزلٌ خَلَقٌ ... عافٍ تَغَيَّر إلا النُّؤْيُ والوَتِدُ
(At al-Ṣarīma they have a worn, effaced abode, all changed except the trench and the tent-peg.)

The difference between qualifying with إلا and qualifying with غير is that with «إلا» definites and indefinites, overt nouns and pronouns may be qualified. Some said: "Only an indefinite, or one made definite by the generic lām — since that is equivalent to an indefinite — may be qualified with it." Al-Mubarrad said: "Its condition is that a badal be suitable in its place." This has a place where we shall discuss it.

Second: that it is ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition). Ibn ʿUṣfūr said: "By qualification with إلا the grammarians only mean ʿaṭf bayān." This is questionable.

Third: that it is nominative by an omitted verb, as though He said: "a few refrained".

Fourth: that it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is omitted, i.e. "except a few of you did not turn away", as they said: "I did not pass by anyone except a man of Banū Tamīm [who is] better than him."

Fifth: that it is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the nominative pronoun. Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned these three aspects. He said: "Sībawayh and his followers call it naʿt and waṣf (qualifier)", meaning the tawkīd. In these aspects that he mentioned there is what is obvious [in weakness], but they have been said.

Sixth: that it is a badal from the pronoun in «تَوَلَّيْتُم». Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "That is permissible even though no negation preceded in the speech, because «تَوَلَّيْتم» means negation, as though He said: 'You did not fulfil the covenant except a few'." What he mentioned regarding the permissibility of the badal is barred by the grammarians: they do not permit «قام القَومُ إلا زيدٌ» as a badal. They said: because the badal takes the place of what it replaces, so it would amount to your saying "قامَ إلا زيدٌ", which is barred. As for his saying that it is "in the sense of negation", there is no affirmative in which that is not possible: do you not see that your saying "the people stood except Zayd" is equivalent to "they did not sit except Zayd"? So every affirmative is like that if you take the negation of its contradictory or its contrary, and the Arabs did not take that into account in their speech. The grammarians permitted «قام القومُ إلا زيدٌ» with the nominative only as an adjective, as has been established.

«منكم» is an adjective of قليلاً, so it is in the position of the accusative or nominative according to the two readings. The apparent [sense] is that by "the few" persons are meant, because it is qualified by His words «منكم». Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It is possible that the fewness is in belief, i.e. when they disobeyed and the last of them disbelieved in Muḥammad ﷺ, nothing remained but a little belief, since it did not benefit them; the first is stronger." End of quotation. This is a very far-fetched, or impossible, view.

His words: {وَأَنْتُمْ مُّعْرِضُونَ}: a clause of mubtadaʾ and khabar in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of «تَوَلَّيْتُم». There are two views about it. First: that it is an emphatic ḥāl, because turning away (التولِّي) and turning aside (الإعراض) are synonyms. It is also said: it is clarifying, for التولِّي is with the body and الإعراض with the heart; Abū al-Baqāʾ said this. After it he said: "It is also said: تَوَلَّيْتم means their forefathers, and أنتم مُعْرِضُون means themselves, as He said {وَإِذْ أَنْجَيْنَاكُمْ مِّنْ آلِ فِرْعَونَ} [al-Aʿrāf: 141], i.e. their forefathers." End of quotation. This leads to the clause {وَأَنْتُمْ مُّعْرِضُونَ} not being a ḥāl, because the agent of the turning away is in reality not the one to whom the ḥāl belongs — and Allah knows best.

Likewise it is clarifying when what التولِّي and الإعراض are attached to differs, as some said: "Then you turned away from the taking of your covenant, while you are turning aside from this Prophet ﷺ." It is also said: التولِّي and الإعراض are taken from travelling a road: when one travels a road and returns the way he came, that is called تولِّي; and if he goes across the breadth (عُرْض) of the road, it is called إعراض.

The ḥāl came as a nominal clause headed by «أنتم» because it is more emphatic, and the khabar of the mubtadaʾ was brought as a noun because it is more indicative of permanence, as though it were said: "and you — your habit is turning away from the truth and turning aside from it."

semin-durr:180-180.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمْ إِذَا حَضَرَ}: «كُتِبَ» is passive, and the fāʿil (agent) was omitted because it is known — namely Allah the Exalted — and for brevity. There are three interpretations of what stands in place of the fāʿil (nāʾib fāʿil, deputy agent). The first: that it is «الوصيةُ» (the bequest), i.e. "the bequest has been prescribed for you"; the masculine form of the verb is permissible for two reasons: first, that what stands in place of the fāʿil is figuratively feminine; second, the separation between it and its nominative. The second: that it is the act of bequeathing (al-īṣāʾ) indicated by His words {الوصية لِلْوَالِدَيْنِ}, i.e. "it was prescribed", meaning the bequeathing.
The third: that it is the preposition and its genitive noun; this is plausible on the opinion of al-Akhfash and the Kufans. «عليكم» is in the position of the nominative on this view, and in the position of the accusative on the first two views.
His words: {إِذَا حَضَرَ}: the governing word in «إذا» is «كُتِب», on the basis that it is a pure adverbial and does not include [the sense of] a condition, as though it were said: "the bequest has been prescribed for you at the time death is present". It is not permissible for the governing word in it to be the word «الوصية», because it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), and what a maṣdar governs may not precede it, since it is resolvable into a relative noun and its ṣila — except on the doctrine of one who allows latitude with the adverbial and its equivalent [the prepositional phrase], namely Abū al-Ḥasan [al-Akhfash], for he does not forbid it; the implied form would then be: "it was prescribed for them «[Translator's note: so in the text («عليهم»), for "for you".]» that you make a bequest at the time death is present".
Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: «In the i'rab of this verse it is plausible that «كُتِب» is the governing word in «إذا», the meaning being: Allah's imposing [of the obligation] and what His writing requires is directed at you when [death] is present; He expressed the directing of the obligation by «كُتب» so that the meaning that it is written from pre-eternity is joined to this meaning. «الوصيةُ» is the object whose agent is not named, by «كُتِب». The apodosis (jawāb) of the two conditions «إنْ» and «إذا» is implied, indicated by what precedes in His words «كُتِب»». The Shaykh said: «This is self-contradictory, because he made the governing word in «إذا» «كُتِبَ», which entails that «إذا» is a pure adverbial not including a condition; this contradicts his saying: "the apodosis of «إذا» and «إنْ» is omitted", because conditional idhā is governed only by its apodosis or by its conditional verb, and «كُتِب» is neither of them. If it is said: some allow the apodosis of a condition to be placed first, so «كُتب» would be the apodosis but placed first, and it governs «إذا», so Ibn ʿAṭiyya would be holding this view — the answer is that this is not possible, because he stated explicitly that its apodosis is omitted, indicated by «كُتب», and did not make «كُتِب» itself the apodosis».
It is permissible for the governing word in «إذا» to be the bequeathing understood from the word «الوصية», which is what stands in place of the fāʿil of «كُتِب», as preceded. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said concerning this interpretation: «This implied bequeathing, indicated by the mention of the bequest afterwards, is the governing word in «إذا»; and «الوصيةُ» is nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and in it is the apodosis of the two conditions, on the [pattern of] what Sībawayh recited:
829 - مَنْ يفعلِ الصالحاتِ اللهُ يحفظُه ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Whoever does righteous deeds, Allah protects him…)
Its nominative is then by being mubtadaʾ, i.e. "then upon him is the bequest", with only the fāʾ implied, as though He said "then the bequest is for the parents"». The Shaykh disputed him on several grounds. The first: that it is self-contradictory, in that when he makes «إذا» governed by the implied bequeathing it becomes purely adverbial, so how can an apodosis be supplied for it, as was worked out above? The second: that this bequeathing is either supplied as an omitted word or as a pronoun, and on both suppositions it cannot govern, because a condition of a maṣdar's governing, according to the Basrans, is that it be neither omitted nor pronominalised; moreover it stands in place of the fāʿil, so it cannot be omitted. The third: his saying "the apodosis of the two conditions", whereas one and the same thing cannot be the apodosis of two; rather each one's apodosis is separate, supplied in its own measure. The fourth: his making the omission of the fāʾ permissible in the Quran, whereas Sībawayh stated explicitly that it is permissible only under poetic necessity, and he recited:
مَنْ يفعلِ الحسناتِ اللهُ يَشْكُرها ... والشرُّ بالشرِّ عند الله سِيَّانِ
(Whoever does good deeds, Allah will reward them; and evil for evil is equal in Allah's sight.)
His reciting it as «مَنْ يَفْعَلِ الصالحات اللهُ يحفظه» may be a variant transmission, except that Sībawayh did not recite it thus but as given above. It is related of al-Mubarrad that he does not allow the omission of the fāʾ at all, neither under necessity nor otherwise, and he transmits it as: «مَنْ يفعل الخيرَ فالرحمنُ يشكُره» (whoever does good, the Merciful will reward him). People answered him that this is no argument against Sībawayh's transmission.
It is permissible for «إذا» to be conditional, so that its apodosis and the apodosis of «إنْ» are both omitted. The precise account: the apodosis of «إنْ» is implied, its implied form being: «The bequest is prescribed for one of you, when death is present to him, if he leaves wealth: let him make a bequest». So His [implied] words «فَلْيُوصِ» are the apodosis of in, omitted because the speech indicates it; and this implied apodosis indicates the apodosis of «إذا», so the omitted element indicates an omitted element like it. This is better than the view of those who say that the second condition is the apodosis of the first and the apodosis of the second is omitted; and better too than the implied form given by those who supply it from the meaning of «كُتِبَ», which is past in meaning — unless one interprets it as meaning "the writing is directed at you if he leaves wealth".
His words: «الوصيةُ»: three interpretations. [The first:] that it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar (predicate) is «للوالدَيْن». The second: that it is the object of «كُتِب», as preceded. The third: that it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, i.e. "then upon him is the bequest"; this is according to those who allow the omission of the fāʾ of the apodosis, namely al-Akhfash, and he is refuted by Sībawayh's report.
His words: {الوصية}: three interpretations. [The first:] that it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is «للوالدَيْن». The second: that it is the object of «كُتِب», as preceded. The third: that it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, i.e. "then upon him is the bequest"; this is according to those who allow the omission of the fāʾ of the apodosis, namely al-Akhfash, and he is refuted by Sībawayh's report. «[Translator's note: this paragraph repeats the preceding one word for word in the source text.]»
His words: «بالمعروف»: two interpretations are permissible. The first: that it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «الوصية» itself. The second: that it is attached to something omitted as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الوصية», i.e. "while it is accompanied by fairness, not by injustice".
His words: {حقاً}: there are three interpretations of its accusative. The first: that it is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar; that omitted maṣdar is either the maṣdar of «كُتِب» or the maṣdar of «أَوْصى», i.e. "a true prescribing" or "a true bequeathing". The second: that it is a ḥāl from the omitted definite maṣdar, [either] the maṣdar of «كُتِب» or of «أَوْصَى», as preceded. The third: that it is accusative as emphasising the content of the clause, so its governing word is omitted, i.e. "that is truly due (ḥaqqa dhālika ḥaqqan)"; al-Zamakhsharī, Ibn ʿAṭiyya and Abū al-Baqāʾ said this. The Shaykh said: «The rules of grammar reject this, because the apparent sense of His words «على المتقين» is that it is attached to «حقاً» or is in the position of an adjective of it, and neither supposition is permissible: the first because an emphasising maṣdar does not govern, and the second because [qualification takes it out of being emphatic]». This does not bind them, for in that case they do not say that «على المتقين» is attached to it. Abū al-Baqāʾ stated this explicitly, for he said: «It has been said that it is attached to the maṣdar itself, but this is weak, because the emphasising maṣdar does not govern; only the maṣdar that is accusative by an omitted verb governs, when it stands in for it, as when you say "ḍarban Zaydan", i.e. "strike [Zayd]"». However, he made it an adjective of «حقّ», and so this [objection] does apply to him.
One of the grammatical analysts said: «It emphasises what the meaning of «المتقين» contains», as though it were said: "upon those who are truly God-fearing", as in His words: {أولائك هُمُ المؤمنون حَقّاً} [al-Anfāl: 74]. This is weak because it precedes its governing word, which is a relative [i.e. the article of al-muttaqīn], and because it does not readily come to mind.
The Shaykh said: «The preferable view in my opinion is that it is a maṣdar from the meaning of «كُتب», because the meaning of "the bequest was prescribed" is: it became due and obligatory; so it is a maṣdar not from the verb's own root, like "qaʿadtu julūsan" (I sat down, a sitting)».

semin-durr:181-181.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {فَمَن بَدَّلَهُ}: «مَنْ» may be conditional or relative; and the fāʾ is either obligatory, if it is a condition, or permissible, if it is relative. … with the feminine form «[Translator's note: the text appears to have a lacuna here; the sentence about the pronoun of «بَدَّلَهُ» referring to «الوصية» (the bequest) seems to have dropped out before «بلفظِ المؤنَّثِ».]», because it has the meaning of a masculine, namely the bequeathing (al-īṣāʾ). Or it refers to the bequeathing itself, indicated by «الوصية»; except that regard for the masculine with a feminine is uncommon even if it is figurative [feminine]. Do you not see that there is no difference between your saying "Hind went out (kharajat)" and "the sun rose (ṭalaʿat)", and one may not say "al-shamsu ṭalaʿa", just as one may not say "Hind kharaja", except under poetic necessity? It has also been said that it refers to the matter and the obligation that Allah commanded and imposed. Likewise the pronoun in «سَمِعَه». The pronoun in «إثمُه» refers to the altered bequeathing, or to the altering understood from His words «بَدَّله».
He took the meaning into account in His words {عَلَى الذين يُبَدِّلُونَهُ}, since had it followed the pattern of the earlier wording He would have said: «then its sin is only upon him — or upon the one who alters it».
It has also been said that the pronoun in «بَدَّله» refers to the prescribing (al-katb), or to the due right, or to fairness. These are six views.
«ما» in His words {بَعْدَمَا سَمِعَهُ} may be maṣdariyya (infinitival), i.e. "after his hearing it", or a relative meaning alladhī (that which). So on the first, the hāʾ in «سَمِعَه» refers to what the hāʾ in «بَدَّله» refers to; on the second, it refers to the relative noun, i.e. "after that which he heard of Allah's commands".

semin-durr:182-182.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {فَمَنْ خَافَ}: the two interpretations allowed for the «مَنْ» before it are allowed here. The fāʾ in «فلا إثم» is [the fāʾ of] the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), or the fāʾ that enters the khabar (predicate). Three interpretations are permissible for «مِنْ موصٍ». The first: that it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «خاف», marking the beginning of the extent. The second: that it is attached to something omitted as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «جَنَفَاً», placed before it, because it was originally an adjective of it, and when it was placed first it became accusative as a ḥāl. Its parallel is «I took wealth from Zayd (akhadhtu min Zaydin mālan)»: if you wish, you attach «مِنْ زيد» to «أَخَذْتُ», and if you wish, you make it a ḥāl from «مالاً», since it is originally its adjective. The third: that it explains the genus of those who deviate, and it is also attached to «خاف». On the first two views the one who deviates is not one of the testators but someone else, while on the third he is one of the testators.
Abū Bakr [Shuʿba], Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read «مُوَصٍّ» with the ṣād doubled, and the rest without doubling. They are from awṣā and waṣṣā, and it has preceded that the two are dialectal variants. However, Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī and Abū Bakr are among those who read {ووصى بِهَآ إِبْرَاهِيمُ} [al-Baqara: 132] with doubling, and Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read «أوصى» with hamza. So were the reading not a followed Sunna that may not be done by opinion, the analogy for the reading of Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr and Ḥafṣ there — «ووصَّى» with doubling — would be that they read «مُوَصٍّ» with doubling here. As for Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir, they read «مُوصٍ» here without doubling, by analogy with their reading «أَوْصَى» there on the pattern afʿala. Likewise Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī and Abū Bakr read «ووصَّى» there with doubling, so they read «مُوَصٍّ» here with doubling, by analogy. «[Translator's note: the text first lists Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī and Abū Bakr among those who read «ووصى» with doubling at 2:132, and then makes the same point again; it is translated as written.]»
Fear (al-khawf) here means apprehension (khashya), which is its basic sense; it has also been said that it means knowledge, which is figurative. The relation between them is that a person does not fear a thing until he knows that it is something to be feared; so it belongs to the class of expressing the cause by the effect. Among instances of khawf meaning knowledge are His words: {إِلاَّ أَن يَخَافَآ أَلاَّ يُقِيمَا حُدُودَ الله} [al-Baqara: 229], and the words of Abū Miḥjan al-Thaqafī:
830 - إذا مُتُّ فادْفِنِّي إلى جَنْبٍ كَرْمَةٍ ... تُرَوِّي عظامي في المَمات عروقُها
ولا تَدْفِنَنِّي في الفلاةِ فإنني ... أخَافُ إذا ما مُتُّ ألاَّ أذوقُها
(When I die, bury me beside a vine, whose roots will water my bones after death; and do not bury me in the open desert, for I fear [i.e. know] that once I am dead I shall not taste it.)
As for al-janaf, the lexicographers have two views about it. The first: inclination. Al-Aʿshā said:
831 - تَجانَفُ عن حُجْرِ اليمَامةِ ناقتي ... وما قَصَدَتْ من أهلِها لِسِوائكا
(My she-camel veers away from Ḥujr of al-Yamāma, and of its people she has aimed for none but you.)
Another said:
832 - هُمُ المَوْلى وإنْ جَنَفُوا عَلَيْنا ... وإنَّا مِنْ لقائِهِمْ لَزُورُ
(They are our kinsmen, even if they have inclined against us; and we, from meeting them, turn aside.)
It has also been said: it is injustice. The poet said:
833 - إني امرؤٌ منعَتْ أَرومةُ عامرٍ ... ضَيْمي وقد جَنَفَتْ عليَّ خُصومُ
(I am a man whom the stock of ʿĀmir has protected from wrong, when adversaries have dealt unjustly with me.)
One says janifa, with kasra on the nūn, yajnafu, with fatḥa on it, so he is janif and jānif; and ajnafa: he committed janaf, like alāma: he did something for which he is blamed.
The pronoun in «بينهم» refers to the testator and the heirs, or to the legatees, or to the heirs and the legatees. The apparent view is that it refers to the legatees, since the word «المُوصي» indicates them. It is a parallel of {وَأَدَآءٌ إِلَيْهِ} [al-Baqara: 178] [in] that the pronoun refers to the one who pardons because «عفا» necessarily implies him. Like it is what al-Farrāʾ recited:
834 - وما أَدْري إذا يَمَّمْتُ أرضاً ... أريدُ الخيرَ أيُّهما يَليِني
(I do not know, when I head for a land seeking good, which of the two will befall me.)
The pronoun in «أيُّهما» refers to good and evil, even though evil has not been mentioned, because its opposite indicates it. The pronoun in «عليه», in «خاف» and in «أصلح» refers to «مَنْ».

semin-durr:129-129.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {مِّنْهُمْ}: in the position of the accusative, because it is an adjective of «رسولاً», so it is attached to something omitted, i.e. "a messenger being from among them".
His words: {يَتْلُواْ}: concerning the position of this clause there are three aspects. The first: it is in the position of the accusative as a second adjective of «رسولاً»; this comes in the better order, since what resembles a single word — namely the prepositional phrase — precedes the clause. The second: it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «رسولا», because once it was described it became specified. The third: it is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «مِنْهم», and what governs it is the [notion of] settledness (istiqrār) to which «منهم» is attached, because it occurs as an adjective.
His words «العزيزُ» were put first because it is an attribute of the Essence, and «الحكيمُ» was put later because it is an attribute of action.
One says: عَزَّ يَعُزُّ, يَعَزُّ and يَعِزُّ, but with a difference in meaning. The form with ḍamma means "overcame", and from it is {وَعَزَّنِي فِي الخطاب} [Ṣād: 23]; the form with fatḥa means hardness, and from it is «عَزَّ لحمُ الناقة», i.e. [the she-camel's flesh] became hard, and «عَزَّ عليَّ هذا الأمرُ» (this matter was hard on me); and the form with kasra means preciousness and rarity of anything comparable.

semin-durr:130-130.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {وَمَن يَرْغَبُ}: «مَنْ» is an interrogative noun with the sense of disavowal (inkār), so it is negation in meaning; for that reason «إلاَّ», which is for affirmation, came after it. Its position is the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «يَرْغَبُ» is its khabar (predicate), containing a pronoun that refers back to it. «الرغبة» originally means seeking. If it is made transitive with «في», it means preferring and choosing something, as in رَغِبْت في كذا (I desired such-and-such); and if it is made transitive with «عن», it means renouncing, as in رَغِبْت عنك (I turned away from you).
His words: {إِلاَّ مَن سَفِهَ}: there are two aspects in «مَنْ». The first: it is in the position of the nominative as a badal (substitute) from the pronoun in «يَرْغَبُ», and this is the preferred one, because the speech is not affirmative. The Kufans make this a case of conjunction: if you say «ما قام القومُ إلا زيدٌ», «إلاَّ» according to them is a conjunction and «زيد» is conjoined to «القوم»; the verification of this is given in the books of grammar. The second: it is in the position of the accusative as the excepted (mustathnā). «مَنْ» may be relative or an indefinite qualified noun; the clause after it has no grammatical position on the first, and its position is the nominative or accusative on the second.
His words: {نَفْسَهُ}: concerning its accusative there are seven aspects. The first — and it is the preferred one — is that it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), because Thaʿlab and al-Mubarrad related that «سَفِه», with kasra on the [fāʾ], is transitive by itself, just as «سَفَّه», with fatḥa on the fāʾ and shadda, is transitive. It is related from Abū al-Khaṭṭāb that it is a dialectal usage. This is the choice of al-Zamakhsharī, for he said: "«سَفِه نفسَه» means he demeaned it and held it in contempt." Then he mentioned other aspects, and then said: "The [correct] aspect is the first, and sufficient as witness for it is what has come in the ḥadīth: 'Arrogance is that you treat the truth as foolish (tasfaha al-ḥaqq) and despise people.'" The second: it is a mafʿūl bihi, but on «سَفِه» being made to include (taḍmīn) the meaning of a transitive verb; al-Zajjāj and Ibn Jinnī took it as meaning «جَهِل» (was ignorant of), and Abū ʿUbayda took it as meaning «أهلك» (destroyed). The third: it is accusative by the dropping of the preposition (manṣūb bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ), the implied form being «سَفِه في نفسه» (he was foolish in himself). The fourth: it is a tawkīd (emphasis) of an omitted emphasised word, the implied form being «سَفِه قولَه نفسَه» (he made foolish his very own saying), and the emphasised word was omitted, by analogy with the adjective and the qualified noun; Makkī related it. The fifth: it is a tamyīz (specification); this is the view of some Kufans. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It may belong to the irregular case of the specification being definite, as in the poet's saying:
727 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... ولا بفَزارةَ الشُّعْرِ الرِّقَابا
(…nor with Fazāra, hairy of neck.)
728 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... أجبَّ الظهرِ ليسَ له سَنامُ
(…cut off at the back, having no hump.)"
So he made «الرِّقاب» and «الظهر» specifications; but it is not so — rather, both are likened to the direct object, because they are governed by a resembling adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha), namely «الشُّعْر», plural of أَشْعر, and «أجَبّ», which is a noun. The sixth: it is likened to the direct object; this is the view of some Kufans. The seventh: it is a tawkīd of «مَنْ سَفِه», because it is in the position of the accusative as the excepted on one of the two views; this is a strange derivation which the author of «العجائب والغرائب» reported. The preferred is the first, because inclusion (taḍmīn) is not regular by analogy, and likewise [dropping] the preposition; as for omitting the emphasised word and keeping the emphasis, the correct view is that it is not permissible; as for the tamyīz, it does not occur definite, and what has come [so] is rare or to be interpreted otherwise; and as for the accusative by likening to the direct object, it does not occur with verbs, but only with resembling adjectives specifically.
His words: {فِي الآخرة}: there are five aspects in it. The first: it is attached to «الصالحين», on the alif and lām being for definiteness and not relative. The second: it is likewise attached to something omitted, but of the same kind as what is uttered, i.e. "and indeed he, being righteous in the Hereafter, is among the righteous". [Translator's note: so in the source; the word "likewise" and the jump from "the second" to "the fourth" indicate that the end of the second aspect and the beginning of the third have dropped out of the text.] The fourth: it is attached to His words «الصالحين» even if «ال» is relative, because with adverbs and their like there is tolerated, by way of latitude, what is not tolerated with others; its parallel is the poet's saying:
729 - رَبَّيْتُه حتى إذا تَمَعْدَدا ... كان جزائي بالعَصَى أَنْ أُجْلَدَا
(I raised him until, when he grew sturdy, my reward was to be beaten with the stick.)
The fifth: it is attached to «اصَطَفْيناه». Al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Faḍl said: "In the speech there is fronting and postponing; its sense is: and We chose him in this world and in the Hereafter." The like of this ought not to be permitted in the Quran, because the ear shrinks from it.
«الاصطفاء» is choosing; it is iftiʿāl from «صَفْوة الشيء», which is its choicest part. Its origin is اصْتَفى; the tāʾ of iftiʿāl was changed into ṭāʾ only to suit the ṣād, since it is an emphatic (iṭbāq) letter; this was given at His words {أَضْطَرُّهُ} [al-Baqara: 126]. He emphasised the clause of choosing with the lām, and the second with «إنّ» and the lām, because the second needs further emphasis: his being among the righteous in the Hereafter is a matter of the unseen, so reporting it needed extra emphasis; whereas Allah's choosing of him they had witnessed of him, and generation after generation had transmitted it.

semin-durr:203-203.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {مَّعْدُودَاتٍ}: a naʿt (adjective) of «أيام». It has already been stated that the adjective of what is non-rational is regularly pluralised with alif and tāʾ. Abū al-Baqāʾ went on at length here with a question and an answer. As for the question, he said: "If it is said: «الأيام» has as its singular «يوم», and «المعدودات» has as its singular «معدودة»; and a day is not described by «معدودة», because the adjective here is feminine while the thing described is masculine — the proper way would be to say «أيامٌ معدودةٌ», describing the plural with the feminine — then the answer is that he made «معدودات» follow the wording of «أيام», matching plural with plural figuratively, the original being «معدودة», as He said: {لَن تَمَسَّنَا النار إِلاَّ أَيَّاماً مَّعْدُودَةً} [al-Baqara: 80]. And if it were said that days comprise hours, and «الساعة» is feminine, so the plural came according to the sense of 'the hours of the days' — and in it there is an indication of the command to remember [Allah] in all the hours of these days or most of them — that would be a sound answer. The like of this is 'the month', 'summer' and 'winter', for these are given as answers to «كم» (how many/how long), and «كم» is only answered with a number; yet the words for these things are not numbers, but rather names of counted things, so they were an answer from this angle." In this question and answer there is prolixity without benefit. And his statement that the singular of «معدودات» is «معدودة», with the feminine, is not conceded; rather its singular is «معدود» with the masculine, and its pluralisation with alif and tāʾ does no harm, since the plural with alif and tāʾ does not require the singular to be feminine — do you not see their saying: «حَمَّامات», «سِجِلاَّت» and «سُرادِقات»?

His saying: {فَمَن تَعَجَّلَ فِي يَوْمَيْنِ}: «مَنْ» admits two analyses. The first: that it is conditional, so «تَعَجَّل» is in the position of jussive (majzūm), and the fāʾ in His saying «فلا» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of the condition, the fāʾ and what lies within its scope also being in the position of jussive as the apodosis. The second: that it is a relative noun, so «تَعَجَّل» has no grammatical position, occurring as a ṣila (relative clause); its wording is past while its meaning may be past or future, since this is the rule for everything that occurs as a ṣila. The fāʾ in «فلا» is then redundant (zāʾida) in the khabar (predicate), and it together with what follows it is in the position of nominative (marfūʿ) as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (subject). «في يومين» is attached to «تعجَّل». A figurative usage must be assumed, because a verb occurring within a counted span of time necessarily occurs in each of its counted units: you say «سِرْت يومين» ("I travelled for two days"), and the travel must have occurred in the first and the second, or part of the second; whereas here the hastening does not occur in the first of these two days in any way. The figurative aspect is either that what occurs in one of them is ascribed as occurring in both, as in His saying: {نَسِيَا حُوتَهُمَا} [al-Kahf: 61] and {يَخْرُجُ مِنْهُمَا الُّلؤْلُؤُ وَالمَرْجَانُ} [al-Raḥmān: 22], where the one who forgot is one of the two, and likewise what is brought forth is from one of the two; or it is by the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. 'in the completion of two days' or 'their completeness'.

«تعجَّل» may have the meaning of «استعجَلَ», like «تكبَّر» and «استكبر»; or be the reflexive-resultative (muṭāwiʿ) of «عجَّل», as in «كَسَّرْتُه فَتَكَسَّر» ("I broke it and it broke"); or have the meaning of the bare form, which is «عَجِل». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The muṭāwaʿa reading fits better, because of His saying «ومَنْ تأخَّر», just as it is so in his saying:
892 - قد يُدْرِك المتأنِّي بعضَ حاجتِه ... وقد يكونُ مع المُسْتعجِلِ الزَّلَلُ
(The deliberate one may attain some of his need, while the hasty one may meet with stumbling.)
because of his saying «المتأني»." «تعجَّل» and «استعجل» may be both intransitive and transitive. The object of the hastening is omitted, so you may supply it as an explicit mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e. 'whoever hastens the departure (النَّفْر)', or supply it as a genitive with a preposition, i.e. 'with the departure (بالنفر)', according to its use as intransitive or transitive.

In these verses, from the science of badīʿ (rhetorical embellishment), there is ṭibāq (antithesis), which is the mention of a thing and its opposite, in «تعجَّل» and «تأخر», like His saying: {هُوَ أَضْحَكَ وأبكى} [al-Najm: 43] and {أَمَاتَ وَأَحْيَا} [al-Najm: 43] [Translator's note: the second phrase is in al-Najm: 44 in the standard numbering; the source gives 43]. This is an unusual ṭibāq, in that He made the opposite of «تَعَجَّل» to be «تأخَّر», whereas the opposite of «تعجَّل» is «تأنَّى» and the opposite of «تأخَّر» is «تقدَّم»; but in «تعجَّل» He expressed the concomitant by the thing it entails (al-malzūm for al-lāzim), and in «تأخَّر» the thing entailed by its concomitant (al-lāzim for al-malzūm). And in them, from the science of bayān, there is verbal correspondence (al-muqābala al-lafẓiyya): the one who delays the departure brings an increase in worship, so he has an increase in reward over the one who hastens; yet He said concerning him too: {فَلاَ إِثْمَ عَلَيْهِ}, to correspond to His saying first: {فَمَن تَعَجَّلَ فِي يَوْمَيْنِ فَلاَ إِثْمَ عَلَيْهِ}. It is thus like His saying: {وَجَزَآءُ سَيِّئَةٍ سَيِّئَةٌ مِّثْلُهَا} [al-Shūrā: 40] and {فَمَنِ اعتدى عَلَيْكُمْ فاعتدوا عَلَيْهِ} [al-Baqara: 194].

The majority read {فلا إِثْمَ} with the hamza pronounced (hamzat al-qaṭʿ), according to the original. Sālim ibn ʿAbd Allāh read «فلا اثمَ» with it elided (connecting) and with the alif of «لا» dropped. Its justification is that he lightened the hamza to an in-between pronunciation (bayna bayna), so it came near to a quiescent letter, and he dropped it, likening it to the alif; thus two quiescent letters met: the alif of «لا» and the thāʾ of «أثم», so the alif of «لا» was dropped because of the meeting of the two quiescents. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "Its justification is that when he merged the noun with «لا», he dropped the hamza, likening it to the alif" — meaning that when «لا» was compounded with its noun they became like a single thing, and the hamza resembles the alif, so it is as if two alifs came together, and the second was dropped for that reason; then the alif was dropped for the reason I have mentioned to you.

His saying: {لِمَنِ اتقى} / this prepositional phrase is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ. They differed over that mubtadaʾ according to their difference over what this prepositional phrase is attached to in terms of meaning, not grammatical technique. It is said: in meaning it is attached to His saying {فلا إِثْمَ عَلَيْهِ}, so you supply for it what suits it, i.e. 'the negation of sin is for whoever is God-fearing'. It is said: it is attached to His saying «واذكروا», i.e. 'remembrance is for whoever is God-fearing'. It is said: it is attached to His saying «غفورٌ رحيم», i.e. 'forgiveness is for whoever is God-fearing'. It is said: the implied form is 'safety is for whoever is God-fearing'. It is said: the implied form is 'that choice, and the negation of sin from the one who hastens and the one who delays, is for the sake of the God-fearing pilgrim, so that nothing of either should trouble his heart and he should think that one of them burdens its doer with sin in undertaking it, because the possessor of taqwā is wary and on guard against everything that causes him doubt.' It is said: the implied form is 'that which has been mentioned of the rulings of the Ḥajj and other matters is for whoever is God-fearing, because he is the one who benefits from it, not anyone else', like His saying: {ذَلِكَ خَيْرٌ لِّلَّذِينَ يُرِيدُونَ وَجْهَ الله} [al-Rūm: 38]. These last two implied forms were stated by al-Zamakhsharī. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "Its implied form is: the permissibility of hastening and delaying is for whoever is God-fearing." All of these are close views. It is also possible that «لمَن اتقى» is in the position of accusative (manṣūb), the lām being the lām of cause (taʿlīl), attached to His saying {فلا إِثْمَ عَلَيْهِ}, i.e. 'sin is negated for the sake of the God-fearing one' [Translator's note: the source reads «انتقى» ("was selected"), evidently a slip for «انتفى» ("was negated"); translated per the evident sense]. The object of «اتَّقى» is omitted, i.e. 'feared Allah'; it has come explicitly in the codex of ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd]. And it is said: 'avoided game'.

semin-durr:144-144.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {قَدْ نرى}: Concerning this «قد», some of them said that it turns the imperfect to the sense of the past, and made this verse and its likes among the instances of that, and the poet's saying:
760 - لِقَوْمٍ لعَمْري قد نَرَى أمسِ فيهمُ ... مرابطَ للأمْهارِ والعَكَرِ الدَّهِرْ
(To a people among whom — by my life — we saw yesterday tethering-places for foals, and great herds of camels.)
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«قد نرى»: perhaps We see (rubbamā narā), and its meaning is the frequency of seeing", as in the poet's saying:
761 - قد أَتْرُكُ القِرْنَ مُصَفْراً أناملُه ... كأنَّ أثوابَه مُجَّتْ بفُرْصادِ
(Many a time I leave the opponent with his fingertips turned yellow, as though his garments had been sprinkled with mulberry juice.)
The Shaykh said: "His explanation of this is, on careful examination, self-contradictory, because he explained «قد نرى» by «ربما نرى», and «رُبَّ», on the doctrine of the careful scholars, is only for diminishing the thing in itself or diminishing its like. Then he said: 'and its meaning is the frequency of seeing', which contradicts what «رُبَّ» signifies on the doctrine of the majority. Moreover, this frequency of seeing that he claimed is not indicated by the wording, because «قد» with the imperfect was not set for frequency, whether the past is meant by it or not; the frequency is only understood from what the seeing is connected to, namely the turning about."

His saying: {فِي السمآء}: Concerning what the preposition is attached to there are three views. The first: that it is the maṣdar (verbal noun), namely «تقلُّب». «في» then has two aspects. The first: that it is in its proper sense of place (ẓarfiyya), and this is the clear one. The second: that it is in the sense of «إلى», i.e.: towards the sky; but there is no need for that, for this maṣdar is established as being made transitive with «في»; He, Exalted is He, said: {[لاَ يَغُرَّنَّكَ] تَقَلُّبُ الذين كَفَرُواْ فِي البلاد} [Āl ʿImrān: 196]. The second of the views: that it is «نرى», in which case «في» is in the sense of «مِنْ», i.e.: We see from the sky; and the sky is mentioned — even though He, Exalted is He, is not confined to a direction — by way of honouring. The third: that it is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «وجهِك»; Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned it; it is then attached to something omitted. The maṣdar here is annexed to its agent, and it is not permissible for it to be annexed to its object, because the maṣdar of that is «التقليب». There is no need to omit a muḍāf (annexed noun) from His saying «وجهك», namely "the sight of your face", because that is hardly used; rather He mentioned the face because it is the noblest of the limbs, and it is what the petitioner turns about in his need. It has been said: He used the face as a metonymy for sight, because it is its place.

His saying: {فَلَنُوَلِّيَنَّكَ قِبْلَةً}: The fāʾ here is for causation, and that is clear. This is the answer of an omitted oath, i.e.: so by Allah We shall surely turn you. And «نُوَلِّي» is transitive to two objects: the first is the kāf and the second is «قبلةً»; and the clause «ترضاها» is in the position of accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of «قبلةً». The Shaykh said: "This — meaning «فلنولينك» — indicates that in the preceding clause there is an omitted ḥāl, its implied form being: We see the turning of your face in the sky, seeking a qibla other than the one you are facing."

His saying: {فَوَلِّ وَجْهَكَ شَطْرَ المسجد}: «وَلَّى» is transitive to two objects, one of them «وجهك» and the second «شطرَ». It is also permissible for «شطر» to be accusative as an adverb of place, so that the verb is transitive to one object; this is the view of al-Naḥḥās, and al-Zamakhsharī mentioned nothing else; but the first is clearer. It is sometimes made transitive to the second of them with «إلى».

Al-shaṭr may be in the sense of half of a thing and a part of it, and it may be in the sense of direction and towards. He said:
762 - ألا مَنْ مُبْلِغٌ عني رسولاً ... وما تُغْني الرسالةُ شطرَ عمروِ
(Is there not someone to convey a message from me? — though what use is a message towards ʿAmr?)
And he said:
763 - أقولُ لأُمِّ زِنْباعٍ أَقيمي ... صدورَ العيسِ شَطْرَ بني تميمِ
(I say to Umm Zinbāʿ: Set the breasts of the camels straight towards Banū Tamīm.)
And he said:
764 - وقد أَظَلَّكُمُ مِنْ شَطْرِ ثَغْرِكُمْ ... هَوْلٌ له ظُلَمٌ يَغْشاكُمُ قِطَعا
(From the direction of your frontier a terror has overshadowed you, with darknesses covering you in pieces.)
And Ibn Aḥmar said:
765 - تَعْدُو بنا شَطْرَ نجدٍ وهيَ عاقِدَةٌ ... قد كارب العقدُ من إيقادها الحُقُبا
(She runs with us towards Najd, her tail raised; with her racing, the knot has come near the girth.)
And he said:
766 - وأَطْعَنُ بالرُّمْحِ شَطْرَ المُلو ... كِ. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(And I thrust with the spear towards the kings …)
And he said:
767 - إنَّ العَسِيرَ بها داءٌ مُخامِرُها ... وشَطْرَها نَظَرُ العينين مَحْسورُ
(The unbroken she-camel has a disease clinging to her, and the gaze of the eyes towards her is wearied.)
All that is in the sense of "towards" and "facing". One says: shaṭara, i.e. he went far; and from it is al-shāṭir, the young man far from his neighbours, absent from his home; one says shaṭara shuṭūran; and al-shaṭīr is the distant one, from which "a distant (shaṭīr) dwelling"; and shaṭara ilayhi, i.e. he came towards him. Al-Rāghib said: "The shāṭir came to express the distant one, and its plural is shuṭur «[Translator's note: the source prints «شَطْر».]»; and al-shāṭir is also for one who distances himself from the truth, and its plural is shuṭṭār."

His saying: {حَيْثُ مَا كُنْتُمْ}: In «حيثما» here there are two aspects. The more apparent of them: that it is conditional, and the condition of its being so is the addition of «ما» after it — contrary to al-Farrāʾ —; «كنتم» is in the position of jussive (majzūm) by it, and «فولُّوا» is its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); it is itself accusative as an adverb by «كنتم», so it governs the jussive in it, while it governs the accusative in it, as in {أَيّاً مَّا تَدْعُواْ فَلَهُ الأسمآء الحسنى} [al-Isrāʾ: 110]. Know that «حيث» is among the nouns that are bound to iḍāfa (annexation), so analogy would require that the clause after it be in the position of genitive by it; but an impediment prevented that, namely its having become one of the governors of verbs. The Shaykh said: "«حيث» is an adverb of place annexed to a clause, so it requires the genitive after it; and what requires the genitive does not require the jussive, because the governors of nouns do not govern verbs. Annexation clarifies what is annexed, just as the ṣila clarifies; so it is incompatible with a conditional noun, because a conditional noun is vague. When it is joined to «ما», the sense of annexation departs from it, it is made to contain the sense of condition, an apodosis is given by it, and it becomes one of the governors of verbs."
The second: that it is an adverb not containing the sense of condition, the word making it accusative being His saying «فَوَلُّوا»; Abū al-Baqāʾ said this, and it is nothing, because whenever «ما» is added to it, it must contain the sense of condition. The origin of «وَلُّوا» is «وَلِّيُوا»; the ḍamma was considered heavy on the yāʾ, so it was elided; then two quiescents met, so the first of them, the yāʾ, was elided, and what precedes it was given ḍamma to harmonise with the pronoun; so its measure is «فَعُّوا». His saying «شَطْرَه» has the two views, namely: either a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) or an adverb, as has preceded.

His saying: {أَنَّهُ الحق}: It is possible that «أَنَّ» with its noun and its predicate stands in place of the two objects of «يَعْلَموْن» according to the majority, and in place of one of them according to al-Akhfash, the second being omitted — on [the view] that it is transitive to two; and it is possible that it stands in place of one object, on [the view] that it is in the sense of recognising (al-ʿirfān).
Concerning the pronoun there are three views. The first: it refers back to the turning indicated by His saying «فولُّوا». The second: to the shaṭr. The third: to the Prophet ﷺ; on this there is an iltifāt (shift of person) from addressing him by His saying «فَلَنُوَلِّينَّكَ» to the third person.

His saying: {مِن رَّبِّهِمْ}: It is attached to something omitted, as a ḥāl from «الحق», i.e.: the truth, being from their Lord. And «عمَّا يعملون» was read with the third person, referring back to those who were given the Book, or referring back to the believers, being then an iltifāt from addressing them by His saying «وجوهكم – كنتم»; and with the second person, on referring it to the believers — and this is the apparent one — or to those [given the Book] by way of iltifāt, to stir and invigorate them.

semin-durr:196-196.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {والعمرة للَّهِ}: the majority read «العمرة» in the accusative, conjoined to what precedes it, and «لله» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أتِمُّوا», the lām being the lām of the mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). It may also be attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the Hajj and the ʿUmra, its implied form being: "complete them, they being for Allah." ʿAlī, Ibn Masʿūd and Zayd ibn Thābit read «والعمرةُ» in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), with «لله» as the khabar (predicate), as a new, resumptive clause.

His words: {فَمَا استيسر}: «ما» is a relative in the sense of «الذي»; making it an indefinite noun described [by what follows] is weak. There are three views about it. The first: it is in the position of accusative, i.e. "let him offer" or "let him sacrifice"; this is the school of Thaʿlab. The second — attributed to al-Akhfash —: it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, its implied form being: "then upon him is what is easy." The third: it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being: "then what is obligatory is what is easy." استيسر here has the meaning of the bare يَسَر, as with صَعُب and استصعَبَ, غَنِيَ and استغنى; it may also have the meaning of tafaʿʿala, as in تكبَّر and استكبر, تعظَّم and استعظم. This was discussed at the beginning of the book.

الحَصْر is prevention; hence the king is called الحَصِير, because he is kept from people. Do حُصِر and أُحْصِر have one meaning, or is there a difference between them? There is disagreement among the scholars. Al-Farrāʾ, al-Zajjāj and al-Shaybānī said that they have one meaning, used both for illness and for the enemy, and they recited:
873 - وما هَجْرُ ليلى أَنْ تكونَ تباعَدَتْ ... عليكَ ولا أَنْ أَحْصَرَتْكَ شُغُولُ
(Your staying away from Laylā is not because she has grown distant from you, nor because occupations have held you back.)
Some distinguished them. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "One says أُحْصِر فلانٌ when some matter [prevents] him — fear, illness or incapacity [Translator's note: the source reads «إذا معه أمر», evidently for «إذا منعه أمر»]; Allah the Exalted said: {الذين أُحصِرُواْ فِي سَبِيلِ الله} [al-Baqara: 273], and Ibn Mayyāda said: 'وما هَجْرُ ليلى أن تكون تباعَدَتْ'; and حُصِر when an enemy or a prison confines him. This is what is most frequent in their speech, and both mean prevention in everything, like صَدَّه and أصدَّه; and likewise al-Farrāʾ and al-Shaybānī." Ibn ʿAṭiyya also agreed with him, for he said: "The well-known usage of the language is: أُحْصِر by illness and حُصِر by the enemy." Ibn Fāris reversed this in his «Mujmal», saying: "حُصِر by illness and أُحْصِر by the enemy." Thaʿlab said: "حُصِر, for confinement, is stronger than أُحْصِر." One says حَصِرَ صدرُه, i.e. his chest became constricted; and رجل حَصِر is one who does not divulge his secret. Jarīr said:
874 - وَلَقَد تَكَنَّفني الوُشاةُ فصادَفُوا ... حَصِراً بسرِّك يا أُمَيْمَ حَصُورا
(The slanderers surrounded me, but they found me close-lipped about your secret, O Umaym, utterly reticent.)
الحَصير (the mat) is well known, because its parts hold one another fast; and الحصير is also the king, as has been said, because he is veiled. Labīd said:
875 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... جِنٌّ لدى باب الحصيرِ قِيامُ
(... [men like] jinn standing at the door of the king.)

His words: {مِنَ الهدي}: there are two views. The first: «مِنْ» is partitive, and its position is accusative as a ḥāl of the latent (mustatir) pronoun in «اسْتَيْسر» that refers back to «ما», i.e. "while it is part of the sacrificial animals." The second: «مِنْ» is for explaining the genus, and so it is also attached to an omitted element.

Regarding الهَدْي there are two views. The first: it is the plural of هَدْيَة, as جَدْي is the plural of جَدْيَة of the saddle. The second: it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) put in the place of the object, i.e. "what is offered," and that is why it is used for singular and plural.
Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ said: "I know no parallel for this word."
Mujāhid and al-Zuhrī read «الهَدِيُّ» with a doubled yāʾ, and there are two views about it. The first: it is the plural of هَدِيَّة, like مطيَّة and مطايا, ركيَّة and رَكايا. The second: it is faʿīl in the sense of mafʿūl, as قتيل in the sense of مَقْتُول.

«مَحِلَّه» may be an adverb of place or of time. As far as I know it has only been read with kasra on the ḥāʾ, though linguistically fatḥa on its ḥāʾ is permissible when it is [a noun of] place. Al-Kisāʾī distinguished between them, saying: "The one with kasra is the release from iḥrām, and the one with fatḥa is the place of halting in the case of being prevented."

[His words] {مِنكُم}: there are two views. The first: it is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl of «مريضاً», because it is originally its naʿt (adjective); when it was put before it, it became accusative as a ḥāl; and «مِنْ» is partitive, i.e. "whoever of you is ill." The second, which Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed: it is attached to «مريضاً». The Shaykh said: "This is scarcely intelligible." «مَنْ» may be conditional or relative.

His words: {أَوْ بِهِ أَذًى}: this may be a case of conjoining single words or of conjoining clauses. As for the first, «به» — this preposition and its genitive noun — is conjoined to «مريضاً», which is the khabar of «كان», so it is in the position of accusative, and «أذىً» is made nominative by it as its fāʿil (agent), because a prepositional phrase, when it is supported, makes the agent nominative according to all; so the implied form becomes: "whoever is such that there is harm in his head." As for the second, «به» is a fronted khabar — its position on this view is nominative, while on the first view it was accusative — and «أذىً» is a postponed mubtadaʾ; and this [clause] is in the position of accusative, because it is conjoined to «مريضاً», which occurs as the khabar of «كان». So although it is a clause in form, it is in the position of a single word, since what is conjoined to a single word is a single word. It is not to be said that this has returned to conjoining single words, so that the two views become one, because the difference is clear. They also allowed «أذى» to be conjoined [to a clause] with «كان» implied, since the first «كان» indicates it. In that case there are two possibilities for the noun (ism) of the omitted «كان».
