One: it is the pronoun of the preceding «مَنْ», so «به» is a fronted khabar and «أذى» a postponed mubtadaʾ, and the clause is in the position of accusative as the khabar of the implied «كان». The other: [its noun] is «أذى», and «به» is its khabar, placed before its noun.

Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed «أو به أذى» to be conjoined to «كان», and he parsed «به» as a fronted khabar attached to [the notion of] settledness, and «أذى» as a postponed mubtadaʾ, the hāʾ in «به» referring back to «مَنْ». The Shaykh declared him wrong in this, saying: "Because he had previously stated that «مَنْ» is conditional, and on this assumption it would be wrong, since what is conjoined to the clause of the condition is a condition, and a conditional clause can only be verbal, whereas this, as you see, is a nominal clause according to how he set it out. So how can it be conjoined to the clause of the condition, which must be verbal? If it is said: if we make «مَنْ» a relative, is what he said valid, namely that «به أذى» is conjoined to «كان»? The answer is that it is not valid either, because when the relative «مَنْ» is made to include the meaning of a conditional noun, its ṣila (relative clause) must be a verbal clause or what is equivalent to one." The bāʾ in «به» admits two views. The first: it is for adherence (ilṣāq). The second: it is locative.

His words: {مِّن رَّأْسِهِ}: there are two views. The first: it is in the position of nominative, because it is a naʿt of «أذى», i.e. "a harm that is from his head." The second: it is attached to what «به» is attached to, namely [the notion of] settledness. On both assumptions «مِنْ» is for the beginning of the extent.

His words: {فَفِدْيَةٌ}: regarding its nominative there are three views. The first: it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, i.e. "then upon him is a ransom." The second: it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "then what is obligatory upon him is a ransom." The third: it is the fāʿil of an implied verb, i.e. "then a ransom becomes obligatory upon him." It has been read irregularly «فَفِدْيَةً» in the accusative, which is by an implied verb, i.e. "let him ransom with a ransom." «مِنْ صيام» is in the position of nominative or accusative according to the two readings, as a naʿt of «فدية», and so attached to an omitted element. «أو» is for choice. A verb must be omitted before the fāʾ, its implied form being: "and he shaves [his head], then a ransom."

Al-Ḥasan and al-Zuhrī read «نُسْك» with a sukūn on the sīn, which is a lightening of the form with ḍamma. الأذى is a maṣdar in the sense of الإيذاء, which is pain; one says آذاه يُؤْذِيه إيذاءً وأذىً. So it is as if الأذى were a maṣdar with the additional letters dropped, or a noun of the maṣdar (ism maṣdar), as العطاء is a noun for الإعطاء and النبات for الإنبات.

Regarding النُّسُك there are two views. The first: it is a maṣdar; one says نَسَكَ ينسُك نُسْكاً ونُسُكاً, with ḍamma, and with sukūn as al-Ḥasan read it. The second: it is the plural of نَسِيكة. Ibn al-Aʿrābī said: "النَّسيكة is originally an ingot of silver; worship was named after it because worship resembles an ingot of silver in its purity and freedom from sins; likewise the worshipper was called ناسك, and the sacrificed animal was called نَسِيكة for that reason."

His words: {فَإِذَآ أَمِنتُمْ}: the fāʾ is conjunctive, upon what preceded, and «إذا» is made accusative by the omitted [notion of] settledness, because the implied form is: "then upon him is what is easy," i.e. "then what is easy is settled upon him."

His words: {فَمَن تَمَتَّعَ}: the fāʾ is the apodosis of the condition with «إذا», and the fāʾ in His words «فما استيْسَرَ» is the apodosis of the second condition. We know of no disagreement that a condition with its apodosis may occur as the apodosis of another condition, with the fāʾ. The discussion of «فما استَيْسَرَ» has already been given, which makes repeating it unnecessary.

His words: {فَصِيَامُ}: regarding its nominative there are the same three views mentioned in His words «فَفِدْيَةٌ». It has also been read «فصيامَ» in the accusative, with the implied form "let him fast." The maṣdar is put in construct with its adverb in meaning, while in wording it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) by latitude. «في الحج» is attached to «صيام». Some implied a muḍāf, i.e. "in the time of the Hajj"; some implied two muḍāfs, i.e. "the time of the acts of the Hajj"; and some implied it as an adverb of place, i.e. "the place of the Hajj"; and rulings follow from that.

His words: {وَسَبْعَةٍ}: the majority read «سبعة» in the genitive, conjoined to «ثلاثة». Zayd ibn ʿAlī and Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «وسبعةً» in the accusative, and there are two explanations of it. The first, stated by al-Zamakhsharī: it is conjoined to the position of «ثلاثة», as if it were said "then fasting three [days]," like His words {أَوْ إِطْعَامٌ فِي يَوْمٍ ذِي مَسْغَبَةٍ يَتِيماً} [al-Balad: 14–15]; he means that the noun to which the maṣdar is put in construct is accusative in meaning, as shown by the overt accusative governance of the nunated [maṣdar] in «يتيماً». The second: it is made accusative by an omitted verb, its implied form being "let them fast." The Shaykh said: "This is the only possible view, because conjoining to the position requires the presence of the one that secures [the position]," meaning according to the school of Sībawayh.

His words: {إِذَا رَجَعْتُمْ}: also made accusative by «صيام»; here it is purely adverbial, with no conditional meaning in it. It is not to be said that it follows that one governing word governs two adverbs of time, because that is permissible with conjunction and substitution; and here there is the conjoining of two things to two things: «سبعةٍ» is conjoined to «ثلاثة», and «إذا» is conjoined to «في الحج».

In His words {رَجَعْتُمْ} there are two things: one is an iltifāt (shift of person), and the other is construing according to meaning. As for the iltifāt: before it is «فَمَنْ تَمَتَّعَ... فَمَنْ لَم يَجِدْ», where He used the third-person pronoun referring back to «مَنْ»; had this been put in the arrangement of the first, it would have been said «إذا رجع» with the third-person pronoun. As for construing [according to meaning]: He used a plural pronoun in consideration of the meaning of «مَنْ»; had He observed the wording, He would have used the singular and said «رَجَعَ».

His words: {تِلْكَ عَشَرَةٌ}: mubtadaʾ and khabar. What is pointed to is the seven and the three. The tamyīz (specification) of the seven and the ten is omitted because it is known. He kept the feminine tāʾ in the number while omitting the tamyīz, which is the better of the two usages; dropping the tāʾ is permissible in that case. In the ḥadīth: "and follows it with six of Shawwāl," and al-Kisāʾī related: "We fasted five of the month."

Regarding His words {تِلْكَ عَشَرَةٌ} — while it is known that three and seven are ten — there are many views of the scholars of meanings. Among them is the saying of Ibn ʿArafa: "When the Arabs mention two numbers, their way is to total them." Al-Zamakhsharī commended this view, saying: "The benefit of the summing-up (al-fadhlaka) in every calculation is that the number be known in total as it is known in detail, so that one is doubly secure and the knowledge is confirmed; and among their proverbs is 'Two knowings are better than one knowing.'" Ibn ʿArafa said: "The Arabs do this only because they have little knowledge of arithmetic; and it has come [in the ḥadīth]: 'We do not reckon and we do not write.'" This occurs in their poetry. Al-Nābigha said:
876 - تَوَهَّمْتُ آياتٍ لها فَعَرَفَتُها ... لستةِ أيامٍ وذا العامُ سابعُ
(I made out traces of her abode and recognised them after six years — and this year is the seventh.)
Al-Farazdaq said:
877 - ثلاثٌ واثنتان فَهُنَّ خَمْسٌ ... وسادسةٌ تَميلُ إلى شَمَام
(Three and two, and they are five, and a sixth leaning toward Shamām.)
Al-Aʿshā said:
878 - ثلاثٌ بالغَدَاةِ فَهُنَّ حَسْبي ... وسِتٌّ حين يُدْرِكُني العِشاءُ
فذلك تِسْعَةٌ في اليومِ رِيِّي ... وشُرْبُ المرءِ فَوْقَ الرَّيِّ داءُ
(Three in the morning, and they suffice me, and six when evening overtakes me; that is nine a day, my fill — and a man's drinking beyond his fill is a sickness.)
Another said:
879 - فَسِرْتُ إليهمُ عِشْرِينَ شهراً ... وأربعةً فذلك حِجَّتانِ
(I journeyed to them twenty months and four — that makes two years.)
It is reported from al-Mubarrad: "«فتلك عشَرَةٌ»: three in the Hajj and seven when [you return]; so there is fronting and postponing." Such a thing is not authentic from him. Ibn al-Bādhish said: "«عشرة» was brought as a preparation for the predicate after it, not as the independent khabar carrying the benefit of the predication, as you say 'Zayd is a righteous man'" — meaning that what is intended is informing of righteousness, and "man" is brought as a preparation, since it is known that he is a man. Al-Zajjāj said: "He combined the two numbers because it might be supposed that what is upon him is three or seven, since the wāw may stand in place of «أو» — and of this is {مثنى وَثُلاَثَ وَرُبَاعَ} [al-Nisāʾ: 3] — so He removed the possibility of choice." This works only according to the Kufans, for they put the wāw in place of «أو». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The wāw may come for permission, in your saying 'Sit with al-Ḥasan [and] Ibn Sīrīn'" [Translator's note: so in the source, without a conjunction; the usual example is «جالس الحسن أو ابن سيرين»] — "do you not see that if he sat with both together or with one of them he would be complying? So it was summed up to negate the supposition of permission." The Shaykh said: "There is an objection to this, because permission is not to be supposed, since the context is the context of obligation, which is incompatible with permission but not incompatible with choice, for choice occurs among obligations; the grammarians have mentioned the difference between choice and permission."

His words: {ذلك لِمَن}: «ذلك» is a mubtadaʾ and the prepositional phrase after it is the khabar. Regarding the lām there are two views. The first: it is in its usual sense, i.e. "that is incumbent for whoever." The second: it is in the sense of «على» (upon), as in His words {أُولَئِكَ عَلَيْهِمْ لَعْنَةُ الله} [al-Baqara: 161]; there is no need for this. «مَنْ» may be a relative or an indefinite described [by what follows]. «حاضري» is the khabar of «يكن», its nūn dropped because of the genitive construct. «شديدُ العقاب» is a case of putting the ṣifa mushabbaha (adjective resembling the participle) in construct with what it makes nominative. It has already been said that the genitive construct arises only from the accusative, and the accusative and the construct are more emphatic than the nominative, because in them the adjective is attributed to the one described and then the one to whom it really belongs is mentioned, whereas in the nominative there is only its attribution to the one to whom it really belongs, without attribution to the one described.

semin-durr:166-166.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {إِذْ تَبَرَّأَ}: there are three views on «إذْ». The first: that it is a badal (substitute) from «إذ يَرَوْن». The second: that it is accusative by His saying «شديدُ العذاب». The third — and it is the weakest of them —: that it is governed by an implied «اذكر» (remember) [Translator's note: the source prints «لا ذكر», evidently for «لاذكر», i.e. "by «اذكر»"]. «تَبَرَّأ» is in the position of the genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it. «التبرُّؤ» is becoming free and separating; from it is «بَرِئْتُ من الدَّيْن» (I became free of the debt). Its verification was given at His saying: {إلى بَارِئِكُمْ} [al-Baqara: 54]. The majority put «اتُّبِعوا», in the passive, before «اتَّبعوا», in the active; Mujāhid read the reverse. Both are clear, except that the reading of the majority occurs more often in the Qur'an.

His saying: {وَرَأَوُاْ العذاب}: this clause admits two views. The more evident of them: that it is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it, and so falls within the scope of the adverb, its implied form being: "when those who were followed disowned, and when they saw". The second: that the wāw is for the ḥāl (circumstantial), the clause after it being circumstantial, with «قد» implied with it; the governor of this ḥāl is «تَبَرَّأ», i.e.: they disowned while seeing the punishment.

His saying: {وَتَقَطَّعَتْ}: the wāw may be conjunctive or circumstantial. If it is conjunctive, did it conjoin «تَقَطَّعَتْ» to «تَبَرَّأ», with His saying «ورأوا» being a ḥāl — and this is the choice of al-Zamakhsharī — or did it conjoin it to «رأوا»? And if it is circumstantial, is it a second ḥāl of «الذين», or a ḥāl of the pronoun in «رَأوا»? It is then an overlapping (mutadākhila) ḥāl, if we make «ورأوا» a ḥāl.

The bāʾ in «بهم» has four views. The first: that it is for the ḥāl, i.e.: the ties were severed while connected with them, as in «خَرَج بثيابه» (he went out with his clothes on). The second: that it is for making transitive, i.e.: the ties severed them, as you say «تَفَرَّقَتْ بهم الطرقُ» (the roads dispersed them), i.e. scattered them. The third: that it is causal, i.e.: because of their unbelief the ties by which they hoped for salvation were severed. The fourth: that it means «عن», i.e.: were severed from them.

«الأسباب» are the connections between them, and it is figurative, for «السبب» is originally a rope; then it was applied to everything by which one reaches something, whether concrete or abstract. «الأسباب» is also applied to events. Zuhayr said:
804 - ومَنْ هابَ أسبابُ المنايا يَنَلْنَه ... ولو نالَ أسبابَ السماءِ بسُلَّمِ
(Whoever fears the causes of death, they will reach him, even if he reached the tracts of the sky with a ladder.)

Here is found one of the kinds of rhetorical embellishment (badīʿ), namely tarṣīʿ (parallel rhyming), which consists in giving speech rhyming cadences. It is here in two places. One: {اتبعوا مِنَ الذين اتبعوا}; for that reason He omitted the returning pronoun of the first relative noun and did not say «من الذين اتَّبعوهم», because that [effect] would be lost. The second: {وَرَأَوُاْ العذاب وَتَقَطَّعَتْ بِهِمُ الأسباب}. It is frequent in the Qur'an: {إِلاَّ أَن تُغْمِضُواْ فِيهِ} [al-Baqara: 73] [Translator's note: so in the source; the words quoted are from al-Baqara 267].

semin-durr:167-167.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {فَنَتَبَرَّأَ مِنْهُمْ}: accusative after the fāʾ by an implied «أَنْ», in answer to the wish with whose meaning «لو» has been imbued; for that reason it was answered with the answer of «ليت», as in His saying: «يا ليتني كنتُ معهم فأفوز». When it is imbued with the meaning of wishing, is it the «لو» of impossibility (imtināʿiyya) that requires an answer, or does it need no answer? The correct view is that it needs an answer, and it is implied in the verse, its implied form being: "we would disown [them]", and the like. It is also said: «لو» in this verse and its parallels is [the particle] for what would have occurred upon the occurrence of something else, and there is no meaning of wishing in it; the verb is accusative by an implied «أَنْ» on the interpretation of conjoining a noun to a noun, namely «كَرَّة», the implied form being: "if we had a return and a disowning". It is then of the type of his saying:
805 - لَلُبْسُ عباءةٍ وتَقَرَّ عيني ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Wearing a cloak, with my eye being content…)
and the answer of «لو» is likewise omitted, as stated.

Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "«فنتبرأ» is accusative by an implied «أنْ», its implied form being: if only we could return and disown." He resolved «كرة» into his saying «أَنْ نَرْجِعَ», because it has its meaning, and that is close; except that the grammarians interpret the accusative verb as a maṣdar (verbal noun) so as to conjoin it to the noun before it, and leave the noun as it is. That is because it may be an explicit noun that is not a maṣdar, as in «لولا زيدٌ ويخرجَ لأكرمتُك» (were it not for Zayd and his going out, I would have honoured you), where it cannot be interpreted as a maṣdar-forming particle and a verb.

The one who holds that the «لو» of wishing has no answer adduced the poet's saying:
806 - فلو نَبْشُ المقابرِ عن كُلَيْبٍ ... فَتُخْبَر بالذَّنائِبِ أيُّ زُورِ
(If only the graves could be dug open from over Kulayb, so that he might be told at al-Dhanāʾib what a [great] slaughter [there was]…)
This is not valid, for its answer is in the verse after it, namely his saying:
807 - بيومِ الشَّعْثَمَيْنِ لقَرَّ عيناً ... وكيف لقاءُ مَنْ تحتَ القبورِ
(…on the day of the two Shaʿthams, he would be content of eye; but how can one meet those beneath the graves?)
This holder of the view also adduced that «أنَّ» takes fatḥa after «لو» just as it takes fatḥa after «ليت», as in his saying:
808 - يا ليتَ أنَّا ضَمَّنا سَفينَهْ ... حتَّى يعودَ البحرُ كَيَّنُونَهْ
(Would that a ship held us together until the sea became as it was.)

Here there is a point one should take note of: the grammarians said: "Wherever the imperfect is put in the accusative by an implied «أَنْ» after the fāʾ, if the fāʾ is dropped it becomes jussive, except in negation." [And] this place too ought to be added, so that one says: "and except in the answer to a wish expressed by «لو»", for the imperfect in it is put in the accusative by an implied «أَنْ» after the fāʾ that comes as its answer, and yet if this fāʾ were dropped it would not become jussive. The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "The reason for that is that it is treated on the model of the particle of wishing, namely «ليت»; and the jussive in the answer to «ليت» is only because it contains the meaning of a condition, or because it indicates that one is omitted, according to the two views. So «لو» became a branch of a branch, and that was weakened in it."

His saying «كما»: the position of the kāf is accusative: either as a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar, i.e.: a disowning like their disowning; or as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun of the omitted definite maṣdar, i.e.: we disown it — meaning the disowning — resembling their disowning, as has been established more than once. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "The kāf in His saying «كما» is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt, either of a maṣdar or of a ḥāl, its implied form being: disowning as…". The Shaykh said: "As for his saying 'of a ḥāl, its implied form being: disowning as…', it is not clear, because «ما» is maṣdar-forming, so the kāf entering upon it became an attribute of actions, while 'disowning' (mutabarriʾīn) is an attribute of persons; so how can it be described with attributes of actions?" He said: "Moreover there is no need to assume this ḥāl, because it would then be a corroborative (muʾakkida) ḥāl, which is contrary to the norm; and moreover omission is incompatible with what is corroborative, because emphasis strengthens it and omission contradicts it."

His saying: {كَذَلِكَ يُرِيهِمُ}: there are two views on this kāf. One: that its position is accusative, either as a naʿt of an omitted maṣdar or as a ḥāl from the definite maṣdar, i.e.: He shows them a showing like that, or gathers them a gathering like that, or requites them a requital like that, or shows them the showing resembling that, and the like. The second: that its position is nominative as the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e.: the matter is like that, or their gathering is like that — said by Abū al-Baqāʾ. The Shaykh said: "It is weak, because it requires the kāf to be redundant and a mubtadaʾ to be omitted, both of which are contrary to the norm." The reference of «ذلك» is to His showing them those terrors; the implied form being: like His showing them the terrors, Allah will show them their deeds as regrets. It is also said: the reference is to their disowning one another.

Seeing here admits two views. One: that it is visual, so that it becomes transitive to two objects by the transferring hamza, the first of them being the pronoun and the second «أعمالَهم»; on this «حسراتٍ» is a ḥāl from «أعمالهم». The second: that it is mental, so that it becomes transitive to three objects, the third of them being «حسرات». «عليهم» admits two views: that it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «حسراتٍ», because «يَحْسَر» is made transitive with «على», and there is an omitted muḍāf, i.e.: over their negligence. The second: that it is attached to an omitted element, because it is a naʿt of «حَسَرات», and so it is in the position of the accusative for being a naʿt of an accusative.

«الكَرَّة» is return; its verb is «كَرَّ يَكُرُّ كَرَّاً». [The poet] said:
809 - أَكُرُّ على الكتيبةِ لا أُبالي ... أفيها كانَ حَتْفِي أَمْ سِواها
(I charge again at the squadron, not caring whether my death lies in it or elsewhere.)
«الحسرة» is intense regret; it is the heart's pain at being cut off from what it hopes for. Its derivation is either from their saying «بعيرٌ حَسِير», i.e. [a camel] whose strength is exhausted, or from «الحَسْر», which is uncovering.

semin-durr:231-231.t:
The words of the Exalted: {وَإِذَا طَلَّقْتُمُ}: a conditional whose apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is «فَأَمْسِكُوهُنَّ», and His words «فبَلَغْنَ» are conjoined to the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). Al-bulūgh (reaching) is arriving at a thing: balaghahu, yablughuhu, bulūghan. Imruʾ al-Qays said:
981 - ومَجْرٍ كَغُلاَّنِ الأُنَيْعِمِ بالِغٍ ... ديارَ العدوِّ ذي زُهاءٍ وَأَرْكَانِ
(A huge army, like the thickets of al-Unayʿim, reaching the enemy's lands, vast in number and with mighty columns.)
From it come al-bulgha and al-balāgh, a name for that by which one gets by (what suffices to reach one's need).

His words: {بِمَعْرُوفٍ} are in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and its owner is either the agent, i.e. "accompanied by what is right", or the object, i.e. "they (fem.) being accompanied by what is right".

His words: {ضِرَاراً} has two aspects. The more evident of them is that it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. "for the sake of harming". The second: that it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the place of a ḥāl, i.e. "while you are harming them".

His words: {وَمَن يَفْعَلْ ذَلِكَ}: Abū al-Ḥārith, transmitting from al-Kisāʾī, assimilated (idghām) the lām into the dhāl when the verb is jussive (majzūm), as in this verse. It occurs in seven places in the Quran: {وَمَن يَفْعَلْ ذَلِكَ فَقَدْ ظَلَمَ نَفْسَهُ} in two places, {وَمَن يَفْعَلْ ذلك فَلَيْسَ مِنَ الله فِي شَيْءِ} [Āl ʿImrān: 28], {وَمَن يَفْعَلْ ذلك عُدْوَاناً وَظُلْماً} [al-Nisāʾ: 30], {وَمَن يَفْعَلْ ذلك ابتغآء مَرْضَاتِ الله} [al-Nisāʾ: 114], {وَمَن يَفْعَلْ ذلك يَلْقَ أَثَاماً} [al-Furqān: 68], {وَمَن يَفْعَلْ ذَلِكَ فأولئك هُمُ الخاسرون} [al-Munāfiqūn: 9]. This was permissible because their points of articulation are close and they share in openness (infitāḥ), lowness (istifāl) and voicing (jahr). He guarded against the non-jussive, such as "يفعلُ ذلك". A group impugned this transmission and said: it is not authentic from al-Kisāʾī because it contradicts his principles; but this is not correct.

His words: {لِّتَعْتَدُواْ}: this is the lām of cause, and Abū al-Baqāʾ permitted "that it be the lām of consequence, i.e. of outcome (al-ṣayrūra)". Concerning what it is attached to (mutaʿallaq) there are two aspects. One of them: that it is «لا تُمْسِكُوهُنَّ». The second: that it is the maṣdar (ضِرَاراً) if we say that it is a ḥāl; and if we say it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi, it is attached to it only, and it is then a cause of the cause, just as you say: "I beat my son as discipline so that he may benefit": the discipline is the cause of the beating and the benefit is the cause of the discipline; and in this case it is not permissible for it to be attached to «لا تُمْسِكُوهن». «تَعْتَدُوا» is accusative (manṣūb) by an implied «أنْ», and it together with what follows it is in the position of the genitive by this lām, as its establishment has preceded more than once. The origin of «تَعْتَدُوا» is taʿtadiyuwā, and it underwent the weak-letter change like its counterparts; that is not hidden from what has preceded.

His words: {عَلَيْكُمْ} admits two aspects. One of them: that it is attached to «النعمة» itself if what is meant by it is the act of bestowing (al-inʿām), because it is a noun of the maṣdar (ism maṣdar), like nabāt from anbata; and the tāʾ of the feminine does not prevent this maṣdar from governing, because it is built upon it, as in his words:
982 - فلولا رجاءُ النصرِ منك ورهبةٌ ... عقابَكَ قد كانوا لنا كالموارِدِ
(Were it not for hope of help from you and dread of your punishment, they would have been to us like watering-places [i.e. they would have trampled us].)
So he made «رهبةٌ» govern «عقابك». What is to be avoided is only that a maṣdar not built upon it (the tāʾ) should govern, such as ḍarb and ḍarba; for that reason people offered an excuse for his words:
983 - يُحايي به الجَلْدُ الذي هو حازِمٌ ... بضربةِ كَفَّيْهِ المَلاَ وهْوَ راكِبُ
(By it the hardy, resolute man keeps himself alive, striking with his two palms the mirage while he rides.)
namely that al-malā, which is the mirage, is accusative by an implied verb, not by «ضربة». The second: that it is attached to an omitted element, as a ḥāl from «نعمة», if what is meant by it is the thing bestowed. On the first, the Divine Name is in the position of the nominative, because the maṣdar puts it in the nominative virtually, since it is its agent; on the second it is genitive both in form and virtually.

His words: {وَمَآ أَنزَلَ عَلَيْكُمْ}: «ما» admits two aspects. One of them: that it is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to «نعمة», i.e. "remember His favour and what was sent down upon you". On this view His words «يَعِظُكُم» are a ḥāl, and concerning its owner there are three aspects. The first: that it is the agent of «أنزل», which is the Name of Allah the Exalted, i.e. "He sent it down admonishing you by it". The second: that it is «ما», the relative noun, and the governor of the ḥāl is "remember" (اذكروا). The third: that it is the omitted referent pronoun going back to «ما», i.e. "and what He sent down, being something by which admonition is given"; so the governor of the ḥāl on this view and on the first view is «أَنْزَل».
The second of the two aspects of «ما»: that it is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «يَعِظُكُم» is then in the position of the nominative as khabar (predicate) of this mubtadaʾ, i.e. "and what was sent down upon you is that by which admonition is given". The first of the two aspects is stronger and better.

His words: {عَلَيْكُمْ} is attached to «أَنْزَلَ». And «من الكتاب» is attached to an omitted element because it is a ḥāl, and concerning its owner there are two aspects. One of them: that it is «ما», the relative noun. The second: that it is its omitted referent pronoun, since the implied form is: "He sent it down while it is from the Book". «مِنْ» may be partitive, or it may be for explaining the genus, according to those who hold that (meaning exists). The pronoun in «به» goes back to «ما», the relative noun.

semin-durr:232-232.t:
The words of the Exalted: {وَإِذَا طَلَّقْتُمُ}: the verse. It is like the one before it, except that the address in «طَلَّقتم» is to the husbands, and in «فلا تعضُلُوهُنَّ» to the guardians. It is also said: the address in both is to the guardians; and this is far-fetched, in that divorce is not attributed to them except by a remote figure of speech (majāz), namely that their causing the divorce is made a divorce. It is also said: the address in both is to the husbands, and al-ʿaḍl (preventing) is attributed to them because that is what they used to do: they would divorce and then refuse to let the woman marry after them, out of wrongdoing and coercion.

His words: {أَزْوَاجَهُنَّ} is figurative (majāz), because if the divorcers are meant, then calling them that is in consideration of what they had been; and if others are meant, whom the women wish to marry, then it is in consideration of what they will become. The fāʾ [in] «فلا تَعْضُلُوهُنَّ» is the apodosis of «إذا».
Al-ʿaḍl: it is said it is prevention. From it: "ʿaḍala amatahu" — he prevented his slave-woman from marrying; yaʿḍiluhā, with kasra and ḍamma on the ʿayn. Ibn Harma said:
984 - وإنَّ قصائدي لك فاصطَنِعْني ... كرائمُ قد عُضِلْنَ عن النِّكاحِ
(My odes to you — so take me into your favour — are noble maidens who have been barred from marriage.)
[Translator's note: the printed text has "ابن هرمز" (Ibn Hurmuz); the poet is usually identified as Ibn Harma. The name is translated as given in sense; the Arabic reads Ibn Hurmuz.]
And he said:
985 - ونحنُ عَضَلْنا بالرماحِ نساءَنا ... وما فيكُمُ عن حُرْمَةِ اللهِ عاضِلُ
(We protected our women with spears, while among you there is none who prevents [anyone] from violating Allah's sanctity.)
From it: "dajāja muʿḍil", i.e. a hen whose egg is held back (stuck). It is also said: its origin is narrowness. Aws said:
986 - تَرى الأرضَ منَّا بالفضاءِ مريضةً ... مُعَضَّلَةً منا بجيشٍ عَرَمْرم
(You see the land in the open country sick because of us, made narrow by us with a huge army.)
i.e. narrow because of them. And "ʿaḍalat al-marʾa", i.e. her child stuck in her womb; and "dāʾ ʿuḍāl", i.e. a disease narrow in remedy (incurable). Laylā al-Akhyaliyya said:
987 - شَفاهَا من الداءِ العُضالِ الذي بها ... غلامٌ إذا هَزَّ القَناةَ شَفاها
(She was cured of the grievous disease within her by a young man who, when he brandishes the spear, cures her.)
And al-muʿḍilāt are difficult problems, because of the narrowness of understanding them. Al-Shāfiʿī said:
988 - إذا المُعْضِلاَتُ تَصَدَّيْنَنِي ... كَشَفْتُ حقائقَها بالنَّظَرْ
(When difficult problems confront me, I uncover their realities by reflection.)

His words: {أَن يَنكِحْنَ} has two aspects. One of them: that it is a badal (substitute) from the accusative pronoun in «تَعْضُلوهُنَّ», a substitute of inclusion (badal ishtimāl), so it is in the position of the accusative, i.e. "do not prevent their marrying". The second: that it is by dropping the preposition, which is either «مِنْ» or «عَنْ»; so in the position of «أَنْ» there are the two well-known aspects, I mean the school of Sībawayh and the school of al-Khalīl. «يَنْكِحْنَ» is the imperfect of the triliteral nakaḥa, and its analogy would have been that its ʿayn be with fatḥa, because its lām is a guttural letter.

His words: {إِذَا تَرَاضَوْاْ}: concerning what puts this adverb in the accusative there are two aspects. One of them: «ينكِحْنَ», i.e. "that they marry at the time of mutual agreement". The second: that it is «تعضُلوهنَّ», i.e. "do not prevent them at the time of mutual agreement". The first is more evident. «إذا» here is purely adverbial. The pronoun in «تراضَوا» may go back to the guardians and the husbands, or to the husbands and wives, and then it is a case of giving the masculine precedence over the feminine (taghlīb).

His words: {بَيْنَهُمْ} is a figurative adverb of place, and what puts it in the accusative is «تراضَوا».

His words: {بالمعروف} has four aspects. The first of them: that it is attached to «تراضَوا», i.e. they agree on what is good in religion and decency. The second: that it is attached to «يَنْكِحْنَ», so «ينكِحْنَ» is what puts the adverb «إذا» in the accusative, and also for this preposition (governs it). The third: that it is attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of «تراضَوا».
The fourth: that it is the naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar indicated by the verb, i.e. "a mutual agreement that is with what is right".

His words: {ذلك} is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «يُوعظ» together with what follows it is its khabar (predicate). The one addressed is either the Messenger, upon him be peace, or every hearer — and for that reason the kāf indicating a single person was brought — or the group, which is the evident view; so «ذلك» is then in the sense of «ذلكم», and for that reason He said after it: «منكم».
«مَنْ كان» is in the position of the nominative because it stands in place of the agent (nāʾib fāʿil). In «كان» is its noun, going back to «مَنْ», and «يؤمِنُ» is in the position of the accusative as its khabar. «منكم» is either attached to «كان», according to those who hold that it governs adverbs and their like, or to an omitted element as a ḥāl from the agent of «يؤمن». He used the demonstrative for the distant to magnify what is pointed to, since what is pointed to is near, namely the ruling mentioned concerning al-ʿaḍl. The alif of «أزكى» derives from a wāw.

His words: {ذلكم} is attached to an omitted element because it is an adjective of «أَزْكى», so it is in the position of the nominative. [Translator's note: so in the source; the attached element described here is evidently «لكم» in «ذلكم أزكى لكم», not «ذلكم».] His words «وَأَطْهَرُ», i.e. "for you"; and that over which preference is given is omitted because it is known, i.e. "than al-ʿaḍl".

semin-durr:246-246.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {مِن بني}: there are two views on it. The first: that it is the ṣila (relative clause) of «الملأ», according to the school of the Kufans, because they treat a noun made definite by «أل» as a relative noun, and they cite:
1018 - لَعَمْرِي لأنتَ البيتُ أُكَرِمُ أهلَه ... وأَقْعُدُ في أفنائِهِ بالأصائِلِ
(By my life, you are the house whose people I honour, and in whose courtyards I sit in the late afternoons.)
So «البيت» is a relative noun; on this view this preposition-phrase has no grammatical position. The second: that it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted element, being a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «الملأ», and «مِنْ» is partitive, i.e. in the state of their being some of the Children of Israel.
«الملأ»: the nobles. They were so called because they fill (yamlaʾūn) the eyes with awe, [or the assemblies when they are present], or because they are capable (malīʾūn) of what they are needed for. Al-Farrāʾ said: "«الملأ» [means the men everywhere in the Quran, and likewise] «القوم», «الرهط» and «النفر»." It is pluralised as «أَمْلاء»; the poet said:
1019 - وقالَ لها الأملاءُ من كلِّ مَعْشَرٍ ... وخيرُ أقاويل الرجالِ سديدُها
(The notables of every clan said to her — and the best of men's sayings is the most correct of them.)
It is a collective noun (ism jamʿ) that has no singular from its own root, like «القوم» and «الرهط».
And {مِن بَعْدِ موسى} is attached to what the first preposition-phrase is attached to, namely the notion of "being" (al-istiqrār). The fact that the two prepositions are identical in wording does no harm, because they differ in meaning: the first is partitive and the second marks the beginning of the extent (ibtidāʾ al-ghāya). Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "«مِنْ بعدِ» is attached to the first preposition-phrase, or to what the first is attached to" — by "the first" he means «من بني» — and he made it the governing element of «مِنْ بعد» because of the notion of "being" it contains; that is why he attributed government to it. This is according to the opinion of some, who attribute government to an adverb or a preposition-phrase that occurs as a khabar (predicate), naʿt (adjective), ḥāl or ṣila; so in something like «زيدٌ في الدار أبوه» they say «أبوه» is a fāʿil (agent) of the preposition-phrase. The precise view is that it is the agent of the "being" to which the preposition-phrase is attached, and that is the second view. Abū al-Baqāʾ also assumed an omitted muḍāf, its implied form being "from after the death of Moses", so that the meaning would be sound thereby.

His words: {إِذْ قَالُواْ}: as for the governing element of this adverb, they allowed two views. The first: that it is what governs «مِنْ بعد», because it is a badal (substitute) from it, since both are times — said by Abū al-Baqāʾ. The second: that it is «ألم تر». Neither is correct. As for the first, it is wrong for two reasons, one relating to the wording and the other to the meaning. As for the one relating to the wording: it would be on the assumption of repeating «مِنْ», and «إذ» is not put in the genitive by «مِنْ». The second: even if «إذ» were among the adverbs that are put in the genitive by «من», such as «وقت» and «حين», that would still not be correct, because the governing element of «مِنْ بعد» is omitted, for it is a ḥāl whose implied form is "being from after"; and if you said: "being from the time when they said to a prophet of theirs, 'Raise up for us a king'", this meaning would not be sound. As for the second, it is because it was stated earlier that the meaning of «ألم تر» is a confirmation of the negation, and the meaning is: "Has your knowledge not reached…", or "You have indeed looked at the chiefs"; and neither his knowledge reaching them nor his looking at them took place at the time of their saying that. And if it is not an adverb of time for the reaching or the looking, how can it be governed by both of them or by either one of them?
Since these two views are void, it must have a governing element by which the meaning is sound, and that is omitted, its implied form being: "Have you not seen the story of the chiefs", or "the account of the chiefs", or something of that meaning. That is because one does not marvel at entities themselves; one marvels only at what they do. So the meaning becomes: "Have you not seen what happened to the chiefs of the Children of Israel…" to the end of it. The governing element is that genitive noun, and it is not correct except with it, for the reason stated above.

His words: {لِنَبِيٍّ} is attached to «قالوا», and the lām in it is the lām of communication (al-tablīgh). «لهم» is attached to an omitted element because it is a naʿt of «نبي», and its position is genitive. «ابعَثْ» and what falls within its scope is in the position of an accusative as the object of the saying. As for «لنا», the apparent view is that it is attached to «ابعَثْ», and the lām is causal, i.e. "for our sake".

His words: {نُّقَاتِلْ}: the majority read it with nūn and in the jussive, as the answer to the imperative. It was also read with yāʾ and in the jussive, on the same basis as above. Ibn Abī ʿAbla read it with yāʾ and the lām in the nominative, as a naʿt of «ملكاً», so its position is accusative. It was also read with nūn and the lām in the nominative, as a ḥāl of «لنا», so its position is likewise accusative, i.e. "raise him up for us, intending to fight"; or as a resumptive answer to an implied question, as though he said to them: "What will you do with the king?" and they said: "We will fight."

His words: {هَلْ عَسَيْتُمْ}: «عسى» and its subject (ism), and its predicate is {أَلاَّ تُقَاتِلُواْ}, the conditional clause being parenthetical between them, and its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) omitted because it is indicated. This is like its intervening in His words: {وَإِنَّآ إِن شَآءَ الله لَمُهْتَدُونَ} [al-Baqara: 70]. This is according to the opinion of those who make «عسى» enter upon a subject and predicate, and say that «أَنْ» is redundant (zāʾida) so that a meaning (an abstract notion) is not predicated of a concrete entity. As for those who hold that it carries the meaning of a transitive verb, they say: «عَسَيْتم» is a verb and its agent, and «أَنْ» with what follows it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), its implied form being "Have you come near to not fighting?"; so for him it is not one of the abrogating particles (al-nawāsikh). The first is the well-known view.
Nāfiʿ read «عَسِيْتُم» here and in [Sūrat] al-Qitāl with kasra on the sīn. This is a dialect form with the agent's tāʾ in all cases, and with «نا» and with the nūn of the feminine plural, e.g. «عَسِينا» and «عَسِين»; it is the dialect of the Hijaz. For this reason whoever said "«عسى» takes kasra with a pronoun" and stated it without qualification erred; rather, he should have restricted it to what I have mentioned, since one never says «الزيدان عَسِيا» or «الزيدون عَسِيوا» with kasra at all.
Al-Fārisī said: "The justification of the kasra is the Arabs' saying «هو عَسٍ بكذا» ("he is apt to do such-and-such"), like «حَرٍ» and «شَجٍ». The patterns faʿala and faʿila have both occurred in words like «نَقَم» and «نَقِم»; likewise «عَسَيْتُ» and «عَسِيْتُ». If the verb is attributed to an overt noun, then the analogy of «عَسِيتم» — i.e. with kasra — would be to say «عَسِيَ زيدٌ», like «رَضِي زيدٌ». If that is said, then it is the analogy; and if it is not said, it is permissible to take both dialects and use one in place of the other, as has been done elsewhere." The apparent sense of this wording is that it is permissible to give its sīn kasra with an overt noun by analogy with the pronoun, while other grammarians forbid that even with a pronoun absolutely; but no attention is paid to [the latter], because [the kasra] has come down by mass transmission (mutawātir). The apparent sense of his words "the Arabs' saying «عسٍ»" is that its active participle has been heard from them; Abū al-Baqāʾ likewise reported this from Ibn al-Aʿrābī. Yet the grammarians have stated explicitly that «عسى» is not inflected (lā tataṣarraf).
Know that what «عسى» signifies is performative (inshāʾ), because it expresses hope or apprehension. On this basis, how can «هل», which requires a question, enter upon it? The answer is that the speech is construed according to the meaning. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The meaning is: 'Have you come near to not fighting?', i.e. 'Is the matter as I expect, that you will not fight?' He meant to say: 'You are apt not to fight', meaning 'I expect your cowardice about fighting', so he brought in «هل», asking about what he expected and supposed; by the question he meant confirmation (al-taqrīr), and it is established that what was expected comes to pass and that he was right in his expectation, like the words of Allah the Exalted: {هَلْ أتى عَلَى الإنسان} [al-Insān: 1], whose meaning is confirmation." This is among the finest of statements, and finer than the statement of those who claimed that it is declarative (khabar), not performative, citing as evidence the entry of the question upon it, and its occurring as the predicate of «إنّ» in the poet's words:
1020 - لا تُكْثِرَنْ إني عَسَيْتُ صائماً ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Do not go on at length; I am likely to be fasting…)
There is no evidence in this, because it is on the assumption of an implied "saying", like the poet's words:
1021 - إنَّ الذين قَتَلْتُمْ أمسِ سيِّدَهمْ ... لا تَحْسَبُوا ليلَهم عن ليلكِم ناما
(Those whose chief you killed yesterday — do not think their night has slept away from your night.)
For that reason relative nouns are not given a ṣila with it, contrary to Hishām.

His words: {وَمَا لَنَآ أَلاَّ نُقَاتِلَ}: this wāw links this speech to what precedes it; if it were omitted it would be possible for it to be cut off from what precedes. «ما» is in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and its meaning is interrogative, a question of disapproval (istifhām inkār). «لنا» is in the position of a nominative as the khabar of «ما».
As for «ألاَّ نقاتِلَ», there are three views on it. The most evident: that it is on the omission of the preposition, the implied form being "And what is with us in that we should not fight", i.e. in abandoning fighting; then «في» was omitted with «أَنْ», and so the well-known disagreement between al-Khalīl and Sībawayh applies to it: is it in the position of a genitive or an accusative? This preposition is attached to the preposition-phrase itself, i.e. «لنا», or to what that is attached to, according to what was said above about {مِن بَعْدِ موسى}. The second: the school of al-Akhfash, that «أَنْ» is redundant; its governing [the verb] despite its redundancy does no harm, just as that does no harm in the redundant prepositions. On this view the negated clause after it is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl, as though it were said: "What is with us, not fighting?", like His words: {مَّا لَكُمْ لاَ تَرْجُونَ لِلَّهِ وَقَاراً} [Nūḥ: 13] and {وَمَا لَنَا لاَ نُؤْمِنُ} [al-Māʾida: 84], and the Arabs' saying «مالك قائماً» ("What is wrong with you, standing?"), and the words of Allah the Exalted: {فَمَا لَهُمْ عَنِ التذكرة مُعْرِضِينَ} [al-Muddaththir: 49]. This school is weak, because the default is the absence of redundancy, so one does not resort to it without necessity. The third — and it is the weakest of them — is the school of al-Ṭabarī, that there is an omitted wāw before His words «أن لا نقاتلَ». He said: "Its implied form is: «وما لنا ولأن لا نقاتلَ», like your saying «إياك أن تتكلَّمَ», i.e. «إياك وأن تتكلم»; the wāw was omitted." This, as you see, is very weak.
As for his saying, "Their saying «إياك أَنْ تتكلم» is on the omission of the wāw", it is not as he claimed; rather, «إياك» has been made to carry the meaning of the verb intended for warning, and «أَنْ تتكلمَ» is in the position of an accusative by it, its implied form being "Beware of speaking."

His words: {وَقَدْ أُخْرِجْنَا}: this clause is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl, and its governing element is «نقاتلُ». They disapproved of abandoning fighting while they were in this state. This is the reading of the majority, I mean with the verb in the passive. ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd read «أَخْرَجَنا» in the active. There are two views on it. The first: that [the agent] is a pronoun referring to Allah the Exalted, i.e. "when Allah has driven us out because of our sins". The second: that it is a pronoun referring to the enemy.
«وأبنائنا» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «ديارنا», i.e. "and from our children"; so a muḍāf must be omitted, its implied form being "from among our children" — so Abū al-Baqāʾ assumed it. It was also said that this is by inversion (al-qalb), the original being "our children have been driven out from us"; but there is no need for this.

His words: {إِلاَّ قَلِيلاً} is accusative as a connected exception (istithnāʾ muttaṣil) from the agent of «تَوَلَّوا». The excepted cannot be indefinite and vague: if you said «قام القومُ إلا رجالاً» it would not be correct. This is correct only because «قليلاً» is in reality a naʿt of an omitted [noun], and because it has been specified by being qualified with His words «منهم», so it has come close to being specified thereby.
Ubayy read: «إلاَّ أن يكونَ قليلٌ منهم», and that is a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ), because "being" is an abstract notion whereas the one excepted from are bodies. This question needs clarifying because of its great usefulness. The Arabs say «قام القومُ إلا أَنْ يكونَ زيدٌ» and «زيداً», in the nominative and the accusative. The nominative is on making «كان» complete (tāmma), «زيدٌ» being its agent; the accusative is on making it incomplete (nāqiṣa), «زيداً» being its predicate, and its subject a pronoun referring to the "some" understood from the force of the speech; the implied form is: "The people stood, except that it — i.e. some of them — be Zayd". The meaning is: "The people stood, except for Zayd's being among those standing"; and when his being standing is negated, his standing is negated. So there is no difference in meaning between the two expressions, I mean «قام القوم إلا زيداً» and «قاموا إلا أن يكون زيداً», except that the first is a connected exception and the second disconnected, for the reason established above.

semin-durr:145-145.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {وَلَئِنْ أَتَيْتَ}: There are two views on it. The first is the view of Sībawayh, namely that the lām is the one that prepares for an omitted oath (al-lām al-muwaṭṭiʾa), and «إنْ» is conditional. So a condition and an oath have come together, and the oath came first, so the answer belongs to it, since nothing having a predicate preceded them both. For that reason the answer to the oath came with the negating «ما» and what follows it, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) was omitted because the answer of the oath stands in its place. For that reason the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) came as a past verb, because whenever the apodosis is omitted the protasis must be past, except under poetic necessity. And «تَبِعوا», although past in wording, is future in meaning, i.e.: they will not follow; because the condition is a restriction on the clause, and the condition is future, so the content of the clause must be future, since what is future cannot be a condition for what is past.
The second — and it is the view of al-Farrāʾ, and it is also transmitted from al-Akhfash and al-Zajjāj — is that «إنْ» is in the sense of «لو», and for that reason «ما» came in the answer; so he made «ما تَبِعوا» the answer to «إنْ», because it is in the sense of «لو». As for when it is not in its sense, it is not answered with «ما» alone; rather the fāʾ is necessary: you say «إن تَزُرْني فما أزورك» ("If you visit me, then I will not visit you"), and al-Farrāʾ does not permit «ما أزورك» without the fāʾ. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "The answer of «لَئِنْ» came like the answer of «لو», although it is its opposite in that «لو» requires the past and occurrence and «إنْ» requires the future; because the oath is arranged before both of them, so the answer belongs only to the oath, because one of the two particles falls in the place of the other. This is the view of Sībawayh." The Shaykh said: "In this there is confusion and a lack of explicit statement of what is meant, because its beginning entails that the answer belongs to «إنْ», while his saying after it 'the answer belongs to the oath' indicates that it does not belong to «إنْ». His giving as the reason 'because one of the two particles falls in the place of the other' is not fit as a reason for «ما تَبِعوا» being the answer of the oath, but rather for its being the answer of «إنْ». And his saying 'the view of Sībawayh' — that is not in the Book of Sībawayh; what is in it is only that «ما تَبِعوا» is the answer of the oath, and that the past has fallen in it in place of the future. Sībawayh said: 'And they said «لَئِنْ فَعَلْتَ ما فَعَلَ» ("If you do, he will not do"), meaning «ما هو فاعِلٌ» and «ما يَفْعَلَ»'."

What emerges in summary from the foregoing is that His saying «ما تَبِعُوا» has two views. The first: that it is the answer of the condition «[Translator's note: so in the source («جوابٌ الشرطِ»); according to the preceding discussion, the first view is that it is the answer of the oath (القسم).]», and for that reason it is not joined with the fāʾ. The second: that it is the answer of «إنْ», treating it as «لو». Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "«ما تَبِعوا», i.e.: they will not follow; so it is a past in the sense of the future. «ما» entered by analogy with the wording of the past, and the fāʾ was omitted in the answer because the protasis is past. Al-Farrāʾ said: «إنْ» here is in the sense of «لو»." This from Abū al-Baqāʾ indicates that the answer belongs to the condition, and that the fāʾ was elided only because the protasis is past; and this from him is not acceptable, because by this statement he opposed both the Basrans and the Kufans.

His saying: {وَمَآ أَنتَ بِتَابِعٍ قِبْلَتَهُمْ}: «ما» admits the two aspects, I mean its being Ḥijāzī or Tamīmī. On the first, «أنتَ» is made nominative by it and «بتابع» is in the position of accusative; on the second, it is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «بتابعٍ» is in the position of nominative. This clause is conjoined to the clause of the condition and its answer, not to the answer alone, since it cannot take its place; because the negation of their following his qibla is restricted by a condition which cannot properly be a restriction on the negation of his following their qibla. This clause is more emphatic in negation than His saying {مَّا تَبِعُواْ قِبْلَتَكَ} in several respects; one of them: its being nominal, with the noun repeated in it, and its negation emphasised by the bāʾ. «[Translator's note: the source says "in several respects" but lists only the first.]»
He made «القبلة» singular, though it is dual — since the Jews have a qibla and the Christians another qibla — for one of two reasons: either because, sharing in falsehood, they became one qibla; or for the sake of correspondence in wording, because before it is {مَّا تَبِعُواْ قِبْلَتَكَ}. And «بتابعِ قبلتِهم» was read with iḍāfa (annexation), for lightening, because in an active participle fulfilling the conditions for governing both aspects are permissible. There was disagreement about this clause: is a prohibition meant by it, i.e.: do not follow their qibla — its meaning being: continue in what you are upon, since he was protected from following their qibla — or pure information negating the following, the meaning being that this qibla will not become abrogated, or the cutting off of the hope of the People of the Book that he would return to their qibla? Two well-known views.

His saying: {وَلَئِنِ اتبعت}: It is like His saying «ولَئِنْ أَتَيْتَ». His saying «إنَّك» is the answer of the oath, and the apodosis is omitted, as has preceded in its parallel. The Shaykh said: "It is not to be said that it is the answer for both of them, because that is impossible in wording and in meaning. As for the meaning, it is because what each requires differs: what the oath requires is that it has no governing effect [on it], because the oath was brought only as an emphasis for the clause sworn upon, and what comes by way of emphasis is not suited to be a governor; whereas what the condition requires is that it governs it, so the clause would be in the position of jussive, the condition governing because of the strength of its demand for it. As for the wording, when this clause is the answer of an oath it does not need an additional linking element, but when it is the answer of a condition it needs an additional linking element, namely the fāʾ; and it cannot be both devoid of the fāʾ and have it present; for that reason it is impossible for it to be the answer for both together."

«إذَنْ» is a particle of answer and recompense (jawāb wa-jazāʾ), by the explicit statement of Sībawayh. It makes the imperfect accusative under three conditions: that it be at the head, that nothing separate it from the verb other than an adverb or an oath, and that the verb not be present [in time]. It has entered here between the noun of «إنَّ» and its predicate to establish the relation between them. Its proper place was to come first or last; it did not come first because an oath and a condition preceded and the answer belongs to the oath, so had it come first it might have been imagined that it was for establishing the relation between the condition and the omitted apodosis; and it did not come last, lest the harmony of the verse-endings and the heads of the verses be lost.
The Shaykh said: "Determining the meaning of «إذَنْ» is difficult; people have been confused about its meaning and about understanding Sībawayh's statement about it, namely that its meaning is answer and recompense." He said: "What has been established about it is that it does not occur at the beginning of speech; rather, speech must precede it in wording or by implication, and what follows it in wording or by implication is caused by what precedes it. In that it is of two kinds. The first: that it indicates the creation of the connection and the condition, such that the connection is not understood from anything other than it. An example of that: [someone says] 'I will visit you', and you say «إذاً أزورَك» ('then I will visit you'); you mean now to make his act a condition for your act; and creating causality in a second state necessarily entails its being in the answer and in actuality in a future time. In this kind it governs, and its governing has conditions mentioned in grammar. The second kind: that it emphasises an answer connected with an antecedent, or draws attention to an effect obtaining in the present; in both cases it does not govern, because emphasising particles are not relied upon, whereas a governor is relied upon. That is, for example, «إنْ تأتني إذاً آتِكَ» ('If you come to me, then I will come to you') and «واللَّهِ إذاً لافعلَنَّ» ('By Allah, then I shall surely do'); were «إذاً» dropped, the connection would still be understood. And since in this kind it is not relied upon, its entry upon an explicitly nominal clause is permissible — as when [someone says] 'I will visit you' and you say «إذاً أنا أكرمُك» ('then I shall honour you') — and its coming in the middle is permissible, as in «أنا إذاً أكرمُك», as is its coming last. Once this is established, «إذاً» came in the verse emphasising the answer connected with what preceded. I have established its meaning here only because it recurs frequently in the Qurʾān, so it is to be taken in every place according to what is suitable from what we have established." End of his words.
Know that when a conjunction precedes it, it may be made to govern or left without governing, the latter being more frequent. It is composed of hamza, dhāl and nūn. The Arabs likened its nūn to the tanwīn of the accusative, so they changed it to alif in pause, and the scribes wrote it accordingly. This is the end of the discussion of it.

In this place there has come {مِّن بَعْدِ مَا جَآءَكَ}, while before this He said {بَعْدَ الذي جَآءَكَ} [al-Baqara: 120], and in al-Raʿd {بَعْدَ مَا جَآءَكَ} [al-Raʿd: 37]. So He did not bring the preposition «من» except here, and singled out one place with «الذي» and two places with «ما». What is the wisdom in that? The answer is what some have mentioned, namely that «الذي» is more specific and «ما» more vague. So where He brought «الذي», it pointed to knowledge of the soundness of the religion that is Islam, which excludes the two religions of the Jews and the Christians; so the more specific and better-known word was more fitting there, because it is knowledge of all the fundamentals of religion. And where He brought the word «ما», it pointed to knowledge of one of the pillars of religion: in one of them, the qibla, and in the other, part of the Book, because He pointed to His saying {وَمِنَ الأحزاب مَن يُنكِرُ بَعْضَهُ} [al-Raʿd: 36]. He said: "As for the entry of «مِنْ», its benefit is evident, namely clarifying the beginning of the time at which it became obligatory [upon] him, peace be upon him, to differ from the People of the Book in their qibla." And what is said about this is that it is a matter of variety in eloquence.

semin-durr:146-146.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {الذين آتَيْنَاهُمُ}: There are six aspects in it, the most apparent of which: that it is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is His saying «يَعْرفونه». The second: that it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e.: they are those to whom We gave. The third: accusative by an implied «أعني» ("I mean"). The fourth: genitive as a badal (substitute) from «الظالمين». The fifth: [genitive] as a naʿt (adjective) of «الظالمين». The sixth: accusative as a badal from {الذين أُوتُواْ الكتاب} in the verse before it.

His saying: «يَعْرفونه» has two aspects. The first: that it is a khabar for «الذين آتيناهم», as has preceded in one of the aspects mentioned for «الذين آتيناهم». The second: that it is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), on the remaining views mentioned. Concerning the ṣāḥib al-ḥāl (the one it describes) there are two aspects. The first: the first object of «آتيناهم». The second: the second object, namely «الكتاب»; because in «يَعْرفُونه» there are two pronouns referring back to them. The pronoun in «يَعْرفونه» [i.e. the attached «ـه»] has several views. The first: that it refers back to the truth, which is the change [of qibla]. The second: to the Qurʾān. The third: to the knowledge. The fourth: to the Sacred House. The fifth: to the Prophet ﷺ; al-Zamakhsharī began with this, and al-Zajjāj and others chose it. They said: he was referred to by a pronoun even though no mention of him had preceded, because the speech indicates him and there is no ambiguity; and such a use of the pronoun contains a glorification of him, as though, because of his fame and his being a known landmark, there is no need to mention him by name. The Shaykh said: "Rather, this is a case of iltifāt (shift of person) from the address in His saying «قولِّ وجهَك» to the third person." «[Translator's note: so printed in the source; the verse reads «فَوَلِّ وَجْهَكَ».]»

His saying: {كَمَا يَعْرِفُونَ}: The kāf is in the position of accusative, either as a naʿt of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e.: a knowing like their knowing of their sons; or in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from the pronoun of that omitted maṣdar, "the knowing", the implied form being: they know him with the knowing, it being similar to their knowing [of their sons]; and this is the doctrine of Sībawayh; its verification has preceded. And «ما» is maṣdar-forming, because a maṣdar is cast from it and what follows it, as its verification has preceded.

His saying: {وَهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ}: A nominal clause in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from the agent of «يكتُمون». The most likely in it is that it is a ḥāl «[Translator's note: so in the source; the intended contrast is probably that it is a confirming ḥāl (ḥāl muʾakkida), as opposed to the "clarifying ḥāl" at the end of the paragraph.]», because the wording «يكتمُون الحق» indicates their knowledge of it, since concealing is hiding what is known. It has been said: what the knowledge is connected to is the punishment due upon the concealer, i.e.: and they know the punishment arranged for one who conceals the truth; so it would then be a clarifying ḥāl (ḥāl mubayyina).

semin-durr:204-204.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {مَن يُعْجِبُكَ}: «مَنْ» may be a relative noun, or an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective (nakira mawṣūfa); its like has already been discussed at the beginning of the sūra, so let it be consulted there. «الإعجاب» is finding a thing fine, inclining towards it and esteeming it. The hamza in it is for transitivity. Al-Rāghib said: "«العَجَب» is a bewilderment that comes upon a person [when ignorant] of the cause of a thing; it is not something having a state in itself, but is according to relations to one who knows the cause and one who does not. The reality of «أعجبني كذا» is: it appeared to me in a way whose cause I did not know." End of quote. One says: «عَجِبْتُ من كذا» ("I marvelled at such-and-such"); [the poet] said: 893 - عَجِبْتُ والدهرُ كثيرٌ عجبُهْ ... مِنْ عَنَزِيٍّ سَبَّني لم أَضْرِبُهْ
(I marvelled — and time is full of marvels — at a man of ʿAnaza who reviled me and whom I did not strike.)

His saying: {فِي الحياة}: there are two analyses. The first is that it is attached to «قوله», i.e. what he says concerning the matter of this world pleases you, because his false claim of love seeks a share of this world. The second is that it is attached to «يعجِبُك», i.e. his speech is sweet and eloquent in this world, so it pleases you, but it will not please you in the Hereafter, because of the tongue-tie and faltering that will overtake him at the Standing, or because they will not be permitted to speak. The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "What seems apparent is that it is attached to «يعجبك», not with the meaning al-Zamakhsharī stated, but with the meaning that you find his speech fine always, throughout the span of his life, since nothing proceeds from him in speech except what is pleasing, charming and graceful; so his speech outwardly is always pleasing — you do not see him turn from that fine, splendid speech to coarse, contrary speech."

His saying: {وَيُشْهِدُ الله}: in this clause there are two analyses. The more apparent is that it is conjoined to «يُعْجِبَك», so it is a ṣila (relative clause) with no grammatical position, or an adjective, and thus in the position of nominative (marfūʿ), according to the view taken on «مَنْ». The second is that it is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); its ṣāḥib al-ḥāl (the one it describes) then admits two analyses: one, that it is the nominative pronoun latent (mustatir) in «يعجبك»; the other, that it is the genitive pronoun in «قوله», the implied form being 'that he speaks about the affairs of this world pleases you, swearing to it'. Making it a ḥāl (circumstantial) is open to question from two angles, one from the side of meaning and the other from the side of grammatical technique. As for the first, it entails that the pleasing and the speaking are restricted by a circumstance, and the apparent sense is otherwise. As for the second, it is an affirmative imperfect verb, and that does not occur as a ḥāl [after wāw] except anomalously, as in «قُمْتُ وأصُكُّ عينه» ("I stood up and struck his eye"), or by poetic necessity, as in:
894 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... نَجَوْتُ وأَرْهُنُهم مالِكا
(…I escaped, leaving Mālik with them as a pledge.)
and supplying a mubtadaʾ before it, i.e. «وهو يُشْهِدُ», goes against the original.

The majority read with ḍamma on the imperfect prefix and kasra on the hāʾ, taken from «أَشْهَدَ», and the Divine Name in the accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object). Abū Ḥaywa and Ibn Muḥayṣin read with fatḥa on both and the Divine Name nominative as fāʿil (agent). Ubayy read: «يستشهد الله». As for the majority's reading together with their interpretation, the meaning is: he swears by Allah and calls Him to witness that he is truthful; and «الشهادة» has come with the meaning of oath in the verse of liʿān (mutual imprecation). It is said: so the name of Allah is accusative through the omission of the preposition, i.e. 'he swears by Allah'. This is an oversight by whoever said it, because what is used in the sense of oath is the triliteral «شَهِد», not the quadriliteral «أَشْهَد»: you do not say «أُشْهِد بالله», but rather «أَشْهَدُ بالله». So the meaning of the majority's reading is: Allah is aware of what is in his heart, and no one else knows it because of how intensely he conceals it.

As for the majority's interpretation, it needs the omission of something by which the meaning becomes sound, its implied form being: 'and he swears by Allah contrary to what is in his heart', because what is in his heart is disbelief, and he does not swear to that; he only swears to its opposite, which is what pleases its hearer. This interpretation is strengthened by the reading of Abū Ḥaywa, since its meaning is: and Allah is aware of the disbelief in his heart.

As for the reading of Ubayy, the form «استَفْعَل» there admits two analyses. One: that it has the meaning of «أَفْعَل», so it agrees with the majority's reading. The second: that it has the meaning of the bare form, which is «شَهِد», and the Divine Name is accusative by removal of the preposition (isqāṭ al-khāfiḍ).

His saying: {وَهُوَ أَلَدُّ الخصام}: what is said about this clause is as about the one before it, and we add to it another analysis, namely that it is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «يُشْهِدُ». «الأَلَدُّ» is the intense one, from «اللَّدَد», which is intensity of quarrelling; [the poet] said:
895 - إنَّ تحتَ الترابَ عَزْماً وحَزْما ... وخَصيماً أَلَدَّ ذا مِغْلاقِ
(Beneath the earth lie resolve and prudence, and a most contentious disputant who silences his opponents.)
One says «لَدِدْتُ» with kasra on the ʿayn [of the verb], «ألَدُّ» with fatḥa on it; and «لَدَدْتُه» with fatḥa on the ʿayn, «ألُدُّ» with ḍamma, i.e. 'I overcame him in that', so it is transitive; [the poet] said:
896 - تَلُدُّ أقرانَ الرجالِ اللَّدَدِ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(She overcomes in contention the peers among contentious men…)
And one says: a man «أَلَدُّ», «أَلَنْدَدٌ» and «يَلَنْدَدٌ», a woman «لَدَّاءُ», and the plural «لُدٌّ», like «حُمْر».

On its derivation there are several views. One: from «لُدَيْدَا العُنُق», which are the two sides of the neck — al-Zajjāj said this. It is said: from «لُدَيْدَا الوادي», which are its two banks, so named because of their crookedness. And it is said: it is from «لدَّه» when he detained him, as if he detains his opponent from negotiating with him.

On «الخصام» there are two views. One: that it is the plural of «خَصْم»/ with fatḥa, like «كَعْب» and «كِعاب», «كَلْب» and «كِلاَب», «بَحْر» and «بِحار»; on this view it needs no interpretation. The second: that it is a maṣdar (verbal noun): one says «خاصَمَ خِصاماً» like «قاتَل قِتالاً». On this view something is needed to make sound its occurring as a khabar (predicate) of a concrete being. So it is said: there is an omission in the first part, i.e. 'and his quarrelling is the most intense quarrelling'; it is said: in the second part, i.e. 'and he is the most intense of the people of quarrelling'. It is said: the maṣdar [is meant] in the sense of the active participle, as it is used as an adjective in their saying «رجلٌ عَدْلٌ» ("a just man"). And it is said: «أفْعَلُ» here is not for the comparative-superlative but has the meaning of «لَديدُ الخِصام», so it belongs to the class of annexation of the resembling adjective (al-ṣifa al-mushabbaha). Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«الخِصامُ» is «المُخَاصَمَة», and the annexation of «الألدّ» is in the sense of «في», as in their saying «ثَبْتُ الغَدْر»" — meaning that «أَفْعَل» here is not of the type annexed to that of which it is a part, but is an annexation in the sense of «في» (in). The Shaykh said: "This goes against what the grammarians hold, that «أَفْعَل» is annexed only to that of which it is a part; and it involves affirming annexation in the sense of «في», which is a less favoured view." It is said: «هو» is not the pronoun of «مَنْ» but the pronoun of the quarrelling, explained by the context of the speech, i.e. 'and his quarrelling is the most intense quarrelling'. Abū al-Baqāʾ made «هو» the pronoun of the maṣdar, which is «قوله», for he said: "And «هو» may be the pronoun of the maṣdar, which is «قولُه», and his speech is quarrelling."

semin-durr:205-205.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَإِذَا تولى سعى}: «سَعَى» is the apodosis (jawāb) of the conditional «إذا». This conditional clause admits two analyses. One: that it is conjoined to what precedes it, namely «يُعْجِبُكَ», so it is either a ṣila (relative clause) or a naʿt (adjective), according to what has preceded on «مَنْ». The second: that it is resumptive, merely reporting his condition, the speech having been completed at His saying «ألدُّ الخصام».

«التولِّي» and «السَّعْي» may be literal, i.e. he turned away from you with his body and went with his feet; or figurative, meaning by «التولِّي» the retraction of his earlier speech, and by «السعي» working and earning, from «السَّعاية». This is a common figurative usage, and from it is: {وَأَن لَّيْسَ لِلإِنسَانِ إِلاَّ مَا سعى} [al-Najm: 39]. Imruʾ al-Qays said:
897 - فلو أنَّ ما أسْعى لأدنى معيشةٍ ... كفاني ولم أَطْلُبْ قليلٌ من المالِ
ولكنَّمَا أسعى لمجدٍ مُؤثَّلٍ ... وقد يُدْرِكُ المجدَ المؤثَّلَ أَمْثَالي
(Were I striving for the meanest livelihood, a little wealth would suffice me and I would seek no more; but I strive for deep-rooted glory, and the like of me may attain deep-rooted glory.)
Another said:
898 - أسعى على حَيِّ بني مالِكِ ... كلُّ امرىءٍ في شَأْنِهِ ساعي
(I labour for the clan of Banū Mālik; every man is labouring in his own affair.)
«السَّعاية» in speech is what brings about separation between close friends; [the poet] said:
899 - ما قلتُ ما قال وشاةٌ سَعَوْا ... سَعْيَ عَدُوٍ بَيْنَنَا يَرْجُفُ
(I did not say what slanderers said, who went about between us like an enemy spreading alarm.)

His saying: {فِي الأرض}: attached to «سَعَى». If it is said: it is known that going about is only on the earth — it is said: because it conveys generality, as if it were said: whatever place of the earth he alights in, he works corruption in it; so the word «الأرض» indicates the abundance of his corruption, since generality of the container (the adverbial) entails generality of what is contained. «ليفسِدَ» is attached to «سعى» as its cause.

His saying: {وَيُهْلِكَ الحرث}: the majority read «يُهْلِكَ» with ḍamma on the yāʾ, kasra on the lām and fatḥa on the kāf; «الحَرْثَ» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). It is a clear reading, from «أَهْلَكَ يُهْلك», and the accusative is by conjunction with the verb before it. This resembles His saying, the Exalted: {وملائكته وَرُسُلِهِ وَجِبْرِيلَ} [al-Baqara: 98], for His saying «ليفسدَ» includes his destroying tilth and offspring, and He singled them out by mention for that reason. Ubayy read «وليُهْلِكَ» with the lām of cause made overt, which is the meaning of the majority's reading. Abū Ḥaywa read — and it was transmitted from Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr — «وَيَهْلِكَ الحرثُ والنَّسْلُ» with fatḥa on the yāʾ and kasra on the lām, from the triliteral «هَلَك», «الحرث» being the fāʿil (agent) and «النسلُ» conjoined to it. Some read «ويُهْلِكُ الحرثَ» from «أَهْلَكَ», «الحرث» being the mafʿūl bihi, except that they made the kāf nominative. This has been explained in four ways: that it is conjoined to «يُعْجِبُك»; or to «سَعَى», because it is in the sense of the future; or that it is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. «وهو يُهْلِكُ»; or that it is resumptive. Al-Ḥasan read «ويُهْلَكَ» as passive, with «الحَرْثُ» nominative; he also read «ويَهَلَكُ» with fatḥa on the yāʾ and the lām and ḍamma on the kāf, «الحرثُ» nominative as the fāʿil. Fatḥa on the middle radical of the imperfect here is anomalous, because the middle radical of its past is with fatḥa, and neither its middle nor its final radical is a guttural letter; so it is like «رَكَنَ يَرْكَنُ» with fatḥa in both. «الحَرث» has been discussed previously.

«النَّسْل» is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of «نَسَلَ يَنسُل», i.e. it came out quickly; from it: «نَسَلَ وَبَرُ البعيرِ» (the camel's hair fell out) and «نَسَلَ ريشُ الطائِر» (the bird's feathers came out and flew off). It is said: «النسل» is coming out in succession, and from it is «نُسالُ الطائر», the feathers that fall from a bird one after another. Imruʾ al-Qays said:
900 - وإنهْ تَكُ قَدْ سَاءَتْكِ مني خليقَةٌ ... فَسُلِّي ثيابي من ثيابِكِ تَنْسُلِ
(If some trait of mine has displeased you, then draw my garments from yours, and they will slip away.)
And His saying: {مِّن كُلِّ حَدَبٍ يَنسِلُونَ} [al-Anbiyāʾ: 96] admits both meanings. «الحرثَ» and «النسلَ», though originally maṣdars, here stand in the place of the mafʿūl bihi.

semin-durr:260-260.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {وَإِذْ قَالَ إِبْرَاهِيمُ}: concerning what governs «إذ» there are three views. The most apparent of them is that it is His saying {أَوَلَمْ تُؤْمِن}, i.e. his Lord said to him at the time he said that. The second: that it is «ألم تَرَ», i.e. "have you not seen when Ibrāhīm said". The third: that it is an implied (muḍmar) verb, its implied form being "and remember". So on these last two views «إذ» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), not a ẓarf (adverb of time). And «ربِّ» is a munādā (the one addressed) annexed to the yāʾ of the speaker; the yāʾ was dropped, the kasra before it making it dispensable, and this is the most eloquent dialect; and the vocative particle has been omitted.

His saying {أَرِنِي}: what it contains of variant readings and their justification has already been discussed at His saying {وَأَرِنَا} [al-Baqara: 128]. The "seeing" here is visual, transitive to one object; when the hamza of transference (hamzat al-naql) entered, it gave it a second object: the first is the yāʾ of the speaker and the second is the interrogative clause, which suspends (muʿallaqa) the "seeing" — visual «رأى» can be suspended just as visual «نظر» is suspended; among their sayings is: «أما تَرى أيُّ برقِ ههنا» ("Do you not see what lightning is here?").

And «كيف» is in the position of the accusative, either by likening it to a ẓarf or by likening it to a ḥāl (circumstantial), as was discussed at {كَيْفَ تَكْفُرُونَ} [al-Baqara: 28]. What governs it is «تُحْيي». Makkī rendered it as "in what state do You give life to the dead", which is an explanation of meaning, not of i'rab.

His saying: {قَالَ أَوَلَمْ تُؤْمِن}: concerning this wāw there are two views. The more apparent is that it is for conjunction, with the interrogative hamza placed before it because the hamza has the right to the head of the sentence, as has been set out more than once. The hamza here is for taqrīr (affirmation), because when the interrogative enters upon a negation it affirms it, as in the poet's saying:
1061 - ألستُمْ خيرَ مَنْ رَكِبَ المطايا ... وأندى العاملينَ بطونَ راحِ
(Are you not the best of those who ride mounts, and the most generous of all the world in the palms of the hand?)
[and]: {أَلَمْ نَشْرَحْ لَكَ صَدْرَكَ} [al-Inshirāḥ: 1]; the meaning is: "you are the best", and "We have indeed expanded".
The second: that it is the wāw of the ḥāl, upon which the alif of affirmation has entered; Ibn ʿAṭiyya said this. There is reservation about it, in that if it were for the ḥāl, the clause after it would be in the position of the accusative, and if so it would call for something to put it in the accusative, and there is no such governing word in the wording; so it must be implied, the implied form being «أسألْتَ ولم تؤمِنْ» ("did you ask while you did not believe?"), so the hamza in reality would have entered upon what governs the ḥāl. This is not apparent; rather the apparent view is the first, and that is why it was answered with «بلى»; on what Ibn ʿAṭiyya said this meaning becomes difficult. And his saying «بلى» is an answer to the negated clause even though its meaning has become affirmative, taking account of the wording, not of the meaning. This belongs to the category in which the side of the wording is taken into account rather than the meaning, like {سَوَآءٌ عَلَيْهِمْ أَأَنذَرْتَهُمْ أَمْ لَمْ تُنْذِرْهُمْ} [al-Baqara: 6], whose precise treatment has preceded.

His saying: {لِّيَطْمَئِنَّ}: the lām is the lām of kay (purpose), so the verb after it is in the accusative by an implied «أَنْ»; it is indeclinable (mabnī) because it is attached to the nūn of emphasis. The lām is attached to (mutaʿalliq) something omitted after «لكنْ», its implied form being: "but I asked You about the manner of giving life for the sake of reassurance". And another omission must be assumed before «لكنْ» so that the istidrāk (rectification) is sound with it; the implied form is: "Yes, I have believed, and I did not ask as a non-believer, but I asked so that my heart may be at rest".

And al-ṭumaʾnīna is "stillness"; it is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of «اطمأنَّ», on the pattern of «اقشعرَّ», and it is irregular among maṣdars, since the regular maṣdar of «اطمأنَّ» would be al-iṭmiʾnān. There is disagreement over «اطمأنَّ»: is it metathesised (maqlūb) or not? The view of Sībawayh is that it is metathesised from «طَأْمَنَ», so the first radical is ṭāʾ, the second is hamza and the third is mīm, and the third radical was placed before the second, so its pattern is ifʿalaʿalla — the evidence being their saying «طامنتُه فتطامَنَ». The view of al-Jarmī is that it is not metathesised; it is as if he says that «اطمأنَّ» and «طَأْمَنَ» are two independent roots. This is the apparent sense of the words of Abū al-Baqāʾ, for he said: "The hamza in «ليطمَئِنَّ» is radical, and its pattern is yafʿalillu; that is why there came {فَإِذَا اطمأننتم} [al-Nisāʾ: 103], like iqshaʿrartum." End quote. So its pattern is according to the original, without metathesis. This is not far-fetched: do you not see that in «جَبَذَ» and «جَذَبَ» they said that neither is metathesised from the other, since both roots are equally in use? The place for weighing each of the two views lies elsewhere.

His saying: {مِّنَ الطير}: concerning what it is attached to there are two views. One: that it is omitted, because the preposition phrase stands as a ṣifa (adjective) of «أربعة», the implied form being "four, being of the birds". The second: that it is attached to «خُذْ», i.e. "take from the birds".
And «الطيرُ» is an ism jamʿ (collective noun), like «رَكْب» and «سَفْر». It was also said that it is rather the plural of «طائر», like «تاجر» and «تَجْر»; this is the view of Abū al-Ḥasan. It was also said that it is lightened from «طَيِّر» with a doubled [yāʾ], as in their saying «هَيْن» and «مَيْت» for «هَيِّن» and «مَيِّت».
