Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is originally the maṣdar of طارَ يطير; then this genus was named by it." So four views result concerning it.
Its being put in the genitive by «مِنْ» after the number comes according to the most eloquent usage, since the most eloquent with a collective noun in the chapter of numbers is to separate it with «مِن», as in this verse; annexation is also permitted, as in His saying, Exalted is He: {تِسْعَةُ رَهْطٍ} [al-Naml: 48], and the poet said:
1062 - ثلاثةُ أنفسٍ وثلاثُ ذَوْدٍ ... لقد جارَ الزمانُ على عيالي
(Three souls and three camels — time has indeed been unjust to my dependants.)
Some claimed that its annexation is rare and not to be taken as a basis for analogy, and some that the collective noun for rational beings is feminine; neither claim is correct, because of the noble verse mentioned above. The collective noun for non-rational beings is treated as masculine and as feminine; here it came as masculine, given the presence of the tāʾ in its number.

His saying: {فَصُرْهُنَّ}: Ḥamza read it with kasra on the ṣād, and the rest with ḍamma and with the rāʾ undoubled. There is disagreement over this. It was said that the two readings may both carry one meaning: it is said «صارَه يَصُوره ويَصِيره» in the sense of "he cut it" or "he inclined it", so the two dialectal forms are a word shared between these two meanings, and both readings can bear both of them; this is the view of Abū ʿAlī. Al-Farrāʾ said: "The ḍamma is shared between the two meanings; as for the kasra, its meaning is cutting only." Someone else said: "The kasra is in the sense of cutting and the ḍamma in the sense of inclining." It is also transmitted from al-Farrāʾ that he said: «صَارَه» is metathesised from their saying «صَراه عن كذا», i.e. "he cut it off from such-and-such". And it is said «صُرْتُ الشيءَ فانصار», i.e. [Translator's note: the gloss after «أي» appears to be missing in the source text]. Al-Khansāʾ said:
1063 - فلو يُلاقي الذي لاقَيْتُه حَضِنٌ ... لَظَلَّتِ الشمُّ منه وَهْيَ تَنْصارُ
(Were Ḥaḍin [a mountain] to meet what I have met, its lofty peaks would be left breaking apart.)
i.e. "breaking off". There is disagreement over this word: is it Arabic or Arabicised? From Ibn ʿAbbās it is reported that it is Arabicised from Nabataean, and from Abū al-Aswad that it is from Syriac; the majority hold that it is Arabic, not Arabicised.
And «إليك»: if we say that «صُرْهُنَّ» means "incline them", it is attached to it; and if we say that it means "cut them up", it is attached to «خُذْ».
Ibn ʿAbbās read «فَصُرَّهُنَّ» with a doubled rāʾ, with ḍamma and with kasra on the ṣād, from «صَرَّه يَصُرُّه» when he gathers it together; except that the coming of a transitive doubled verb on yafʿilu, with kasra on the middle radical in the imperfect, is rare. Abū al-Baqāʾ transmitted, concerning those who doubled the rāʾ, that some of them give it ḍamma, some fatḥa and some kasra, like «مُدَّهُنَّ»: the ḍamma is by assimilation (itbāʿ), the fatḥa for lightness, and the kasra on the basic rule for the meeting of two quiescent letters.
When Abū al-Baqāʾ explained «فَصُرْهُنَّ» in the sense of "incline them", he assumed something omitted after it, its implied form being "so incline them towards you, then cut them up"; and when he explained it as "cut them up", he assumed something omitted to which «إلى» is attached, its implied form being "cut them up after you have inclined them [towards you]". Then he said: "The best in my view is that «إليك» be a ḥāl of the implied object, the implied form being: cut them up, brought near to you, or inclined, or the like."

His saying: {ثُمَّ ا} [Translator's note: the Quranic quotation is truncated thus in the source; the phrase discussed is {ثُمَّ اجْعَلْ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ جَبَلٍ مِّنْهُنَّ جُزْءًا}]: «جَعَلَ» may be in the sense of "casting", and so be transitive to one object, which is «جزءاً»; on this view «على كل» and «منهنَّ» are attached to «اجعَلْ». Or it may be in the sense of «صَيَّر» (to make into), and so be transitive to two objects, with «جُزْءاً» as the first and «على كل» as the second, so that it is attached to something omitted. And «منهنَّ» may, on this view, be attached to something omitted as a ḥāl of «جزءاً», because originally it is the ṣifa of an indefinite noun, and when it was placed before it, it was put in the accusative as a ḥāl. Abū al-Baqāʾ permitted it to be an object of «اجْعَلْ» — meaning when «اجْعَلْ» is in the sense of «صَيِّر» — so that «جزءاً» is the first object and «منهنَّ» the second object placed before the first, in which case it is attached to something omitted. [And an omitted specifying ṣifa must be assumed after] his saying «كلِّ جبلٍ», its implied form being "on every mountain in your presence, or adjoining you", so that the meaning is sound.
The majority read «جُزْءاً» with a sukūn on the zāy and with the hamza; Abū Bakr gave ḍamma to the zāy; and Abū Jaʿfar doubled the zāy without the hamza. Its justification is that when he dropped the hamza he paused on the zāy and then doubled it, as they said «هذا فَرَجّْ», then the connected speech was treated like the pause. The establishment of this has preceded at His saying {هُزُواً} [al-Baqara: 67]. There is another dialectal form of it, namely with kasra on the jīm. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "I do not know anyone who read with it." And al-juzʾ is a piece of a thing; the root basically indicates cutting and separating, and from it come al-tajziʾa and al-ajzāʾ.

His saying: {يَأْتِينَكَ}: the apodosis (jawāb) of the imperative, so it is in the position of the jussive, but it is indeclinable because it is attached to the nūn of the feminine plural.

His saying: «سَعْياً»: there are several views on it. One: that it is a maṣdar standing in the place of a ḥāl from the pronoun of the birds, i.e. "they will come to you running", or "possessed of running". The second: that it is a ḥāl from the one addressed. Something transmitted from al-Khalīl strengthens this, for it is related from him that "the meaning is: they will come to you while you run (tasʿā saʿyan)". On this view «سعياً» is accusative as a maṣdar (mafʿūl muṭlaq, absolute object), and the governing verb of this maṣdar is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the kāf in «يأتينك». I say: what led al-Khalīl — may Allah have mercy on him — to this interpretation is that, in his view, one does not say «سَعَى الطائرُ» ("the bird ran"); so he made the running an attribute of al-Khalīl [Ibrāhīm], upon him be peace, not an attribute of the birds. The third: that «سَعْياً» is accusative as a type of maṣdar (expressing a kind), because it is a kind of coming, since it is coming with speed, as though it were said: "they will come to you with a swift coming". Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It may be a maṣdar of emphasis (muʾakkid), because running and coming are close to each other." This is open to reservation, because the maṣdar of emphasis does not add to the meaning of what governs it; except that he was lax in his expression.

semin-durr:183-183.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمُ الصيام}: «الصيامُ» is the object whose agent is not named (i.e. the nāʾib fāʿil, deputy agent). This complement (faḍla) [«عليكم»] was placed before it, even though its basic position is after it, because beginning with the mention of those on whom something is prescribed is more emphatic than mentioning what is prescribed, since the prescribing concerns the one who performs it.
Al-ṣiyām is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of ṣāma yaṣūmu ṣawman; its original form is ṣiwām, and the wāw was changed into yāʾ. Al-ṣawm is also a maṣdar. These two patterns — I mean faʿl and fiʿāl — are common in every verb whose ʿayn is wāw and whose lām is sound. A little of it has come on fuʿūl: they said ghāra ghuwūran; but they found it disagreeable because of the meeting of two wāws, and therefore some pronounced it with hamza and said al-ghuʾūr. Lexically, al-ṣiyām is refraining from something in general. From it: ṣāmat al-rīḥ, the wind refrained from blowing; and [ṣāma] the horse, it refrained from running. [The poet said]:
835 - خيلٌ صِيامُ وخيلٌ غيرُ صائمةٍ ... تحتَ العَجاجِ وأُخْرى تَعْلِكُ اللُّجُما
(Horses standing still, and horses not standing still beneath the dust, and others champing at the bits.)
And Allah the Exalted said: {إِنِّي نَذَرْتُ للرحمن صَوْماً} [Maryam: 26], i.e. silence, because of His words {فَلَنْ أُكَلِّمَ اليوم إِنسِيّاً}. And ṣāma al-nahār, i.e. its heat became intense. The poet said:
836 - حتى إذا صامَ النهارُ واعتَدَلْ ... ومالَ للشمسِ لُعابٌ فَنَزَلْ
(Until, when the day stood still and was at its height, and the sun's shimmer slanted, he dismounted.)
It is as though they imagined that at that time the sun refrains from moving. Maṣām al-nujūm is the stars' refraining from moving. Imruʾ al-Qays said:
837 - كأنَّ الثُّرِيَّا عُلِّقَتْ في مَصامِها ... بأمراسِ كُتَّانٍ إلى صُمِّ جَنْدَلِ
(As though the Pleiades were hung in their resting-place by flaxen ropes to solid rocks.)
His words: {كَمَا كُتِبَ}: five interpretations. The first: that its position is accusative as an adjective (naʿt) of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "it was prescribed with a prescribing like what was prescribed". The second: that it is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the definite maṣdar, i.e. "fasting was prescribed for you, the prescribing [being] like what was prescribed". On these two interpretations «ما» is maṣdariyya (infinitival). The third: that it is an adjective of a maṣdar from the word al-ṣiyām, i.e. "a fasting like what was prescribed"; on this interpretation «ما» means alladhī (that which), i.e. "a fasting similar to the fasting prescribed for those before you". «صوماً» here is an emphasising maṣdar in meaning, because al-ṣiyām means "that you fast a fasting"; Abū al-Baqāʾ said this. This implies that the emphasising maṣdar can be qualified, and its prohibition has preceded at His words {بالمعروف حَقّاً عَلَى المتقين} [al-Baqara: 180]. The Shaykh said, after reporting this from Ibn ʿAṭiyya: «This is far-fetched, because likening the fasting to the prescribing is not valid — that is if «ما» is maṣdariyya; and if it is relative, it is also far-fetched, because likening fasting to fasting is valid only on a far-fetched interpretation».
The fourth: that it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from «الصيام», with «ما» relative, i.e. "resembling that which was prescribed"; the governing word in it is «كُتِبَ», because it governs the one to whom the ḥāl refers. The fifth: that it is in the position of the nominative because it is an adjective of al-ṣiyām. This is rejected on the ground that a preposition with its genitive noun counts as indefinite, while al-ṣiyām is definite; so how can a definite noun be qualified by an indefinite? Abū al-Baqāʾ answered this «that al-ṣiyām is not specified», as though he means that the «أل» in it is generic, and a noun made definite by the generic al is, in their view, close to the indefinite; for that reason it is permissible to take account of its wording at one time and its meaning at another. They said: «The red dinar and the white dirham have ruined people» (with plural adjectives); and from it:
838 - ولقد أَمُرُّ على اللئيمَ يَسُبُّنِي ... فَمَضَيْتُ ثمَّتَ قُلْتُ لا يَعْنِيني
(I pass by the base man who reviles me, and go on, then say: he does not mean me.)
[And His words:] {وَآيَةٌ لَّهُمُ الليل نَسْلَخُ مِنْهُ النهار} [Yā Sīn: 37]. Discussion of the like of His words {الذين مِن قَبْلِكُمْ} — how the relative noun is given such a ṣila — and the answer to it has preceded at His words: {خَلَقَكُمْ والذين مِن قَبْلِكُمْ} [al-Baqara: 21].
His words: {أَيَّاماً}: there are four interpretations of its accusative. The most apparent: that it is accusative by an implied governing word indicated by the context of the speech, its implied form being "fast days". This accusative admits two interpretations: either as an adverbial (ẓarfiyya), or as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) by extension (ittisāʿan).
The second: that it is accusative by «الصيام»; al-Zamakhsharī mentioned no other and compared it to your saying «I intended going out on Friday». This is worthless, because it entails separating the maṣdar from what it governs by something extraneous, namely His words «كما كُتِبَ», since that is not governed by the maṣdar on any implied form you may supply. If it is said: «كما كُتِبَ» may be made an adjective of al-ṣiyām — on the opinion of those who allow qualifying a noun made definite by generic al with what is treated like an indefinite — so it is not extraneous; the reply is: that entails qualifying the maṣdar before mentioning what it governs, which is impossible.
The third: that it is accusative by al-ṣiyām on the basis that you take the kāf as an adjective of a maṣdar from al-ṣiyām, as some have held, even though it is weak; the implied form is then: «the fasting, a fasting like what was prescribed»; so it is permissible for «الصيامُ» to govern «أياماً», because it then governs «صوماً», which is qualified by «كما كُتِبَ»; thus the separation between them is not by something extraneous but by what the maṣdar governs.
The fourth: that it is accusative by «كُتب», either as an adverbial or as a mafʿūl bihi by extension. Al-Farrāʾ inclined to this, and Abū al-Baqāʾ followed him. The Shaykh said: «Both views are mistaken. As for the accusative as an adverbial, it is the locus of the action, and the prescribing does not take place in the days; rather what it concerns is what takes place in the days. As for the accusative as object by extension, that is built on its being an adverbial of «كُتِبَ», and it has been shown that this is a mistake».
«معدوداتٍ» is an adjective; the plural with alif and tāʾ of an adjective qualifying [a plural of] non-rational things is regular, as here, and as in «جبال راسيات» (firm mountains) and «أيام معلوماتٌ» (known days).
His words: {أَوْ على سَفَرٍ}: in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the khabar of kāna. «أو» here is for division into kinds (tanwīʿ). He turned away from the active participle and did not say «أو مسافراً» (or travelling), to suggest mastery over the journey, since it involves choice — unlike illness, which is compulsory.
His words: {فَعِدَّةٌ مِّنْ أَيَّامٍ أُخَرَ}: the majority read «فَعِدَّةٌ» in the nominative, and there are several interpretations. The first: that it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is omitted, either before it, its implied form being "then upon him is a number", or after it, i.e. "then a number [of days] is better for him". The second: that it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "then what is obligatory is a number".
The third: that it is nominative by an omitted verb, i.e. "then a number suffices him". It has also been read «فَعِدَّةً» in the accusative, by an omitted verb, its implied form being "then let him fast a number". It seems Abū al-Baqāʾ did not come across this reading, for he said: «Had it been read in the accusative, it would have been sound». A muḍāf must be supplied, its implied form being «then the fasting of a number», and a clause must be supplied between the two verbs for the speech to be sound, its implied form being "and he breaks the fast, then a number"; its parallel is {أَنِ اضرب بِّعَصَاكَ البحر فانفلق} [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 63], i.e. "so he struck, and it split". «عدةٌ» means "counted", like al-ṭiḥn (what is ground) and al-dhibḥ (what is slaughtered). He made His words «فَعِدَّةٌ» indefinite and did not say «فَعِدَّتُها» (then its number), relying on the meaning. «من أيامٍ» is in the position of the nominative or the accusative, according to the two readings, as an adjective of «عِدَّة».
His words: {أُخَرَ}: an adjective of «أيَّامٍ». «أُخَرُ» is of two kinds: a kind that is the plural of «أخرى», the feminine of «آخَر», which is an elative (afʿal al-tafḍīl); and a kind that is the plural of ukhrā in the sense of ākhira, the feminine of «آخِر» (last), the opposite of first; of this is His word: {قَالَتْ أُخْرَاهُمْ لأُولاَهُمْ} [al-Aʿrāf: 49] «[Translator's note: the reference is given thus in the text; the phrase is in al-Aʿrāf: 38.]». The first kind is a diptote, and the cause preventing it from full declension is being an adjective together with deflection (ʿadl).
The grammarians differed over the manner of the deflection. The majority said: it is deflected from the al-form. That is because «أُخَر» is the plural of ukhrā, ukhrā is the feminine of «آخَر», and ākhar is an elative; and an elative is used in one of three ways: with al, with «مِنْ», or with annexation. But «مِنْ» is excluded, because with it singular and masculine are obligatory; and there is no annexation in the wording; so we took its deflection to be from al. This is as they said of «سَحَر» (dawn) that it is deflected from al, except that this one is together with being a proper name. Sībawayh's doctrine is that it is deflected from one form to another, because properly in your saying «I passed by other women (bi-niswatin ukhara)», on the pattern fuʿal, it should be «bi-niswatin ākhara», on the pattern afʿal, since the meaning involves an implied min; so it was deflected from the singular to the plural. The full treatment of the two doctrines has a place more suitable for it than this.
As for the second kind, it is fully declined, since the said cause is absent. The difference between «أُخْرَى» of the elative and «أُخرى» meaning "later" is that the meaning of the elative one is that of «غير» (other), while the meaning of the latter is "later". Because the first has the meaning of «غير», what is connected with it may only be of the same genus as what precedes it, as in «I passed by you and by another man»; and one may not say "I bought this camel and another horse", because it is of a different genus. As for the poet's words:
839 - صَلَّى على عَزَّةَ الرحمانُ وابنتِها ... ليلى وصَلَّى على جاراتِها الأُخَرِ
(May the Merciful bless ʿAzza and her daughter Laylā, and bless her other neighbours.)
— he made her daughter a neighbour of hers; were it not for that, it would not be permissible. The meaning of the elative in ākhar and awwal and their derivatives is unstable «[Translator's note: «ومعنا» as written, for «ومعنى».]»; its full treatment is in the books of grammar, and I have explained it in «Sharḥ al-Tashīl», so let it be consulted.
The days were qualified by «أُخَر» only because they are a plural of non-rational things, and a plural of non-rational things may be treated like a feminine singular or like a feminine plural. Of the first is {وَلِيَ فِيهَا مَآرِبُ أخرى} [Ṭā Hā: 18]; of the second, this verse and its parallels. Treating it as a plural was preferred here only because had it been brought as a singular, so that it was said «عِدَّةٌ من أيامٍ أخرى», it would have given the false impression that it is an adjective of «عِدَّة», and the intended meaning would be lost.
His words: {يُطِيقُونَهُ}: the majority read «يُطِيقُونه», from aṭāqa yuṭīqu, like aqāma yuqīmu. Ḥumayd read «يُطْوِقُونه», from aṭwaqa, like their saying aṭwala for aṭāla and aghwala for aghāla; this is an anomalous retention of the sound form. Like it in anomaly, among verbs with wāw: ajwada meaning ajāda; and among verbs with yāʾ: aghyamat al-samāʾ (the sky clouded over), ajyalat, aghyalat al-marʾa (the woman suckled while pregnant), and aṭyabat. The modified form has come in all of these, and it is the regular one; no one held the forms like «أَغْيَمَت» and «أطْوَل» to be regular except Abū Zayd.
Ibn ʿAbbās and Ibn Masʿūd read «يُطَوَّقونه», passive, from ṭawwaqa with doubling, on the pattern qaṭṭaʿa. ʿĀʾisha and Ibn Dīnār read «يَطَّوَّقُونَه», with doubled ṭāʾ and wāw, from aṭwaqa «[Translator's note: so in the text; the explanation that follows derives it from taṭawwaqa.]»; its original is taṭawwaqa: when the tāʾ was to be assimilated into the ṭāʾ, it was changed into ṭāʾ, and the connecting hamza was brought in to make it possible to begin with a vowelless letter. The account of this has preceded at His words: {أَن يَطَّوَّفَ بِهِمَا} [al-Baqara: 158]. ʿIkrima and a group read «يَطَّيَّقونُه», with fatḥa on the yāʾ and with the ṭāʾ and yāʾ doubled; it is also related from Mujāhid. It has also been read in the same way but with the verb in the passive.
Some people rejected this reading. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: «Doubling the yāʾ in this word is weak». They declared this reading invalid only because in their view it is from a root with wāw, namely al-ṭawq; so where would the yāʾ come from? This reading is neither invalid nor weak, and it has a good explanation: this reading is not from tafaʿʿala, so that the difficulty they raised would follow, but rather from tafayʿala; the original is taṭaywaqa, from al-ṭawq, like tadayyara and taḥayyara from al-dawarān and al-ḥawr, whose originals are tadaywara and taḥaywara. The yāʾ and wāw met, the first of them being vowelless, so the wāw was changed into yāʾ and the yāʾ assimilated into the yāʾ. The original was yataṭaywaqūnahu, then it was assimilated after the change. Whoever read «يَطَّيَّقونه» with fatḥa on the yāʾ made it active, and whoever gave it ḍamma made it passive. The reading with doubling of the wāw or of the yāʾ may be [in the sense] of strained effort (takalluf), i.e. they make strained efforts to bear it; that is figurative, from al-ṭawq, which is the necklace, as though it were like a necklace on their necks.
Far-fetched is the view of one who claimed that «لا» is omitted before «يُطِيقُونَه», and that the implied form is «they are not able to bear it» (lā yuṭīqūnahu), comparing it to the poet's words:
840 - فحالِفْ فلا واللَّهِ تَهْبِطُ تَلْعَةً ... من الأرضِ إلا أنت للذلِّ عارِفُ
(Then make alliances; for, by Allah, you will not descend into any valley of the land but you will be acquainted with humiliation.)
And his words:
841 - آليتُ أمدحُ مُغْرَما أبداً ... يَبْقى المديحُ وَيذْهَبُ الرِّفْدُ
(I have sworn I shall never praise one burdened with debt; praise remains while the gift is gone.)
And his words:
842 - فقلتُ يمِينَ اللَّهِ أَبْرَحُ قاعِداً ... ولو قَطَعوا رأسي لديك وأَوْصَالي
(I said: by Allah's oath, I shall [not] cease sitting here, even if they cut off my head and my limbs before you.)
The meaning is: "you will not descend", "I shall not praise", "I shall not cease". This is worthless, because omitting it creates ambiguity; as for the verses mentioned, [it is allowed there] because the oath indicates the negation.
The hāʾ in «يُطِيقُونَه» refers to the fasting; it has also been said: to the ransom (fidāʾ); al-Farrāʾ said this.
«فِدْيَةٌ» is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is in the preposition before it. The body of readers read «فِدْيَة» with tanwīn, «طعام» in the nominative and «مسكين» in the singular. Hishām likewise, except that he read «مساكين» in the plural. Nāfiʿ and Ibn Dhakwān read «فدية» annexed to «طعام مساكين», in the plural. In the first reading «طعام» is a badal (substitute) from «فِدْية»; by this badal the meaning of the ransom is explained. Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed it to be the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "it is food". As for annexing the ransom to the food, it belongs to the class of annexing a thing to its genus, the purpose being explanation, as in your saying "a ring of iron", "a garment of silk", "a door of teak", because the ransom may be food or something else. Some said: «This annexation may belong to the class of annexing the qualified noun to its adjective»; he said: «because the ransom has an essence, and its description is that it is food». This is unsound, because he either means by «طعام» the maṣdar in the sense of feeding (iṭʿām), as ʿaṭāʾ is in the sense of iʿṭāʾ, or he means the object [i.e. what is eaten]; and on both suppositions it cannot be used as an adjective. For a maṣdar is not used as an adjective except for hyperbole, which is not intended here; and [a noun] in the sense of the object is not formed on a verb and is not regular — you do not say ḍirāb meaning maḍrūb, nor qitāl meaning maqtūl — and because such forms are not formed on a verb they do not govern as it does: you do not say «I passed by a man whose bread is food (ṭaʿāmin khubzuhu)». And if it is not an adjective, how can it be said that the qualified noun was annexed to its adjective? «فِدْية» was made singular for two reasons. The first: that it is a maṣdar, and a maṣdar is made singular; the tāʾ in it is not that of a single instance but for mere femininity. The second: that since it was annexed to a word annexed to a plural, it conveyed plurality — this in the reading «مساكين» in the plural. Whoever made «مساكين» plural did so to match plural with plural; and whoever made it singular did so having regard to the singularity of the general [distributive] sense, i.e. "and upon each one of those able to fast, for every day he breaks the fast, is the feeding of a poor person". Its parallel is: {والذين يَرْمُونَ المحصنات ثُمَّ لَمْ يَأْتُواْ بِأَرْبَعَةِ شُهَدَآءَ فاجلدوهم ثَمَانِينَ جَلْدَةً} [al-Nūr: 4].
From the singular «المسكين» it becomes clear that the ruling is one poor person for every day on which he breaks the fast, which is not understood from the plural. By al-ṭaʿām is meant feeding (al-iṭʿām), so it is a maṣdar; it is weak for the object [i.e. the food] to be meant by it. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: «Because He annexed it to the poor person, and the food does not belong to the poor person before it is made his property; were it taken in that sense it would be figurative, because its implied form would become: "then upon him is giving out food that becomes the poor people's", so it would belong to the class of naming a thing by what it will become. Although that is permissible, it is figurative, and the literal is preferable to it».
His words: {فَمَن تَطَوَّعَ خَيْراً}: its parallel has preceded, with full discussion, at His words: {وَمَن تَطَوَّعَ خَيْراً فَإِنَّ الله شَاكِرٌ عَلِيمٌ} [al-Baqara: 158], so let it be consulted. The pronoun in His words «فهو» is the pronoun of the maṣdar indicated by His words «فَمَنْ تَطَوَّع», i.e. "then volunteering is better for him". «له» is in the position of the nominative because it is an adjective of «خير», so it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to something omitted, i.e. "a good that is his".
His words: {وَأَن تَصُومُواْ}: an interpreted maṣdar, nominative as mubtadaʾ, its implied form being «your fasting», and «خَيْرٌ» is its khabar. Like it is {وَأَن تعفوا أَقْرَبُ للتقوى} [al-Baqara: 237]. His words {إِن كُنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ} are a condition whose apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, its implied form being: "then fasting is better for you". The object of "knowing" is omitted, either for restriction to the verb itself (iqtiṣāran), i.e. "if you are people of knowledge and discernment", or for brevity (ikhtiṣāran), i.e. "you know what its being prescribed and its explanation are" «[Translator's note: «ما شرعيتُه وتبيينُه» as written; the wording is uncertain.]», or "the merit of what you have come to know".

semin-durr:147-147.t:
The words of the Exalted: {الحق مِن رَّبِّكَ}: there are three views on it. The most apparent of them is that it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is the preposition and its genitive noun after it. On this view there are two possibilities regarding the alif and lām: one is that they are for prior reference (al-ʿahd), the allusion being to the truth upon which the Messenger, upon him be peace, stands, or to the truth mentioned in His words «يكتمون الحقَّ», i.e. this which they conceal is the truth from your Lord; and [the other is] that they are for the genus, in the sense: the truth is from Allah, not from anyone else. The second: that it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "it is the truth from your Lord", the pronoun referring back to the concealed truth, i.e. what they concealed is the truth. The third: that it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, its implied form being: "the truth from your Lord, they know it". On these two latter views the preposition and its genitive noun are in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «الحق»; and it may also be a second khabar in the second view.

ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib read it {الحقَّ من ربك} in the accusative, and there are three views on it. The first: that it is accusative as a badal (substitute) of the concealed الحقّ; al-Zamakhsharī said this. The second: that it is accusative through an implied «الزم» ("hold fast to"), indicated by the address after it [in] His words «فلا تكونَنَّ». The third: that it is accusative by «يَعْلَمون» before it. Ibn ʿAṭiyya mentioned these two [latter] views. On this last view it is one of the cases in which an overt noun is put in the place of a pronoun, i.e. "while they know it, being from your Lord"; and that is permissible and good in contexts of magnifying and making something awesome, as in:

768 - لا أَرى الموتَ يَسْبِقُ الموتَ شيءٌ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(I see nothing that outstrips death — "death" repeated in place of the pronoun.)

Prohibiting someone from being in a state characterised by an attribute is more emphatic than prohibiting the attribute itself, and that is why the Revelation came in this form, as in {فَلاَ تَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الممترين} and {فَلاَ تَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الجاهلين} [al-Anʿām: 35], rather than "do not doubt" (لا تَمْتَرِ), "do not be ignorant" (لا تَجْهَلْ), and the like. The explanation of this is that saying "لا تكُنْ ظالماً" ("do not be a wrongdoer") is a prohibition of being in this state, and prohibiting being in a state is more emphatic than prohibiting that attribute, since prohibiting being in a state indicates that all future states of being are [to be kept free] of that attribute. The meaning is: do not do wrong in any of your states of being, i.e. in every single one of your states of being, so that no time passes over you in which wrongdoing is found in you; it thus becomes as if there were an explicit statement covering all states of being — unlike "لا تَظْلِمْ" ("do not do wrong"), which [only] entails the states of being; and there is a difference between what indicates by explicit statement and what indicates by entailment.

al-Imtirāʾ (الامتراء) is the iftiʿāl form from al-mirya, which is doubt; from it comes al-mirāʾ (disputation). [The poet] said:

769 - فإيَّاك إيَّاكَ المِراءَ فإنَّه ... إلى الشَّرِّ دَعَّاءٌ وللشَّرِّ جَالِبُ
(Beware, beware of disputation, for it is a great summoner to evil and a bringer of evil.)

Māraytuhu means: I argued with him and contended with him over what he claimed. Iftaʿala here has the sense of tafāʿala; one says tamāraw fī kadhā and imtaraw fīhi ("they disputed about such-and-such"), like tajāwarū and ijtawarū ("they were neighbours"). al-Rāghib said: "al-Mirya is wavering in a matter, and it is more specific than doubt (shakk). al-Imtirāʾ and al-mumārāh are arguing over something in which there is mirya. Its origin is from maraytu al-nāqa, when I stroke the she-camel's udder for milking." So he distinguished between mirya and doubt, as you see, just as he previously drew a distinction between rayb and doubt. al-Ṭabarī cited the verse of al-Aʿshā:

770 - تَدُرُّ على أَسْؤُقِ المُمْتَرِي ... ن رَكْضاً إذا ما السرابُ ارْجَحَنْ
(She pours forth a gallop upon the shanks of those who urge her on, when the mirage spreads wide.)

as evidence that al-mumtarūn are those who doubt. He said: "He erred in that, because Abū ʿUbayda and others said: al-mumtarūn in the verse are those who urge on the horses with their legs, spurring them so that they run, [as if] they were milking the running out of them." [Translator's note: the source does not name who is speaking in "He said"; the quoted critic is evidently someone commenting on al-Ṭabarī.]

semin-durr:261-261.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {مَّثَلُ الذين يُنْفِقُونَ}: «مَثَلُ» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «كمثلِ حبةٍ» is its khabar (predicate). An omission must be assumed for the comparison to be sound, because those who spend are not likened to the grain itself. There is disagreement over what is omitted. It is said: it is from the first term, its implied form being "and the likeness of what is spent by those who…" or "the spending of those who…". It is also said: it is from the second term, its implied form being "and the likeness of those who spend is like the sower of a grain"; or it is from both the first and the second, according to different construals, i.e. "the likeness of those who spend, and of their spending, is like a grain and its sower". These aspects were already set out precisely, with the fullest explanation, at His saying, Exalted is He: {وَمَثَلُ الذين كَفَرُواْ كَمَثَلِ الذي يَنْعِقُ} [al-Baqara: 171], so let it be consulted there. The view that the kāf or «مثل» is redundant (zāʾida) is very far-fetched, and the one who holds it is not to be heeded.

«الحَبَّةُ» (grain) is the singular of «الحَبُّ», which is what is sown for sustenance; it is most often applied to wheat. Al-Mutalammis said:
1064 - آليتُ حَبَّ العراقِ الدهرَ أَطْعَمُه ... والحَبُّ يأكلُه في القَرْيَةِ السُّوسُ
(I have sworn never in my life to eat the grain of Iraq, while the grain in the town is eaten by the weevil.)
«الحِبَّة» with kasra is the seeds of herbs that are not used for sustenance, and «الحُبَّة» with ḍamma is love.
[Translator's note: the source as printed reads «الحُبَّة» بالضم الحُبُّ; it is translated here as "love" (al-ḥubb).]

His saying: {أَنبَتَتْ سَبْعَ سَنَابِلَ}: this clause is in the position of the genitive, because it is a naʿt (adjective) of «حبة», as though it were said: "like the likeness of a grain that grows…".

Abū ʿAmr, Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī and Hishām assimilated the tāʾ of the feminine into the sīn of «سبع», while the rest pronounced it distinctly. The tāʾ is close to the sīn, and for that reason it has been substituted for it: they said «ناس» and «نات», «أكياس» and «أكيات». The poet said:
1065 - عمروَ بنَ يربوعٍ شرارَ الناتِ ... ليسوا بأجيادٍ ولا أَكْياتِ
(ʿAmr ibn Yarbūʿ, the worst of people: they are neither noble nor clever.)
That is: «شرار الناس» and «ولا أكياس».

The tamyīz (specification) here came on the pattern mafāʿil, whereas in Sūrat Yūsuf it came as a plural with alif and tāʾ. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: why was it not said «سبع سنبلات», giving the tamyīz its due with the plural of paucity, as He said: {وَسَبْعَ سُنْبُلاَتٍ خُضْرٍ}? I say: this is due to what I stated earlier at His saying «ثلاثَةُ قروء», namely that the plural patterns occur interchangeably in one another's places." He means that it belongs to the category of latitude of usage and one of the two plurals occurring in the place of the other. What he said is neither a resolution nor a real explanation, so a useful rule must be mentioned on this matter:

Know that the two sound plurals are not used as the tamyīz of a number except in two cases. The first: that the singular has no other plural, as in «سبع سماوات», «سبع بقرات», «تسع آيات» and «خمس صلوات», because these things are pluralised only with the sound plural. As for the poet's saying:
1066 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... . . . فوقَ سَبْعِ سَمائيا
(… above seven heavens.)
it is anomalous and explicitly declared rare, so no attention is paid to it. The second: that it is chosen because of adjacency to something else, as in His saying: {وَسَبْعَ سُنْبُلاَتٍ خَضْرٍ}, where He turned from «سنابل» to «سنبلات» because of its adjacency to «سبع بقرات». For that reason, when there is no adjacency, the tamyīz is given with the broken plural rather than the sound plural, even if the sound plural exists, as in «سبع طرائق» and «سبع ليالٍ», though «طريقات» and «ليلات» are permissible.

In sum: if a noun has two plurals, a sound plural and a broken plural, the broken plural is either of paucity or of multitude. If it is of multitude, it is either of the mafāʿil pattern or of another. If it is of the mafāʿil pattern, it is preferred to the sound plural: you say «ثلاثة أحامد» and «ثلاث زيانب», and «أحمدِين» and «زينبات» are permissible to a small extent.

If it is not of the mafāʿil pattern, then either forms other than the sound plural and the plural of multitude are frequent in it, or they are rare. If the first, then neither the sound plural nor the plural of multitude is permissible except rarely, as in «ثلاثة زيود», «ثلاث هنود» and «ثلاثة أفلس»; it is not permissible to say «ثلاثة زيدين», «ثلاث هندات» or «ثلاثة فلوس» except rarely. If the second, the sound plural and the plural of multitude are preferred, as in «ثلاث سعادات» and «ثلاثة شُسُوع», and rarely «ثلاث سعائد» and «ثلاثة أَشْسُع» are permissible. Once this is established, His saying «سبع سنابل» came according to the preferred usage, while «سبعِ سنبلات» is due to adjacency, as stated above.

Regarding «السنبلة» (the ear of grain) there are two views. The first: its nūn is a root letter, because of their saying «سَنْبَلَ الزرعُ», i.e. the crop put forth its ears. The second: it is augmentative, and this is the well-known view, because of their saying «أسبلَ الزرعُ». Its pattern according to the first is fuʿlula, and according to the second funʿula. On the basis of the established report of both usages, «سَنْبَلَ الزرعُ» and «أَسْبَلَ», it belongs to the category of «سَبِط» and «سِبَطْر».

His saying: {فِي كُلِّ سُنبُلَةٍ}: this preposition with its genitive is in the position of the genitive as a naʿt of «سنابل», or in the position of the accusative as a naʿt of «سبع», as in «رأيتُ سبعَ إمَّاءٍ أحرارٍ» and «أحراراً». On both construals it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted element. Regarding the nominative of «مئة» there are two aspects. The first: it is a fāʿil (agent) of the preposition phrase, because the phrase is supported, since it has occurred as a naʿt. The second: it is a mubtadaʾ and the preposition phrase before it is its khabar, the clause being a naʿt, either in the position of the genitive or of the accusative according to what was said above. However, the first aspect is preferable, because the basic principle is to describe with single words rather than with clauses. A pronoun must be assumed to be omitted, i.e. "in every ear of them", meaning: of the ears.

The majority read «مئة» in the nominative as stated, and it was read in the accusative. Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed two aspects for the accusative. The first: by an implied verb, i.e. "it grew" or "it brought forth". The second: that it is a badal (substitute) of «سبع». This is open to consideration, because it would be either a substitute of the whole for the whole, or of part for whole, or of inclusion. The first is not sound, because the hundred is not the seven ears themselves. The second is not sound either, because of the absence of a pronoun referring back to the substituted-for term; and even if it be granted that the pronoun is not a condition, the hundred is not a part of the seven, because the thing contained is not a part of the container, and the ear is a container for the grain — do you not see His saying {فِي كُلِّ سُنبُلَةٍ مِّئَةُ حَبَّةٍ}, so He made the ear a vessel for the grain? The third is also not sound because of the absence of the pronoun; and even if that is granted, what contains «مئة حبة» is one ear out of seven ears — unless it is said that what contains the container of a thing itself contains that thing: the ear contains a hundred, and the ear is contained by the seven ears, so it follows that the seven contain «مئة حبة». Easier than all of this is that there is an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "the grain of seven ears"; on this basis «مئة حبة» is a badal of part for whole.

semin-durr:247-247.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {طَالُوتَ مَلِكاً}: «مَلِكاً» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «طالوت», so the governor (ʿāmil) of the ḥāl is «بَعَثَ». Concerning «طالوتُ» there are two views. The more evident of them is that it is a foreign (aʿjamī) noun, and for that reason it is a diptote, on account of the two causes, I mean proper-nounhood (ʿalamiyya) and personal foreignness (al-ʿujma al-shakhṣiyya). The second is that it is derived from al-ṭūl (tallness), its pattern being faʿalūt like rahabūt and raḥamūt, its origin being ṭawalūt; the wāw was changed into an alif because it was vowelled and the letter before it took a fatḥa. It is as though what led the one holding this view to it is what is related in the story, that he was the tallest man of his time. However, this view is rejected on the ground that, had it been derived from al-ṭūl, it ought to have been fully declinable, since there is nothing in it but proper-nounhood. They have answered this by saying that, even though it is not foreign, it resembles the foreign, in that there is nothing among the morphological patterns of the Arabs on this form; this is like what they said about ḥamdūn and sarāwīl, and Yaʿqūb and Isḥāq according to whoever makes the latter two from saḥaqa and ʿaqib, and this has preceded.

His words: {أنى يَكُونُ لَهُ الملك}: concerning «أنَّى» there are two aspects. The first is that it means "how" (kayfa), and this is the correct one. The second is that it means "from where" (min ayna); Abū al-Baqāʾ permitted it, but the meaning is not on it. Its position is the accusative as a ḥāl, and the discussion of what its governor is will come. Concerning «يكون» there are two aspects. The first is that it is complete (tāmma), «الملك» is a fāʿil (agent) of it, «له» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to it, and «علينا» is attached to «الملك»: you say «فلان مَلَك على بني فلان أمرَهم» ("so-and-so held rule over the affairs of the tribe of so-and-so"), so this root is made transitive with «على». It may also be attached to something omitted, as a ḥāl from «المُلْك»; and «يكون» is what governs «أنَّى». Neither of the two adverbial phrases, I mean «له» and «علينا», may govern it, because it would be a semantic governor (ʿāmil maʿnawī), and a ḥāl does not precede a semantic governor according to the well-known view. The second is that it is deficient (nāqiṣa), «له» is the khabar (predicate), and «علينا» is attached either to what this khabar is attached to, or to something omitted as a ḥāl from «المُلك» as preceded — the governor of this ḥāl being «يكون» according to whoever permits deficient «كان» to govern the adverbial and what resembles it — or to «المُلْك» itself, as its exposition has preceded; and the governor of «أنَّى» is also what the khabar is attached to. «علينا» may also be the khabar, with «له» accusative as a ḥāl, its governor being the notion of settledness (al-istiqrār) to which the khabar is attached, as its exposition has preceded, or «يكون» according to whoever permits that for the deficient one. I have not seen anyone who permitted «أنى» to be in the position of the accusative as the khabar of «يكون», in the sense of «كيف يكون الملك علينا له» ("how could kingship over us belong to him?"); yet were that said, it would be impossible neither in meaning nor in grammatical technique.

His words: {وَنَحْنُ أَحَقُّ} is a ḥāl clause, and «بالمُلْك» and «منه» are both attached to «أحقُّ». {وَلَمْ يُؤْتَ سَعَةً}: this verbal clause is conjoined to the nominal clause before it, so it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl; the wāw entered upon the imperfect because it is negated. «سعةً» is the second object of «يُؤْتَ», and the first has taken the place of the fāʿil (i.e. it is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent)).

The pattern of «سَعَةً» is «عَلَة», with the first radical (fāʾ) elided, its origin being «وُسْعَة». The fāʾ was elided in the maṣdar (verbal noun) only by analogy with the imperfect, and it was elided in the imperfect only because it fell between a yāʾ — the prefix of the imperfect — and an implied kasra. That is because «وَسِع» is like «وَثِق», so its imperfect ought properly to come on yafʿil with a kasra on the middle radical; what prevented that in «يَسَع» is only that its final radical is a guttural letter, so the middle radical of its imperfect was given a fatḥa for that reason, even though its origin is the kasra. Hence we said: between a yāʾ and an implied kasra. The evidence for that is that they said wajila yawjalu and did not elide it, since the fatḥa there is original, not incidental, unlike the fatḥa of «يَسَع» and «يَهَب» and their class.

If it is said: we have seen them elide this wāw even when it does not fall between a yāʾ and a kasra, namely when the imperfect prefix is a hamza, as in «أَعِدُ», or a tāʾ, as in «تَعِد», or a nūn, as in «نَعِد», and likewise in the imperative and the maṣdar, as in «عِدْ عِدة حسنةً» ("make a good promise"), the answer is that this is by analogy with the imperfect with the yāʾ, so as to keep the class uniform, just as preceded for us regarding the elision of the hamza of afʿala when it becomes an imperfect, because of the hamza of the first person, after which the rest of the class was assimilated to it.

The sīn of «السَّعة» was given a fatḥa since it had a fatḥa in the imperfect because of the guttural letter, just as the ʿayn of «عِدة» was given a kasra since it had a kasra in «يَعِد». [Translator's note: in «عِدة» the kasra is on the first letter of the maṣdar, which corresponds to the middle radical of يَعِد; the source says "ʿayn", translated as written.] However, wahaba yahabu hiba poses a difficulty for this, for they gave the hāʾ a kasra in the maṣdar even though it has a fatḥa in the imperfect because the middle radical is a guttural letter. There is no difference between «يَهَب» and «يَسَع» in the fatḥa being incidental and the kasra implied, yet the hāʾ is given a kasra in «هِبة», whereas it ought properly to have had a fatḥa, as it has a fatḥa in the imperfect, like «سَعَة».

Concerning «من المال» there are two aspects. The first is that it is attached to «يُؤْتَ». The second is that it is attached to something omitted, because it is a naʿt (adjective) of «سَعَة», i.e. "an abundance that is of wealth".

His words: {فِي العلم}: there are two aspects concerning it. The first is that it is attached to «بَسْطَة», as in your saying «بَسَطْتُ له في كذا» ("I gave him ample scope in such-and-such"). The second is that it is attached to something omitted, because it is a naʿt of «بَسْطَة», i.e. an abundance settled or existing [in knowledge].

Concerning «واسعٌ» there are three aspects. The first is that it is by way of relation (al-nasab), i.e. possessing abundance of mercy, like their saying lābin and tāmir, i.e. one who has dates and milk. The second is that it came with the omission of the augment letters from awsaʿa, its origin being mūsiʿ; but this expression is used by the grammarians only for maṣdars, so they say: a maṣdar "with the omission of the augment letters". The third is that it is an active participle from the triliteral «وَسِع». Abū al-Baqāʾ said: the implied form on this view is "vast in forbearance", because you say «وَسِعَ حلمُه» ("his forbearance was vast").

semin-durr:284-284.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {فَيَغْفِرُ}. Ibn ʿĀmir and ʿĀṣim read «يغفرُ» and «يعذبُ» in the nominative (rafʿ), and the rest of the Seven read them in the jussive (jazm). Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Aʿraj and Abū Ḥaywa read «فيغفرَ» in the accusative (naṣb).

As for the nominative, it may be nominative by way of resumption (istiʾnāf), and in this there are two possibilities. The first: that it is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. «فهو يغفرُ» "so He forgives". The second: that this is a verbal clause, made up of a verb and its fāʿil (agent), conjoined to what precedes it. As for the jussive, it is by conjunction with the jussive apodosis (jazāʾ).

As for the accusative, it is by implying «أَنْ», and it together with what falls within its scope is in the sense of a maṣdar (verbal noun) conjoined to the maṣdar imagined from the verb before it, its implied form being: "there will be a reckoning, then forgiveness and punishment". The saying of al-Nābigha has been transmitted with all three forms, namely:

1144 - فإنْ يَهْلِكْ أبو قابوسَ يَهْلِكْ ... ربيعُ الناسِ والبلدُ الحرامُ
ونأخذْ بعدَه بذِنابِ عيشٍ ... أجَبَّ الظهرِ ليسَ له سَنامُ
(If Abū Qābūs perishes, the spring of the people and the sacred land perish; and after him we shall cling to the tail end of a life, like a camel with a flattened back that has no hump.)

with «نأخذ» in the jussive by conjunction with «يَهْلك ربيع», and in the accusative and the nominative, according to what I mentioned to you regarding «فَيغفر». This is a consistent rule: whenever a verb occurs after the apodosis of a condition, following a fāʾ or a wāw, these three forms are permitted in it; but if it stands between the condition and the apodosis, its jussive and accusative are permitted and its nominative is barred, as in: «إن تأتني فَتَزُرْني» or «فتزورَني», or «وتزرْني» or «وتزورَني» ("If you come to me and visit me…").

Al-Juʿfī, Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif and Khallād read «يَغْفِرْ» dropping the fāʾ, and it is likewise in the codex (muṣḥaf) of ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd]. It is a badal (substitute) from the apodosis, like His saying, the Exalted: {وَمَن يَفْعَلْ ذلك يَلْقَ أَثَاماً يُضَاعَفْ لَهُ العذاب} [al-Furqān: 68-69]. Abū al-Fatḥ [Ibn Jinnī] said: "It is a substitute from «يُحاسِبْكم», so it is an explanation (tafsīr) of the reckoning." The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "It is not an explanation; rather, both [forgiveness and punishment] are consequent upon the reckoning." Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The meaning of this substitution is the detailing of the reckoning as a whole, because the detailed is clearer than the summary; so it runs along the lines of the substitute of part for whole or the substitute of inclusion (badal al-ishtimāl), as when you say «ضربتُ زيداً رأسه» 'I struck Zayd, his head' and «أحببتُ زيداً عقله» 'I loved Zayd, his intellect'. This substitution occurs in verbs just as it occurs in nouns, because both categories need clarification."

The Shaykh said: "There is some room for dispute in this. As for the first point, his saying 'The meaning of this substitution is the detailing of the reckoning as a whole': punishment and forgiveness are not a detailing of the reckoning as a whole, because the reckoning is only the enumeration of a person's good deeds and bad deeds and their full accounting, such that nothing of them escapes; forgiveness and punishment are consequent upon the reckoning, so the reckoning is not detailed by forgiveness and punishment. As for the second point, it is his saying, after he had mentioned the substitute of part for whole and the substitute of inclusion: 'This substitution occurs in verbs just as it occurs in nouns, because both categories need clarification.' As for the substitute of inclusion, it is possible and it has occurred, because the verb denotes a genus under which there are species that it includes; for that reason, when negation falls upon it, all of its species are negated. As for the substitute of part for whole, it is not possible in the verb, since the verb does not admit of division; so it cannot be said of a verb that it has a whole and a part except by a far-fetched figure of speech. It is not like the noun in this respect. For that reason the existence of the substitute of part for whole is impossible with respect to Allah the Exalted, since the Creator, the Exalted, is not divided and has no parts."

I say: I do not know what prevents forgiveness and punishment from being an explanation or a detailing of the reckoning, when that is the result of the reckoning; and al-Zamakhsharī's wording carries the same meaning as Ibn Jinnī's wording. As for his saying: "The substitute of part for whole in the verb is impossible, since no division is realized in it", that is not evident, because wholeness and partness hold true of a genus and its species: the genus is a whole and the species is a part. As for his analogy with the Creator, the Exalted, I do not know what connects the two. And there was in al-Zamakhsharī's words something more deserving of objection. For he said: "Al-Aʿmash read «يَغْفر» without a fāʾ, in the jussive, as a substitute from «يحاسِبْكم», like his saying:

1145 - متى تَأْتِنا تُلْمِمْ بنا في ديارِنا ... تَجِدْ حَطَباً جَزْلاً وناراً تَأَجَّجا
(Whenever you come to us, alighting with us in our dwellings, you will find thick firewood and a fire blazing.)"

This is open to question, because it does not agree with what he mentioned after that, as already reported from him: in the verse the substitution is from the verb of the condition (fiʿl al-sharṭ), not from its apodosis, whereas in the verse [of the Quran] the substitution is from the apodosis itself. But what unites the two is that the second is a substitute for what precedes it and a clarification of it.

Abū ʿAmr read with assimilation (idghām) of the rāʾ into the lām, and the rest with it pronounced distinctly (iẓhār). Here Ibn Kathīr — with a disagreement in the transmission from him — and Warsh from Nāfiʿ pronounced the bāʾ distinctly before the mīm, and the rest with assimilation. Some people have attacked the reading of Abū ʿAmr, because the assimilation of rāʾ into lām is weak in their view.

Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: 'How does the one who reads with the jussive read it?' I say: he pronounces the rāʾ distinctly and assimilates the bāʾ. The one who assimilates the rāʾ into the lām commits a solecism (lāḥin) and is grossly mistaken, and the one who transmits it from Abū ʿAmr is mistaken twice over, because he commits a solecism and attributes to the most learned of people in Arabic something that betokens great ignorance. The cause of these transmissions is the transmitters' lack of precision, and the cause of the lack of precision is lack of understanding; and none but the grammarians can be precise about such things."

[Translator's note: the source prints «لا حنٌ», evidently «لاحنٌ» "one who commits a solecism", and it is translated as such.]

I say: This from Abū al-Qāsim [al-Zamakhsharī] is not acceptable, since the Quran readers are devoted to this matter, for they received it from their shaykhs letter by letter — so how could their precision be little? It is something perceived through the sense of hearing. What prevents the assimilation of rāʾ into lām and nūn is the trilling (takrīr) of the rāʾ and its strength, and the stronger is not assimilated into the weaker. This is the doctrine of the Basrans: al-Khalīl, Sībawayh and those who followed them. But al-Farrāʾ, al-Kisāʾī, al-Ruʾāsī and Yaʿqūb al-Ḥaḍramī permitted it, as did the head of the Basrans, Abū ʿAmr. His saying, "This transmission is an error attributed to him", is not to be conceded. Then the Shaykh cited many quotations from the readers, which are stated in their books; I did not see any benefit in mentioning them here, since their sum is summarized in what I have mentioned. How can it be said that the one who transmits that from Abū ʿAmr is mistaken twice over, when among its transmitters is al-Yazīdī, an imam of grammar and lexicon, who used to contend with al-Kisāʾī for his leadership, and whose standing is well known among the people of this field?

semin-durr:262-262.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {الذين يُنْفِقُونَ}: there are two aspects regarding it. The first: that it is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is the clause in His saying: «لهم أجرُهم». The mubtadaʾ here was not made to include the sense of a condition, and for that reason the fāʾ did not enter its khabar, because the intent of this clause is to explain the clause before it: the clause before it was presented as something established and settled, namely the likening of their spending to the grain mentioned, so this clause came likewise, and the khabar in it was presented as something established and fixed, not needing to make the deserving of it dependent on the occurrence of something else before it.

The second: that «الذين» is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "they are those who spend". On this basis there are two aspects regarding His saying «لهم أجرُهم». The first: it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). The second — and it is preferable — that it is resumptive, a clause with no grammatical position, as though it were the answer to someone asking: "Do they have a reward?"

He conjoined with «ثم» following what is most usual, because the one who gives charity for other than the sake of Allah does not usually reproach immediately after his charity, nor cause hurt straight away; so this followed what is usual, even though the ruling on reproach and hurt occurring right after the charity is the same.

Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The meaning of «ثُمَّ» is to show the disparity between spending and refraining from reproach and hurt, and that refraining from them is better than the spending itself, just as He made steadfastness in faith better than entering into it, by His saying: {ثُمَّ استقاموا} [Fuṣṣilat: 30]." So he made it denote remoteness in rank, not in time, and he has repeated this more than once.

«ما» in His saying «ما أَنْفَقُوا» may be a nominal relative, in which case the referent pronoun is omitted, i.e. "what they spent it"; or it may be maṣdarī, in which case it needs no referent, i.e. "they do not follow up their spending". There must be an omission after «مَنَّاً», i.e. "reproach towards the one spent upon, and no hurt to him"; it was omitted because it is indicated.

«المَنُّ» is counting a favour against someone; its original meaning is cutting, and for that reason it is applied to a benefaction, because the benefactor cuts off a portion of his wealth for the beneficiary. «المَنُّ» is also diminishing a right, and «المَنُّ» is the weight used for weighing; in this sense one also says «منا», like «عَصَا». The derivation of «الأذى» has already been discussed.

«مَنَّاً» is a second object, and «لا أذى» is conjoined to it. Far-fetched is the one who made «ولا أذى» resumptive and made it one of the attributes of the one giving charity, as though He said: "those who spend and are not hurt by spending", so that «أذى» would be the noun of lā and its khabar omitted, i.e. "and no hurt befalls them", making it a negated clause with the meaning of prohibition. This is strained, and this person ought to read «ولا أذى» with an alif and without nunation, because it would be indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa according to the well-known doctrine of the grammarians.

semin-durr:263-263.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {قَوْلٌ مَّعْرُوفٌ}: there are three aspects regarding it. The first: it is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and beginning with an indefinite noun is permitted because it is described and because something is conjoined to it. «مغفرةٌ» is conjoined to it, and what permits beginning with it is the conjunction or an implied adjective, since the implied form is "and forgiveness from the one who asks" or "from Allah". «خيرٌ» is the khabar (predicate) of both. [Abū al-Baqāʾ said on this aspect: "The implied form is: and the cause of forgiveness], because forgiveness is from Allah the Exalted, so there is no comparison of superiority between it and the act of the servant. It is also possible that the forgiveness is the giver's overlooking and bearing with the poor man, in which case there is no omitted muḍāf."

The second: that «قولٌ معروفٌ» is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, i.e. "is more fitting" or "more appropriate for you", and «مغفرةٌ» is a mubtadaʾ and «خيرٌ» its khabar, so they are two clauses. Al-Mahdawī and others mentioned it. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "This takes away the splendour of the meaning." The third: that it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "what is commanded is a kind word".

His saying: {يَتْبَعُهَآ أَذًى} is in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of «صدقة». He did not mention reproach again, saying "followed by reproach and hurt", because hurt includes reproach and other things. It was mentioned explicitly in His saying {لاَ يُتْبِعُونَ مَآ أَنْفَقُواُ مَنّاً وَلاَ أَذًى} because of how frequently it occurs among those who give charity and how hard it is for them to guard against it; for that reason it was put before hurt.

semin-durr:248-248.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {أَن يَأْتِيَكُمُ التابوت}: «أَنْ» and what falls within its scope are in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of «إنَّ», its implied form being: "the sign of his kingship is the Ark's coming to you."

Concerning «التابوتِ» there are two views. The first is that it is fāʿūl, and no derivation of it is known. The one holding this view refused that its pattern be faʿalūt, derived from tāba yatūbu, like malakūt from al-mulk and rahabūt from al-rahb; he said: because the meaning does not support that. The second view is that its pattern is faʿalūt like malakūt; [its holder] made it derived from al-tawb, which is returning, and held its meaning sound in it, because the tābūt is the chest in which things are placed, and its owner returns to it when he needs it; so we have found in it the meaning of returning.

The well-known practice is to pause on its tāʾ with a tāʾ, without changing it into a hāʾ, because it is either radical, if its pattern is fāʿūl, or augmentative for something other than femininity, as in malakūt. Some change it into a hāʾ, and it has been read that way as an irregular (shādhdh) reading: Ubayy and Zayd ibn Thābit read it so, and it is the dialect of the Anṣār. It is related that when they were writing the codices in the time of ʿUthmān, may Allah be pleased with him, they disagreed about it: Zayd said, "With the hāʾ", and [Ubayy] said, "With the tāʾ". [Translator's note: the bracketed name is in the source; elsewhere the story is usually told of Zayd and the Qurashī scribes.] So they came to ʿUthmān, who said: "Write it according to the dialect of Quraysh", meaning with the tāʾ.

Is this hāʾ radical in its own right, so that there are two dialectal forms of the word, its pattern on this view being fāʿūl and nothing else; or is it a substitute for the tāʾ because it is close to it, the two sharing voicelessness (al-hams); or is it treated in the manner of the tāʾ of the feminine? Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: what is the pattern of al-tābūt? I say: it must be either faʿalūt or fāʿūl. It cannot be fāʿūl because of the rarity of [words] like salis and qaliq" — meaning that identity of the first and final radicals in form is very rare — "and because it is an unknown composition" — meaning among the Arabic patterns — "and the known may not be abandoned [for it]. So it is faʿalūt from al-tawb, which is returning, because it is a receptacle in which things are deposited, and it is returned to at every time."

As for whoever read it with the hāʾ, it is fāʿūl in his view, except for whoever makes its hāʾ a substitute for the tāʾ because the two share voicelessness and because both are among the letters of augmentation; for that reason the tāʾ of the feminine was replaced by it.

His words: {فِيهِ سَكِينَةٌ}: «فيه» alone may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «التابوت», so that it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to something omitted, and «سكينة» is nominative as its fāʿil (agent), its governor being the notion of settledness (al-istiqrār); the ḥāl here is of the class of single words. «فيه» may also be a fronted khabar and «سكينةٌ» a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject), the clause being in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl; the ḥāl here is of the class of clauses. «سكينةٌ» is faʿīla from al-sukūn (stillness), and it is gravity/composure (al-waqār). Abū al-Sammāl read it with a doubled kāf; al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is strange."

His words: {مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ}: it may be attached to something omitted as a naʿt (adjective) of «سكينة», its position being the nominative. It may also be attached to the same notion of settledness to which «فيه» is attached. «مِنْ» may be for the beginning of the extent (ibtidāʾ al-ghāya) or partitive (tabʿīḍ). And there is an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "of the tranquillities of your Lord".

The pattern of «بَقِيَّة» is faʿīla, and the origin is baqīya with two yāʾs, the first augmentative and the second the final radical of the word; then they were assimilated. One may not infer that the final radical of «بَقِيَّة» is a yāʾ from their saying «بَقِيَ» in the past tense, because a wāw preceded by a kasra is changed into a yāʾ: do you not see that «رَضِي» and «شَقِيَ» are originally from wāw — al-shiqwa and al-riḍwān?

«مِمَّا تَرَك» is in the position of the nominative because it is a naʿt of «بَقَيَّة», so it is attached to something omitted, i.e. "a remnant existing…". «مِنْ» is partitive, i.e. "of the remnants of your Lord" [Translator's note: so in the source; one would expect "of what … left"]. «ما» is a nominal relative noun; it is neither an indefinite noun nor maṣdar-forming.

«آل» has already been discussed. It is said that here it is redundant (zāʾida), as in his words:

1022 - بثينةُ من آلِ النساءِ وإنَّما ... يَكُنَّ لوصلٍ لا وصالَ لغائِبِ
(Buthayna is of the "folk" of women; and women are only for one who is present to unite with — there is no union for one who is absent.)

He means: Buthayna is one of the women. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It may mean: of what Mūsā and Hārūn left, the āl being inserted to magnify their standing", i.e. redundant for glorification. The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] found it problematic how magnification is conveyed by the addition of āl. «هارون» is foreign. It is said that it does not occur in anything of the language of the Arabs; al-Rāghib said this, meaning its root does not occur in their language.

His words: {تَحْمِلُهُ الملائكة}: this clause may have a grammatical position, as a ḥāl from «التابوت», i.e. borne by the angels; or it may have no position, because it is resumptive (mustaʾnafa), since it is the answer to an implied question, as though it were said: "How will it come?", and it was said: "The angels will carry it."

Mujāhid read «يَحْمِلُه» with the lower-dotted yāʾ, because the verb is predicated of a broken plural, so both options are permissible in its verb. «ذلك» is a demonstrative pointing, it is said, to the Ark; it is also said, to its coming, and this is better, so that the end of the verse corresponds to its beginning. As for «إنْ», the more evident view is that it keeps its proper function of being conditional, its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) being omitted. It is also said that it means «إذ» ("since").

semin-durr:148-148.t:
The words of the Exalted: {وَلِكُلٍّ وِجْهَةٌ}: the majority of the readers read «كل» with tanwīn, and its tanwīn is in compensation for the muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct). The preposition [with its noun] is a fronted khabar (predicate), and «وِجْهَةٌ» is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject). There is disagreement over the omitted muḍāf ilayhi of «كل»: it was said that its implied form is "and for every group of the followers of the religions", and it was said: "and for the people of every place among the Muslims there is their direction towards the Kaaba", to the right, to the left, behind and in front.

There are two views on «وِجْهَة». One of them — attributed to al-Mubarrad, al-Fārisī and al-Māzinī in one of his two opinions — is that it is a noun of place, [denoting] the place towards which one turns; on this view retaining the wāw is regular, since it is not a maṣdar (verbal noun). Sībawayh said: "If you formed fiʿla from al-waʿd you would say wiʿda, and if you formed a maṣdar you would say ʿida." The second: that it is a maṣdar; this is attributed to al-Māzinī and it is the apparent sense of Sībawayh's words, for after mentioning the dropping of the wāw from maṣdars he said: "But they have retained it, saying wijha for jiha." On this view retaining the wāw is anomalous (shādhdh), drawing attention to the abandoned original form in ʿida and the like. What appears [to me] is that what permitted retaining the wāw, even though it is a maṣdar, is that it is a maṣdar formed with the augmenting letters dropped, since the verbs heard from this root are tawajjaha and ittajaha, whose maṣdars are al-tawajjuh and al-ittijāh, and its verb has not been heard as wajaha yajihu like waʿada yaʿidu. What necessitated dropping the wāw from ʿida and zina was modelling them on the imperfect, because [there] the wāw falls between a yāʾ and a kasra; but here no imperfect has been heard on which its maṣdar could be modelled. That is why I said that «وِجْهَة» is a maṣdar of tawajjaha or ittajaha with the augmenting letters dropped. Abū al-Baqāʾ touched on something of this.

His words: {هُوَ مُوَلِّيهَا}: a clause of mubtadaʾ and khabar, in the position of the nominative because it is a naʿt (adjective) of وِجْهَة. There are two views on «هو». One of them: that it refers back to the wording of «كل», not its meaning, which is why it is singular; the second object is omitted because the meaning is understood, its implied form being "he is turning his face — or himself — towards it". This is supported by the reading of Ibn ʿĀmir «مُوَلاَّها», in the passive (mā lam yusamma fāʿiluhu), as will come. The second: that it refers back to Allah the Exalted, i.e. Allah is the one who turns him — that is, that group — towards the qibla.

The majority read «مُوَلِّيها» as an active participle, and it has already been mentioned that one of its two objects is omitted. Ibn ʿĀmir read — and it is attributed to Ibn ʿAbbās — مُوَلاَّها as a passive participle; in it there is a nominative pronoun standing in the place of the agent (as nāʾib fāʿil), and the second [object] is the pronoun attached to it, namely «ها», which refers back to the direction (al-wijha) — and it was said: to the turning (al-tawliya); Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned that. On this reading «هو» must refer to the group, since it is impossible in meaning for it to refer to Allah the Exalted. [Translator's note: the printed text has «بتعيَّن», evidently for «يتعيَّن» ("must"); translated accordingly.] Some read «ولكلِّ وِجْهَةٍ» with the genitive construct, and it is attributed to Ibn ʿĀmir. They disagreed about it on three views. The first — the view of al-Ṭabarī — is that it is an error; and this is nothing, since venturing to declare erroneous what is established from the imams is not an easy matter.

The second — the view of al-Zamakhsharī and Abū al-Baqāʾ — is that the lām is in origin redundant (zāʾida). al-Zamakhsharī said: "The meaning is: and every direction Allah is the one who turns [people] towards it; the lām was added because the object is fronted, as when you say: li-Zaydin ḍarabtu ('Zayd I struck'), and li-Zaydin abūhu ḍāribuhu ('Zayd, his father is striking him')."

The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: This is unsound, because when the governing word is transitive to the pronoun of a noun, it is not transitive to the overt form of that noun put in the genitive by the lām. You do not say: li-Zaydin ḍarabtuhu, nor: li-Zaydin anā ḍāribuhu, lest one of two forbidden things follow: either that the governing word would be both strong and weak — strong in that it is transitive to the pronoun by itself and weak in that it is transitive to the overt noun through the lām — or that a verb transitive to one object would become transitive to two. That is why the grammarians interpreted what gives the impression of this, namely the verse:

771 - هذا سُراقَةُ للقرآنِ يَدْرُسُه ... والمرءُ عند الرُّشا إنْ يَلْقَهَا ذِيْبُ
(This is Surāqa, studying the Qurʾān; yet a man, when he meets bribes, is a wolf.)

as meaning that the pronoun in «يدرسه» is for the maṣdar, i.e. "he studies the study", not for the Qurʾān, because the verb is already transitive to [the Qurʾān]. As for his example "li-Zaydin ḍarabtu", it is not parallel to the verse, because in this example [the verb] is not transitive to [Zayd's] pronoun. Nor may the question be treated as one of ishtighāl (preoccupation of the verb), by supposing a governing word for «لكلِّ وِجْهةٍ» which «مُولِّيها» explains, because when the pronoun of the noun from which [the verb] is preoccupied is put in the genitive by a preposition, that noun is made accusative by a verb that agrees in meaning with the overt governing word, and it is not permissible to put the preoccupied-from noun in the genitive with a preposition. You say: Zaydan marartu bihi, i.e. "I had to do with Zayd — I passed by him", but you may not say: li-Zaydin marartu bihi. The Exalted said: {والظالمين أَعَدَّ لَهُمْ} [al-Insān: 31], and [the poet] said:

772 - أثعلبَةَ الفوارسٍ أم رياحا ... عَدَلْتَ بهم طُهَيَّةَ والخِشابا
(Is it Thaʿlaba of the horsemen, or Riyāḥ, that you have equated with Ṭuhayya and al-Khishāb?)

So he brought the preoccupied-from noun in the accusative. As for his example "li-Zaydin abūhu ḍāribuhu", it is a non-Arabic construction. [End of the Shaykh's words.]

The third: that «لكلِّ وجهةٍ» is attached to His words «فاستبقوا الخيراتِ», i.e. "so race towards good things for every direction", and it was only placed before the governing word out of concern for it, just as the object is fronted; Ibn ʿAṭiyya mentioned this. It is not permissible to account for this reading by taking «لكلِّ وجهةٍ» as being in the position of the second object of مولِّيها, the first object being the [pronoun] to which the active participle «مُوَلٍّ» is annexed, namely «ها», referring back to the groups, the implied form being: "and every direction Allah is the one who turns the groups, the people of the qiblas, [towards it]", with the lām added to the object because it is fronted and because the governing word is a derived (secondary) one — because the grammarians stated explicitly that adding the lām of strengthening is not permissible except with a verb transitive to one object only, and «مُوَلٍّ» is among those transitive to two, so that is ruled out for it. This impediment is what prevents answering on al-Zamakhsharī's behalf against the Shaykh's objection that when the verb is transitive to the overt noun it is not transitive to its pronoun. [The answer] would have been possible — that the pronoun attached to «مُوَلّ» is not the pronoun of the object but the pronoun of the maṣdar, namely the turning (al-tawliya), and the first object is omitted, the implied form being: Allah is «مُولِّي التوليةِ» — the one who effects the turning — of every direction to its people; then, when the object was fronted before the governing word, it was strengthened with the lām — were it not that they stated explicitly that adding it is forbidden with verbs transitive to two or three objects.

His words: {فاستبقوا الخيرات}: «الخيرات» is accusative by removal of the preposition, the implied form being "towards (إلى) the good things", as in the verse of al-Rāʿī:

773 - ثنائي عليكم آلَ حربٍ ومَنْ يَمِلْ ... سِواكمْ فإني مُهْتَدٍ غيرُ مائِلِ
(My praise is for you, O family of Ḥarb; and whoever inclines to others than you — I am rightly guided, not inclining.)

i.e. "towards others than you". That is because «استبق» either has the sense of the bare verb sabaqa or the sense of tasābaqa. It cannot be in the sense of sabaqa, because the meaning is not "outstrip the good things"; so it remains that it is in the sense of tasābaqa ("race one another"), which is not transitive by itself.

al-Khayrāt is the plural of khayra, and there are two possibilities for both: one is that it is lightened from «خَيِّرَة» with the doubled [yāʾ], on the pattern fayʿila, as mayt from mayyit; the second is that it is not lightened but is established on the pattern faʿla, like jafna. One says: rajulun khayrun and imraʾatun khayrun. On both suppositions they are not [forms] of preference (tafḍīl). al-Sabq is reaching something first; its origin is going ahead in travelling, and then it was used figuratively for every going ahead.

His words: {أَيْنَ مَا تَكُونُواْ}: «أين» is a conditional noun that puts two verbs in the jussive, like إنْ, and «ما» is added to it optionally. It is an adverb of place, and here it is in the position of the accusative as the khabar of kāna; its fronting is obligatory because it contains the meaning of something that has the right to the head of the sentence. «تكونوا» is jussive (majzūm) by it as the condition, and it is what makes [أين] accusative; and «يأتِ» is its apodosis (jawāb). It is also used as an interrogative, and then it governs nothing. It is indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because it contains the meaning of the conditional particle or of the interrogative.

semin-durr:264-264.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {كالذي}: in «كالذي» the kāf is in the position of the accusative. It is said: as a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "do not nullify them with a nullifying like the nullifying of the one who spends to be seen by people". It is said: it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun of the implied maṣdar, as is the view of Sībawayh. And it is said: it is a ḥāl from the fāʿil (agent) of «تُبْطِلُوا», i.e. "do not nullify them, resembling the one who spends for show".

Regarding «رئاءَ» there are three aspects. The first: it is a naʿt of an omitted maṣdar, its implied form being "a spending that is showing off to people"; Makkī mentioned this. The second: it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. "for the sake of being seen by people", and it has fulfilled the conditions for the accusative. The third: it is in the position of a ḥāl, i.e. "he spends, showing off".

The maṣdar here is annexed to its object, which is «الناس». «رئاء» is the maṣdar of «راءى», like «قاتَلَ قِتالاً». Its original form is «رِئايا»: the first hamza is the middle radical of the word, and the second is a substitute for a yāʾ which is the final radical of the word, because it occurred at the end after an augmentative alif. The mufāʿala in «راءى» has its proper sense, because the one who shows off makes people see his deeds so that they show him praise and veneration. Ṭalḥa read — and it is also reported from ʿĀṣim —: «رِياء», changing the first hamza into a yāʾ, and this is the regular way of lightening it, because it is with fatḥa after a kasra.

His saying: {فَمَثَلُهُ كَمَثَلِ} is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). The fāʾ entered — Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "to connect the clause with what precedes it"; something similar was discussed earlier. Regarding the hāʾ in «فَمَثَلُهُ» there are two views. The more evident of them: it refers back to {كالذي يُنْفِقُ مَالَهُ رِئَآءَ الناس}, because it is the nearest thing mentioned. The second: it refers back to the one who reproaches and hurts, as though He, Exalted is He, likened him to two things: to the one who spends for show and to a smooth rock with dust on it; in that case He would have turned from address to the third person, and from plural to singular.

«الصَّفْوان» is a large smooth stone. There are two usages regarding it: the better known has sukūn on the fāʾ, and the second has fatḥa on it; Ibn al-Musayyib and al-Zuhrī read with the latter, and it is anomalous, because «فَعَلان» occurs only in maṣdars, such as «النَّزَوان» and «الغَلَيَان», and in adjectives, such as «رجلٌ طَغَيَان» and «تيسٌ عَدوَان»; in nouns it is very rare. There is disagreement over «صَفْوَان». It is said: it is a plural whose singular is «صَفا»; Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "The plural of «فَعَل» on «فَعْلاَن» is rare." It is said: it is a generic noun; Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "This is the best view, and for that reason the pronoun refers back to it in the singular in His saying «عليه»." And it is said: it is a singular, whose plural is «صُفِيٌّ»; al-Kisāʾī said this, and al-Mubarrad rejected it. He said: "Because «صُفِيّ» is the plural of «صفا», like «عُصِيّ» from «عَصَا» and «قُفِيّ» from «قَفَا»."
[Translator's note: the source says «واحدُ صُفِيٌّ» ("the singular of ṣufiyy"); the sense is that ṣafwān is a singular of which ṣufiyy is the plural.]

It is also transmitted from al-Kisāʾī that he said: "«صَفْوَان» is a singular, and it is pluralised as «صِفْوان» with kasra." Al-Naḥḥās said: "It is also possible that the form with kasra on the ṣād is a singular.
