His saying: {لَهَا مَا كَسَبَتْ}: this clause has no grammatical position because it is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya), and it is like an explanation of what precedes it, because its not being held to account for what another earned, and its bearing only what it itself acquired, are part of its not being burdened with what is beyond its capacity. Does a [difference of] meaning appear between the two different forms of the verb of earning, or not? Some said: Yes, and distinguished them by [saying] that «الكسب» is more general, since one says «كَسَب» "he earned" for himself and for others, while «اكتسب» is more specific, since one does not say «اكتسب لغيرِه» "he earned for another". He recited the saying of al-Ḥuṭayʾa:

1150 - أَلْقَيْتَ كاسِبَهم في قَعْرِ مُظْلِمَةٍ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(You have cast their breadwinner into the depth of a dark [pit]…)

And one says: «هو كاسبُ أهلهِ» "he is his family's earner", but not «مكتسبُ أهلِه».

Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: Why did He assign good to «الكَسْب» and evil to «الاكتساب»? I say: In «الاكتساب» there is exertion (iʿtimāl). Since evil is among what the soul craves, and it is drawn to it and commands it, it is more exertive and more earnest in obtaining it, so for that reason it was made «مكتسبة» in it. And since it is not so in the matter of good, it was described with what carries no indication of exertion."

Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "He repeated the verb of earning and varied its morphological form, for the beauty of the style of the discourse, as the Exalted said: {فَمَهِّلِ الكافرين أَمْهِلْهُمْ} [al-Ṭāriq: 17]. This is one view. What appears to me in this is that good deeds are among what is earned without strain, since the one who earns them is on the highway of Allah's command and the path of His law; whereas bad deeds are «تكتسب», with the form of intensification, since the one who earns them strains himself in their matter to tear through the veil of Allah the Exalted's prohibition and to go beyond [it] to them. So the coming of the two forms in the verse is fitting, in order to secure this meaning." Some said: "There is no difference; the Quran has used «الكسب» and «الاكتساب» in a single context. The Exalted said: {كُلُّ نَفْسٍ بِمَا كَسَبَتْ رَهِينَةٌ} [al-Muddaththir: 38], and the Exalted said: {وَلاَ تَكْسِبُ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ إِلاَّ عَلَيْهَا} [al-Anʿām: 164], and the Exalted said: {بِغَيْرِ مَا اكتسبوا} [al-Aḥzāb: 58]; so He used both «الكَسْب» and «الاكتساب» for evil."

Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "Some people said: There is no difference between them" — and he mentioned something like what has preceded. "Others said: The form iftaʿala indicates intensity of effort, and doing an evil deed is grave because of what it leads to." Al-Wāḥidī said: "What is correct according to the lexicographers is that «الكسب» and «الاكتساب» are one, with no difference between them. Dhū al-Rumma said:

1151 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... ألفَى أباه بذاك الكسبِ يَكْتَسِبُ
(… he found his father earning by that [same] earning.)"

I say: He brought the lām with «الكسب» and «على» with «الاكتساب» only because the lām entails possession, and good is loved and rejoiced in, so with it was brought what entails possession; and since evil is something to be wary of, and it is a weight and a burden on the one who bears it, with it was brought «على», which entails its being upon him.

Someone said: "In it there is an intimation that the least act among acts of good is credited to a person as a generosity from Allah toward His servant, so that what his son does for him without his knowledge reaches him, because it is of his earning in general; unlike punishment, for no one is held to account for it except one who strove and exerted himself in it." This is built on the view that there is a difference between the two forms, and it is the more evident [view].

[Translator's note: the source prints «ابنُ من غيرِ علمِه» and «فإنه فا يُؤَاخَذُ»; «ابنُه» "his son" and «لا يُؤاخَذ» "is not held to account" are evidently intended and are translated as such.]

His saying: {لاَ تُؤَاخِذْنَا} is read with the hamza, and it is from «الأخْذ بالذَّنْب» "taking to task for a sin". It is [also] read with the wāw, and this admits two possibilities. The first: that it is also from «الأخْذ», the hamza having been changed into a wāw because it carries fatḥa and what precedes it carries ḍamma, which is a regular lightening (takhfīf qiyāsī). And it may be from «واخذه» with the wāw; Abū al-Baqāʾ said this. He used here the form of mutuality (mufāʿala) although it is the act of one party, because the wrongdoer has given [others] power over himself and opened the way to himself by his act; so it is as if he helped the one who punishes him for his sin and holds him to it against himself, and thus the form of mutuality was fitting. It may also be of the category of «سافرت» "I travelled", «عاقبت» "I punished" and «طارقت» "I doubled [the sandal]".

Ubayy read: «ربَّنا ولا تُحَمِّلْ علينا إصْراً» with the mīm doubled.

Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: What difference is there between this doubled [form] and the one in «ولا تُحَمِّلْنا»? I say: This one is for intensification in «حَمَّل عليه», and that one is for transferring «حَمَلَه» from one object to two objects." End of quotation. He means that the doubling in the first is for intensification, and for that reason it is transitive to only one object; and in the second it is for transitivization, and for that reason it is transitive to two, the first of which is «نا» and the second {مَا لاَ طَاقَةَ لَنَا بِهِ}.

[Translator's note: the source prints «أولُهما «ن»»; the pronoun «نا» "us" is evidently intended.]

«الإِصْر» is in origin weight and hardship. Al-Nābigha said:

1152 - يا مانعَ الضَّيْمِ أَنْ يَغْشَى سَرَاتَهُمُ ... والحاملَ الإِصرِ عنهم بعد ما عَرِقُوا
(O you who prevent injustice from overtaking their nobles, and who carry the burden off them after they have sweated.)

It has been applied to the covenant and the pledge because of their weight, as in His saying, the Exalted: {وَأَخَذْتُمْ على ذلكم إِصْرِي} [Āl ʿImrān: 81], i.e. "My covenant"; {وَيَضَعُ عَنْهُمْ إِصْرَهُمْ} [al-Aʿrāf: 157], i.e. the onerous obligations. Then it is applied to everything that is heavy, so that it is related from one of them that he explained «الإِصر» here as the gloating of enemies, and he recited:

1153 - أَشْمَتَّ بيَ الأعداءَ حينَ هَجَرْتَني ... والموتُ دونَ شماتةِ الأَعْدَاءِ
(You made the enemies gloat over me when you abandoned me — and death is easier than the gloating of enemies.)

It is also said that «الإِصْر» is affection and kinship; one says «ما يَأْصِرُني عليه آصِرَةٌ», i.e. "no kinship or womb-tie inclines me toward him". He recited for al-Ḥuṭayʾa:

1154 - عَطَفُوا عليَّ بغير آ ... صِرَةٍ فقد عَظُمَ الأواصِرْ
(They inclined toward me without any tie of kinship — so great are the ties [of their kindness].)

It has been said: «الإِصر» is the thing by which things are tied, and from it is «الإِصار» for the rope with which loads are bound. One says «أَصَرَ يأصِرُ أَصْراً» with fatḥa on the hamza; with kasra it is a noun. It is also said with ḍamma, and it has been read so as an anomalous reading (shādhdh).

Ubayy read: {وَلاَ تُحَمِّل عَلَيْنَآ} with doubling, as an intensification of the act.

«الطاقَة» is the ability to do a thing. It is in origin a maṣdar that came with the omission of the augment letters; by right it should have been «إطاقة», since it is from «أَطَاق», but it is anomalous, as a few small words are anomalous, such as «أَغار غارةً» and «أَجابَ جابةً»; they said «ساء سمعاً فساءَ جابة» "He heard badly, so he answered badly". It is not analogically extended, so one does not say «طال طالة». A parallel of «أجابَ جابةً» is {أَنبَتَكُمْ مِّنَ الأرض نَبَاتاً} [Nūḥ: 17], and «أعطى عَطاءً» in his saying:

1155 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... وبعدَ عطائِك المئةَ الرِّتاعا
(… and after your giving the hundred grazing [camels].)

His saying, the Exalted: {مَوْلاَنَا}: «المَوْلَى» is the mafʿal form from «وَلِي يَلِي». Here it is a maṣdar by which the agent is meant; so it may be on the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "the One in charge of our protection", i.e. our support — and for that reason He said «فانصُرْنا». «المَوْلَى» may also be a noun of place and a noun of time.

His saying, the Exalted: {فانصرنا}: He brought the fāʾ here to signal causation, because since Allah the Exalted is their Patron, the Owner of their affairs and their Disposer, it followed from that that they called upon Him to give them victory over their enemies; as when you say: «أنت الجوادُ فتكرَّمْ عليَّ وأنت البطلُ فاحْمِ حَرَمَك» "You are the generous one, so be generous to me; and you are the hero, so protect your sanctuary."

This sūra has comprised many kinds of knowledge, most of which have been pointed out; and the intelligent person is spared the need for explicit statement by an allusion.

semin-durr:234-234.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {والذين يُتَوَفَّوْنَ مِنكُمْ} — the verse: there are several views about it. The first: «الذين» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) that has no khabar (predicate); rather, the predication was made about the wives, mention of whom is connected to it, because the discourse concerns them in observing the waiting period; so the khabar came about what is intended, since the meaning is: whoever's husband has died away from her, she waits. Al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ held this, and al-Farrāʾ cited:
995 - لعَلِّيَ إنْ مَالَتْ بِيَ الريحُ مَيْلَةً ... على ابن أبي ذِبَّانَ أَنْ يتندَّما
(Perhaps I — if the wind sways me once against Ibn Abī Dhibbān — [perhaps] he will come to regret.)
He said «لعلي» (perhaps I), then said «أن يتندم» (that he will regret), making the predication about Ibn Abī Dhibbān and leaving the speaker aside, since the implied form is: perhaps Ibn Abī Dhibbān will regret if the wind sways me once. Another said:
996 - بني أسدٍ إنَّ ابن قَيسٍ وقَتْلَه ... بغيرِ دَمٍ دارُ المَذَلَّةِ حُلَّتِ
(O Banū Asad, Ibn Qays and his killing without blood-guilt — the abode of humiliation has been settled.)
He made the predication about his killing, that it is an abode of humiliation, and left aside predicating about Ibn Qays.
The precise statement of the school of al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ is that when a noun is mentioned, and a noun annexed to it is mentioned which carries the sense of the predication, the first is left aside and the predication is made about the second, as in «إنَّ زيداً وأخته منطلقةٌ» (Zayd and his sister — she is departing), the meaning being: Zayd's sister is departing. But the noble verse and the first verse of poetry are not of this type; what he cited by way of likening it to this type is the poet's saying:
997 - فَمَنْ يكُ سائِلاً عني فإني ... وجِرْوَةَ لا تَرُودُ ولا تُعارُ
(Whoever asks about me — I and Jirwa [my mare]: she does not roam and is not lent out.)
The precise statement of this school, its refutation and the interpretation of its proofs belong to a book other than this one.
The second: it has a khabar, namely «يتربَّصْن», and some omission is necessary to make it sound for this clause to be the khabar of the first, since it lacks a linking element (rābiṭ). The implied form is: «وأزواجُ الذين يُتَوفَّوْن يتربَّصْنَ» (and the wives of those who die wait). His saying «ويَذَرون أزواجاً» indicates this omitted element, so the muḍāf was omitted and the muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) put in its place on account of that indication. The third: the khabar is also «يتربَّصْن», but the referent-pronoun (ʿāʾid) was omitted from the speech because something indicates it; the implied form is: «يتربصن بعدهم» (they wait after them) or «بعد موتِهم» (after their death); al-Akhfash said this. The fourth: «يتربَّصْنَ» is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, the implied form being «أزواجُهم يتربَّصْنَ» (their wives wait), and this clause is the khabar of the first; al-Mubarrad said this. The fifth: the khabar is omitted in its entirety before the mubtadaʾ, its implied form being: «فيما يُتْلى عليكم حكمُ الذين يُتَوَفَّوْن» (among what is recited to you is the ruling on those who die), and His saying «يتربَّصْنَ» is a clause clarifying and explaining the ruling, so it has no position in i'rab; this is attributed to Sībawayh. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "Al-Mahdawī related from Sībawayh that the meaning is: «وفيما يُتْلَى عليكم الذين يُتَوَفَّون» (and among what is recited to you: those who die). I do not recognise this that he related, because that is only tenable when there is an imperative wording after the mubtadaʾ, as in His saying, Exalted is He: {والسارق والسارقة فاقطعوا} [al-Māʾida: 38], {الزانية والزاني فاجلدوا} [al-Nūr: 2]. This verse has the meaning of a command but not its wording, so with this implied form it needs another implied form, which is dispensed with when the imperative wording is present." The sixth: part of the clause stands in the place of something annexed to the referent-pronoun of the mubtadaʾ, the implied form being: «والذين يُتَوفَّون منكم ويذرون أزواجاً يتربصُ أزواجُهم» (and those of you who die and leave wives — their wives wait); «أزواجهُم» was omitted in its entirety, and the nūn, which is the pronoun of the wives, stood in their place with the qualification of their being annexed to the pronoun of the mubtadaʾ.
The reading of the majority is «يُتَوَفَّوْنَ», built for what has not had its agent named (i.e. passive). The Commander of the Faithful [Translator's note: i.e. ʿAlī; the source has «مير المؤمنين», with the initial alif dropped] read it — and al-Mufaḍḍal narrated it from ʿĀṣim — with a fatḥa on the yāʾ, built for the agent (active); its meaning is "they complete (yastawfūn) their terms"; Abū al-Qāsim al-Zamakhsharī said this.
What is related — that Abū al-Aswad was behind a funeral bier and a man said to him: "Who is the «متوفِّي»?" with a kasra on the fāʾ [i.e. "the one who takes the soul"], and he said: "Allah"; and that this was one of the causes that moved ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, to order him to compose a book on grammar — [this] is contradicted by this reading.
Possibilities have already been discussed regarding His saying «يَتَرَبَّصْنَ بأنفسِهن ثلاثةَ قُروء»: whether «بأنفسهن» is tawkīd (emphasis) or not, and whether the accusative of «قروء» is as an adverbial or as an object; they apply here.
His saying: {مِنكُمْ} is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the nominative of «يَتَوَفَّوْن», and what governs it is omitted, its implied form being: «حالَ كونِهم منكم» (while they are from among you). «مِنْ» may be partitive or for clarifying the genus.
His saying: {وَعَشْراً}: He only said «عشراً» without the feminine marker in the number for one of several reasons. The first: what is meant is «عَشْر ليال» (ten nights) together with their days; nights were preferred over days in reckoning dates because they come first. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It has been said «عَشْراً» with reference to the nights, the days being included in them. You never see them use the masculine [number form] with reference to days; you say «صُمْت عشراً» (I fasted ten), and if you used the masculine form you would depart from their speech. Among what is clear is His saying, Exalted is He: {إِن لَّبِثْتُمْ إِلاَّ عَشْراً} [Ṭā Hā: 103], {إِن لَّبِثْتُمْ إِلاَّ يَوْماً} [Ṭā Hā: 104]."
The second — and it is the view of al-Mubarrad —: the tāʾ was omitted because the implied form is «عشرُ مُدَدٍ» (ten periods), each period of them being a day and a night. The Arabs say «سِرْنا خمساً» (we travelled five), i.e. between day and night. The poet said:
998 - فطافَتْ ثلاثاً بين يومٍ وليلةٍ ... وكان النكيرُ أَنْ تُضِيفَ وتَجْأرا
(She circled three [periods] between day and night, and her only protest was to take fright and low aloud.)
The third: the counted noun is masculine, namely the days, and the tāʾ was omitted only because when a masculine counted noun is mentioned, the tāʾ must be attached to its number, but when it is omitted in wording, both options are allowed in the number: mentioning the tāʾ and not. Al-Kisāʾī related: «صُمْنَا من الشهرِ خمساً» (we fasted five of the month), and among it is the ḥadīth: «وأتبعَه بستٍّ من شوال» (and follows it with six of Shawwāl). Another said:
999 - وإلاَّ فسيري مثلَ ما سار راكبٌ ... تيمَّمَ خَمْساً ليس في سيره أَمَمْ
(Otherwise, travel as a rider travels who has set out on a five-day journey, with no shortness in his travelling.)
The grammarians stated this explicitly. The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "So there is no need to interpret it as nights or as periods, as al-Zamakhsharī and al-Mubarrad respectively gave its implied form." He said: "When this is established, His saying «وعشراً» came according to one of the two permissible forms. The omission of the tāʾ is good here only because it is the end of a section of speech, so it resembles the verse-endings (fawāṣil), just as its being a verse-ending made His saying {إِن لَّبِثْتُمْ إِلاَّ عَشْراً} [Ṭā Hā: 103] good. So his saying 'if you used the masculine form you would depart from their speech' is not as he mentioned; rather, it is the most eloquent. The point of his mentioning «إن لبثتم إلاَّ يوماً» after His saying «إلا عَشْراً» is that, according to his claim, He meant the nights, the days being included with them, and His saying «إلا يوماً» is evidence that the days are meant." The Shaykh said: "This, in our view, indicates that what is meant by the ten is days, because they disagreed about the length of the stay: some of them said 'ten' and some of them said 'a day'; this indicates that what is contrasted with 'a day' is only days, since it would not be good in a contrast for some of them to say 'ten nights' and the others to say 'a day'."
His saying: {بالمعروف}: there are four views about it. The first: it is a ḥāl of the agent of «فَعَلْنَ», i.e. they did [it] being engaged in and accompanied by what is fair. The second: it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e. the bāʾ is the bāʾ of transitivity. The third: it is the naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. «فَعَلْنَ فِعْلاً بالمعروف» (they did a doing [that is] with what is fair), i.e. being so. The school of Sībawayh applies to it: that it is a ḥāl of the definite pronoun of the maṣdar, i.e. «فَعَلْنَه» — i.e. the doing — being engaged in what is fair; this is the fourth view.
«بما تعملون» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «خبيرٌ», and was fronted for the sake of the verse-ending. «ما» may be maṣdar-forming, or mean «الذي» (that which), or be an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective, which is weak. On these latter two views there must be an omitted referent-pronoun; on the first it is not needed, except according to a weak opinion.

semin-durr:250-250.t: The words of Allah the Exalted: {بَرَزُواْ لِجَالُوتَ}: concerning this lām there are two aspects. The first is that it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «برزوا». The second is that it is attached to something omitted, it and its genitive noun being a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «بَرَزوا». Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It may be a ḥāl, i.e. they went out heading for Jālūt." The meaning of «برزوا» is: they went out to an open stretch (barāz) of land, which is the part of it that is exposed and level; from it is al-mubāraza (single combat) in war, because each opponent comes out into the open to his counterpart. In their calling out with their words «رَبَّنا» ("our Lord") there is an acknowledgement on their part of servitude and a request for their rectification, because the word «الرب» conveys that, unlike other words. They used the word «على» in their saying «أَفْرِغ علينا» ("pour upon us"), requesting that patience be set over them and enveloping them, like a container.

semin-durr:251-251.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {وَالهَزْمُ}: [Translator's note: so quoted in the source; the verse reads فَهَزَمُوهُم, and the author is discussing the root هزم.] Its original meaning is breaking; from it is «سِقاء مُتَهَزِّم» ("a cracked waterskin") and «قَصَبٌ متهزِّمٌ» ("cracked reeds"), i.e. broken. His words: «بإذنِ الله»: there are in it the two aspects mentioned before, I mean its being a ḥāl (circumstantial) or a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). In «مِمَّا يشاء», the fāʿil (agent) of «يشاء» is the pronoun of Allah the Exalted; it is also said: the pronoun of Dāwūd; the first is more evident.

His words: {وَلَوْلاَ دَفْعُ}: Nāfiʿ read here and in [Sūrat] al-Ḥajj «دِفاع», and the rest «دَفْع». As for «دَفْع», it is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of the triliteral dafaʿa yadfaʿu. As for «دفاع», it admits two aspects: that it is likewise a maṣdar of the triliteral dafaʿa, like kataba kitāban, or that it is the maṣdar of «دافع», like qātala qitālan. Abū Dhuʾayb said:

1028 - ولقد حَرَصْتُ بأَنْ أدافعَ عنهُم ... فإذا المَنِيَّةُ أَقْبَلَتْ لا تُدْفَعُ
(I strove eagerly to ward [death] off from them, but when fate approaches it is not warded off.)

«فاعَل» here has the meaning of the bare faʿala, so the two readings coincide in meaning.

Whoever read «دفاع» and read in al-Ḥajj {يُدَافِعُ عَنِ الذين آمنوا} [verse 38] — namely Nāfiʿ — or read «دَفْع» and read «يَدْفَع» — namely Abū ʿAmr and Ibn Kathīr — has kept to his principle, bringing the maṣdar in agreement with the verb. As for those who read «دَفْع» here and «يُدافِع» in al-Ḥajj — namely the rest — they have combined the two usages, using the verb from the quadriliteral [form] and the maṣdar from the triliteral. The maṣdar here is annexed to its fāʿil, which is Allah the Exalted; «الناسَ» is the first object, and «بعضهم» is a badal (substitute) from «الناسِ», a substitute of part for whole.

«ببعضٍ» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to the maṣdar, and the bāʾ is for transitivity, so its genitive noun is the second object in meaning. The bāʾ is for transitivity only with an intransitive verb, such as «ذَهَبَ به» ("he took him away"). As for the verb transitive to one object, it is made transitive [to a second] only by the hamza: you say «طَعِمَ زيدٌ اللحم وأَطْعَمْتُه اللحم» ("Zayd ate the meat, and I fed him the meat"), and you do not say «طَعِمْته باللحم», making it transitive to the second with the bāʾ, except in what is anomalous with respect to analogy, namely «دَفَع» and «صَكَّ», as in «صَكَكْتُ الحجرَ بالحجرِ» ("I struck the stone with the stone"), i.e. I made one of them strike the other; for that reason they said «صَكَكْتُ الحجرَيْنِ أحدَهما بالآخر» ("I struck the two stones, one against the other").

His words: {ولكن الله}: the point of the rectification (istidrāk) is that, since He divided people into those repelled and those by whom [others] are repelled, and that by this repelling the corruption of the earth is prevented, it might occur to the mind of one who has been prevented from the corruption he wants that Allah is not bountiful toward him, since He did not let him attain his aims and his object. So He rectified this for him: even if he did not attain his aims, Allah is bountiful toward him and good to him, because he is included among «العالمين» (the worlds), and there is no one but that Allah has bounty over him, and He has the bounty of originating and bringing into existence.

«على» is attached to «فَضْل», because its verb is made transitive by it; it is sometimes omitted with the verb. He said — combining omission and retention:

1029 - وجَدْنا نَهْشَلاً فَضَلَتْ فُقَيْماً ... كفَضْلِ ابنِ المَخاض على الفَصيلِ
(We found [the tribe of] Nahshal surpassing Fuqaym, as the yearling camel surpasses the weanling.)

As for when it is doubled [i.e. faḍḍala], «على» is not omitted at all, as in His words: {فَضَّلْنَا بَعْضَهُمْ على بَعْضٍ} [al-Baqara: 253]. «على» may also be attached to something omitted, because it occurs as a naʿt (adjective) of «فَضْل».

semin-durr:252-252.t: The words of Allah the Exalted: {تِلْكَ آيَاتُ الله}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). Concerning «نَتْلوها» there are two views. The first is that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial), its governor being the meaning of the demonstrative. The second is that it is resumptive, so it has no grammatical position. Other [analyses] are permissible, and deriving them from what has passed is easy. It is pointed to with the demonstrative of the distant for what preceded at His words: {ذَلِكَ الكتاب} [al-Baqara: 2]. His words: «بالحقِّ»: it may be a ḥāl from the object of «نَتْلوها», i.e. accompanied by the truth; or from its fāʿil (agent), i.e. We recite them with the truth being with Us; or from the genitive pronoun of «عليك», i.e. [you] being accompanied by the truth.

semin-durr:253-253.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {فَضَّلْنَا بَعْضَهُمْ}: it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from what is pointed to, its governor being the meaning of the demonstrative, as preceded. It may be resumptive. It may also be the khabar (predicate) of «تلك», on the basis that «الرسلُ» is a naʿt (adjective) of «تلك», or an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition), or a badal (substitute). [Translator's note: the source has «خيرَ», an evident misprint for «خبرَ» (khabar).]

His words: {مِّنْهُمْ مَّن كَلَّمَ الله}: this clause admits two aspects. The first is that it has no grammatical position because it is resumptive. The second is that it is a badal from the clause «فَضَّلْنا». The majority read the Majestic Name in the nominative as the fāʿil (agent), the object being omitted, namely the pronoun referring back to the relative noun, i.e. "whom Allah spoke to". It was read in the accusative, on the basis that the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, which is also the pronoun referring back to the relative, and the Majestic Name is accusative by way of glorification. [Translator's note: so in the source; i.e. "who spoke to Allah".]

Abū al-Mutawakkil and Ibn al-Samayfaʿ read «كالَمَ اللهَ» on the pattern fāʿala, with the Majestic Name in the accusative; «كليم» on this [reading] has the meaning of «مكالِم» (one who converses), as jalīs means mujālis (companion in sitting) and khalīṭ means mukhāliṭ (associate). In this speech there is iltifāt (a shift of grammatical person), because it is a move from the pronoun of the speaker magnifying Himself in His words «فَضَّلْنا» to the overt noun, which is in the status of the third person.

His words: {دَرَجَاتٍ}: there are six aspects concerning its accusative. First, that it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) occurring in the place of a ḥāl. Second, that it is a ḥāl with the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "possessors of degrees". Third, that it is a second object of «رفع», on the basis that it is made to include the meaning of "He made some of them attain degrees". Fourth, that it is a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl), i.e. "He raised the degrees of some of them", the meaning being: [He raised them] above the degrees of others. Fifth, that it is a maṣdar according to the meaning of the verb, not its wording, because al-daraja means elevation, as though it were said: "and He raised some of them [many] raisings". Sixth, that it is by dropping the preposition (manṣūb bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ), that preposition possibly being «على», «في» or «إلى», its implied form being "upon degrees", "in degrees" or "to degrees"; when the preposition was omitted, what follows it became accusative.

His words: {وَلَوْ شَآءَ الله}: its object is omitted. It is said its implied form is "that you not differ"; it is said "that you not lose heart"; it is said "that you not be commanded to fight"; and it is said "that He compel them to faith". All of them are close to one another.

«مِنْ بعدِهم» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to something omitted, because it is a ṣila (relative clause), and the pronoun refers to the messengers. Concerning {مِّن بَعْدِ مَا جَآءَتْهُمُ} there are two views. The first is that it is a badal from His words «مِنْ بعدِهم», with repetition of the governor. The second is that it is attached to «اقتتل», since in the clear proofs — the manifest indications — there is what makes fighting and disagreement unnecessary. The pronoun in «جاءتهم» refers to "those after them", who are the nations of the prophets.

His words: {ولكن اختلفوا}: the point of this rectification (istidrāk) is clear, for «لكن» falls between two opposites, since the meaning is: had Allah willed agreement they would have agreed, but He willed disagreement, so they disagreed. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "«لكنْ» is a rectification of what the speech indicated, because their fighting was due to their disagreement." Then He explained the disagreement with His words: {فَمِنْهُمْ مَّنْ آمَنَ وَمِنْهُمْ مَّن كَفَرَ}, so in that case His words {فَمِنْهُمْ مَّنْ آمَنَ} have no grammatical position.

His words: {وَلَوْ شَآءَ الله مَا اقتتلوا}: there are two views. The first is that it is the first clause repeated for emphasis; al-Zamakhsharī said this. The second is that it is not for emphasising the first, but conveys a new point, the difference arising from the difference of their objects, for the object of the first [will] differs from the object of the second will. The implied form in the first is: "Had Allah willed to come between them and fighting, by stripping them of strength and minds"; and in the second: "Had He willed, He would not have commanded the believers to fight; but He willed, and commanded them to do so." His words: {ولكن الله يَفْعَلُ مَا يُرِيدُ}: this too is a rectification according to the meaning, because the meaning is: "Had Allah willed, He would have prevented them [from that]; but Allah does what He wills, namely not preventing them from that", or "does what He wills, namely their disagreeing".

semin-durr:254-254.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {أَنْفِقُواْ}: its object is omitted, its implied form being: "something of what We have provided you". On this view «ممَّا رزقناكم» is originally attached (mutaʿalliq) to something omitted, because it occurs as a naʿt (adjective) of that object. If you do not posit an omitted object, it is attached to the verb itself.

«ما» may mean «الذي» (that which), the referring pronoun being omitted, i.e. «رزقناكُموه» ("which We provided you with"); or it may be maṣdar-forming, so no referring pronoun is needed — but provision in the sense of the maṣdar is not spent, so what is meant by it is the passive participle; or it may be an indefinite noun qualified [by what follows]. The verification of this has preceded at His words: {وَممَّا رَزَقْنَاهُمْ يُنْفِقُونَ} [al-Baqara: 3].

His words: {مِّن قَبْلِ}: it too is attached to «أنفِقوا». It is permissible for two prepositions of the same wording to be attached to one verb because they differ in meaning, for the first is partitive and the second for the beginning of the extent. «أَنْ يأتي» is in the position of the genitive through the annexation of «قبل» to it, i.e. "before its coming".

His words: {لاَّ بَيْعٌ فِيهِ وَلاَ خُلَّةٌ} to its end: the negated clause is a naʿt of «يوم», so its position is the nominative. Nāfiʿ, the Kufans and Ibn ʿĀmir read «بَيْعٌ» and what follows it in the nominative with nunation, and Abū ʿAmr and Ibn Kathīr with fatḥa. The rationale of this is mentioned at His words: {فَلاَ رَفَثَ وَلاَ فُسُوقَ} [al-Baqara: 197], so let it be consulted there.

Al-khulla is friendship, as though it permeates (tatakhallal) the limbs, i.e. enters their interstices (khilāl), i.e. their midst.

Al-khulla is also the friend himself. He said:

1030 - وكان لها في سالفِ الدهرِ خُلَّةً ... يُسارِقُ بالطَّرْفِ الخِباءَ المُسَتَّرا
(She had in bygone times a bosom friend who would steal glances at the curtained tent.)

It is as though it is from applying the maṣdar (verbal noun) to the concrete thing, for intensification, or with the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "she had one possessing friendship". Al-khalīl is the friend, because of his intimate entry into you; it may properly have the meaning of an agent or of a patient. Its plural is «خُلاَّن»; fuʿlān as a plural of faʿīl is transmitted for adjectives, but it is frequent only in non-derived nouns, such as «رُغفان» (loaves). His words: «هم الظالمون»: «هم» may be a separating pronoun (faṣl), or a mubtadaʾ (subject) with what follows it as its khabar (predicate), the clause being the khabar of the first [mubtadaʾ].

semin-durr:266-266.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {مِّن نَّخِيلٍ}: it is in the position of the nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of «جنة», i.e. "consisting of palms". Regarding «نخيل» there are two views. The first: it is a quasi-plural noun (ism jamʿ). The second: it is the plural of «نخل», which is the generic noun, like «كَلْب» and «كَلِيب». Al-Rāghib said: "It was so named because it is the sifted best (mankhūl) of the trees and their choicest, since it is the noblest of what grows", and he mentioned its benefits and a resemblance it has to human beings. «الأعناب» is the plural of «عِنَبَة»; one also says «عِنَباء», like «سِيرَاء», with the long vowel, so it is a diptote. Wherever these two are mentioned in the Quran, the text names the palm itself rather than its fruit, and the fruit of the vine rather than the vine, because the palm is all benefits, whereas the greatest benefit of the vine is its fruit rather than the rest of it.

[His saying: {تَجْرِي مِن تَحْتِهَا}: regarding the position of this clause there are two aspects. The first: it is in the position of the nominative as a naʿt of «جنة».] The second: it is in the position of the accusative, and here too there are two aspects. It is said: as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «جَنَّة», because it has been described. And it is said: as the khabar (predicate) of «تكون»; Makkī transmitted this.

His saying: {لَهُ فِيهَا مِن كُلِّ الثمرات} is a clause made of a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar: the khabar is His saying «له», and {مِن كُلِّ الثمرات} is the mubtadaʾ. That does not hold on the face of it, since a mubtadaʾ cannot be a preposition with its genitive noun, so it must be interpreted. There is disagreement over this. It is said: the mubtadaʾ is in reality omitted, and this preposition phrase is an adjective standing in its place, its implied form being "he has in it provision of all fruits", or "fruit of all fruits"; the described noun was omitted and its adjective remained. Similar is the saying of al-Nābigha:
1071 - كأنَّك من جِمالِ بني أُقَيْشٍ ... يُقَعْقِعُ خلفَ رِجْلَيه بِشَنِّ
(As though you were one of the camels of Banū Uqaysh, with a dry waterskin rattled behind its legs.)
i.e. "a camel of the camels of Banū Uqaysh"; and His saying, Exalted is He: {وَمَا مِنَّآ إِلاَّ لَهُ مَقَامٌ [مَّعْلُومٌ]} [al-Ṣāffāt: 164], i.e. "and there is none of us but has a known station". It is also said: «مِنْ» is redundant (zāʾida), its implied form being "he has in it all the fruits"; that is according to al-Akhfash, because he does not stipulate anything for its redundancy. The Kufans stipulate indefiniteness, and the Basrans stipulate that together with a non-affirmative context. If we hold it to be redundant, what is meant by His saying «كلّ الثمرات» is abundance, not comprehensiveness, because comprehensiveness is impossible. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is not permissible for «مِنْ» to be redundant, neither according to the view of Sībawayh nor that of al-Akhfash, because the meaning would become: 'he has in it all the fruits', and the matter is not so — unless abundance rather than exhaustiveness is meant here, in which case it is permissible according to al-Akhfash, because he allows the redundancy of «مِنْ» in affirmative contexts."

His saying: {وَأَصَابَهُ الكبر}: there are three aspects regarding it. The first: the wāw is circumstantial, and the clause after it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, with «قد» implied, i.e. "when old age had struck him". The one to whom the ḥāl refers is «أحدُكم», and what governs it is «يَودُّ». Analogous to it are {وَكُنْتُمْ أَمْوَاتاً فَأَحْيَاكُمْ} [al-Baqara: 28] and His saying, Exalted is He: {وَقَعَدُواْ لَوْ أَطَاعُونَا} [Āl ʿImrān: 168], i.e. "when you had been" and "when they had sat".

The second: He has put the past in place of the imperfect, the implied form being "and old age strikes him", as in His saying: {يَقْدُمُ قَوْمَهُ يَوْمَ القيامة فَأَوْرَدَهُمُ} [Hūd: 98], i.e. "and leads them". Al-Farrāʾ said: "This is permissible with «يودُّ», because it is followed at one time by «أَنْ» and at another by «لو», so it is permissible for one of them to be implied in place of the other."

The third: it is construed in the conjunction according to the meaning, because the meaning is: "would one of you wish that he had …, and old age struck him". This aspect involves interpreting the imperfect as a past so that conjoining the past to it is sound — the reverse of the previous aspect, which involves interpreting the past as an imperfect. Abū al-Baqāʾ considered this aspect weak because it leads to altering the wording although the meaning is sound. Al-Zamakhsharī also inclined to this aspect, for he said: "It is also said: one says «وَدِدْتُ لو كان كذا» (I wished it were so), so the conjunction was construed according to the meaning, as though it were said: would one of you wish he had a garden and old age struck him."

The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "The apparent sense of his words is that «أصابه» is conjoined to the complement of «أيودُّ», which is «أَنْ تَكُونَ», because it has the sense of «لو كانَتْ», since one says «أيودُّ أحدُكم لو كانَتْ». This is worth nothing, because it is impossible in terms of meaning for it to be conjoined to «كانت» preceded by «لو», since that is the object of the wishing, whereas «أصابه الكبر» cannot be the object of the wishing, because no one wishes for or desires being struck by old age. However, al-Zamakhsharī's words can be taken to mean that, since «أيودُّ» is a question whose meaning is disapproval, the object of the wishing was made the combination of the two things — his having a garden and old age striking him — not that each of them is wished for separately; what they disapproved of was wishing for the combination of the two."

His saying: {وَلَهُ ذُرِّيَّةٌ}: this clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the hāʾ in «وأَصابَه». The derivation of «الذرية» has already been discussed. It was read «ضِعاف». Both «ضُعَفاء» and «ضِعاف» are regular plurals of «ضَعيف», like «ظَريف», «ظُرَفاء» and «ظِراف», and «شَريف», «شُرَفاء» and «شِراف».

His saying: {فَأَصَابَهَآ إِعْصَارٌ}: this clause is conjoined to the description of the garden before it; Abū al-Baqāʾ said this, meaning to His saying «مِنْ نخيل» and what follows it.

In all these verses there came [expressions] like «فأصَابه وابلٌ», «وأَصابَه الكِبَر» and «فأصابها إعصارٌ», because this is more eloquent and indicates the effect more strongly, through the act falling upon that thing, than if it had not been mentioned with the word «الإصابة»; so that if it had been said «وَبَل», «كَبِر» and «وأَعْصَرَتْ», it would not contain the intensity that the word «الإصابة» contains.

«الإعصار» is a violent wind that rises up; the common people call it «الزَّوْبعة» (the whirlwind). It is also said: it is the scorching wind (al-samūm). It was so named because it twists as a wrung-out garment is twisted; al-Mahdawī reported this. It is also said: because it wrings the clouds. It is pluralised as «أعاصير». The poet said:
1072 - وبَيْنما المرءُ في الأحياءِ مغتبطٌ ... إذ هُوَ في الرَّمْسِ تَعْفُوه الأعاصِيرُ
(While a man is among the living, envied for his good fortune, suddenly he is in the grave, the whirlwinds effacing it.)
Among all the names of the wind, «الإعصار» is masculine, and for this reason the pronoun refers back to it in the masculine in His saying: «فيه نارٌ».

For «نار» the two aspects are possible: namely, being a fāʿil (agent), with the preposition phrase before it as a naʿt of «إعصاراً» [Translator's note: so in the source, in the accusative form]; or being a mubtadaʾ, with the preposition phrase before it as its khabar and the clause as a naʿt of «إعصار». The first is preferable for the reason stated earlier, namely that describing with a single word is preferable, and the preposition phrase is closer to that than a clause.

His saying: {فاحترقت}, i.e. "it burned it, so it was burned"; it is the reflexive (muṭāwiʿ) of the quadriliteral «أَحْرَق». As for «حَرَقَ», from their saying «حَرَق نابُ الرجل» (the man's tooth grated) when his rage is intense, it is used both intransitively and transitively. The poet said:
1073 - أَبى الضيمَ والنعمانُ يَحْرِقُ نابَهُ ... عليه فَأَفْضى والسيوفُ مَعاقِلُهْ
(He refused injustice while al-Nuʿmān was grinding his teeth at him, and he went out into the open, the swords being his strongholds.)
It is narrated with «نابه» both in the nominative and in the accusative. His saying «كّذلك يُبَيَّن» to the end has already had its analogue discussed.

semin-durr:235-235.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {مِنْ خِطْبَةِ النسآء}: it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). About the one it qualifies (ṣāḥib al-ḥāl) there are two views. The first: the genitive hāʾ in «به». The second: «ما», made genitive by «في». On both suppositions what governs it is omitted. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is a ḥāl of the genitive hāʾ, so what governs it is «عَرَّضْتم»; and it may be a ḥāl of «ما», so what governs it is the 'being established' (al-istiqrār)." Taken at face value this is not good, because what governs it is omitted, as has been established — unless one means [this] in terms of meaning, not technical grammar, in which case it may be allowed to him.
«الخِطْبَة» is a maṣdar (verbal noun) annexed to its object, i.e. «من خِطْبَتِكم النساء» (of your proposing to the women), the agent being omitted because it is known. «الخِطْبَة» is originally a maṣdar meaning «الخَطْب», and «الخَطْب» is need; then it was specialised for seeking marriage, because that is one of the needs. One says «ما خطبُكَ؟», i.e. what is your need? Al-Farrāʾ said: "«الخِطْبَة» is a maṣdar meaning «الخَطْب», and it is from your saying «إنه لَحَسَنُ الجِلْسَةِ والقِعْدَةِ» (he has a fine manner of sitting), i.e. sitting." [Translator's note: the source text opens the quotation mark here but its close is not clearly marked.] «الخُطْبَة» — with ḍamma — is speech containing exhortation and admonition; both are from «الخَطْب» meaning speech. It used to be said to Sajāḥ: «خِطْبٌ» (a proposal!), and she would say: «نِكْحٌ» (a marriage!).
His saying: {أَوْ أَكْنَنتُمْ}: «أو» here is for permission, or choice, or detailing, or leaving the addressee in vagueness. «أَكَنَّ في نفسِهِ شيئاً» means he concealed it; «كَنَّ الشيءَ بثوبٍ ونحوهِ» means he covered it with it. So the hamza in «أكنَّ» serves to distinguish between the two usages, like «أشرَقَتْ» and «شَرَقَتْ». The object of «أكنَّ» is omitted and refers to the relative «ما» in His saying «فيما عَرَّضْتم», i.e. «أو أكننتموه» (or you concealed it). «في أنفسكم» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «أَكْنَنتم»; making it a ḥāl of the implied object is weak.
His saying: {ولكن}: about this rectification (istidrāk) there are three views. The first: it is a rectification of the clause before it, namely His saying «ستذكرونَهُنَّ» (you will mention them), for mentioning occurs in many manners and numerous ways, so one way was rectified out of it, in which a particular kind of mention is forbidden; had it not been rectified it would have been permissible, being included under mention in general. It is parallel to «زيدٌ سيلقى خالداً ولكنْ لا يواجهُهُ بِشَرٍّ» (Zayd will meet Khālid, but he will not confront him with evil): since the circumstances of meeting are many, among them confronting him with evil, this circumstance was rectified out from among them. The second — said by Abū al-Baqāʾ; said by al-Zamakhsharī [Translator's note: so in the source, which names both with a repeated «قاله»] — is that what is rectified is an omitted clause before «لكنْ», its implied form being: «فاذكروهُنَّ، ولكن لا تواعِدُوهُنَّ سراً» (so mention them, but do not promise them secretly). It has already been stated that the meaning is a rectification of the clause before it, so there is no need to omit . . . [Translator's note: there is a gap in the source text here]. What [the clause] after «لكن» needs is only the occurrence of what is before it in terms of meaning, not in terms of wording, because denying confrontation with evil requires that the meeting occur. [Translator's note: only two of the three announced views are given in the source.]
His saying: {سِرّاً}: there are five views about it. The first: it is a second object of «تواعِدُوهُنَّ».
The second: it is a ḥāl of the agent of «تواعدوهُنَّ», i.e. do not make promises to them while concealing that. The third: it is the naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. «مواعدةً سراً» (a secret promising). The fourth: it is a ḥāl of that maṣdar made definite, i.e. the promising being concealed. The fifth: it is accusative as an adverbial (ẓarf) figuratively, i.e. «في سِرٍّ» (in secret). On the [last] four views an object must be omitted, its implied form being: «لا تواعدوهُنَّ نكاحاً» (do not promise them marriage).
«السِّرّ» is the opposite of openness. It has been said that it is applied to intercourse, and to fornication specifically, and they cited al-Ḥuṭayʾa:
1000 - ويَحْرُم سِرُّ جارتِهم عليهم ... ويأكلُ جارُهُمْ أُنُفَ القِصاعِ
(Their neighbour-woman's intimacy is forbidden to them, and their neighbour eats the first helpings of the bowls.)
and the saying of another — he is al-Aʿshā —:
1001 - ولا تَقْرَبَنَّ جارةً إنَّ سِرَّها ... حَرامٌ عليكَ فانكِحَنْ أو تَأَبَّدا
(Do not approach a neighbour-woman, for her intimacy is forbidden to you; so marry, or remain celibate.)
His saying: {إِلاَّ أَن تَقُولُواْ}: about this exception there are two views. The first: it is a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ), because it is not included under «سِرّ» whatever explanation you give it, as though [He said]: but say an honourable word. The second: it is connected (muttaṣil), and there are two interpretations of it which al-Zamakhsharī mentioned, for he said: "If you say: to what is the particle of exception attached? I say: to «لا تواعِدُوهُنَّ», i.e. do not promise them any promising at all except an honourable, unobjectionable promising; or: do not promise them except by your saying, i.e. do not promise them except by allusion (taʿrīḍ). It cannot be a disconnected exception from «سراً», because that would lead to your saying: do not promise them except the allusion." End of quote. So he made it a connected, emptied exception (mufarragh) on one of two interpretations. The first: it is excepted from the maṣdar, which is why he gave its implied form as: do not promise them any promising at all except an honourable promising. The second: it is from an omitted genitive, which is why he gave its implied form as «إلاَّ بأَنْ تقولوا» (except by your saying), because the implied form in his view is: do not promise them anything except by your saying; then he explained his "by your saying" as "by allusion". When the bāʾ was omitted from «أَنْ» — and it is the causal bāʾ — the well-known disagreement remained regarding «أَنْ» after the omission of the preposition: is it in the position of the accusative or the genitive? His saying "because that would lead to your saying…" to the end means that it is not sound for the governor to act upon it, for the honourable word in his view means allusion, and if you said «لا تواعِدُوهُنَّ إلاَّ التعريض» (do not promise them except the allusion) it would not be sound, because allusion is not a promising.
The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] answered him that it is not a condition of the disconnected exception that the governor can soundly act upon it; rather, it is of two kinds. One kind in which that is sound, and in it there are two dialects: the dialect of the Ḥijāz requires the accusative absolutely, as in «ما جاء أحدُ ألا حماراً» (no one came except a donkey) [Translator's note: «ألا» here is a copying slip for «إلا»]; and the dialect of Tamīm treats it like the connected exception, applying to it the accusative and substitution (badaliyya) under its condition. And a kind in which that is not sound, as in «ما زادَ إلا ما نَقَصَ» (it did not increase except what decreased) and «ما نفَعَ إلا ما ضَرَّ» (it did not benefit except what harmed); the ruling of this is the accusative among all the Arabs. Both kinds share being interpreted with «لكن» according to the Basrans, except that in one of them the governor can soundly act upon it: in your saying «ما جاء أَحدٌ إلا حمار», if you said «ما جاءَ إلا حمارٌ» (only a donkey came) it would be sound — unlike the second kind, upon which the governor cannot be directed. The verification of this has a place more fitting for it, and a good part of it has preceded.
His saying: {عُقْدَةَ}: about its accusative there are three views. The first: it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), on the basis that «عَزَم» was made to imply the meaning of something that is transitive by itself, namely «تَنْووا» (intend) or «تباشِروا» (undertake) and the like. The second: it is accusative by removal of the preposition, namely «على», for «عَزَم» is made transitive by it; the poet said:
1002 - عَزَمَتُ على إقامةِ ذي صباحٍ ... لأمرٍ ما يُسَوَّدُ مَنْ يَسُودُ
(I resolved to stay until morning — for some reason is he made lord who becomes lord.)
And omitting it is permissible, as in the saying of ʿAntara:
1003 - ولقد أبيتُ على الطَّوى وأظلُّه ... حتى أنالَ به كريمَ المَطْعَمِ
(I spend the night in hunger and pass the day in it, until I attain by it noble food.)
i.e. «وأظلُّ عليه» (and I pass the day upon it). The third: it is accusative as a maṣdar, for the meaning is «ولا تَعْقِدُوا عقدةَ» (and do not tie a tie), so it is as though it were a maṣdar not of the verb's own root [Translator's note: the source has «على غير الصدر», a slip for «على غير المصدر»], as in «قَعَدْتُ جلوساً» (I sat a sitting). «العُقْدَة» is a maṣdar annexed to its object, the agent being omitted, i.e. «عُقْدَتَكم النكاحَ» (your tying of the marriage).
His saying: {فاحذروه}: the hāʾ in «فاحذَرُوه» refers to Allah the Exalted, and a muḍāf must be omitted, i.e. «فاحذَرُوا عقابَه» (so beware of His punishment). It may also refer to «ما» in His saying {مَا في أَنْفُسِكُمْ}, in the sense of: what is in your souls of resolve upon what is not permissible; al-Zamakhsharī said this.

semin-durr:267-267.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {أَنْفِقُواْ مِن طَيِّبَاتِ مَا كَسَبْتُمْ}: regarding the object of «أنفقوا» there are two views. The first: it is the noun in the genitive with «مِنْ», and «مِنْ» is partitive, i.e. "spend part of what We have provided you". The second: it is omitted and its adjective stands in its place, i.e. "something of what We have provided you"; analogues of this have already been given. «ما» may be a nominal relative, with the referent pronoun omitted because the conditions are fulfilled, i.e. "what you earned it"; or it may be maṣdarī, i.e. "of the good things of your earning", in which case this maṣdar (verbal noun) must be interpreted as a passive participle, i.e. "what you have earned". For this reason the first aspect is preferable.

«مِمَّا اَخْرَجْنا» is conjoined to the noun in the genitive with «مِنْ», with the preposition repeated, for one of two meanings: either emphasis, or to indicate another, implied governing verb, i.e. "and spend of what We have brought forth". A muḍāf must be assumed omitted, i.e. "and of the good things of what We have brought forth". «لكم» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «أخرجنا», and the lām denotes cause. «مِنْ الأرض» is also attached to «أخرجنا», and «مِنْ» marks the beginning of the extent.

His saying: {وَلاَ تَيَمَّمُواْ الخبيث}: the majority read «تَيَمَّموا». The original is «تَتَيَمَّمُوا» with two tāʾs, and one of them was omitted for lightness — either the first or the second. The precise discussion of this was given at His saying: {تَظَاهَرُونَ} [al-Baqara: 85].

Al-Bazzī read here and in other places with a doubled tāʾ, on the basis that he assimilated the first tāʾ into the second. This is permissible here and in its analogues because the first quiescent letter is a soft letter (a letter of līn). This differs from his reading of {نَاراً تلظى} [al-Layl: 14] and {إِذْ تَلَقَّوْنَهُ} [al-Nūr: 15], for there he combined two quiescent letters, the first being a sound consonant; the Arabic grammarians have discussion of this, which will be mentioned, if Allah the Exalted wills.

Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Zuhrī read «تُيَمِّمو» with ḍamma on the tāʾ and kasra on the first mīm; its past form is «يَمَّم», so the pattern of «تُيَمِّموا» on this reading is tufaʿʿilū, with no omission. It is narrated from ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd] «تُؤَمِّموا», from «أَمَّمْتُ», i.e. "I aimed at".

«التيمُّم» is aiming at. One says «أَمَّ», like «ردَّ»; «أَمَّمَ», like «أَخَّرَ»; «يَمَّم»; «تَيَمَّم», with both tāʾ and yāʾ; and «تَأَمَّم», with tāʾ and hamza — all meaning "to aim at". Al-Khalīl, may Allah have mercy on him, distinguished between them with subtle differences. He said: "«أَمَّمْتُه»: I aimed at what is in front of him; «يَمَّمْتُه»: I aimed … and «يَمَّمْتُه»: I aimed at him from whatever direction it was."
[Translator's note: the quotation is defective in the source, which marks a gap with dots and repeats «يَمَّمْتُه».]

«الخبيث» (the bad) and «الطيب» (the good) are two adjectives that have come to be used as nouns, whose described noun is not mentioned. He said: {والطيبون لِلْطَّيِّبَاتِ} [al-Nūr: 26] and {وَيُحَرِّمُ عَلَيْهِمُ الخبآئث} [al-Aʿrāf: 157], and the Prophet ﷺ said: «مِنَ الخُبْث والخَبائث» ("from the male and female devils" / "from evil and evil things").

His saying: {مِنْهُ تُنْفِقُونَ}: «منه» is attached to «تنفقون». «تُنْفِقُون» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of {تَيَمَّمُواْ}, i.e. "do not aim at the bad, spending from it". They said: it is an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara), because the spending from it occurs after aiming at it; Abū al-Baqāʾ and others said this. The second: it is a ḥāl from «الخبيث», because the clause contains a pronoun referring to it, i.e. "do not aim at [the bad] as something spent from".

The third: it is resumptive, beginning a statement of that. The sentence was complete at His saying {وَلاَ تَيَمَّمُواْ الخبيث}, then He began another statement, saying: "you spend from it while you would not take it unless you closed your eyes", as though this were a reproach and rebuke to people. The meaning rejects this.

His saying: {وَلَسْتُمْ بِآخِذِيهِ}: there are two views on it. The first: it is resumptive, with no grammatical position; Abū al-Baqāʾ held this. The second: it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl. This appears very strongly for whoever holds that the sentence was complete at His saying {وَلاَ تَيَمَّمُواْ الخبيث} and that what follows is resumptive. Its meaning has already been explained.

The hāʾ in «بآخذِيه» refers back to «الخبيث». About it, and about similar pronouns attached to an active participle, there are two well-known views. The first: it is in the position of the genitive, even though its position [in meaning] is accusative, because it is an object in meaning. The second — the view of al-Akhfash —: it is in the position of the accusative, and the nunation and the nūn were dropped in such cases as «ضاربيك» only because of the lightness of the pronoun. The doctrine of Hishām is that the nunation may be retained with the pronoun, so he allows «هذا ضارِبُنْك» with the nunation retained. His doctrine may be argued for with the poet's saying:
1074 - همُ الفاعلونُ الخيرَ والآمِرُونه ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(They are the doers of good and the ones who command it …)
and the other's saying:
1075 - ولم يَرْتَفِقْ والناسُ مُحْتَضِرُونه ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(And he did not lean on his elbow, while the people were present at it …)
For they combined the nūn standing in for nunation with the pronoun. These views have proofs mentioned in the books of the grammarians.

His saying: {إِلاَّ أَن تُغْمِضُواْ}: the original is «إلاَّ بأَنْ»; the preposition was omitted with «أَنْ», so the two views arise about it: is it in the position of the genitive or of the accusative? This bāʾ is attached to «تُيَمِّموا» «بآخذيه» [Translator's note: so in the source; the intended sense is evidently that it is attached to «آخذيه»]. Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed «أَنْ» and what is in its domain to be in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, governed by «آخذيه», the meaning being: "you would not take it in any state except in the state of closing your eyes". It has already been stated that Sībawayh does not allow «أَنْ» and what is in its domain to occur in the place of a ḥāl. Al-Farrāʾ said: "The meaning is that of condition and response, because its meaning is: if you closed your eyes you would take it; but when «إلاَّ» fell upon «أَنْ», it gave it fatḥa. Similar are {إِلاَّ أَن يَخَافَآ} [al-Baqara: 229] and {إَلاَّ أَن يَعْفُونَ} [al-Baqara: 237]." This view is refuted in the books of grammar.

The majority read «تُغْمِضوا» with ḍamma on the tāʾ and kasra on the unstressed mīm, from «أَغْمَض». There are two aspects regarding it. The first: its object is omitted, the implied form being "you close your eyes" or "your inner sight". The second: it has the sense of an intransitive verb, the meaning being "unless you overlook", from their saying «أَغْضَى عنه» (he overlooked it).

Al-Zuhrī read «تُغْمِّضوا» with ḍamma on the tāʾ, fatḥa on the ghayn and a doubled mīm with kasra; its meaning is like the first. It is also narrated from him: «تَغْمَضوا», with fatḥa on the tāʾ, sukūn on the ghayn and fatḥa on the mīm, the imperfect of «غَمِضَ» with kasra on the mīm, which is a dialectal variant of the quadriliteral «أَغْمض»; so it is among those in which faʿila and afʿala agree. It is narrated from al-Yazīdī: «تَغْمُضوا», with fatḥa on the tāʾ, sukūn on the ghayn and ḍamma on the mīm. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is from «غَمُضَ يَغْمُضُ», like «ظَرُف يظرُفُ», i.e. your judgement about it was obscure to you."

It is narrated from al-Ḥasan: «تُغَمِّضُوا», with ḍamma on the tāʾ, fatḥa on the ghayn and a doubled mīm with fatḥa, in the passive. Qatāda read likewise except that he did not double the mīm. The meaning is: "unless you are induced to overlook it and be lenient about it". Abū al-Baqāʾ said about Qatāda's reading: "It may be from «أَغْمَضَ», i.e. 'found in that state', as when you say «أَحْمَدْتُ الرجل», i.e. I found him praiseworthy." Abū al-Fatḥ [Ibn Jinnī] held this too. It is also said about it that its meaning is: "unless you are brought into it and drawn to it".

semin-durr:268-268.t: His saying, Exalted is He: {الشيطان يَعِدُكُمُ}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). The derivation of «الشيطان» and what pertains to it has [already been discussed]. The pattern of «يَعِدُكم» is yaʿilukum, with the omission of the first radical, which is the wāw, because it falls between a yāʾ and a kasra. The majority read «الفَقْر» with fatḥa on the fāʾ and sukūn on the qāf. Abū Ḥaywa narrated from some of them «الفُقْر» with ḍamma on the fāʾ, which is a dialectal variant, and it was also read «الفَقَر» with two fatḥas. His saying «منه»: there are two aspects regarding it. The first: it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted element, because it is a naʿt (adjective) of «مغفرة». The second: it is an object attached to «يَعِد», i.e. "He promises you from Himself". «فَضْلاً» has its adjective omitted, i.e. "and bounty from Him"; this is on the first aspect, while on the second there is no omission.

semin-durr:255-255.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {الله لاَ إله إِلاَّ هُوَ [الحي]}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). Concerning «الحيّ» there are seven aspects. First, that it is a second khabar of the Majestic Name. Second, that it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "He is the Living". Third, that it is a badal (substitute) from His words «لا إله إلا الله هو» [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse reads «لا إله إلا هو»], so that in meaning it is a khabar of the Majestic Name; this is like the first in meaning, except that here the Majestic Name is given only one khabar, unlike the first. Fourth, that it is a badal from «هو» alone; this then belongs to the chapter of putting the overt noun in place of the pronoun, because the negative clause is a khabar about the Majestic Name, and if you make it a badal it takes the place of the first, so the implied form becomes: "Allah — there is no god but Allah". Fifth, that it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is {لاَ تَأْخُذُهُ سِنَةٌ}. Sixth, that it is a badal from «الله». Seventh, that it is a naʿt (adjective) of «الله», and this is the best of them, because both were read in the accusative, «الحيَّ القيومَ», by way of severance (qaṭʿ), and severance occurs only in the chapter of the naʿt. It cannot be objected against this aspect that the adjective and the qualified are separated by the khabar, because that is permissible and good [: you say «زيدٌ قائمٌ العاقلُ» ("Zayd, the intelligent, is standing")].

Concerning «الحيُّ» there are two views. The first is that its origin is ḥayyun with two yāʾs, from ḥayiya yaḥyā, so he is ḥayy; this is clear, and Abū al-Baqāʾ held it. The second is that its origin is ḥaywun, its final radical being a wāw, and the wāw was changed into a yāʾ because the letter before it has a kasra while it is final. There is no need for this. It is as though what drove the one holding this view to claim it is that the middle and final radicals being of the same kind is rare in their speech relative to its absence; for that reason they wrote «الحياة» with a wāw in the orthography of the noble codex, as a pointer to this origin, and «الحيوان» supports it, the wāw appearing in it. The supporter of the first view may say: the second yāʾ was changed into a wāw for lightness, because when an alif and nūn were added at its end the two identical letters were found heavy.

Concerning its pattern there are also two views. The first is that it is faʿl. The second is that it is fayʿil, then lightened, as they said mayt and hayn, the origin being hayyin and mayyit.

Al-qayyūm is fayʿūl from qāma bi-l-amr yaqūmu bihi, when one manages it. Umayya said:

1031 - لم تُخْلَقِ السماءُ والنجومُ ... والشمسُ معها قَمَر يَعُومُ
قَدَّره مهيمنٌ قَيُّومُ ... والحشرُ والجنةُ والنعيمُ
إلا لأمرٍ شأنُه عظيمُ
(The sky and the stars were not created, nor the sun with a moon floating alongside it — decreed by a Guardian, Self-Subsisting — nor the Gathering, the Garden and bliss, except for a matter whose import is mighty.)

Its origin is qaywūm; the yāʾ and the wāw met, the first of them quiescent, so the wāw was changed into a yāʾ and the yāʾ was assimilated into it, and it became qayyūm.

Ibn Masʿūd and al-Aʿmash read «القَيَّام», and ʿAlqama read «القَيِّم»; this is as they say dayyūr, dayyār and dayyir. Its pattern may not be faʿʿūl like «سَفُّود», since were it so its form would be qawwūm, because the doubled middle radical is always of the same kind as the original one, as in subbūḥ, quddūs, ḍarrāb and qattāl, the augment being of the kind of the middle radical. So when it came with yāʾ rather than wāw, we knew that its origin is fayʿūl, not faʿʿūl. Some counted fayʿūl among the patterns of intensification, like ḍarūb and ḍarrāb.

His words: {لاَ تَأْخُذُهُ سِنَةٌ}: concerning this clause there are five aspects. First, that it is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of «الحيّ», as preceded in one of the aspects of the nominative of «الحيّ». Second, that it is a khabar about Allah the Exalted, according to whoever permits multiple predicates. Third, that it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun latent (mustatir) in «القَيُّوم», as though it were said: "He manages the affairs of creation without being heedless"; Abū al-Baqāʾ said this. Fourth, that it is a resumptive statement: the Exalted informed of that about His eternal Essence. Fifth, that it is an emphasis of «القَيُّوم», because one to whom that could happen could not possibly be qayyūm; al-Zamakhsharī said this. So on his view that it is an emphasis, its position may be the accusative as an emphasising ḥāl, or it may be resumptive while carrying the meaning of emphasis; so the aspects become four.

Al-sina is drowsiness (al-nuʿās), which is the languor that precedes sleep. ʿAdī ibn al-Riqāʿ said:

1032 - وَسْنانُ أَقْصَدَه النُّعاسُ فَرَنَّقَتْ ... في عينِه سِنَةٌ وليس بنائمِ
(Drowsy — slumber struck him, and a doze hovered in his eye, yet he is not asleep.)

It is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of wasana yasinu, like waʿada yaʿidu; the reason for the elision has preceded at His words {سَعَةً مِّنَ المال} [al-Baqara: 247]. Ibn Zayd said: "Al-wasnān is one who gets up from sleep without being in his right mind, so that he may even draw the sword against his family." This view is worthless, because that is not understood from the language of the Arabs. Al-Mufaḍḍal said: "Al-sina is heaviness in the head, drowsiness is in the eyes, and sleep is in the heart."

«لا» was repeated in His words «ولا نومٌ» for emphasis. Its benefit is the negation of each one of the two; had it not been mentioned, it would have been possible that they are negated on condition of being together, which does not entail the negation of each one separately. For that reason you say «ما قامَ زيدٌ وعمروٌ بل أحدُهما» ("Zayd and ʿAmr did not [both] stand, but one of them did"), whereas if you said «ما قامَ زيدٌ ولا عمرو بل أحدُهما» it would not be sound. The meaning is: He is not heedless of anything, minute or great. He expressed heedlessness by that because it is its cause, so He applied the name of the cause to what it causes.

His words: {لَّهُ مَا فِي السماوات}: it is like the one before it, except as regards its being an emphasis. «ما» is for comprehensiveness. The lām in «له» is for ownership. He repeated «ما» for emphasis. Here He mentioned what is contained rather than the container, because the purpose is to negate divinity from other than Allah the Exalted, and that none should be worshipped but Him; for what is worshipped besides Him is either in the heaven, like the sun, the moon and the stars, or on the earth, like idols and some of the children of Ādam, and all of them are owned by Him, the Exalted, under His dominion. He dispensed with mentioning that the heavens and the earth are owned by Him by having mentioned before that that He is the Creator of the heavens and the earth.

His words: {مَن ذَا الذي يَشْفَعُ عِنْدَهُ} are like His words {مَّن ذَا الذي يُقْرِضُ} [al-Baqara: 245]. «مَنْ», though interrogative in wording, is negative in meaning; for that reason «إلا» entered in His words «إلاّ بإذنه».

Concerning «عنده» there are two aspects. The first is that it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «يَشْفَع».

The second is that it is attached to something omitted because it is [a ḥāl] from the pronoun in «يَشْفع», i.e. intercedes while being settled with Him. This aspect was strengthened on the ground that, if one who is with Him and near to Him does not intercede with Him, the intercession of another is even more remote. Some considered the ḥāl reading weak, on the ground that the meaning is "intercedes with Him".

«إلاَّ بإذنه» is attached to something omitted, because it is a ḥāl from the fāʿil (agent) of «يَشْفَع», so it is an emptied exception (istithnāʾ mufarragh). The bāʾ is for accompaniment, and the meaning is: none intercedes with Him except as one permitted by Him. It may also be a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e. "by His permission they intercede", as you say «ضَرَب بسيفه» ("he struck with his sword"), i.e. it is the instrument of striking, and the bāʾ is for transitivity.

«يَعْلَمُ»: this clause may be a khabar of one of the two preceding mubtadaʾs, or resumptive, or a ḥāl. The pronoun in «أيديهم» and «خلفهم» refers to «ما» in His words {لَّهُ مَا فِي السماوات وَمَا فِي الأرض}, because He gave precedence to those endowed with reason over others. It is said: it refers to the rational beings among those included in the word «ما», to the exclusion of others. It is said: it refers to the angels and prophets indicated by «مَنْ ذا». It is also said: to the angels specifically.

His words: {بِشَيْءٍ} is attached to «يحيطون». Knowledge here means what is known, because His knowledge, the Exalted — which is an attribute subsisting in His holy Essence — is not divisible into parts. An example of knowledge occurring in place of the known is their saying «اللهم اغفر لنا عِلْمَك فينا» ("O Allah, forgive us what You know about us"), and the ḥadīth of Mūsā and al-Khaḍir, peace be upon them both: "My knowledge and your knowledge have not diminished from His knowledge except as this sparrow has diminished from this sea." Because knowledge means what is known, it is sound for the partitive and the exception to enter upon it. «مِنْ علمه» may be attached to «يحيطون», or attached to something omitted because it is a naʿt of «شيء», so it is in the position of the genitive. «بما شاءَ» is also attached to «يُحيطون», and it does no harm that these two prepositions, identical in wording and meaning, are attached to a single governor, because the second with its genitive noun are a badal of the first two, with repetition of the governor, by way of exception, as in your saying «ما مررت بأحدٍ إلا بزيدٍ» ("I passed by no one except Zayd"). The object of «شاء» is omitted, its implied form being: "except what He wills that they encompass"; I posited it so only because of the indication of His words {وَلاَ يُحِيطُونَ بِشَيْءٍ مِّنْ عِلْمِهِ}.

His words: {وَسِعَ كُرْسِيُّهُ}: the majority read «وَسِعَ» with a fatḥa on the wāw, a kasra on the sīn and a fatḥa on the ʿayn, as a past verb.

«كرسيُّه» is nominative as its fāʿil. It was read «وَسْعَ», making the middle radical of the verb quiescent for lightness, as in ʿalma for ʿalima. It was also read «وَسْعُ كرسيِّه», with a fatḥa on the wāw, sukūn on the sīn and a ḍamma on the ʿayn, as a mubtadaʾ, «كرسيِّه» genitive by annexation, and «السماواتُ» nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ.

In al-kursī the yāʾ is not for relation (nisba). It is derived from al-kirs, which is gathering; from it is al-kurrāsa, for the leaves that gather knowledge, and from it is the saying of al-ʿAjjāj:

1033 - يا صاحِ هل تَعْرِفُ رسماً مُكْرَساً ... قال نَعَمْ أعرِفُه وأَبْلَسا
(O companion, do you recognize a trace of encampment heaped [with dung]? He said: yes, I recognize it — and fell silent in dismay.)

Its plural is karāsiyy, like bukhtiyy and bakhātiyy. There are two dialectal forms of it: the well-known one with a ḍamma on its kāf, and the second with a kasra, and it is as though it is a kasra of vowel-harmony (itbāʿ). It may be used to denote the king, because he sits on it, naming the occupant by the name of the place; from it is:

1034 - قد عَلِمَ القُدُّوسُ مَوْلى القُدْسِ ... أنَّ أبا العباسِ أَوْلِى نَفْسِ
في مَعْدِنِ المَلِكِ القديمِ الكُرْسي
(The Most Holy, Master of holiness, knows that Abū al-ʿAbbās is the most worthy soul, in the mine of ancient kingship — the kursī.)

And [it is used] for knowledge, naming the attribute by the name of the place of its possessor; from it the scholars were called «الكَراسيّ». He said:

1035 - يَحُفُّ بهم بيضُ الوجوه وعُصْبَةٌ ... كراسِيُّ بالأحداثِ حين تَنُوبُ
(They are surrounded by men of bright faces and a band who are kursīs — learned — in events when they befall.)

He described them as knowing about the events of affairs and their calamities. It is also used for the secret. He said:

1036 - مالي بأَمْرِكَ كُرْسِيٌّ أُكاتِمُهُ ... ولا بِكُرْسِيِّ - عَلْمَ اللَّهُ - مَخْلُوقِ
(I have no secret of your affair that I conceal, nor — Allah knows — any secret of a created being.)

It is also said: the kursī of everything is its root.

His words: {وَلاَ يَؤُودُهُ}: it is said «آدَه كذا», i.e. it weighed on him and hardship from it overtook him. He said:

1037 - ألا ما لسَلْمَى اليومَ بَتَّ جَدِيدُها ... وَضَنَّتْ وما كانُ النَّوالُ يَؤُودُها
(Alas, what is with Salmā today — her new bond is cut, and she has been stingy, though giving never used to weigh on her.)

i.e. burden her. From it is al-mawʾūda, for the girl buried alive, because they weigh her down with earth. It was read «يَوْدُه» with the hamza elided, as the hamza of «أناس» is elided; and it was read «يَوُوده» with the hamza changed into a wāw.

«حِفْظ» is a maṣdar annexed to its object, i.e. it does not burden Him to preserve them both.

The origin of «العليّ» is ʿaliywun; it was assimilated as in mayyit, because it is from ʿalā yaʿlū. He said:

1038 - فَلَمَّا عَلَوْنَا واستَوَيْنَا عليهِمُ ... تَرَكْنَاهُمُ صَرْعَى لنسرٍ وكاسِرِ
(When we rose over them and mastered them, we left them felled for the vulture and the swooping bird of prey.)

«العظيمُ»: its meaning has preceded. It is said that here it means "the one magnified", as they said «عتيق» meaning «مُعَتَّق» (aged). He said:

1039 - فكأنَّ الخمرَ العتيقَ من الإِسْ ... فَنْطِ ممزوجةً بماءٍ زُلالِ
(As though aged wine of the isfanṭ, mixed with pure, clear water…)

It is said: that was rejected because this description would be absent before creation and after their extinction, since there would then be none to magnify Him. This [objection] is corrupt, because He deserves this description. It was also said in reply to it: it is an attribute of action, like creating and providing; the first is more correct.

Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: how are the clauses of the Verse of the Throne arranged without a conjunction? I say: there is no clause among them but that it comes by way of clarifying what it follows, and the clarification is one with what is clarified; had a conjunction come between them it would be as the Arabs say: 'between the stick and its bark'. The first is a clarification of His undertaking the management of creation and His being Guardian over it, not heedless of it; the second, of His being Owner of what He manages; the third, of the majesty of His standing; the fourth, of His encompassing the states of creation and His knowledge of whom among them He is pleased with, who merits intercession, and whom He is not pleased with; the fifth, of the vastness of His knowledge and its relation to all objects of knowledge, or of His majesty and the greatness of His power." End quote. He means most of the clauses; otherwise some of the clauses in it are conjoined, namely His words «ولا يُحيطُونَ», His words «ولا يَؤُودُه», and His words {وَهُوَ العلي العظيم}.

semin-durr:269-269.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {وَمَن يُؤْتَ الْحِكْمَةَ}: the majority read «يُؤْتِي» and «ومَنْ يُؤْتَ» with yāʾ in both. Al-Rabīʿ ibn Khuthaym [Translator's note: the source spells it «خيثم»] read with tāʾ, in the second person, in both; this is an address to the Creator by way of iltifāt (shift). The majority read «ومن يُؤْتَ» in the passive, and what stands in place of the fāʿil (agent) is the pronoun of the conditional «مَنْ», which is the first object, while «الحكمةَ» is the second object. Yaʿqūb read «يُؤْتِ» in the active, the fāʿil being a pronoun referring to Allah the Exalted, «مَنْ» a fronted object, and «الحكمة» a second object, as when you say: «أيّاً يُعْطِ زيدٌ درهماً أُعْطِه درهماً» (whomever Zayd gives a dirham, I will give him a dirham) [Translator's note: the source prints «يَّاً», evidently for «أيّاً»].

Al-Zamakhsharī said: it means "and whomever Allah gives it". The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "If he meant an explanation of the meaning, it is correct; but if he meant the grammatical analysis, it is not so, since there is no omitted accusative pronoun there; rather the object of «يُؤْتِ» is the fronted conditional «مَنْ»." I say: al-Zamakhsharī's construal is supported by the reading of al-Aʿmash: {ومَنْ يُؤْتِه الحكمةَ}, with the pronoun hāʾ stated. In his reading «مَنْ» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), because the verb is occupied with its own governed element. According to those who allow ishtighāl (preoccupation of the verb) with conditional and interrogative nouns, «مَنْ» may be accusative by an implied verb, which they imply as coming after it, or nominative as a mubtadaʾ. The precise account of this has been given in the course of this analysis.

His saying: {أُوتِيَ} is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). A past verb joined with «قد» occurring as the apodosis of a condition is sometimes past in wording and future in meaning, as in this verse, and then it is truly the apodosis; and sometimes it is past in both wording and meaning, as in {وَإِن يُكَذِّبُوكَ فَقَدْ كَذَّبَتْ} [Fāṭir: 4], and this is not the apodosis; rather the apodosis is omitted, i.e. "then take consolation, for messengers were denied [before you]". Further explanation of this will come.

Concerning the indefiniteness in «خيراً», al-Zamakhsharī said: "It conveys magnification, as though He said: then he has been given what an abundant good!" The Shaykh said: "Construing it thus leads to omitting the noun described by «أيّ» and putting the adjective in its place, since the implied form is 'then he has been given a good — what an abundant good'; and to omitting «أيّ», which is an adjective, and putting what it is annexed to in its place; and to describing the noun to which «أيّ», used as an adjective, is annexed, as in «مَرَرْتُ برجلٍ أيِّ رجلٍ كريمٍ». All of this requires evidence to establish. What is preserved from the Arabs is that «أيّ» used as an adjective is annexed to something identical to the described noun, as in «دَعَوْتُ امرَأً أيَّ امرىءٍ، فأجابني» (I called a man — what a man! — and he answered me). The noun described by «أيّ» is sometimes omitted, as in the poet's saying:
1076 - إذا حارَب الحَجَّاجُ أيَّ منافقٍ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(When al-Ḥajjāj makes war on what a hypocrite! …)
its implied form being 'a hypocrite — what a hypocrite!' — and this is rare." It has already been stated that al-Zamakhsharī's construal is likewise, i.e. that he omitted the noun described by «أيّ». The original of «يَذَّكَّرُ» is «يَتَذَكَّر», and it was assimilated.

semin-durr:236-236.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {مَا لَمْ تَمَسُّوهُنَّ}: about this «ما» there are three views. The most apparent of them is that it is maṣdar-forming and temporal (maṣdariyya ẓarfiyya), its implied form being: «مدةَ عدمِ المَسيس» (for the period of not touching), as in the poet's saying:
1004 - إني بحبلِكَ واصلٌ حَبْلِي ... وبريش نَبْلِكَ رائِشٌ نَبْلي
ما لم أَجِدْكَ على هُدَى أَثَرٍ ... يَقْرُو مِقَصَّكَ قائِفٌ قَبْلي
(I join my rope to your rope, and feather my arrows with the feathers of your arrows, so long as I do not find you on the trail of a track, a tracker following your footprints before me.)
The second: that it is conditional, meaning «إنْ»; Abū al-Baqāʾ transmitted this. It is not apparent, because it would then be of the chapter of one condition intervening upon another, so the second would be a restriction on the first, as in «إنْ تأتِ إنْ تُحْسِنْ إليَّ أكرمْك» (if you come, if you do me good, I will honour you), i.e. if you come doing good; likewise in the noble verse: if you divorce them without having touched them. Rather, what is apparent is that this speaker only meant to explain the meaning, because temporal «ما» resembles conditional «ما», and for that reason it entails generality. The third: that it is a relative meaning «الذي» and refers to the women, as though it were said: if you divorce the women whom you have not touched. This is weak, because the relative «ما» is not used as an adjective, even though «الذي», «التي» and their derived forms are.
The majority read «تَمَسُّوهُنَّ» as a triliteral verb, and it is clear. Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read «تماسُّوهُنَّ», of the pattern mufāʿala. It is possible that «فاعَلَ» here means «فَعَل», as in «سافر» (to travel), so that it agrees with the first reading; and it is possible that it has its usual sense of participation, since the act is from the man and the yielding from the woman, which is why she is called «زانية» (a fornicatress).
