Al-Fārisī preferred the reading of the majority on the ground that the verbs of this category are all triliteral, as in «نكح» (to marry), «فرع», «سفد» (to cover, of animals) and «ضربَ الفحلُ» (the stallion covered).
His saying: {أَوْ تَفْرِضُواْ}: there are four views about it. The first: it is jussive (majzūm), conjoined to «تَمَسُّوهُنَّ», and «أو» has its usual sense of being for one of two things; Ibn ʿAṭiyya said this. The second: it is subjunctive by an implied «أَنْ», conjoined to an imagined maṣdar (verbal noun), and «أو» means «إلاَّ» (unless), the implied form being: «ما لم تَمَسُّوهُنَّ إلا أَنْ تَفْرِضُوا» (as long as you have not touched them, unless you specify), as in their saying «لألزَمَنَّكَ أو تقضيَني حقي» (I will stick to you unless/until you pay me my due); al-Zamakhsharī said this. The third: it is conjoined to an omitted clause, its implied form being «فَرَضْتُم أو لم تَفْرِضُوا» (whether you specified or did not specify), so this would be of the chapter of omitting the jussive-making particle while keeping its effect; this is very weak, and it seems what made it seem good is that the word «لم» is present before it. The fourth: «أو» means «و» (and), and «تَفْرِضُوا» is conjoined to «تَمَسُّوهُنَّ», so it too is jussive.
His saying: {فَرِيضَةً}: there are two views about it. The more apparent of them is that it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), in the sense of a passive participle («مفعولة»), i.e. unless you specify for them something specified. The second: it is accusative as a maṣdar, in the sense of «فَرْضاً» (a specifying). Abū al-Baqāʾ judged the first view good; he said: "And that it be a direct object, and this is the good [view]," the qualified noun being omitted, its implied form being «متعةً مفروضةً» (a specified provision).
His saying: {وَمَتِّعُوهُنَّ}: Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "«وَمَتِّعُوهُنَّ» is conjoined to an omitted verb, its implied form being: «فَطَلِّقُوهُنَّ ومَتِّعُوهُنَّ» (so divorce them and provide for them)." There is no need for this, for the accusative pronoun in «مَتِّعوهن» refers to the women divorced before touching and before specifying, who are mentioned in His saying: {إِن طَلَّقْتُمُ النسآء} to the end of it.
His saying: {عَلَى الموسع قَدَرُهُ} is a clause made of a mubtadaʾ (subject) and a khabar (predicate). About it there are two views. The first: it has no position in i'rab; rather, it is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya), clarifying the state of the divorcing man in relation to his affluence and straitness. The second: it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), the one it qualifies being the agent of «متِّعوهن». Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "Its implied form is «بقَدر الوُسْع» (according to the measure of capacity)," and this is an explanation of the meaning. On making it a ḥāl clause there must be a link between it and the one it qualifies, which is omitted, its implied form being: «على الموسِع منكم» (upon the affluent among you). According to the school of the Kufans and those who followed them, it is also allowed that the alif and lām stand in the place of the pronoun annexed to it, its implied form being «على مُوْسِعِكُم قَدَرُه» (upon your affluent one is his measure).
The majority read «المُوسِعِ» with sukūn on the wāw and kasra on the sīn, as an active participle from «أَوْسع يُوسع». Abū Ḥaywa read it with a fatḥa on the wāw and a doubled sīn [with fatḥa], as a passive participle from «وسَّعَ». Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, Ibn Dhakwān and Ḥafṣ read «قَدَرَه» with a fatḥa on the dāl in both places, and the rest with sukūn.
They disagreed: do they have one meaning or are they different? Abū Zayd, al-Akhfash and the greatest of the authorities on Arabic held that they have one meaning. Abū Zayd related: «خُذْ قَدَر كذا وقَدْر كذا» (take the measure of such-and-such) with one meaning. He said: "And it is read in the Book of Allah: «فسالتْ أوديةٌ بقدَرها» and «قَدْرها»." And He said: {وَمَا قَدَرُواْ الله حَقَّ قَدْرِهِ} [al-Raʿd: 17] [Translator's note: the reference [al-Raʿd: 17] belongs to the preceding «فسالت أودية بقدرها»; {وَمَا قَدَرُواْ الله حَقَّ قَدْرِهِ} is al-Anʿām: 91 (also al-Ḥajj: 74, al-Zumar: 67)], and had the dāl been given a vowel it would have been permissible. A group held that they are different: the one with sukūn is a maṣdar and the one with a vowel is a noun, like «العَدّ» and «العَدَد», «المَدّ» and «المَدَد». It is as though «القَدْر» with sukūn were capacity; one says «هو يُنفق على قَدْرِهِ» (he spends according to his means), i.e. his capacity. It has been said: with sukūn it is ability, and with a vowel it is quantity. Abū Jaʿfar said: "It is most often used with a vowel when it is equal to the thing; one says «هذا على قدَر هذا» (this is in the measure of this)."
Some read it with a fatḥa on the rāʾ. About its accusative there are two views. The first: it is accusative according to the meaning; Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is an object according to the meaning, because the meaning of «مَتِّعوهن» is: let each of you pay the measure of his capacity." The explanation of what he said is that it is of the chapter of implication (taḍmīn): «مَتِّعوهنَّ» was made to imply the meaning of «أدُّوا» (pay). The second: it is accusative by an implied verb, its implied form being: «فَأَوْجِبوا على الموسِعِ قَدَره» (so make his measure obligatory upon the affluent). Abū al-Baqāʾ made this better than the first. In al-Sajāwandī: "Ibn Abī ʿAbla said: «قَدَرَه», i.e. Allah decreed it." End of quote. The apparent meaning of this is that he read it with a fatḥa on the dāl and the rāʾ, so that «قَدَرَه» is a past verb, with an agent pronoun in it referring to Allah the Exalted, and the accusative pronoun referring to the maṣdar understood from «مَتِّعوهن». The meaning is: Allah decreed and prescribed the provision upon the affluent and upon the straitened.
His saying: {مَتَاعاً}: about its accusative there are two views. The first: it is accusative as a maṣdar; precisely stated, it is a noun of the maṣdar (ism maṣdar), because the maṣdar running on its source verb is only «التمتيع», so it is of the chapter of:
{أَنبَتَكُمْ مِّنَ الأرض نَبَاتاً} [Nūḥ: 17]. The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "They said: it is accusative as a maṣdar; precisely stated, «المتاع» is what one is provided with, so it is a noun for it, then it was applied to the maṣdar figuratively, and what governs it is «وَمَتِّعوهُنَّ». This is open to consideration, because what is familiar is that the maṣdar is applied to concrete nouns, like «ضَرْب» in the sense of «مَضْروب» (struck); as for applying concrete nouns to the maṣdar, it is not allowed, even though some allowed it rarely, as in their saying «تِرْبَاً وَجَنْدلاً» (dust and stones [to him]!) and «أقائماً وقد قَعَدَ الناسُ» (standing, when the people have sat down?). The correct view is that «تِرْباً» and the like is a direct object, and «قائماً» is accusative as a ḥāl."
The second of the two views on «متاعاً» is that it is accusative as a ḥāl, what governs it being the verbal meaning contained in the preposition and its genitive noun, and the one it qualifies being that pronoun latent (mustakinn) in that governor; the implied form is: the measure of the affluent is established upon him, while it is a provision.
His saying: {بالمعروف}: there are two views about it. The first: it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «متِّعوهن», so the bāʾ is for transitivity. The second: it is attached to something omitted, being an adjective of «متاعاً», so it is in the position of the accusative, the bāʾ being for accompaniment, i.e. a provision accompanied by what is fair. Al-Ḥūfī allowed a third view, namely that it is attached to «متاعاً» itself.
His saying: {حَقّاً}: about its accusative there are four views. The first: it is a maṣdar emphasising the meaning of the clause before it, as in your saying «هذا ابني حقاً» (this is my son, truly). The governor of this maṣdar must be implied, its implied form being: «حَقَّ ذلك حقاً» (that is truly due); and this maṣdar may not be placed before the clause preceding it. The second: it is an adjective of «متاعاً», i.e. a provision obligatory upon the doers of good. The third: it is a ḥāl of what «متاعاً» was a ḥāl of; this is according to the opinion of those who allow multiple ḥāls. The fourth: it is a ḥāl of «المعروف», i.e. by what is recognised, while being obligatory upon the doers of good. «على المحسنين» may be attached to «حقاً», because it means «الواجب» (obligatory), or attached to something omitted, being an adjective of it.

semin-durr:270-270.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {وَمَآ أَنفَقْتُمْ مِّن نَّفَقَةٍ} is like His saying: {مَا نَنسَخْ} [al-Baqara: 106] and {وَمَا تَفْعَلُواْ مِنْ خَيْرٍ} [al-Baqara: 197], and the precise account of both has already been given. The root «نذر» was also discussed earlier at His saying: {أَأَنذَرْتَهُمْ} [al-Baqara: 6], except that «النَّذْر» (the vow) has a particular sense: it is a person's binding his conscience to something and committing himself to it. Its verb is «نَذَرَ», with fatḥa, «ينذُرُ» and «ينذِرُ», with kasra and ḍamma in the imperfect. One says «نَذَرَ», so he is «ناذِرٌ». ʿAntara said:
1077 - الشاتِمَيْ عِرْضي ولَمْ أَشْتُمهما ... والناذِرين إذا لمَ ألقهما دَمي
(The two who revile my honour though I did not revile them, and who vow to shed my blood when I have not met them.)

His saying: {فَإِنَّ الله يَعْلَمُهُ} is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) if «ما» is conditional, or [the fāʾ] is added in the khabar (predicate) if it is a relative. He made the pronoun in «يَعْلَمُهُ» singular, even though two things preceded — the spending and the vow — because the conjunction here is with «أو», which is for one of two things. You say: «إن جاء زيدٌ أو عمروٌ أكرمته» (if Zayd or ʿAmr comes, I will honour him), and it is not permissible to say «أكرمتهما» (I will honour them both). Rather, you may take account of the first, as in «زيدٌ أو هندٌ منطلقٌ», or of the second, as in «زيدٌ أو هندٌ منطلقة», and the verse is of this kind; it is not permissible to say «منطلقان». For this reason the grammarians interpreted {إِن يَكُنْ غَنِيّاً أَوْ فَقَيراً فالله أولى بِهِمَا} [al-Nisāʾ: 135], as will come. Of taking account of the first is His saying: {وَإِذَا رَأَوْاْ تِجَارَةً أَوْ لَهْواً انفضوا إِلَيْهَا} [al-Jumuʿa: 11]. With what I have established, there is no need for the interpretations the commentators mentioned here. It is narrated that al-Naḥḥās said: "The implied form is: whatever spending you spend, Allah knows it, or whatever vow you vow, Allah knows it; and it was omitted." He compared it with His saying: {والذين يَكْنِزُونَ الذهب والفضة وَلاَ يُنفِقُونَهَا} [al-Tawba: 34], and with the poet's saying:
1078 - نحنُ بما عندَنَا وأنت بما ... عندَكَ راضٍ والرأيُ مختلِفُ
(We are content with what we have, and you with what you have, and opinion differs.)
and another's saying:
1079 - رماني بأمرٍ كنت منه ووالدي ... بريئاً ومن أجل الطَوِيِّ رماني
(He accused me of something of which I and my father were innocent, and it was because of the well that he accused me.)
There is no need for this, because that applies only to the wāw, which entails combining the two things; as for «أو», which entails one of the two things, it does not. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "He made the pronoun in «يَعْلَمُهُ» singular although He mentioned two things, in that He meant 'what He mentioned' or 'what He specified'." There is no need for this either, given what you have learned of the rule of «أو».

semin-durr:272-272.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {لَّيْسَ عَلَيْكَ هُدَاهُمْ}: «هُداهم» is the noun of «ليس», and its khabar (predicate) is the preposition with its genitive noun. «الهُدَى» is a maṣdar (verbal noun) annexed to its object, i.e. "it is not upon you to guide them". It may also be annexed to its agent, i.e. "it is not upon you that they be guided", meaning: it is not upon you to compel them to be guided.

It contains an antithesis (ṭibāq) in meaning, since the implied form is "guidance for those who are astray". In His saying {ولكن الله يَهْدِي} together with His saying «هداهم» there is a paronomasia of differing form (jinās mughāyir), because one of the two words is a noun and the other a verb. The object of «يشاءُ» is omitted, i.e. "[whose] guidance [He wills]".

His saying: {فَلأَنْفُسِكُمْ} is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "then it is for yourselves". Regarding His saying «إلاَّ ابتغاءَ» there are two aspects. The first: it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. "for the sake of seeking the Face of Allah", and the conditions are present here. The second: it is a maṣdar in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "except seeking". In both cases it is an unbounded exception (istithnāʾ mufarragh). The meaning is: "you do not spend any spending whose acceptance counts except in seeking the Face of [Allah]"; or those addressed by this are particular people, namely the Companions, because they were like that. We needed these two interpretations only because many spend seeking something other than the Face of Allah.

His saying: {يُوَفَّ} is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). It has already been stated that one says «وَفَّى» with doubling, «وفَى» without doubling, and the quadriliteral «أَوْفَى».

His saying: {وَأَنْتُمْ لاَ تُظْلَمُونَ} is a clause made of a mubtadaʾ and khabar, in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the pronoun in «إليكم», and what governs it is «يُوَفَّ». It resembles an emphatic ḥāl, because its meaning is understood from His saying «يوفَّ إليكم», since if they are paid their dues in full they are not wronged. It may also be resumptive, with no grammatical position: He informs them in it that no wrong befalls them, so the full payment of their rewards for their spending in obedience to Allah the Exalted is included in it with priority.

semin-durr:256-256.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {لاَ إِكْرَاهَ فِي الدين} is like His words {لاَ رَيْبَ فِيهِ} [al-Baqara: 2], and it has preceded. The majority assimilate the dāl of «قد» into the tāʾ of «تَبَيَّن», because it is from its point of articulation. The meaning of al-ikrāh [here] is attributing to them aversion to Islam. Al-Zajjāj said: "Do not attribute aversion to one who embraced Islam under compulsion." It is said «أَكْفَره», [meaning] he attributed him to unbelief. He said:

1040 - وطائفةٌ قد أَكْفروني بحبِّهم ... وطائفةٌ قالوا مسيءٌ ومُذْنِبُ
(A party have called me an unbeliever for loving them, and a party said: a wrongdoer and a sinner.)

[The al in «الدين» is for prior reference (ʿahd); it is also said: it is a substitute for the annexation, i.e. "in the religion of Allah".]

Al-rushd is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of rashada, with a fatḥa on the middle radical, yarshudu with a ḍamma on it. Al-Ḥasan read «الرُّشُد» [with two ḍammas, like al-ʿunuq; this may be its origin, or it may be vowel-harmony (itbāʿ), and it is a disputed question — I mean the ḍamma on the middle radical. Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān read] «الرَّشَد» with a fatḥa on the first and middle radicals, and it is the maṣdar of rashida, with a kasra on the middle radical, yarshadu with a fatḥa on it. It is also related from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān: «الرَّشادُ» with an alif.

His words: {مِنَ الغي} is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «تبيَّن», and «مِنْ» is for separation and distinction, as in your saying «مَيَّزتُ هذا من ذاك» ("I distinguished this from that"). Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is in the position of the accusative as an object"; this is not apparent, because the meaning of its being a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) does not suit this place. This clause has no grammatical position, because it is a resumptive statement functioning as a giving of the reason for there being no compulsion in religion. Al-ghayy is the maṣdar of ghawā with a fatḥa on the middle radical; He said: {فغوى} [Ṭāhā: 121]. It is said «غَوَى الفصيلُ» ("the weanling ghawā") when it is surfeited and also when it is hungry, so it is one of the words with opposite meanings (aḍdād). The origin of al-ghayy is «غَوْيٌ»; the yāʾ and the wāw met, and they were assimilated, as in mayyit and its class.

His words: {بالطاغوت} is attached to «يكْفر». Al-ṭāghūt is a pattern of intensification like al-jabarūt and al-malakūt. There has been disagreement about it. It is said that it is originally a maṣdar, and for that reason it is used in the singular and masculine, like other maṣdars applied to concrete things; this is the doctrine of al-Fārisī. It is said that it is a singular generic noun, and for that reason it is consistently singular and masculine; this is the doctrine of Sībawayh. It is also said that it is a plural; this is the doctrine of al-Mubarrad. It is feminine, as evidenced by His words, the Exalted: {والذين اجتنبوا الطاغوت أَن يَعْبُدُوهَا} [al-Zumar: 17]. Its derivation is from ṭaghā yaṭghā, or from ṭaghā yaṭghū, according to what preceded at the beginning of the sūra: is it from the roots with final wāw or from those with final yāʾ? On either supposition its origin is ṭaghayūt or ṭaghawūt, because of their saying «طُغْيان» in its meaning. Then the word was metathesized, the final radical being brought forward and the middle radical put after; the weak letter was then vowelled with the letter before it having a fatḥa, so it was changed into an alif, and its pattern now is falaʿūt. It is also said that its tāʾ is not augmentative, but is a substitute for the final radical of the word, its pattern being fāʿūl. Makkī said: "It may be that the origin of its final radical is wāw, so that its origin is ṭaghawūt, because one says ṭaghā yaṭghā and yaṭghū, ṭaghaytu and ṭaghawtu. Similar to it in metathesis, weakening and pattern is ḥānūt, because it is from ḥanā yaḥnū, its origin being ḥanawūt, then it was metathesized and weakened. It cannot be from ḥāna yaḥīnu, because of their saying in the plural ḥawānīt." End quote.

It is as though, when he saw that the wāw is sometimes replaced by a tāʾ, as in tujāh, tukhama, turāth and tukaʾa, he claimed that the wāw which is the final radical was changed into a tāʾ; this is worthless.

He put the mention of disbelief in al-ṭāghūt before the mention of belief in Allah, out of concern for the obligation of disbelieving in al-ṭāghūt, and its being joined to the word «الغَيّ» suited it.

Al-ʿurwa is the place where the hands grip. The root fundamentally indicates attachment; from it is «عَرَوْتُه»: I came to him, attaching myself, and «اعتراه الهَمُّ»: worry attached itself to him. Al-wuthqā is fuʿlā of the elative, the feminine of al-awthaq, like fuḍlā the feminine of al-afḍal. Its plural is wuthaq, like kubrā and kubar; as for «وُثُق» with two ḍammas, it is the plural of wathīq.

His words: {لاَ انفصام لَهَا} is like His words {لاَ رَيْبَ فِيهِ} [al-Baqara: 2]. The clause has three aspects. The first is that it is resumptive, so it then has no grammatical position. The second is that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «العُرْوة», its governor being «استمسَكَ». The third is that it is a ḥāl from the pronoun latent (mustatir) in «الوُثْقى». «لها» is in the position of the khabar (predicate), so it is attached to something omitted, i.e. "existing for it". Al-infiṣām — with fāʾ — is cutting without separation, and al-qaṣm with qāf is cutting with separation; the one with fāʾ is sometimes used in place of the one with qāf.

semin-durr:257-257.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {والذين كفروا أَوْلِيَآؤُهُمُ}: «الذين» is a first mubtadaʾ (subject), «أولياؤهم» a second mubtadaʾ, and «الطاغوت» its khabar (predicate), the clause being the khabar of the first. Al-Ḥasan read [«الطواغيت» in the plural; although it is originally a maṣdar (verbal noun), when] it was applied to what is worshipped besides Allah, its kinds became diverse. This is supported by the pronoun referring back in the plural in His words «يُخْرِجونهم».

His words: {يُخْرِجُونَهُمْ}: concerning this clause and the one before it, namely His words «يُخْرِجُهم», it is best that they have no grammatical position, because both come forth as an explication of the guardianship (wilāya). «يُخْرِجُهم» may also be a second khabar of His word «الله», or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «وليُّ»; likewise «يُخْرجونهم», the governor of the ḥāl being what is in the meaning of «الطاغوت». This is analogous to what al-Fārisī said about His words {نَزَّاعَةً} [al-Maʿārij: 16], that it is a ḥāl whose governor is «لَظَى»; its verification will come. «من» [and] «إلى» are both attached (mutaʿalliq) to the two verbs of bringing out.

semin-durr:258-258.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى الذي}: its analogue has preceded at His words {أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى الذين خَرَجُواْ} [al-Baqara: 243]. ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, read «تَرْ» with a quiescent rāʾ, and its rationale has also preceded. Concerning the hāʾ in «ربه» there are two views. The more evident is that it refers to «إبراهيم»; the second, that it refers to «الذي». The meaning of «حاجَّه» is: he displayed contention in his argument.

His words: {أَنْ آتَاهُ الله}: there are two aspects. The more evident is that it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose) with the omission of the particle of cause, i.e. "because He had given him". In that case there are in the position of «أَنْ» the two well-known aspects, I mean the accusative or the genitive. A preposition must be posited before «أَنْ», because the object of purpose here lacks a condition, namely that the agent not be the same [Translator's note: so in the source; the usual condition is that the object of purpose share the agent of the verb, which is lacking here]. The lām was elided only because the elision of the preposition is regular with it and with «أنَّ», as has preceded more than once. In its being an object of purpose there are two meanings. The first is that it belongs to the chapter of inversion in speech, meaning that he put disputation in the place of thanks, since it was his duty to give thanks in return for being given kingship, but he acted contrary to what was required. From this is {وَتَجْعَلُونَ رِزْقَكُمْ أَنَّكُمْ تُكَذِّبُونَ} [al-Wāqiʿa: 82], and you say: «عاداني فلانٌ لأني أَحْسنت أليه» ("so-and-so became hostile to me because I did good to him"); it is an eloquent chapter. The second is that being given kingship drove him to that, because it bred in him arrogance and insolence, from which disputation resulted.

The second aspect: «أَنْ» and what falls within its scope occur in the place of an adverb of time. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The implied form may be: he disputed at the time that He gave him." What al-Zamakhsharī permitted here is open to consideration, because if he means that this is by the omission of a muḍāf, it is far-fetched in that the disputation did not occur at the time that Allah gave him kingship — unless one is lax regarding the time, so that it is not taken in its apparent sense, namely that the disputation occurred at the start of the giving of kingship, but rather is taken to mean that the disputation occurred at a time when the kingship existed. And if he means that «أَنْ» and what falls within its scope occur in the place of the adverb, the grammarians have explicitly forbidden that, saying: only the explicit maṣdar (verbal noun) substitutes for the adverb of time, as in «أتيتُك صياحَ الديك» ("I came to you at the cock's crowing"); if you said «أن يصيح الديك» it would not be permissible. So said the Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān]; but this is open to consideration, because he said: "only the explicit maṣdar substitutes for the adverb", and this is contradicted by their having explicitly stated that maṣdar-forming «ما» substitutes for time, though it is not an explicit maṣdar.

Concerning the pronoun in «آتاه» there are two aspects. The first — and it is the more evident — is that it refers to «الذي». Al-Mahdawī permitted it to refer to «إبراهيم», i.e. the kingship of prophethood. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "This is a forced interpretation." The Shaykh said: "This is the view of the Muʿtazila. They said: because Allah the Exalted said {لاَ يَنَالُ عَهْدِي الظالمين} [al-Baqara: 124], and kingship is a covenant; and because of His words, the Exalted: {فَقَدْ آتَيْنَآ آلَ إِبْرَاهِيمَ الكتاب والحكمة وَآتَيْنَاهُمْ مُّلْكاً عَظِيماً} [al-Nisāʾ: 54]."

His words: {إِذْ قَالَ}: there are four aspects. The most evident is that it is governed by «حاجَّ». The second is that it is governed by «آتاه»; Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned it. This is open to consideration in that the time of giving kingship is not the time of Ibrāhīm's saying {رَبِّيَ الذي يُحْيِي وَيُمِيتُ}, unless one is lax regarding the adverb, as preceded. The third is that it is a badal (substitute) from «أنْ آتاه الله المُلْك» when that is taken to mean the time; al-Zamakhsharī permitted it, building on his view that «أَنْ» occurs in the place of the adverb; its weakness has preceded. Moreover, the two adverbs differ, as preceded, except by the laxity mentioned. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "Some mentioned that it is a badal from «أَنْ آتاه», and this is worthless, because the adverb is other than the maṣdar, so if it were a badal it would be a badal of mistake (badal ghalaṭ) — unless «إذ» is made to mean maṣdar-forming «أَنْ», and that has occurred." End quote. This is built by him on «أَنْ» being an object of purpose and not occurring in the place of the adverb. But if «أَنْ» occurs in the place of the adverb, it would not be a badal of mistake but a badal of whole for whole, as is the view of al-Zamakhsharī, with what has preceded about it. Moreover, it may be a badal from «أَنْ آتاه» — with «أن آتاه» a maṣdar that is an object of purpose — as a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl), because the time of the saying, owing to its extent, includes it and other things. The fourth is that what governs it is «تَرَ» from His words «ألم ترَ»; Makkī mentioned it. This is worthless, because the seeing, on both interpretations mentioned at its analogue, was not at the time of his saying {رَبِّيَ الذي يُحْيِي وَيُمِيتُ}.

{رَبِّيَ الذي يُحْيِي} is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate) in the position of the accusative by «القول» (the verb of saying). His words: {قَالَ أَنَا أُحْيِي}: a mubtadaʾ and khabar, likewise accusative in position by the verb of saying. He predicated of «أنا» with the verbal clause, and of «ربي» with the relative noun whose ṣila (relative clause) it is, because predication with the relative noun conveys exclusivity to the subject, unlike the second; for he did not claim for his base self exclusivity in that.

«أنا» is a detached nominative pronoun. The noun of it is «أَنْ», and the alif is augmentative, to make the vowel clear in pause; for that reason it is elided in continuous speech. Some Arabs retain it absolutely, and it is said: continuous speech was treated like pause. He said:

1041 - وكيفَ أنا وانتحالِ القوا ... في بعدَ المشيبِ كفى ذاك عارَا
(And how could I lay false claim to rhymes after grey hair? That is disgrace enough.)

Another said:

1042 - أنا سيفُ العشيرةِ فاعرِفوني ... حَمِيداً قد تَذَرَّيْتُ السَّناما
(I am the sword of the clan, so know me as praiseworthy; I have mounted to the top of the hump [of glory].)

The correct view is that there are two dialectal forms in it. The first is the dialect of Tamīm, which is retaining its alif in continuous speech and in pause. On it is construed the reading of Nāfiʿ, for he read with the alif retained in continuous speech before a hamza with ḍamma, as in «أنا أُحيي», or with fatḥa, as in {وَأَنَاْ أَوَّلُ} [al-Aʿrāf: 143]; there is disagreement in what is transmitted from him before one with kasra, as in {إِنْ أَنَاْ إِلاَّ [نَذِيرٌ]} [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 115]. [On it too is construed] the reading of Ibn ʿĀmir {لكنا هُوَ الله رَبِّي}, as will come. This is better than the rationale of whoever says: "continuous speech was treated like pause." The second form: retaining it in pause and eliding it in continuous speech; it may not be retained in continuous speech except in poetic necessity, as in the two preceding verses. It is also said: rather «أنا» is a pronoun in its entirety.

There are several dialectal forms in it: anā; an — like the word «أَنْ» that makes the imperfect accusative —; and ān, as though the alif were put before the nūn, so that it became aʾan. It is said that what is meant by it is time. [And] they said anah, the hāʾ being the hāʾ of pause (hāʾ al-sakt), not a substitute for the alif. He said: «هكذا فَرْدِي أَنَهْ» ("this is how I use my single [arrow]"). Another said:

1043 - إنْ كنتُ أدري فعليَّ بَدَنَهْ ... من كَثْرةِ التخليطِ فيَّ مَنْ أَنَهْ
(If I know who I am, amid all the confusion in me, then I owe a sacrificial camel.)

Nāfiʿ retained its alif before the hamza only to combine the two dialectal forms, or because pronouncing the hamza is difficult, so he gave himself ease for it with the alif, since it is a letter of prolongation.

His words: {فَإِنَّ الله}: this fāʾ is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, its implied form being: "Ibrāhīm said: if you claim, or make a false show of, that, then Allah…". Had the clause been reported by the verb of saying, this fāʾ would not have entered; rather the construction of the speech would have been: "Ibrāhīm said: Allah brings…". Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "The fāʾ entered to signal that this speech is connected with what precedes it; the meaning is: if you claim giving life and causing death and you do not understand, then the proof is that Allah brings… This is the meaning." The bāʾ in «بالشمسِ» is for transitivity: you say «أَتَتِ الشمسُ» ("the sun came") and «أتى اللهُ بها» ("Allah brought it"), i.e. He made it come. «من المشرق» and «مِن المغرب» are attached (mutaʿalliq) to the two verbs before them. Abū al-Baqāʾ, after having forbidden it, permitted them to be two ḥāls (circumstantials), and made the implied form "subjugated" or "submissive". Would that he had persisted in forbidding it.

His words: {فَبُهِتَ}: the majority [read] «بُهِتَ» in the passive, the relative noun being nominative by it [as nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent)]. The original fāʿil (agent) is Ibrāhīm, because he is the one debating with him. It is also possible that the original fāʿil is the pronoun of the maṣdar understood from «قال», i.e. "Ibrāhīm's saying confounded him". Ibn al-Samayfaʿ read «فَبَهَتَ» with a fatḥa on the bāʾ and the hāʾ, in the active voice. This admits two aspects. The first is that the verb is transitive, its fāʿil being a pronoun referring to Ibrāhīm, and «الذي» being the object, i.e. "Ibrāhīm confounded the unbeliever", i.e. overcame him in argument; or the fāʿil is the relative noun and the object is omitted, namely Ibrāhīm, i.e. "the unbeliever slandered Ibrāhīm", i.e. when he was cut off from argument he slandered him. The second is that it is intransitive and the relative noun is the fāʿil, the meaning being that of «بُهِت», so the two readings coincide; or it means "he came out with a slander". Abū Ḥaywa read «فَبَهُتَ» with a fatḥa on the bāʾ and a ḍamma on the hāʾ, like ẓarufa, the fāʿil being the relative noun. Al-Akhfash related «فَبُهِتَ» with a kasra on the hāʾ, and it is likewise intransitive. [Translator's note: the vowelling in the source shows a ḍamma on the bāʾ; the description "with a kasra on the hāʾ" refers to fa-bahita, as the following list shows.] So three dialectal forms result in it: bahata with fatḥa on both, bahuta with a ḍamma on the middle radical, and bahita with a kasra on it. The one with fatḥa can be intransitive or transitive; He said: {فَتَبْهَتُهُمْ} [al-Anbiyāʾ: 40]. Al-baht is bewilderment and astonishment; «باهَتَه» and «بَهَته» mean he confronted him with a lie. From it is the ḥadīth: "The Jews are a people given to slander (buhut)", and that is because a lie bewilders the one lied about.

semin-durr:271-271.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {فَنِعِمَّا هِيَ}: the fāʾ is that of the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). «نِعْمَ» is a past verb of praise, the opposite of «بئس»; its rule regarding non-inflection, its fāʿil (agent) and its dialectal forms is the rule of «بئس», as stated earlier, so there is no need to lengthen by repeating it.

Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read here and in [Sūrat] al-Nisāʾ «فَنَعِمَا» with fatḥa on the nūn and kasra on the ʿayn; this is according to the original, because the original is on the pattern faʿila, like «عَلِم». Ibn Kathīr, Warsh and Ḥafṣ read with kasra on both the nūn and the ʿayn; the nūn has kasra only to harmonise with the kasra of the ʿayn, and this is the dialect of Hudhayl. It is said: the reading with kasra on the ʿayn may also be explained as the ʿayn originally having sukūn; when «ما» came after it and the mīm of «نِعْم» was assimilated into it, the ʿayn was given kasra because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. This is possible. Abū ʿAmr, Qālūn and Abū Bakr read with kasra on the nūn and a concealed (slurred) vowel on the ʿayn. Sukūn is also narrated from them; Abū ʿUbayd chose it and reported it as a usage of the Prophet ﷺ, as in his saying: «نِعْمَّا المالُ الصالحُ مع الرجلِ الصالحِ» ("How excellent is righteous wealth with a righteous man!").

The majority choose the slurring (ikhtilās) over the sukūn; indeed some of them regard [the sukūn] as an error of the narrators from Abū ʿAmr. Among those who rejected it are al-Mubarrad, al-Zajjāj and al-Fārisī. They said: because it involves combining two quiescent letters in a way other than their proper one. Al-Mubarrad said: "No one is able to pronounce it; he only attempts to combine two quiescent letters, and so he gives a vowel without realising it." Al-Fārisī said: "Perhaps Abū ʿAmr concealed [the vowel], and the narrator thought it was sukūn."

The discussion of «ما» attached to «نِعْم» and «بِئْس» has already been given. «هي» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), a pronoun referring back to the charities with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "how excellent is disclosing them". It is also possible not to imply a muḍāf; rather the pronoun refers back to «الصدقات» as restricted by the attribute of disclosure, its implied form being "how excellent they are", i.e. the disclosed charities. The clause of praise is the khabar (predicate) of «هي», and the link is generality; this is the best of the aspects, and their precise account has already been given.

The pronoun in «وإنْ تخفوها» refers back to the charities. It is said: it refers back to them in both wording and meaning. And it is said: it refers back to the charities in wording, not in meaning, because what is meant by the disclosed charities is the obligatory ones, and by the concealed ones the voluntary ones; so it would belong to the category of «عندي درهمٌ ونصفُه» (I have a dirham and half of it), i.e. half of another dirham; and like the poet's saying:
1080 - كأنَّ ثيابَ راكبِهِ بريحٍ ... خَرِيقٌ وهْي ساكنةُ الهُبوبِ
(As though the clothes of its rider were in a violent wind, while it is a wind that blows calmly.)
i.e. "and another wind that blows calmly". There is no need for this in the verse.

The fāʾ in His saying «فهو» is that of the apodosis, and the pronoun refers back to the maṣdar (verbal noun) understood from «تُخْفُوها», i.e. "then the concealing", as in His saying: {اعدلوا هُوَ أَقْرَبُ} [al-Māʾida: 8]. «لكم» is a naʿt (adjective) of «خير», so it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted element. «خير» may be an elative, in which case what it is preferred over is omitted, i.e. "better than disclosing them"; or it may be meant as a description of goodness, i.e. "a good thing for you among good things".

In His saying «إنْ تُبْدوا» and «وإن تُخْفُوها» there is a type of rhetorical embellishment (badīʿ), namely verbal antithesis (ṭibāq lafẓī).

In His saying «وتُؤتوها الفقراء» there is an antithesis in meaning, because only the rich give charities, so it is as though it were said: "If the rich disclose the charities, and if the rich conceal the charities and give them to the poor"; so He contrasted disclosure with concealment [in wording], and the rich with the poor in meaning.

His saying: {وَيُكَفِّرُ}: the majority read «ويُكَفِّرُ» with the wāw, and al-Aʿmash without it, with yāʾ and the rāʾ in the jussive. There are two explanations of this. The first: it is a badal (substitute) for the position of His saying {فَهُوَ خَيْرٌ لَّكُمْ}, because that is the apodosis, as though the implied form were: "and if you conceal them, it will be better for you and will expiate". The second: the conjunction was omitted, so it would be like the well-known reading, the implied form being «ويكفِّرُ»; this is very weak.

Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr and Abū Bakr read with nūn and the rāʾ in the nominative. Nāfiʿ, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read with nūn and the rāʾ in the jussive. Ibn ʿĀmir, and Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim, read with yāʾ and the rāʾ in the nominative. Al-Ḥasan read with yāʾ and the rāʾ in the jussive. It is also narrated from al-Aʿmash with yāʾ and the rāʾ in the accusative. Ibn ʿAbbās read «وتُكَفِّرْ» with the feminine tāʾ and the rāʾ in the jussive. ʿIkrima read likewise, except that he gave fatḥa to the fāʾ, in the passive. Ibn Hurmuz read with tāʾ and the rāʾ in the nominative. Shahr ibn Ḥawshab — and it is also narrated from ʿIkrima — read with tāʾ and the rāʾ in the accusative. It is also narrated from al-Aʿmash with nūn and the rāʾ in the accusative, and also from al-Aʿmash with nūn and the rāʾ in the accusative [Translator's note: this clause is repeated in the source]. These are eleven readings, of which three are well known.

Whoever read with yāʾ, there are three aspects regarding it. The most evident: he implied in the verb a pronoun referring to Allah the Exalted, because He is the one who truly expiates; this is supported by the reading with nūn, for it is restricted to Him. The second: it refers back to the giving [of charity] indicated by the force of the speech, i.e. "and the giving of charities will expiate". The third: it refers back to the concealing understood from His saying «وإنْ تُخْفُوها». Expiation is attributed to the giving and the concealing figuratively, because they are a cause of expiation; just as it is permissible to attribute a verb to its agent, it is permissible to attribute it to its cause.

Whoever read with tāʾ, the verb contains a pronoun referring to the charities, and expiation is attributed to them figuratively, as stated. Whoever made it passive, the agent is Allah the Exalted, or what was mentioned above. Whoever read with nūn, it is the nūn of the speaker who magnifies himself. Whoever put the rāʾ in the jussive did so by conjunction with the position of the clause that is the apodosis; its analogue is His saying {مَن يُضْلِلِ الله فَلاَ هَادِيَ لَهُ وَيَذَرُهُمْ} in the reading of whoever put {وَيَذَرُهُمْ} [al-Aʿrāf: 186] in the jussive. Whoever put it in the nominative did so on three aspects. The first: it is resumptive, with no grammatical position, the wāw conjoining one sentence to another sentence. The second: it is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, that mubtadaʾ being either a pronoun referring to Allah the Exalted or the concealing, i.e. "and He expiates" for whoever read with yāʾ, or "and We expiate" for whoever read with nūn, or "and they expiate" for whoever read with the feminine tāʾ. The third: it is conjoined to the position of what comes after the fāʾ, since if an imperfect verb occurred after it, it would be nominative, as in His saying: {وَمَنْ عَادَ فَيَنْتَقِمُ الله مِنْهُ} [al-Māʾida: 95]; its analogue is {وَيَذَرُهُمْ فِي طُغْيَانِهِمْ} [al-Aʿrāf: 186] in the reading of whoever put it in the nominative.

Whoever put it in the accusative did so by implying «أَنْ», in conjunction with an imagined maṣdar taken from His saying {فَهُوَ خَيْرٌ لَّكُمْ}, the implied form being: "and if you conceal them, there will be (or: there will exist) good and expiation".

Its analogue is the reading of whoever put «فيغفرَ» in the accusative after His saying {يُحَاسِبْكُمْ بِهِ الله} [al-Baqara: 284], except that implying the maṣdar in His saying «يحاسِبْكم» is easier than here, because there is an explicit verb there, namely «يحاسبْكم», and the implied form is "a reckoning occurs, and then forgiveness"; unlike here, since there is no verb pronounced, and we have only extracted the maṣdar from the whole of His saying {فَهُوَ خَيْرٌ لَّكُمْ}.

Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Its meaning is: and if you conceal them, it will be better for you, and [it will be] that He expiates." The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "The apparent sense of these words of his is that his implied form «وأَنْ يكفِّرَ» is to be implied as a maṣdar and is conjoined to «خيراً», which is the khabar of the «يَكُنْ» he implied, as though he said: 'the concealing will be good for you and an expiation', so that «أَنْ يكفِّر» would be in the position of the accusative. What is established among the Basrans is that this maṣdar, formed from the implied «أَنْ» together with the verb it puts in the accusative, is nominative, conjoined to an imagined nominative maṣdar which you imply from the meaning. So if you say «ما تأتينا فتحدثَنا» (you do not come to us and talk to us), the implied form is 'there is no coming from you and then talking'; likewise «إنْ تجيءْ وتُحْسِنَ إليَّ أُحْسِنْ إليك» (if you come and do good to me, I will do good to you): the implied form is 'if there is coming and doing good from you, I will do good to you'. On this basis the implied form would be: 'and if you conceal them and give them to the poor, there will be an increase of good for the concealing over the good of disclosing, and an expiation'." End of quotation. I do not know what led the Shaykh to turn away from the construal of Abū al-Qāsim [al-Zamakhsharī] to his own construal and to lengthen the discussion of it, when what lies between the two construals is evident.

Al-Mahdawī said: "It is likened to the accusative in the response to a question, since through the conditional response a thing becomes due because of another thing becoming due, as with a question." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "The jussive on the rāʾ is the most eloquent of these readings, because it signals that the expiation enters into the conditional response and is conditional upon the concealing occurring; the nominative on the rāʾ does not carry this meaning." The Shaykh said: "We say that the nominative is more eloquent and more general, because the jussive is on the basis that it is conjoined to the response of the second condition, whereas the nominative indicates that the expiation follows, in terms of meaning, from giving charities, whether disclosed or concealed; for we know that this expiation is connected with what precedes it, and expiation is not restricted to concealing alone, while the jussive restricts it to it. It cannot be said that the one who discloses charities does not have some of his evil deeds expiated; so expiation has come to include both kinds, disclosing charities and concealing them, even though concealing is better."

His saying: {مِّن سَيِّئَاتِكُمْ}: regarding «مِنْ» there are three views. The first: it is partitive, i.e. "some of your evil deeds", because charities do not expiate all evil deeds. On this basis the object is in reality omitted, i.e. "something of your evil deeds"; this is how Abū al-Baqāʾ construed it. The second: it is redundant (zāʾida), which follows the doctrine of al-Akhfash; Ibn ʿAṭiyya reported it from al-Ṭabarī from a group, and he regarded it as an error, meaning in terms of meaning. The third: it is causal, i.e. "because of your sins"; this is weak. «السيئات» is the plural of «سيِّئة», whose pattern is fayʿila, and its middle radical is a wāw; the original is «سَيْوِئَة», and the same was done to it as was done to «ميِّت», as stated earlier.

semin-durr:237-237.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {وَقَدْ فَرَضْتُمْ}: this clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). The one it qualifies may be the pronoun of the agent or the pronoun of the object, because the linking element (rābiṭ) is present in both. The implied form is: if you divorce them while specifying for them, or while [something] is specified for them. «فريضة» allows here the two views mentioned before.
The fāʾ in «فنصفُ» is [the fāʾ of] the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), so the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis of the condition. The nominative of «نصفُ» is on one of two views: either as a mubtadaʾ (subject), the khabar (predicate) then being omitted — if you wish you may imply it before it, i.e. «فعليكم» (then upon you) or «فلَهُنَّ نصفُ» (then theirs is half), and if you wish, after it, i.e. «فنصفُ ما فرضتُم عليكم» (then half of what you specified is upon you) — or «لَهُنَّ» (is theirs) —; or as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being «فالواجبُ نصفُ» (then what is obligatory is half).
A group read «فنصفَ» in the accusative, on the implied form «فادْفَعُوا» (then hand over) or «أَدُّوا» (pay). Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "Had it been read in the accusative, its justification would be «فأَدُّوا نصفَ» (then pay half)," so it seems he did not come across it as a transmitted reading.
The majority read «نِصْف» with a kasra on the nūn. Zayd and ʿAlī read — and al-Aṣmaʿī narrated it as a reading from Abū ʿAmr — «فَنُصف» with a ḍamma on the nūn, here and throughout the Qurʾān; they are two dialect forms. There is a third form in it: «نَصيف» with an added yāʾ, and from it is the ḥadīth: «ما بَلَغ مُدَّ أحدِهم ولا نَصِيفه» (it would not reach the mudd of one of them, nor half of it). «ما» in «ما فرضتم» means «الذي» (that which), and the referent-pronoun (ʿāʾid) is omitted because the conditions are fulfilled; making it an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective is weak.
His saying: {إَلاَّ أَن يَعْفُونَ}: about this exception there are two views. The first: it is a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ); Ibn ʿAṭiyya and others said: "because their forgoing the half is not of the same kind as their taking." The second: it is connected (muttaṣil), but from the circumstances, because His saying {فَنِصْفُ مَا فَرَضْتُمْ} means: what is obligatory upon you is half of what you specified in every circumstance except in the circumstance of their forgoing, for then it is not obligatory. Abū al-Baqāʾ inclined to this, and it is apparent. Its parallel is: {لَتَأْتُنَّنِي بِهِ إِلاَّ أَن يُحَاطَ بِكُمْ} [Yūsuf: 66]. The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "Except that whoever disallows «أَنْ» and its ṣila from occurring as a ḥāl — like Sībawayh — disallows that, and it would then be disconnected."
Al-Ḥasan read «يَعْفُونَه» with a ḍamma-marked hāʾ. There are two views about it. The first: it is a pronoun referring to the half, the original being «إلاَّ أَنْ يَعْفُونَ عنه» (unless they forgo it); the preposition was omitted, so the pronoun became attached to the verb. The second: it is the hāʾ of pausing and resting (hāʾ al-sakt), and he only gave it a ḍamma by likening it to the pronoun hāʾ, as in the saying of another:
1005 - هم الفاعلونَ الخيرَ والآمرونَه ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(They are the doers of good and the commanders of it …)
according to one of the two interpretations of the verse as well.
Ibn Abī Isḥāq read «تَعْفُون» with the tāʾ of address. Its justification is a shift (iltifāt) from the third-person pronoun to address; the benefit of this shift is urging their forgoing and [indicating] that it is recommended.
«يَعْفُون» is subjunctive by «أَنْ» in an implied way (taqdīran), for it is indeclinable (mabnī) because of being attached to the nūn of the feminine plural. This is the opinion of the majority; as for Ibn Durustawayh and al-Suhaylī, in their view it is declinable. Al-Zamakhsharī and Abū al-Baqāʾ distinguished between your saying «الرجالُ يَعْفُون» (the men forgo) and «النساءُ يَعْفُون» (the women forgo) — even though this is among the obvious points of grammar —: in your saying «الرجالُ يَعْفُون», the wāw is the pronoun of the masculine plural, and before it another wāw was deleted, which is the final radical of the word, for the original is «يَعْفُوُون»; the ḍamma on the first wāw was found heavy and was deleted, so it remained with sukūn, and after it the pronoun wāw also with sukūn, so the first wāw was deleted lest two sukūns meet; its pattern is «يَفْعُون», and the nūn is the marker of the nominative, for it is one of the five forms (al-amthila al-khamsa).
In your saying «النساء يَعْفُون», the wāw is the final radical of the word and the nūn is the pronoun of the feminine plural, and the verb with it is indeclinable, the governor leaving no visible trace on it. The Shaykh took al-Zamakhsharī to task, [saying] that this is among the obvious things known by the slightest reading in this science, that he did not explain the deletion of the wāw in your saying «الرجال يعفون», and that he did not mention any disagreement about the indeclinability of the imperfect attached to the nūn of the feminine plural. All of this is easy, and one should not be taken to task over the like of it.
His saying: {أَوْ يَعْفُوَاْ الذي}: about «أو» here there are two views. The first: it is for variety (tanwīʿ). The second: it is for choice (takhyīr). The well-known reading is with a fatḥa on the wāw, conjoined to the subjunctive before it. Al-Ḥasan read it with sukūn: he found the fatḥa on the wāw heavy and so implied it, as it is implied on the alif. The rest of the Arabs find it light, and it may not be implied except under poetic necessity, as in the saying — he is ʿĀmir ibn al-Ṭufayl —:
1006 - فما سَوَّدَتْني عامِرٌ عن وراثةٍ ... أبى اللَّهُ أَنْ أَسْمو بأمٍّ ولا أَبِ
(ʿĀmir did not make me lord by inheritance; Allah refused that I should rise by a mother or a father.)
When he gave the wāw sukūn, it was deleted because of the sukūn after it, namely the lām of «الذي». Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "What I hold is that he found the fatḥa heavy on a final wāw preceded by a voweled letter, because of how rarely it occurs in their speech. Al-Khalīl said: 'There has not come in speech a final wāw with fatḥa preceded by a fatḥa except their saying «عَفَوة», the plural of «عَفْو», which is the young of the donkey; likewise any vowel, whatever it is, before a wāw with fatḥa is heavy.'" End of quote. The Shaykh said: "His saying 'because of how rarely it occurs' means [a wāw] with fatḥa preceded by fatḥa. What he mentioned needs detailing: the vowel before it is either a ḍamma, a kasra or a fatḥa. If it is a ḍamma, it is either in a noun or in a verb. If in a verb, it is common: that is, all the forms of the imperfect entered by a subjunctive particle, as in «لَنْ يغزُوَ» (he will not raid), and those of them to which the nūn of emphasis is attached, as in «هلَ يَغْزُوَنَّ» (will he indeed raid?), and likewise the imperative, as in «اغزُوَنَّ» (do raid!), and likewise the past tense on the pattern «فَعُل» in exclamation, as in «سَرُوَ الرجل» (how noble the man is!) — so much so that verbs with final yāʾ are returned to wāw in exclamation and they say «لَقَضُوَ الرجلُ» (how well the man judges!), as is established in the chapter on morphology. If it is in a noun, then either it is built upon the feminine hāʾ, in which case it is also common, as in «عَرْقُوة», «تَرْقُوة» (collarbone) and «قَمَحْدُوَة» (occiput). If there is a fatḥa before it, it is rare, as al-Khalīl mentioned. If there is a kasra before it, the wāw is changed to yāʾ, as in «الغازي» and «الغازية»; anomalous exceptions to this are «أَفْرِوَة», the plural of «فَرِوَة», which is a dog's drinking vessel; «سواسِوَة», those who are equal in evil; and «مقاتِوَة», the plural of «مُقْتَوٍ», which is the servant groom.
The upshot of this is that what is meant by rare is a final wāw with fatḥa [preceded by fatḥa] in a noun not joined to the feminine tāʾ. So Ibn ʿAṭiyya's saying 'what I hold…' to the end is not apparent."
What is meant by His saying {الذي بِيَدِهِ عُقْدَةُ النكاح}: it has been said: the husband; and it has been said: the guardian (walī). The «أل» in «النكاح» is for prior reference (ʿahd), and it is a substitute for the annexation [Translator's note: the source reads «وقيد», apparently a slip for «وقيل» (and it has been said)], i.e. «نكاحُه» (his marriage), as in the poet's saying:
1007 - لهمْ شَيمَةٌ لم يُعْطِها اللهُ غيرَهم ... من الجودِ، والأحلامُ غيرُ عَوازِبِ
(They have a nature of generosity which Allah has given to none but them, and the minds are not absent.)
i.e. «أحلامُهم» (their minds); this is the opinion of the Kufans. Some said: there is an omission in the speech, its implied form being «بيده حلُّ عقدةِ النكاحِ» (in whose hand is the untying of the knot of marriage), just as that was said about His saying {وَلاَ تعزموا عُقْدَةَ النكاح} [al-Baqara: 235], i.e. the tying of the knot of marriage; and this supports that what is meant is the husband.
His saying: {وَأَن تعفوا أَقْرَبُ}: «أن تَعْفُوا» is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ, because it is interpreted as «عَفْوُكم» (your forgoing), and «أقربُ» is its khabar. The majority read «تَعْفُوا» with address, what is meant being the men and the women, with the masculine given predominance. What is apparent is that it is for the husbands specifically, because they are those addressed at the beginning of the verse; on this view it is a shift from the third person — namely His saying {الذي بِيَدِهِ عُقْدَةُ النكاح}, on our view that what is meant by it is the husband, which is the preferred view — to the first address at the beginning of the verse. Al-Shaʿbī and Abū Nahīk read «يَعْفوا» with the lower-dotted yāʾ. The Shaykh said: "He made it third person, and it was put in the plural according to the meaning of «الذي بيدِه عقدةُ النكاح», because it is for the genus and not one person is meant." He means that His saying «وأن يَعْفوا» is originally «يَعْفُوُون»; when the subjunctive-making particle entered, the nūn of the nominative was deleted, then the wāw that is the final radical of the word was deleted, and this [remaining wāw] in it is the pronoun of the plural, put in the plural according to the meaning of the relative, because although it is singular in wording it is plural in meaning, being a genus [Translator's note: the source says "this yāʾ in it is the pronoun of the plural"; it is the wāw that is the plural pronoun]. Another view appears in it: that the wāw is the final radical of the word, and in this verb [Translator's note: the source has «الفصل», apparently a slip for «الفعل»] there is a singular pronoun referring to the one in whose hand is the knot of marriage, except that he implied the fatḥa on the wāw because of heaviness, as preceded in the reading of al-Ḥasan; its implied form is «وأَنْ يعفو الذي بيده عقدةُ» (and that the one in whose hand is the knot should forgo).
His saying: {للتقوى} is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «أقرب», and [the lām] here is for transitivity; it has also been said that it is causal. «أقربُ» is made transitive sometimes with the lām, as in this verse, and sometimes with «إلى», as in His saying, Exalted is He: {وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ الوريد} [Qāf: 16]. «إلى» does not mean the lām; it has also been said that it does mean it, and this is the school of the Kufans, I mean loose usage in particles. The meaning of the lām and «إلى» in this place is close.
Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "Outside the Qurʾān one may say «أقربُ من التقوى» and «إلى التقوى», except that the lām here indicates a meaning other than the meaning of «إلى» and other than the meaning of «مِنْ». The meaning of the lām is: forgoing is nearer for the sake of piety; the lām indicates the cause of forgoing's nearness. When you say «أقربُ إلى التقوى», the meaning is: it approaches piety, as you say «أنت أقربُ إليَّ» (you are nearer to me). «أقرب من التقوى» entails that forgoing and piety are both near, but forgoing is nearer than piety, and the meaning of the verse is not this." End of quote.
So he made the lām causal, not for transitivity, and «إلى» for transitivity.
Know that the verb of exclamation and the elative (afʿal al-tafḍīl) are made transitive with the particle with which their verb is made transitive before becoming exclamatory or elative, as in «ما أزهدني فيه وهو أزهدُ فيه» (how abstinent I am from it, and he is more abstinent from it). If it is from an originally transitive verb: if the verb conveys knowledge or ignorance, they are made transitive with the bāʾ, as in «هو أعلمُ بالفقه» (he is more knowledgeable of jurisprudence); if it does not convey that, they are made transitive with the lām, as in «ما أضربَكَ لزيدٍ» (how much you strike Zayd!) and «أنت أضربُ لعمروٍ» (you strike ʿAmr more) — except in the category of love and hatred, for these are made transitive to the object with «في», as in «ما أحبَّ زيداً في عمروٍ وأبغضه في خالدٍ، وهو أحبُّ في بكر وأبغض في خالد» [Translator's note: so in the source; the usual rule makes these transitive to the object with the lām and to the logical agent with «إلى»], and to the logical agent with «إلى», as in «زيدٌ أحبُّ إلى عمروٍ من خالد» (Zayd is dearer to ʿAmr than Khālid) and «ما أحبَّ زيداً إلى عمرو» (how dear Zayd is to ʿAmr!), i.e. ʿAmr loves Zayd. This is an important rule which few master.
That over which [something] is preferred in the noble verse is omitted, its implied form being: nearer to piety than not forgoing. The yāʾ in «التقوى» is a substitute for a wāw, and its wāw is a substitute for a yāʾ, because it is from «وَقَيْتُ أقِي وقايةً»; that has preceded at the beginning of the sūra.
His saying: {وَلاَ تَنسَوُاْ الفضل}: the majority read «تَنْسَوا» with a ḍamma on the wāw, because it is a pronoun wāw. Ibn Yaʿmar read it with a kasra, likening it to the wāw of «لو», just as they gave a ḍamma to the wāw of «لو» by likening it to the pronoun wāw. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "Regarding the wāw of «تَنْسَوا», the readings and their justifications are what we mentioned at {اشتروا الضلالة} [al-Baqara: 16]." He had given five readings there, so the apparent sense of his words is that all of them return here, except that only the two views I mentioned have been transmitted here.
ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, read «ولا تناسَوا» (and do not mutually neglect). Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It is a reading well-grounded in meaning, because it is a place of deliberately disregarding, not of forgetting, except by way of likening." Abū al-Baqāʾ said: [it is] on the pattern of mufāʿala, meaning mutual leaving aside, not inadvertence; and this is close to Ibn ʿAṭiyya's saying.
His saying: {بَيْنَكُمْ}: there are two views about it. The first: it is accusative by «تَنْسَوُا». The second: it is attached to something omitted as a ḥāl of «الفضل», i.e. being between you. The first is preferable, because forbidding an act that takes place between them is more forceful than [forbidding] an act that does not take place between them.

semin-durr:238-238.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {حَافِظُواْ}: about «فاعَل» here there are two views. The first: it means «فَعِل» [Translator's note: so vowelled in the source; the bare form «فَعَل» is presumably meant], as in «طارَقْتُ النعل» (I layered the sandal) and «عاقَبْتُ اللصَّ» (I punished the thief). Since He made «المحافظة» (guarding) imply the meaning of «المواظبة» (persevering), He made it transitive with «على». The second: «فاعَل» has its usual sense of being between two parties. It has been said: between the servant and his Lord, as though it were said: guard this prayer and Allah will guard you. And it has been said: between the servant and the prayer, i.e. guard it and it will guard you.
Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "The obligation of repeating the guarding runs the course of the agents, since the obligation urges the act, so it is as though it were a partner of the agent in the guarding, as they said regarding {وَاعَدْنَا موسى} [al-Baqara: 51]: the promise is from Allah, and the acceptance from Moses is in the status of a promise. In «حافِظوا» there is a meaning not found in «احفظوا», namely repetition of the guarding." This is open to consideration, since the pattern mufāʿala does not indicate repetition of an act at all.
His saying: {والصلاة الوسطى}: He mentioned the particular after the general; its benefit has been given at His saying: {مَن كَانَ عَدُوّاً للَّهِ} [al-Baqara: 98]. «الوُسْطى» is of the pattern «فُعْلَى», and its meaning is elative (tafḍīl), for it is the feminine of «الأوسط», as in the poet's saying — praising the Messenger, upon him be peace —:
1008 - يا أوسطَ الناسِ طُرَّاً في مفاخِرهمْ ... وأكرمَ الناسِ أمَّا بَرَّةً وأَبَا
(O best of all people in their glories, and noblest of people in a righteous mother and father.)
It is [from] «الوسط» meaning the choicest, not from «الوَسَط» meaning intermediate between two things, because «فُعْلى» means the elative, and the elative is only formed from what admits of increase and decrease. «الوَسَط» meaning just and choicest admits of both, unlike what is intermediate between two things, which does not admit of them, so the elative pattern «أفعل» is not formed from it.
ʿAlī read «وعلى الصلاة», repeating the preposition for emphasis. ʿĀʾisha — may Allah be pleased with her — read «والصلاةَ» in the accusative. About it there are two views. The first: it is by way of specification (ikhtiṣāṣ); al-Zamakhsharī mentioned it. The second: it is [conjoined] to the position of the genitive noun, like «مررتُ بزيدٍ وعَمْراً» (I passed by Zayd and ʿAmr); its explanation will come in al-Māʾida.
His saying: {قَانِتِينَ} is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the agent of «قوموا». In «لله» the lām may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to «قوموا», or it may be attached to «قانتين»; His saying, Exalted is He: {كُلٌّ لَّهُ قَانِتُونَ} [al-Baqara: 116] points to the second. The meaning of the lām is causal.

semin-durr:239-239.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {فَرِجَالاً}: accusative (manṣūb) as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and what governs it is omitted, its implied form being: «فَصَلُّوا رجالاً» (then pray on foot), or «فحافِظُوا عليها رِجالاً» (then keep to it on foot); and this is preferable, because it … [Translator's note: the source sentence breaks off here: «وهذا أَوْلَى لأنه و»; the following «رجال» begins a new statement]. «رجال» is the plural of «راجِل» (one on foot), like «قائِم» and «قيام», «صاحِب» and «صِحاب». From it one says: «رَجِل يَرْجَلُ رَجْلاً», so he is «راجِلٌ» and «رَجُلٌ» on the pattern of «عَضُد»; this is the dialect of the Ḥijāz: they say «رَجِل فلانٌ فهو رَجُلٌ». One also says «رَجْلان» and «رَجِيل». The poet said:
1009 - عليَّ إذا لاقَيْتُ ليلى بخُفْيَةٍ ... أَنَ أزدارَ بيتَ اللهِ رَجْلانَ حافِيا
(It is incumbent on me, if I meet Laylā in secret, to visit the House of Allah on foot and barefoot.)
All of this means walking on one's feet for lack of a mount. This word has many plurals: «رِجال», as mentioned — He said, Exalted is He: {يَأْتُوكَ رِجَالاً وعلى كُلِّ ضَامِرٍ} [al-Ḥajj: 27], and the poet said:
1010 - وبنو غُدانَةَ شاخِصٌ أبصارُهُمْ ... يَمْشُون تحتَ بُطونِهِنَّ رِجَالا
(And the Banū Ghudāna, their eyes staring, walk on foot beneath their [the horses'] bellies.)
— and «رَجِيل», «رُجالى» (it is narrated as a reading from ʿIkrima), «رَجالى», «رَجَّالة», «رُجَّال» (ʿIkrima and Ibn Makhlad read with it), «رُجَّالى», «رُجلان», «رِجْلة», «رَجْلَة» with sukūn and with fatḥa on the jīm, «أَرْجِلَة», «أراجِل», «أراجِيل», and «رُجَّلاً» with a ḍamma on the rāʾ and a doubled jīm without an alif, with which it was read anomalously (shādhdhan).
«رُكْبَان» is the plural of «راكِب» (rider). It has been said that it is only said of one who rides a camel; as for the rider of a horse, he is «فارس», and the rider of a donkey or a mule is «حَمَّار» and «بَغَّال», though it is better to say «صاحبُ حمارٍ» and «صاحب بَغْلٍ». «أو» here is for division (taqsīm); it has also been said: for permission; and it has been said: for choice.
His saying: {كَمَا عَلَّمَكُم}: the kāf is in the position of the accusative, either as the naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), or as a ḥāl of the pronoun of the omitted maṣdar. It may also be causal, i.e. remember Him because of His teaching you. «ما» may be maṣdar-forming, and this is the apparent view, or it may mean «الذي» (that which), the meaning then being: pray the prayer like the prayer which He taught you, with "remembrance" expressing the prayer, and the comparison being between the forms of the two prayers, the one occurring before the fear and after it in the state of security. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "On this interpretation His saying {مَّا لَمْ تَكُونُواْ} is a badal (substitute) of «ما» in «كما»; otherwise the wording of the verse would not be coherent." The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "This is a possible construal, and better than it is that «ما لم تكونوا» be a badal of the omitted pronoun in «عَلَّمكم» referring to the relative, since the implied form is «عَلَّمكموه» (He taught it to you). The grammarians stated explicitly that it is allowed to say «ضَرَبْتُ الذي رأيتُ أخاك» (I struck the one I saw, your brother), i.e. «رأيته أخاك» (I saw him, your brother), so «أخاك» is a badal of the omitted referent-pronoun."

semin-durr:240-240.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {والذين يُتَوَفَّوْنَ}: there are eight views about it [Translator's note: so in the source; the views listed below number five for the nominative reading and three for the accusative]. The first: it is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «وصيةٌ» is a second mubtadaʾ; what permits beginning with it [though indefinite] is that it is qualified by an implied adjective, since the implied form is «وصيةٌ من الله» (a bequest from Allah) or «منهم» (from them), according to the disagreement about it: is it obligatory from Allah or recommended to the husbands? «لأزواجِهم» is the khabar (predicate) of the second mubtadaʾ, so it is attached to something omitted, and the second mubtadaʾ with its khabar is the khabar of the first. In this clause there is [an implied] pronoun of the first. It is parallel to their saying «السمنُ مَنَوانِ بدرهمٍ» (ghee: two manns for a dirham), its implied form being «مَنَوانِ منه» (two manns of it). Ibn ʿAṭiyya made what permits beginning with it its being in a position of specification; he said: "just as it is good for «سلامٌ عليك» (peace be upon you) and «خيرٌ بين يديك» (good be before you) to be in the nominative, because it is a position of supplication." This is open to consideration.
The second: «وصيةٌ» is a mubtadaʾ, «لأزواجِهم» its adjective, and the khabar is omitted, its implied form being «فعليهم وصيةٌ لأزواجِهم» (then upon them is a bequest for their wives), and the clause is the khabar of the first.
The third: it is nominative by an omitted verb, its implied form being «كُتِبَ عليهم وصيةٌ» (a bequest is prescribed for them), «لأزواجهم» being an adjective, and the clause is likewise the khabar of the first. The reading of ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd] supports this: «كُتِبَ عليهم وصيةٌ». This is an explanation of meaning, not of i'rab, since this is not one of the places where the verb is implied.
The fourth: «الذين» is a mubtadaʾ with a muḍāf omitted from the first, its implied form being «ووصيةُ الذين» (and the bequest of those who).
The fifth: it is likewise, except that a muḍāf is omitted from the second, its implied form being «والذين يُتَوَفَّوْنَ أهلُ وصية» (and those who die are people [obliged to make] a bequest). Al-Zamakhsharī mentioned these two views. The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "No necessity calls for that."
These five views are for those who read «وصيةٌ» in the nominative, namely Ibn Kathīr, Nāfiʿ, al-Kisāʾī, and Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim. The rest read it in the accusative, and on their reading there are three views about the nominative of «الذين». The first: it is the fāʿil (agent) of an omitted verb, its implied form being «وَلْيُوصِ الذين» (and let those … bequeath), the accusative of «وصية» being as a maṣdar (verbal noun). The second: it is nominative by a passive verb that takes two objects, its implied form being «وأُلْزِم الذين يُتَوَفَّوْنَ» (and those who die are obliged), the accusative of «وصية» being as a second object of «أُلْزِم»; al-Zamakhsharī mentioned it. This and the one before it are weak, because this is not one of the places where a verb is implied. The third: it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, and that [khabar] is what makes «وصية» accusative, its implied form being «والذين يُتَوَفَّوْنَ يُوصُون وصيةً» (and those who die bequeath a bequest); Ibn ʿAṭiyya gave its implied form as «لِيوصوا» (let them bequeath), «وصيةً» being likewise accusative as a maṣdar. In the reading (ḥarf) of ʿAbd Allāh: «الوصيةُ», nominative as a mubtadaʾ, the khabar being the preposition after it, or implied, i.e. «فعليهم الوصيةُ» (then upon them is the bequest), the preposition after it being a ḥāl (circumstantial), a second khabar, or a clarification (bayān).
His saying: {مَّتَاعاً}: about its accusative there are seven views. The first: it is made accusative by the word «وصية», because it is a maṣdar with tanwīn; its being feminine with the tāʾ does no harm, since it is built upon it, so it is like the poet's saying:
1011 - فلولا رجاءُ النصر مِنْكَ ورهبةٌ ... عقابَك قد كانوا لنا كالموارِدِ
(Were it not for hope of victory from you, and fear of your punishment, they would have been to us like watering-places.)
The original is «وصيةٌ بمتاعٍ» (a bequest of provision); then the preposition was omitted by way of extension (ittisāʿ), so what follows it became accusative. This is when you do not make «الوصية» accusative as a maṣdar, because the emphasising maṣdar does not govern; that only comes when it is nominative or accusative as an object, as its detailing has preceded.
The second: it is accusative by a verb, either from its own root, i.e. «مَتِّعوهن متاعاً» (provide for them a provision), i.e. «تمتيعاً», or from another root, i.e. «جَعَل اللَّهُ لهنَّ متاعاً» (Allah has appointed for them a provision). The third: it is an adjective of «وصية». The fourth: it is a badal (substitute) of it. The fifth: it is accusative by what made it [«وصية»] accusative, i.e. «يُوصُون متاعاً» (they bequeath a provision), so it too is a maṣdar not from the verb's own root [Translator's note: the source again has «على غير الصدر», a slip for «المصدر»], like «قَعَدْتُ جُلوساً» (I sat a sitting); this is for those who read «وصية» in the accusative. The sixth: it is a ḥāl of the bequeathers, i.e. providing, or possessing provision. The seventh: it is a ḥāl of «أزواجهم», i.e. being provided for, or possessing provision; and it is an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara) if the bequest is from the husbands.
Ubayy read «متاعٌ لأزواجِهِم» in place of «وصيةٌ»; and «فمتاعٌ» is narrated from him, the fāʾ entering the khabar of the relative because it resembles a condition. In these two narrations «متاعاً» is accusative as a maṣdar by this maṣdar, for it means «التمتيع», as in «يعجبني ضربٌ لك زيداً ضرباً شديداً» (I like a striking of yours of Zayd, a severe striking); its parallel is: {فَإِنَّ جَهَنَّمَ جَزَآؤُكُمْ جَزَاءً مَّوْفُوراً} [al-Isrāʾ: 63]. «إلى الحَوْلِ» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «مَتاع», or to something omitted as an adjective of it.
His saying: {غَيْرَ إِخْرَاجٍ}: about its accusative there are six views. The first: it is a naʿt (adjective) of «متاعاً». The second: it is a badal of it. The third: it is a ḥāl of the wives, i.e. not being expelled. The fourth: it is a ḥāl of the bequeathers, i.e. not expelling. The fifth: it is accusative as a maṣdar, its implied form being «لا إخراجاً» (without expulsion); al-Akhfash said this. The sixth: it is with a preposition omitted, its implied form being «مِنْ غيرِ إخراجٍ» (without expulsion); Abū al-Baqāʾ said this, and it is open to consideration.
His saying: {فِي مَا فَعَلْنَ في أَنْفُسِهِنَّ}: these two prepositional phrases are attached to what the khabar of «لا», namely «عليكم», is attached to, i.e. the "being established" (istiqrār); the implied form is: «لا جُنَاح مستقرٌّ عليكم فيما فَعَلْنَ في أنفسِهِنَّ» (no blame is established upon you in what they do with themselves). «ما» is a nominal relative (mawṣūla ismiyya), and the referent-pronoun is omitted, its implied form being «فَعَلْنَهُ» (they did it). «مِنْ معروف» is attached to something omitted, because it is a ḥāl of that omitted referent-pronoun, its implied form being: «فيما فَعَلْنَه كائناً من معروف» (in what they did, it being of what is fair).
In this verse «من معروفٍ» came as an indefinite noun made genitive by «مِنْ», whereas in the verse before it [came] «بالمعروفِ», definite and made genitive by the bāʾ, because this is the lām of prior reference (ʿahd), as in your saying «رأيتُ رجلاً فأكرمْتُ الرجلَ» (I saw a man, and I honoured the man) — except that this [verse], even though it is later in wording, is earlier in revelation, and for that reason the scholars made it abrogated by that [one], except for an anomalous few. The parallels of these clauses have preceded, so there is no need to repeat the discussion of them.

semin-durr:273-273.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {لِلْفُقَرَآءِ}: regarding what this preposition phrase is attached to (mutaʿalliq) there are five aspects. The first — and it is the apparent one —: it is attached to an implied verb indicated by the context of the speech. The analysts' wordings of it differ. Makkī said — and he mentioned nothing else —: "Give to the poor". This is open to consideration, because it entails the lām being redundant (zāʾida) on one of the two objects of «أعطى», and the lām is added only because of the weakness of the governing word: either through its governed element being fronted, as in His saying, Exalted is He: {لِلرُّؤْيَا تَعْبُرُونَ} [Yūsuf: 43], or through its being a secondary form, as in His saying, Exalted is He: {فَعَّالٌ لِّمَا يُرِيدُ} [Hūd: 107]. It is far-fetched to say that, since the governing word is implied, it is weak and so is strengthened by the lām — although some allow this even when the governing word is not weak, and include among it {رَدِفَ لَكُم} [al-Naml: 72]; its explanation will come in its place, if Allah the Exalted wills. Abū al-Baqāʾ construed it as "wonder at the poor"; this is open to consideration, because there is no indication of wonder in the context. Al-Zamakhsharī construed it as "direct" or "assign what you spend [to the poor]". Better than that is what Makkī construed, but it has the problem stated above.

The second: this preposition phrase is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "the charities" or "the expenditures that you spend are for the poor". In meaning it is an answer to an implied question, as though, when they were urged to give charity, they said: "Then for whom is it?" And they were urged [with the reply] that it is for these people [Translator's note: the source reads «فَأُحِثُّوا» "they were urged"; the context suggests "they were answered"]. It carries the benefit of explaining where the charities are to be directed. This is the choice of Ibn al-Anbārī. He said: "It is as you say «عاقل لبيب» (intelligent, discerning) after a man has been described, i.e. the one described is intelligent; and you write on purses «ألفان ومئتان» (two thousand and two hundred), i.e. what is in the purse is two thousand." And he recited:
1081 - تسأَلُنِي عن زوجِها أيُّ فتى ... خَبٌّ جَروزٌ وإذا جاعَ بكى
(She asks me about her husband, what sort of young man he is: a deceiver, a glutton, and when he is hungry he weeps.)
He means: "he is a deceiver".

The third: the lām is attached to His saying: {إِن تُبْدُواْ الصدقات} [al-Baqara: 271]. This is the doctrine of al-Qaffāl, and people considered it far-fetched because of the many intervening elements.

The fourth: it is attached to His saying: {وَمَا تُنفِقُواْ مِنْ خَيْرٍ}. This is open to consideration, in that it entails separating the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) from its governed element by the apodosis clause, so it would be analogous to your saying «مَنْ يُكْرِمْ أُحْسِنْ إليه زيداً». Al-Wāḥidī explicitly prohibited this, giving the reason I mentioned. He said: "It is not permissible for what governs this lām to be the last «تنفقوا» in the preceding verse, because the governing word and the governed are not separated by what does not belong to it, just as it is not permissible to say «كانت زيداً الحُمَّى تأخُذُ» (the fever was, Zayd, seizing)."

The fifth: «للفقراء» is a badal (substitute) for His saying «فلأنفسِكم». This is rejected. Al-Wāḥidī and others said: "Because a thing is substituted for something other than itself only when the meaning includes it, and the mention of the self here is not like that, because the spending is [for yourselves] in that it returns to them, and is for the poor in that it reaches them. It is not of the category of {وَللَّهِ عَلَى الناس حِجُّ البيت مَنِ استطاع إِلَيْهِ سَبِيلاً} [Āl ʿImrān: 97], because there the obligation is binding on the one who is able in particular." I say: he means that the poor are not the selves, nor a part of them, nor included in them. It is as though the one who said this imagined that it is of the category of His saying, Exalted is He: {وَلاَ تقتلوا أَنْفُسَكُمْ} [al-Nisāʾ: 29], on one of the two interpretations.

«الفقير» (the poor man): it is said that its origin is from «فَقَرَتْه الفاقِرة», i.e. the calamity broke the vertebrae (faqār) of his back. Al-Rāghib said: "The origin of «الفقير» is the one whose vertebrae are broken; one says «فَقَرَتْه الفاقرةُ», i.e. the calamity that breaks the vertebrae; and «أَفْقَرك الصيدُ فارمِه» (the game has given you its back, so shoot it), i.e. it has enabled you [to reach] its vertebrae." It is also said: it is from «الفُقْرَة», i.e. the pit; from this every pit in which water collects is called «فقير». «فَقَرْتُ للفسيل» [Translator's note: the source prints «للغسيل», evidently for «للفسيل», the palm-shoot]: I dug a pit for it and planted it in it. The poet said:
1082 - ما ليلةُ الفقيرِ إلا شيطانْ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(The night of al-Faqīr is nothing but a devil …)
It is said: it is the name of a well. «فَقَرْتُ الخَرَزَ»: I pierced the bead. Al-Harawī said: one says «فَقَره» when one strikes the vertebrae of his back, like «رَأَسه», i.e. struck his head, and «بَطَنه», i.e. struck his belly. Al-Aṣmaʿī said: "«الفَقْر» is to notch the nose of a camel until the notch reaches the bone, then a halter is twisted over it, by which the intractable camel is tamed; from this it is said: «عَمِل به الفاقرة» (he did a crippling thing to him)." «الفِقَرات», with kasra on the fāʾ and fatḥa on the qāf, the plural of «فِقَرة», are great matters; from this is the ḥadīth of «السعي» [Translator's note: so in the source]: «فِقَراتُ ابنِ آدم ثلاثُ: يوم وُلد ويومَ يموتُ، ويوم يُبْعَثُ» ("The great moments of the son of Adam are three: the day he is born, the day he dies, and the day he is raised"). «الفُقَر», with ḍamma on the fāʾ and fatḥa on the qāf, is the plural of «فُقْرَة», which is the notch and the piercing of the nose; from this is the saying of Abū Ziyād: «يُفْتقَرُ الصَعبُ ثلاثَ فُقَرٍ في خَطْمِه» (the intractable camel is notched with three notches in its nose), and the ḥadīth of Saʿd: «فأشار إلى فُقَرٍ في أنفه» ("he pointed to notches in his nose"), i.e. a slit and a notch. The discussion of «الإحصار» and the difference between faʿala and afʿala from it has already been given.

His saying: {فِي سَبِيلِ}: two aspects are possible. The first: it is attached to the verb before it, so it is an adverbial of it. The second: it is attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the nominative [pronoun] of «أُحْصِروا», i.e. "being in the way of Allah". Abū al-Baqāʾ construed it as "striving in the way of Allah"; this is an explanation of meaning, not of grammatical analysis, because the preposition phrase is attached only to absolute being.

His saying: {لاَ يَسْتَطِيعُونَ}: there are two possibilities for this clause. The more evident: it is a ḥāl, and regarding the one to whom it refers there are two aspects: the first, that it is «الفقراء»; the second, that it is the nominative [pronoun] of «أُحْصِروا». The second possibility: it is resumptive, with no grammatical position. «ضرباً» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and here it is travelling for trade. The poet said:
