As for «من نسائهم», regarding this prepositional phrase there are eight possibilities. The first: that it is attached to «يُؤْلُون». Al-Zamakhsharī said: «If you say: how is it made transitive with "min" when it is made transitive with "ʿalā"? I say: the specific oath has been given the sense of distancing, as if it had been said: "they distance themselves from their wives, swearing or taking an oath".» The second: that «ālā» is made transitive with «ʿalā» and with «min»; Abū al-Baqāʾ said it, reporting from others, that one says "ālā min imraʾatihi" and "ʿalā imraʾatihi". The third: that «min» stands in the place of «ʿalā», and this is the view of the Kufans. The fourth: that it stands in the place of «fī», and there is then an omitted muḍāf, that is: "on leaving intercourse with their wives" or "in leaving intercourse with their wives". The fifth: that «min» is redundant and the implied form is "yuʾlūna an yaʿtazilū nisāʾahum" (they swear to keep away from their wives). The sixth: that it is attached to an omitted word, the implied form being: "and for those who swear, from their wives, a waiting of four (months)", so it is attached to what the omitted «lahum» is attached to. The Shaykh implied it thus and ascribed it to al-Zamakhsharī, and there is room for consideration in it, for al-Zamakhsharī said: «It is possible that it be meant: "for them, from their wives, a waiting", as you say "lī minka kadhā".» His saying «lahum» did not intend that there is something omitted, namely the word «lahum»; he only intended to attach «min» to the "istiqrār" (settling) to which «lil-ladhīna» is attached; the utmost in it is that he brought the pronoun of «alladhīna» to clarify the meaning. And Abū al-Baqāʾ went in this direction, for he said: «And it was said: the origin is "ʿalā", and it is not permitted that "min" stand in the place of "ʿalā"; then "min" is attached to the meaning of settling», he meaning the settling to which His saying «lil-ladhīna» is attached. And even granting that the word «lahum» is implied and is intended, then it would be only a badal (substitute) of «lil-ladhīna» with repetition of the governor, or else His saying «lil-ladhīna yuʾlūna» would remain disconnected. In sum, its attachment to the settling is not evident. As for the Shaykh's implying, "wa-alladhīna yuʾlūna lahum min nisāʾihim tarabbuṣun", it is not so, because if «alladhīna» had come thus, not governed by the lām, what he claimed would be easy, but it came, as you see, governed by the lām. Then the Shaykh said: «All of this is weak and the Qur'an is to be held above it; it is attached to «yuʾlūna» only in one of two ways: either «min» is for causation, that is, they swear because of their wives; or it is given the sense of refraining, so that it is made transitive with «min», as if it had been said: "for those who refrain from their wives by ilāʾ".» These are two possibilities with the six preceding, which makes eight; and if you consider generally the giving of a sense (taḍmīn), they come to seven.

Al-īlāʾ is swearing, the maṣdar of ālā yūlī, like akrama yukrimu ikrāman, and the origin is «iʾlāʾ», so the second hamza was changed to yāʾ because of its being unvowelled and the kasra before it, like «īmān».

One says also taʾallā and ayta lā, on the pattern ifta ʿala, the origin being «iʾtalā», so the second was changed for the reason that has preceded.

The oath is called al-aliyya, al-alūwa, al-alwa and al-ilwa; and al-aliyya is pluralised as «alāyā», like ʿashiyya and ʿashāyā, and it is permissible that al-alūwa also be pluralised as «alāyā», like rakūba and rakāʾib. Kuthayyir ʿAzza said:

966 - قليلُ الأَلايا حافظٌ ليمينِه ... إذا صَدَرَتْ منه الأَلِيَّةُ بَرَّتِ
("Sparing of oaths, guarding his vow; when an oath issues from him it is fulfilled")

It has already preceded how aliyya and alāyā are inflected, at His saying {نَّغْفِرْ لَكُمْ خَطَايَاكُمْ} [al-Baqara: 58], the plural of khaṭīʾa.

Al-tarabbuṣ is waiting, and it is the reversal of al-taṣabbur. He said:

967 - تَرَبَّصْ بها رَيْب المنونِ لعلَّها ... تُطَلَّقُ يوماً أو يموتُ حليلُها
("Wait for the misfortunes of fate with her; perhaps she will one day be divorced, or her husband will die")

As for the annexation of al-tarabbuṣ to the months, there are two views. One: that it is a case of annexing the maṣdar to its object, by extension of the adverb until it became a direct object and was annexed to, in this state. The second: that the event is annexed to the adverb without extension, so the annexation is in the sense of «fī», and this is a Kufan position; and the agent is omitted, its implied form being: "their waiting four months".

His saying: {فَآءُوا}: the alif of «fāʾa» is changed from yāʾ, for they say fāʾa yafīʾu fayʾatan, meaning he returned. Al-fayʾ is the shade, because of its returning after the decline of the sun. ʿAlqama said:

968 - فقلتُ لها فِيئي فما تَسْتَفِزُّني ... ذَواتُ العيونِ والبنانِ المُخَضَّبِ
("So I said to her: return! For I am not moved by women with beautiful eyes and henna-stained fingertips")

semin-durr:215-215.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {مَاذَا يُنْفِقُونَ}: It has already preceded that «ماذا» has six uses, and the verification of the matter is at His saying {مَاذَآ أَرَادَ الله بهذا} [al-Baqara: 26]. Here «ماذا» may be like a single noun with the sense of the interrogative, so it is a fronted object; and «ما» and «ذا» may be (separate), with «ما» a mubtadaʾ and «ذا» its khabar, and «ذا» is a relative: «ينفقون» is its ṣila and the returning pronoun is omitted. «ماذا» suspends the asking, so it is in the position of the second object, and its verification has already preceded in His saying: {سَلْ بني إِسْرَائِيلَ كَمْ آتَيْنَاهُم} [al-Baqara: 211]. «ينفقون» came in the wording of the third person because the agent of the verb before it is a third-person pronoun in «يسألونك»; and "mādhā nunfiqu" (what do we spend) is permitted in speech, as it is permitted to say "aqsama Zaydun la-yaḍribanna" and "la-aḍribanna"; more explanation of this will come at His saying {يَسْأَلُونَكَ مَاذَآ أُحِلَّ لَهُمْ} [al-Māʾida: 4] in al-Māʾida.

[His saying]: {قُلْ مَآ أَنْفَقْتُمْ مِّنْ خَيْرٍ}: in «ما» two views are permitted. The first: that it is conditional, which is the apparent view, to agree with what follows it; so «ما» is in the position of the accusative as a fronted object whose fronting is obligatory, because it has the head of the sentence. «أنفقْتُمْ» is in the position of the jussive by the condition, and «مِنْ خيرٍ» has had its i'rab given at His saying {مَا نَنسَخْ مِنْ آيَةٍ} [al-Baqara: 106].

His saying: {فَلِلْوَالِدَيْنِ} is the apodosis of the condition. This preposition and its genitive noun is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "so its place of expenditure is for the parents", so it is attached to an omitted element, either a single word or a clause, according to what was mentioned of the disagreement in what passed. The clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis of the condition. The second: that «ما» is a relative, «أنفقتم» is its ṣila, and the returning pronoun is omitted because of the completeness of the conditions, i.e. "that which you spent". The fāʾ is redundant in the khabar, which is the preposition and its genitive noun. Abū l-Baqāʾ said on this view: "«ومِنْ خيرٍ» is a ḥāl from the omitted returning pronoun."

They asked only about what is spent, so how were they answered with the explanation of the place of expenditure, that is, of those spent upon? There are answers to this, among them: that the verse has an omission, namely the one spent upon, which was omitted, the implied form being: "what do they spend, and to whom do they give it?", so the answer came for both: He answered about what is spent by His saying «مِنْ خيرٍ», and about those spent upon by His saying «فللوالدَيْن» and what follows it. Among them: that «ماذا» is a question about the place of expenditure with an omitted annexed word, its implied form being: "the place of expenditure of what do they spend?" Among them: that he omitted from the first the mention of the place of expenditure and from the second the mention of what is spent, and both are intended; something of that has preceded in the saying of the Exalted {وَمَثَلُ الذين كَفَرُواْ كَمَثَلِ} [al-Baqara: 171]. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "His saying {مَآ أَنْفَقْتُمْ مِّنْ خَيْرٍ} includes the explanation of what they spend, which is every good thing; and the speech was built on what is more important, which is the explanation of the place of expenditure, because spending is not counted unless it falls in its proper place. [He said]:

925 - إنَّ الصنيعة لا تكونُ صنيعةً ... حتى يُصابَ بها طريقُ المَصْنَعِ
(A kindness is not a kindness until it reaches the proper path of the doing of it.)

As for His saying {وَمَا تَفْعَلُواْ}, «ما» there is only conditional, because its jussive effect is apparent, unlike the first. ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, read «وما يفعلوا» with the yāʾ, in the third person; it may be an iltifāt from the second person, or it may be from implying (a subject) because the context indicates it, i.e. "and whatever people do"."

semin-durr:216-216.t:
It was read: {كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمُ القتال}: with «كَتَب» as active, its subject being a pronoun for Allah the Exalted, and with «القتال» in the accusative.

His saying: {وَهُوَ كُرْهٌ}: this is the wāw of ḥāl, and the clause after it is in the position of the accusative as that. The apparent view is that «هو» returns to the fighting. It was said: it returns to the maṣdar understood from «كَتَب», i.e. "its prescription and its obligation". The majority read «كُرْهٌ» with ḍamma on the kāf, and al-Sulamī read it with fatḥa. It was said: the two have one meaning, i.e. two maṣdars like ḍaʿf and ḍuʿf; al-Zajjāj said it and al-Zamakhsharī followed him. [Translator's note: the source spells the name «الزمشخري», a slip for «الزمخشري».] It was said: the one with ḍamma is a passive participle and the one with fatḥa is the maṣdar. It was said: the one with fatḥa has the sense of ikrāh (compulsion); al-Zamakhsharī said it in directing the reading of al-Sulamī, except that this is of the category of a maṣdar coming with the augmentations dropped, which is not analogical. It was said: the one with fatḥa is what a man is forced to do, and the one with ḍamma is what he himself dislikes.

If al-karh and al-kurh are a maṣdar, then an interpretation is needed by which predicating it of «هو» is permissible, and that interpretation is either on the omission of an annexed word, i.e. "fighting is a thing of dislike", or by way of exaggeration, or by its occurrence in the place of a passive participle. If we say that «كُرْهاً» with ḍamma is a passive participle, none of this is needed. «لكم» is in the position of the nominative because it is an adjective of «كُره», so it is attached to an omitted element, i.e. "dislike that is for you".

His saying: {وعسى أَن تَكْرَهُواْ}: «عسى» is a past verb transferred to the composing (inshāʾ) of hope and apprehension. It raises the subject and puts the predicate in the accusative, and its predicate is only an imperfect verb joined to «أَنْ». It may come as an explicit noun, as in his saying:

926 - أَكْثَرْتَ في العَذْلِ مُلِحَّاً دائماً ... لا تُكْثِرَنْ إني عَسَيْتُ صائِماً
(You have been excessive in blame, insisting constantly; do not be excessive, for I may be fasting.)

and al-Zabbāʾ said: «عسى الغُوَيْرُ أَبُؤسا» ("Perhaps the little cave (will bring) misfortunes"). Its predicate may also be bare of «أَنْ», as in his saying:

927 - عسى فَرَجٌ يأتي به اللهُ إنه ... له كلَّ يومٍ في خَلِقَتِهِ أَمْرُ
(Perhaps relief will come, brought by Allah; every day, in His creation, He has a matter.)

and another said:

928 - عَسَى الكربُ الذي أَمْسَيْتَ فيه ... يكونُ وراءَه فرجٌ قَرِيبُ
(Perhaps the distress you have come to be in will have near relief behind it.)

and another said:

929 - فأمَّا كَيِّسٌ فَنَجا ولكِنْ ... عَسَى يَغْتَرُّ بي حَمِقٌ لَئيمُ
(As for a clever man, he escaped; but perhaps a foolish, base man will be deceived by me.)

It is complete (tāmma) when it is predicated of «أَنْ» or «أنَّ», because the two take the place of its subject and predicate. The sounder view is that it is a verb, not a particle, because of the attachment of the overt nominative pronouns to it; its pattern is «فَعَل» with fatḥa on the ʿayn, and kasra on its ʿayn is permitted when it is predicated of a first- or second-person pronoun or the feminine plural nūn, which is the reading of Nāfiʿ, and it will come. It is not conjugated but obligatorily stays in the past. The difference in meaning between apprehension and hope by it is that hope concerns what is loved and apprehension concerns what is disliked. «عسى» from Allah the Exalted is obligatory (wājiba), because hope and apprehension are impossible in His case. It was said: every «عسى» in the Qur'an is for certainty, meaning occurrence, except the saying of the Exalted {عسى رَبُّهُ إِن طَلَّقَكُنَّ} [al-Taḥrīm: 5] to the end of the verse. In this verse it is not defective (nāqiṣa) needing a predicate, but complete, because it is predicated of «أَنْ», and it has already preceded that it takes the place of the two objects (subject and predicate) after it.

Al-Ḥawfī claimed that «أَن تكرهوا» is in the position of the accusative, but this is not possible except by a remote affectation.

His saying: {وَهُوَ خَيْرٌ لَّكُمْ}: about this clause there are two views. The most apparent: that it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, even though a ḥāl from an indefinite noun without one of the known conditions is rare. The second: that it is in the position of the accusative as an adjective of «شيئاً». The wāw entered the clause that occurs only because its form is the form of a ḥāl; so just as the wāw enters it as a ḥāl, it enters it as an adjective; Abū l-Baqāʾ said this. Similar to that is what al-Zamakhsharī permitted in His saying: {وَمَآ أَهْلَكْنَا مِن قَرْيَةٍ إِلاَّ وَلَهَا كِتَابٌ مَّعْلُومٌ}, for he made «ولها كتابٌ» an adjective of «قرية». He said: "The analogy was that this wāw not come between them, as in His saying: {وَمَآ أَهْلَكْنَا مِن قَرْيَةٍ إِلاَّ لَهَا مُنذِرُونَ}; it came between them only to emphasize the attachment of the adjective to the described, and like what is said of the ḥāl: 'Zayd came to me, a garment upon him' and 'and a garment upon him'." What Abū l-Baqāʾ permitted here and al-Zamakhsharī there is the opinion of Ibn Jinnī, and the rest of the grammarians differ from him.

semin-durr:227-227.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {عَزَمُواْ الطلاق}: there are two possibilities for the accusative of «الطلاق». One: that it is by dropping of the preposition, because «ʿazama» is made transitive with «ʿalā». He said:

969 - عَزَمْتُ على إقامةِ ذي صباحٍ ... لأمرٍ ما يُسَوَّدُ مَنْ يسَودُ
("I resolved upon staying on for a morning for a purpose; by some purpose is whoever becomes a chief made chief")

The second: that «ʿazama» is given the sense of «nawā» (to intend), so that it is accusative as a direct object.

Al-ʿazm is the tying of the heart and its determination: ʿazama yaʿzimu ʿazman and ʿuzman, with fatḥa and ḍamma, and ʿazīmatan and ʿizāman with kasra. It is also used in the sense of the oath: "ʿazamtu ʿalayka la-tafʿalanna".

Al-ṭalāq is the loosening of the tie; one says ṭalaqat (with fatḥa on the lām), taṭluqu, so she is ṭāliq and ṭāliqa. Al-Aʿshā said:

970 - أيا جارتا بيني فإنَّكِ طالِقَهْ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
("O my neighbour-wife, depart, for you are divorced…")

Thaʿlab reported «ṭaluqat» with ḍamma, and al-Akhfash denied it. Al-ṭalāq may be a maṣdar or a noun of the maṣdar, which is al-taṭlīq.

His saying: {فَإِنَّ الله}: its apparent sense is that it is the apodosis of the condition. The Shaykh said: «It seems that the apodosis is omitted, that is: "let them carry it out". ʿAbd Allāh read "فإن فاؤوا فيهنَّ" and Ubayy read "فيها", the pronoun being for the months.

The reading of the majority apparently means that the returning (fayʾa) and the divorce occur only after the four months have passed. But since al-Zamakhsharī followed the position of Abū Ḥanīfa, namely that the returning is within the period of four months, and the preceding reading supports him, he needed to interpret the verse with what is given here verbatim: «If you say: what is the place of the fāʾ if the returning is before the end of the period of waiting? I say: a sound place, because His saying "فإنْ فاؤوا، وإنْ عَزَموا" is a detailing of His saying "للذين يُؤْلُون مِنْ نسائِهِم", and the detailing follows what is detailed, as you say "I am your guest this month; if I praise you, I will stay with you to its end, and if not, I will not stay except for the time I take to move on".» The Shaykh said: «It is not correct, because what he gave as an example is not a parallel to the verse. Do you not see that the example has a report about the one whose condition is detailed, namely his saying "I am your guest this month", and after the two conditions the answer is stated explicitly, indicating the difference in what the verb of the consequence relates to; but the verse is not so, because those who swear are not reported about, and no ruling is attributed to them; what is judged is their waiting, and the meaning is: the waiting of the swearers for four months is legislated for them after their oath; then He said: "if they return, and if they resolve" — the apparent sense is that it follows the waiting of the legislated period in its entirety, because the returning occurs within it, and the resolve upon divorce after it, since a differing restriction is not indicated by the wording. What fits the verse is that you say: "For the guest, three days of hospitality; if he stays we are generous and preferential, and if he resolves to leave, he may leave", so what first comes to mind is that the two conditions are implied after his being honoured.»

semin-durr:228-228.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {والمطلقات يَتَرَبَّصْنَ}: mubtadaʾ and khabar. Is this clause of the type of a khabar in the place of a command, that is, "let them wait", or on its own sense? Two views. The Kufans said: its wording is a command on the implication of the lām of command; and whoever took it on its own sense implied: "the ruling for divorced women is that they wait", so he omitted «ruling» from the first and the maṣdarī «an» from the second, and this is very far-fetched.

«Tarabbaṣa» is made transitive by itself because it is in the sense of «intaẓara» (to wait). This verse admits two possibilities. One: that the object of al-tarabbuṣ is omitted, and this is the apparent view, its implied form being: "they wait for marriage" or "for husbands", and «ثلاثة قروء» on this basis is accusative as an adverbial, because it is a number noun annexed to an adverbial. The second: that the object is «ثلاثةَ قروءٍ» itself, that is, they wait for three qurūʾ to pass.

As for His saying: {بِأَنْفُسِهِنَّ}, it admits two possibilities. One, and it is the apparent one: that it is attached to «يتربَّصْنَ», the bāʾ being causal, that is, "by reason of themselves"; and mentioning the selves, or the detached pronoun, in a construction like this is obligatory, and it is not permitted to bring the attached pronoun; were it said in its like "al-Hindātu yatarabbaṣna bihinna", it would not be permitted, lest the verb of the detached pronoun become transitive to its attached pronoun, other than in the chapters in which that is permitted.

The second: that «بأنفسهنّ» is tawkīd (emphasis) for the attached nominative pronoun, which is the nūn, with the bāʾ redundant in the emphasis, for it is permitted to add it in nafs and ʿayn when they are used to emphasise. You say: jāʾa Zaydun nafsuhu and bi-nafsihi, ʿaynuhu and bi-ʿaynihi. On this basis it is not attached to anything, because it is redundant. It is not to be said: it cannot be emphasis for the pronoun, because it would have to be emphasised by a detached nominative pronoun, since an attached nominative pronoun is not emphasised by nafs and ʿayn except after being emphasised by the detached nominative pronoun, so that one says "Zaydun jāʾa huwa nafsuhu ʿaynuhu"; for this emphasised word left its original state when it was governed by the redundant bāʾ and resembled the dispensable items (faḍalāt), and so went out of the rule of the followers (tawābiʿ) and what is binding in others was not binding in it. What supports that is their saying "aḥsin bi-Zaydin wa-ajmil", that is, "bihi"; this governed word is an agent in the view of the Basrans, and the agent in their view is not omitted, but since it ran in the course of the dispensable items by reason of its being governed by the particle, it went out of the original rule of the agent chapter, and therefore its omission was permitted; besides that Abū al-Ḥasan al-Akhfash mentioned in the «Masāʾil» that they said "qāmū anfusuhum" without emphasis. The benefit of the emphasis here is that they themselves undertake the waiting, not that others undertake the waiting on their behalf, so as to be more emphatic as to what is intended.

Al-qurūʾ is a plural of abundance (jamʿ kathra), and from three to ten one specifies with plurals of paucity (jumūʿ qilla), and one does not turn away from paucity to that except when no plural of paucity is used, mostly; and here the plural of paucity exists, which is «aqrāʾ», so what is the wisdom in bringing the plural of abundance while the plural of paucity exists?

There are four possibilities. The first: that when He pluralised the divorced women He pluralised qurūʾ, because every divorced woman waits three aqrāʾ, so they became many by this consideration.

The second: that it is a matter of latitude, putting one of the two plurals in the place of the other. The third: that qurūʾ is the plural of qarʾ with fatḥa on the qāf, so if it had come as «aqrāʾ» it would have come against analogy, because afʿāl is not regular for faʿl with fatḥa on the fāʾ. The fourth, and it is the position of al-Mubarrad: that the implied form is "thalāthatan min qurūʾ", so he omitted «min». And he allowed "thalāthatu ḥamīr" and "thalāthatu kilāb", that is, "min ḥamīr" and "min kilāb". Abū al-Baqāʾ said: «It was said: the implied form is "thalāthat aqrāʾ min qurūʾ"», and this is al-Mubarrad's position exactly, only that he explained its meaning and made it plain.

As for al-qarʾ in the language: it was said its origin is the customary time whose recurrence is habitual, and from it "qarʾ al-najm" for the time of its rising and setting; one says "aqraʾa al-najm", that is, it rose or set. [And from it was said for] the time of the blowing of the wind, «qarʾuhā and qāriʾuhā». The poet said:

971 - شَنِئْتُ العَقْر عَقْرَ بني شُلَيْلٍ ... إذا هَبَّتْ لقارِئِها الرِّياحُ
("I hated the slaughter of the Banū Shulayl's camels when the winds blew at their time")

that is, at its time. It was said: its origin is going out from purity to menstruation or the reverse. It was said: it is from their saying "qaraytu al-māʾ fī al-ḥawḍ", that is, I gathered it; and this is a mistake, because this belongs to the yāʾ-final verbs while al-qarʾ is hamzated.

When what I have mentioned to you is settled, then know that the people of knowledge differed over its application to menstruation and purity: is it a case of verbal homonymy (ishtirāk lafẓī), so that it is among the words having opposite meanings (aḍdād), or of semantic sharing (ishtirāk maʿnawī), so that it is a mutawāṭiʾ (univocal) term, as when we take the common amount: either gathering, or time, or going out, and the like? The qarʾ of a woman is the time of her menstruation and of her purity, and of both it is said: "aqraʾat the woman", that is, she menstruated or became pure. Al-Akhfash said: "aqraʾat" means she became a possessor of menstruation, and "qaraʾat", without alif, means she menstruated. It was said: al-qarʾ is menstruation together with purity; it was said: what is between the two menstruations. It was said: its origin is gathering, and from it "qaraʾtu al-māʾ fī al-ḥawḍ", I gathered it, and from it "qaraʾa al-Qurʾān"; and their saying "mā aqraʾat hādhihi al-nāqa fī baṭnihā salāqiṭ", that is, she did not gather a foetus in it; and from it is the saying of ʿAmr ibn Kulthūm:

972 - ذِرَاعَيْ عَيْطَلٍ أدماءَ بِكْرٍ ... هِجانِ اللونِ لَم تَقْرأْ جَنِينَا
("The forearms of a tall, white she-camel, young, pure of colour, who has never carried a foetus")

On this basis, if menstruation is meant, it is for the gathering of blood in the womb, and if purity is meant, it is for the gathering of blood in the body; but those who say verbal homonymy and make the two opposites are the majority of the people of the language, like Abū ʿAmr, Yūnus and Abū ʿUbayda.

Among the occurrences of al-qarʾ where purity is meant is the saying of al-Aʿshā:

973 - أفي كلِّ عامٍ أنتَ جاشِمُ غَزْوَةٍ ... تَشُدُّ لأقْصاها عظيمَ عَزائِكا
مُوَرِّثَةً عِزَّاً وفي الحي رفعةً ... لِما ضاعَ فيها مِنْ قُروءِ نِسائكا
("Are you, every year, one who undertakes a raid, for the farthest of which you gird the great resolve of your patience, bequeathing might, and in the clan loftiness, for the qurūʾ of your wives that were lost in it")

and among its occurrences for menstruation is his saying:

974 - يا رُبَّ ذي ضِغْن عليَّ فارِضِ ... له قُروءٌ كقُروءِ الحائِضِ
("Many a spiteful man against me, old and worn, who has qurūʾ like the qurūʾ of a menstruating woman")

that is, his blood flowed like the blood of a menstruating woman. One says «qurʾ» with ḍamma, reported by al-Aṣmaʿī, and «qarʾ» with fatḥa, reported by Abū Zayd, and they have one meaning.

Al-Ḥasan read «ثلاثَةَ قَرْوٍ» with fatḥa on the qāf, sukūn on the rāʾ and light wāw, without hamza; the justification is that he annexed the number to a generic noun, and al-qarw is a dialect form of al-qarʾ. Al-Zuhrī read, and it is reported from Nāfiʿ, «قُرُوّ» with shadda on the wāw; it is like the reading of the majority except that he lightened it, changing the hamza to wāw and assimilating the wāw before it into it.

His saying: {لَهُنَّ}: attached to «يَحِلُّ», and the lām is for conveying, like that in «qultu laka».

His saying: {مَا خَلَقَ}: regarding «mā» two possibilities. The most evident: that it is a relative in the sense of «alladhī»; the second: that it is an indefinite noun with a qualifier. On both implications the returning pronoun is omitted because the conditions are met, the implied form being "mā khalaqahu"; and «mā» may be meant for the foetus, which is in the ruling of the non-rational, and so «mā» was applied to it; and it may be meant for menstrual blood.

His saying: {في أَرْحَامِهِنَّ}: two possibilities. One: that it is attached to «خلق». The second: that it is attached to an omitted word as a ḥāl from the returning pronoun of «mā» which is omitted, the implied form being: "what Allah created, being in their wombs"; they said it is a ḥāl muqaddara (an anticipated state); Abū al-Baqāʾ said: «because the time of its creation is nothing until its creation is complete.» Mubashshir ibn ʿUbayd read: «في أرحامهنَّ» and «بردِّهُنَّ» with ḍamma on the pronoun hāʾ, and it has preceded that this is the origin and that it is the dialect of the Ḥijāz, and that the kasra is for homogeneity with the yāʾ or the kasra.

His saying: {إِن كُنَّ}: this is a condition, and regarding its apodosis there are the two well-known positions: either it is omitted, its implied form being from the wording of what precedes it so that the indication of it is stronger, that is: "if they believe in Allah and the Last Day, it is not lawful for them to conceal"; or it is that which precedes, as is the position of the Kufans and Abū Zayd; and it was said that «in» is in the sense of «idh» (since), and this is weak.

His saying: {وَبُعُولَتُهُنَّ}: the majority read with ḍamma on the tāʾ of «بعولتهن»; Maslama ibn Muḥārib made it sukūn, owing to the succession of vowels, so he lightened it, and its parallel is the reading {وَرُسُلُنَا لَدَيْهِمْ يَكْتُبُونَ} [al-Zukhruf: 80] with sukūn on the lām, reported by Abū Zayd; and Abū ʿAmr reported that the dialect of Tamīm is to make the nominative sukūn in «yuʿallimuhum» and the like. It was said: that was made to run like ʿaḍud and ʿajuz, likening the detached to the attached. This has been dealt with more fully before. [Translator's note: the source prints the Zukhruf verse as 30; it is 80 in the standard numbering. Translated as printed.]

And «aḥaqq» is a khabar for «بُعولتهنّ» and is in the sense of «ḥaqīqūn» (entitled), since there is no sense of comparative here, for others than husbands have no right over them at all, and women have no right in that either, so that if she refuses the taking back it is not reckoned; therefore I said that «aḥaqq» here carries no comparative sense.

Al-buʿūla is the plural of «baʿl», which is the husband of the woman. . . ; they said it was so named . . . the one who rises above . . . and because of what rises of the land . . . so it drinks with its roots, baʿl; and one says baʿala al-rajulu yabʿalu, like manaʿa yamnaʿu. The tāʾ in buʿūla is for the feminisation of the plural, like fuḥūla and dhukūra, and this is not analogical: were you to say kaʿb and kuʿūba, it would not be permitted. [Translator's note: the source text has gaps (ellipses) in the etymology of baʿl; reproduced as printed.]

Al-buʿūla is also a maṣdar of baʿala al-rajulu buʿūlatan and biʿālan, and one says "a woman of good taba ʿʿul" (conduct towards her husband), and "bāʿalahā" is a euphemism for intercourse.

His saying: {بِرَدِّهِنَّ}: attached to «aḥaqq». As for «في ذلك», it has two possibilities. One: that it too is attached to «aḥaqq», and what is pointed to by «dhālika» on this basis is the ʿidda (waiting period), that is, he has the greater right to take her back as long as she is in the ʿidda, and the meaning is not that he has a greater right to take her back during the ʿidda, but that he takes her back in marriage or into marriage. The second: that it is attached to «al-radd», and what is pointed to by «dhālika» on this basis is the marriage; said by Abū al-Baqāʾ.

The pronoun in «بُعولَتِهِنّ» returns to some of the divorced women, namely the revocably divorced specifically. The Shaykh said: «The more fitting in my view is that there is an omitted muḍāf indicated by the ruling, that is: "the husbands of their revocably divorced ones"»; so, according to what the Shaykh said, the pronoun returns to all the divorced women.

His saying: {وَلَهُنَّ مِثْلُ الذي عَلَيْهِنَّ}: a fronted khabar, attached to an omitted word, and, on the position of al-Akhfash, of the type verb and agent. This is of the wonders of speech: something has been omitted from its beginning whose like is put at its end, and something has been omitted from its end whose like is put at its beginning; the original composition is: "wa-lahunna ʿalā azwājihinna mithlu alladhī li-azwājihinna ʿalayhinna", so «ʿalā azwājihinna» was omitted for the putting of its like, which is «ʿalayhinna», and «li-azwājihinna» was omitted for the putting of its like, which is «lahunna».

His saying: {بالمعروف}: two possibilities. One: that it is attached to what «lahunna» is attached to, of settling, that is: "it is settled for them in accordance with what is customary". The second: that it is attached to an omitted word as an adjective of «mithl», because «mithl» does not become definite by annexation; so on the first it is in the position of the accusative, and on the second in the position of the nominative.

His saying: {وَلِلرِّجَالِ عَلَيْهِنَّ دَرَجَةٌ}: two possibilities. The more evident: that «lil-rijāl» is a fronted khabar and «daraja» a postponed mubtadaʾ, and for «ʿalayhinna» on this implication two possibilities: either attachment to what «lil-rijāl» is attached to, or attachment to an omitted word as a ḥāl from «daraja» put before it, because it was an adjective in the origin, and when it was fronted it became accusative as a ḥāl. The second: that «ʿalayhinna» is the khabar and «lil-rijāl» a ḥāl from «daraja», because it may be an adjective for it in the origin; but this is weak in that it necessitates putting the ḥāl before its semantic governor, because «ʿalayhinna» is then the governor in it, by its being the khabar. Although some of them said: whenever the ḥāl itself is an adverbial or a preposition and its genitive noun, its fronting before its semantic governor is strong, and this is of that kind; this is the meaning of the statement of Abū al-Baqāʾ. The Shaykh refuted it: this ḥāl has been fronted before both parts of the clause, so it is the parallel of "qāʾiman fī al-dāri Zaydun"; he said: «This is forbidden, not weak, as some claimed; and he made the place of the disagreement the case where the ḥāl, whose governor is the meaning, is not fronted before both parts of the clause but is placed in the middle, like "Zaydun qāʾiman fī al-dār"; he said: Abū al-Ḥasan permits it and others forbid it.»

semin-durr:217-217.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {قِتَالٍ فِيهِ}: The reading of the majority is «قتالٍ» in the genitive, and there are three views on it. The first: that it is genitive as a badal (substitute) from «الشهر», a substitute of inclusion (badal ishtimāl), since the fighting occurs in it, so it includes it. The second: that it is genitive by repetition (of the governor). Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "He means that the implied form is «عن قتالٍ فيه»." This is the meaning of al-Farrāʾ's saying, for he said: "It is governed by an implied «عَنْ». But this is very weak, because the operation of a preposition does not remain after its omission in preferred usage." This should not be counted as a disagreement between the Basrans and al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ, because the substitute according to the majority of the Basrans is on the intention of repeating the governor, and this is precisely the view of al-Kisāʾī. As for his saying "because the operation of a preposition does not remain after its omission": if he means in other than the substitute, it is conceded; if he means in the substitute, it is disputed, and this is what al-Kisāʾī meant. The third, said by Abū ʿUbayda: that it is genitive by adjacency (jiwār). Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "This is more remote than the saying of the two, meaning al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ, because jiwār belongs to the places of necessity or anomaly, so what has an alternative is not to be interpreted by it." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It is an error." The Shaykh said: "If Abū ʿUbayda meant by jiwār the technical term, then it is an error. The ground of the error is that the genitive by adjacency is an expression for a thing being a follower of a nominative or accusative in wording and meaning, so it is diverted from following its leader in wording and put in the genitive because of its adjacency to a genitive, as in their saying: 'hādhā juḥru ḍabbin kharibin' (this is the burrow of a ruined lizard) with «خرب» in the genitive, though it should have been nominative because it is an attribute of the burrow, not of the lizard. This question has more explanation that will come in its place, if Allah the Exalted wills. Here «قتالٍ» is not a follower of a nominative or accusative that was adjacent to a genitive and so put in the genitive. But if he meant that it follows a genitive, so its genitive case is due to its adjacency to a genitive, i.e. it became a follower of it, it would not be an error, except that he was obscure in his expression, so it was confused with the technical term."

Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Aʿmash read «عن قتالٍ» with «عن» overt, and it is thus in the codex of ʿAbd Allāh. ʿIkrima read «قَتْلٍ فيه، قل قتلٌ فيه» without an alif.

It was read irregularly «قتالٌ فيه» in the nominative, and there are two views on it. The first: that it is a mubtadaʾ and the preposition and its genitive noun after it is the khabar; and beginning with it though it is indefinite is justified because it is on the intention of the interrogative hamza, the implied form being "a-qitālun fīhi". The second: that it is nominative by an active participle, the implied form being "a-jāʾizun qitālun fīhi" (is fighting in it permitted), so it is the agent of it. Abū l-Baqāʾ expressed this view as being the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ; so its being nominative came from three directions: either a mubtadaʾ, or an agent, or the khabar of a mubtadaʾ.

They said: this is apparent in that their question was not about whether fighting occurred in the month or not; their question was only whether fighting in it was permitted or not. On both views this clause that is asked about is in the position of the genitive as a substitute from «الشهر الحرام», because «سأل» has already taken its two objects, so it is not the object even if it is the focus of the question.

His saying {فِيهِ}: on the reading with «قتالٍ» in the genitive there are two views. The first: that it is in the position of the genitive because it is an adjective of «قتال». The second: that it is in the position of the accusative because it is attached to «قتال» since it is a maṣdar. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "as it is attached to «قاتل»." There is no need for this comparison, for the maṣdar governs by being carried over from the verb. The pronoun in «يسألونك»: it was said to be for the polytheists, and it was said for the believers. The alif and lām in «الشهر»: it was said it is for a specific reference, and it is Rajab; and it was said it is generic, so it includes all the sacred months.

His saying: {قِتَالٌ فِيهِ كَبِيرٌ}: a clause of mubtadaʾ and khabar, its position being the accusative by «قُلْ». Beginning with an indefinite is permitted for one of two reasons: either the description, if we make His saying «فيه» an adjective of it, or the specification by governing, if we make it attached to «قتال», as preceded in its like. If it is said: an indefinite word has preceded and been repeated without the alif and lām entering upon it, though it should have had it, as in the saying of the Exalted: {كَمَآ أَرْسَلْنَآ إلى فِرْعَوْنَ رَسُولاً فعصى فِرْعَوْنُ الرسول} [al-Muzzammil: 15-16], then Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "What is meant is not the magnification of any fighting whatsoever, so on this the second «قتالٌ» is other than the first." This is not clear; for the alif and lām in a noun repeated after being first mentioned do not convey magnification but only convey the specific reference to the preceding noun. Better than it is the saying of some: "The second is other than the first, because their question was about the fighting of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaḥsh, which was for the support of Islam and the abandonment of unbelief, so it is not among the major sins; rather what is among the major sins is a fighting other than this, namely that in which there is humiliation of Islam and support of unbelief. So the indefinite form was chosen in these two words for this subtlety; and had they been brought both definite, or one of them definite, this benefit would be void."

His saying: {وَصَدٌّ}: two views on it. The first: that it is a mubtadaʾ and what follows it is conjoined to it, and «أكبرُ» is the khabar of all. Beginning with «صدّ» is permitted for one of three reasons: either its specification by the description in His saying {عَن سَبِيلِ الله}, or its governing (something), or its being conjoined, and conjunction is among the justifications. The second: that it is conjoined to «كبيرٌ», i.e. "fighting in it is great, and a barring"; al-Farrāʾ said this. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "This is an error, because the meaning leads to His saying «وكفرٌ به» also being conjoined to «كبيرٌ», and from that it follows that expelling the people of the Mosque from it is greater than unbelief, and its corruption is plain." What he refuted al-Farrāʾ's view with is not binding on him, since he may say: His saying «وكفرٌ به» is a mubtadaʾ and what follows it is conjoined to it, and «أكبرُ» is the khabar of the two, i.e. the sum of the two matters is greater than the fighting and the barring; and it does not follow from that that expelling the people of the Mosque is greater than unbelief, but rather that it is greater than the fighting in the sacred month.

[Translator's note: the source has here a stray fragment: «في الشهرِ الحرامِ.» ("in the sacred month."), translated as given: "in the sacred month."]

It is a maṣdar whose agent and object are omitted, since the implied form is: "your barring, O unbelievers, the Muslims from the way of Allah, which is Islam."

«كفرٌ»: two views on it. The first: that it is conjoined to «صَدّ» on our view that «صداً» is a mubtadaʾ, not on our view that it is a second khabar of «قتال», because it would follow that fighting in the sacred month is unbelief, and that is not so, unless what is meant by the second fighting is that in which there is the demolition of Islam and the strengthening of unbelief, as preceded from some of them, so it would be unbelief, and its conjunction to it is sound absolutely. It too is a maṣdar, but an intransitive one, so only its agent is omitted: "and your unbelief". The second: that it is a mubtadaʾ, as the detail of the saying on it will come. The pronoun in «به» has two views. The first: that it returns to «سبيل», because it is what is being spoken of. The second: that it returns to Allah, and the first is more apparent. «به» has the two views, I mean its being an adjective of «كفر» or attached to it, as preceded in «فيه».

His saying: {والمسجد الحرام}: the majority read it genitive. It was read irregularly nominative. As for its being genitive, the grammarians differed about it in four ways. The first, which is the view of al-Mubarrad, followed in that by al-Zamakhsharī and Ibn ʿAṭiyya (Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It is the sound view"): that it is conjoined to «سبيلِ الله», i.e. "and a barring from the way of Allah and from the Mosque". This is rejected because it leads to separating the parts of the ṣila by an alien element. Its explanation is that «صداً» is a maṣdar implied as «أَنْ» and the verb, and «أَنْ» is a relative; and you have made «والمسجدِ» conjoined to «سبيلِ», so it is part of the completion of its ṣila, and the two were separated by an alien, which is «وكفرٌ به». The meaning of its being alien is that it has no connection to the ṣila. If it is said: latitude is allowed with the adverb and the preposition that is not allowed with others, it is said: that is said only about fronting, not about separation.

The second: that it is conjoined to the hāʾ in «به», i.e. "and unbelief in it and in the Mosque". This is derived from the view of the Kufans. As for the Basrans, they require, for conjunction to a genitive pronoun, the repetition of the governing preposition except in necessity, so this derivation is invalid according to them. This question must be addressed, and what is sound in it. I say, with Allah's help: the grammarians differed on conjunction to a genitive pronoun in three schools. The first, which is the school of the majority of the Basrans: the obligation of repeating the preposition except in necessity. The second: that it is permitted in broad usage absolutely, which is the school of the Kufans, followed by Abū l-Ḥasan, Yūnus and al-Shalawbīn.

The third: distinction, namely that if the pronoun is emphasized, conjunction is permitted without repeating the governing preposition, as in "marartu bika nafsika wa-Zaydin" (I passed by you yourself and Zayd), and otherwise it is not permitted except of necessity; this is the view of al-Jarmī. What is proper is that it is permitted absolutely, because of the abundance of the attested usage, the weakness of the proof of those who forbid, and its support by analogy.

As for attested usage: in prose, as in their saying: "mā fīhā ghayruhu wa-farasihi" (there is in it nothing but him and his horse) with «فرسه» in the genitive, conjoined to the hāʾ in «غيره». And His saying: {تَسَآءَلُونَ بِهِ والأرحام} in the reading of a large group, among them Ḥamza, and this verse will come, if Allah wills. And from it: {وَمَن لَّسْتُمْ لَهُ بِرَازِقِينَ} [al-Ḥijr: 20], where «مَنْ» is conjoined to «لكم» in the saying of the Exalted {لَكُمْ فِيهَا مَعَايِشَ}; and His saying {مَا يتلى عَلَيْكُمْ} [al-Nisāʾ: 127], conjoined to «فيهِنّ» (i.e. "about them and about what is recited to you"). In verse, where it is very frequent, among it the saying of al-ʿAbbās ibn Mirdās:

930 - أَكُرُّ على الكتيبةِ لا أُبالي ... أفيها كان حَتْفي أم سواها
(I charge upon the squadron without caring: was my death in it or other than it?)

where «سواها» is conjoined to «فيها». And the saying of another:

931 - تُعَلَّقُ في مثلِ السَّوارِي سيوفُنا ... وما بينها والأرضِ غَوْطٌ نَفانِفٌ
(Our swords are hung on things like pillars, and between them and the ground are vast hollows.)

And the saying of another:

932 - هَلاَّ سَأَلْتَ بذي الجماجم عنهمُ ... وأبي نُعَيْم ذي اللِّواء المُحْرِقِ
(Why did you not ask at Dhū l-Jamājim about them, and Abū Nuʿaym, the one with the burning banner?)

And the saying of another:

933 - بنا أبداً لا غيرِنا تُدْرَكُ المُنَى ... وتُكْشَفُ غَمَّاءُ الخطوبِ الفَوادِحِ
(Through us always, not others, are hopes attained and the gloom of crushing calamities lifted.)

And the saying of another:

934 - لو كانَ لي وزهيرٍ ثالثٌ وَرَدَتْ ... من الحِمامِ عِدانا شَرَّ مَوْرودِ
(Had Zuhayr and I a third, our enemies would have come to the worst watering-place of death.)

And another said:

935 - إذا أَوْقدوا ناراً لحربِ عَدُوِّهمْ ... فَقَدْ خابَ مَنْ يَصْلَى بها وسعيرِها
(When they kindle a fire for war on their enemy, he who is scorched by it and its blaze has surely failed.)

And another said:

936 - إذا بنا بل أُنَيْسانَ اتَّقَتْ فِئَةٌ ... ظَلَّتْ مُؤَمَنَّةً مِمَّنْ يُعادِيها
(When a band guarded itself by us — rather by Unaysān — it remained secure from those who oppose it.) [Translator's note: the wording of this verse is corrupt in the source; the gloss is tentative.]

And another said:

937 - آبَكَ أيِّهْ بيَ أو مُصَدَّرِ ... من حُمُرِ الجِلَّةِ جَأْبٍ حَشُوَرِ
(... "Is it you? Come, by me or by one in the lead, from among the large, dark-grey, bulky-flanked wild asses..." ) [Translator's note: this verse is obscure and the source text appears corrupt; the gloss is tentative.]

And Sībawayh recited:

938 - فاليومَ قَرَّبْتَ تهجُونا وَتشْتِمُنا ... فاذهبْ فما بك والأيام مِنْ عَجَبِ
(So today you have drawn near, satirizing and reviling us; go, for there is no wonder in you and the days.)

The frequency of this occurring and their freedom in the conjunction particles, for they came at times with wāw, at others with «لا», at others with «أم», and at others with «بل», is proof of its permissibility. As for the weakness of the proof: it is that they forbade that because the pronoun is like the tanwīn, so just as there is no conjunction to the tanwīn, there is none to it except by repeating the preposition. The ground of its weakness is that by the requirement of this reason there would be no conjunction to the pronoun at all, I mean whether it is nominative in position, accusative or genitive, and whether the governing preposition is repeated with it or not, like the tanwīn.

As for analogy: it is one of the five followers, so just as the genitive pronoun is emphasized and has a substitute, so likewise conjunction may be made to it.

The third: that it is conjoined to «الشهر الحرام», i.e. "they ask you about the sacred month and about the Sacred Mosque." Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "This is weakened by the fact that the people did not ask about the Sacred Mosque, since they did not doubt its magnification; they asked only about the fighting in the sacred month because it occurred from them and they were not aware of its having begun, so they feared sin, and the polytheists had reproached them for it." Its weakness is not apparent by that, because on this derivation their question would be about two things: the first, fighting in the sacred month; the second, fighting in the Sacred Mosque, because they did not ask about the essence of the month nor the essence of the Mosque, but asked only about fighting in them, as you mentioned. So they were answered that fighting in the sacred month is great, and a barring from the way of Allah the Exalted, so that «قتال» is reported of as being great and as being a barring from the way of Allah; and they were answered that fighting in the Sacred Mosque and expelling its people is greater than fighting in it. In sum, conjoining it to the sacred month is very affected, and the composition of the Qur'an and eloquent construction is far from it.

The fourth: that it is attached to an omitted verb indicated by the maṣdar, the implied form being: "and they bar from the Mosque", as the Exalted said: {هُمُ الذين كَفَرُواْ وَصَدُّوكُمْ عَنِ المسجد الحرام} [al-Fatḥ: 25]. Abū l-Baqāʾ said this and considered it good. It is not good, because it entails omitting the preposition while retaining its operation, and that is not permitted except in cases of which this is not one, with disagreement over some of them; and the grammarians stated that it is a necessity, as in his saying:

939 - إذا قيل: أيُّ الناسِ شَرُّ قبيلةٍ ... أشارَتْ كليبٍ بالأكفِّ الأصابعُ
(When it is asked, "Which people are the worst tribe?", the fingers pointed with the palms to Kulayb.)

i.e. "ilā Kulayb". These are four views, the best of which is the second.

As for its being nominative, its ground is that it is conjoined to «وكفرٌ به» with an omitted annexed word, the implied form being «وكفرٌ بالمسجدِ»; so the bāʾ was omitted and «كفرٌ» annexed to the Mosque, then the annexed word was omitted and the genitive-annexed one put in its place. The affectation in it is not hidden, but this irregular reading cannot be derived with more than that.

His saying: {وَإِخْرَاجُ أَهْلِهِ}: conjoined to «كفرٌ» or to «صدٌّ», according to the disagreement that preceded; it is a maṣdar whose agent is omitted and which is annexed to its object, the implied form being: «وإخراجُكم أهلَه». The pronoun in «أهله» and «منه» returns to the Mosque. It was said: the pronoun in «منه» returns to the way of Allah, and the first is more apparent. «منه» is attached to the maṣdar.

His saying: {أَكْبَرُ}: two views on it. The first: that it is a khabar of the three, I mean: the barring, the unbelief and the expelling, as preceded; and in that case there are two possibilities. The first: that it is a khabar of the sum; the other possibility is that it is a khabar of them by considering each one, as you say: "Zaydun wa-Bakrun wa-ʿAmrun afḍalu min Khālidin" (Zayd, Bakr and ʿAmr are better than Khālid), i.e. each one of them individually is better than Khālid. This is the apparent view. The khabar was made singular only because it is afḍal min, and its implied form: "greater than fighting in the sacred month"; it was omitted because the meaning indicates it.

The second of the two views on «أكبر»: that it is the khabar of the last, and the khabar of «وصد» and «كفر» is omitted because the khabar of the third indicates it, the implied form being: "and the barring and the unbelief are greater". Abū l-Baqāʾ said on this view: "The omitted one on this view must be «أكبر», not «كبير» as some implied it; because that would require that expelling the people of the Mosque from it be..." [Translator's note: the source text is garbled at this point; it continues:] the khabar of «وصد» and «كفر» is omitted because the khabar of «قتال» indicates it, i.e. "fighting in the sacred month is great, and the barring and the unbelief are also great, and expelling the people of the Mosque is greater than fighting in the sacred month."

It does not follow from that that it is greater than the sum of what preceded, so that what he said of the objection would follow.

His saying: {عِندَ الله}: attached to «أكبر»; "being with" here is figurative, as is known. The one surpassed is stated explicitly here in His saying {والفتنة أَكْبَرُ مِنَ القتل}, because nothing would indicate it if omitted, unlike the one before it where it was omitted. His saying: «حتى يَرُدُّوكم»: «حتى» is a preposition, and its meaning admits two views: the first, the limit (ghāya); the second, cause, with the sense of «كي». Cause is better because it mentions what moves them to the act, and the limit has not that; for that reason al-Zamakhsharī mentioned only its being for cause. He said: "«حتى» has the sense of cause, as in your saying: 'so-and-so worships Allah in order to enter Paradise'," i.e. "they fight you in order that they turn you back." Ibn ʿAṭiyya mentioned only its being a limit; he said: "«ويردُّوكم» is accusative by «حتى» because it is a pure limit." The apparent sense of his saying "accusative by «حتى»" is that he does not imply «أَنْ», but he does not intend that, though some say it. The verb after it is accusative by an obligatorily implied «أن».

«يزالون» is the imperfect of zāla, the defective one that raises the subject and puts the predicate in the accusative; it operates only on condition that negation, prohibition or supplication precede it, and the negative particle may be omitted regularly when the verb is imperfect in the answer to an oath, and otherwise only by transmission; its rules are in the books of grammar. Its pattern is fa ʿila with kasra on the ʿayn, and it is of the yāʾ-final (hollow-yāʾ) verbs by the proof of what al-Kisāʾī related for its imperfect: yazīlu, even though the more common is yazālu. As for the complete zāla, its pattern is faʿala with fatḥa, and it is of the wāw-type, by their saying in its imperfect yazūlu, and its meaning is transformation. «عن دينكم» is attached to «يردوكم». His saying «إن استطاعوا» is a condition whose apodosis is omitted because of indication, i.e. "if they are able to do that, then they will not cease to fight you"; and whoever holds that putting the apodosis first is permitted makes «لا يزالون» a fronted apodosis; its refutation has already preceded, namely that the fāʾ should have been obligatory in their saying: "anta ẓālimun in faʿalta" (you are unjust if you did).

His saying: {وَمَن يَرْتَدِدْ}: «مَنْ» is conditional, in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ. No one read it here with assimilation (idghām), and in al-Māʾida they differed over it, so we postpone the discussion of this question to there, if Allah the Exalted wills.

«يَرْتَدِدُ» is the form yaftaʿilu from al-radd, which is returning, as in His saying: {فارتدا على آثَارِهِمَا قَصَصاً} [al-Kahf: 64]. The Shaykh said: "Some have counted it among the verbs that are transitive to two when it is, for them, in the sense of ṣayyara (made), and they made from that His saying {فارتد بَصِيراً} [Yūsuf: 96], i.e. 'he returned'. This is an oversight on his part, because the disagreement is only about whether it has the sense of ṣāra (became) or not, and for that reason they exemplified with His saying «فارتدَّ بصيراً»; some made it with the sense of «صار», and some made the accusative after it a ḥāl; otherwise, where are the two objects here? As for what they counted as transitive to two with the sense of «صَيَّر», it is radda, not irtadda, so he confused radda with irtadda and ṣayyara with ṣāra."

«منكم» is attached to an omitted element because it is a ḥāl from the latent pronoun in «يَرْتَدِدْ», and «من» is partitive, the implied form being: "whoever turns back, while being among you, i.e. some of you". «عن دينه» is attached to «يرتددْ». «فَيَمُتْ» is conjoined to the condition, and the fāʾ signals immediate succession.

{وَهُوَ كَافِرٌ}: a ḥāl clause from the pronoun of «يَمُتْ», and it is as if a corroborating ḥāl, because had it been omitted its meaning would be understood, since what precedes it indicates succession after apostasy; and the ḥāl was brought as a clause here for exaggeration in emphasis, in that the pronoun is repeated, unlike if it had been brought as a single noun.

His saying: {فأولائك}: the apodosis of the condition. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "«مَنْ» is in the position of a mubtadaʾ, and the khabar is the clause that is His saying «فأولئك حَبِطَتْ»." He had earlier, at His saying {فَمَن تَبِعَ هُدَايَ} [al-Baqara: 38], stated that the khabar of the conditional noun is the protasis, not the apodosis, and refuted whoever claims that with what I related from him there. It is remote from him to imagine that it is a relative, because of the apparent jussive in the verb after it, and the like of him does not fall into that.

«حَبِط» has two dialects: kasra on the ʿayn, which is the famous one, and fatḥa, with which Abū l-Sammāl read throughout the Qur'an, and which was also related from al-Ḥasan. Al-ḥubūṭ: its origin is corruption, and from it "ḥabiṭa baṭnuhu" (his belly swelled), i.e. became swollen, and from it "rajulun ḥabanṭā", i.e. a man with a swollen belly.

It was carried first on the wording of «مَنْ», so it was singular in His saying «يَرْتَدِدْ، فيمتْ وهو كافر», and secondly on its meaning in His saying «فأولئك» to the end, so it is plural. It has already preceded that the like of this construction is the better of the two usages, I mean carrying first on the wording then on the meaning. His saying «في الدنيا» is attached to «حَبِطَتْ».

His saying: {وأولائك أَصْحَابُ النار}: to the end; the i'rab of its like has preceded. They differed about this clause: is it resumptive, i.e. merely to report that they are the people of the Fire, so it does not enter into the apodosis of the condition but is conjoined to the protasis clause; or is it conjoined to the apodosis, so its position is the jussive? Two views; the first is preferred by its independence and lack of restriction, the second by the fact that its conjunction to the apodosis is nearer than its conjunction to the protasis clause, and nearness is a ground of preference.

semin-durr:229-229.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {الطلاق مَرَّتَانِ}: mubtadaʾ and khabar. Al-ṭalāq may be the maṣdar of "ṭalaqat the woman, ṭalāqan", and may be a noun of the maṣdar, which is al-taṭlīq, like al-salām in the sense of al-taslīm. An omitted muḍāf before the mubtadaʾ is necessary so that the mubtadaʾ may be identical with the khabar, the implied form being: "the number of divorces in which taking back is legislated is two".

The dual in «marratān» is real, meant for the pair of one. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «It is of the dual that is meant for repetition, and he made it like labbayka, saʿdayka and hadhādhayka.» The Shaykh refuted that «in that it contradicts, on the surface, what he said first, and in that it is contrary to the ruling in the matter itself. As for the contradiction, he said: "Divorce is twice", that is, the legislated divorce is one pronouncement after another, by separation, not sending out at once; and this statement of his is apparent in the real dual. As for the contrariety, it is because what is intended is not that the legislated divorce occurs three times or more, but twice only; and what shows it is His saying after that: "فإمساكٌ", that is, by taking back after the second pronouncement, "أو تسريحٌ", that is, by the third pronouncement; and for that reason "فإن طلَّقها" comes after it.» End of what he refuted him with. But al-Zamakhsharī said that only for the sake of a meaning he mentioned; so look at his statement in the «Kashshāf», for it is sound.

The alif and lām in «الطلاق»: it was said it is for a previously known referent, indicated by His saying: {وَبُعُولَتُهُنَّ أَحَقُّ بِرَدِّهِنَّ}; and it was said it is for inclusiveness, and this is on our view that this clause is cut off from what precedes it and has no connection with it.

His saying: {فَإِمْسَاكٌ}: regarding the fāʾ there are two possibilities. One: that it is for sequence, that is: after He made known the ruling of the legislated divorce, that it is twice, one of these two things follows from it. The second: that it is the apodosis of an implied condition, its implied form being: "if he pronounced the two divorces and took the wife back, then there is retaining".

The nominative of «إمساك» is on one of three possibilities: either it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted and placed before it, the implied form according to some being "fa-ʿalaykum imsākun"; Ibn ʿAṭiyya implied it as later, its implied form being: "fa-imsākun amthalu or aḥsanu". The second: that it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is: "so what is obligatory is retaining". The third: that it is the agent of an omitted verb, that is: "let there be retaining with kindness".

His saying: {بِمَعْرُوفٍ} and «بإحسان»: regarding this bāʾ there are two views. One: that it is attached to the maṣdar itself that follows it, and its meaning is attachment (ilṣāq). The second: that it is attached to an omitted word as an adjective of what precedes it, and so it is in the position of the nominative, that is: "retaining that is with kindness, or releasing that is with goodness".

Al-tasrīḥ is sending out and releasing, and from it the grazing livestock is called saraḥ, and a she-camel suruḥ, that is, easy in gait because of her free movement in it. They said: it is permissible in Arabic to put «fa-imsākun» and «tasrīḥun» in the accusative as maṣdar, that is: "so retain them with kindness or release them with goodness", except that nobody read it so.

His saying: {أَن تَأْخُذُواْ}: «an» and what is within its range is in the position of the nominative as the agent of «yaḥillu», that is: "it is not lawful for you to take anything of what you gave them".

And «mimmā» has two possibilities. One: that it is attached to «takhudhū» itself, and «min» on this basis is for the beginning of the extent. The second: that it is attached to an omitted word as a ḥāl from «shayʾan» put before it, because had it come after it, it would have been an adjective; and «min» on this basis is partitive. «Mā» is a relative and the returning pronoun is omitted, the implied form being "min alladhī ātaytumūhunna iyyāhu". The difficulty and its answer regarding the omission of the detached accusative returning pronoun has preceded at His saying {وَممَّا رَزَقْنَاهُمْ يُنْفِقُونَ} [Yā Sīn: 54], and this is like it, so let it be looked at. [Translator's note: the source cites this verse as Yā Sīn 54; the phrase is in fact found at al-Baqara 3 and Yā Sīn 47. Translated as printed.]

«Ātā» is made transitive to two, the first being «hunna» and the second the omitted returning pronoun. «Shayʾan» is a direct object governed by «takhudhū». It may also be a maṣdar, that is, "something of taking". The two possibilities are reported at His saying: {لاَ تُظْلَمُ نَفْسٌ شَيْئاً}. His saying: {إِلاَّ أَن يَخَافَآ}: this is an unrestricted exception (istithnāʾ mufarragh), and regarding «an yakhāfā» there are two possibilities. One: that it is in the position of the accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi, so it is an exception from that omitted general term, the implied form being: "it is not lawful for you to take by any cause, except by reason of fear of not establishing the limits of Allah"; the particle of cause was omitted because the conditions for the accusative are complete, especially with «an»; and the disagreement of al-Khalīl and Sībawayh does not arise here, as to whether it is in the position of accusative or genitive after the lām is dropped; rather it is in the position of the accusative only, because this maṣdar, if stated explicitly, would be accusative, and the grammarians have stated this, I mean that «an» and what follows is in the position of the accusative without disagreement when it occurs in the place of the mafʿūl lahu.

The second: that it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, so it is also an exception from the general term, its implied form being: "it is not lawful for you in any state except in the state of fearing that they will not establish the limits of Allah." Abū al-Baqāʾ said: «The implied form is "illā khāʾifīn", and in it there is an omitted muḍāf, its implied form being: "it is not lawful to take in every state or in every state except in the state of fear".» The first possibility is better, because «an» and what is within its range is interpreted as a maṣdar, and that maṣdar stands in the place of the active participle accusative as a ḥāl, and the maṣdar does not regularly occur as a ḥāl, so what of what is in its interpretation!! Moreover, Sībawayh stated that the maṣdarī «an» does not occur in the place of the ḥāl.

The alif in His saying «yakhāfā» and «yuqīmā» refers back to the two classes of spouses. There is an iltifāt in this speech, for had it followed the course of the speech it would have been said: «illā an takhāfū allā tuqīmū» with the tāʾ of address to the group; and ʿAbd Allāh read it so, and it is also reported from him with the yāʾ of the third person, which is also an iltifāt.

The reading of «yakhāfā» with fatḥa on the yāʾ is clear; Ḥamza read it with ḍamma, as passive. A group found it difficult and others attacked it, for lack of knowledge of the tongue of the Arabs. They mentioned many justifications for it. The best of them is that «an yuqīmā» is a badal (substitute) from the pronoun in «yukhāfā», because it takes its place, its implied form being: "unless the failure of the two to establish the limits of Allah is feared", and this is a badal al-ishtimāl, like your saying "al-Zaydāni aʿjabanī ʿilmuhumā"; and the origin was: "illā an yakhāfa al-wulātu al-zawjayni allā yuqīmā ḥudūda Allāh", so the agent, which is «the authorities», was omitted owing to the indication of it, and the pronoun of the two spouses stood in place of the agent, and «an» and what follows remained in the position of the nominative as a badal, as its implied form has preceded.

Ibn ʿAṭiyya derived it on the ground that «khāfa» is made transitive to two objects like «istaghfara», that is, to one of them by itself and to the other by a preposition; and he made the alif the first object standing in place of the agent, and «an» and what is within its range the second, and made «an» in the position of the genitive according to Sībawayh and al-Kisāʾī. The Shaykh refuted this derivation on the ground that «khāfa» is not made transitive to two, and the grammarians did not count it when they counted what is made transitive to two; and because the second accusative after it in your saying "khiftu Zaydan ḍarbahu" is only a badal, not a direct object, so it is not like the second in "istaghfartu Allāha dhanban"; and because ascribing to Sībawayh that «an» is in the position of the genitive is not correct, for his position is that it is in the position of the accusative, and al-Farrāʾ followed him; while the position of al-Khalīl is that it is in the position of the genitive, and al-Kisāʾī followed him. And this has preceded more than once.

Another said the like of his statement, except that he implied the preposition «ʿalā», the implied form being: "illā an yakhāfa al-wulātu al-zawjayni ʿalā allā yuqīmā", so it was made passive, and the pronoun of the two spouses stood in the place of the agent, and the preposition was dropped from «an», and the aforementioned disagreement between Sībawayh and al-Khalīl comes in it.

What Ibn ʿAṭiyya said was preceded in it by Abū ʿAlī, except that he did not draw the parallel with «istaghfara».

A group found this reading difficult and others, who have no knowledge of that, attacked it. Al-Naḥḥās said: «I know of nothing more remote in Ḥamza's choices than this word, because neither the iʿrāb, nor the wording, nor the meaning requires it. As for the iʿrāb: Ibn Masʿūd read {إلاَّ أَنْ تخافوا ألاَّ يقيموا}; if this were referred, in Arabic, to the passive, it should be said {إلاَّ أَنْ يُخاف}. As for the wording: if it is on the wording of «yukhāfā» it would have to be said "fa-in khīfa", and if it is on the wording of «khiftum» it would have to be said "illā an takhāfū". As for the meaning: I find it remote that it be said "and it is not lawful for you to take anything of what you gave them unless someone other than you fears"; and the Exalted did not say: "there is no blame on you in taking from her a ransom for him", so that the khulʿ (divorce for compensation) would be for the ruler; yet the supposition is that khulʿ does not need the ruler.»

People have replied to al-Naḥḥās. As for what he mentioned from the side of iʿrāb, what ʿAbd Allāh read is not binding on Ḥamza. As for the side of wording, it is a case of iltifāt as I presented it first, and al-Naḥḥās would be bound, on the reading of other than Ḥamza, to read "fa-in khāfā", whereas it is in both readings of the iltifāt that is esteemed in Arabic. As for the side of meaning, it is because the rulers are the basis for removing wrongdoing among people, and they are the ones who command taking and giving.

Al-Farrāʾ justified Ḥamza's reading by his having taken into account ʿAbd Allāh's reading {إلا أن تَخافوا}, and al-Fārisī declared him mistaken and said: «He was not right, because in ʿAbd Allāh's reading the fear falls on "an", whereas in Ḥamza's reading it falls on the man and the woman.» And what he declared al-Farrāʾ mistaken by is nothing, because the meaning of ʿAbd Allāh's reading is: "unless you fear for the two, that is, the guardians fear for the two spouses, that they will not establish", so the fear falls on «an»; and likewise it is in Ḥamza's reading: the fear falls on it as well by one of the two preceding ways: either on its being a badal from the pronoun of the two spouses as its exposition has preceded, or on the dropping of the preposition, which is «ʿalā».

As for fear here, there are three possibilities. One: that it is on its normal sense of caution and dread, so «an» in the reading of other than Ḥamza is in the position of the genitive or accusative according to the disagreement over it after the dropping of the preposition, the origin being "min allā yuqīmā", or in the position of the accusative only, by the verb's being made transitive to it by itself, as if it had been said: "unless they are wary of the failure to establish the limits of Allah". The second: that it is in the sense of knowledge, and this is the view of Abū ʿUbayda, and he recited:

975 - فقلتُ لهم خافُوا بألفَيْ مُدَجَّجٍ ... سَراتُهُمُ في الفارسِيِّ المُسَرَّدِ
("So I said to them: know that there are two thousand armed men, whose leaders are in woven Persian mail")

and from it also:

976 - ولا تَدْفِنَنِّي في الفَلاةِ فإنَّني ... أخافُ إذا ما مِتُّ أَلاَّ أَذُوقُها
("Do not bury me in the open desert, for I fear that if I die I shall not taste it")

and for that reason the verb after «an» was put in the nominative; and this is not valid in the verse because the accusative is evident. As for the verse, the well-known version of its transmission is "فقلت لهم ظُنُّوا بألفَيْ". The third: supposition (ẓann), said by al-Farrāʾ, and what supports it is Ubayy's reading: {إلاَّ أنْ يَظُنَّا}, and he recited:

977 - أتاني كلامٌ مِنْ نُصَيْبٍ يقولُه ... وما خِفْتُ يا سَلاَّمُ أنَّكَ عائِبي
("Words reached me from Nuṣayb, which he says, and I did not think, Sallām, that you would find fault with me")

On these two possibilities, «an» and what is within its range fills the place of the two objects according to Sībawayh, and the place of the first, the second being omitted, according to al-Akhfash, as its exposition has preceded more than once; and the first is the correct one, because «khāfa» is one of the verbs of expectation, and supposition in it may lean to one of the two possibilities; and for that reason al-Rāghib said: «Fear is said of what contains some hope, and for that reason it is not said "I fear that I cannot ascend to the sky or blow away the mountains".»

The origin of «yuqīmā» is «yuqwimā», so the kasra of the wāw was transferred to the unvowelled letter before it, then the wāw was changed to yāʾ because of its being unvowelled after a kasra; and its exposition has preceded at His saying: {الصراط المستقيم} [al-Fātiḥa: 5]. Some claimed that His saying {وَلاَ يَحِلُّ لَكُمْ} is parenthetical between His saying {الطلاق مَرَّتَانِ} and His saying {فَإِنْ طَلَّقَهَا فَلاَ تَحِلُّ لَهُ مِن بَعْدُ}, and there is remoteness in this.

His saying: {فَلاَ جُنَاحَ عَلَيْهِمَا}: «lā» with its noun and khabar, and His saying: {فِيمَا افتدت بِهِ} is attached to the settling that the khabar comprises, which is «ʿalayhimā». It is not permitted that «ʿalayhimā» be attached to «junāḥ» and «fīmā iftadat» be the khabar, because then it would be a prolonged one (muṭawwal), and the prolonged one is declinable, while this, as you see, is indeclinable.

The pronoun in «ʿalayhimā» refers back to the two spouses, that is: there is no blame on the husband in what he took, nor on the woman in what she gave. Al-Farrāʾ said: «It refers back only to the husband, and he returned it as a dual while one is meant, as in His saying, the Exalted: {يَخْرُجُ مِنْهُمَا الُّلؤْلُؤُ وَالمَرْجَانُ} [al-Raḥmān: 22] and {نَسِيَا حُوتَهُمَا} [al-Kahf: 61] and his saying:

978 - فإنْ تَزْجُرَاني يا بنَ عَفَّانَ أَنْزَجِرْ ... وإنْ تَدَعاني أَحْمِ عِرْضاً مُمَنَّعَا
("If you two rebuke me, son of ʿAffān, I shall desist; and if you two leave me, I shall defend a protected honour")

and the pearl comes out only of the salt sea; and the one who forgot was Yūshaʿ alone; and the one addressed is one in "yā ibna ʿAffān".» «Mā» is in the sense of «alladhī» or an indefinite noun with a qualifier; it cannot be maṣdarī because of the returning of the pronoun of «bihi» to it, except according to the view of one who makes the maṣdarī an ism, like al-Akhfash, Ibn al-Sarrāj and those who followed them.

His saying: {تِلْكَ حُدُودُ الله}: mubtadaʾ and khabar, and what is pointed to is all the verses from His saying {وَلاَ تَنْكِحُواْ المشركات} up to here.

And His saying: {فَلاَ تَعْتَدُوهَا}: its origin is «taʿtadiyūhā», so the ḍamma on the yāʾ was found heavy and was dropped, so the yāʾ became unvowelled, and after it is the wāw of the pronoun, unvowelled, so the yāʾ was dropped on account of the meeting of two unvowelled letters, and the letter before the wāw was given ḍamma so that it would be sound; the pattern of the word is «taftaʿūhā».

His saying: {وَمَن يَتَعَدَّ}: «man» is conditional, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ, and regarding its khabar there is the disagreement that has preceded.

And His saying: {فأولئك} is its apodosis. It cannot be a relative with the fāʾ redundant in the khabar, because its effect of jussive is evident in what follows it. And «hum» in «فأولئك هم» admits three possibilities. One: that it is a separator (faṣl). The second: that it is a badal; and «الظالمون» on these two is the khabar of «ulāʾika», the predication being by a single word. The third: that it is a second mubtadaʾ and «الظالمون» its khabar, and the clause is the khabar of «ulāʾika», the predication on this basis being by a clause; and the emphasis in this clause is not hidden, from the side of bringing the demonstrative for the distant, the placing of the separator in the middle, and the definiteness by the lām in «الظالمون», that is, those who go to extremes in wrongdoing. He first took it on the wording of «man», so he used the singular in His saying «yataʿadda», and second on its meaning, so he used the plural in His saying: {فأولئك هُمُ الظالمون}.

semin-durr:230-230.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {فَإِنْ طَلَّقَهَا}: that is, after the third divorce; and when «baʿdu» was cut off from annexation it was made indeclinable on ḍamma, for the reason whose exposition has preceded. «Lahu», «min baʿdu» and «ḥattā» are all three attached to «yaḥillu». The meaning of «min» is the beginning of the extent, the lām is for conveying, and «ḥattā» is for reason; so said the Shaykh. The apparent view is that it is for the end-point (ghāya), because the meaning is so: that is, the absence of permissibility for him extends until she marries a husband other than him; so when he divorces her and her ʿidda from him is completed, she becomes lawful for the first man who divorced her three times; and what indicates this omission is the tenor of the speech.

«Ghayrahu» is an adjective of «zawjan», although it is indefinite, because «ghayr» and its sisters do not become definite by annexation, being in the force of an active participle that governs. Is «zawjan» for restriction or for preparation (tawṭiʾa)? A benefit is built on that: if it is for restriction, then were the woman a slave girl whom her husband divorced three times and her master then had intercourse with her, she would not be lawful for the first, because he is not a husband; and if it is for preparation, she would be lawful, because the mention of the husband is as if disregarded, as though it had been said: "until she marries someone other than him", and the word «zawj» was used only because it is the usual case.

His saying: {فَإِنْ طَلَّقَهَا}: the nominative pronoun refers back to the indefinite «zawjan», that is: "if that second husband divorces her"; and He used the conditional «in» rather than «idhā» as a warning that his divorce must be by his own choice, without that being made a condition upon him, because «idhā» is for what is certain to occur, while «in» is for what is of uncertain occurrence or what is certain to occur but of uncertain time of occurrence, as in His saying, the Exalted: {أَفَإِنْ مِّتَّ فَهُمُ الخالدون} [al-Anbiyāʾ: 34].

His saying: {عَلَيْهِمَآ}: the pronoun in «ʿalayhimā» may refer back to the woman and the first husband who divorced her three times, that is: "if the second divorces her and her ʿidda from him is completed, there is no blame on the husband who divorced three times, nor on her, that they return to each other". It may also refer back to her and the second husband, that is: "there is no blame on the woman nor on the second husband that they return to each other, so long as her ʿidda remains"; and on this basis there is no need to omit that implied clause, namely «and her ʿidda is completed», and the verse would have conveyed two rulings: one, that she is not lawful for the first except after she marries another; the second, that it is permissible for the second to take her back so long as her ʿidda from him remains, and that would be a repelling of the fancy of one who imagines that if she marries someone other than the first she becomes lawful for the first only, and the second would have no right of taking her back.

His saying: {أَن يَتَرَاجَعَآ}: that is, fī an; so regarding its position there are the two well-known views. «ʿAlayhimā» is the khabar of «lā», and «fī an» is attached to the settling; and it has preceded that «ʿalayhimā» may not be attached to «junāḥ», with the prepositional phrase as khabar, because of the necessity of tanwīn in the noun of «lā», for it would then be a prolonged one.

His saying: «in ẓannā»: a condition whose apodosis is omitted according to Sībawayh owing to the indication of what precedes it, and fronted according to the Kufans and Abū Zayd. Ẓann here is on its normal sense of preferring one of two sides, and this strengthens the view that the preceding fear is in the sense of ẓann. Abū ʿUbayda and others claimed that it is in the sense of certainty, and al-Zamakhsharī weakened this view for two reasons. One, from the side of wording: that the accusative «an» is not governed by certainty, which is only for the doubled and the lightened forms of it; you do not say "ʿalimtu an yaqūma Zaydun", you say "ʿalimtu anna Zaydan yaqūmu". The second, from the side of meaning: for a person does not have certainty of what is in tomorrow, but only supposes it.

The Shaykh said: «As for what he mentioned, that one does not say "ʿalimtu an yaqūma Zaydun", others have mentioned it, such as al-Fārisī and others, except that Sībawayh permitted "mā ʿalimtu illā an yaqūma Zaydun", and this is evidently a refutation of al-Fārisī. Some said: the way to combine the two is that «ʿalima» may be meant as strong supposition, as in His saying: {فَإِنْ عَلِمْتُمُوهُنَّ مُؤْمِنَاتٍ} [al-Mumtaḥana: 10] and his saying:
