979 - وأعلمُ علمَ حقٍ غيرِ ظنٍّ ... وتَقْوى اللَّهِ من خير العتادِ
("I know with the knowledge of truth, not supposition, that fear of Allah is among the best of provisions")

for his saying «ʿilm ḥaqq» it is understood from it that there may be knowledge that is not truth, and likewise his saying «ghayr ẓann» it is understood from it that there may be ʿilm in the sense of ẓann. And what indicates that «ʿalima» in the sense of «ẓanna» governs the accusative «an» is the saying of Jarīr:

980 - نرضَى عن الناسِ إنَّ الناسَ قد علموا ... أنْ لا يدانَينا مِنْ خَلْقِهِ أَحَدُ
("We are content with people, for people have known that none of His creation can approach us")

Then the Shaykh said: «It is established by the saying of Jarīr and Sībawayh's permission that "ʿalima" governs the accusative "an", so it is not a fault from the side of the wording, as al-Zamakhsharī mentioned. As for his saying "because a person does not know what is in tomorrow", it is not as he said; rather a person knows many things that will occur tomorrow and is certain of them.» This refutation by the Shaykh is very astonishing: how can it be said of the verse that ẓann is in the sense of certainty, and then certainty be made in the sense of ẓann justifying its governing the accusative «an»? And his statement "because a person may be certain of things tomorrow" is granted, but this is not among them.

And His saying: {أَن يُقِيمَا}: it either fills the place of the two objects, or of the first with the second omitted, according to the two preceding positions.

His saying: {يُبَيِّنُهَا}: regarding this clause two possibilities. One: that it is in the position of the nominative as a khabar after a khabar, according to one who sees that. The second: that it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, whose owner is «ḥudūd Allāh», the governor in it being the demonstrative; and it was read «nubayyinuhā» with nūn, and this is reported from ʿĀṣim, on an iltifāt from the third person to the first for glorification. «Li-qawmin» is attached to it. «Yaʿlamūn» is in the position of the genitive as an adjective of «qawm». And He singled out the knowers by mention because they are the ones who benefit from the clarification, not others.

semin-durr:282-282.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {إلى أَجَلٍ}: it is attached to «تدايَنْتُمْ», and it may be attached to an omitted element as a ṣifa of «دَيْن». And «مُسَمَّى» is a ṣifa of «دَيْن», so he would have put the interpreted ṣifa before the explicit one, which is weak; so the first aspect is the more sound.
«تَدَايَنَ» is of the pattern «تفاعَلَ» from «الدَّيْن», like «تبايَعَ» from «البَيْع». One says: «داينْتُ الرجل», i.e. I dealt with him on credit, whether you were the giver or the taker. Ruʾba said:
1121 - دايَنْتُ أَرْوى والديونُ تُقْضى ... فَمَطَّلَتْ بعضاً وأَدَّتْ بَعْضَا
(I extended credit to Arwā, and debts are to be settled; she delayed part and paid part.)
One says: «دِنْتُ الرجلَ» when I sold to him on credit, and «أَدِنْتُه» when I took from him on credit; so they distinguished between «فَعَل» and «أَفْعَلَ».
His saying: {فاكتبوه}: the pronoun refers back to «بدَيْن». He mentioned the words «بدَيْن» only so as to have this pronoun refer back to it, even though the debt is understood from His saying «تدايَنْتُم»; or because it might be said «تَداينوا» meaning that they requited one another, so He said «بِدَيْن» to remove this ambiguity; or to indicate generality by it, i.e. whatever debt it be, small or large.
His saying: {إِلَى أَجَلٍ} is by way of emphasis, since a debt is only ever deferred. The alif of «مُسَمَّى» is converted from a yāʾ, and that yāʾ is converted from a wāw, because it is from «التسمية»; it has already been presented that the root is from «سما يسمو».
His saying: {بالعدل} has several aspects. One: that the preposition and its genitive noun is attached to the verb before it. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "«بالعدلِ» is attached to His saying «فَلْيَكْتُبْ», i.e. 'let him write with the truth'; it may be a ḥāl, i.e. 'let him write justly', and it may be a mafʿūl bihi, i.e. 'by reason of justice'." His first saying "«بالعدلِ» is attached to His saying «فَلْيَكْتُب»" means attachment in meaning, since he later permits it to be a ḥāl, and if it is a ḥāl it is attached to an omitted element, not to the verb itself. And his saying "it may be a mafʿūl bihi" means that then the bāʾ is attached to the verb itself.
The second: that it is attached to «كاتب». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is attached to «كاتب» as a ṣifa of it, i.e. a scribe trusted with what he writes", and it is as presented in the interpretation of Abū al-Baqāʾ's words. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "The bāʾ is attached to His saying «وَلْيَكْتُب», and it is not attached to His saying «كاتبٌ», because it would then follow that none should write a document except one just in himself, whereas a boy or a slave may write it."
The third: that the bāʾ is redundant, its implied form being: «فَلْيكتب بينكم كاتبُ العدلِ» (let the scribe of justice write between you).
His saying: {أَنْ يَكْتُبَ} is a mafʿūl bihi, i.e. "let him not refuse writing".
And «كما عَلَّمه الله» may be attached to His saying «أَنْ يَكْتُبَ», as a naʿt of an omitted maṣdar, or a ḥāl from the pronoun of the maṣdar according to Sībawayh; the implied being: "that he write a writing like what Allah taught him", or "that he write it, i.e. the writing, like what Allah taught him". It may also be attached to His saying «فَلْيَكْتُبْ» which follows.
The Shaykh said: "The apparent is the attachment of the kāf to His saying «فَلْيَكْتُب», but it is unsettled because of the fāʾ, and because if it were attached to His saying «فَلْيكتب» the arrangement would be «فَلْيكتب كما عَلَّمه الله», and there would be no need to put forward what is later in meaning."
Al-Zamakhsharī said – after mentioning its attachment to «أَنْ يكتُبَ» and to «فليكتب» – "If you say: what is the difference between the two aspects? I say: if you attach it to «أَنْ يكتب», He has forbidden refusing the qualified writing, then it is said to him «فَلْيَكْتُب» that writing, not deviating from it; and if you attach it to His saying «فَلْيكتب», He has forbidden refusing writing in absolute terms, then commanded it qualified." It may be attached to His saying «لا يَأْبَ», the kāf then being causal. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It is possible that «كما» is attached to the meaning contained in His saying «ولا يأْبَ», i.e. 'as Allah has favoured him with the knowledge of writing, let him not refuse, and let him be bountiful as bounty was shown to him.'" The Shaykh said: "This is contrary to the apparent, and the kāf in this view is causal." I say: on the view that it is attached to His saying «فَلْيكتب», it may also be causal, i.e. "for the sake of what Allah taught him, let him write."
The common people read «فَلْيكتب» with the lām quiescent, as they say «كَتْف» for «كَتِف», treating the detached as attached. Al-Ḥasan read it with kasra, which is the original.
His saying: {وَلْيُمْلِلِ} is an imperative of «أَمَلَّ يُمِلُّ». When the second letter became quiescent by the jussive, two dialects applied: unpacking (fakk), the dialect of the Hijaz, and assimilation (idghām), the dialect of Tamīm; likewise when it becomes quiescent in pause, such as «أملِلْ عليه» and «أَمِلَّ». This is regular for every geminate, and its investigation will come, if Allah wills, at the two readings «مَنْ يَرْتَدِدْ» and «يرتدَّ» in al-Māʾida, together with the reason for each dialect.
Here «وَلْيُمِلَّ» with assimilation was also read anomalously. One says: «أَمَلَّ يُمِلُّ إملالاً» and «أَمْلَى يُملي إملاءً». Of the first is the saying:
1122 - ألا يا ديارَ الحيِّ بالسَّبُعان ... أَمَلَّ عليها بالبِلَى المَلَوانِ
(O abodes of the tribe at al-Sabuʿān, upon you night and day have dictated decay.)
and of the second the saying of the Exalted: {فَهِيَ تملى عَلَيْهِ} [al-Māʾida: 54]. [Translator's note: the source gives al-Māʾida: 54; the verse {فَهِيَ تُمْلَى عَلَيْهِ} is in al-Furqān 5, as printed.] One says «أَمْلَلْتُ» and «أَمْلَيْتُ»; it is said they are two dialects, and it is said that the yāʾ is a substitute for one of the two identical letters; the origin of both roots is repetition, time after time.
«الحقُّ» may be a mubtadaʾ with «عليه» a fronted khabar; or it may be an agent of the preposition and its genitive noun before it, since it relies on the relative noun, the relative noun being the agent of «يملل», and its object omitted, i.e. «وَلْيُمْلِلِ الديَّانُ الكتابَ ما عليه من الحقِّ» (let the debtor dictate to the scribe what is upon him of the right), the two objects being omitted because they are known. It is made transitive by «على» to one of them: one says «أَمْلَلْتُ عليه كذا», and the noble verse is of this.
His saying: {وَلاَ يَبْخَسْ مِنْهُ}: regarding «منه» it may be attached to «يبخَسْ», «مِنْ» being for the beginning of the extent, and the pronoun in «منه» referring to «الحق». The second: that it is attached to an omitted element because it is originally a ṣifa of the indefinite noun, and when put before the indefinite noun it was made accusative as ḥāl.
«شيئاً» is either a mafʿūl bihi or a maṣdar.
«البَخْسُ» is diminution; one says «بَخَس زيدٌ عمراً حقَّه يَبْخَسُهُ بَخْسَاً». Its origin is from «بَخَسْتُ عينه» (I gouged his eye), and from it «بَخْسُ الحق» was borrowed, as they said «عَوَرْتُ حَقَّه» (I blinded his right), a borrowing from the blindness of the eye. One also says «بَخَصْتُه» with ṣād. «التباخُسُ» in sale is mutual diminishing, because each of the two parties to a sale lessens the other's right.
His saying: {أَن يُمِلَّ هُوَ}: «أَن» and what is within its scope is in the position of an accusative as mafʿūl bihi, i.e. "he cannot dictate", and «هو» is emphasis of the latent pronoun. The benefit of emphasis by it is the removal of the figurative sense that the attribution of the verb to the pronoun could have allowed, and the specification that he is unable by himself; al-Shaykh said this.
It was also read with the hāʾ of «هو» quiescent, and this is a weak reading because this pronoun is an independent word, detached from what precedes it. Whoever makes it quiescent treats the detached as attached, and the investigation of this was presented at the beginning of this sūra. The Shaykh said: "This is more anomalous than the reading of the one who read {ثُمَّ هُوَ يَوْمَ القيامة} [al-Qaṣaṣ: 61]." I say: so he made that reading anomalous and this one more so, which is not good, for it is a mutawātir (widely transmitted) reading, read by Nāfiʿ ibn Abī Nuʿaym, the reader of the people of Medina, as Qālūn related from him, and he is the most accurate of his transmitters of his reading; and al-Kisāʾī also read it, and he is the chief of the grammarians.
The hāʾ in «وَليُّه» refers to the one who owes the right, when he is characterised by one of the three attributes. And His saying «بالعَدْل» is as presented for its parallel, so there is no need to repeat it.
And His saying: {واستشهدوا}: the sīn may be in its basic sense of seeking, i.e. "seek two witnesses"; or «استفعل» may have the sense of «أَفْعَلَ», such as «اسْتَعْجَلَ» meaning «أَعْجَل», and «استيقن» meaning «أَيْقَنَ». In His saying «شهيدين» there is an alert that the witness should be of those from whom testimony is repeated, since He used the intensive form.
His saying: {مِّن رِّجَالِكُمْ} may be attached to «استشهِدوا», with «مِنْ» for the beginning of the extent; and may be attached to an omitted element as a ṣifa of «شهيدَيْن», with «مِنْ» partitive.
His saying: {فَإِن لَّمْ يَكُونَا رَجُلَيْنِ}: they allowed this «كان» to be either the incomplete or the complete, and the meaning differs by the two analyses: if it is incomplete, then the alif is its ism (name), referring back to the two witnesses, i.e. "if the two witnesses are not two men"; the meaning on this is: if the owner of the right neglected that, or intended not to call two men as witnesses for some purpose of his. If it is complete, «رجلين» is accusative as a confirmatory ḥāl, like His saying {فَإِن كَانَتَا اثنتين} [al-Nisāʾ: 176], and the meaning on this is that one does not turn to what was mentioned except in the absence of men. The alif in «يكونا» refers back to «شهيدين», conveying masculinity, the implied being: "if the two witnesses are not found as two men."
His saying: {فَرَجُلٌ وامرأتان}: what follows the fāʾ may be nominative as mubtadaʾ with an omitted khabar, implied as "a man and two women suffice in testimony", or "are sufficient", or the like.
It is said: it is a khabar and the mubtadaʾ is omitted, implied as "the witness is a man and two women". It is said: rather it is nominative by an implied verb, implied as "a man suffices", i.e. the testimony of a man, with the muḍāf omitted because it is known, and the muḍāf ilayhi put in its place. It is said: the verb's implied form is "let a man testify", which is the best, since it does not require omitting a muḍāf, and this is the implication of Abū al-Qāsim al-Zamakhsharī. It is said: it is nominative by the incomplete «كان», the implied being "let there be among those who testify a man and two women". It is said: rather by the complete one, and this is preferable, because it involves omitting only a verb, with its agent remaining, whereas implying the incomplete involves omitting it together with its khabar, and what is in that is known. It is said: it is nominative as deputy agent, implied as "let a man be called to testify". Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "Had it been read in the accusative, the implied would have been «فاسْتَشْهِدُوا»." I say: this is fine speech.
It was also read «وامرأْتان» with the hamza that is the lām of the word quiescent, and there are two analyses of it. One: that he substituted the hamza with an alif, and the analogy of its lightening is not this but "between-between" (bayna bayna); and when he substituted it by alif he pronounced hamza on it, as the Arabs pronounced hamza in «العَأْلَم» and «الخَأْتم» and the saying:
1123 - وخِنْدِفٌ هامةُ هذا العَأْلَمِ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(And Khindif is the head of this world...)
The investigation of that was presented in Sūrat al-Fātiḥa, and more explanation will come, if Allah wills, in the reading of Ibn Dhakwān {مِنسَأَتَهُ} [Sabaʾ: 14].
Abū al-Baqāʾ said, in establishing this aspect, inclining to analogy: "Its justification is that he lightened the hamza – meaning between-between – so it came near the alif, and what is brought near the alif has its ruling, hence one does not begin with it; when it became like the alif he turned it into a quiescent hamza, as they said «خَأْتم» and «عَأْلم»."
The second: that he found the succession of vowels heavy, and the hamza is a letter resembling a weak letter, so a vowel on it is felt heavy, and so it was made quiescent. The Shaykh said: "It is possible that he made it quiescent for lightness, because of the succession of many vowels; and the lightening of the like of this hamza has come in the saying of the poet:
1124 - يَقُولون جَهْلاً ليس للشيخِ عَيِّلٌ ... لَعَمْرِي لقد أَعْيَلْتُ وأْنَ رَقُوبُ
(They say in ignorance: the old man has no dependants; by my life, I have had dependants, and I am childless.)
meaning «وأنا رَقوب», making the hamza of «أنا» quiescent after the wāw, and dropping the alif of «أنا» in connected speech, according to the rule." I say: Ibn Jinnī explicitly stated that this aspect is not permissible, saying: "It is not possible that he made the hamza quiescent, because what has fatḥa is not made quiescent, owing to the lightness of the fatḥa." This from Abū al-Fatḥ is to be taken as the general rule, otherwise we have just now presented in the reading of al-Ḥasan «ما بَقِي من الربا» and before that as well the discussion of this issue, and its occurrence in words in verse and prose, even in easy sound letters, so how of a heavy letter that resembles the lowly?
His saying: {مِمَّن تَرْضَوْنَ} has several aspects. One: that it is in the position of a nominative, a naʿt of «رجل وامرأتين». The second: that it is in the position of an accusative, being a naʿt of «شهيدين». The Shaykh weakened the first aspect, saying: "because the description implies its specificity to the described, so this description would be negated from «شهيدين»"; and Abū al-Baqāʾ weakened the second, saying: "because of the separation between them."
The third aspect: that it is a badal of His saying «من رجالكم» by repetition of the governor, the implied being «واستشهِدوا شهيدَيْن مِمَّنْ تَرْضَوْن». Abū al-Baqāʾ did not mention its weakness; he ought to have weakened it by what he weakened the aspect of the description, namely the separation between them. The Shaykh weakened it by the fact that the badal also implies specificity to the two witnesses who are men, so it would be bare of «رجلٌ وامرأتان». There is something to examine in this, because this is badal of part from whole if we take «رجالكم» generally, or whole from whole if we take them specifically, and on both assumptions that does not negate it from others; as for description, it is granted, because it has a mafhūm (implied contrary) according to the chosen view. Fourth: that it is attached to «استشهدوا», i.e. "call witnesses from those with whom you are satisfied." The Shaykh said: "It would be a qualification of all, and for that reason it came postponed after all."
His saying: {مِنَ الشهدآء} may be attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl from the omitted returning pronoun, the implied being: "from those with whom you are satisfied, being some of the witnesses." It may be a badal from «مِنْ» by repetition of the governor, as presented regarding «مِمَّنْ تَرْضَوْن» itself, so this would be a badal of a badal on one of the two views regarding each.
His saying: {أَن تَضِلَّ}: Ḥamza read with kasra on «إنْ» as conditional, and the others with fatḥa, as the maṣdarī that governs the subjunctive. As for the first reading, the apodosis in it is His saying «فتذكِّرُ», because Ḥamza, may Allah have mercy on him, reads «فَتُذَكِّرُ» with the kāf doubled and the rāʾ nominative, so it is sound that the fāʾ and what is in its scope be an apodosis; and he made the verb nominative because it is on the implication of a mubtadaʾ, i.e. «فهي تُذِكِّر». On this reading, does the clause of condition and consequence have a grammatical position or not? Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "Its position is nominative, as a ṣifa of «امرأتين»." It had been presented that His saying «مِمَّنْ تَرْضَوْن» is a ṣifa of His saying «فرجلٌ وامرأتان». The Shaykh said: "So it becomes like «جاءني رجلٌ وامرأتان عقلاءُ حُبْلَيَان», and in the permissibility of such a construction there is something to examine; rather what analogies require is putting «حُبْلَيَان» before «عقلاء». But if it is said that «ممَّنْ تَرْضَوْن» is a badal of «رجالكم» or attached to «استشهدوا», it becomes impossible to make it a ṣifa of «امرأتين», since that would necessitate separation between the ṣifa and the described by a foreigner." I say: Ibn ʿAṭiyya did not invent this i'rab; rather al-Wāḥidī preceded him to it, for he said: "The position of the condition and its apodosis is nominative as they are a description of the two mentioned, namely «امرأتان» in His saying «فرجلٌ وامرأتان», because condition and consequence can be used to describe, as they are used as ṣila in His saying {الذين إِنْ مَّكَّنَّاهُمْ فِي الأرض أَقَامُواْ الصلاة} [al-Ḥajj: 41]." [Translator's note: the source gives [الحجر: 41]; the verse {الَّذِينَ إِن مَّكَّنَّاهُمْ فِي الْأَرْضِ} is in al-Ḥajj 41.]
The apparent is that this conditional clause is resumptive, to announce this ruling, and is an answer to an implied question, as though someone asked: what is the matter that two women were made equal to a man? and it was answered by this clause.
As for the second reading, «أَنْ» in it is maṣdarī and governs the subjunctive after it, and the fatḥa in it is a vowel of declension, unlike in Ḥamza's reading, where it is the fatḥa of the meeting of two quiescents, since the first lām is quiescent for assimilation into the second and the second quiescent for the jussive, and assimilation into a quiescent is impossible, so we gave the second a fatḥa to escape their meeting, and the vowel was fatḥa because it is the lightest of vowels. «أَنْ» and what is within its scope is in the position of an accusative or genitive after the omission of the preposition, which is the lām of cause, the implied being «لأنْ تَضِلَّ» or «إرادةَ أَنْ تَضِلَّ».
Regarding what this preposition is attached to, there are three aspects. One: an implied verb indicated by the preceding discourse, the implied being "call a man and two women as witnesses so that one of them may err", the verb being indicated by His saying {فَإِن لَّمْ يَكُونَا رَجُلَيْنِ فَرَجُلٌ وامرأتان}; al-Wāḥidī said this, and there is no need of it, because what makes «رجل وامرأتين» nominative suffices without implying something else, and likewise the implied khabar of your saying «فرجلٌ وامرأتان», for the implied of the first is «فَلْيَشْهد رجلٌ», and of the second «فرجلٌ وامرأتان يشهدون لأَنْ تَضِلَّ»; these two implications are the second and third aspects of the three mentioned.
Here there is an obvious question that the muʿribīn and the exegetes habitually ask: how is the error of one of them made a reason for seeking witnesses, or the thing willed by Allah the Exalted, according to the two implications mentioned first? Sībawayh and others answered that error, since it is the cause of reminding, and reminding is caused by it, and they place each of cause and effect in the position of the other because of their interconnection, so willing the error from which the reminding results is willing the reminding. It is as though it were said: "in order that one of them remind the other if she errs." Its parallel is their saying: «أَعْدَدْتُ الخشبةَ أَنْ يميلَ الحائطُ فأدعمَه» (I prepared the beam in case the wall leans so that I support it) and «أعدْدتُ السلاحَ ان يجيءَ عدوٌ فأدفعَه» (I prepared the weapon in case an enemy comes so that I repel him). Your preparing the beam is not for the wall to lean, nor your preparing the weapon for an enemy to come; they are only for propping when it leans and for repelling when the enemy comes. This is among the things for which one returns to the meaning and abandons the side of the wording.
Al-Jurjānī held regarding this verse that the implied is «مخافةَ أَنْ تَضِلَّ» (for fear that she err), and he recited the saying of ʿAmr:
1125 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... فَعَجَّلْنا القِرى أَنْ تَشْتِمُونا
(...so we hastened the hospitality, lest you revile us.)
that is, «مخافَةَ أَنْ تَشْتِمونا». And this is correct if one limited oneself to it, without His saying «فَتُذَكِّرَ» being conjoined to it, since the implied would then be "call a man and two women as witnesses for fear that one of them err"; but the conjoining of His saying «فتذكِّر» spoils it, since the implied becomes "for fear that one of them remind the other", and the reminding of one by the other is not something feared, but is the intended. Abū Jaʿfar said: "I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān relate from Abū al-ʿAbbās that the implied is «كراهةَ أَنْ تَضِلَّ» (dislike that she err)." Abū Jaʿfar said: "This is a mistake, since the meaning becomes: dislike that one of them remind the other." End.
Al-Farrāʾ went to something stranger than all this, claiming that the implied form of the noble verse is «كي تذكِّر إحداهما الأخرى إنْ ضَلَّت» (so that one of them remind the other if she err); when the consequent was put first it connected to what precedes it, and «أَنْ» was given fatḥa. He said: "Similar to it in speech is: «إنه ليعجبُني أَنْ يسألَ السائلُ فيُعْطى», whose meaning is «إنه ليعجبني أَن يُعْطَى السائلُ إن سَأَلَ», because what pleases is the giving, not the asking; so when they put the asking before the giving, they accompanied it with the fatḥa-vowelled «أَنْ» so that the meaning would be revealed." According to him, the «أنْ» in «أَنْ تَضِلَّ» is that of the consequent, except that it was put first and given fatḥa, its basic position being later.
The Basrans rejected this saying and rebutted it in the most forceful way. Al-Zajjāj said: "I do not know why, if the consequent is put first, and it is in its place and not in its place, it became obligatory to give fatḥa to «أن»." Al-Fārisī said: "What al-Farrāʾ mentioned is a claim with no proof, and analogy spoils it. Do we not find that a governing particle, when its vowel changes, does not entail a change in its governing or its meaning? That is what Abū al-Ḥasan related, the fatḥa on the prepositional lām with a noun, from Yūnus, Abū ʿUbayda and Khalaf al-Aḥmar; for just as this lām, when given fatḥa, suffered no change in its governing or its meaning, so the conditional «إنْ», when given fatḥa, should suffer no change in its governing or its meaning. What also makes it remote is that we find a governing particle's government does not change by preposing or postposing: do you not see that you say «مررتُ بزيدٍ», then you say «بزيد مررت», and the government of the bāʾ did not change by its being preposed from postposition?"
Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read «فَتُذْكِرَ» with the kāf light and the rāʾ accusative, from «أَذْكَرْتُه», i.e. I made him remember something after forgetting it, for what is meant here by error is forgetting, like His saying, the Exalted: {فَعَلْتُهَآ إِذاً وَأَنَاْ مِنَ الضالين} [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 20]. They recited the verse of al-Farazdaq:
1126 - ولقد ضَلَلْتَ أباكَ يَدْعُو دارمِاً ... كضلالِ ملتمسٍ طريقَ وِبارِ
(You lost your father when he called upon Dārim, like the loss of one seeking the way to Wabār.)
The hamza in «أَذْكَرْتُه» is for transfer and transitivity, and the verb before it is transitive to one, so another is needed; and there is only one object in the verse, so the omission of the second must be assumed, the implied being: "so that one remind the other of the testimony after her forgetting it, if she forgot it". This interpretation is the well-known.
Some anomalously said: "The meaning of «فَتُذْكِرَ إحداهما الأخرى» is: she makes her a male (dhakar), i.e. makes her ruling the ruling of the male in acceptance of testimony." Al-Aṣmaʿī narrated from Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ that he said: "«فَتُذَكِّر إحداهما الأخرى» with doubling is by way of reminding after forgetting, saying to her: 'Do you remember when we testified such-and-such on such a day in such a place against so-and-so?' And whoever read «فَتُذْكِرَ» with lightening said: when one woman testifies and then the other comes and testifies with her, she has made her male («أَذْكَرَتْها»), because the two of them stand in the position of a male." The exegetes and people of the language did not accept this from Abū ʿAmr; rather they did not deem the transmission of it from him sound, given their knowledge of his standing in learning, and they rejected it against its sayer for reasons, among them: that eloquence requires matching the error, by which forgetting is meant, with reminding and bringing to mind, and there is no fit in the matching with the transmitted meaning. Among them: that women, however many they reach, must have with them a man who testifies with them, so if that meaning were sound she would remind her by herself without a man joining; thus they said, though this should apply to what is accepted of a man with two women, otherwise we find women alone in testimonies with no man joined to them. Among them: that if she made her male, this should apply in all rulings, and not be limited to this one. And in this there is also something to examine, since the objection applies equally to them: for it may be said: if you interpret it as reminding after forgetting, it does not cover all rulings either, so what is answered with is also their answer.
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Among the innovations of exegeses is «فَتُذَكِّرَ» as 'she makes one of them the other a male', meaning that when the two are together they are in the position of a male." End. He did not make this saying specific to one reading over another.
As for the accusative of the rāʾ, it is conjoined to «أَنْ تَضِلَّ», because the two (Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr) read «أَنْ تَضِلَّ» with the governing «أَنْ». The others read with the kāf doubled, from «ذَكَّرْتُه», also meaning I made him remember; it has been presented that Ḥamza alone makes the rāʾ nominative.
From the two words together it emerges that the readers are on three levels: Ḥamza alone: «إنْ تَضِلَّ فتذكِّرُ», with kasra on «إنْ», kāf doubled and rāʾ nominative; Abū ʿAmr and Ibn Kathīr: with fatḥa on «أنْ», kāf light and rāʾ [accusative]; and the others likewise, except that they double the kāf.
The second object is also omitted in this reading as in the reading of Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr, and «فَعَّل» and «أَفْعَل» here have one sense, [like] «أَكْرَمْتُه» and «كَرَّمته», «فَرَّحته» and «أَفْرحته». They said: doubling in this word is more used than lightening, and on it is His saying:
1127 - على أنني بعدَ ما قد مضى ... ثلاثونَ للهَجْرِ حَوْلاً كميلا
يُذَكِّرُنِيك حنينُ العَجولِ ... ونَوْحُ الحمامةِ تَدعُو هَدِيلا
(Even though, after thirty full years of separation have passed, the yearning of the bereaved she-camel and the cooing of the dove calling Hadīl remind me of you.)
ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar and al-Jaḥdarī read «تُضَلَّ» in the passive, and from al-Jaḥdarī also «تُضِلَّ» with ḍamma on the tāʾ and kasra on the ḍād, from «أَضَلَّ كذا», i.e. he lost it, the object being omitted, i.e. «تُضِلَّ الشهادة» (she loses the testimony). Ḥumayd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān and Mujāhid read «فَتَذْكُرُ» with rāʾ nominative and kāf light, and Zayd ibn Aslam «فتُذاكِرُ», from «المذاكرة» (mutual recollection).
His saying: {إِحْدَاهُمَا} is the agent and «والأخرى» the object, and this is among the cases where the agent must come first owing to the concealment of the declension and the meaning, such as «ضَرَب موسى عيسى». Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "«إحداهما» is the agent and «الأخرى» the object, and the reverse is sound too, except that it is barred on the apparent statement of the grammarians regarding declension, because when the declension does not show in the agent and the object, it is obligatory to put the agent first [in cases] where confusion is feared; so, on this, when confusion is safe, putting the object first is permissible, as in your saying «كسر العصا موسى». This verse is of this kind, because forgetting and reminding are not determined in either one of them but this is left indefinite, and it is known from His saying «فَتُذَكِّرَ» that the one who reminds is the one who remembers and the one who is reminded is the one who forgets, just as from the word «كَسَر» it is known who can do the breaking; so on this it is permissible to make «إحداهما» the agent and «الأخرى» the object, and to reverse it." End.
Since He left the agent indefinite in His saying {أَن تَضِلَّ إْحْدَاهُمَا}, He left it indefinite also in His saying «فَتُذَكِّر إحداهما», because each of the two women may undergo what may befall her companion, of erring and reminding; and the meaning is: if this one errs, that one reminds her, so the sense of generality entered the discourse. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "If it is said: why was it not said «فتذكِّرها الأخرى»? It is said there are two aspects. One: he repeated the overt noun to indicate the indefiniteness in remembering and forgetting; had he used the pronoun, its reference to the mentioned would be determined. The second: he put the overt noun in the place of the pronoun, the implied being «فتذكِّرها»; and this indicates that the second «إحداهما» is a fronted object and cannot be an agent in this aspect, because the pronoun is the overt noun itself, and the first overt noun is the agent of «تضِلَّ»; so if the pronoun were made to refer to that overt noun, the forgetting one would be the reminding one, which is impossible." I say: it may come to mind, before reflection, that the two aspects return to one, because his saying "he repeated the overt noun" is close to his saying "he put the overt noun in the place of the pronoun".
«إحدى» is the feminine of «الواحد». Al-Fārisī said: "They made it feminine on a non-corresponding form"; and there is something to examine in this: rather it is the feminine of «أَحَد», and for that reason they match it with it in «أحد عشرَ» and «إحدى عَشَرَة», [and] «واحدٍ وعشرين» and «إحدى وعشرين». «إحدى» takes the plural «إحَد», like «كِسْرَة» and «كِسَر». Abū al-ʿAbbās said: "They made the alif in «الإحدى» like the tāʾ in «الكِسْرة», so they said in its plural «إحَد» as they said «كَسْرة» and «كِسَر», as they made it like it in «الكُبْرَى» and «الكُبَر», «العُلْيا» and «العُلى»; and as they made these like «ظُلْمة» and «ظُلَم», they made the first like «سِدْرَة» and «سِدَر»." He said: "And as they made the short alif like the tāʾ in what was mentioned, they made the extended one also like it in their saying «قاصِعَاء» and «قواصِع», and «دامّاء» and «دوامّ»", meaning that «فاعِلَة», such as «ضارِبَة», takes the plural «ضوارب», and likewise «فاعِلاء», such as «قاصِعاء» and «راهِطاء», takes the plural «فَواعِل». Ibn al-Aʿrābī recited, for «إحدى» and «إحَد», the saying of the poet:
1128 - حتى استثاروا بيَ إحدى الإِحَدِ ... ليثاً هِزَبْراً ذا سلاحٍ مُعْتَدي
(Until they roused against me the one of ones, a lion, a fierce one, armed and aggressive.)
He said: one says «هو إحدى الإِحَدِ» and «أَحَدُ الأَحَدَيْنِ» and «واحدُ الآحادِ», as one says «واحدٌ لا مِثْلَ له», and he recited the verse.
Know that «إحدى» is used only annexed to something else, so one says «إحدى الإِحَدِ» and «إحداهما», and does not say «جاءَتْني إحدى» or «رأيت إحدى»; this is unlike its masculine.
«الأُخْرى» is the feminine of «آخَر», which is the elative («أَفْعَلُ التفضيلِ»), and it may mean «آخِرة» (last), like His saying, the Exalted: {قَالَتْ أُخْرَاهُمْ لأُولاَهُمْ} [al-Aʿrāf: 38]; each of them takes the plural «أُخَر», but the plural of the first is a diptote, and about its reason there is disagreement, while the plural of the second is triptote, and there is a difference between them in meaning. All this I shall clarify, if Allah the Exalted wills, in al-Aʿrāf, for it is more suited to it.
His saying: {وَلاَ يَأْبَ الشهدآء}: its object is omitted for the meaning is understood, i.e. "they shall not refuse to give testimony". It is said: the omitted is a genitive phrase, because «أبى» means "refused", so it is made transitive like it, i.e. "from giving testimony".
{إِذَا مَا دُعُواْ} is an adverbial for «يَأْبَ», i.e. "they shall not refuse at the time of their being called to deliver it or to give it". It may be purely adverbial, and may be conditional with an omitted apodosis, i.e. "when they are called, let them not refuse".
His saying: {أَن تَكْتُبُوهُ} is a mafʿūl bihi and what governs it is «تَسْأَموا», because it is transitive by itself. He said:
1129 - سَئِمْتُ تكاليفَ الحياةِ ومَنْ يَعِشْ ... ثمانينَ حَوْلاً لا أبا لَكَ يَسْأَمِ
(I am weary of life's burdens; and whoever lives eighty years – with no father for you [an exclamation] – grows weary.)
It is said: rather it is transitive by a preposition, the original being «مِنْ أَنْ تكتبُوه», and the preposition was omitted because it is known, so the well-known disagreement about «أَنْ» after the omission applies. What indicates its transitivity by «مِنْ» is the saying:
1130 - ولقد سَئِمْتُ من الحياةِ وطولِها ... وسؤالِ هذا الناسِ كيف لبيدُ
(I have grown weary of life and its length, and of this people's asking, "How is Labīd?")
«السَّأَم» and «السَّآمَةُ»: weariness of something and vexation with it.
The hāʾ in «تَكْتبوه» may refer to the debt at the beginning of the verse, and may refer to «الحق» in His saying «فإنْ كان الذي عليه الحقُّ», which is the nearest mentioned, what is meant by it being «الدَّيْن». It is also said: it refers to the document understood from «يَكْتبوه»; al-Zamakhsharī said this.
«صغيراً أو كبيراً» is a ḥāl, i.e. whatever the state of the debt, small or large, and whatever the state of the document, brief or full. Al-Sajāwandī allowed it to be accusative as the khabar of an implied «كان», and there is no need calling for this, nor is it one of the places where it is implied.
Al-Sulamī read {ولا يَسْأَموا أَنْ يَكْتبوه} with the yāʾ of the third person in both. The agent on this reading is the pronoun of the witnesses, and it may be a case of iltifāt, so it refers back either to the parties to the transaction or to the scribes.
His saying: {إلى أَجَلِهِ} may have three aspects. The most apparent: that it is attached to an omitted element, i.e. "that you write it as established in the liability until the term of its falling due". The second: that it is attached to «تكتبُوه»; Abū al-Baqāʾ said this. The Shaykh rejected it, saying: "It is attached to an omitted element, not to «تكتبوه», because the writing does not continue until the term of the debt, since it ends in a short time; so it is not like «سرت إلى الكوفةِ» (I travelled to Kufa)." The third: that it is attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl from the hāʾ; Abū al-Baqāʾ said this.
His saying: {ذَلِكُمْ}: the demonstrative points to the nearest mentioned, which is the writing. It is said: to it and to calling witnesses; it is said: to all that was mentioned, and this is the best. «أَقْسَطُ»: it is said to be from «أَقْسَطَ» when one acts justly, and not from «قسَطَ», because «قَسَط» means "acted unjustly" while «أَقْسَط» means "acted justly", so the hamza is for privation (salb); but this entails forming «أَفْعَل» (elative) from a quadriliteral, which is anomalous.
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: from what are the two elatives («أَقْسَط» and «أَقْوَم») formed? I say: according to the position of Sībawayh it is permissible that they be formed from «أقسط» and «أقام», and that «أَقْسَط» be from «قاسِط» in the manner of relation (nisba), meaning 'possessing equity' (dhī qisṭ), and «أقوم» from «قويم»." The Shaykh said: "Sībawayh did not state explicitly that the elative is formed from «أَفْعل»; that is taken only by inference, for he stated at the beginning of his book that «أَفْعَل» of wonder is formed from «فَعَل», «فَعِل», «فَعُل» and «أَفْعَل», and the apparent of this is that «أَفْعَل» of wonder is the one from which the elative is built; so what is analogical in wonder is analogical in the elative, and what is anomalous in it is anomalous in it. The grammarians disagreed on the formation of wonder and the elative from «أَفْعَل» in three positions: permissible absolutely, forbidden absolutely, and distinction between the hamza being for transfer, in which case it is barred, or not, in which case it is permitted, and Sībawayh's words are interpreted accordingly, where he said 'it is formed from «أَفْعَل»', i.e. the one whose hamza is not for transitivity. And whoever forbade it absolutely said: Sībawayh did not say «وأَفْعَلَ» in the past-tense form, he said it only as «أَفْعِل» in the imperative form, and it was confused for the hearer, meaning that the verb of wonder is on «أَفْعِلْ», formed from «فَعَل», «فَعِل» and «فعُل», and on «أفعِل». These positions have a place more suited to their discussion."
Ibn ʿAṭiyya reported that it is taken from «قَسُط» with ḍamma on the sīn, like «أَكْرَمَ» from «كَرُم». It is said: it is from «القِسْط» with kasra, which is justice, being a maṣdar from which no verb is derived, and it is not from «الإقساط», because «أفعل» is not built from «الإفعال». All that I said is built by them on the premise that the triliteral means injustice and the quadriliteral means justice.
It is related that when the tyrant [al-Ḥajjāj] ibn Yūsuf asked Saʿīd ibn Jubayr: "What do you say about me?", he said: "I say that you are a qāsiṭ and ʿādil," and only [al-Ḥajjāj] understood him, saying: "He has made me unjust and an unbeliever", and recited His saying, the Exalted: {وَأَمَّا القاسطون فَكَانُواْ لِجَهَنَّمَ حَطَباً} [al-Jinn: 15] and {ثْمَّ الذين كَفَرُواْ بِرَبِّهِمْ يَعْدِلُونَ} [al-Anʿām: 1].
But if we make it common to «عَدَلَ» and «جارَ», the matter is clear. Ibn al-Qaṭṭāʿ said: "«قَسَط» قُسوطاً وقِسْطاً: acted unjustly and acted justly, the two being opposites." Ibn al-Sīd related in his book «al-Iqtiḍāb» from Ibn al-Sikkīt in his book «al-Aḍdād» from Abū ʿUbayda: "«قَسَط» means acted unjustly, and «قَسَط» means acted justly, while «أَقْسطَ» with alif means only acted justly." Abū al-Qāsim al-Rāghib al-Aṣfahānī said: "«القِسْطُ» is to take another's share, and that is injustice; «الإقساطُ» is to give another's share, and that is fairness; therefore one says «قَسَط» when one acted unjustly, and «أَقْسَط» when one acted justly." More explanation of this too will come in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ, if Allah the Exalted wills.
«عند الله» is an adverbial accusative governed by «أَقْسَط», i.e. in His judgement. His saying «وَأَقْوَمُ»: the wāw remains sound in it only because it is an elative, and the elative remains sound by analogy with the verb of wonder, and the verb of wonder remains sound because it runs the course of nouns, being fixed and non-inflecting.
«أَقْوَمُ» may be from the transitive quadriliteral «أقام», but he omitted the extra hamza and then brought the hamza of «أَفْعل», like His saying, the Exalted: {أَيُّ الحِزْبَيْنِ أحصى} [al-Kahf: 12]; the meaning would then be: "more firm for your establishing the testimony". It may also be from the intransitive «قام», and the meaning: "that is firmer for the testimony to stand", and «قامَتِ الشهادةُ» means the testimony was established; Abū al-Baqāʾ said this.
His saying «للشهادةِ» is attached to «أَقْوَم», and it is an object in meaning, the lām being redundant; its omission and putting its genitive noun in the accusative after an elative is not permissible except by necessity, like the saying:
1131 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... وأضْرَبَ منا بالسيوفِ القَوانِسا
(...and more striking than we with swords at helmet-tops.)
It has been said that «القوانسَ» is accusative by an implied verb indicated by the elative; this is the meaning of the Shaykh's words, and it proceeds on the basis that «أَقْوَم» is from the transitive «أقام»; but if you make it from «قَام» meaning "was firm", the lām is not redundant.
His saying: {أَلاَّ ترتابوا}, i.e. "nearer"; the preposition is omitted. It is said to be the lām, i.e. "nearer in order that you not doubt"; it is said to be «إلى»; it is said to be «من», i.e. "nearer to not being in doubt" and "nearer than not being in doubt". In their implying «مِنْ» there is something to examine, since the meaning does not support it. «ترْتابوا» is of the pattern «تَفْتَعِلُوا» from «الرِّيبة»; the origin is «تَرْتَيِبوا», and the yāʾ was turned into alif because it is vowelled and what precedes it has fatḥa. The thing compared with is omitted since the meaning is understood, i.e. "more equitable, firmer and nearer to such-and-such than the absence of writing"; and the omission is made fine by the elative being the khabar of a mubtadaʾ, unlike its being a ṣifa or ḥāl. Al-Sulamī read {أَنْ لا يرتابوا} with the yāʾ of the third person, like the reading {ولا يَسْأموا أَنْ يكتبوه}, and the justification of that was presented.
His saying: {إِلاَّ أَن تَكُونَ تِجَارَةً}: regarding this exception there are two views. One: that it is connected (muttaṣil). Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "The excepted clause is in the position of an accusative, because it is an exception from the same class, as He commanded calling witnesses in every transaction, and excepted from it the present trade; the implied is: except in the state of the trade being present." The second: that it is disconnected (munqaṭiʿ). Makkī ibn Abī Ṭālib said: "«أَنْ» is in the position of an accusative as a disconnected exception." I say: this is the apparent, as though it were said: "but as for the present trade, it is permissible to dispense with calling witnesses and writing in it."
ʿĀṣim read here «تجارةً» in the accusative, and likewise «حاضرةً» because it is its ṣifa; in al-Nisāʾ the two Kufan readers (Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī) agreed with him, and the others read the nominative in both. The nominative has two aspects. One: that it is the complete «كان», i.e. "unless a trade occurs or takes place"; on this «تُديرونها» is in the position of a nominative as ṣifa of «تجارةً» as well, and it came here in the eloquent manner, since he put the explicit description before the interpreted one.
The second: that it is the incomplete, its ism being «تجارةٌ» and the khabar being the clause «تُديرونها», as though it were said "unless a present trade be carried on among you", and the description made the indefinite ism of «كان» permissible; this is the position of al-Farrāʾ, followed by others.
As for ʿĀṣim's reading, its ism is a latent pronoun: it was said its implied form is "unless the dealing, or the sale, or the trade be...". Al-Zajjāj implied "unless the debt-dealing (mudāyana) be...", which is the best. Al-Fārisī said: "It is not permissible that «التداين» be the ism of «كان», because «التداين» is a concept (maʿnā), and the present trade is meant as a concrete thing (ʿayn), and the rule for the ism is that it be the khabar in meaning; and debt-dealing is a right in the liability of the debtor, to which the creditor may lay claim, and when so, it cannot be the ism of «كان», owing to the difference between debt-dealing and the present trade." What al-Fārisī said does not appear a refutation of Abū Isḥāq, because «التجارة» is also a maṣdar, so it is a concept among concepts, not a concrete among concretes; and between al-Fārisī and al-Zajjāj there was a dialogue about some matter.
Al-Fārisī also said: "Nor is it permissible that its ism be «الحقُّ» in His saying «فإن كان الذي عليه الحق», for the meaning we mentioned regarding debt-dealing, because that right is a debt. And when this is not permissible, the ism of «كان» cannot be other than one of two things. One: that these matters which required calling witnesses and taking pledges have had mutual sale understood from their import, so he implied the mutual sale because the situation indicates it, as it was implied on the indication of the situation in what Sībawayh related: «إذا كان غداً فأتني» (when it is tomorrow, come to me); and on this the following is recited:
1132 - أعينيَّ هَلاَّ تبكِيان عِفاقا ... إذا كان طَعْناً بينهم وعِناقا
(O my two eyes, why do you not weep for ʿIfāq, when there is spearing and embracing between them?)
that is, «إذا كان الأمر». The second: that he implied the trade, as though it were said: «إلا أن تكونَ التجارةُ تجارةً», and similar is what al-Farrāʾ recited:
1133 - فَدىً لبني ذُهْلِ بن شيبانَ ناقتي ... إذا كان يوماً ذا كواكبَ أَشْهَبَا
(May my she-camel be a ransom for the Banū Dhuhl ibn Shaybān when it is a day with stars [of dust], ashen-grey.)
and al-Zamakhsharī recited:
1134 - بني أسدٍ هل تَعْلَمُون بلاءنا ... إذا كان يوماً ذا كواكبَ أَشْنَعا
(O Banū Asad, do you know our trial when it is a day with stars, a most dreadful one?)
that is, «إذا كان اليومُ يوماً». And «بينكم» is an adverbial for «تُديرونها».
His saying: {فَلَيْسَ}: Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "The fāʾ entered «فليس» to signal that what follows is connected to what precedes." I say: it conjoins this clause to the clause beginning at {إِلاَّ أَن تَكُونَ تِجَارَةً} up to its end, and the causality in it is clear, i.e. because of that the blame was lifted in not writing.
And His saying {أَلاَّ تَكْتُبُوهَا}, i.e. «في أن لا»; the preposition was omitted, so the two aspects remain in the position of «أَنْ».
His saying: {إِذَا تَبَايَعْتُم} may be conditional, its apodosis either preceding it, according to some, or omitted because what precedes indicates it, the implied being «إذا تبايَعْتُم فَأَشْهِدوا»; and it may be purely adverbial, i.e. "perform the testimony at the time of mutual sale".
His saying: {وَلاَ يُضَآرَّ}: the common people read with fatḥa on the rāʾ as a jussive, and «لا» is prohibitive, and the verb has fatḥa as presented in Ḥamza's reading «إن تَضِلَّ».
This verb may be active, the origin being «يضارِرْ» with kasra on the first rāʾ, so «كاتب» and «شهيد» would be agents, forbidden from harming the one for whom writing is done and the one for whom testimony is given: the scribe is forbidden to add a letter by which he nullifies a right, or to remove one, and the witness forbidden to conceal the testimony. Al-Zajjāj chose this and preferred it, because Allah the Exalted said {فَإِنَّهُ فُسُوقٌ بِكُمْ}, and there is no doubt that this on the part of the scribe and witness is wickedness (fisq), whereas it would not be fitting for the pressing of the scribe and witness and importuning them to be wickedness. This meaning is transmitted in exegesis from Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid and Ṭāwūs. Al-Dānī reported from ʿUmar, Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid and Ibn Abī Isḥāq that they read the first rāʾ with kasra when they unpacked it.
It may be that the verb is passive, the meaning being that no one should harm the scribe or the witness; this was preferred because if the prohibition were directed to the scribe and the witness, He would have said "and if the two do, it is wickedness in you two", and because the context from the start of the verses is concerned only with the one for whom writing is done and the one for whom testimony is given. This meaning is also transmitted in exegesis from Ibn ʿAbbās and those mentioned with him. Al-Dānī also mentioned from them that they read the first rāʾ with fatḥa. I say: there is nothing strange in this, since the verse is to them open to both aspects; they interpreted and read it in this sense at one time and in the other at another.
Abū Jaʿfar and ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd read «ولا يُضارّ» with the rāʾ doubled and quiescent in connected speech; there is weakness in it in that three quiescents are combined, but since the alif is a letter of prolongation, its prolongation stood in the place of a vowel, and the meeting of two quiescents is tolerated in pause, then waṣl was treated as waqf in that.
ʿIkrima read «ولا يُضارِرْ كاتباً ولا شهيداً» with unpacking and kasra on the first rāʾ, the agent being the pronoun of the owner of the right, and «كاتباً» and «شهيداً» accusative as objects, i.e. "let the owner of a right not harm a scribe or a witness, by compelling and pressing him to write and testify, or by making him do what is not permissible."
Ibn Muḥayṣin read «ولا يُضارُّ» with the rāʾ nominative, which is a negation, so the report has the sense of prohibition, like His saying {فَلاَ رَفَثَ وَلاَ فُسُوقْ} [al-Baqara: 197]. ʿIkrima, in the transmission of Miqsam, read «ولا يُضارِّ» with kasra on the doubled rāʾ, according to the basic rule for the meeting of two quiescents. The investigation of these matters was presented to you at His saying {لاَ تُضَآرَّ وَالِدَةٌ بِوَلَدِهَا} [al-Baqara: 233].
His saying: {وَإِن تَفْعَلُواْ}, i.e. "you do any of what Allah forbade", so the mafʿūl bihi is omitted because it is known. The pronoun in «فإنه» refers back to the refusal or the harming. «بكم» is attached to an omitted element, which Abū al-Baqāʾ implied as «لاحِقٌ بكم» (attached to you); it should be implied as general existence, since it is a ṣifa of «فسوق», i.e. "wickedness established in you", that is, adhering to you and cleaving to you.
His saying: {وَيُعَلِّمُكُمُ الله}: this clause may be resumptive – which is the apparent – and may be a ḥāl from the agent in «اتَّقوا». Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "Its implied form is «واتقوا اللهَ مضموناً لكم التعليمُ أَو الهدايةُ» (fear Allah, with teaching or guidance guaranteed to you), and it may be an anticipated ḥāl." I say: in these two aspects there is something to examine, because an affirmative imperfect is not directly joined by the circumstantial wāw, and if something appears to be so it is interpreted; but no necessity calls for that here.

ukberi-tibyan:24-24.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَإِنْ لَمْ تَفْعَلُوا وَلَنْ تَفْعَلُوا فَاتَّقُوا النَّارَ الَّتِي وَقُودُهَا النَّاسُ وَالْحِجَارَةُ أُعِدَّتْ لِلْكَافِرِينَ (٢٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَإِنْ لَمْ تَفْعَلُوا): the jussive (jazm) is caused by لم, not by إن, because ((لم)) is an operator very closely joined to what it governs, and it occurs only with a verb that is imperfect in form, whereas إن has entered on a verb that is past in form, and a noun has followed it directly, as in His saying, Exalted is He: (وَإِنْ أَحَدٌ مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ).
(وَقُودُهَا النَّاسُ): the majority read it with fatḥa on the wāw, and it means firewood; it has also been read with ḍamma, which is a dialectal variant for firewood. The better view is that it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) meaning "burning", and that there is an omitted muḍāf in the speech, its implied form being: "its burning is the burning of people", or "the blazing of people", or "possessed of that whose fuel is people".
(أُعِدَّتْ): a clause in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from النار, and its operator is فاتقوا.
It is not permissible for it to be a ḥāl from the pronoun in «وقودها» for three reasons: first, that it is a muḍāf ilayhi; second, that firewood does not govern a ḥāl; third, that you would be separating the maṣdar, or what operates like it, from what it governs by the khabar (predicate), which is الناس.

ukberi-tibyan:25-25.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَبَشِّرِ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ أَنَّ لَهُمْ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ كُلَّمَا رُزِقُوا مِنْهَا مِنْ ثَمَرَةٍ رِزْقًا قَالُوا هَذَا الَّذِي رُزِقْنَا مِنْ قَبْلُ وَأُتُوا بِهِ مُتَشَابِهًا وَلَهُمْ فِيهَا أَزْوَاجٌ مُطَهَّرَةٌ وَهُمْ فِيهَا خَالِدُونَ (٢٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَنَّ لَهُمْ جَنَّاتٍ): (أنّ) takes fatḥa here because the implied form is بأنّ لهم ("that they have"), and the position of أنّ together with what it governs is accusative (naṣb) by بشّر, because when the preposition is omitted the verb reaches [its object] by itself. This is the doctrine of Sībawayh.
Al-Khalīl allowed it to be in the position of the genitive (jarr) by the omitted bāʾ, because this is a position in which it is added, so it is as if it were pronounced. That is not permissible with anything other than أنّ: if you said بشّره بأنه مخلّد في الجنة ("give him the glad tidings that he will be immortal in Paradise"), omitting the bāʾ would be permissible because of the length of the speech, but if you said بشّره الخلودَ it would not be permissible. This is a principle that recurs very often in the Qur'an, so reflect on it and look for it here. (تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ): the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ṣifa (adjective) of الجنات, and الأنهار is nominative by (تجري), not by being a mubtadaʾ (subject) with من تحتها as the khabar (predicate), nor by تحتها, because تجري contains no pronoun, since the gardens do not flow; only their rivers flow. The implied form is "from beneath its trees", not "from beneath its ground", and the muḍāf was omitted.
If it were said that الجنة is the trees themselves, so that there is no omission in the speech, that would be a valid view.
(كُلَّمَا رُزِقُوا مِنْهَا...) up to His saying (مِنْ قَبْلُ) is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الذين آمنوا, its implied form being: "continually provided for". It may also be a ḥāl from الجنات, because they have been described and the clause contains a pronoun referring back to them, namely His saying: منها. (رُزِقْنَا مِنْ قَبْلُ): that is, رُزِقناه ("we were provided with it"), and the referring pronoun (ʿāʾid) was omitted. قبلُ is indeclinable (mabnī) because it is cut off from the iḍāfa, since the implied form is من قبلِ هذا ("before this").
(وَأُتُوا بِهِ): it may be a ḥāl, with قد intended along with it, its implied form being: "they said that, and they had been given it". It may also be resumptive. And (مُتَشَابِهًا) is a ḥāl from the hāʾ in به. (وَلَهُمْ فِيهَا أَزْوَاجٌ): أزواج is the mubtadaʾ, لهم is the khabar, and فيها is an adverbial (ẓarf) of the [implied] istiqrār ("being settled"). فيها cannot be the khabar, because the benefit [of the statement] would be diminished, since the benefit lies in making the spouses theirs. The second (فيها) is attached to «خالدون». These two clauses are resumptive. The second may also be a ḥāl from the hāʾ and mīm in لهم, its operator being the meaning of istiqrār.

ukberi-tibyan:26-26.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَسْتَحْيِي أَنْ يَضْرِبَ مَثَلًا مَا بَعُوضَةً فَمَا فَوْقَهَا فَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا فَيَعْلَمُونَ أَنَّهُ الْحَقُّ مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ وَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا فَيَقُولُونَ مَاذَا أَرَادَ اللَّهُ بِهَذَا مَثَلًا يُضِلُّ بِهِ كَثِيرًا وَيَهْدِي بِهِ كَثِيرًا وَمَا يُضِلُّ بِهِ إِلَّا الْفَاسِقِينَ (٢٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لَا يَسْتَحْيِي): its pattern is يستفعل; no verb from it is used without the sīn, and its meaning is not that of seeking [as the istafʿala pattern often implies]. Its second and third radicals (ʿayn and lām) are both yāʾ, and its root is الحياء ("modesty"); the hamza of الحياء replaces a yāʾ.
In an irregular (shādhdh) reading it was read يستحي, with a single yāʾ; the omitted one is the lām, as it is omitted in the jussive, and on this reading its pattern is يستفِع, except that the yāʾ had its vowel transferred to the ʿayn and became quiescent. It has also been said that the omitted letter is the ʿayn, but that is far-fetched. (أَنْ يَضْرِبَ): that is, من أن يضرب; so its position is accusative according to Sībawayh and genitive according to al-Khalīl.
(مَا): a redundant (zāʾida) particle for emphasis, and «بعوضة» is a badal (substitute) from مثلا.
It has also been said: (ما) is an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective (nakira mawṣūfa), and بعوضة is a badal from ما.
It is read irregularly as بعوضةٌ, in the nominative, on the basis that ما is taken in the sense of الذي and the mubtadaʾ is omitted, i.e. "that which is a gnat". It is also possible that ما is a particle and the mubtadaʾ is implied, its implied form being: "a parable, it being a gnat". (فَمَا فَوْقَهَا): the fāʾ is for conjunction, and ما is an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective or equivalent to الذي; the operator in فوق on both views is the [implied] istiqrār, and what it is conjoined to is بعوضة.
(أَمَّا): a particle standing in for the conditional particle and the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). It is mentioned to detail what was stated in summary; the noun after it occurs as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the fāʾ is obligatory on its khabar (predicate). The original form is مهما يكن من شيء فالذين آمنوا يعلمون ("whatever the case may be, those who believe know"); but since أمّا stands in for the conditional particle, they disliked placing the fāʾ directly after it, so they deferred it to the khabar, and the mention of the mubtadaʾ after it became a compensation for pronouncing the protasis. (مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ): in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). The implied form is: "that it is established" or "settled from their Lord", and the operator is the meaning of الحق; the one to whom the ḥāl refers is the latent (mustatir) pronoun in it. (مَاذَا): there are two views on it. First: that «ما» is an interrogative noun whose position is nominative as a mubtadaʾ, ذا is in the sense of الذي, and أراد is its ṣila (relative clause), the referring pronoun being omitted; الذي with its ṣila is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ.
Second: that ما and ذا form a single interrogative noun whose position is accusative by (أراد), with no pronoun in the verb; the implied form is: "what thing did Allah intend?". (مَثَلًا): a tamyīz (specification), i.e. "in terms of a parable". It may also be a ḥāl from هذا, i.e. "being presented as a parable" (mutamaththilan), or "being cited as a parable" (mutamaththalan bihi), in which case it is a ḥāl from the name of Allah. (يُضِلُّ): it may be in the position of the accusative as a ṣifa (adjective) of المثل; it may be a ḥāl from the name of Allah; and it may be resumptive. (إِلَّا الْفَاسِقِينَ): the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of يضل, and it is not accusative as an excepted noun, because يضل had not taken its object before إلا.

ukberi-tibyan:27-27.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (الَّذِينَ يَنْقُضُونَ عَهْدَ اللَّهِ مِنْ بَعْدِ مِيثَاقِهِ وَيَقْطَعُونَ مَا أَمَرَ اللَّهُ بِهِ أَنْ يُوصَلَ وَيُفْسِدُونَ فِي الْأَرْضِ أُولَئِكَ هُمُ الْخَاسِرُونَ (٢٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (الَّذِينَ يَنْقُضُونَ): in the position of the accusative as a ṣifa (adjective) of الفاسقين.
It may also be accusative by an implied أعني ("I mean"), or nominative as a khabar (predicate), i.e. "they are those who".
It may also be a mubtadaʾ (subject), with the khabar being His saying: أولئك هم الخاسرون.
(مِنْ بَعْدِ): من is for the beginning of the extent of time, according to the view of those who allow that, and redundant (zāʾida) according to the view of those who do not allow it; but this is problematic on the latter's own principle, because he does not allow من to be redundant in an affirmative statement.
(مِيثَاقِهِ): a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the sense of الإيثاق ("binding by covenant"). The hāʾ refers to the name of Allah or to العهد. If you refer it to the name of Allah, the maṣdar is annexed to its agent; if you refer it to العهد, it is annexed to its object.
(مَا أَمَرَ): ما is in the sense of الذي, and it may also be an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective. «أن يوصل» is in the position of the genitive as a badal (substitute) from the hāʾ, i.e. "[commanded] its being joined". It may also be a badal from ما, a badal of inclusion (badal al-ishtimāl), its implied form being: "and they sever the joining of what Allah commanded".
It may also be in the position of the nominative, i.e. "it is that it be joined".
(أُولَئِكَ) is a mubtadaʾ; «هم» is a second mubtadaʾ or a separating pronoun (faṣl), and «الخاسرون» is the khabar.

ukberi-tibyan:28-28.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (كَيْفَ تَكْفُرُونَ بِاللَّهِ وَكُنْتُمْ أَمْوَاتًا فَأَحْيَاكُمْ ثُمَّ يُمِيتُكُمْ ثُمَّ يُحْيِيكُمْ ثُمَّ إِلَيْهِ تُرْجَعُونَ) ((٢٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (كَيْفَ تَكْفُرُونَ بِاللَّهِ): كيف is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and the operator in it is تكفرون; the one to whom the ḥāl refers is the pronoun in «تكفرون», and the like. [Translator's note: the Arabic reads «والعامل في تكفرون», apparently for «والعامل فيه تكفرون»; translated according to the evident sense.] And (تكفرون) is made transitive by a preposition, but it has been made transitive by itself in His saying: (أَلَا إِنَّ عَادًا كَفَرُوا رَبَّهُمْ); that is construed according to the meaning, since the meaning is "they denied". (وَكُنْتُمْ): «قد» is implied along with it, and the clause is a ḥāl.
(ثُمَّ إِلَيْهِ): the hāʾ is the pronoun of the name of Allah. It may also be the pronoun of the giving of life, indicated by His saying: فأحياكم.

ukberi-tibyan:29-29.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (هُوَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ لَكُمْ مَا فِي الْأَرْضِ جَمِيعًا ثُمَّ اسْتَوَى إِلَى السَّمَاءِ فَسَوَّاهُنَّ سَبْعَ سَمَوَاتٍ وَهُوَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ) (٢٩).
His saying, Exalted is He: (جَمِيعًا): a ḥāl (circumstantial) in the sense of مجتمعا ("all together"). (فَسَوَّاهُنَّ): the pronoun is plural only because السماء is the plural of سماوة; the wāw in it was changed to hamza because it occurred word-finally after an extra alif. (سَبْعَ سَمَوَاتٍ): سبع is accusative as a badal (substitute) from the pronoun. It has also been said that the implied form is: "so He fashioned of them seven heavens", as in His saying: (وَاخْتَارَ مُوسَى قَوْمَهُ), so it would be a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). It has also been said that سوّى is in the sense of صيّر ("made into"), so it would be a second object. (وَهُوَ): it is read with the hāʾ made quiescent, though its original vowel is ḍamma; it was made quiescent only because it became like عضُد and so was lightened; and the same holds for it with the fāʾ and the lām, as in فهو and لهو. It is [also] read with ḍamma, according to the original form.

ukberi-tibyan:30-30.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَإِذْ قَالَ رَبُّكَ لِلْمَلَائِكَةِ إِنِّي جَاعِلٌ فِي الْأَرْضِ خَلِيفَةً قَالُوا أَتَجْعَلُ فِيهَا مَنْ يُفْسِدُ فِيهَا وَيَسْفِكُ الدِّمَاءَ وَنَحْنُ نُسَبِّحُ بِحَمْدِكَ وَنُقَدِّسُ لَكَ قَالَ إِنِّي أَعْلَمُ مَا لَا تَعْلَمُونَ (٣٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَإِذْ قَالَ): it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), its implied form being: "and remember when [your Lord] said".
It has also been said: it is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being: "and the beginning of My creation was when your Lord said". It has also been said: it is redundant (zāʾida). And (لِلْمَلَائِكَةِ): there is disagreement about its singular and its origin. Some said that its singular was originally مألك on the pattern مفعل, because it is derived from الألوكة, which is "message"; from this is the poet's saying:
وَغُلَامٍ أَرْسَلَتْهُ أُمُّهُ بِأَلُوكَ فَبَذَلْنَا مَا سَأَلْ.
(And many a lad whose mother sent him with a message, so we gave what he asked.)
So the hamza is the first radical (fāʾ) of the word; then it was moved back and placed after the lām, and they said ملأك; the poet said:
فَلَسْتُ لِإِنْسِيٍّ وَلَكِنْ لِمَلَاكٍ تَنَزَّلَ ... مِنْ جَوِّ السَّمَاءِ يَصُوبُ.
(For I am not [kin] to a human, but to an angel who descended from the vault of the sky, swooping down.)
So its pattern now is معفل, and the plural is ملائكة on the pattern معافلة.
Others said: the root of the word is لأك, so the second radical (ʿayn) of the word is a hamza, and the origin of ملك is ملأك without any transposition. On both views the vowel of the hamza was cast onto the lām and the hamza was omitted; then when it was put in the plural it was restored, so its pattern now is مفاعلة.
Others said: the second radical of the word is wāw, and it is from لاك يلوك, said when one turns something over in one's mouth; as if the bearer of the message turns it over in his mouth. So the origin of ملك would be like معاد, then its second radical was omitted for lightness, and the origin of ملائكة would be like مقاولة; then the wāw was changed to hamza, as the wāw of مصائب was changed.
Others said: ملك is فعل from المُلك, which is strength; so the mīm is a radical and there is no omission in it, but it was given the plural on the pattern فعائلة irregularly (shādhdh). (جَاعِلٌ): the future is intended by it, and for that reason it governs.
It may be in the sense of خالق ("creating"), and so take one object, or in the sense of مصيّر ("making into"), and so take two objects, in which case في الأرض is the second. (خَلِيفَةً): فعيلة in the sense of فاعل, i.e. one who succeeds another; the hāʾ was added for intensiveness.
(أَتَجْعَلُ): the hamza is for seeking guidance, i.e. "will You place therein one who will cause corruption, as there was in it before?"
It has also been said: they were asking about their own states, i.e. "will You place therein one who causes corruption while we remain in obedience to You, or will we change?" (يَسْفِكُ): the majority read it without doubling and with kasra on the fāʾ; it has also been read with ḍamma on it, and both are dialectal variants; and it is read with doubling (tashdīd) for multiplicity. The hamza of (الدِّمَاءَ) is converted from a yāʾ, because the original form is دمى, since they said دميان.
(بِحَمْدِكَ): in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), its implied form being: "we glorify [You], encompassed by Your praise", or "worshipping by Your praise". (وَنُقَدِّسُ لَكَ): i.e. "for Your sake"; the lām may also be redundant, i.e. "we sanctify You".
It may also be a lām that makes the verb transitive, like the transitivizing bāʾ, as in سجدت لله ("I prostrated to Allah").
(إِنِّي أَعْلَمُ): the original form is إنّني; the middle nūn was omitted, not the nūn of protection (nūn al-wiqāya); this is the correct view. (وَأَعْلَمُ): it may be a verb, with ما as its object, either in the sense of الذي or as an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective, the referring pronoun being omitted. It may also be a noun like أفضل, in which case ما is in the position of the genitive by iḍāfa.
It may also be in the position of the accusative by أعلم, as in their saying: هؤلاء حواجُّ بيتَ الله ("these are pilgrims to the House of Allah"), with the accusative and the genitive; and the tanwīn is dropped because this noun is a diptote. If you say: "أفعل does not take an object in the accusative", it is answered: if من is intended along with it, it does not; but أعلم here is in the sense of عالم ("knowing"). It may also be that by أعلم is meant "more knowing than you", in which case «ما» is in the position of the accusative by an omitted verb indicated by the noun; and similar to it is His saying: (هُوَ أَعْلَمُ مَنْ يَضِلُّ عَنْ سَبِيلِهِ).

ukberi-tibyan:72-72.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِذْ قَتَلْتُمْ نَفْسًا فَادَّارَأْتُمْ فِيهَا وَاللَّهُ مُخْرِجٌ مَا كُنْتُمْ تَكْتُمُونَ (٧٢)).
(وَإِذْ قَتَلْتُمْ): its implied form is "remember when (اذْكُرُوا إِذْ)".
(فَادَّارَأْتُمْ): the original form of the word is تَدَارَأْتُمْ, and its pattern is تَفَاعَلْتُمْ. Then they wanted to lighten it, so they changed the tāʾ into a dāl, so that it would be of the same kind as the dāl which is the first radical (fāʾ) of the word, to make assimilation (idghām) possible. Then they made the dāl quiescent, since the condition of assimilation is that the first letter be quiescent; and since it was not possible to begin with a quiescent letter, a connecting hamza (hamzat al-waṣl) was brought in for it. So its pattern now is افَّاعَلْتُمْ with a doubled fāʾ, transformed from اتْفَاعَلْتُمْ. The first fāʾ is redundant (zāʾida), but it has become of the same kind as the radical, so it is pronounced doubled — not because both are radicals, but because the added letter is of the same kind as the radical. So it is
parallel to your saying ضَرَّبَ with the doubling: one of the two rāʾs is added, and its pattern is فَعَّلَ with a doubled ʿayn, just as the rāʾ is so. We did not say in the pattern فَعْرَلَ or فَرْعَلَ, bringing the added rāʾ into the model; rather the ʿayn was added in the model just as it was added in the original, and it was of the same kind as it. Likewise the tāʾ in تَدَارَأْتُمْ became, by substitution, a dāl of the same kind as the first radical of the word.
If one asks about the pattern in order to distinguish the radical from the added letter, by its first or its second form, the answer is to say: the pattern of its first original form is تَفَاعَلْتُمْ; of the second, اتْفَاعَلْتُمْ; and of the third, افَّاعَلْتُمْ. Like this case is: (اثَّاقَلْتُمْ إِلَى الْأَرْضِ), and (حَتَّى إِذَا ادَّارَكُوا فِيهَا).
His saying, the Exalted: (مُخْرِجٌ مَا كُنْتُمْ تَكْتُمُونَ): ((مَا)) is in the position of the accusative, governed by مُخْرِجٌ. It means "that which" (al-ladhī), and the returning pronoun (al-ʿāʾid) is omitted. It may also be maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun), the maṣdar (verbal noun) then having the sense of the passive participle; i.e. "He brings out your concealing", i.e. "what you conceal".

ukberi-tibyan:73-73.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَقُلْنَا اضْرِبُوهُ بِبَعْضِهَا كَذَلِكَ يُحْيِي اللَّهُ الْمَوْتَى وَيُرِيكُمْ آيَاتِهِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَعْقِلُونَ (٧٣)).
His saying, the Exalted: (كَذَلِكَ يُحْيِي اللَّهُ): the kāf is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), its implied form being: "Allah gives life to the dead with a giving of life like that". And in the speech there is an omission, its implied form being: "so they struck it, and it came to life".

ukberi-tibyan:74-74.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (ثُمَّ قَسَتْ قُلُوبُكُمْ مِنْ بَعْدِ ذَلِكَ فَهِيَ كَالْحِجَارَةِ أَوْ أَشَدُّ قَسْوَةً وَإِنَّ مِنَ الْحِجَارَةِ لَمَا يَتَفَجَّرُ مِنْهُ الْأَنْهَارُ وَإِنَّ مِنْهَا لَمَا يَشَّقَّقُ فَيَخْرُجُ مِنْهُ الْمَاءُ وَإِنَّ مِنْهَا لَمَا يَهْبِطُ مِنْ خَشْيَةِ اللَّهِ وَمَا اللَّهُ بِغَافِلٍ عَمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ (٧٤)).
His saying, the Exalted: (فَهِيَ كَالْحِجَارَةِ): the kāf is a preposition attached (mutaʿalliq) to something omitted, its implied form being: "so they are settled (مُسْتَقِرَّةٌ) like the stones". It may also be a noun meaning "like" (مِثْل), in the position of the nominative, and then it is not attached to anything.
(أَوْ أَشَدُّ): «أَوْ» here is like أَوْ in His saying: (أَوْ كَصَيِّبٍ). And أَشَدُّ is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the kāf, its implied form being: "or they are harder". It was also read with a fatḥa on the dāl, as being genitive by conjunction with الْحِجَارَةِ, its implied form being: "or like what is harder than the stones". And (قَسْوَةً): a tamyīz (specification), and it is a maṣdar (verbal noun). (لَمَا يَتَفَجَّرُ): مَا means "that which", in the position of the accusative as the noun of إِنَّ, and the lām is for emphasis.
Had it been read with the tāʾ [i.e. تَتَفَجَّرُ], it would be permissible; and were it outside the Quran, «مِنْهَا» would be permissible, according to the sense. (يَشَّقَّقُ): its original form is يَتَشَقَّقُ; the tāʾ was changed into a shīn and assimilated. Its fāʿil (agent) is the pronoun of مَا.
Its fāʿil may also be the pronoun of الْمَاءُ, because يَشَقَّقُ may be assigned to the water according to the sense; so you have two verbs, and the second of them governs الْمَاءُ, while the fāʿil of the first is concealed on condition of its being explained [by what follows]. According to the Kufans, the first governs, so that in the second there is its pronoun.
(مِنْ خَشْيَةِ اللَّهِ): مِنْ is in the position of the accusative, governed by (يَهْبِطُ), just as you say: "it descends through fear of Allah (يَهْبِطُ بِخَشْيَةِ اللَّهِ)".
(عَمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ): مَا means "that which", and it may also be maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun).

ukberi-tibyan:75-75.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَفَتَطْمَعُونَ أَنْ يُؤْمِنُوا لَكُمْ وَقَدْ كَانَ فَرِيقٌ مِنْهُمْ يَسْمَعُونَ كَلَامَ اللَّهِ ثُمَّ يُحَرِّفُونَهُ مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا عَقَلُوهُ وَهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ (٧٥)).
His saying, the Exalted: (أَنْ يُؤْمِنُوا لَكُمْ): the preposition is omitted, i.e. "in that they should believe (فِي أَنْ يُؤْمِنُوا)"; and mention has already been made of the grammatical position of the like of this. (وَقَدْ كَانَ): the wāw is the wāw of the ḥāl (circumstantial), and the implied meaning is: "Do you then hope for their belief, when their way is lying and distortion?" مِنْهُمْ is in the position of the nominative as an adjective of فَرِيقٌ, and يَسْمَعُونَ is the khabar (predicate) of كَانَ. Some allowed يَسْمَعُونَ to be an adjective of فَرِيقٌ and مِنْهُمْ to be the khabar, but that is weak. (مَا عَقَلُوهُ): مَا is maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun). وَهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ is a ḥāl, and what governs it is يُحَرِّفُونَهُ; it may also be that what governs it is عَقَلُوهُ, and then it is a corroborative ḥāl (ḥāl muʾakkida).

ukberi-tibyan:76-76.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِذَا خَلَا بَعْضُهُمْ إِلَى بَعْضٍ قَالُوا أَتُحَدِّثُونَهُمْ بِمَا فَتَحَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْكُمْ لِيُحَاجُّوكُمْ بِهِ عِنْدَ رَبِّكُمْ أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ (٧٦)).
His saying, the Exalted: (بِمَا فَتَحَ اللَّهُ): مَا may mean "that which", may be maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun), and may be an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective (nakira mawṣūfa). (لِيُحَاجُّوكُمْ): the lām has the sense of كَيْ ("so that"), and what puts the verb in the accusative is a concealed أَنْ, because the lām is in reality a preposition and enters only on a noun. Most of the Arabs give this lām a kasra, and some of them give it a fatḥa.

ukberi-tibyan:31-31.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَعَلَّمَ آدَمَ الْأَسْمَاءَ كُلَّهَا ثُمَّ عَرَضَهُمْ عَلَى الْمَلَائِكَةِ فَقَالَ أَنْبِئُونِي بِأَسْمَاءِ هَؤُلَاءِ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صَادِقِينَ (٣١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَعَلَّمَ): it may be resumptive, or conjoined to (قَالَ رَبُّكَ), and [then] in the position of the genitive, like the position of قال; this is strengthened by the agent being implied. It has been read «وَعُلِّمَ آدَمُ», as a verb whose agent is not named (passive). And (آدَمَ) is أفعل, and the alif in it replaces a hamza which is the first radical (fāʾ) of the word, because it is derived from أديم الأرض ("the surface of the earth") or from الأُدمة ("brown complexion"). Its pattern cannot be فاعل, since if it were so it would be fully declinable, like عالم and خاتم; definiteness alone does not prevent declension, and it is not a foreign word.
(ثُمَّ عَرَضَهُمْ): meaning the bearers of the names; for that reason the pronoun is masculine.
(هَؤُلَاءِ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ): it is read with full pronunciation (taḥqīq) of both hamzas, according to the original form. It is also read with a single hamza; it has been said that the omitted one is the first, because it is the last radical (lām) of the word, while the other is the beginning of the next word, and omitting the final one is more appropriate.
It has also been said that the omitted one is the second, because the heaviness arose with it.
It is also read with softening (talyīn) of the first hamza and full pronunciation of the second, and the reverse; and some of them change the second into a quiescent yāʾ, as if he regarded the two as being in a single word, seeking lightness.

ukberi-tibyan:32-32.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالُوا سُبْحَانَكَ لَا عِلْمَ لَنَا إِلَّا مَا عَلَّمْتَنَا إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ الْعَلِيمُ الْحَكِيمُ (٣٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (سُبْحَانَكَ): سبحان is a noun occupying the place of the maṣdar (verbal noun); from it سبّحتُ and التسبيح were derived. It is hardly ever used except as a muḍāf, because the iḍāfa makes clear who is being glorified. When it is detached from the iḍāfa it is a proper name (ʿalam) for glorification, a diptote because of definiteness and the alif and nūn at its end, like عثمان. It has occurred in poetry with tanwīn, in the manner of the tanwīn of a proper name when it is made indefinite. What it is annexed to is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), because it is the one glorified.
It may also be the agent, because the meaning is "You are exalted above [all imperfection]". It is accusative as a maṣdar by an omitted verb, its implied form being: سبّحتُ الله تسبيحا ("I glorify Allah with glorification").
(إِلَّا مَا عَلَّمْتَنَا): ما is maṣdariyya (forming a maṣdar), i.e. "except a knowledge You have taught us"; its position is nominative as a badal (substitute) from the position of لا علم, as in your saying: لا إلهَ إلا اللهُ.
It may also be that ما is in the sense of الذي, with علم in the sense of معلوم ("what is known"), i.e. "nothing known to us except what You have taught us". It is not permissible for ما to be in the position of the accusative by العلم, because the noun of لا, when it governs what comes after it, is not made indeclinable. (إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ الْعَلِيمُ): أنت is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and العليم is its khabar (predicate), and the clause is the khabar of إنّ.
It may also be that أنت is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the accusative pronoun; it occurs in the form of the nominative because it is, in meaning, the kāf itself. إياك does not occur here for emphasis, because if it occurred it would be a badal, and إياك is not used for emphasis.
It may also be a separating pronoun (faṣl) having no grammatical position.
And (الْحَكِيمُ): a second khabar, or a ṣifa (adjective) of العليم according to the view of those who allow an adjective of an adjective; and that is correct, because this adjective is in meaning the thing described.
العليم is in the sense of العالم ("knowing"). As for الحكيم, it may be in the sense of الحاكم ("judging"), or in the sense of المُحكِم ("making precise").

ukberi-tibyan:33-33.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالَ يَا آدَمُ أَنْبِئْهُمْ بِأَسْمَائِهِمْ فَلَمَّا أَنْبَأَهُمْ بِأَسْمَائِهِمْ قَالَ أَلَمْ أَقُلْ لَكُمْ إِنِّي أَعْلَمُ غَيْبَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَأَعْلَمُ مَا تُبْدُونَ وَمَا كُنْتُمْ تَكْتُمُونَ (٣٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَنْبِئْهُمْ): it is read with full pronunciation of the hamza, according to the original form, and with yāʾ by softening the hamza; he did not change it by a regular (qiyāsī) change, because if it were so, the yāʾ would be omitted, as it is omitted in your saying أبقِهم, from بقيتُ.
